Wear seat belts, in both front and back seats
A

Wearing a seat belt in the front seat of a passenger car reduces the risk of death in an accident by more than four-tenths. In a light truck, it reduces it by six-tenths. In the US in 2022, among those who died in vehicles where seat belt use was known, half were unrestrained.
Free. Takes an extra 2 seconds each time you get in the vehicle.

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) estimates that wearing seat belts reduces the risk of fatal injury for front-seat passenger car occupants by 45%. For light trucks, the reduction is 60%. In 2022, among passenger vehicle occupants who died in the US where restraint use was known, 50% were unrestrained. According to World Health Organization (WHO) calculations, seat belts reduce the risk of death for vehicle occupants by up to 50%. The WHO estimates that in 2021, China had 248,099 road traffic deaths, or 17.4 per 100,000 population. The National Bureau of Statistics (China) Yearbook recorded 62,218 road traffic deaths in 2021.
Wear a helmet and fasten the strap when riding a motorcycle or electric bicycle
A

Wearing a helmet and fastening the strap properly reduces the risk of death for motorcyclists by about four-tenths in an accident. Head injuries are reduced by about seven-tenths. The strap must be tight; wearing it loosely on the head does not count as wearing it.
A helmet costs ⟦100~300⟧. Takes 5 seconds each time you put it on.

Cochrane pooled multiple studies for a meta-analysis. Motorcyclists wearing helmets have a 42% lower risk of death. The original value is OR = 0.58, 95% CI from 0.50 to 0.68. Head injuries are reduced by 69% (OR = 0.31, 95% CI from 0.25 to 0.38).
Install smoke alarms; if burning coal or using gas heating indoors in winter, also install CO alarms
B

A working smoke alarm reduces the risk of dying in a home fire by about six-tenths. In the US, in fatal home fires, four-tenths of the people were asleep when the fire started. If burning coal or using gas indoors during winter, install an additional CO alarm. In 2018, China had 11,500 deaths from CO poisoning; during the three winter months, about seven-tenths died right inside their homes.
Smoke alarms cost ⟦30~100⟧ each. CO alarms cost ⟦50~150⟧ each. Once installed, replace batteries once a year.

In the state of North Carolina (USA), a study reviewed a series of home fires, comparing houses with fatalities to those without. Having one working smoke alarm reduced the risk of death by about six-tenths. The original value is OR = 0.39, 95% CI from 0.18 to 0.83. In the US from 2018 to 2020, in fatal fires in occupied homes, 24% of homes had no smoke alarms, and 41% of people were asleep when the fire started. In 2018, China recorded 11,523 deaths due to CO poisoning. Of these, 72.59% in December, 67.42% in January, and 66.48% in February occurred at home.
Replace expired gas hoses and stoves, do not repair pipes yourself, and refuse door-to-door sales from gas companies
C

Replacing expired gas hoses and stoves is a user obligation clearly stated in the "Regulations on the Administration of Urban Gas" (China). Self-repairing pipes or dismantling gas meters is explicitly prohibited by the regulations. The same regulations also state: gas companies cannot force you to buy products or services they designate. If a door-to-door salesperson says a replacement is "mandatory," you can simply refuse.
A standard gas hose costs a few dozen yuan. Gas stoves are replaced every few years. When replacing, check if they have expired.

The regulations state that "timely replacement of gas-burning appliances, connecting hoses... that the State has ordered to be eliminated or have reached the end of their service life" is the user's obligation: you must replace stoves and hoses that have reached their limit or been phased out by the State. The regulations also classify "unauthorized installation, modification, or dismantling of indoor gas facilities and gas metering devices" as prohibited acts; repairing pipes yourself or dismantling gas meters falls into this category. The regulations also clearly state that gas business units shall not force users to purchase products they designate, nor shall they force users to accept services they provide.
Do not pick, buy, or eat wild mushrooms; all "folk tips for identifying poisonous mushrooms" are incorrect
A

In 2025 alone, the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention (China CDC) investigated 828 mushroom poisoning incidents, involving 2,165 people and 13 deaths. That year, 34 mushroom species not previously recorded as poisonous were identified. Testing with silver needles, assuming mushrooms eaten by insects are safe, or believing only brightly colored mushrooms are toxic—these claims are all false.
Free. The difficulty lies in giving up a seasonal delicacy.

In 2025, the China CDC investigated 828 mushroom poisoning incidents involving 2,165 people and 13 deaths. The case fatality rate was 0.6%, meaning 0.6% of poisoned individuals died. From 2019 to 2024, there were 276 to 676 incidents annually, with fatality rates ranging from 0.87% to 2.86%. In 2025 alone, 138 poisonous mushroom species were identified, 34 of which were recorded for the first time in China. A public education article from the China CDC debunked various folk identification methods. Only brightly colored ones are poisonous: false, toxicity is unrelated to color. Mushrooms with insect damage or maggots are safe: false, many highly toxic species are eaten by insects when mature. Cooking with silver items or garlic that change color indicates toxicity: false, mushroom toxins do not contain sulfur; silver turns black due to sulfur. Frying at high temperatures to detoxify: also unreliable. The article concluded that "there is currently no simple, easy, fast, and effective way to identify whether a mushroom is poisonous." In 2026, the Beijing Municipal Administration for Market Regulation (China) advised that if you feel unwell after accidental ingestion, "seek medical attention immediately, absolutely do not self-treat," and keep leftover mushrooms and food to help doctors identify the toxin.
Do not bring electric bicycles into hallways or elevators, and do not charge them indoors
A

Leaving or charging electric bicycles in the lobbies, hallways, or stairwells of high-rise residential buildings is explicitly prohibited by regulations from the Ministry of Emergency Management (China). Failure to comply can result in fines of ⟦500~1000⟧ for individuals and ⟦2000~10000⟧ for businesses. The fine is a minor issue; the real danger is that such fires often block your only escape route.
Free. The difficulty is having to leave the vehicle at a centralized charging point downstairs every time and walking an extra few dozen meters.

Regulations from the Ministry of Emergency Management (China) explicitly prohibit: "Parking electric bicycles or charging electric bicycles in public lobbies, evacuation passages, stairwells, or safety exits of high-rise residential buildings." Lobbies, passages, stairwells, and safety exits are all off-limits for parking and charging. Failure to correct the behavior results in fines of ⟦500~1000⟧ for non-business entities and individuals, and ⟦2000~10000⟧ for businesses. These regulations do not mention elevators or interiors. In response to National People's Congress deputies, the Ministry of Emergency Management stated it has made rectifying the illegal indoor storage and charging of electric bicycles and batteries a focus for major fire risk management. The Ministry warned the public about the dangers of "bringing vehicles indoors, pulling wires out of windows, and unauthorized disassembly or repair." Elevators are managed by local laws: Beijing, as of May 1, 2025, prohibits bringing electric bicycles or batteries into elevator cabs, with fines of ⟦500~1000⟧ for individuals who refuse to comply.
Measure your blood pressure; if it is high, take medication to reach your target
A

For every 10 mmHg reduction in systolic blood pressure (the top number), the risk of major cardiovascular events drops by two-tenths, and stroke risk drops by 27%. Heart failure risk drops by 28%, and the risk of death decreases by 13%. In China, among people aged 35 to 75, 44.7% have hypertension, but only 7.2% actually have it under control.

An electronic blood pressure monitor costs ⟦100~200⟧. One measurement takes 1 minute. Most antihypertensive drugs cost a few to a few dozen yuan per month. The difficulty is continuing to take them even when there are no symptoms.

A meta-analysis of 123 trials involving over 610,000 people was conducted. For every 10 mmHg reduction in systolic blood pressure, major cardiovascular events decreased by about two-tenths. The original value is RR = 0.80, 95% CI from 0.77 to 0.83. Systolic blood pressure is the higher of the two readings. Strokes decreased by about 27% (RR = 0.73). Heart failure decreased by about 28% (RR = 0.72). Overall mortality decreased by 13% (RR = 0.87, 95% CI from 0.84 to 0.91). China once screened 1.7 million people aged 35 to 75: 44.7% had hypertension. Among these, 44.7% were aware of their condition, 30.1% were receiving treatment, and only 7.2% had it under control.
If overweight after age 35, get a fasting blood glucose test; if normal, retest every three years
A

Spending a few dozen yuan on a blood draw can detect prediabetes before any symptoms appear. The official US screening recommendation is: people aged 35 to 70 who are overweight or obese should be tested. If results are normal, retest every three years. The US defines overweight starting at a Body Mass Index (BMI) of 25, lowered to 23 for people of Asian descent; the Chinese standard considers 24 as overweight.
Fasting blood glucose costs over ten yuan. HbA1c costs a few dozen yuan. One trip to the hospital for a blood draw is all it takes.

The United States Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF) is the official body that issues screening recommendations in the US. Their current recommendation is: screen for prediabetes and type 2 diabetes in adults aged 35 to 70 who are overweight or obese, even if they have no symptoms. Overweight is BMI ≥ 25, and obesity is BMI ≥ 30. For Asian Americans, they recommend lowering the threshold to BMI ≥ 23, because at the same BMI, people of Asian descent have a higher risk of diabetes. China's industry standard is: BMI from 24.0 to less than 28.0 is overweight, and ≥ 28.0 is obese. The recommendation level for this is B. The recommendation also explicitly states: "for adults with normal blood glucose levels, screening every 3 years is reasonable."
Do not speed, do not drive after drinking, do not look at your phone, and stop to rest if sleepy
B

For every 1% increase in average speed, the risk of a fatal crash increases by about 4%. There is no safe threshold for alcohol, like "a little is fine." Operating a handheld phone while driving makes an accident 3.6 times more likely than focused driving; dialing a number makes it 12.2 times more likely. Being so sleepy that it is visible to others makes an accident about 3.4 times more likely.

Free. Driving a bit slower adds a few minutes to each trip. The difficulty is drinking less at social gatherings and resisting the urge to check messages. For long-distance driving, stop and rest for at least 20 minutes every 4 hours.

According to the World Health Organization (WHO): for every 1% increase in average speed, the risk of a fatal accident increases by 4%. The risk of driving after drinking alcohol starts to increase even at very low blood alcohol concentrations. The WHO also states that drivers using mobile phones are about 4 times more likely to be involved in a crash than those not using them; using headsets or speakers is not much safer. A US study installed cameras in the vehicles of over 3,500 drivers, recording 905 crashes involving injury or property damage. The control group consisted of segments of alert, focused driving without alcohol. Aggregating handheld phone operations, the risk of an accident was 3.6 times higher (OR = 3.6). Dialing was 12.2 times higher, texting was 6.1 times higher, reaching for a phone was 4.8 times higher, browsing was 2.7 times higher, and talking on a handheld device was 2.2 times higher. Visible drowsiness in the video was associated with a 3.4 times higher risk (OR = 3.4).
Use safety seats for children under 4 in cars; do not hold them in your lap
A

For children under 1 year old, using a safety seat in a car reduces the risk of fatal injury in an accident by about seven-tenths. For children aged 1 to 4, it reduces it by about half. Holding them in your lap does not provide this protection.
A seat costs ⟦300~2000⟧ and lasts several years. It takes an extra 1 minute to secure the child each time you get in the car.

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) estimates that using safety seats reduces the risk of fatal injury for infants under 1 year old in passenger cars by 71%. For children aged 1 to 4, the reduction is 54%. According to World Health Organization (WHO) calculations, deaths among young children are reduced by 71%.
If there are young children at home, install window and balcony restrictors; mosquito nets are not protective gear
B

A set of restrictors costs a few dozen yuan. New York City installed free window guards for high-risk households and provided on-site instructions; the number of reported child falls in one borough decreased by half after three years. Subsequently, New York passed a law requiring landlords to install guards for apartments with children aged 10 or younger. Mosquito nets are not protective gear.
A set of window restrictors or child safety locks costs a few dozen yuan. Installation takes ten minutes.

Since 1972, New York has had a program called "Children Can't Fly," distributing free window guards in high-risk areas and providing on-site instructions. The number of reported falls in the Bronx decreased by 50% from 1973 to 1975. New York then amended its health code, requiring landlords to install window guards for apartments with children aged 10 or younger.
Keep eyes on children near water; wear life jackets when boating or swimming in rivers and lakes
A

If you fall into the water while boating, wearing a life jacket reduces the chance of drowning by about half compared to not wearing one. To date, drowning remains the leading cause of death for children aged 1 to 14 in China. The drowning rate in rural areas is approximately double that of urban areas.
Life jacket ⟦50~200⟧. Additionally, the attention required to supervise children.

A study using U.S. Coast Guard data paired individuals with similar conditions for comparison. People who fell into the water during recreational boating had their risk of drowning reduced by about half if they wore a life jacket. The original value is adjusted RR = 0.51, 95% CI 0.35 to 0.74. The drowning rate for people under 20 in China decreased from 6.60 per 100,000 population in 2013 to 3.28 per 100,000 in 2021. Rural rates are about 2 times higher than urban rates. In 2021, the rural rate was 3.84 per 100,000, while the urban rate was 2.01. Drowning remains the leading cause of death for children aged 1 to 14. In 2021, the drowning rate for the 1 to 14 age group was 3.23 per 100,000, higher than the second leading cause, road traffic injuries, at 0.99. In 2021, among injury-related deaths for those aged 0 to 19, drowning accounted for 31.1% and road traffic for 27.9%. The 15 to 19 age group had the highest drowning rate at 3.95 per 100,000, with males specifically at 5.99.
If over 60, practice balance and leg strength; renovate bathrooms and indoor stairs
A

Practicing balance two to three times a week, such as Tai Chi, reduces the number of falls among the elderly by about 23% and the number of people who fall by 15%. Having a professional conduct a home assessment and renovation reduces the frequency of falls by about two-tenths. Falls are the leading cause of injury-related death for people over 65 in China, and more than half of these falls occur right inside their own homes.

Practice 2 to 3 times a week, 30 minutes each of Tai Chi or balance exercises. Anti-slip bathroom mats, handrails, and night lights cost a few dozen to a few hundred yuan. The difficulty lies in long-term persistence.

Cochrane pooled 108 trials involving 23,407 people for a meta-analysis. Exercise reduced the number of falls in older adults by 23%. The original value is the rate ratio RaR = 0.77, 95% CI 0.71 to 0.83. The number of people falling decreased by 15% (RR = 0.85). Professional home safety assessments and modifications reduced fall frequency by about two-tenths (RR = 0.81, 95% CI 0.68 to 0.97). Practicing Tai Chi reduced the risk of falling by about 29% (RR = 0.71). In China, falls are the leading cause of injury-related death for people over 65. In 2018, among monitored falls in the elderly, 55.97% occurred at home.
Test for Hepatitis B markers and check vaccination records to see if catch-up vaccination is needed
A

In a study in Qidong, children vaccinated against Hepatitis B at birth later showed an 84% reduction in the risk of liver cancer. This reduction rate cannot be directly applied to adults, nor should one receive three catch-up doses solely due to low antibodies. People who have completed the full series, once had protective antibodies, and have normal immunity usually do not need a booster. If unsure of your status, bring your test results to a vaccination clinic for evaluation.

A single test costs a few dozen yuan. For adults needing vaccination, three doses of Hepatitis B vaccine total approximately ⟦100~300⟧, depending on the clinic's price. Usually administered on a 0, 1, 6-month schedule.

The Qidong trial used cluster randomization by community rather than individuals, with a 30-year follow-up. Newborns vaccinated against Hepatitis B had an 84% reduction in primary liver cancer. 95% CI 23% to 97%. The Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) positivity rate decreased by 72% (95% CI 68% to 75%); this positivity rate indicates the proportion of people testing positive for the virus. In the control group, 67.8% received catch-up vaccination at ages 10 to 14. The effectiveness of catch-up vaccination on HBsAg positivity in early adulthood was only 21% (95% CI 10% to 30%), far inferior to vaccination at birth. The HBsAg positivity rate in the general Chinese population decreased by 52% from 1992 to 2014, and by 97% in children under 5. These figures cannot be directly applied to adult catch-up vaccination. Immunocompetent individuals who completed the full series and once had protective antibodies usually do not need boosters even if antibodies decline, as they retain immune memory. Immune memory allows the body to mobilize defenses very quickly upon re-exposure. Whether catch-up is needed depends on a simultaneous review of vaccination records, surface antigen, surface antibody, and core antibody. If vaccination history is unknown, go to a vaccination clinic for evaluation.
If punctured by iron nails or wood splinters, or if a wound is contaminated with soil, seek treatment the same day and ask if a tetanus shot is needed
B

In the U.S., about 1 in 10 people who develop tetanus die. Deep wounds and soil-contaminated wounds pose the highest risk. For dirty wounds, if the last shot was over 5 years ago, a booster is required. Seeking treatment on the same day costs only a few dozen yuan; do not delay.
Consultation and wound treatment cost a few dozen yuan. If a doctor deems it necessary, the vaccine or immunoglobulin costs a few dozen to a few hundred yuan.

Among tetanus cases in the U.S., about 1 in 10 results in death. Deep wounds and wounds contaminated with soil carry higher risks. China's 2024 diagnostic and treatment guidelines categorize wounds into two levels. Shallow wounds treated within 6 hours, not contaminated with soil, feces, or animal saliva, are low risk. Wounds treated after 6 hours, contaminated with those substances, or punctures, avulsions, crush injuries, burns, frostbite, or wounds with foreign bodies are high risk. For those with 3 or more doses where the last dose was less than 5 years ago, no treatment is needed. Between 5 to 10 years, high-risk wounds require 1 booster. After 10 years, any wound requires 1 booster. Those with fewer than 3 doses or unknown history must complete the vaccine series. High-risk wounds also require simultaneous passive immunization (immunoglobulin or antitoxin, which injects antibodies directly).
Women should get the HPV vaccine as early as possible
A

Sweden followed 1.67 million women. Those vaccinated against HPV before age 17 had only about one-eighth the risk of developing invasive cervical cancer later compared to those unvaccinated. Vaccination between ages 17 and 30 still reduced the risk by about half. Therefore, the earlier the vaccination, the more worthwhile it is.
Domestic (Chinese) bivalent vaccine is about ⟦300⟧ per dose; imported 9-valent is about ⟦1300⟧ per dose. Total of 2 to 3 doses. Each visit takes half a day.

Sweden followed 1.67 million women to gather statistics: vaccinated individuals had lower incidence rates of invasive cervical cancer than unvaccinated ones. Vaccination before age 17 reduced risk by approximately 88% (IRR = 0.12, 95% CI 0.00 to 0.34). Vaccination between ages 17 and 30 reduced risk by approximately 53% (IRR = 0.47, 95% CI 0.27 to 0.75). The World Health Organization prioritizes girls aged 9 to 14 who have not yet been sexually active for vaccination.
Women from age 40 should undergo breast cancer screening with a mammogram every two years
A

Women aged 40 to 74 should have a mammogram every two years; this is a clear official screening recommendation in the U.S. For those aged 75 and older, and regarding supplemental ultrasound or MRI for women with dense breasts, the official conclusion is that evidence is insufficient. If a health checkup package charges extra for these items, you may choose not to purchase them.
A mammogram costs two to three hundred yuan per session. Many places have free screening programs. It takes half a day every two years.

The U.S. Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF) is the official body providing screening recommendations in the U.S. Their current recommendation is: "recommends biennial screening mammography for women aged 40 to 74 years." This is a Grade B recommendation. For women aged 75 and older, and for supplemental ultrasound or MRI for dense breasts, they assess that "current evidence is insufficient." China's 2021 breast cancer screening guidelines recommend average-risk women start at age 45, every 1 to 2 years. High-risk women should start at age 40, once a year.
Women from age 30 should undergo cervical cancer screening, with HPV testing as the priority
A

In a trial in rural India, women who received just one HPV test reduced their risk of dying from cervical cancer by about half. The likelihood of being diagnosed with late-stage cervical cancer also decreased by about five-tenths. One test costs one to two hundred yuan; according to U.S. recommendations, it should be done every 5 years.
An HPV test costs ⟦100~300⟧. If the result is negative, once every 5 years is sufficient. Sampling takes a few minutes.

A trial in rural India used cluster randomization by community. Subjects were women aged 30 to 59. With just a single round of HPV screening, the risk of death from cervical cancer was reduced by approximately 48%. The original value is HR = 0.52, 95% CI 0.33 to 0.83. The risk of being diagnosed with late-stage cervical cancer decreased by about 53% (HR = 0.47, 95% CI 0.32 to 0.69). The interval between tests follows the 2018 USPSTF recommendation: for women aged 30 to 65, high-risk HPV testing alone every 5 years.
Start colorectal cancer screening between ages 45 and 50, using fecal immunochemical tests or colonoscopy
A

Performing a fecal occult blood test costing a few dozen yuan every one to two years reduces the risk of dying from colorectal cancer by about 16%; those who completed at least one round saw a 25% reduction. For those invited for a single colonoscopy, the risk of developing colorectal cancer over the next ten years decreased from 1.20% to 0.98%.

Fecal tests cost a few dozen yuan, performed every 1 to 2 years. Colonoscopy costs a few hundred to over ⟦1000⟧; if the result is negative, once every 10 years is sufficient. One day is required for bowel preparation before the colonoscopy.

Cochrane pooled multiple studies for a meta-analysis. Screening with fecal occult blood tests reduced the risk of colorectal cancer death by approximately 16%. The original value is RR = 0.84, 95% CI 0.78 to 0.90. Those who participated in at least one round saw a reduction of about 25% (RR = 0.75). Looking at the NordICC randomized trial, for those invited to undergo colonoscopy, the 10-year incidence of colorectal cancer decreased from 1.20% to 0.98%. The original value is RR = 0.82, 95% CI 0.70 to 0.93.
People with cardiovascular disease and the elderly should receive an annual influenza vaccine
A

In a trial of influenza vaccination following myocardial infarction, the one-year mortality rate decreased from 4.9% to 2.9%. For people with cardiovascular disease and the elderly, an additional shot every autumn costs ⟦50~150⟧.
One shot costs ⟦50~150⟧. Administered once a year in the autumn.

A trial conducted on 2,571 patients who recently had a myocardial infarction used random assignment. Neither doctors nor patients knew which injection was given. Those who received the influenza vaccine had a 12-month all-cause mortality rate of 2.9%. The placebo group was 4.9%. The original value is HR = 0.59, 95% CI 0.39 to 0.89. A placebo is a control injection with no active ingredients. The HR for cardiovascular death was 0.59. Another meta-analysis showed that those vaccinated against influenza had a major cardiovascular event rate of 3.6%, compared to 5.4% in the control group. The original value is RR = 0.66, 95% CI 0.53 to 0.83. Cardiovascular death RR = 0.74 (95% CI 0.42 to 1.30, this difference remains within the margin of error and is not statistically significant).
Get the shingles (zoster) vaccine after age 50
A

In phase 3 trials, this vaccine blocked 97% of shingles cases, with similar results across all age groups. The downside is that two doses cost ⟦4000⟧, paid entirely out-of-pocket. That amount buys a ninety-seven percent reduction in cases.
The recombinant shingles vaccine requires two doses, totaling approximately ⟦3000~4000⟧. This amount is paid entirely out-of-pocket.

A phase 3 trial in 18 countries involving 15,400 people. The trial was randomized into two groups: one receiving the vaccine and one receiving a control injection, with a mean follow-up of 3.2 years. Results showed 6 cases in the vaccine group and 210 cases in the placebo group. This translates to 0.3 per 1,000 person-years compared to 9.1; 1,000 person-years means the number of cases occurring when following 1,000 people for one year. The original paper states "overall vaccine efficacy against herpes zoster was 97.2% (95% confidence interval, 93.7 to 99.0; P < 0.001)". Efficacy across age groups ranged from 96.6% to 97.9%. Within 7 days after vaccination, injection-site and systemic reactions were more common in the vaccine group. Grade 3 symptoms (the most severe) were reported by 17.0% of the vaccine group and 3.2% of the placebo group. The rates of serious adverse events and deaths were similar in both groups.
Get the pneumococcal vaccine from age 65 onwards
A

In a trial of 84,500 elderly people, the 13-valent pneumococcal vaccine blocked about 46% of pneumonia cases caused by the strains included in the vaccine. For the most dangerous invasive infections, it blocked 75%. However, no effect was seen for "all-cause pneumonia," so do not expect it to prevent every type of pneumonia.
A few hundred yuan. Some places provide it free of charge for the elderly.

The Netherlands randomized 84,500 people aged 65 and older into two groups for comparison. The vaccine used was the 13-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine. Efficacy against vaccine-type pneumonia was 45.6%. The 95.2% confidence interval was 21.8 to 62.5. Vaccine-type strains are the bacterial strains that this vaccine protects against. Efficacy against invasive pneumococcal disease was 75.0% (95% confidence interval, 41.4 to 90.8), which is the most dangerous type of infection. For all-cause pneumonia combined, it had no effect.
Test for HP (Helicobacter pylori) bacteria and treat for eradication if positive
A

In a trial in Linqu County, Shandong Province, followed for 22 years, people who successfully eradicated HP bacteria later reduced their risk of stomach cancer by about half. The risk of dying from stomach cancer decreased by about four-tenths. The test costs one or two hundred yuan, and eradication involves taking medication for two weeks.

C13 or C14 breath test ⟦100~200⟧. Eradicating HP requires taking four types of medication simultaneously; the cost for two weeks of medication is ⟦200~500⟧. The difficulty lies in taking them on time for the full two weeks.

A randomized controlled trial in Linqu County, Shandong Province, followed for 22 years. People who received treatment to eradicate HP bacteria reduced their risk of stomach cancer by about half. The original value was OR = 0.48, 95% confidence interval 0.32 to 0.71. The risk of death from stomach cancer decreased by approximately 38% (HR = 0.62, 95% confidence interval 0.39 to 0.99).
Heavy smokers should have a low-dose chest CT scan once a year
A

Eligible heavy smokers who have a low-dose CT scan annually have a 20% lower risk of dying from lung cancer compared to those who only receive chest X-rays. The overall mortality rate is 6.7% lower. The trade-off is the need for follow-up scans for suspicious results and the anxiety experienced during that period.
⟦200~400⟧ per scan, completed in 10 minutes. Additionally, one must account for follow-up scans after a false alarm and the anxiety during that interval.

The NLST randomized trial in the US included 53,454 people, all aged 55 to 74, with a smoking history of 30 pack-years or more, who had quit no more than 15 years prior. A pack-year is a unit for measuring smoking volume; one pack per day for one year equals one pack-year. The results were as follows: for those receiving low-dose CT compared to those receiving only chest X-rays, lung cancer mortality was reduced by a relative 20.0%. The 95% confidence interval was 6.8 to 26.7. Overall mortality was reduced by a relative 6.7%, 95% confidence interval 1.2 to 13.6. Each person was screened for three consecutive years; across the three rounds, 24.2% of low-dose CT results were suspicious. Among the suspicious results, 96.4% were false alarms (false positives).
Call 12356 if depressed or having suicidal thoughts; do not stockpile sleeping pills or pesticides at home
B

Keep lethal means out of reach: evidence for this approach is growing stronger. After tightening regulations on painkillers, related suicides dropped by 43%. Locations where people frequently jump saw an 86% reduction after barriers were installed. Therefore, do not stockpile sleeping pills or pesticides at home. If feeling desperate, call 12356 first; it is a nationwide number open at least 18 hours a day.
Free of charge. Make a phone call. Additionally, lock the medicine cabinet and do not keep pesticides in the house.

A systematic review of studies over nearly 10 years shows that evidence for restricting access to lethal means is increasingly strong. After tightening regulations on painkillers, painkiller-related suicides decreased by 43%. Locations where people frequently jump saw an 86% reduction (ranging from 79% to 91%, the confidence interval for this figure) after barriers were installed. School-based awareness programs reduced suicide attempts by about 55% (OR = 0.45, 95% confidence interval 0.24 to 0.85). Medication and psychotherapy for depression are vital parts of suicide prevention. Starting May 1, 2025, in China, calling 12356 from anywhere in the country connects to a psychological support hotline, open no less than 18 hours a day.
Equip your home with fire extinguishers, fire blankets, escape respirators, and a first aid kit; inspect them annually
B

Fire extinguishers, fire blankets, escape masks, and first aid kits are all on the Ministry of Emergency Management's (China) list of 11 essential household emergency items. The entire set costs a few hundred yuan and is a one-time purchase. In studies where safety instructors visited homes, injury rates dropped by about a quarter.
A fire extinguisher, a fire blanket, one respirator per person, plus a first aid kit cost a few hundred yuan for the set. It is a one-time purchase, followed by a ten-minute annual inspection.

The "Recommended List of Household Emergency Supplies, National Basic Version" by the Ministry of Emergency Management (China) contains 11 items. Among them, "fire extinguishers and fire blankets" are used to "extinguish initial fires"; the list also specifies that "fire blankets can be wrapped around the body for escape." "Respirators" are "fire self-rescue filter masks used when escaping from a fire." "External medications" include "hemostatic powder, adhesive bandages, gauze, roll bandages... used for wound treatment." Cochrane pooled 98 studies involving 2,605,044 people for a combined analysis. Home safety interventions reduced injury rates to IRR = 0.89, 95% confidence interval 0.78 to 1.01. For home-visit interventions specifically, the injury rate was about 25% lower (IRR = 0.75, 95% confidence interval 0.62 to 0.91).
If you see blood in your urine, even if painless and gone the next day, see a doctor once
B

According to outpatient records in the UK, about 2.8% of people aged 60 and older with visible blood in their urine were eventually diagnosed with bladder cancer. For those aged 40 to 59, it was about 1.2%. These figures are not high, but high enough to mandate a medical check-up. Even if it only happens once, in a small amount, and without pain, you must go.
A routine urinalysis costs a few dozen yuan, and a urinary system ultrasound costs one to two hundred yuan. If the doctor deems it necessary, a cystoscopy costs about ⟦1000⟧.

A UK study used electronic medical records from community general practices (primary care), comparing 4,915 bladder cancer cases with 21,718 controls. Among those with visible blood in their urine, the percentage who actually had bladder cancer was as follows: 2.8% for those aged 60 and older (95% confidence interval 2.5 to 3.1) and 1.2% for those aged 40 to 59 (confidence interval 0.6 to 2.3). This rate is technically known as the positive predictive value. Blood in the urine visible only under a microscope also had significance: the odds ratio was 20, 95% confidence interval 12 to 33. For those aged 60 and older, this rate was 1.6%, confidence interval 1.2 to 2.1. The UK National Health Service (NHS) states that blood in the urine can be a sign of cancer and must be checked. Even if there are no other symptoms, even if it is the first time, and even if the amount is small, you should book an appointment with a doctor promptly.
If you have erectile dysfunction, check your heart first; don't treat it as just a "bedroom issue"
A

Men with erectile dysfunction are about four-tenths more likely to develop cardiovascular disease later and about six-tenths more likely to have a heart attack. The younger the person, the larger the difference. Therefore, check your blood pressure, blood sugar, and blood lipids first, rather than just buying medication to get by.
A consultation fee of a few dozen yuan. Blood pressure measurement and blood tests for sugar and lipids cost one to two hundred yuan. It requires one hospital visit and a few days' wait for results.

A meta-analysis combined 14 longitudinal studies totaling 92,757 men, with a mean follow-up of 6.1 years. Compared to men without erectile dysfunction, those with the condition faced the following risks: overall cardiovascular events were about 44% higher (RR = 1.44, 95% confidence interval 1.27 to 1.63). Myocardial infarction was about 62% higher (RR = 1.62, 1.34 to 1.96). Cerebrovascular events were about 39% higher (RR = 1.39, 1.23 to 1.57). All-cause mortality was about 25% higher (RR = 1.25, 1.12 to 1.39). Cardiovascular mortality specifically showed no significant difference (RR = 1.19, 0.97 to 1.46). The younger the age, the higher the multiplier. The group with moderate baseline cardiovascular risk had a higher multiplier than both the high-risk and low-risk groups. Studies using questionnaires found a multiplier of 1.61 (1.38 to 1.86). Studies asking only a single question found 1.27 (1.18 to 1.37).
Losing weight, quitting smoking, and controlling blood pressure and blood sugar will also improve erectile function
A

Controlling cardiovascular risk factors will inherently improve erectile function. Measured by a questionnaire, the average score increased by 2 to 3 points. This questionnaire has a total score of 25, with 22 or above considered normal.
Free of charge, and may even save money. The difficulty lies in long-term persistence: diet, exercise, and quitting smoking.

A meta-analysis combined 6 randomized controlled trials involving 740 men. Interventions were lifestyle changes or medication to control cardiovascular risk factors, with at least 6 weeks of follow-up. Results: the International Index of Erectile Function (IIEF-5) score increased by an average of 2.66 points (95% confidence interval 1.86 to 3.47). Excluding 2 trials using statins (143 people), the remaining 4 trials involving only lifestyle changes (597 people) still showed an increase of 2.40 points (1.19 to 3.61). The IIEF-5 is a 5-question survey with a total score from 5 to 25. The original paper categorized scores into five levels: 22 to 25 points indicates no dysfunction, while 5 to 7 points indicates severe dysfunction.
Use condoms from start to finish during sex; do not share needles or injection equipment
A

Using a condom consistently every time reduces the risk of HIV transmission between men and women by about seven-tenths or more. The effectiveness of "using them most of the time" is not much different from not using them at all. Condoms also protect against other STDs, but they cannot block syphilis or herpes if the sores are in areas the condom does not cover.
One to two yuan per piece. The difficulty is not the cost, but using them every time and putting them on right from the start.

A meta-analysis of 25 studies involving 10,676 heterosexual couples. These were serodiscordant couples, where one partner was HIV-positive and the other was HIV-negative. Compared to those who never used them, those who used condoms every time had an approximately 71% lower risk of HIV transmission. The original figure was RR = 0.29, 95% confidence interval 0.20 to 0.43. Compared to inconsistent users, the risk was about 77% lower (RR = 0.23, 95% confidence interval 0.13 to 0.40). The authors concluded that while condoms are not perfect, "consistent use can reduce HIV transmission by more than 70%." The World Health Organization states that correct and consistent condom use is one of the most effective ways to prevent STDs (including HIV). However, condoms do not prevent syphilis or genital herpes if the sores are located in areas not covered by the condom.
If you have ever engaged in high-risk behavior, get tested for HIV once at a free disease control center; results are kept confidential
A

HIV testing at Centers for Disease Control (China) is free of charge. Without your consent, no unit or individual may disclose your name, address, workplace, or medical history. A positive result is not a death sentence: people who take medication regularly to the point where the virus is suppressed to undetectable levels can no longer transmit it to their partners. In studies, there was not a single case of transmission between such couples.
Free of charge. Take one trip to a center for disease control or a designated medical facility to have a tube of blood drawn. The difficult part is the step of speaking up to request the test.

Article 23 of the "AIDS Prevention and Control Regulations" (China) clearly states: health authorities at the county level or above shall designate certain medical facilities. These facilities "must provide free consultation and initial screening tests for those who voluntarily seek AIDS consultation and testing." The significance of early testing is not just for peace of mind: current antiretroviral therapy suppresses the virus to undetectable levels. The World Health Organization's phrasing is "people living with HIV who are on antiretroviral therapy and have an undetectable viral load do not transmit HIV to their sexual partners." The PARTNER study followed 782 same-sex couples where one partner was infected and the other was not; the technical term is serodiscordant. A total of 1.593 couple-years (the sum of follow-up years for each couple) were recorded. During that time, there were a total of 76.088 instances of unprotected sex, resulting in 15 new infections. After comparing viral genes using phylogenetic analysis, none of these 15 cases came from the partner; transmission between the two people in the couple was zero. Article 39 of the Regulations stipulates: "Without the consent of the individual or their guardian, no unit or individual may disclose the name, address, workplace, portrait, medical records, and other information that could infer the specific identity of people living with HIV, AIDS patients, and their families."
The moment a suicidal thought arises, tell someone nearby immediately and entrust those few dozen minutes to them
B

In an interview study, nearly half of survivors of suicide attempts said that the time from the thought arising to the act was no more than 10 minutes. Three-quarters had contact with someone nearby during that time frame. Among people hospitalized for self-harm, about 2% die by suicide after 1 year, and about 7% after 9 years or more; the vast majority do not eventually die by suicide.
Free of charge. The difficulty lies in speaking up at that exact moment and admitting that for these few hours, one cannot be alone.

82 survivors of suicide attempts were interviewed within 3 days of hospitalization: 47.6% (39 people) said the time from when the suicidal thought first arose during this episode to the actual act was no more than 10 minutes. Those for whom this process lasted longer had significantly higher suicide intent scores. Impulsivity scale scores were not related to the length of the process. 76.8% (63 people) said they had some contact with a spouse, family member, or friend during that time. The author's conclusion: the window for intervention is often very short, and professionals have little opportunity to intervene at this stage. Therefore, the author advocates for popularizing ways to recognize signs and intervention methods among ordinary people. Another systematic review synthesized 90 follow-up studies. For people seeking medical attention for self-harm, the rate of repeated non-fatal self-harm after 1 year had a median of 16%. After 1 year, 2% died by suicide. In studies with follow-up of 9 years or more, about 7% died by suicide.
Do not treat "being saved" as a safety net: after drinking pesticides or carbon monoxide poisoning, emergency care may save your life but might not save your lungs or brain
B

Paraquat has no effective antidote; in a group of patients in Bangladesh, more than four out of ten could not be saved. It causes the lungs to become inflamed and then gradually stiffen, with the kidneys and liver also suffering damage. Carbon monoxide poisoning victims who are saved but only receive standard oxygen therapy have nearly half of their cognitive functions impaired after six weeks; for those receiving hyperbaric oxygen, it is still one-quarter.
Free of charge. You just need to know this beforehand.

A systematic review of paraquat poisoning: the mortality rate is extremely high because the substance itself is highly toxic and effective treatments are lacking. It is actively transported into lung tissue against the concentration gradient (the technical term is active uptake against a concentration gradient), resulting in pneumonia and pulmonary fibrosis. It also causes kidney and liver damage. The review clearly states: gastric lavage is not recommended. Hemodialysis and hemoperfusion are unlikely to change the clinical course. Evidence for the effectiveness of corticosteroids and immunosuppressants is very weak. The review also notes: "the mortality rate in all centers is very high, despite widely varying treatments." 10 tertiary hospitals in Bangladesh from 2013 to 2024 received 1.420 cases, of which 257 were analyzed: the mortality rate was 43.2%. Common manifestations included leg edema due to acute renal failure (71.2%), vomiting (65.8%), and abdominal pain (58.0%). A trial on acute CO poisoning was a randomized double-blind trial with 76 people per group. Neither doctors nor patients knew who was in which group. At week six, the number of people with cognitive sequelae: hyperbaric oxygen group 19/76 (25.0%). Normobaric oxygen group 35/76 (46.1%), P = 0.007. After adjusting for other factors, OR = 0.45 (95% confidence interval from 0.22 to 0.92). Another study following 73 consecutive cases: 30% had cognitive sequelae, 12% had increased brain white matter signal. From July 1, 2014, China revoked the registration and production licenses for liquid paraquat and ceased production. From July 1, 2016, the liquid form was banned from domestic sale and use. From September 26, 2020, the sale and use of soluble gel forms were banned within Chinese territory. The document explicitly states the direct reason for tightening management was "frequent occurrences of suicide by drinking paraquat."
Do not gamble "recovering in a few days" against falling from a height: most people admitted to the trauma ICU survive, but the price is measured in years
B

At a hospital in Xinjiang, only 5.5% of people who fell from a height and were admitted to the trauma ICU died, but they were severely injured and required long-term treatment. Nearly half were injured in three or more body regions simultaneously, more than one-third required mechanical ventilation, and the longest ICU stay was 132 days. Half of the falls were from heights of no more than 3 meters. Less than six out of ten severely injured people were able to return to work later.
Free of charge. You just need to calculate this trade-off clearly beforehand.

A trauma ICU (intensive care unit) in southern Xinjiang compiled statistics. From April 2020 to July 2024, the facility received a total of 289 cases of falls from heights. The average age of this group was 40.3. The median fall height was 3 meters, with 26.6% falling from over 5 meters and 11.4% falling from over 10 meters. The median Injury Severity Score (ISS) was 24; the higher this score, the more severe the injury, with 63.3% having an ISS over 20. 47.1% were injured in 3 or more body regions, and 18.3% in 4 or more regions. 36% required mechanical ventilation, with a median ventilation time of 103.5 hours. The median ICU stay was 8 days, ranging from 1 day to 132 days. The in-hospital or 30-day mortality rate was 5.5% (16/289). A trauma center in Germany received 84 polytrauma patients with ISS ≥ 25; polytrauma refers to injuries in multiple regions simultaneously. During the follow-up period, the return-to-work rate was 58%. Age, duration of ICU treatment, and self-rated health were predictive factors. In 2024, the average cost per hospitalization (China) was ⟦9870⟧, a 4.3% decrease from the previous year in constant prices. In the same year, total national health expenditure was ⟦9089550000000⟧, of which personal health spending was ⟦2500750000000⟧, accounting for 27.5%.
Do not trade "losing one kidney is fine" for money: the remaining kidney must do the work of two, and 86% of people who sold a kidney say their health declined
A

In the US, legitimate kidney donors who undergo multiple layers of screening before donating have a rate of 31 per 10.000 people progressing to end-stage renal failure after 15 years. For similar healthy people who did not donate, it is 4 per 10.000. In a group of kidney sellers in India, 6 years later 86% said their health had declined, and three-quarters were still in debt.
Free of charge. You just need to calculate this trade-off clearly beforehand.

The US compared 96.217 living kidney donors with 20.024 similarly healthy non-donors. The latter group was drawn from the US National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES III). The estimated risk of progressing to end-stage renal failure within 15 years post-donation was then examined. For donors, it was 30.8 per 10.000 people, 95% CI 24.3 to 38.5. For healthy non-donors, it was 3.9 per 10.000 people, 95% CI 0.8 to 8.9, P < 0.001. End-stage renal failure is technically termed end-stage renal disease (ESRD); at this stage, one must survive on dialysis or a kidney transplant. The estimated lifetime risk of ESRD: donors 90 per 10.000, unscreened general population 326 per 10.000, healthy non-donors 14 per 10.000. Norway also conducted a comparison. One side consisted of 1.901 kidney donors, median follow-up 15.1 years. The other side was 32.621 control subjects eligible for donation, median follow-up 24.9 years. Kidney donors had an all-cause mortality rate about three-tenths higher (HR = 1.30, 95% CI 1.11 to 1.52). Cardiovascular mortality was about four-tenths higher (HR = 1.40, 1.03 to 1.91). Progression to ESRD was about ten times higher (HR = 11.38, 4.37 to 29.6). The overall ESRD incidence for this donor group was 302 per million people. In the US, another 3.698 kidney donors were studied, of whom 11 developed ESRD, equivalent to 180 cases per million person-years of observation, compared to 268 cases in the general population during the same period. In this group, 255 people returned for follow-up, an average of 12.2 ± 9.2 years after donation. Among them, 85.5% had a kidney filtration function GFR ≥ 60 ml/min/1.73 m²; 60 is the clinical lower limit of normal. 32.1% had hypertension. 12.7% had proteinuria (protein leaking into urine). In Chennai, India, a survey of 305 kidney sellers an average of 6 years after the sale found: 96% sold to pay off debts, receiving an average of 1.070 US dollars. After the nephrectomy, average family income decreased by one-third (P < 0.001), the number of people living below the poverty line increased, and three-quarters were still in debt at the time of the survey. 86% said their health was worse than before the surgery, and 79% would not recommend selling a kidney to others.
Do not pick up, disassemble, or sell metal components of unknown origin; stay away if you see a trefoil warning sign
A

Radioactive rays are invisible to the naked eye, and radiation sources are solid pellets encased in small metal shells, so "looking fine" cannot be used for judgment. The chance of an ordinary person encountering one is extremely low, with fewer than 1 accident per 10.000 radiation sources annually. But once encountered, the consequences are severe: in 1987 in Brazil, someone dismantled a radiotherapy machine from an abandoned clinic, and ultimately 4 people died.
Free of charge. If you see a strange metal cylinder, a lead box, or parts removed from equipment, walk around them; do not pick them up, disassemble them, or put them in your pocket.

Public awareness materials from the National Nuclear Safety Administration (China) state that a radiation source is radioactive material in solid form permanently sealed in a container or having a tight protective coating. Industrial level gauges, flaw detection machines, and gamma knives in hospitals all use this type. Category III radiation sources, if unshielded, can cause permanent damage within a few hours of contact and can be fatal within a few days to weeks. X-rays are invisible to the naked eye, and γ-rays are electromagnetic waves just like them. External radiation protection relies on three things: shortening time, maintaining distance, and having shielding. γ-rays have strong penetration and require thick concrete walls or lead to be blocked. As of 2025, there are approximately 178.000 radiation sources in use and 355.000 radiation-emitting devices (sets) nationwide (China). The annual radiation accident rate for radiation sources remains stable at below 1 accident per 10.000 sources. Classification is as follows: Loss, theft, or loss of control of Category I or II sources is a major radiation accident. Category III is a relatively large radiation accident. Loss or theft of Category IV or V sources, or causing an individual to exceed the annual dose limit, is an ordinary radiation accident. Official domestic case: In June 2020, an iron smelting plant of the Ningxia Steel Group conducted γ-ray flaw detection during a blast furnace pipeline renovation project. A Category II iridium-192 source irradiated three workers. A person surnamed Chen suffered Grade III acute radiation skin damage on the left hand. A person surnamed Liu suffered Grade IV on the left thumb and index finger, and Grade III on the middle, ring, and pinky fingers. A person surnamed Fan suffered Grade I–II on the left hand. The exposure doses for all three far exceeded the national standard dose limits; the two responsible units had their radiation safety licenses revoked and were fined ⟦70000⟧. International case: In 1987 in Goiânia, Brazil, a teletherapy machine from an abandoned clinic was dismantled. The 50.8 TBq cesium-137 source inside was removed, and the sealed capsule containing the source was broken. Approximately 112.000 people were monitored. Among them, 249 people were found to have internal or external radioactive contamination. Of these 249, 129 had moderate to severe contamination, and 50 required close medical monitoring. Ultimately, 4 people died (Domestic / International).
If gambling reaches the point of borrowing money to recoup losses and your mood remains low for a long time, call 12356 first, then hand over your bank cards and payment passwords to family members
B

In Sweden, people who have sought specialist care for gambling have a suicide death rate 15 times higher than people of the same age, and an overall mortality rate 1.8 times higher. A predictable sign of who will commit suicide is depression. Therefore, if gambling reaches the point of borrowing money to recoup losses and your mood remains low for a long time, call 12356 first.

Free of charge. Make one phone call. Hand over bank cards, payment passwords, and loan apps to family members for safekeeping. The difficulty lies in admitting beforehand that you cannot control yourself.

A Swedish national registry study identified 2.099 individuals diagnosed with gambling disorder in specialist care between 2005 and 2016. Gambling disorder is the inability to control gambling to the point that it affects one's life. Compared to Swedes of the same age, this group aged 20 to 74 had an overall mortality rate 1.8 times higher and a suicide death rate 15 times higher (these two figures are Standardized Mortality Ratios, SMR). During the follow-up period, 67 people died, 21 of whom died by suicide. The predictor for suicide death was depression. In 2023, the authors published a correction: suicide was 12.1 times higher for men and 16.1 times higher for women. From May 1, 2025, calling 12356 from anywhere in China will connect to a psychological support hotline, open at least 18 hours a day (Sweden / China).
Men who have sex with men engaging in high-risk sexual behavior: go to an HIV treatment hospital to ask about pre-exposure prophylaxis; taking it on time reduces infection by about seven-tenths
A

Uninfected people take an antiretroviral drug beforehand, called pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP). Those who take it on time have a risk of infection reduced by about seven-tenths. For those who take it sporadically, it has almost no effect. This is a prescription drug; you must be examined at a hospital before it is prescribed, followed by regular follow-up visits.

This is a prescription drug; in most places, you must pay out of pocket, with prices ranging from several hundred to several thousand yuan. Before prescribing, tests for HIV, kidney function, and hepatitis B are required. After that, follow-up visits are required every 3 months. The difficulty is taking it on time every day.

This drug is a combination tablet of emtricitabine and tenofovir. The iPrEx trial gave 2.499 men who have sex with men and transgender women either the daily pill or a placebo. The group taking the drug had 44% fewer infections (95% CI 15 to 63). For those with detectable drug levels in their blood, the protective effect was much stronger. The PROUD trial in the UK involved 544 men who have sex with men. The group taking the drug immediately had 86% fewer infections than the group that deferred for one year (90% CI 64 to 96). The IPERGAY trial in France used on-demand dosing, before and after sex, and had 86% fewer infections (95% CI 40 to 98). A meta-analysis used by the World Health Organization aggregated the trials. Overall RR = 0.49 (0.33 to 0.73, about 51% lower). In trials with adherence rates over seven-tenths, RR = 0.30 (0.21 to 0.45, about 70% lower). In trials with adherence rates below four-tenths, RR = 0.95, showing almost no effect. In August 2020, the National Medical Products Administration (China) approved this drug for pre-exposure prophylaxis. Adults and adolescents weighing at least 35 kg are eligible for use (Multiple countries / China).
Women over 65 should have their bone density measured once using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry; postmenopausal women with osteoporosis risk factors do not need to wait until 65
A

Women over 65, and postmenopausal women with osteoporosis risk factors, should have their bone density measured once. Assessing risk first and then providing medication to those at high risk reduces hip fractures by about 17%. This translates to about 5 fewer hip fractures for every 1.000 people screened. No change in overall mortality was observed.

Go to a hospital to have bone density measured once using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (abbreviated as DXA), measuring the lumbar spine and hip; it takes a few minutes lying down. Out-of-pocket costs are usually one to two hundred yuan, with prices varying by location. The type of heel ultrasound where you place your foot in a device, often included in health check-up packages, is only for preliminary screening and cannot be used for diagnosis.

The 2025 recommendation from the US Preventive Services Task Force is: women aged 65 and older should be screened for osteoporosis (Grade B recommendation). Postmenopausal women younger than 65 who are found to be at increased risk of fracture upon assessment are also recommended for screening (Grade B). For men, evidence is insufficient to make a recommendation. The evidence review for this recommendation included 3 randomized trials involving 42.009 older women in Europe. The screening method involved assessing fracture risk first, measuring bone density for those at high risk, and providing medication if the risk was indeed high. The screening group had about 17% fewer hip fractures. The original RR = 0.83, 95% CI 0.73 to 0.93. In absolute numbers, this is 5 fewer hip fractures per 1.000 people screened. Among these, the SCOOP trial in the UK included 12.483 women aged 70 to 85; the screening group had about 28% fewer hip fractures (HR = 0.72, 95% CI 0.59 to 0.89), with no difference in mortality rates. The 2017 clinical practice guidelines from the Chinese Medical Association recommend: women over 65 and men over 70 should have their bone density measured. Those younger than these ages who have one or more osteoporosis risk factors should also be measured. In a 2017–2018 national survey, the prevalence of osteoporosis among women over 40 was 20.6%, and for men, it was 5.0% (China).

If osteoporosis is detected, or if you have ever fractured a bone from a minor fall, ask a doctor to prescribe anti-osteoporosis medication and use it consistently; do not substitute it with calcium supplements
A

Postmenopausal women diagnosed with osteoporosis or who have previously suffered a fracture have about a 50% reduction in hip fractures when taking alendronate. Symptomatic vertebral fractures are reduced by more than half. Elderly people who begin annual infusions after hip fracture surgery see a reduction in subsequent fractures of about thirty-five percent over two years. Calcium supplements alone cannot replace these medications.

Requires a prescription and several years of continuous use. Commonly used types include a weekly oral pill or an annual infusion. When starting the medication, bone density is measured annually; once stable, it is measured every 1 to 2 years. The difficulty is continuing regular use even when no symptoms are felt.

Fragility fractures are fractures occurring from minor trauma or during daily activities. The 2017 guidelines from the Chinese Medical Association identify three groups requiring medication. First, those who have suffered a fragility fracture of the spine or hip. Second, those with a bone density T-score of −2.5 or lower, regardless of prior fractures. Third, those with low bone mass who have suffered a fragility fracture of the wrist, upper arm, or pelvis, or who are calculated to be at high risk of fracture. The guidelines explicitly state: "there is currently insufficient evidence that calcium supplementation alone can replace treatment with other anti-osteoporosis drugs." In 2025, Cochrane updated its review of alendronate. In postmenopausal women with osteoporosis or prior fractures, the group taking the drug had about 51% fewer hip fractures. Original RR = 0.49, 95% CI 0.25 to 0.96. Symptomatic vertebral fractures were about 55% fewer (RR = 0.45, 95% CI 0.28 to 0.73). The HORIZON trial included 2.127 people who had undergone hip fracture surgery, average age 74.5. Within 90 days post-surgery, they began annual zoledronic acid infusions, with a median follow-up of 1.9 years. New fractures decreased from 13.9% to 8.6%, about 35% fewer. Mortality decreased from 13.3% to 9.6%, about 28% fewer. The guidelines state: within one year after a hip fracture, about 20% of people die from various complications. In a 2017–2018 national survey, only 1.4% of women diagnosed with osteoporosis or prior fractures were taking medication, and only 0.3% of men (China).
Before stepping onto outdoor ice, drill a hole to measure the thickness; if it is less than 15 cm, do not go on; stay away from ice on rivers and around ice fishing holes
C

The official domestic (China) recommendation is that ice must be 15 cm thick for adults to skate on. The minimum in the US and Canada is 10 cm, and this only applies to new clear ice. White ice is only half as strong, so the thickness must be doubled. On the same ice surface, one spot might be one Chinese foot thick (about 33 cm), while a few steps away it might only be one or two Chinese inches (about 3–7 cm), so you must measure as you go.

The easiest way is to go to a formal skating rink with a manager, which costs no extra money. If you must go on outdoor ice, bring an ice drill or an ice chisel to drill holes and measure thickness. Buy an additional pair of ice safety picks—two spikes with handles worn on the chest. This totals from a few dozen to one or two hundred yuan. Measuring every once in a while as you walk takes a bit more time.

Educational materials from the China Meteorological Administration state that adults can skate when ice is 15 cm thick. Outdoor skating rinks must also have 15 cm of ice to open. The Beijing Water Authority says formal natural skating rinks must have 15 cm of ice, and then the temperature must stay between −8 °C and 1 °C for a week without strong winds before opening. Wild ice often has holes drilled by fishermen, which are difficult to freeze solid again. The Minnesota Department of Natural Resources (USA) guidelines apply only to new clear ice: do not go out if it is under 4 inches (about 10 cm); 4 inches is okay for walking and ice fishing. White ice formed by melting and refreezing snow is only about half as strong as clear ice, so the thickness must be doubled. On the same body of water, ice can be a foot thick in one spot and only an inch or two a few feet away. Ice over moving water is often dangerous, especially near springs, bridges, and culverts. Ice near the shore can also be thinner than further out. The walking, ice fishing, and skating threshold provided by the US National Weather Service is also 4 inches. The Canadian Centre for Occupational Health and Safety cites recommendations from the Canadian Red Cross. For a few people skating or walking, 15 cm is needed; for a large group skating, 20 cm is required. These are all safety guidelines; there are no studies calculating exactly how many deaths are prevented by following them (China / USA, Canada)
Install all protective guards, wear safety goggles with a face shield before using an angle grinder, hold it firmly with both hands, and never install a wood saw blade to cut wood
C

Angle grinders rotate extremely fast; a broken disc will fly out and cause injury; installing a wood saw blade can also cause the machine to kick back unexpectedly. Two domestic (China) accidents both involved installing saw blades without protective guards: one person severed a femoral artery and another tore a carotid artery; neither could be saved. Protective guards, safety goggles with face shields, and holding with both hands cost very little.

One pair of safety goggles plus a face shield costs a few dozen yuan. Checking the guard and disc before each startup and unplugging before changing discs takes an extra minute or two. The difficulty is not removing the guard even when it feels inconvenient and not operating with one hand.

Procedures listed by the Canadian Centre for Occupational Health and Safety and the Queensland (Australia) safety authority are as follows. Check the guard and disc before starting; do not use if the disc has cracks, chips, or deformation. The maximum speed marked on the disc must not be lower than the speed marked on the machine, and the diameter and center hole must also match the machine. Disconnect power before changing discs. Secure the workpiece before grinding or cutting. Wear safety goggles or glasses, plus a face shield on the outside. Use both hands on the handles and stand firmly. Do not use a cutting disc for grinding, as this makes the disc more likely to break. Do not put the machine down until the disc has completely stopped. Direct sparks and debris away from people and keep flammable items away. The Queensland notice states the design speed at the edge of a cutting disc is about 70 meters per second. Installing a large 356 mm disc on a 230 mm machine increases the edge speed to at least 120 meters per second, making the disc prone to breaking. In February 2016, a worker there was hit in the chest by a fragment from a 230 mm angle grinder and died of internal injuries. There are two accident investigation reports in China. In 2019 in Harbin, a worker replaced a cutting disc with a toothed saw blade, did not install a guard, and went to cut wooden boards. The saw blade caught his trouser leg, severed his femoral artery, and he died of blood loss. In 2024 in Futian, Shenzhen, a worker used an angle grinder with a wood saw blade, without a guard or auxiliary handle, to cut a wooden door frame. The machine kicked back, slashed his carotid artery, and he died. The national standard cited in the report states: "do not install saw chains, wood carving blades, or toothed saw blades." In emergency department injury monitoring data from South Korea between 2011 and 2018, there were 8,697 injuries from high-speed rotating cutting tools, of which 4,603 occurred while using tools like grinders. Injuries to the hand accounted for 46.4% and to the head 23.0%. Compared to other similar tools, grinders are about twice as likely to cause severe injury (OR = 2.07, 95% CI 1.88 to 2.29). A hospital in Mianyang, Sichuan, admitted 36 inpatients with eye injuries from angle grinders over two years. After surgery, even with glasses, 10 people had a best-corrected vision below 0.05. At a hospital in Turkey, out of 742 acute hand and forearm injuries in one year, angle grinders caused 82 cases. Except for 8 cases, all were injured while not at work; 44% were retirees. At a trauma center in Japan, among 15 people injured by angle grinders from 2017 to 2018, 9 used the wrong setup by installing saw blades to cut wood. Among them, 2 suffered complete finger amputations and 1 lost a finger joint (Canada, Australia / China / South Korea, Turkey, Japan)
Directly ask someone who is emotionally struggling, "Have you ever thought about suicide?"; asking this does not make them think about it more
B

The fear that "mentioning suicide suggests the idea" is not found in research. Adding questions about suicide to questionnaires for high school students did not make respondents more distressed, nor did the number of people wanting to commit suicide increase. Students who already had depressive symptoms felt less distressed after being asked, and those who had previously attempted suicide had fewer suicidal thoughts.
Costs no money. Ask one question, then spend some time listening to the person speak. The difficulty is starting the conversation; many people fear that asking will plant the idea.

2,342 students in 6 high schools in New York State were randomly assigned by class into two groups. One group's questionnaire included questions about suicide; the other's did not. Immediately after completing the questionnaire and 2 days later, distress levels did not differ between the two groups (P = 0.66 and P = 0.41; P greater than 0.05 means no difference found). 2 days later, the rate of reporting suicidal ideation was 4.7% in the group that was asked and 3.9% in the group that was not, showing no difference (P = 0.49). Students with pre-existing depressive symptoms felt less distressed after being asked (P = 0.01). Students who had previously attempted suicide had fewer suicidal thoughts after being asked (P = 0.02). In 2022, a meta-analysis evaluated 17 studies, pooling 8 studies that compared "asking" with "not asking." After asking, suicidal ideation and behavior (both immediate and subsequent), non-suicidal self-injury, and psychological distress did not increase significantly. The strongest evidence comes from 8 randomized controlled trials with low or unclear risk of bias. Another literature review in 2014 also stated: no study found that suicidal ideation increased significantly after asking

If you have palpitations or an irregular heartbeat, get an ECG; if atrial fibrillation is detected, ask a doctor to evaluate using anticoagulants to prevent stroke, and do not use aspirin as a substitute
A

Atrial fibrillation is an irregular heartbeat where blood pools in the heart and easily clots; if it travels to the brain, it causes a stroke. Taking anticoagulants as evaluated by a doctor reduces stroke by about six-tenths and death by about three-tenths. Drugs like aspirin only reduce it by about two-tenths and cannot be a substitute. In a 2014–2016 survey, only 6% of high-risk atrial fibrillation patients in China were taking anticoagulants.

An ECG costs a few dozen yuan. Warfarin is very cheap but requires regular blood tests to adjust the dose. New generation anticoagulants do not require frequent blood tests but are slightly more expensive. The difficulty is having to take it every day even without symptoms, and informing doctors before tooth extractions or surgery that you are on anticoagulants.

In atrial fibrillation, the atria quiver irregularly, blood pools in the atria, and clots easily form. A blood clot traveling to the brain's blood vessels causes a stroke. The most common symptoms are palpitations, fatigue after minor activity, and chest discomfort; however, about 25% of people report having no symptoms. A single-lead ECG of 30 seconds or more, or a standard 12-lead ECG of 10 seconds or more, can provide a diagnosis. In 2007, a meta-analysis pooled 29 randomized trials involving 28,044 people. Compared to no medication, properly dosed warfarin reduced stroke by about six-tenths (64% reduction, CI 49% to 74%). Antiplatelet drugs like aspirin only reduced it by about two-tenths (22% reduction, CI 6% to 35%). In direct comparison, warfarin reduced risk by an additional 39% compared to antiplatelet drugs. The absolute annual increase in major extracranial bleeding was no more than 0.3%. A Cochrane review focusing on 2,313 people who had never had a stroke found warfarin reduced mortality by about three-tenths (OR = 0.69, 95% CI 0.50 to 0.94). 4 large trials totaling 71,683 people compared new oral anticoagulants (NOACs) with warfarin. The new drugs further reduced stroke and systemic embolism by 19% (RR = 0.81) and mortality by 10% (RR = 0.90). Intracranial hemorrhage was reduced by 52% (RR = 0.48), but gastrointestinal bleeding increased by 25% (RR = 1.25). Aspirin cannot replace anticoagulants. In 5,599 people unsuitable for warfarin, apixaban compared to aspirin reduced stroke and systemic embolism by 55% (HR = 0.45). Major bleeding was 1.4% per year versus 1.2%, showing no significant difference (HR = 1.13, CI 0.74 to 1.75). Another trial enrolled 973 people over age 75. Combining fatal or disabling stroke, intracranial hemorrhage, and arterial embolism, warfarin was 52% lower than aspirin (RR = 0.48). Extracranial bleeding was 1.4% per year versus 1.6%. The 2023 Chinese atrial fibrillation guidelines use the CHA2DS2VASc-60 score. Heart failure, hypertension, diabetes, vascular disease, age 60 to 64, and female sex each count for 1 point; age 65 or older and previous stroke each count for 2 points. Men with 2 or more points and women with 3 or more points are recommended to take oral anticoagulants. For men with 1 point and women with 2 points, it is considered after weighing bleeding risk and patient preference. The guidelines do not recommend antiplatelet drugs for stroke prevention in atrial fibrillation. The 2023 US guidelines state clearly: the decision to medicate is based on stroke risk, regardless of whether the atrial fibrillation is paroxysmal or persistent. These guidelines also state: bleeding risk scores should not be used alone to decide against medication, but rather to identify modifiable bleeding factors. A survey of people over 45 in China in 2014–2016 found atrial fibrillation prevalence at 1.8%, about 7.9 million people. The awareness rate was 78.3% in cities but only 35.3% in rural areas. Among high-risk atrial fibrillation patients, only 6.0% were using anticoagulants. In a 2020–2021 national survey, 43.8% of detected atrial fibrillation cases were newly diagnosed. Among those previously diagnosed, 32.1% were using anticoagulants, but only 19.8% in rural areas.
Adults should get a hepatitis C antibody test once; if positive, follow up with a nucleic acid test; if diagnosed, take medication for 8 to 12 weeks, and the vast majority will be cured
A

Hepatitis C infection can be asymptomatic for decades; a single antibody test, followed by a nucleic acid test if positive, will provide the answer. Once diagnosed, taking medication for 8 to 12 weeks clears the virus in over 95% of cases. People who clear the virus have a subsequent mortality risk about six-tenths lower and liver cancer risk about seven-tenths lower. In 2019, these drugs were included in medical insurance (China), with prices dropping by over 85% on average.

A blood draw for a hepatitis C antibody test usually costs a few dozen yuan out-of-pocket, with prices varying by location. If the antibody is positive, another blood draw for a nucleic acid test is needed to see if the virus is still present. Once diagnosed, go to a designated local hepatitis C treatment hospital for a prescription; most regimens involve 1 pill daily for 8 to 12 weeks, with drug costs covered by medical insurance (China). The difficulty is remembering to get tested when there are no symptoms.

Hepatitis C is transmitted through blood, and there is no vaccine. The World Health Organization states that chronic hepatitis C is often asymptomatic for decades; by the time symptoms appear, the liver is already severely damaged. A positive antibody test only indicates past infection; a nucleic acid test is required to see if the virus is still present. About 30% of infected people do not need treatment and clear the virus spontaneously within 6 months. The World Health Organization says direct-acting antiviral (DAA) oral medications taken for 8 to 12 weeks can cure almost all patients. A evidence review for the US Preventive Services Task Force pooled 49 treatment studies, showing cure rates for all genotypes were over 95%. Cure means the virus is not found in the blood 12 weeks after stopping medication. Serious side effects were 1.9%, and discontinuation due to side effects was 0.4%. The same review pooled follow-up studies without non-randomized control groups. Those cured had an overall mortality rate about 60% lower than those not cured (HR = 0.40, 95% CI 0.28 to 0.56, 13 studies). Liver cancer was about 71% lower (HR = 0.29, 95% CI 0.23 to 0.38, 20 studies). France followed 9,895 chronic hepatitis C patients for a median of 33.4 months. After adjusting for age, liver fibrosis level, alcohol consumption, and other factors, those taking medication had an overall mortality rate about 52% lower (HR = 0.48, 95% CI 0.33 to 0.70). Liver cancer was about 34% lower (HR = 0.66, 95% CI 0.46 to 0.93). Among US veterans, 15,059 hepatitis C patients already in advanced liver disease took these drugs. With a median follow-up of about 1.6 years, 2.6 deaths occurred per 100 person-years among those cured, compared to 12.3 deaths among those not cured. Excluding other factors, the mortality risk was about 74% lower (HR = 0.26, 95% CI 0.22 to 0.31). In 2020, the US Preventive Services Task Force recommended that all adults aged 18 to 79 be tested (Grade B recommendation). For most people, testing once in a lifetime is sufficient. The 2022 Chinese prevention and control guidelines recommend antibody screening for all adults; those with ongoing high risk should be tested periodically; all antibody-positives should undergo nucleic acid testing. In a 2006 national survey, the antibody positivity rate in the 1 to 59 age group was 0.43%. Pooling multiple studies, it was 0.60% in the general population, 48.67% among drug users, and 6.59% among hemodialysis patients. The National Healthcare Security Administration (China) stated that before negotiations, the cost of a hepatitis C treatment course mostly exceeded ⟦50000⟧. Three hepatitis C drugs negotiated into medical insurance in 2019 saw an average price reduction of over 85% (USA, France / China)

Before entering manure pits, manholes, sewage tanks, vegetable cellars, underground vaults, fermentation tanks, and other confined spaces: ventilate first, measure gas levels, ensure protection and a supervisor are present; do not enter if conditions are not met. If someone collapses inside, do not follow them down; call 119 and 120
C
