Cardiovascular events were about 26% lower (HR = 0.74, 0.59 to 0.92). Severe microvascular complications in the eyes, kidneys, and nerves were about 35% lower (HR = 0.65, 0.45 to 0.95). Cardiovascular mortality was about 33% lower (HR = 0.67, 0.48 to 0.94). Overall mortality was about 26% lower (HR = 0.74, 0.61 to 0.89). They lived an average of 1.44 years longer (0.20 to 2.68). The US DPP trial randomized 3,234 people with slightly high blood sugar. The lifestyle group's goal was at least 7% weight loss and 150 minutes of weekly exercise. At a mean follow-up of 2.8 years, the lifestyle group had a 58% lower risk of diabetes than the placebo group (95% CI 48% to 66%). The metformin group was 31% lower (17% to 43%), performing worse than lifestyle changes. At a mean follow-up of 15 years, the lifestyle group was still 27% lower (HR = 0.73, 0.65 to 0.83), though the gap narrowed over time. At a median follow-up of 21 years, overall mortality in the lifestyle group did not differ from the placebo group (HR = 1.02, 0.81 to 1.28). Cardiovascular mortality also did not differ (HR = 1.18, 0.77 to 1.81). The Finnish DPS trial randomized 522 overweight people with impaired glucose tolerance. Cumulative diabetes incidence after 4 years: intervention group 11%, control group 23%. During the trial, the risk was 58% lower. After stopping one-on-one counseling, at a median of 7 years, it was still 43% lower. At a mean follow-up of 10.6 years, overall mortality showed no significant difference (HR = 0.57, 0.21 to 1.58). Cardiovascular disease also showed no difference (HR = 1.04, 0.72 to 1.51). The Healthy China Action Program (China) defines pre-diabetes as fasting blood sugar from 6.1 to less than 7.0 mmol/L. A 2-hour post-load blood sugar from 7.8 to less than 11.1 mmol/L also counts. The program advises overweight or obese individuals to lower their BMI to or near 24, or lose at least 7% of their weight. Daily total energy intake should be reduced by at least 400 to 500 kcal, with at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity exercise per week. Check fasting blood sugar or 2-hour post-meal blood sugar every six months.
If peanuts, corn, nuts, rice, or flour in your home become moldy, discard the entire package; do not pick out the moldy parts and eat the rest; if you bite into a bitter nut, spit it out immediately
B

Moldy peanuts and corn produce aflatoxin, which causes liver cancer. In a Shanghai study, people with this toxin in their urine had about 3.4 times the risk of liver cancer compared to those without. Hepatitis B carriers with the toxin had about 59.4 times the risk of those with neither. This toxin is very difficult to destroy by roasting, boiling, or frying.

Discarding a package of peanuts, nuts, or a bag of rice or flour costs from a few yuan to dozens of yuan. Normally, store grains and nuts in a dry, ventilated, cool place; buy small packages and avoid stockpiling. The difficulty lies in the reluctance to waste food, especially when persuading elderly family members.

Aflatoxin is classified as Group 1 (carcinogenic to humans) by the International Agency for Research on Cancer, specifically causing liver cancer. It is most commonly found in peanuts and corn; standard cooking methods like roasting, boiling, and frying are very difficult to destroy it. A Shanghai study starting in 1986 followed 18,244 middle-aged men, each providing a urine sample at enrollment. Over approximately 70,000 person-years of follow-up, 55 cases of liver cancer were identified. 50 of these cases were compared to 267 controls from the same cohort. People with aflatoxin in their urine had about a 3.4-fold risk of liver cancer (RR = 3.4, 95% CI 1.1 to 10.0). Those positive for Hepatitis B surface antigen had about a 7.3-fold risk (2.2 to 24.4). Those with both had about a 59.4-fold risk (16.6 to 212.0) compared to those with neither. In an early analysis of the same cohort, after adjusting for Hepatitis B, smoking, alcohol, and education, those with the toxin had about a 3.8-fold risk (1.2 to 12.2). Qidong, Jiangsu was previously a high-incidence area for liver cancer; since the 1980s, the staple grain there changed from corn to rice. Median blood toxin biomarkers in residents dropped from 19.3 pg/mg in 1989 to undetectable levels in 2009 (below 0.5). Liver cancer mortality in residents under age 35 dropped by more than half across birth cohorts from the 1960s to the 1980s. These cohorts were born before newborn Hepatitis B vaccination became widespread. The authors estimated that about 65% of the reduction in liver cancer mortality could be attributed to lower toxin intake, with 83% of that benefit occurring in Hepatitis B-infected individuals. Global estimates suggest that Hepatitis B carriers who ingest the same amount of toxin are about 30 times more likely to develop cancer than non-carriers. Every year in China, a number of liver cancer cases can be attributed to this toxin. This includes approximately 5,300 to 14,400 cases in Hepatitis B carriers and about 1,990 to 4,430 cases in non-carriers.

Do not eat raw fish salad, raw fish, raw fish congee, or "drunken shrimp" made from freshwater fish or shrimp; frequent eaters should go to a hospital for a liver fluke test and take praziquantel as prescribed if positive
B

Eating raw freshwater fish or shrimp leads to infection with Clonorchis sinensis (small liver fluke). This parasite is a confirmed carcinogen; infected individuals are about four to five times more likely to develop cholangiocarcinoma (bile duct cancer) than those uninfected. Vinegar, alcohol, and mustard cannot effectively kill it. Once infected, taking medication for two days cures over nine-tenths of cases.

Not eating raw fish costs nothing; the difficulty lies in giving up a long-standing culinary preference and declining it at social gatherings. Frequent eaters should go to a hospital for a fecal egg count test; costs vary by location. If flukes are found, take praziquantel according to the doctor's dosage, usually for 1 to 2 days.

Clonorchis sinensis is commonly known as the small liver fluke. The International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC), under the World Health Organization, met in 2009 and evaluated that chronic infection with this fluke causes cancer in humans. It causes cholangiocarcinoma and is classified as Group 1. The 1994 evaluation only classified it as Group 2A (probably carcinogenic). Pooling published studies, people infected with liver flukes have about a 4.8-fold risk of cholangiocarcinoma. The original text states a relative risk of 4.8 (95% CI 2.8 to 8.4). This figure includes another type of liver fluke found in Southeast Asia. In the same paper, Hepatitis B was 2.6-fold, Hepatitis C was 1.8-fold, making liver fluke the strongest factor. Another paper pooled 36 studies. In case-control studies, cholangiocarcinoma was about 4.37-fold (OR = 4.37, 2.84 to 6.72). In follow-up studies, it was about 10.43-fold (RR = 10.43, 2.90 to 37.47). Cholangitis and cholecystitis were about 7.80-fold (RR = 7.80). Gallstones were about 2.42-fold (RR = 2.42). Hepatocellular carcinoma was about 4.69-fold (OR = 4.69). Liver cirrhosis showed no statistically significant association. The heavier the infection, the higher the incidence of these diseases. A national survey (China) from 2014 to 2015 found an infection rate of 0.47%, roughly 6 million people. Four provinces with infection rates over 1% were Guangdong, Guangxi, Heilongjiang, and Jilin. Extrapolating from monitoring data from 2016 to 2021, the national rate in 2020 was about 0.67%, roughly 9.46 million people. Among them, Guangxi was about 8.92% and Guangdong about 2.99%. In 2024, 15 agencies, including the National Disease Control and Prevention Administration (China), jointly issued a prevention plan. The plan used the average infection rate at monitoring points from 2018 to 2022 as a baseline: Guangxi 8.75%, Jilin 4.38%, Heilongjiang 3.16%, Guangdong 2.95%. In 2026, the National Center for Food Safety Risk Assessment (China) warned: seasonings like alcohol, vinegar, and mustard do not effectively kill liver flukes. Freezing must be below -20℃ for at least 7 consecutive days. Heating must bring the core temperature of the food to above 70℃ for over 10 minutes. The IARC also clearly states that salted or smoked freshwater fish can still transmit the parasite. Regarding treatment, a 2022 meta-analysis of 26 trials involving 3,340 people found that the WHO-recommended praziquantel regimen is 25 mg per kg of body weight, 3 times a day for 2 days. The predicted cure rate for Clonorchis sinensis is 98.5% (85.4% to 99.9%).
Turn off unnecessary notifications and keep your phone out of sight while working
B

When a phone pings, even if you do not look at or touch it, concentration test scores drop. The drop is equivalent to when you actually answer a call or send a text. There is another case: even if the phone is just sitting on the table and you resist looking at it, your mind still has less free capacity. The more someone is inseparable from their phone, the more their performance drops.
Costs nothing. Takes a few minutes to adjust settings and requires almost no willpower.

Simply receiving a notification, without looking at or touching it, significantly impairs concentration test results. The impairment is equivalent to actually making a call or texting. This was a laboratory experiment with university students. Two other experiments showed that even if one resists looking at the phone, its mere presence nearby reduces the brain's available processing capacity. Those most dependent on their phones saw the greatest reduction.
Wake up at a fixed time, even on weekends
B

The one-fifth of people with the most irregular schedules have a biological clock about 2.5 hours later than the one-fifth with the most regular schedules. It is like living in a permanent state of jet lag. Students with more regular schedules perform better academically.
Costs nothing. Requires giving up sleeping in on weekends, which takes a little willpower.

61 students recorded their schedules for 30 days. The one-fifth with the most irregular schedules had a biological clock (circadian rhythm) about 2.5 hours later than the one-fifth with the most regular schedules. Specifically, the time the body began secreting melatonin was 00:08 compared to 21:32. The sleepiest period was also about 1.8 hours later. More regular schedules correlated with better academic performance (correlation coefficient r = 0.37).
Get 7 to 8 hours of sleep every night; do not consider 6 hours to be enough
A

After two weeks of sleeping only 6 hours a night, mental performance drops to the level of staying awake for two consecutive days and nights. The difficulty is that you do not realize it yourself. Self-rated sleepiness only increases for the first few days and then plateaus; people sleeping 6 hours and those sleeping 4 hours rate their sleepiness the same. Therefore, the feeling that "6 hours is enough for me" cannot be trusted.
Costs nothing. Requires dedicating an extra 1 to 2 hours a day to sleep. Going to bed earlier takes a little willpower.

48 healthy adults aged 21 to 38 slept only 6 hours a night for 14 consecutive days. Their cognitive performance declined cumulatively to a level equivalent to 2 nights of total sleep deprivation. Meanwhile, self-rated sleepiness only increased during the first few days, then leveled off. The 6-hour group and 4-hour group did not differ in self-assessed sleepiness. This was a randomized controlled trial (RCT). Additionally, short-term sleep deprivation (acute, not exceeding 48 hours) has an effect size on lapses in simple attention tasks of g = -0.776, and on reasoning accuracy of g = -0.125. This part is based on a meta-analysis of 70 studies.
Do not consume caffeine after 2 PM
A

Consuming 400 mg of caffeine 6 hours before bed—about three to four cups of coffee—results in over 1 hour less sleep according to monitors. Yet, self-recorded sleep diaries showed no perceived difference. A 250 mL cup of coffee (107 mg) must be finished more than 8.8 hours before bedtime to avoid affecting sleep. For someone going to bed at 11 PM, 2 PM is the cutoff.
Costs nothing. Those used to afternoon coffee must abstain, which takes a little willpower.

Taking a pill containing 400 mg of caffeine 6 hours before bed resulted in 1.1 to 1.2 hours less total sleep time measured by machines compared to a placebo pill. Based on a 250 mL cup of coffee containing 107 mg, 400 mg is roughly three to four cups. The placebo pill looked identical but contained no caffeine. However, participants' self-recorded sleep diaries showed no difference; they did not realize it themselves. A meta-analysis of multiple studies found that caffeine reduces total sleep time by an average of 45 minutes. The percentage of time actually spent sleeping while in bed (sleep efficiency) decreased by 7%. A 250 mL cup of coffee (107 mg) must be finished more than 8.8 hours before bedtime to avoid affecting sleep.
Batch your emails and messages; process them in a few fixed sessions each day
B

The same group of people was compared over two weeks. During the week limited to checking email only 3 times a day, daily stress was significantly lower, even though the number of emails sent and received remained the same. When unrestricted, people checked their email an average of 15.5 times a day.
Costs nothing. Takes a little time to clarify with colleagues how often you respond. Resisting the urge to check email constantly takes a little willpower.

124 adults were compared before and after in a two-week self-controlled study. The week limited to checking email 3 times a day showed significantly lower daily stress compared to the unrestricted week (effect size Cohen's d = 0.37). The number of emails received and answered did not differ between the two weeks. Initially, when unrestricted, people checked their email an average of 15.5 times per day.
Maintain continuous focus while working; block interruptions even if they only last a few seconds
B

An interruption averaging 2.8 seconds has been shown to double the likelihood of making an error on the next step. An interruption of 4.4 seconds triples it. Real-world tracking also shows that once a task is interrupted, it takes an average of 25 minutes to return to it, with two other tasks often intervening. Interrupted workers tend to work faster, but experience higher levels of stress, frustration, and effort.
Free. Close the door, wear headphones, or hang a "Do Not Disturb" sign.

An interruption averaging 2.8 seconds doubles the error rate in sequential tasks. An interruption of 4.4 seconds triples it. This was a laboratory experiment. Another study observed 24 information workers on-site. On average, they switched to a different work topic every 11 minutes. 57% of work topics were interrupted. To return to an interrupted task during the day, it took an average of 25 minutes 26 seconds. An average of 2.26 other tasks intervened. Additionally, an experiment with 48 people found that interrupted workers worked faster but reported higher stress, frustration, time pressure, and effort.
Do only one thing at a time; do not answer messages while in a meeting
B

Every time you switch tasks, your reaction time slows down and you become more prone to errors. Frequent heavy multitaskers do not actually train their ability to multitask; on the contrary, they perform worse on task-switching tests.
Free. Refraining from answering messages during meetings requires a bit of willpower.

After switching tasks, reaction times are significantly slower and errors are more likely. This part is taken from a meta-analysis of multiple studies. Another laboratory study involving college students found that heavy media multitaskers were more easily distracted by irrelevant stimuli and irrelevant memories. They also performed worse on task-switching tests.
Avoid glowing screens for one hour before sleep; if you want to read, use paper books or an E-ink reader with the light off
B

Reading on a glowing screen before bed results in falling asleep about 10 minutes later than reading a paper book. Melatonin is suppressed by 55%. The next day, the biological clock is delayed by more than 1.5 hours, leading to increased morning sleepiness and longer wake-up times.
Free. Putting down the phone an hour before bed requires resisting a long-term habit and takes willpower.

In a laboratory setting, the same group of people underwent both conditions (cross-over trial). One condition involved reading an e-book on an iPad at maximum brightness for about 4 hours for 5 consecutive nights. The other condition involved reading a paper book in the same dimly lit room. Reading a glowing e-book before bed resulted in falling asleep about 10 minutes slower than reading a paper book (25.7 minutes vs. 15.8 minutes). Evening melatonin was suppressed by 55%. The biological clock (circadian rhythm) the next day was delayed by more than 1.5 hours, with the onset of melatonin secretion at 22:31 compared to 21:01. The following morning, participants felt sleepier and took longer to fully wake up.
Go to bed on time; do not stay up late for games, short videos, or pornographic content
B

In 2025, Chinese people slept an average of 6.97 hours per night, falling asleep at 0:10 on average. Among children and adolescents, those who use phones or tablets before bed are twice as likely to have insufficient sleep and 2.7 times more likely to experience daytime sleepiness. Even if devices are just kept in the bedroom without being used, the figures are nearly the same. Therefore, the easiest way is to not bring the phone into the bedroom.
Free. The difficulty lies in resisting the long-term habit of "watching just one more episode." Not bringing the phone into the bedroom is the most effortless approach.

In 2025, Chinese citizens slept an average of 6.97 hours per night, with an average bedtime of 0:10 (Chinese Sleep Research Society). Those who use handheld devices before bed are approximately 2.17 times more likely to have insufficient sleep (OR = 2.17). Poor sleep quality is approximately 1.46 times more likely (OR = 1.46). Daytime sleepiness is approximately 2.72 times more likely (OR = 2.72). Even when devices are just present in the bedroom but not used, the figures are similar, at approximately 1.79, 1.53, and 2.27 times (OR = 1.79/1.53/2.27). This part is calculated from a meta-analysis of 20 cross-sectional surveys involving 125,198 children and adolescents. Another cross-sectional survey of 844 adults aged 18 to 94 found that those who still used phones after turning off the lights took longer to fall asleep, had a lower percentage of actual sleep time while in bed, and were more tired during the day.
Do not make major decisions or send important messages late at night
B

When well-rested, people quickly learn to avoid high-risk options. After two consecutive nights without sleep, they repeatedly choose high-risk options, a tendency that becomes more pronounced with age. While the impact of losing just a few hours of sleep hasn't been directly measured to the same extent, important decisions should still be postponed until after waking up.
Free. It is simply a matter of rescheduling the task for after you wake up.

34 healthy individuals performed the Iowa Gambling Task after 49.5 hours of sleep deprivation. This is an experiment measuring decision-making under risk. When well-rested, they quickly learned to avoid high-risk choices. After sleep deprivation, they chose high-risk options more frequently. Older adults were more affected. This was an experiment, and there is only this one study.
If you feel sleepy in the afternoon, take a 10-minute nap, not a 30-minute one
B

When you haven't had enough sleep the night before, a 10-minute nap provides immediate alertness, with some effects lasting up to two and a half hours. A 5-minute nap is almost useless. A 20-minute nap takes 35 minutes for the effects to be felt. With a 30-minute nap, you wake up in a state of grogginess, during which performance is even worse than if you hadn't slept at all.
Free. It takes 10 minutes, plus finding a place to lie down or lean over a desk.

After a night of insufficient sleep, a 10-minute nap immediately improves sleepiness, fatigue, vigor, and cognitive performance, with some benefits lasting more than 155 minutes. A 5-minute nap provides almost no benefit. For a 20-minute nap, benefits only appear 35 minutes later. A 30-minute nap initially causes sleep inertia: performance immediately after waking is worse than before, only improving later.
Use earplugs in open offices, or find a quiet room for tasks requiring memorization
B

An increase in background noise from 39 to 51 decibels leads to fewer words remembered, higher fatigue, and increased reluctance to work. During breaks, watching nature videos with sound helps recovery better than continuing to listen to office noise.
Earplugs cost a few dozen yuan. Booking a quiet meeting room takes a bit of time.

Students were asked to work in a simulated open office. When background noise increased from 39 to 51 decibels (dB, LAeq), they remembered fewer words, self-reported higher fatigue, and were more reluctant to work. During breaks, watching nature videos with sound restored self-reported vigor scores better than listening to just the sound of a running stream or office noise.
Do not keep adding weekly work hours: beyond approximately 49 hours, each additional hour becomes increasingly less productive
B

Data from British munitions factories during WWI show that for up to 49 hours per week, output is proportional to hours worked. Beyond 49 hours, the output from each additional hour decreases. A 70-hour work week produces nearly the same total output as a 56-hour week; those 14 extra hours generate almost no additional production.
You might receive less overtime pay. It may also require the effort of negotiating with a supervisor.

Output data from British munitions workers during WWI: up to 49 hours per week, output was proportional to hours worked. Beyond 49 hours, output growth began to slow. It peaked at around 63 hours. Total output for a 70-hour week was almost no different from a 56-hour week; those 14 extra hours generated almost no additional production.
If you find yourself ruminating on an upsetting matter, switch to a manual task
B

Repeatedly thinking about an upsetting matter (rumination) worsens depression, locks in negative thoughts, makes people poorer at problem-solving, and makes it harder to take actual action. It also exhausts the patience of those around you who were initially willing to listen. When you realize you are stuck in a loop, go do something that requires using your hands.
Free. The difficulty lies first in recognizing that you are ruminating, which requires practice.

A meta-analysis of multiple studies indicates that ruminating on upsetting matters worsens depression. It also reinforces negative thinking and weakens problem-solving abilities. It hinders practical action and exhausts the patience of supportive listeners. It is associated with anxiety, binge eating, alcohol abuse, and self-harm.
Treat thoughts like "things will definitely get worse" as symptoms, not facts
B

In a 20-year follow-up study of twins, each one-level increase in pessimism was associated with a 13% higher risk of death during the same period and a 20% higher risk of death from cardiovascular disease. Conversely, high optimism scores did not provide a corresponding benefit. Therefore, the issue to address is pessimism, not a "lack of positive energy."
Free. The difficulty lies in viewing these thoughts as symptoms rather than facts.

2,978 twins aged 50 and older in Australia were followed for an average of 20 years, during which 1,068 died. For every 1 standard deviation increase in the pessimism scale score, the risk of death during the same period was approximately 13% higher (Hazard Ratio = 1.134). The 95% Confidence Interval for this figure was 1.065 to 1.207, P = 8.85×10⁻⁵. Cardiovascular mortality was approximately 20% higher (1.196, from 1.045 to 1.368, P = 0.0093). There was no association with cancer mortality. Optimism scores also showed no significant association with mortality rates.
Reduce relationships that drain you, learn to refuse tasks you do not want to accept
C
In a survey of widows aged 60 to 89, unpleasant contacts were more strongly and consistently related to well-being than pleasant contacts. Therefore, subtract first, then add.
Zero cost. In the short term, there will be friction in communication, and some relationships may be lost. Saying no requires a fair amount of willpower.

A survey of 120 widows aged 60 to 89: unpleasant contacts were more consistently and strongly related to mental well-being than pleasant contacts. According to these results, the damage caused by a person who drains you is greater than the benefit provided by a person who supports you.
If you are angry, leave first; view the other person as the weather rather than the enemy
B

Looking at what just happened from a different perspective, or putting yourself in the other person's shoes, both calm emotions, with the latter being more effective. Simply not showing your emotions outwardly also has some effect. However, trying to suppress feelings inside or trying not to think about it is useless. People who punished those who offended them ruminated on the matter longer, while those who did not retaliate moved on faster.
Zero cost. At that moment, you must refrain from arguing back and turn away, then decide whether to handle it later. This requires a bit of practice.

A meta-analysis of 306 experimental comparisons: explaining what happened from a different perspective (cognitive reappraisal) had an effect size on emotion of d = 0.36. Putting oneself in the other person's shoes: d = 0.45. Distraction: d = 0.27. Suppressing the outward expression of emotion (not showing it) was effective, d = 0.32. Trying to suppress feelings was useless (d = -0.04), and trying not to think about it was also useless (d = -0.12). These figures combine internal feelings, outward expressions, and bodily responses; the summary does not separate them. Three other experiments showed: people who punished their offenders ruminated on them longer; those who did not punish "let it go" faster. Previously, people overestimated the sense of satisfaction that retaliation would bring.
When your mood is down, do the most worthwhile things first: exercise, get more sunlight, sleep on time, find someone to talk to, call 12356
A

Brisk walking, jogging, yoga, and strength training all reduce depression; higher intensity is more effective, see Chapter 22 Section 6 (walk or run when in a bad mood) for details. Light therapy is very effective for seasonal depression and also works for non-seasonal depression. Online cognitive behavioral therapy self-help courses are effective; if symptoms are more severe, having a guide is better. If having suicidal thoughts, call 12356 first.
Zero cost, or very little. Brisk walk, jog, or strength train a few times a week. Go outside for sunlight during the day. Keep a fixed schedule. Make a phone call when having suicidal thoughts.

A network meta-analysis of 218 randomized controlled trials involving 14,170 people. The control group consisted of people doing other activities. Compared to them, walking or jogging had an effect size on depression of g = -0.62 (95% CI -0.80 to -0.45). Yoga -0.55, strength training -0.49. Higher intensity led to better effectiveness. A meta-analysis of multiple light therapy studies: for seasonal depression, the effect size was 0.84 (0.60 to 1.08), for non-seasonal depression it was 0.53 (0.18 to 0.89). There is also an individual patient data meta-analysis of internet-delivered cognitive behavioral therapy (online self-help courses). Whether guided or unguided, they were better than control groups. At moderate to severe levels (PHQ-9 score above 9), the guided type was better. 12356 is the national psychological support hotline (China), open no less than 18 hours a day.
View police, doctors, and counter staff as employees following regulations, not as characters: what moves things forward is paperwork and deadlines, not emotions
C

Police, doctors, and counter staff are all people working according to the regulations of their positions, governed by paperwork, deadlines, and management supervision. How many days a task must be completed in, and what documents are required if it cannot be done, are all written in the regulations. Therefore, get a receipt, record the deadline, and complain through the right channels; do not expect to reason with them until they agree with you.
Zero cost. What changes are your expectations and the order of your actions. For the first time, you must resist the urge to "reason until they agree with you."

Changing the way of working with authorities: from "begging, getting angry, repeatedly telling grievances" to "getting paperwork, recording deadlines, complaining through the right channels." What is saved is the time of repeated communication and rumination. This is a one-time cognitive adjustment, not a daily time-saver. What can be cross-checked are these deadlines themselves, which are recorded in documents. Public security cases (China) are calculated from the date of acceptance, with a handling period not exceeding 30 days; serious, complex cases approved by the next higher public security organ can be extended by another 30 days. In cases where a person reports a crime but a decision is made not to file a case, the notice of non-filing must be delivered within 3 days. The informant can apply for reconsideration within 7 days, and the public security organ makes a decision within 30 days. If still disagreeing, apply for a review from the next higher level within the following 7 days.
Do not treat "how others live" as something to read every day: set limits or turn off apps where you browse peer updates
A

Acquaintances who compare themselves online with those living better lives often have worse moods and lower self-esteem. People who stopped using Facebook for four weeks felt slightly happier, but their knowledge of current events also dropped significantly. People who limited three social media platforms to 10 minutes each per day felt less lonely and less depressed after three weeks.
Zero cost. Setting app limits or deactivating accounts takes only a few minutes. The difficulty is not reopening them afterward and resisting long-term habits.

A meta-analysis of 54 independent samples, 94 effect sizes, N = 36,583, using a three-level random-effects model. The average correlation between upward social comparison online and psychological maladjustment was r = 0.330 (95% CI 0.289 to 0.370). Broken down by specific outcomes: negative emotions like fear of negative evaluation 0.438, anxiety 0.382. Depression 0.306, low well-being 0.268, low self-esteem 0.263. Age, culture, and the year of data collection did not strengthen or weaken this association. Longitudinal studies also did not show stronger results than cross-sectional surveys. Another randomized controlled trial involved 2,743 Facebook users in the US. Among them, 61% were willing to stop using it for compensation under 102 US dollars. These people were randomly assigned to a four-week cessation group and a control group. Stopping use gave participants an average of 60 extra minutes of free time per day. Subjective well-being indices increased by 0.09 standard deviations. Broken down: life satisfaction 0.12, anxiety 0.10, depression 0.09, happiness 0.08. After correcting for multiple comparisons, these results remained robust. The study authors provided a benchmark: psychological interventions to make people more positive increase subjective well-being by about 0.34 standard deviations and reduce depression by about 0.23 standard deviations. Thus, this effect is about 25% to 40% of a typical psychological intervention. The simultaneous cost: current events knowledge index decreased by 0.19 standard deviations, and political polarization decreased by 0.16 standard deviations. After the experiment ended, the cessation group still used Facebook 12 minutes less per day than the control group (0.31 standard deviations, a 23% reduction). Another randomized controlled trial with 143 college students divided them into two groups. One group limited Facebook, Instagram, and Snapchat to 10 minutes each per platform per day, while the other used them as usual. After three weeks, the time-limited group showed significantly less loneliness and depression. Both groups showed less anxiety and fear of missing out than at the start.
When you feel "everyone saw me embarrass myself," halve the number you estimated
B

When wearing a T-shirt with an embarrassing image into a room, the wearers thought nearly half of the people noticed who was on the shirt, while in reality, it was less than a quarter. When switching to a decent T-shirt, they also overestimated similarly. After group discussions, people also thought their mistakes stood out more to others than they actually did; after talking, they often underestimated how much the other person liked them. So when you feel "everyone saw me embarrass myself," the reality is usually only half or less.
Zero cost. It is just a matter of asking yourself one more question when stressed: did they really see it?

Experiment 1: participants wore a T-shirt with Barry Manilow's face and entered a room with other participants. The wearers estimated that on average 46% of people around them could correctly identify the person on the shirt. In reality, 23% of people around them were correct, making the estimate exactly double the reality. Subtracting the actual number from the estimated number for each session, the average overestimation was 23 percentage points (95% CI 9 to 38). Excluding two sessions with only two or three people around, it was 27 percentage points (11 to 43). Experiment 2: switched to T-shirts chosen by participants that they considered positive. The average estimate was 48%, while in reality 8% of people around them were correct—a sixfold difference. The study authors noted that in both experiments, wearers' estimates were nearly the same (48% and 46%); the difference was the accuracy rate of those around them (8% and 23%). The authors suspected the main cause was that the questionnaire for observers in Experiment 2 was more demanding, not that wearing a decent shirt makes one more prone to overestimation. Experiment 3: students were divided into groups of 3 to 7, discussed a given topic for 20 minutes, and then co-wrote a policy proposal. Immediately after the discussion, each person privately estimated how others in the group would rank everyone, with smaller numbers being higher rank. In the category of "making mistakes," the average self-estimated rank was 2.30, while the actual rank given by others was 2.96, a difference of -0.66 (p < 0.01). Thus, people thought their mistakes were more prominent to others than they actually were. The same applied to "comments that might offend others" (2.35 vs 2.90, p < 0.01), while "comments that would be challenged by others" had a smaller gap (2.61 vs 2.82, p < 0.05). Another series of studies in three contexts: strangers paired for conversation, freshman roommates, and adult education classes. The result was that people systematically underestimated how much their conversation partner liked them and how much the partner enjoyed the conversation. The authors called this the "liking gap." This phenomenon exists in conversations of various lengths and persisted for several months among freshman roommates.
Treat the thought "others demand I be perfect" as a symptom, not a fact
B

People who constantly feel "those around me demand I be perfect, and if I fail I am rejected" are more likely to have suicidal thoughts. "I demand perfection of myself" is much more weakly related to suicidal thoughts, only about one-third as much as the former. Even after controlling for pre-existing thoughts, the former feeling is still associated with an increase in suicidal thoughts later, though the magnitude is not large.
Zero cost. The difficulty lies in viewing this thought as something to be addressed, rather than an accurate measure of others' actual demands.

A meta-analysis of 45 studies, N = 11,747, involving college students, medical students, community adults, and psychiatric patients, using a random-effects model. Below are the weighted average correlations with suicidal ideation. Perfectionistic concerns r = 0.28 (95% CI 0.24 to 0.32; 42 studies, 7,936 people). Perfectionistic concerns is a composite group including socially prescribed perfectionism, concern over mistakes, doubts about actions, and the gap between reality and standards... Within this, socially prescribed perfectionism alone was r = 0.28 (0.25 to 0.32; 30 studies, 3,640 people). Perfectionistic strivings r = 0.10 (0.07 to 0.13; 31 studies, 4,588 people), which is a composite group of self-oriented perfectionism and personal standards. Parental criticism r = 0.20 (0.11 to 0.29). Looking further at the association with non-fatal suicidal behavior: Perfectionistic concerns r = 0.12 (0.07 to 0.17; 15 studies, 5,275 people). Socially prescribed perfectionism r = 0.19 (0.08 to 0.29; 8 studies, 689 people). Looking at longitudinal follow-up: after controlling for baseline suicidal ideation, socially prescribed perfectionism still positively correlated with suicidal ideation at follow-up, though the magnitude was small. Self-oriented perfectionism and other-oriented perfectionism showed no association.
When angry, do not vent by punching a bag or going for a run; slow your body down first
A

Punching a bag, cycling, or going for a run—these venting methods that increase physiological arousal—generally do not resolve anger. Slow breathing, mindfulness, and meditation—these methods that calm the body—significantly curb anger and the urge to act out.

Zero cost. When angry, switch to doing something for a few minutes that helps slow the heart rate: breathe slowly, sit down, be still. The difficulty is that at that moment, the thing you want to do most is vent.

A meta-analysis of 154 studies, totaling 184 samples and 10,189 people. Activities that calm the body, such as deep breathing, mindfulness, and meditation, reduced anger and aggression. The effect size was g = -0.63, 95% CI -0.82 to -0.43. This result was stable across gender, race, age, and culture. Activities that increase arousal, such as punching a bag, jogging, and cycling, were generally useless. Their effect size was g = -0.02, 95% CI -0.13 to 0.09. The study authors' conclusion: venting anger or going for a run are not effective ways to resolve anger.
When something is weighing on your mind, you can write down your thoughts and feelings for several days, but do not expect it to cure an illness
B

Writing down upsetting matters has a small average benefit, but it is very minor. Meta-analyses are also inconsistent; two reviews found no significant effect. It costs almost nothing and is worth a try. If emotional issues are severe, do not use this as a substitute for seeing a doctor.
Zero cost. A common method in studies is writing 3 to 4 times, for 15 to 20 minutes each. Write about something that bothers you, expressing your deepest thoughts and feelings.

A meta-analysis of 146 randomized studies. Participants wrote or spoke about matters important to them. The average effect was positive and statistically significant, but very small, with an effect size of r = 0.075. Another review focusing only on randomized controlled trials, pooling 30 trials, found no statistically significant effect on either physical or mental health. A meta-analysis of 16 randomized trials on cancer patients and survivors found no statistical significance across psychological, physical, or quality-of-life dimensions. Within this, the psychological dimension had g = 0.04, 95% CI -0.06 to 0.14.
For menstrual pain, take painkillers like ibuprofen, do not just endure it; if pain is severe enough to miss work or school and does not improve after three months of medication, see a gynecologist
A

Taking drugs like ibuprofen for menstrual pain increases the rate of significant relief from less than two in ten to about half; it is more effective than paracetamol but has slightly more side effects. If pain is severe enough to miss work or school, causes deep pain during intercourse, or does not improve after three months of medication, see a gynecologist to check for endometriosis. In a study across ten countries, the average delay from symptom onset to diagnosis for this disease was 6.7 years.
A box of ibuprofen costs a dozen or so yuan, only taken during the few days of pain. If a gynecological exam is needed, registration and an ultrasound cost a small amount of money and half a day.

A Cochrane systematic review of 80 randomized controlled trials involving 5,820 women with primary dysmenorrhea. Primary dysmenorrhea is menstrual pain where no other disease is found. Compared to placebo, non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) were more effective at reducing pain (OR 4.37, 95% CI 3.76 to 5.09). This translates to 18% of those taking placebo having moderate or better relief, compared to 45% to 53% for those taking this group of drugs. The cost is slightly more side effects (OR 1.29, 1.11 to 1.51). 10% of those taking placebo experienced side effects, compared to 11% to 14% for this group of drugs. The increase was mainly in gastrointestinal discomfort (OR 1.58) and neurological reactions (OR 2.74). Compared to paracetamol, this group of drugs was also more effective at reducing pain (OR 1.89, 1.05 to 3.43), but there were only 3 trials. Which drug in this group is best has not been differentiated. UK NICE guidelines (updated 2024) list several situations where endometriosis should be suspected. These include chronic pelvic pain, menstrual pain affecting daily activities and quality of life, and deep pain during or after intercourse. Other signs include pain during bowel movements during menstruation, blood in urine or painful urination during menstruation, and infertility accompanied by these symptoms. This also applies to girls aged 17 and under. The guidelines recommend trying paracetamol or this group of drugs first, for example, for 3 months. If pain relief is insufficient, refer for further investigation. Normal gynecological exams and ultrasounds do not rule out this disease. A study surveyed 1,418 women undergoing laparoscopy in 16 hospitals across 10 countries. From symptom onset to diagnostic surgery for endometriosis, the average delay was 6.7 years, mainly due to delays at the primary care level. Women already diagnosed worked an average of 10.8 hours less per week, mostly due to being present at work but performing less effectively. An online survey in the Netherlands asked 32,748 women aged 15 to 45. 13.8% had taken time off work due to their period, averaging 1.3 days per year. 80.7% were present at work during their period but performed less effectively, equivalent to 8.9 fewer workdays per year.
For chronic insomnia (three nights per week or more, lasting over three months), try cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia first; do not start long-term sleeping pills immediately
A

After completing this therapy, the time to fall asleep is on average about 19 minutes faster, and time spent awake during the night is reduced by about 26 minutes. The effect gradually weakens, but remains significant 12 months later. Online self-help courses are nearly as effective as in-person sessions. Sleeping pills provide very little help for people over 60: for every 6 people taking them, 1 experiences side effects, and only 1 in 13 sleeps better.

Undergoing therapy at a sleep clinic, psychiatric department, or psychology department of a hospital involves consultation and treatment fees. Online self-help courses are much cheaper. A course usually lasts 6 to 8 weeks, requiring a daily sleep diary. The part you can do yourself first is stimulus control: only go to bed when sleepy; if you can't sleep, get up. The bed is only for sleep and sex; wake up at the same time every day and do not nap during the day. The difficult part is sleep restriction: in the first few weeks, you must shorten your time in bed, which makes you sleepier during the day.

The 2020 Diagnostic and Treatment Guidelines of the National Health Commission (China) list the key points for diagnosing insomnia disorder according to international classifications. First, difficulty falling asleep, easily waking up after falling asleep, or waking up early. Second, daytime fatigue, sleepiness, and impaired work performance. Third, these conditions occur at least 3 times per week and last for at least 3 months. Less than 3 months is called short-term insomnia disorder. The guidelines rank cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I) as the first-line treatment. The therapy consists of 5 parts: sleep restriction, stimulus control, cognitive therapy, relaxation training, and sleep hygiene, usually in cycles of 6 to 8 weeks. The guidelines state its short-term effectiveness is equal to medication, and in the long term, it is better than medication. The guidelines also specify that continuous use of sleeping pills should generally not exceed 4 weeks; if continued use is necessary, an evaluation should be done once a month. The 2016 guidelines from the American College of Physicians strongly recommend that all adults with chronic insomnia should receive CBT-I first. If CBT-I alone is not effective, then discuss with a doctor whether to add short-term medication. A meta-analysis of 20 randomized controlled trials involving 1,162 people calculated that after therapy, sleep onset latency was shortened by 19.03 minutes (95% CI 14.12 to 23.93). Wake after sleep onset decreased by 26.00 minutes (15.48 to 36.52). The percentage of time actually spent sleeping while in bed (sleep efficiency) was 9.91% higher (8.09% to 11.73%). Total sleep time only increased by 7.61 minutes, which was not statistically significant (−0.51 to 15.74). No studies reported adverse consequences. Another meta-analysis of 30 randomized controlled trials looked at how long the effects lasted. Compared to those who did not receive therapy, the improvement in insomnia severity decreased over time. At month 3, g = 0.64; month 6, 0.40; month 12, 0.25. The effect weakens, but the authors believe it remains clinically significant within one year. Regarding online methods, a meta-analysis of 11 randomized controlled trials involving 1,460 people was conducted. All sleep indices improved, with effect sizes (g) ranging from 0.21 to 1.09. The authors stated this effectiveness is equivalent to in-person sessions; the longer the course and the more closely monitored, the greater the effect. Another online randomized trial with 1,711 people used a control group that only received sleep hygiene materials. Those using digital therapy had significantly improved sleep-related quality of life, while daytime physical and mental states improved slightly. Regarding sleeping pills, a meta-analysis of 24 randomized controlled trials involved 2,417 people over 60 with insomnia. Every trial involved taking medication for at least 5 consecutive nights. Compared to a placebo, those taking sleeping pills slept an extra 25.2 minutes, and the number of nighttime awakenings decreased by 0.63 times. For every 13 people taking the medication, 1 had improved sleep quality. For every 6 people taking the medication, 1 experienced side effects (number needed to harm NNH 6, from 4.7 to 7.1). Side effects related to memory and thinking were 4.78 times higher than in the placebo group (OR 4.78, from 1.47 to 15.47). Daytime fatigue was 3.82 times higher (OR 3.82, from 1.88 to 7.80).

If you snore very loudly, others observe you stop breathing during sleep, or you are so sleepy during the day that you fall asleep while driving, go to a hospital for a sleep study to check for sleep apnea; for moderate to severe cases, use a CPAP machine at night
A

Sleep apnea is when breathing repeatedly stops or becomes shallow during sleep, causing the person to choke and wake up, leading to daytime sleepiness. Using a CPAP machine significantly reduces daytime sleepiness and decreases driving accidents by about seven-tenths. However, trials have not shown that it prevents heart disease or helps people live longer; it is worn to ensure daytime alertness.

First, visit a sleep clinic, respiratory department, or ENT department at a hospital. Diagnosis requires an overnight sleep study, either sleeping at the hospital or borrowing a device to wear at home. People who need a CPAP machine usually have to buy it themselves, which is a significant expense. The difficulty lies in persistence: you must wear a mask to sleep every night; in the first few weeks, many people take it off after a few hours before getting used to it.

The 2017 diagnostic guidelines from the American Academy of Sleep Medicine (AASM) list who is likely to have moderate to severe sleep apnea. These are individuals who are very sleepy during the day on most days, plus at least two of the following three conditions: first, frequent loud snoring; second, someone has observed you stop breathing, gasp, or choke awake during sleep; third, you have been diagnosed with hypertension. The guidelines require diagnosis via a sleep study and not just based on questionnaires. If breathing stops or becomes shallow 5 or more times per hour and symptoms are present, it is considered the disease. Regardless of symptoms, 15 or more times per hour also counts. A 2019 systematic review by the AASM pooled 38 randomized controlled trials. Compared to no treatment, CPAP users had a self-reported sleepiness score reduction of 2.4 points (95% CI 1.9 to 2.8). This scale is the Epworth Sleepiness Scale, with a maximum of 24 points; higher scores indicate more sleepiness. For those who were not originally sleepy, 5 trials showed a reduction of 1.0 point, which the authors deemed not clinically significant. The same review pooled 10 studies comparing before and after treatment. With CPAP, the car accident rate was 0.3 times the pre-treatment rate (RR 0.3, 0.2 to 0.4), a reduction of about seven-tenths. Another 2010 analysis pooled 9 similar studies, resulting in an RR of 0.278 (0.22 to 0.35). This analysis also stated that daytime sleepiness significantly decreased after just one night of use, and simulated driving ability improved within 2 to 7 days. A 2009 analysis by the same group indicated that untreated patients have a car accident risk roughly 1.21 to 4.89 times higher than others. Regarding cardiovascular health and longevity, the SAVE trial recruited 2,717 moderate-to-severe patients aged 45 to 75, all of whom had coronary artery disease or a history of stroke. After random assignment, they were followed for an average of 3.7 years. The rate of cardiovascular or cerebrovascular events in the CPAP group was 17.0%, compared to 15.4% in the non-CPAP group. There was no difference between the two groups (HR 1.10, 0.91 to 1.32). Users wore the device for an average of only 3.3 hours per night. They snored less, were less sleepy during the day, and their quality of life and mood improved. A 2017 analysis pooled 10 randomized trials involving 7,266 people. Overall mortality rates also showed no difference (RR 1.13, 0.99 to 1.29). A 2019 estimate stated that among Chinese people aged 30 to 69, approximately 176 million have this disease, accounting for 23.6%. Among them, moderate to severe cases account for about 65.52 million people (8.8%), the largest number in the world.
Change "intend to do" into "at what time, in what place, in what situation, do what"
A

Change the sentence "I will do this" to "At 8 a.m. on Tuesday, when I sit at my desk, I will write the introduction first." Pooling 94 tests together, people who write this way achieve their goals significantly more often, with a medium to large effect size. It only requires changing one sentence, costing no money and no extra effort.
Costs no money. Each task takes 1 to 2 minutes to write an "if... then..." sentence. For example: "At 8 a.m. on Tuesday, when I sit at my desk, I will write the introduction first."

Pooling 94 independent tests, people who pre-formulate their intentions into "if... then..." sentences have a higher goal achievement rate. In psychology, this method is called implementation intention. The effect size is d = 0.65, which is medium to large. It works at three stages: getting started, staying on track when interrupted, and disengaging from tasks that are certain to fail.
Before starting a task, write down the stopping conditions
B

Before starting, write a sentence: if by [date] I haven't reached [target], then stop. Pooling multiple studies, this method indeed helps people withdraw from actions that are certain to fail. What you save is all the time you would have otherwise continued to pour into it.

Costs no money. Spend 5 minutes at the start to clearly write "if by [date] I haven't reached [target], then stop." The difficulty lies in admitting defeat on that day; stopping in front of others can be a bit embarrassing.

Pooling multiple studies on implementation intentions, pre-set "if... then..." sentences also help people withdraw from actions that are certain to fail. The original text of the paper calls this "disengagement from failing courses of action." The time saved is the portion you would have otherwise continued to invest.
When deciding whether to continue, only look at future costs and future returns; ignore how much has already been invested
B

Money and time already invested make people more likely to want to continue. Pooling 98 datasets, this trend is real and stable. Therefore, when considering whether to continue, only calculate how much more needs to be invested and how much will be gained later. Do not include what has already been spent.
Costs no money. The difficulty lies in accepting one thing: the time previously invested is gone and cannot be recovered.

Money, effort, and time already invested make people more likely to want to continue. In psychology, this is called the sunk cost effect. Pooling 98 datasets, analysis confirms this trend is real and stable. By avoiding it, you won't continue to waste time just because you "don't want to waste" what's already gone.
Estimate the time to complete a task based on the actual time of similar tasks in the past, not from a plan
B

Students estimated they would finish their thesis in 33.9 days, but it actually took 55.5 days; only 29.7% finished within their estimated time. Another group was asked to recall how long a similar task took last time before making an estimate. The on-time completion rate increased from 29.3% to 60.0%.
Costs no money. Before estimating, spend a few minutes reviewing how long a similar task actually took last time.

Students planned to finish their thesis in 33.9 days, but it actually took 55.5 days. Only 29.7% finished within their estimated time. Researchers asked another group to link past experience to the current task before estimating. This group's on-time completion rate increased from 29.3% (control group) to 60.0%. The optimistic bias of estimating less time than reality disappeared in this group.
Send the meeting agenda in advance; if there is no agenda, do not meet; if you can stand, then stand
B

Meetings with an agenda sent in advance make participants feel the meeting is more useful. In experiments, sitting meetings lasted 34% longer than standing meetings, while the quality of decisions made by both types was the same.
Costs no money. The organizer spends 5 to 10 minutes before the meeting to write the agenda. Standing meetings require cooperation from participants.

Two surveys involved 958 and 292 people respectively. Results: meetings with an agenda sent in advance were perceived by participants as more effective; this correlation was statistically significant. Another experiment involved 55 sitting meeting groups and 56 standing meeting groups. Sitting meetings lasted 34% longer. The quality of decisions between the two types did not differ.
Reduce the number of meetings; if something can be resolved via text and doesn't require an immediate response, don't meet
B

The more meetings in a day, the more tired people feel and the more they perceive their workload as heavy. Eliminating a meeting saves exactly the amount of time that meeting would have lasted, not a minute less.
Costs no money. Requires cooperation from colleagues and superiors. The difficulty is that writing a clear paragraph takes more effort than saying a sentence.

Two surveys were conducted on employees working 35 hours or more per week, with 676 and 304 participants respectively. The impact of meeting time on work attitude and happiness is not fixed but depends on two things: the quality of the meeting and how much the work depends on others. Another study had participants keep a diary for a week. Results: the more meetings per day, the more fatigue and the heavier the perceived workload. The time saved is exactly the duration of the meetings you skip.
Break large tasks into sub-tasks before estimating time and starting work
B

When estimating time, people do not automatically break down a task to calculate each part. Listing sub-tasks first before estimating prevents underestimating a significant portion. Once broken down, every small step is immediately actionable, which also reduces procrastination.
Costs no money. The act of breaking it down takes 5 to 15 minutes.

When estimating time, people do not automatically break a multi-faceted task into parts. For example, writing a literature review, writing the discussion, and organizing references are different tasks. Listing sub-tasks first before estimating reduces the error of underestimating time; this error is called the planning fallacy. Once divided, each small step becomes an action that can be started immediately, and procrastination decreases accordingly. In research, the strongest predictors of procrastination include task aversion and the task being delayed.
If a task has no external deadline, set one for yourself
B

When there is an external deadline, 80.6% of students finish before the deadline. When finishing within their own estimated time, only 38.7% succeed. Completion time almost always follows the deadline and has little to do with the estimated figure. Therefore, if a task has no deadline, set one for yourself and keep your word.
Costs no money. The difficulty lies in keeping your word; if the day comes and you ignore it, it's as if you never set it.

Students with an external deadline: 80.6% finished before the deadline. For those finishing within their own estimated time, it was only 38.7%. Completion time closely follows the deadline, with a correlation coefficient r = 0.82; the closer to 1, the tighter the link. For self-estimated figures, the correlation was very weak.
View procrastination as avoiding discomfort, not as a lack of effort
A

How unpleasant a task is, whether one feels capable of doing it, how easily one is distracted by immediate rewards, and the strength of self-control: these factors are most strongly linked to procrastination. Personality traits like neuroticism or sensation-seeking are only weakly related. Therefore, you can fix the issue by making the task less unpleasant or shrinking the first step, rather than just relying on scolding yourself and trying harder.
Zero cost. Only a shift in perspective: first ask what makes this task unpleasant, then find a solution.

A meta-analysis synthesizing 691 correlation coefficients found that factors strongly and consistently associated with procrastination include: task averseness, time remaining until the deadline, self-efficacy (believing one can do it), impulsivity, as well as conscientiousness and its components: self-control, distractibility, organization, and achievement motivation. Meanwhile, neuroticism, rebelliousness, and sensation-seeking were only weakly related to procrastination. The authors explain these results using temporal motivation theory: the current attractiveness of a task decreases rapidly as the reward becomes more distant.
Keep necessary items within reach and move unwanted items away; don't rely on willpower in the moment
B

When items are placed slightly further away, people take them slightly less often. For the same snack, moving it further away significantly reduces consumption, with a moderate effect size. Displaying fewer choices also significantly reduces the number of people who take them. This method doesn't force you to resist in the moment; it only takes a few minutes to arrange.
Zero cost, takes a few minutes each time. Move your phone to another room, and have books and your computer ready on the desk.

A Cochrane review of 24 randomized trials. Moving food further away reduced consumption, with a standardized mean difference of −0.60 (95% CI −0.84 to −0.36; 12 studies, 1,098 participants, low-certainty evidence), a moderate effect. Reducing the number of options more significantly decreased the selection of that item, with a standardized mean difference of −1.13 (95% CI −1.90 to −0.37; 3 studies, 154 participants, low-certainty evidence). Regression analysis showed: the further the distance and the fewer the choices, the stronger the effect.
If you want to force yourself to succeed, place a bet, but first ask if you are willing to wager
A

To force yourself to succeed, you can choose to receive a reward upon completion, or place a deposit upfront, where the deposit is returned plus a bonus only if you succeed. Among those willing to participate in both types, the deposit group was 13 percentage points more successful. However, only 13.7% of people were willing to make a deposit, while 90% accepted the reward. Thus, deposits are only useful for those willing to bet.
The deposit model requires putting up your own money upfront; if you fail, you lose it. In the trial, the deposit was 150 US dollars.

A randomized trial in the US with 2,538 participants, randomly assigning employees and their relatives or friends into four types of financial incentives or usual care. The reward model (receiving approximately 800 US dollars upon success) had a 90.0% acceptance rate; the deposit model (depositing 150 dollars upfront, plus a 650 dollar bonus) was 13.7%. Smoking cessation rates sustained after six months: the four incentive models ranged from 9.4% to 16.0%, while usual care was 6.0%. The reward model was 15.7%, and the deposit model was 10.2%. However, considering only the 13.7% of people "willing to participate in both types," the six-month cessation rate for the deposit model was 13.2 percentage points higher than the reward model (95% CI 3.1 to 22.8).
Measure new habits in months, not by the "21 days" rule
B

The idea that "it takes 21 days to form a habit" has no basis. A study tracking participants for 12 weeks calculated that for an action to become an automatic reflex, the fastest person took 18 days, while the slowest took 254 days. It is normal if things don't feel effortless after two or three weeks. Missing a single day in the middle does not reset your progress to zero.
Zero cost. Requires repeating the same action in the same context every day, consistently for several months.

96 volunteers each chose an action related to eating, drinking, or exercise, performed daily in a fixed context (e.g., "after breakfast") for 12 consecutive weeks, self-rating their level of automaticity daily. Data from 82 participants were sufficient for analysis, and the model fit 62 participants. The number of days required to reach 95% of each individual's peak automaticity ranged from 18 to 254 days. The study also found that missing a single performance did not significantly affect the habit formation process.
If procrastination affects your life, use self-help materials proven by randomized trials; a therapist is not always necessary
A

Even severe procrastination that causes distress can be improved. Practicing with self-help materials based on cognitive behavioral therapy for ten weeks, whether guided by someone or entirely self-directed, is significantly better than doing nothing. No significant difference was found between having a guide or not, so self-study is also effective.
A self-help book costs a few dozen yuan, and some are free. Requires about ten weeks, reading one lesson and doing one exercise per week.

150 participants were randomly assigned to three groups: self-help with therapist guidance, self-help without guidance, and a waitlist control group. After ten weeks, on the Pure Procrastination Scale, the effect sizes between groups were d = 0.70 for the guided group (95% CI 0.29 to 1.10) and d = 0.50 for the unguided group (0.10 to 0.90). On the Irrational Procrastination Scale, the figures were 0.81 (0.40 to 1.22) and 0.69 (0.29 to 1.09), respectively. Clinically significant improvement rates: guided group 31.3% to 40.0%, unguided group 24.0% to 36.0%. The two groups did not differ statistically in any outcome.
Use your hourly wage to decide which household chores to outsource
B

On average, Chinese people spend 1 hour 17 minutes a day on housework. Specifically, those who actually do chores on a given day spend 1 hour 59 minutes. People who spend money to buy time are more satisfied with life. For the same amount of money, using it to buy time brings more immediate happiness than buying physical goods.
Requires spending money on outsourcing, the amount depending on the service. Additionally, requires a one-time effort to calculate your exact hourly wage.

Chinese residents spend an average of 1 hour 17 minutes on housework daily. Considering only those who do housework, the average is 1 hour 59 minutes. This is from a 2024 survey of 38,500 households and 107,000 individuals. Another study sampling 6,271 people across four countries found that those who spend money to buy time are more satisfied with life. Researchers also conducted real-world experiments: for the same amount of money, using it to buy time resulted in higher immediate feelings of happiness than buying material objects.
Set hard limits on short videos and aimless scrolling
C

In 2024, Chinese people spent an average of 5 hours 37 minutes online daily; specifically, those who actually went online spent 6 hours 3 minutes. In 2018, using the same calculation, it was only 2 hours 42 minutes. This is the largest figure in this chapter. Cutting one hour a day gives you an extra 365 hours a year.

Zero cost. The setup takes only a few minutes: turn off push notifications, delete apps, or set daily time limits for apps. The difficulty lies in keeping your hands off and resisting the urge to open them.

Chinese residents spend an average of 5 hours 37 minutes online daily. Considering only those who actually go online, the average is 6 hours 3 minutes. People who use the internet daily account for 92.9%. These are 2024 figures. In 2018, using the same calculation, it was only 2 hours 42 minutes. This is the largest figure in this chapter. Cutting one hour a day from that is equivalent to gaining 365 hours per year. Additionally, according to the China Internet Network Information Center (CNNIC), as of June 2025, the average internet user spent 30.6 hours online per week, 1.9 hours more than six months prior. Short video users numbered 1.068 billion, accounting for 95.1% of internet users.
Avoid television and continuous news feeds; consume necessary information in one batch at a fixed time
C

Americans aged 15 and older watch 2.6 hours of television daily, accounting for half of their total leisure time. In 2018, Chinese people watched an average of 1 hour 40 minutes daily, with seniors aged 75 to 84 watching 3 hours 16 minutes. By switching to batching necessary information at a fixed time, the savings come from this portion.
Zero cost. The difficulty lies in breaking the habit of reflexively turning it on, and you might miss some real-time news.

Americans aged 15 and older watch 2.6 hours of TV daily. Their total leisure time is 5.2 hours, with TV watching accounting for half. These are 2025 figures. Chinese residents watch an average of 1 hour 40 minutes of TV daily, while those aged 75 to 84 watch 3 hours 16 minutes. These are 2018 figures.
Invest time once to learn shortcuts and automation for frequently used software
B

Most people accustomed to using Word still click icons on the toolbar. In controlled experiments, keyboard shortcuts were faster than both menus and icons. Learning once is a one-time cost, after which every operation every day yields a return. The longer you perform the same type of work, the greater the profit.
Zero cost. Requires a one-time investment of a few to several dozen hours to learn. The difficulty is that initially, it may be slower than using a mouse.

A study examined 251 experienced Word users: most rarely used shortcuts despite them being faster, primarily clicking toolbar icons. Controlled experiments confirmed: among the three methods—menus, icons, and shortcuts—shortcuts were the fastest. Time saved accumulates bit by bit with the number of daily operations. People doing the same type of work long-term benefit the most.
When choosing a place to live, prioritize commute time and shorten the one-way distance
B

In tracking data from Germany, the further people commute, the lower their perceived quality of life. This loss is not compensated for by salary or housing quality. Reducing each way by 30 minutes results in 5 extra hours per week.
High cost. May involve paying higher rent or moving to a smaller home. The act of moving itself is also time-consuming.

Chinese residents spend an average of 50 minutes daily on travel. Considering only those who travel on a given day, it is 1 hour 2 minutes. These are 2024 figures. Long-term tracking data of the same group in Germany shows: the more time people spend commuting between home and work, the lower their subjective well-being (how well they feel they are living) consistently is. And this loss is not offset by income or housing. A systematic review of multiple studies also confirmed: the longer the commute time, the more dissatisfied people are with commuting, regardless of the mode of transport. Reducing each way by 30 minutes saves approximately 5 hours per week.
Turn off all auto-renewals and manually renew upon expiration
C

What you save are the subscriptions you haven't used for a long time but are still being charged for every month. Checking the list of "auto-deductions" on Alipay, WeChat, Apple, and Android takes less than 20 minutes. According to regulations, before deducting money, sellers must clearly remind you and provide a place to cancel at any time that is easy to find and easy to click.
Free. Checking the "auto-deduction" list on Alipay, WeChat, Apple, and Android takes 10 to 20 minutes each time. In the future, you will have to click one more time for each renewal.

The amount saved is the total of subscriptions you no longer use but are still being charged for. This varies for each person, so there is no general figure. Regulatory authorities require sellers to clearly remind you before renewal and provide a "simple cancel anytime" option, with no extra fee for cancellation (China, applied since 2021).
Perform a personal income tax settlement once a year from March to June, and fully declare all eligible deductions
A

These types of people usually get a refund after doing this: those who only worked for a few months in the year, changed jobs mid-year, or haven't declared deductions such as children's education, mortgage interest, rent, or elderly support. It takes about ten minutes on a phone. If your total comprehensive annual income is below ⟦120000⟧, or the additional tax payable is below ⟦400⟧, you may skip it.
Free. Done on the "Personal Income Tax" app (China), it takes about ten minutes.

Combine four types of income—wages and salaries, labor remuneration, author's remuneration, and royalties—to calculate the total once. Overpayments are refunded, and underpayments must be settled. There are two cases where you can skip it: total comprehensive annual income does not exceed ⟦120000⟧, or the tax to be paid back does not exceed ⟦400⟧. These two conditions are stipulated by the 2023 announcement of the State Taxation Administration (China), applicable until December 31, 2027. Conversely, the following types of people usually get a refund: those with income for only a few months of the year, those who changed jobs mid-year, or those with deductions like children's education, mortgage interest, rent, or elderly support that haven't been declared.
Housing Provident Fund is not just for buying a house: rent, renovations, and management fees can all be withdrawn; follow new regulations from September 20, 2026
A

The Housing Provident Fund (China) is not only accessible when buying a house. The new regulations list nine cases for withdrawal, including paying rent, renovating your own residence, and paying building management fees. After you submit an application, the fund center must respond within 3 days of acceptance regarding whether the withdrawal is approved.
Free. Just go through the withdrawal procedures once.

The revised regulations list nine cases for withdrawal. These include: paying rent, renovating your own residence, and paying management fees for your own residence. The Housing Provident Fund management center must make a decision to allow or disallow the withdrawal within 3 days from the date of accepting your application.
Recalculate phone and internet plans once a year; downgrade if not fully used; complain if the carrier refuses the switch
A

The old plan you are using is often dozens of yuan more expensive than the plans currently on sale. Dozens per month adds up to hundreds of yuan wasted per year. According to regulations, carriers cannot refuse your request to switch networks without a valid reason, cannot delay the process, and especially cannot set a separate price list for users who switch. If they hold you back, file a complaint.
Free. Reviewing the bill once takes about ten minutes. The difficulty lies in standing your ground when the operator refuses to let you downgrade.

Regulations from the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (China) clearly state that carriers must not "refuse, obstruct, or delay the provision of number portability services to users without a valid reason." They also must not "use technical measures such as blocking or restricting to affect the communication quality of number portability users." Furthermore, they must not "set specific rate plans and specific promotional programs for number portability users." Old plans are usually dozens of yuan more expensive than current ones. Not switching means wasting hundreds of yuan every year.
Do not buy lottery tickets
A

According to regulations, the prize payout for lotto-type lotteries is at least 50% of revenue; for Double Color Ball, it is 51%. If you spend ⟦1⟧, in the long run, you will only get back an average of ⟦0.51⟧, steadily losing 49%. In 2024, the country sold ⟦623486000000⟧ in lottery tickets, of which ⟦161031000000⟧ went directly into public welfare funds; this portion is not included in the prize money.
Free. Not buying is saving.

The Ministry of Finance (China) stipulates the minimum ratio of prize money to revenue: 50% for lotto and number-selection lotteries, 65% for instant scratch-offs, and 73% for sports betting lotteries. Double Color Ball allocates 51% of revenue for prizes; for every ⟦100⟧ sold, only ⟦51⟧ is taken out for prizes. For you, for every ⟦1⟧ spent, in the long run, you only get back an average of ⟦0.51⟧, losing 49%. In 2024, the country sold ⟦623486000000⟧ in lottery tickets, of which ⟦161031000000⟧ went into public welfare funds and did not return to the hands of ticket buyers (China, 2024).
If you see "high profit," "capital preservation," or "guaranteed profit," walk away immediately
A

In 2018, the former Chairman of the China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission once said: if the yield is over 6%, question it; over 8% is very dangerous; and from 10% upwards, be prepared to lose all your capital. Formal investment products are now prohibited from promising capital preservation or guaranteed returns. Money lost due to participation in illegal fundraising is your own responsibility according to regulations; no one will bear the loss for you if something goes wrong.
Free. Just stop for a moment when you hear these words.

In 2018, at the Lujiazui Forum, the former Chairman of the China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission made a statement. The original quote is: "if the yield is over 6%, you must question it; over 8% is very dangerous; from 10% upwards, you must be prepared to lose all your capital." New asset management regulations require financial institutions "not to promise capital preservation or guaranteed returns," and "when facing payment difficulties, financial institutions must not advance funds for payment in any form." Therefore, formal investment products no longer offer capital preservation. Losses from participating in illegal fundraising are "borne by the fund participants themselves," and no one will compensate you if something happens (China, 2018, 2021).
Do not pay the minimum on credit cards, do not use installments or consumer loans for shopping; if you must borrow, convert the interest to an annual rate before comparing
C

Paying the minimum is a loan with interest calculated daily; according to the ceiling before 2020, this converted to about 18% per year, and using it immediately voids the interest-free period. An installment plan listed as a "0.6% monthly fee" is actually about 13.8% annually, not 7.2%. This is because the principal is being paid down every month, while the fee is still calculated based on the original amount. To compare which loan is more expensive, only look at the annual interest rate, not the daily interest or monthly fee.

Free. You must have enough cash ready to pay the full balance before the statement date. The difficulty is resisting the urge to use installments to break up a large expense. If you must borrow, take a few minutes to clarify the annual interest rate for each loan.

Credit card overdraft interest rates before 2020 had a ceiling and a floor: the ceiling was a "daily interest rate of 0.05%," and the floor was 0.7 times the ceiling. 0.05% per day converts to 18.25% per year; this is simple interest: calculated at 18.25% per year, the interest is not added to the principal. From 2021, this changed to being negotiated between the card issuer and the cardholder. Once the minimum payment is used, the entire unpaid principal is charged interest daily, and the interest-free period is lost. The central bank (China) has required card issuers to clearly display the annual interest rate (the rate converted for the whole year), "not just the daily interest rate or the daily payment amount." Since 2021, all lending institutions must clearly state the annual interest rate when advertising or signing contracts. They may include daily or monthly rates, but these must not be more prominent than the annual rate. The annual rate must include both interest and all fees directly related to the loan.
