For loans with gradual principal repayment, the calculation is based on the amount you actually use according to the remaining principal after each period. The People's Bank of China provided an example: borrowing ⟦100000⟧, repaid over 12 months, with a monthly installment fee of 0.5% of the original principal. At the time of borrowing, a ⟦1000⟧ service fee is also paid. Calculated as simple interest, the annual rate is about 12.80%. Calculated as compound interest (Internal Rate of Return method), the annual rate is about 13.58%. Looking only at the fee level, you might think it only costs 0.5% × 12 + 1% = 7% per year. In reality, it is nearly double, because the principal decreases each month while the installment fee is still collected based on ⟦100000⟧. Using the same method, a credit card split into 12 periods with a 0.6% fee per period and no other fees is nominally 7.2% per year. Calculated as compound interest, the annual rate is about 13.8%, roughly 1.9 times the nominal figure. Splitting from 6 to 36 periods all fall within the 1.8 to 2 times range. If the lender is an individual or a regular company, it is a civil loan. If the agreed interest rate exceeds 4 times the 1-year LPR at the time of contract signing, the court will not protect the excess portion. The 1-year LPR on August 20, 2026, was 3.0%, so 4 times is 12%. If interest is deducted upfront from the loan, the court calculates the principal based on the amount actually received. This threshold does not apply to licensed financial institutions such as banks and consumer finance companies. Seven types of local financial organizations, such as small loan companies, pawnshops, and financial leasing companies, also do not apply this. Therefore, 12% cannot be applied to their loans; you must check the annual interest rate stated in the contract (China, 2020, 2021).
Do not give gifts to livestreamers, do not top up games, and do not click to buy on impulse
B

Gamers in China spend an average of about ⟦480⟧ per person per year on games; once spent, it is almost impossible to get back. The law only allows for the recovery of money spent by minors without parental consent; there is no such provision for adults. The least strenuous way is prevention: turn off password-free payments, set per-transaction and daily limits, and unlink payment methods.

Free. It takes a few minutes to do three things: turn off password-free payments, set per-transaction and daily limits, and delete linked payment methods on platforms. The difficulty is restraining your finger in the heat of the moment.

This is a very large expense. In 2024, the actual revenue of the Chinese game market was ⟦325783000000⟧, with 674 million users, averaging about ⟦480⟧ per person (this figure is derived by dividing the two numbers). Money spent is almost impossible to get back. There is only one exception: if a person with limited capacity for civil conduct (in this case, a minor) gives gifts or tops up without the guardian's consent, when the guardian demands the money back, "the people's court must accept it." For adults who give gifts or top up themselves, there is no such regulation. Additionally, minors are originally only allowed to play online games on Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays. The allowed playing time is only 1 hour, from 20:00 to 21:00 each day (China, 2020, 2021).
Children using phones to top up or give gifts: large expenses by children aged 8 and over that parents do not acknowledge can be reclaimed
A

If a child aged 8 or over spends an amount of money inconsistent with their age and intelligence, it must have parental consent or subsequent acknowledgment to be valid. If parents do not consent and do not acknowledge the expense, the transaction is invalid and can be reclaimed. Children under 8 are inherently not allowed to make spending decisions. If parents remain silent and do not express an opinion, it is legally considered a non-acknowledgment of the expense.

Free. Time must be spent gathering evidence and negotiating with the platform; platforms often refuse at first and refund later. If negotiation fails, the only way is to file a lawsuit, which is measured in months or more, and lawyer fees are self-paid. Therefore, preparing all documents in advance and going through the platform and the 12315 hotline (China's consumer complaint hotline) is more beneficial. The difficulty is if the child refuses to tell you; you must patiently ask to clarify.

Minors aged 8 and over are persons with limited capacity for civil conduct, meaning they can only perform acts consistent with their age and intelligence. Civil transactions inconsistent with their age and intelligence must be consented to or acknowledged by a legal representative to be valid: parents must nod beforehand or accept afterward. Children under 8 are persons without capacity for civil conduct and cannot decide for themselves; their affairs are handled by a legal representative. If the legal representative does not express an opinion, it is considered a refusal to acknowledge: if parents remain silent, it is counted as not accepting the expense.
Teach your child one sentence: anyone online who tells you to take your parents' phone to operate it or read a verification code is a scammer
B

These six types of scams each have a different trick, but the final step is always the same: telling the child to take their parents' phone to transfer money. Therefore, teaching one sentence is enough: anyone who tells you to touch your parents' phone or read a verification code is a scammer. Add one more sentence: "if you are scammed, tell your parents first; we won't scold you."

Free. Tell your child about the six types below, then make a pact with them: "if you are scammed, tell your parents first; we won't scold you." At the same time, set limits for password-free payments, turn on youth mode, and do not let your child know the payment password. The difficulty is that if the child actually gets scammed, you must restrain your anger.

The Quanzhou Anti-Fraud Center and the Quanzhou Municipal Education Bureau (China) analyzed six types of scams specifically targeting teenagers. Each has a different trick, but the final step is always the same: telling the child to take their parents' phone to transfer money. Type one: private trading of game accounts and items at low prices. Little Wang transferred ⟦260⟧ privately; the other side said "transferring money as a minor is a violation, the account will be locked," the child used the father's phone to click a "check link," and more than ⟦30000⟧ in the account was transferred away. The original article reminds that scammers will ask for bank cards, passwords, and SMS verification codes from parents; these "must absolutely not be given." Type two: "removing game addiction restrictions." The other side threatened "if you don't transfer money to cancel it, your parents will go to jail," and the child used the mother's phone to transfer ⟦7000⟧. The original article states that anti-addiction systems are set by the state and "there is absolutely no 'private unlocking' channel." Type three: gift refunding. Scammers pose as "official customer service," saying money spent by minors on gifts can be refunded, requiring the user to "use the parents' Alipay to give gifts to a designated livestream room to get the refund"; ⟦73000⟧ in the mother's account was given away, and the contact was blocked. The original article says "anyone who adds you as a friend and says 'give gifts to get a refund' is 100% a scammer." Type four: posing as classmates or teachers. Scammers hijack accounts and send voice messages calling out names to borrow money. During the school opening season, they also infiltrate class groups posing as teachers, sending "pay tuition and miscellaneous fees of ⟦500⟧," with profile pictures and display names identical to the real teachers, even planting "shills" in the group saying "already paid." Type five: idol chasing. Scammers pull children into "star fan groups to receive ⟦888⟧ red envelopes." First, they tell the child to transfer ⟦48.88⟧ for "verification." Then they threaten "participation by a minor is a violation, the platform will freeze ⟦80000⟧, and parents will go to jail." A total of ⟦16000⟧ was scammed. The original article says "real police and lawyers will absolutely not contact minors online for investigations, let alone tell them to use their parents' phones to operate." Type six: using cheap goods on second-hand markets to lure people off-platform for private transfers. The same document also lists three red lines children should not cross themselves. One: bank cards and SIM cards must not be lent, sold, or rented; if a card is used to transfer dirty money, it may constitute the crime of assisting information network criminal activities (China). A criminal record will affect graduate school and civil service exams. Two: part-time jobs like "lending a phone to act as a call forwarding station" are illegal. Three: "high-salary recruitment" abroad, where a person might be controlled as soon as they arrive (China nationwide, October 2025).
Decline extended warranties for electronics
B

Extended warranties are often sold at 10% to 50% of the device's price; sellers make over ten times more profit on these plans than on regular goods, and that difference is the extra money you pay. Major components such as washing machine motors and refrigerator compressors are already mandated by the state to have a 3-year warranty. If you encounter a very cheap extended warranty, divide the plan price by the cost of a single repair; the result is how high the probability of breaking down at least once during those years must be just to break even.
Costs no money. The price is that once the warranty expires, you pay for repairs yourself if they occur, but the probability of this is not high.

The price of extended warranty plans is usually 10% to 50% of the product's original price. Industry estimates cited in research state the average gross profit margin for extended warranties is 50% to 60%: for every 100 units sold, 50 to 60 units are profit. This figure is about 18 times the gross profit margin of regular goods. In 2003, extended warranties accounted for only 3% to 4% of Best Buy's revenue but contributed over 50% of profits (USA, retail data from the 2000s). If you find a plan priced significantly lower than this range, you can calculate it yourself: plan price ÷ cost of one repair = probability of failure needed to break even. You should only buy it if you estimate the chance of breaking down at least once during the extended warranty years is greater than this number. For example, for a ⟦25⟧ plan, assuming a single repair costs ⟦300⟧, the probability of failing at least once must exceed about 8% to break even. ⟦300⟧ here is just an example, not a statistical figure. Before calculating, subtract the portion already covered by state-mandated warranties. The "three guarantees" period (repair, replacement, return) stipulated by the state (China) starts from the invoice date: 1 year for the whole unit of washing machines and refrigerators, and 3 years for major components. Major components for washing machines are the motor, timer, program controller, and capacitor; for refrigerators, they are the compressor, thermostat, etc. Any extended warranty period that overlaps with the three guarantees is essentially paying for something that is already provided (National China, since 1995)
Prioritize generic drugs that have passed consistency evaluations and centralized procurement drugs
A

Drugs in the second round of centralized procurement saw an average price reduction of 53%, with a maximum reduction of 93%. As of April 2026, 11 rounds have been conducted, covering 490 types of drugs. When getting a prescription or buying medicine, ask one more question: "Is there a centralized procurement drug or a generic name drug?" Using the same active ingredient can save a significant amount.
Costs no money. When the doctor prescribes or when you buy medicine, ask one more question: "Is there a centralized procurement drug or a generic name drug?"

Centralized drug procurement is organized by the state (China); the second round saw an average price reduction of 53%, with a maximum of 93%. As of April 2026, 11 rounds have been implemented, covering 490 types of drugs. The number of drugs that have passed or are deemed to have passed consistency evaluations reached 1,695. This figure accounts for about 2/3 of the chemical drugs commonly used in clinical practice (China, official data from 2020 to 2026)

Set up a one-time family support link on the medical insurance app so that funds in an employee's medical insurance personal account can be used for a spouse, parents, or children's medical visits and medicine purchases
A

Link it once, and the funds in your employee medical insurance personal account can be used for your spouse, parents, or children's medical visits and medicine purchases. If not linked, this money can only be used by you and will remain idle in the account.
Costs no money. On the medical insurance app (China) of the insured location, or at the insurance office, set up a one-time family support link.

Funds in the personal account can be used to pay for the out-of-pocket portion of medical expenses when you and your spouse, parents, or children visit designated medical institutions. They can also be used to pay for the out-of-pocket portion when purchasing drugs, medical devices, and medical supplies at designated retail pharmacies. Documents also propose trialing the use of personal accounts to pay the individual portion of urban and rural resident medical insurance for family members
Drink boiled tap water; do not order bottled water for water dispensers year-round, and do not buy bottled water
C

If a large bottle for a water dispenser costs ⟦20⟧, it is about ⟦1⟧ per liter, which is over 200 times more expensive than Beijing tap water. A household drinking one bottle per week spends over ⟦1000⟧ a year, while the equivalent amount of tap water costs less than ⟦5⟧. Tap water follows mandatory national standards; normally, boiling it for consumption is sufficient.
Buy a kettle. Each boiling takes a little time and a small amount of money for gas or electricity.

The price for the first tier of domestic water in Beijing is ⟦5⟧ per cubic meter, which is ⟦0.005⟧ per liter. A bottle of water for a home dispenser is 18.9 liters; at ⟦20⟧ per bottle, it is about ⟦1.06⟧ per liter, approximately 210 times the price of tap water. A household drinking one bottle per week, or 52 bottles a year, consumes about 983 liters; bottled water costs about ⟦1040⟧, while the equivalent tap water costs about ⟦4.9⟧. Small bottled water at ⟦1⟧ for 500 ml is ⟦2⟧ per liter, 400 times the price of tap water. Domestic water applies the mandatory national standard GB 5749-2022. This standard was released on March 15, 2022, and implemented from April 1, 2023. The regulatory authority is the National Administration of Disease Control and Prevention (China) (China, water prices from 2015 and standards from 2022)
Do not trade stocks constantly; when the market surges or plunges, you should interfere even less
A

In the 1990s, the most active trading American households earned only 11.4% profit per year, while the overall market was at 17.9% during the same period; the difference was mainly due to trading costs. In China, during the 2014–2015 surge and plunge, 85% of households with the smallest accounts traded too much. Compared to just holding steady, they earned ⟦250000000000⟧ less, about three-tenths of their capital.
Costs no money. The difficulty is resisting the urge to act when seeing news or seeing others making money and wanting to jump in with more capital.

This study examined 66,465 household accounts at a US discount brokerage from 1991 to 1996. The most active trading group had an annual return of 11.4%, meaning an average annual profit of 11.4%. During the same period, the overall market was 17.9%, and the average household was 16.4%. An average household had a turnover rate of 75% per year, replacing three-quarters of their stock holdings within a year. The high-trading group and low-trading group differed very little in gross returns (profit before deducting transaction fees). Thus, the gap mainly came from transaction costs paid during trading (USA, 1991 to 1996). China data: the study used daily account data from the Shanghai Stock Exchange, covering all approximately 40 million accounts. The sample period was July 2014 to December 2015, totaling 18 months. During these 18 months, the Shanghai Composite Index first rose over 150%. It peaked at 5,166.35 points on June 12, 2015, then fell 40% by the end of December. Household accounts were divided into four groups based on initial market value. The smallest group accounted for 85% of total household accounts, while the largest group accounted for 0.5%. The total initial stock value of the two groups was similar, at ⟦880000000000⟧ and ⟦808000000000⟧ respectively. The result was that the smallest 85% lost ⟦250000000000⟧ due to active trading, while the largest 0.5% gained ⟦254000000000⟧. "Lost" here is compared to holding steady and doing nothing during that same market cycle. Both figures represent about three-tenths of their respective group's initial stock value, the former being 28% and the latter 31%. For comparison, in the two and a half years before June 2014, the market was quite calm. Taking any 18-month period during that time, the similar gap was only 1% to 3% of the initial value. During this period, the average household account turned over its entire stock holding about every three weeks, nearly 18 times a year (Shanghai, China, 2014 to 2015; control period 2012 to 2014)
Do not borrow money to invest, do not use leverage, and do not buy what you do not understand
B

If you borrow money to buy stocks, once the price drops below a threshold and you cannot provide more funds, the stocks will be forcibly sold. Paper losses immediately become real losses, and there is no chance to "wait for it to go back up." Regulations clearly state that securities traders with less than half a year of experience and average daily assets below ⟦500000⟧ in the last 20 sessions cannot open a margin trading account. This threshold itself shows it is not for ordinary people.
Costs no money. The difficulty is resisting when the market is good; do not think "borrow a bit more to earn more."

Leverage is borrowing money to buy, which magnifies losses. If you use margin trading to buy, the value of the collateral may fall below the maintenance margin ratio. This threshold is set by the brokerage and applied to the assets you have pledged with them. If it falls below the threshold and you do not supplement the collateral in time, a forced liquidation will occur, and the brokerage will sell on your behalf. Paper losses immediately become real losses, with no chance to "wait for it to go back up." Regulations state that customers whose "securities trading time is less than half a year, lack risk tolerance, and average daily securities assets in the last 20 sessions are below ⟦500000⟧" are not allowed to open a credit account. This threshold itself indicates it is not a tool intended for ordinary people (China, 2015)
Use broad index funds instead of actively managed funds for the long-term core portion (money held for a long time without touching)
B

Taken together, the stocks that active funds in the US are buying are very close to the entire market. However, the extra management fees they charge are directly deducted from the returns you receive. Treating fund performance as luck and re-calculating many times for comparison shows that very few funds earn enough extra profit to offset the fees they charge.
Costs no money. The price is that you give up the possibility of "picking a star fund manager." The difficulty is that when the index falls, you must also endure it and not run away midway.

The overall portfolio of active equity funds in the US is similar to the market portfolio: the stocks held by these funds collectively represent almost the entire market. However, the high costs of active management translate directly into lower net returns for investors (returns received after all fees). Research used bootstrap simulations, randomly shuffling performance many times to see what could be achieved by luck alone. The results showed that very few funds generated enough alpha to cover costs: the portion where the fund outperformed the market was not enough to equal the fees it charged (USA, published 2010). S&P Dow Jones Indices statistics once a year: in 2024, 65% of actively managed US large-cap equity funds underperformed the S&P 500. Over 24 years of statistics, an average of 64% underperformed each year. In the 15 years ending in 2024, there was no category where the majority of active funds beat the index
For funds of the same type, prioritize those with lower fees
C

If annual fees are 1 percentage point higher, the money received after 20 years is about 18% less, and after 30 years about 26% less. Choosing low-fee funds within the same category means less of your money is eaten away by these fees.
Costs no money. Before buying, check one more time the total of the three fees: "management fee + custody fee + sales service fee."

Fee differences eat into capital through compounding, meaning the small portion deducted each year accumulates year after year. If the annual fee is 1 percentage point higher, the terminal value after 20 years is about 18.2% less (1 − 0.99^20 ≈ 0.182), and after 30 years about 26% less. Terminal value is the amount remaining in the account at that time. Starting in 2023, China implemented a reform of public fund fees, lowering the fee caps for active equity funds (the type that mainly buys stocks selected by a fund manager). Since July 7, 2023, newly registered funds of this type have management fees of no more than 1.2% and custody fees of no more than 0.2%. 136 fund management companies have lowered these two fees for existing products below those thresholds
Do not put all your money into one stock, one platform, or one house
B

As long as assets do not move perfectly in sync, diversifying your money keeps the average return the same but reduces account fluctuations. Conversely, if you concentrate all your money in one stock, one platform, or one house, if something happens to it, it happens to your entire wealth.
Costs no money. The difficulty is accepting one thing: you will not hit exactly the one that profits the most.

As long as assets do not move perfectly in sync, diversifying money keeps the expected return (average profit level) unchanged, but volatility (account ups and downs) is smaller. This is the fundamental conclusion on portfolio selection presented by Markowitz in 1952, which has been used for decades. Conversely, concentrating all money in one stock or one platform means its variance is your entire variance; you go up and down as much as it does. When something goes wrong, there is no hedge, and no other assets to help you compensate

Before opening a personal pension account, calculate the tax savings and check withdrawal conditions; those who do not pay income tax or only face a 3% tax rate should not contribute just for the tax deduction
A

Contributing the full ⟦12000⟧, if the entire amount stays within the same tax bracket, results in net savings of 840, 2,040, or ⟦3240⟧ for the 10%, 20%, and 30% brackets respectively. These figures already subtract the 3% tax paid upon withdrawal; if the deduction spans two brackets, it must be recalculated. For those in the 3% bracket, the saved tax will be paid back upon withdrawal, at best breaking even. Do not put money here that you might need at any time; early withdrawal is limited to regulated cases such as medical treatment, unemployment, or minimum living allowance.

Opening an account costs no money, but contributed funds cannot be withdrawn at any time. Besides reaching the age to receive basic pension, withdrawals are possible for qualified medical expenses, unemployment, or receiving minimum living allowances; see the Notes for specific thresholds. If conditions are not met, you may still have to wait many years.

Contributions, up to ⟦12000⟧ per year, are deducted from comprehensive income or business income. Investment profits in the account are temporarily exempt from individual income tax; upon withdrawal, they are not included in comprehensive income and are taxed separately at 3%. Tax savings for the year must be calculated by taking the total annual tax before the deduction and subtracting the total annual tax after the deduction. The deduction may push the income into a lower tax bracket, so you cannot always just multiply the current marginal tax rate by the contribution amount. The marginal tax rate is the bracket applied to each additional unit of currency earned. For example, after other deductions are calculated, if the annual taxable comprehensive income before contribution is ⟦40000⟧, the tax due is ⟦1480⟧. After contributing and deducting ⟦12000⟧, the taxable income is ⟦28000⟧, the tax is ⟦840⟧, and ⟦640⟧ less is paid that year. Assuming no investment profit or time value of money, later withdrawing the ⟦12000⟧ principal requires paying ⟦360⟧ in tax, resulting in a net tax difference of ⟦280⟧. You must contribute the full ⟦12000⟧, and the entire deduction must stay within the same tax bracket, to use that bracket's rate to calculate the year's tax savings. Again, considering only the principal and ignoring investment profit and time value, the net tax differences for the 10%, 20%, and 30% brackets are 840, 2,040, and ⟦3240⟧ respectively. These are tax differences occurring at different times and should not be considered an investment return rate, let alone divided directly by the number of years to create an annual yield. Those who do not pay income tax save no tax that year but still pay 3% upon withdrawal. For those already in the 3% bracket, the tax saved that year does not exceed 3% of the contribution. If annual comprehensive income after deductions does not exceed ⟦36000⟧, it falls into this bracket. Considering only the principal and not the time value, this saving does not exceed the tax on the principal withdrawal later; one cannot say it is worthwhile based solely on the tax deduction. Having income tax withheld from a monthly salary does not mean you are in the 10% bracket for the whole year. The annual contribution limit accumulates by calendar year; unused limits do not carry over. The personal pension system (China) has been applied nationwide since December 15, 2024. Starting September 1, 2025, early withdrawals are also allowed for qualified medical expenses, receiving unemployment benefits, or meeting minimum living allowance conditions. If withdrawal conditions are not met, funds cannot be withdrawn at any time, making it unsuitable for an emergency fund needed at any moment (National China).
Pay for the gym per session or short-term, unless you have been going regularly for at least a year
B

In a three-year dataset from the US, members who chose monthly contracts over 70 dollars only went an average of 4.3 times per month, which works out to over 17 dollars per session. Meanwhile, buying a 10-session pass costs only 10 dollars per session. These individuals paid an average of 600 dollars extra during their membership period. Unless you have been going regularly for at least a year, paying per session or buying short-term is more profitable.
Buying per session makes the price per visit slightly more expensive than the average calculated from an annual pass. You must honestly estimate how many times a month you actually go.

This study looked at 3 years of data from 7,752 members at 3 fitness clubs in the US. Members choosing monthly contracts over 70 dollars averaged only 4.3 visits per month, equating to over 17 dollars per visit. Meanwhile, a 10-session pass was only 10 dollars per visit. These individuals paid an average of 600 dollars extra during their membership. Additionally, the rate of members paying monthly for over a year without canceling was 17% higher than those paying annually (US, three-year panel data).
Prepayments must have a written contract; if the seller faces risks and must stop collecting, you have the right to claim the unused balance before they disappear
A

Sellers collecting prepayments from you are required to sign a written contract with you, clearly stating the refund method. If the seller encounters major business problems, they must stop collecting money; if they want to close or relocate, they must notify you in advance. At that point, you can request they continue providing the service or refund the unused balance. Sellers violating these regulations can be fined.
Costs no money. The difficulty is insisting on a written contract right on the spot, not accepting the "just top up first and we'll figure it out later" approach.

Regulations stipulate that sellers collecting prepayments must sign a written contract and agree on the prepayment refund method in the contract. Sellers facing serious business risks must stop collecting prepayments. Sellers deciding to cease business or relocate must notify consumers in advance. Consumers have the right to request continued performance or a refund of the unused balance. Violations can be fined from 1 to 10 times the amount of illegal gains; if there are no illegal gains, the fine is up to ⟦500000⟧.
Wait 24 hours for non-essential large items to cool off; for online purchases, utilize the seven-day unconditional return right
C

What you save are the items you no longer want the next day. For goods purchased online, you can return them without a reason within seven days from the date of receipt. A few types cannot be returned: custom-made items, fresh and perishable goods, opened digital products, and newspapers or magazines.
Costs no money. The item you want to buy will arrive one day later. You usually bear the return shipping fee. The difficulty is resisting the urge to order immediately on the same day.

What is saved is the "no longer wanted the next day" portion of impulse purchases. It is impossible to provide a general ratio for how much this accounts for. For goods purchased online, returns without reason are allowed within seven days of receipt. Four exceptions: custom orders, fresh/perishable goods, opened digital products, newspapers and magazines (China, effective since 2017).
Do not stockpile goods because of "slashed prices" and major promotion periods
C

People's judgment of whether an item is expensive or cheap is anchored by the first number they see, and subsequent adjustments are often insufficient. Therefore, "original price 999, today's price 499" makes you consistently overestimate how cheap it is. According to regulations, the benchmark used to calculate discounts is only the lowest transaction price of that store in the seven days preceding the promotion. The slashed price might not have ever been a real selling price.

Costs no money. The price is that you might skip some genuine discounts. You must remember the regular prices of items you often buy. The difficulty is resisting the urge to stockpile on major promotion days.

Human judgment is anchored by the first number seen, and subsequent adjustments are often insufficient. Therefore, "original price 999, today's price 499" always inflates your estimate of "how much is saved." Regulatory rules: the discount benchmark must be the lowest transaction price of the store itself in the seven days before the promotion. To calculate the discount percentage, the store's actual lowest selling price in the seven days before the promotion must be used as the benchmark. The slashed price may not have ever been a real selling price (China, effective since 2020).
Prioritize purchasing pure protection insurance; treat "premium refunds" and "dividend distributions" as non-guaranteed parts
C

The dividend distribution and premium refund parts are not guaranteed to be paid to you by the insurance company. Introductory materials must print the line "future contract dividends are non-guaranteed benefits" in bold. The extra premiums you pay to get a refund should be viewed as money kept by the insurance company on your behalf; profits are not guaranteed, and withdrawing is not easy.

Pure protection insurance does not return money upon expiration, which might make you feel like "this money is wasted." You must handle saving money yourself. The main difficulty is accepting that this money will not be recovered.

Regulatory requirements demand that introductory materials for dividend-paying products must print in bold the reminder: "future contract dividends are non-guaranteed benefits, dividend distribution is uncertain." Dividend illustrations are calculation tables provided by the insurance company; the interest rate spread used therein is at most 4.5% minus the product's predetermined interest rate. The predetermined interest rate is the fixed yield specified in the contract. Extra premiums for refundable and dividend-paying types are equivalent to savings managed by the insurance company. They do not guarantee profits, have poor liquidity, and are not easy to withdraw (China, effective since 2023).
Buy sufficient third-party liability insurance: mandatory insurance limits are uniform nationwide and not high; your family pays the excess
A

When you are at fault, mandatory insurance (China) pays a maximum of three categories: death and disability ⟦180000⟧, medical expenses ⟦18000⟧, and property damage ⟦2000⟧. The three categories are calculated separately and cannot be transferred. Compensation for hitting and injuring someone can exceed these limits; your family must pay the excess out of pocket, so you must buy sufficient commercial third-party liability insurance.
Commercial third-party liability insurance costs from a few hundred to over ⟦1000⟧ per year. The higher the coverage limit you buy, the cheaper the premium per dollar of insurance becomes.

Mandatory insurance (China) applies a uniform liability limit nationwide. The limit is divided into four separately calculated categories: death and disability, medical expenses, property damage, and compensation when you are not at fault. After the 2020 comprehensive auto insurance reform, the current total limit is ⟦200000⟧. Within this 200,000: death and disability 180,000, medical expenses 18,000, property damage ⟦2000⟧. When you are not at fault: death and disability 18,000, medical expenses 1,800, property damage ⟦100⟧. The portion exceeding the limit is borne by the party causing the damage; the person who hit someone must pay out of pocket. Vehicles without mandatory insurance will be impounded and fined twice the required premium.
Save an emergency fund equal to 3 to 6 months of expenses in a place where it can be withdrawn at any time
C

Keep 3 to 6 months of living expenses in a place where they can be withdrawn immediately. This way, if you lose your job or fall ill, you won't have to take out high-interest loans like credit card minimum payments, nor will you have to sell existing investments at a loss. Bank deposits are protected by deposit insurance, with each bank paying a maximum of ⟦500000⟧.

Costs no money. The price is that this amount must forgo higher returns, being kept only in demand deposits, money market funds, or deposits that can be withdrawn at any time. The difficulty is resisting the urge to touch it while accumulating.

Having an emergency fund means you don't have to borrow or sell investments at a loss when losing a job or falling ill. For annual interest rates on consumer loans and credit card minimum payments, see section 7 of this chapter (do not pay credit card minimums). Bank deposits are protected by deposit insurance, with each bank paying a maximum of ⟦500000⟧ (China, 2015).
Before making an early mortgage repayment, do a comparison calculation; do not act on feeling
C

Repaying a mortgage early is equivalent to definitely earning exactly the interest rate of the loan. So just ask one question: is the long-term stable after-tax profit you can earn higher than the mortgage interest rate? If it is higher, do not rush to repay; if it is not higher or you are unsure, then repay. For equal installments (principal and interest combined are equal each period), interest accounts for the majority in the first few years; the earlier you repay, the more you save. The "early repayment simulation" function in bank apps provides the exact figures immediately.
Costs no money. Takes half an hour to do a calculation. You must honestly estimate the stable after-tax rate of return you can actually earn.

The calculation is as follows. Let the annual mortgage interest rate be r, according to your contract. On August 20, 2026, the Loan Prime Rate (LPR) for terms over 5 years (China) was 3.5%; the actual interest rate is LPR plus or minus a margin. Let g be the annual after-tax profit of another investment you could choose: if this money were put elsewhere, what percentage would it earn on average per year? The guaranteed profit of early repayment is exactly r; every bit repaid early definitely earns r. If g is stably greater than r, keeping the money in the investment is more profitable. If g is smaller than r, or if g is completely uncertain, then early repayment locks in a risk-free return of r. With equal installments, interest makes up the bulk of your payments in the early years, so repaying earlier saves more interest. For this point, check the figures directly using the "early repayment simulation" function in bank apps (China, 2026 interest rates).
When shopping online, trust platform regulations and laws, not livestreamers and "good reviews"
A

If a seller defrauds you, they must compensate three times the amount you paid, with a minimum of ⟦500⟧ if the amount is below that. If the platform knows a seller is violating rules and fails to act, they must provide joint compensation. Deposits are capped at 20% of the contract value; if you break the contract, you lose the deposit; if the seller breaks it, they must pay you double. Livestream rooms creating fake orders or fake reviews must be held accountable; "big data price discrimination against existing customers" is explicitly prohibited.

Costs no money. Before ordering, check the after-sales terms and deposit regulations. After receiving the goods, keep the order records, screenshots of livestream replays, and exchange messages. The difficulty is not getting swept up in the atmosphere created by the livestreamer.

Business operators engaging in deceptive behavior must compensate three times the price, with a minimum of ⟦500⟧. If a platform knows or should know a seller is infringing on rights and fails to act, they bear joint liability; you can demand this compensation directly from the platform. Livestream rooms and livestreamers are not allowed to fake transaction volumes, followers, views, or likes, nor post false information; they bear civil liability for damages. Organizing fake transactions or fake reviews to help others advertise is fined up to ⟦1000000⟧; serious cases are fined ⟦1000000~2000000⟧ and may result in business license revocation. Deposits cannot exceed 20% of the contract value. If you fail to perform the contract, the deposit is not refunded; if the seller fails to perform, they must pay you double. Using personal information for automated decision-making must not involve unreasonable discrimination regarding transaction prices and other conditions; this is what is known as "big data price discrimination against existing customers" (Nationwide, China).
If items bought in a livestream room have problems, first request the platform to provide information on the seller and the livestreamer; the platform is required to provide it
A

When problems arise with goods bought in a livestream room, the most common bottleneck is not knowing who to sue. At that point, you can directly request the platform to provide the information of the livestream room operator and the livestreamer, along with relevant business activity records. The platform is mandatory required to provide this.
Costs no money. Just send a request to the platform.

In consumer disputes, livestream marketing platform operators must, upon consumer request, provide relevant information about the livestream room operator, the livestreamer, and relevant business activity records. The most common difficulty in claiming rights in livestream cases is not finding out who to sue; having this information tells you who to sue.
If you buy unsafe food, you can claim ten times the price in addition to a refund; if the additional compensation is under ⟦1000⟧, it is calculated as 1,000
A

If you buy food that is expired or deteriorated, the item itself, its packaging, and the receipt are your evidence—do not throw them away. You can claim compensation of ten times the price or three times the damages; if it is under ⟦1000⟧, it is calculated as 1,000. You can choose to claim from either the seller or the manufacturer; the party you approach must pay first and cannot push the responsibility to the other side.

No cost. Keep the food, packaging, and receipt; do not throw them away or wash them, and take photos on the spot. First, contact the seller or the platform; if no agreement is reached, call 12315. If you actually have to sue, it takes a few months. The difficulty is resisting the urge to throw the items away beforehand.

If you suffer damages due to food that does not meet food safety standards, you can claim compensation from the business operator or the manufacturer. The party receiving your compensation request applies a first-responsibility system: they must pay first and cannot shirk responsibility. This means whoever you find must pay first and cannot push you to the other party. In addition to claiming damages, you can also demand the other party pay punitive damages of ten times the price or three times the loss, and "if the increased compensation amount is less than ⟦1000⟧, it shall be calculated as ⟦1000⟧". However, there is one exception: "except where the labels or instructions of the food have defects that do not affect food safety and do not mislead consumers." Judicial interpretations (China) further define several points. First, three conditions must be met simultaneously: the buyer purchased for personal or family consumption needs; the food does not meet safety standards; and there is no evidence the buyer knew this at the time of purchase. If met, "the actual price paid shall be used as the basis to calculate punitive compensation of ten times the price." Second, if one clearly knows the standards are not met but still buys to claim compensation, the people's court only accepts it "within the scope of reasonable living consumption needs." For continuous purchases and repeated lawsuits, the total quantity purchased across all instances is summed and judged within that same scope of reasonable living consumption. Third, there are several types of defects for which the court does not accept punitive compensation, provided they do not mislead consumers regarding food safety. These types are: font size not meeting regulations, typos, extra or missing characters, and incorrect formatting of net weight or specifications. For food with no special storage requirements, failure to label storage conditions is also included (National China).
Before buying big-ticket items, check national sampling inspection notices, 3C certification, and energy labels
B

In 2024, China conducted sampling inspections on 25,250 batches of products, with 14.3% failing. E-commerce channels were worse: 7,297 batches inspected, 23.5% failed; physical stores were at 15.1%. Before buying big items, spend a few minutes checking sampling inspection notices, then verify if the 3C certificate is authentic. Goods required to have energy labels must not lack them.
No cost. Takes a few minutes to search on the websites of the State Administration for Market Regulation and the Certification and Accreditation Administration (China).

In 2024, China's national-level supervisory sampling inspections covered 25,250 batches of products, with a failure rate of 14.3%. Among these, 7,297 batches from e-commerce channels were inspected with a failure rate of 23.5%, up 1.8 percentage points from the previous year. Physical stores had 8,055 batches inspected with a failure rate of 15.1%. The authenticity of China Compulsory Certification (3C) can be verified under the "certification results" section on the website of the Certification and Accreditation Administration (China). Energy labels are managed mandatorily according to a product catalog; the label must include the energy efficiency grade, energy efficiency index, and energy information code. Forging, misusing energy labels, or failing to post a required label is penalized under the 节约能源法 (Energy Conservation Law of China) (National China).
Beaded bracelets, jade, luxury watches, and collectibles: count them as "spent money," not "savings"
A

The prices of these items already include a built-in consumption tax (China), with value-added tax calculated separately. Watches priced at ⟦10000⟧ or more per piece are taxed at 20%; gold, silver, platinum, and diamond jewelry at 5%; and other types of jewelry and gemstones at 10%. This tax cannot be recovered when reselling. If you truly like them, buy them as consumption; do not count them as financial management.
No cost. Just do not include "it will appreciate later" as a reason for purchase. The difficulty is resisting the urge to increase the budget because it "holds its value."

First, look at the purchase side. The 《消费税税目税率表》 (Table of Consumption Tax Items and Rates of China) defines rates as follows: "High-end watches" at 20%. Under "precious jewelry and jade/gemstones," gold and silver jewelry, platinum jewelry, diamonds, and diamond jewelry are at 5%. Other precious jewelry and jade/gemstones are at 10%. The scope of "high-end watches" includes "various watches with a sales price (excluding VAT) of ⟦10000⟧ or more per piece." Next, look at the resale side, based on the 《典当管理办法》 (Measures for the Administration of Pawning of China). Article 36: the maximum pawn term shall not exceed 6 months. Article 37 discusses pawn interest, which is the interest on the loan the pawnshop gives you. This is calculated based on the statutory 6-month loan interest rate published by the People's Bank of China, converted according to the pawn term. Interest cannot be deducted in advance from the principal given to you. Article 38: for pawning movables (like watches or jade), the monthly comprehensive fee must not exceed 42‰ of the pawn loan. That is, the additional monthly fee is no more than 4.2% of the loan amount. Real estate mortgages are 27‰, and property rights pledges are 24‰. Article 40: if the item is not redeemed or renewed within 5 days after expiration, it becomes "forfeited pawn" (loss of redemption rights), and the item will no longer wait for you. Article 43: forfeited pawns valued at ⟦30000⟧ or more can be entrusted for auction. Auction proceeds must first cover auction costs and the pawn principal and interest. The remainder is returned to the pawner; if there is a shortfall, the pawner is still liable for the difference (National China). The 消费税暂行条例 (Provisional Regulations on Consumption Tax of China) only stipulates in Article 11 that taxable goods for export are exempt; there is no provision for refunding consumption tax when an individual resells a purchased item.
For jewelry and gemstones, only trust certificates with the CMA mark, and verify the agency on the licensing authority's website
A

Certificates can be forged, so what needs to be verified is the issuing agency. An inspection agency must have recognized qualifications to issue result reports to the public, and the CMA mark must be printed on the report. The licensing authority publishes a list of agencies on its official website; you can check if the agency is on the list yourself. In cases handled by state authorities, some "national inspection certificates" accompanying goods were found to be self-made by hired individuals.
No cost. Before placing an order, check the qualifications of the issuing agency once; a few minutes is enough.

First, look at the regulations, based on the 《检验检测机构资质认定管理办法》 (Measures for the Administration of Qualification Accreditation of Inspection and Testing Institutions of China). Article 2: qualification accreditation is the evaluation and licensing of inspection agencies to "provide data and results to society that have a certifying effect": they are audited first, then granted the qualification to issue papers. Article 15: the qualification accreditation mark consists of two parts: the CMA graphic and the qualification accreditation certificate number. Article 21: agencies providing data and results to the public must print the qualification accreditation mark on the inspection result reports. Article 22: the accreditation authority must publish information on accredited agencies on its official website, clearly stating the status of the certificate. Article 34: providing data and results to the public without legal qualification accreditation results in a fine of ⟦30000⟧. Article 37: forging, altering, or misusing certificates or accreditation marks results in a fine of up to ⟦30000⟧. Next, look at official cases from the "anti-counterfeiting and source cleaning" series in traditional handicraft markets published by the State Administration for Market Regulation (China) on June 4, 2026. One: a livestream room in Donghai, Jiangsu, advertised goods as "natural Grade A, no acid leaching, no treatment, from Myanmar." The livestream also included "national inspection certificates." Re-inspection results showed quartzite (dyed), jadeite (treated), glass, and plastic. Those papers were created by the seller contacting others. Two: in the same county, 469 items suspected of being fake natural quartz were seized; 210 were natural quartz, while 259 were synthetic quartz. Three: a store in Zhenping, Henan, made its own board for livestreaming. The board read "Certified Cooperative Unit of the GIA CMA Zhongyu Jewelry and Jade Appraisal Center." This store also bought 181 compliance labels for the "National Jewelry and Jade Quality Supervision and Inspection Center" online. These labels were sold along with bracelets (National China).
Blind boxes, card draws, and random sales: treat them as "this money will not come back"
A

Sellers must display draw rules, winning probabilities, and limited edition quantities in a conspicuous place, and are not allowed to manipulate results from the system side or have empty boxes. Mechanisms for guaranteed wins and limits on spending or draw frequency are only encouraged by the documents. For blind boxes bought online where the seller has clearly stated terms and you have confirmed them, you cannot use the 7-day no-reason return policy once opened.
No cost. Just set a hard budget before buying. The difficulty is stopping when you haven't drawn the item you want.

The basis is the 《盲盒经营行为规范指引（试行）》 (Guidelines for the Regulation of Blind Box Business Operations (Trial) of China). Article 9 lists a series of key information that must be prominently disclosed to ensure consumers know before buying: product name, category, style, draw rules, product distribution, limited quantities released, winning probabilities, and product value ranges. This same article also stipulates three prohibited actions. First, manipulating the system to change draw results, arbitrarily adjusting probabilities, or other methods to induce disguised consumption. Second, using cash conversion, buybacks, or exchanges to refuse or intentionally delay the delivery of blind boxes. Third, having empty boxes. Article 11 only "encourages" business operators to establish guaranteed win mechanisms and guide rational consumption by setting draw times, spending limits, and draw frequency limits. Article 17 governs blind boxes sold via the Internet. If the operator has fully notified and reminded the consumer, and the consumer has confirmed during that purchase, the 7-day no-reason return policy may not apply once the blind box is opened. Operators must not use default pre-checked boxes to replace the consumer's confirmation step. Article 21: blind boxes must not be used as a pretext for gambling or disguised gambling. Article 23: blind boxes must not be sold to children under 8 years old; sales to minors aged 8 and above must be legally confirmed to have guardian consent (National China).
If you care about what additives are in food, buy pre-packaged versions: bulk counters are not legally required to list ingredients
A

The law only requires pre-packaged food to have an ingredient list; bulk goods do not. Bulk counters only need to list the name, production date, shelf life, and manufacturer. Therefore, "no additives listed" does not mean "none added," it just means the law doesn't require listing them. If you care, buy the pre-packaged version; the ingredient list and additive names are all printed there.
No cost. For the same item, the pre-packaged version is usually slightly more expensive than the bulk version. Checking the ingredient list takes a few seconds.

Article 67 of the 食品安全法 (Food Safety Law of China) stipulates that pre-packaged food packaging must have a label. The label must include nine items. The second item is the "ingredients or raw materials list," and the seventh is the "generic names of food additives used according to national standards." Article 68 has much fewer requirements for bulk food. Original text: food business operators selling bulk food must indicate on the containers or outer packaging of the bulk food the "name of the food, production date or production batch number, shelf life, as well as the name, address, and contact information of the producer/operator, and other contents." This article does not mention an ingredient list or additives. Frozen seafood is where this difference is most apparent. GB 2760—2024 (China) allows the use of phosphoric acid and phosphate salts as humectants in frozen seafood, commonly called water-retaining agents. The maximum usage is 5.0 g/kg, calculated as phosphate. Usage within this limit is legal. The issues are excessive use and ice glazing to increase weight. In 2025, after CCTV's 3.15 program exposed peeled shrimp "containing excessive water-retaining agents (compound phosphates) against regulations and ice glazing to increase weight," market regulators required enterprises that "product labels must clearly state the water-retaining agent ingredients (such as phosphates), net weight (excluding the weight of the ice layer), and the ingredient list" (National China, Food Safety Law of China third revision 2025, effective from December 1, 2025).
Sell losing stocks according to pre-set rules; do not rely on buying more as the price drops to average down and recover
A

People often sell when they have a profit and hold when they have a loss. In a seven-year record of ten thousand accounts in the US, winning stocks were over fifty percent more likely to be sold than losing stocks. That same group also preferred buying more of their losing stocks. However, the losing stocks they kept still underperformed the winning stocks they sold by an average of 3.4 percentage points in the following year.
No cost. The difficulty is admitting the position is at a loss and then selling it.

This study examined the entire transaction history of 10,000 accounts at a US discount brokerage from 1987 to 1993. The Proportion of Gains Realized (PGR) was 0.148. The Proportion of Losses Realized (PLR) was 0.098. The difference between the two is 0.050, with a t-value over 35. On a daily basis, winning stocks were 50% or more likely to be sold than losing stocks. These same accounts were more aggressive in buying more of their losing stocks. The rate of buying more of a losing stock was 0.135, compared to 0.094 for winning stocks, with a t-value of 19. The study also tested the idea that "holding on will lead to a recovery." The result was the opposite: the average excess return in the following year for sold winning stocks was 3.4 percentage points higher than for the losing stocks held. Excess return is the portion earned above the market index. The author also calculated an example based on averages: for every $1,000 of stock sold, selling the loser instead of the winner resulted in a return about 4.4% higher one year later. This 4.4% includes tax savings from selling losing stocks early to offset taxes. The tax deduction part is based on the US tax system (USA, 1987 to 1993).
To buy overseas assets like US stocks, use QDII funds or Hong Kong Stock Connect; do not open accounts with foreign brokerages or use the annual foreign exchange quota
A

Foreign brokerages like Tiger, Futu, and Longbridge are no longer allowed to open accounts for domestic residents (China) as of May 2026. Existing accounts are only permitted to sell and transfer funds back within two years, with no further buying allowed. The foreign exchange quota also cannot be used to buy overseas stocks; violators will be barred from using the quota for that year and the following 2 years. To buy overseas assets, use QDII funds or Hong Kong Stock Connect.
No cost. Buying QDII funds directly in your bank or brokerage app takes a few minutes. The trade-off is fewer products to choose from compared to foreign brokerages.

On May 22, 2026, eight agencies including the Securities Regulatory Commission, Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, Ministry of Public Security, People's Bank, State Administration for Market Regulation, National Financial Regulatory Administration, Cyberspace Administration of China, and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (China) issued the "Implementation Plan for the Comprehensive Rectification of Illegal Cross-border Securities, Futures, and Fund Business Activities." The general requirement is to "completely eliminate the illegal cross-border business activities of foreign securities, futures, and fund institutions through 2 years of concentrated rectification." Foreign organizations are prohibited from marketing to or soliciting domestic customers, and from "providing transaction services such as account opening, order processing, and fund transfers." For those who have already opened accounts, the plan states: "foreign organizations are prohibited from illegally providing existing domestic investors with services such as buy transactions or fund inflows; only one-way sell transactions and fund outflows are permitted." After two years, "domestic websites, trading software, and associated servers shall be completely shut down." On the same day, the Securities Regulatory Commission (China) announced plans to confiscate all illegal income from relevant domestic and foreign entities of Tiger, Futu, and Longbridge, and impose strict penalties according to law. The accompanying Q&A stated it would "guide domestic investors to invest overseas through legal channels such as Hong Kong Stock Connect, qualified domestic institutional investors (QDII), and cross-border Wealth Management Connect." Regarding foreign exchange, the "Personal Foreign Exchange Purchase Application" from the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (China) clearly states that purchased personal foreign exchange "shall not be used for unopened capital account items such as purchasing overseas real estate, securities investment, purchasing life insurance or investment-type return/dividend insurance." Violators are placed on a "watch list," "will not enjoy the personal convenience quota for that year and the following 2 years," and face administrative penalties, anti-money laundering investigations, and inclusion in personal credit records (National China, from May 2026).
Only buy insurance for losses you cannot afford; for losses you can afford, let an emergency fund handle them
C

The insurance premiums you pay are not fully returned; a portion must cover the insurance company's costs and profits. Therefore, what is worth buying is coverage for losses that rarely occur but would be unaffordable if they did, such as serious illness, injuring someone in a car accident, or the death of the household breadwinner. Small losses that your savings can cover should be handled by an emergency fund.
No cost. What needs to be done is to list the major potential losses your family might face and see which ones savings cannot cover. Takes half an hour each time.

Only a portion of the premiums collected by the company is paid out as compensation. The remainder covers sales costs, operations, and company profit. Regulators (China) require companies selling individual short-term health insurance to publish their "comprehensive loss ratio" on their official websites every half year. This is roughly the ratio of compensation paid to premiums collected; if you want to know how much a company pays out, check their website. Therefore, for any type of loss, buying insurance is, on average, a small financial loss in the long run. In exchange, a large expense that could crush a family is converted into a small annual payment. The smaller the loss and the more affordable it is for you, the less worthwhile this exchange becomes. Based on this standard, the types mentioned in the book are worth buying: one-year medical insurance (see Chapter 7, Section 20), auto insurance (see Section 26 of this chapter on third-party liability), overseas travel (see Chapter 21, Section 4 on overseas medical), and if someone depends on your income, see Section 40 of this chapter on term life insurance (National China, since 2021).
If someone depends on your income, buy term life insurance for the breadwinner first; do not buy it for the child first
C

Term life insurance only covers a fixed number of years; if the insured person passes away during these years, the family receives a sum of money. It is meant for dependents who rely on your income, such as for an unpaid mortgage or young children. If no one depends on you, it is not needed. Children do not earn income, and the law even limits the payout amount for life insurance bought for children.

A few hundred to a few thousand yuan per year, depending on age, coverage amount, and insurance term (author's rough estimate, no official figures). You must honestly disclose your health status before buying, which takes half an hour each time.

The regulatory definition of life insurance (China) is: personal insurance that uses a person's lifespan as the object of insurance, divided into term life, whole life, endowment insurance, etc. Term life insurance uses the death of the insured as the condition for payment, with a fixed insurance term. Whole life insurance covers the entire lifespan. Accident insurance only pays for death or disability caused by accidents; it does not pay for death due to illness, so it cannot replace life insurance. Contracts using death as a condition for payment must be agreed to by the insured person themselves, including the coverage amount, otherwise the contract is void. Parents buying death insurance for minor children are not restricted by this, but the total insurance payout for a child's death cannot exceed the limits set by the regulatory authority. Life insurance coverage is usually in the range of several hundred thousand yuan, so the benefit is ranked as large. There is no official formula for how much coverage to buy. The author's calculation method is: remaining mortgage debt, plus the child's expenses until adulthood, plus several years of living expenses (National China, revised 2015).
If you regret signing a personal insurance contract for over one year, canceling it during the cooling-off period allows for a near-full refund of premiums
A

Personal insurance policies with a term of over one year all have a cooling-off period. For those purchased at a bank, it is 15 days from the date of receiving the contract; canceling during this time incurs a maximum deduction of ⟦10⟧ for paperwork fees. If canceled after the cooling-off period, you only get back the cash value specified in the contract, which is usually less than the amount paid. When the insurance company calls to verify your understanding, do not say you understand if you are still unclear.

Zero cost. Call the insurance company's hotline or visit the counter; it takes about fifteen minutes. The difficulty lies in staying calm enough to read through the contract once within 15 days of signing.

For personal insurance with a term of over one year, the regulatory authority (China) requires the cooling-off period to be clearly stated, including its start date and duration. The rights of the policyholder during this period must also be explicitly listed. Long-term health insurance must have a cooling-off period of no less than 15 days. For insurance purchased at banks with a term of over one year, contracts uniformly set a 15-day cooling-off period. This is calculated in calendar days starting from the date you receive the contract and sign the written acknowledgment. The cover of such contracts must print the reminder: "Within 15 days after receiving the insurance contract, you have the right to cancel and receive a full refund of premiums (minus paperwork fees not exceeding ⟦10⟧). Canceling after 15 days will result in a loss." After the cooling-off period, you can still terminate the contract at any time. The insurance company must return the cash value of the contract (the refundable portion per the agreement) within 30 days. Risk warnings from the financial regulatory authority (China) state that the cash value for long-term personal insurance canceled after the cooling-off period is usually lower than the total premiums paid. For new personal insurance contracts over one year, the insurance company must make a follow-up call during the cooling-off period. The call must confirm whether you are aware of the losses incurred upon cancellation and your rights during the cooling-off period (Nationwide China, since 2010, 2019).
Before signing at a bank counter, clearly identify whether the product in your hand is a deposit or insurance
B

Banks are permitted to sell insurance on behalf of companies but are forbidden from misrepresenting it as a deposit. The cover of an insurance contract must print "Insurance Contract" and the name of the insurance company in large font; words like "deposit" or "savings" are prohibited. If the cover lists an insurance company, the money is not a deposit, and canceling after the cooling-off period will result in a loss. In principle, individuals over 65 buying at a bank should only purchase products with fixed benefits.
Zero cost. Spend two extra minutes looking at the contract cover before signing.

Regulations (China) explicitly state that banks must not bundle insurance with savings deposits, funds, or bank wealth management products for sale. Insurance returns must not be simply compared to deposit interest, and uncertain returns must not be described as guaranteed. Insurance documents and promotional materials must not use the bank's name or logo, nor contain terms like "deposit," "savings," or "launched jointly with the bank." The contract cover must print "Insurance Contract" in a font size no smaller than size 72, and the insurance company's name in a font size no smaller than size 2. For three types of buyers, products with fixed contract benefits should, in principle, be the only ones sold: policyholders over 65; those over 60 buying periodic premium products; and those whose declared annual income is lower than the local average per capita disposable income. Contracts for these three types of people must also be sent back to the insurance company for manual underwriting and cannot be automatically issued at the transaction point. Insurance company employees are not allowed to sell insurance within bank transaction areas. Insurance over one year sold through banks has a 15-day cooling-off period; canceling after this period results in a loss (Nationwide China, since October 2019).
To cancel insurance, contact the insurance company yourself; do not use "surrender assistance" services; call 12378 to complain if misled
B

Online advertisements claiming "full refund for insurance cancellation" are flagged as false information by regulators. These "assistance" services take 30% to 50% of the refund and collect your bank cards, SIM cards, and home address. Canceling insurance also means losing coverage. If you feel misled, first contact the insurance company's hotline; if no agreement is reached, call 12378, which is completely free.
Zero cost. Call the hotline or visit the counter yourself; it requires one or two more trips compared to using an intermediary.

In February 2026, the National Financial Regulatory Administration, the Cyberspace Administration of China, the Ministry of Public Security, the People's Bank of China, and the China Securities Regulatory Commission jointly issued a risk warning. The warning stated that claims like "full refund for insurance cancellation" are false information and inconsistent with the 保险法 (Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China) and other laws. Those providing "rights protection assistance" charge high service fees, and if you try to withdraw midway, you may be sued for "breach of contract." They also collect SIM cards, bank cards, insurance contracts, home addresses, and children's schools... This information is resold, potentially leading to phone scams and unauthorized withdrawals. A warning from the Ningxia Financial Regulatory Bureau (China) in June 2026 provided more detail. These intermediaries agree to charge an agency fee of 30% to 50% of the refund upon success, with high penalties for quitting. They teach people to fabricate reasons like being misled during the sale or forged signatures to file complaints. Those who follow this may violate the 治安管理处罚法 (Law of the People's Republic of China on Penalties for Administration of Public Security), and in serious cases, may be suspected of being accomplices in crimes of malicious accusation or extortion. Once insurance is canceled, the coverage terminates immediately. Buying the same type of insurance later may result in higher premiums or rejection due to increased age or diagnosed illnesses. If truly misled, first complain and negotiate with the official hotline of the insurance company; if no agreement is reached, call 12378, the consumer rights protection hotline for banking and insurance, which is free. If you temporarily cannot afford premiums, ask the insurance company first about services like reducing the sum insured and stopping premiums, or taking a policy loan. Reducing the sum insured and stopping premiums means no further payments are made, and the sum insured is lowered proportionally (Nationwide China, 2026).
Designate a specific person as the beneficiary in insurance contracts and remember to claim the money: 5 years for life insurance, 2 years for others
A

If no beneficiary is named, or if the beneficiary dies first, the insurance money becomes part of the estate and must be used to pay the deceased's debts first. If a beneficiary is listed as "wife is..." and you later divorce, it is treated as if no one was named. Family members must know about the contract: life insurance must be claimed within 5 years of knowing about the event, and other insurance within 2 years.
Zero cost. Fill it out once when purchasing; if you want to change the beneficiary later, notify the insurance company in writing.

The 保险法 (Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China) stipulates that the beneficiary is designated by the insured or the policyholder. If designated by the policyholder, the insured's consent is required. There are three cases where insurance money is treated as the insured's estate and distributed according to inheritance rules. First, no beneficiary is designated, or the designation is unclear. Second, the beneficiary dies before the insured, and there is no other beneficiary. Third, the beneficiary loses or waives the right to the benefit according to law, and there is no other beneficiary. If the beneficiary and the insured die in the same event and the order of death cannot be determined, it is presumed the beneficiary died first. Funds counted as an estate must first pay taxes and debts of the deceased before the remainder is distributed. Interpretations by the Supreme People's Court (China) clarify: if a beneficiary is listed in the format of "name plus personal relationship" and the relationship has changed at the time of the event, it is treated as if no beneficiary was designated. Changing a beneficiary without notifying the insurance company is not effective against the company. The statute of limitations for claiming funds is 5 years for life insurance and 2 years for other insurance, both calculated from the date the event was known or should have been known. Life insurance amounts are often several hundred thousand RMB, so the interest level is ranked as high (Nationwide China, amended 2015, since 2021).
Do not spend money on cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin or USDT, and do not join others in investing: transactions are not protected by law, and losses cannot be recovered through lawsuits
A

China does not recognize cryptocurrency as legal tender; individual coin purchase transactions may be declared void, and losses are borne by the individual. Someone spent approximately ⟦448000⟧ to buy USDT from another person, and when the platform failed to withdraw funds, the court dismissed the lawsuit for recovery. Theft is a different matter; someone who stole coins was convicted of theft and sentenced to 7 years in prison.
Zero cost. Do not buy coins, and do not join "signal-leading" or "guaranteed profit" coin groups. The trade-off is missing out when coin prices rise.

In February 2026, the People's Bank of China and seven other agencies (China) issued Notice No. 42 of 2026 (China). The notice clearly states that cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin, Ether, and USDT "do not have legal tender status, should not and cannot be circulated or used as currency in the market." Exchanging RMB for coins, exchanging coins for coins, and issuing coins for fundraising are all illegal financial activities and are "strictly prohibited." Foreign organizations are also prohibited from providing these services to domestic residents. Regarding individual investors, the original text of the notice is: "any unit or individual investing in virtual currencies, asset-backed tokens, and related financial products that violate public order and good customs shall have the relevant civil transaction declared void, and losses arising therefrom shall be borne by the individual." Notice No. 237 of 2021 was simultaneously repealed, but this sentence was retained in the new notice. Court case: from February 2018 to July 2019, Mr. Tang bought USDT from two people claiming to be platform merchants, paying approximately ⟦448000⟧ (exactly 448,000). Later, the platform could not withdraw funds or be logged into. He sued to recover the money. The court held that using RMB to exchange for virtual currency is a void investment behavior, and the loss is borne by himself. The court dismissed the lawsuit, and the appeal upheld the verdict (Yixing, Jiangsu, published March 2025). Theft is different. A "hacker" stole virtual currency worth over ⟦4000000⟧ from an account; one of the thieves was convicted of theft, sentenced to 7 years, and fined ⟦20000⟧ (Zhengzhou, Henan).

For those without an employer, paying for employee pension insurance: paying at the lowest level and for the minimum years is most profitable; do not assume any payment is profitable, as even the lowest level takes about 10 years of collection to break even
A

For individuals without an employer paying for employee pension insurance (China), paying at the lowest level for the minimum required years is the most profitable. A large part of the pension received follows the local average salary of the retirement year. Based on the salary levels at that time, paying at the lowest level for 15 years and collecting from age 60 takes about 10 years to break even; additional payments at higher levels require about 17 years. It is worth paying, but not every payment is equally profitable.

The individual pays the full amount, which is 20% of the contribution base; the lowest monthly payment ranges from several hundred to over a thousand RMB. Payments must be made on time for at least 15 years, a requirement that will gradually increase to 20 years starting from 2030. If the minimum years are not met by retirement, this money cannot be withdrawn.

How to pay and how to receive are clearly stated in a 2005 State Council (China) decision. Individuals without an employer who pay themselves (officially called flexible employment workers) pay 20% of the contribution base, of which 8% is recorded in a personal account. Since 2019, the contribution base can be self-selected within a range of 60% to 300% of the average salary of all urban unit employees in the province. The pension after retirement is divided into two parts. The first part is the basic pension. It takes the average monthly salary of local employees in the previous year, adds your own average contribution salary, divides by 2, and grants 1% for each year of contribution. The second part is the personal account pension, which is the money in the account divided by the number of months for calculation. For retirement at age 60, the number of months is 139; at age 55, it is 170; the later the retirement, the fewer the months. Below is a self-calculation example based on the formula, not official figures. Assume the local average monthly salary in the year of retirement is ⟦8000⟧, and both types of average salaries are calculated as the same number. All amounts below are adjusted to the salary level of the retirement year, with personal account interest exactly matching the rate of salary increase. Paying at the lowest level of 60%, the contribution base is ⟦4800⟧, and the monthly payment is ⟦960⟧. 15 years of contributions total approximately ⟦173000⟧ (exactly 172,800). From age 60, the monthly collection is about ⟦1457⟧: basic pension of 960, personal account pension of about 497. One year is about ⟦17500⟧ (exactly about 17,487), requiring about 9.9 years to break even, i.e., collecting until about age 70. Paying at the 100% level, 15 years of contributions total approximately ⟦288000⟧ (exactly 288,000), with a monthly collection of about ⟦2029⟧. The portion paid above the lowest level is about ⟦115000⟧ (exactly 115,200), but only yields an additional ⟦572⟧ per month, requiring about 16.8 years to break even. The reason is that half of the basic pension is based on the local average salary regardless of how much you pay, benefiting those who pay less. At the lowest level, each additional year of payment keeps the break-even period at about 9.9 years, which is more profitable than raising the contribution level. At the lowest level, the basic pension makes up the bulk of the amount received. This break-even period does not depend on whether local salaries are high or low.
