The recommended intake in China is 800 mg daily for those aged 18 to 49, 1,000 mg for those 50 and older, with an upper limit of 2,000 mg daily. Medical standards setting these figures also state that excessive long-term calcium intake increases the risk of kidney stones. A US trial of 36,282 postmenopausal women taking 1,000 mg of calcium and 400 IU of vitamin D daily, followed for an average of 7 years, found a 17% higher risk of kidney stones (HR = 1.17, 95% CI 1.02 to 1.34). Hip fractures were 12% lower but not statistically significant (HR = 0.88, 0.72–1.08). It seems worthwhile because of the intuition that "bones are made of calcium, so eating more calcium makes bones grow faster."
Do not rely on AI chatbots for self-diagnosis or legal matters; before seeing a doctor, litigating, or spending large sums, find and cross-check the original source documents they cite
A

If you provide a full medical record to an AI, it identifies the disease in over nine out of ten cases. However, when ordinary people use it to ask about symptoms, fewer people identify the disease than those who search the internet themselves, and it is no better at judging whether to go to the ER. Regarding legal matters, at least 58% of answers from general-purpose AI contain fabrications, and it often agrees with incorrect premises in your questions.

Zero cost. Each cross-check takes a few minutes to half an hour. Ask the AI to write out the specific law, guideline, or article it is based on, then open the original text yourself to find that sentence. The habit to change: do not follow its advice just because it speaks with certainty.

First, regarding medical diagnosis: In 2026, Nature Medicine published a randomized trial with 1,298 laypeople in the UK using a pre-registered protocol. Each person received two hypothetical cases and had to diagnose the disease and decide whether to go to the ER or monitor at home. Some used AI chatbots (GPT-4o, Llama 3, Command R+). The control group used their usual methods, mostly searching the web or the UK National Health Service (NHS) website. When the full case was given directly to the AI, it identified the relevant disease in 94.9% of cases and correctly judged where to seek care in 56.3%. When laypeople used the same AI, they identified the disease in less than 34.5% of cases and correctly judged where to seek care in less than 44.2%. The control group was 1.76 times more likely to identify the relevant disease than the AI users (95% CI 1.45 to 2.13). They were 1.57 times more likely to recognize severe diseases with red flags (1.28–1.92). Regarding where to seek care, both groups were nearly identical. The authors reviewed the transcripts and found two issues: users did not describe symptoms adequately, and the AI mentioned the correct disease but the users did not follow it. Next, regarding legal matters: A 2024 US research group used ChatGPT-4 and other public models to ask about US federal court precedents. ChatGPT-4 had fabrications in 58% of its answers; Llama 2 reached 88%. Fabrication means the content does not match legal facts, referred to in the paper as "hallucinations." The models cannot distinguish which of their own sentences are fabricated. When a user's question contains a false legal premise, the AI often accepts it. In 2025, the same group tested professional legal AI tools for lawyers. These tools claimed not to hallucinate, but in reality, 17% to 33% of their answers contained fabrications. It seems worthwhile because AI is always available, free, and speaks as confidently as a doctor or lawyer.
Do not fail to save money because "one could die at any time, so it is better to spend it all early"; about nine out of ten thirty-year-olds will live to sixty
B

According to World Health Organization figures for China, about 92% of thirty-year-olds live to sixty, and more than half live to eighty. Young people often overestimate their chance of dying young; living by that feeling results in saving about one-quarter less than they should. Based on these figures, most people need to save for when they live to old age.

Zero cost. What needs to be done is when the thought "who knows when I might die" arises, first consider the probability of living to sixty. The difficulty lies in the fact that everyone around you says the same thing, and the item you want to buy is right in front of you.

First, regarding life expectancy: The World Health Organization's Global Health Observatory calculated the 2023 life table for China. A life table estimates how long a group of people will live based on age-specific mortality rates in that year. According to this table, a 30-year-old has a 92.0% probability of living to age 60 (males 89.2%, females 94.9%). The probability of living to age 65 is 87.4% (males 83.0%, females 92.0%). Living to age 80 is 55.6% (males 45.8%, females 66.1%). These three sets of numbers are calculated by dividing the number of survivors at those ages in the table. People who live to age 65 live an average of 17.5 more years. Next, regarding self-estimation: A 2019 study in The Journal of Finance used a questionnaire to ask people to estimate how long they would live. The result was that young people underestimated their probability of survival, while the elderly overestimated it. An earlier working paper of the article gave an example: a 28-year-old male has a 99.4% actual probability of living another 5 years, but he estimated it at 92.8%. The authors plugged self-estimated probabilities into a standard model of "life-cycle saving and spending." Compared to calculations based on actual mortality rates, young people saved 26% less, and retirees spent their savings 27% slower. In the questionnaire, the more someone's estimate deviated from reality, the more their saving behavior deviated, even after controlling for risk appetite, cognitive ability, and family conditions. The authors suggested one reason is that people overemphasize rare, vivid types of death.

Do not undergo arthroscopic cleaning or meniscus resection for gradual knee pain in middle-aged or elderly people (osteoarthritis, degenerative meniscus tears); first, lose weight and strengthen thigh muscles
A

For middle-aged and elderly people with knee pain due to degeneration, arthroscopic cleaning or meniscus resection is no better than sham surgery. Sham surgery involves only skin incisions, yet those who received it reported pain and mobility nearly identical to those who had real surgery. The maximum benefit lasts only a few months and can cause blood clots in the legs. Persistent leg exercises help reduce knee pain; overweight individuals who lose weight see even more relief.

Saves the cost of surgery and avoids 2 to 6 weeks of post-operative recovery. What is needed is long-term strengthening of thigh and gluteal muscles several times a week, ideally after a lesson from a rehabilitation doctor or physical therapist. Overweight individuals must also eat less and move more to lose weight. The difficulty is that exercise and weight loss take a long time to show results, while surgery sounds like a one-time fix.

First, regarding osteoarthritis: In 2002, a trial divided 180 patients with knee osteoarthritis into three groups: arthroscopic debridement, arthroscopic lavage, and sham surgery. Sham surgery involved only skin incisions without inserting the endoscope. Neither patients nor evaluators knew who received which procedure. At every follow-up over two years, pain and function in the two real surgery groups were no better than the sham group. Knee pain was scored from 0 to 100, with higher scores indicating more pain. At the one-year mark, the sham group scored 48.9, the lavage group 54.8, and the debridement group 51.7. In 2008, another trial took 178 people with moderate to severe knee osteoarthritis. One group received arthroscopic debridement plus physical therapy and medication. The other group received only physical therapy and medication. Total symptom scores ranged from 0 to 2,400, with higher scores being more severe. After two years, the groups scored 874 vs. 897, a difference of 23 points (95% CI -208 to 161), which was not significant. Next, regarding the meniscus: In 2013, a trial in Finland involved 146 people aged 35 to 65 with symptomatic degenerative medial meniscus tears and no osteoarthritis. One group had partial meniscectomy, and the other had sham surgery. At 12 months, the three primary scores did not differ. For example, knee pain after exercise (0 to 10 scale) decreased by 3.1 and 3.3 points, respectively. In 2015, a meta-analysis of 9 trials found that surgery patients at 3 to 6 months had 3 to 5 points less pain (0 to 100 scale). By 1 to 2 years, there was no difference, and function did not improve. Next, regarding harms: Symptomatic deep vein thrombosis in the leg occurred in approximately 4.13 per 1,000 surgeries (1.78–9.60). There are also risks of pulmonary embolism, infection, and death. In 2017, an international expert panel organized by the British Medical Journal (BMJ) strongly opposed arthroscopy for almost everyone with knee degeneration. The panel noted that recovery takes 2 to 6 weeks. Finally, regarding what to do: In 2016, a trial in Norway took 140 middle-aged people with degenerative meniscus tears. One group did 12 weeks of supervised exercise, and the other had partial meniscectomy. After two years, knee scores differed by only 0.9 points (-4.3 to 6.1), showing no difference. The exercise group had stronger thigh muscles at month 3. A 2015 Cochrane systematic review of 44 trials and 3,537 people found that exercise reduced knee pain by an equivalent of 12 points (0 to 100 scale, 95% CI 10 to 15), with high-quality evidence. Pain reduction remained at 6 points two to six months after stopping exercise. In 2013, a US trial of 454 overweight or obese people over 55 with knee osteoarthritis found that those on a diet plus exercise lost an average of 10.6 kg (11.4% of body weight). At 18 months, their pain score (0 to 20) was 3.6, while the exercise-only group was 4.7. It seems worthwhile because "cleaning out worn or torn parts" sounds like it addresses the cause, and many people do feel better after surgery.
Do not rely on melatonin to cure chronic insomnia; on average, it only helps you fall asleep about 7 minutes faster; try cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia first
A

For poor sleepers, melatonin on average only helps them fall asleep about 7 minutes faster than a placebo and stay asleep for about 8 minutes longer. The American Academy of Sleep Medicine does not recommend it for treating chronic insomnia. In China, it is sold as a dietary supplement with labels stating "this product cannot replace medicine." However, it can reduce jet lag when flying across 5 or more time zones.

Zero cost; it also saves money on long-term melatonin purchases. The difficulty is that it is available everywhere, and taking a pill is much less hassle than going to a hospital for several weeks of treatment.

First, regarding the extent of the effect: In 2013, a meta-analysis synthesized 19 trials involving 1,683 people. Every trial was randomized and placebo-controlled. Participants' sleep disorders were not caused by other diseases; 14 of these trials studied insomnia. Melatonin users shortened their sleep onset latency by an average of 7.06 minutes (95% CI 4.37 to 9.75). Total sleep time increased by 8.25 minutes (1.74–14.75). Sleep quality also improved very slightly (SMD 0.22; 0.12–0.32). The authors explicitly stated that this reduction in sleep onset time is less than that of other sleeping pills. Next, regarding guidelines: In 2017, the American Academy of Sleep Medicine issued clinical practice guidelines for the pharmacological treatment of chronic insomnia. The guidelines advised clinicians against using melatonin for sleep onset or maintenance insomnia, with a "weak" recommendation. This was based on 3 trials, all using 2 mg of slow-release melatonin in participants over 55. The quality of evidence was rated "very low." Only one sleep quality index could be pooled (SMD 0.21; -0.36 to 0.77), which did not reach clinical significance. In China, dietary supplements containing melatonin list their function as "helping to improve sleep." The precautions state "this product cannot replace medicine," and it should not be used by children, adolescents, pregnant women, or breastfeeding women. A 2026 public education article from the Beijing Municipal Administration for Market Regulation (China) also stated it is "absolutely not a 'miracle drug'." Jet lag is different: A Cochrane systematic review of 10 trials found that in 9 of them, taking melatonin near local bedtime after flying across 5 or more time zones reduced jet lag. Doses of 0.5 to 5 mg were similarly effective. It seems worthwhile because it is a naturally occurring hormone, sounds gentle, and does not require a prescription.
Do not demand IV fluids for common colds or fevers, and do not get IV fluids during seasonal changes to "cleanse" or "clear" blood vessels
C

The common cold and viral pharyngitis are classified by the Guangdong Provincial Health Commission (China) as diseases that, in principle, do not require IV fluids. At a National Health Commission (China) press conference, experts debunked the idea: IV fluids during seasonal changes cannot wash away atherosclerotic plaques and may worsen the burden on the heart and kidneys. In national adverse drug reaction reports (China), over half occur with injectable drugs, nine-tenths of which are intravenous.

Zero cost; it also saves the expense of the IV and several hours spent at the clinic. The difficulty is that many people feel an IV makes them recover faster, and some elderly people are accustomed to getting seasonal IVs; a doctor refusing an IV may seem like they are not performing a thorough examination.

Since no studies have specifically compared IV fluids to no IV fluids for the common cold, this section relies on official documents and monitoring data. First, regarding the common cold: In 2017, the Health and Family Planning Commission of Guangdong Province (China) issued a document requiring primary healthcare institutions to reduce unnecessary IV fluids. The document explicitly stated that medication should follow the World Health Organization's principle: "do not inject if you can take it orally; do not use IV if you can use intramuscular injection." Intravenous infusion is only for three cases: 1. Difficulty swallowing. 2. Severe absorption obstacles, such as vomiting or severe diarrhea. 3. Critical, rapidly progressing illness requiring high drug concentrations quickly. The document included a table of common outpatient and emergency diseases that, in principle, do not require IV fluids. The first item under internal medicine was "upper respiratory tract infection: common cold, viral pharyngitis." Next, regarding "cleansing blood vessels": On August 6, 2025, the National Health Commission (China) held a press conference. A chief physician from Dongfang Hospital, Beijing University of Chinese Medicine, debunked this rumor. The quote was: "the claim that seasonal IV fluids can clear blood vessels and prevent cerebral infarction is a false argument." IV fluids cannot "wash away" or "clear" atherosclerotic plaques. Arbitrary IV fluids can worsen the burden on the heart or kidneys, even causing heart failure. Finally, regarding risks: The National Adverse Drug Reaction Monitoring Annual Report (China, 2024) categorized reports by route of administration. Among reported adverse reactions, injections accounted for 57.2%, and oral administration for 33.1%. Within injections, intravenous administration accounted for 91.0%. This is the composition of reports, not the probability of an event occurring per infusion. It seems worthwhile because the IV bag is visible and the process takes time, making people feel the medicine enters faster and more completely.
If you lose your job, apply for unemployment benefits online first
A

If your company and you have contributed for at least 1 year, you did not quit voluntarily, you have registered as unemployed, and you are looking for work, you are eligible for payments. Contributing for 1 to less than 5 years grants a maximum of 12 months; 5 to less than 10 years grants a maximum of 18 months; 10 years or more grants a maximum of 24 months. While receiving benefits, the unemployment insurance fund pays for your employee medical insurance on your behalf.

Zero cost. Apply via smartphone through three channels: the "12333 in Hand" app, the electronic social security card mini-app in WeChat or Alipay, or the National Social Security Public Service Platform (China). It can be done with a social security card or ID card; in most places, there is no need to go to a counter. The prerequisite is having completed unemployment registration.

Three conditions must be met simultaneously. First, the company and you must have cumulative unemployment insurance contributions for at least 1 year. Second, you must not have quit voluntarily (legally termed "loss of employment not due to one's own will"). Third, you must have registered as unemployed and intend to find work. The duration of benefits depends on the years of contribution: 1 to less than 5 years allows a maximum of 12 months; 5 to less than 10 years allows a maximum of 18 months; 10 years or more allows a maximum of 24 months. The monthly amount is determined by provincial governments and varies by province. This level is lower than the local minimum wage but higher than the urban minimum living allowance. The state's goal is to gradually raise it to 90% of the minimum wage. While receiving unemployment benefits, you still participate in basic medical insurance for employees and enjoy basic medical insurance benefits. The required medical insurance premiums are paid from the unemployment insurance fund; you do not pay them (National, regulations in effect since 1999).
If you are owed wages, complain to the labor inspectorate first, then apply for labor arbitration; both routes are free, and most cases yield results within a few months
A

First, call 12333 or go to the human resources and social security department (China) to file a complaint with the labor inspectorate; once accepted, the investigation must be completed within 60 working days. If wages are indeed owed, the agency can compel the company to pay within a deadline; failure to pay results in an additional penalty of 50% to 100%. If that fails, apply for labor arbitration, which must conclude within 45 days. However, "concluding the case" does not mean "money in your account": if the company has no assets or the boss has fled, you may not get the money even if you win.

Zero cost; both complaints and arbitration are free of charge. You must prepare labor contracts, pay stubs, attendance records, bank statements, and chat logs, and visit the labor department or arbitration commission 1 to 3 times. There is a 1-year limit for arbitration (legally called the arbitration statute of limitations). Those still working at the company who are owed wages are not subject to this 1-year limit. Those who have left must file within 1 year of their departure. The difficulty is the back-and-forth travel and gathering every piece of evidence, which can be discouraging.

Step one is filing a complaint. Call 12333 or visit the labor inspectorate of the local human resources and social security department (China). The law stipulates that investigations must be completed within 60 working days after acceptance, with complex cases extendable by 30 working days. If wages are owed, the agency can order the company to pay within a deadline. If they still fail to pay, the company must pay an additional compensation of 50% to 100% of the amount owed. In 2024, inspection agencies nationwide (China) handled 137,000 cases, recovering ⟦8650000000⟧ in wages for 654,000 people. If there is a debt note or payroll showing clear wage arrears, you can also apply directly to a primary court for a payment order. A payment order is a court command to the company to pay, issued within 15 days of acceptance. Step two is applying for arbitration. The law stipulates the case must conclude within 45 days of acceptance, extendable by 15 days. For wage claims, you can apply for preliminary execution: a portion can be enforced before the entire case is settled. If the debt does not exceed 12 times the local monthly minimum wage, it is a final arbitration: the ruling is final, and the company cannot litigate further. In 2024, 4.257 million cases were accepted nationwide (China), with 4.156 million cases resolved. The amount involved in resolved cases was ⟦93470000000⟧. The mediation success rate was 79.6%, the arbitration conclusion rate was 98.2%, and the rate of cases ending at arbitration was 73.7%. Some say this process takes "half a year or a year," referring to cases that go to court after arbitration. These take 6 months for first instance (3 months for summary procedure) plus 3 months for appeal. In 2024, courts concluded 88,000 cases for labor remuneration, recovering ⟦28540000000⟧; 998 people were convicted of the crime of intentionally failing to pay labor remuneration (National).
If you lack funds for a lawsuit, apply for legal aid; wage claims, maintenance claims, and work injuries are inherently eligible
A

Claims for wages, parental maintenance, social insurance benefits, minimum living allowances, or damages from acts of heroism are eligible for free legal aid (China). Call 12348 or visit a local legal aid center. You no longer need to return to your hometown for a poverty certificate; a truthful self-declaration is sufficient. Defendants facing the death penalty, or those who are blind, deaf, mute, or minors, are assigned a lawyer.
Zero cost. Legal aid does not charge the recipient a single cent.

State Council regulations (China) specify six types of civil legal aid matters. The original text is: "requesting state compensation according to law; requesting social insurance benefits or minimum living allowance; requesting pension or relief funds; requesting maintenance, child support, or spousal support; requesting labor remuneration; claiming civil rights arising from acts of heroism." Simply put: suing the state for compensation, claiming social insurance or welfare, claiming pensions, claiming maintenance/support, claiming wages, or damages from heroic acts. In criminal cases, defendants facing the death penalty, as well as those who are blind, deaf, mute, or minors, are assigned a lawyer regardless of their financial situation.
If you are at the end of your rope, go to a relief station: they provide food, shelter, and a ticket home
A

Relief stations provide food, shelter, medical care if you are sick, help contacting family, and a travel ticket if you cannot afford to go home. Usually, stays are limited to 10 days. Entry and exit are voluntary; it is not a forced detention facility, nor does it provide cash. Tickets are issued to your place of household registration or residence; think carefully about where you want to go before arriving.

Zero cost. Go to a local relief management station (China) yourself to request help, or tell the police or civil affairs authorities so they can take you there. Upon entry, you must truthfully declare your name and belongings. The difficulty is admitting to others that you have no money and nowhere to go.

Relief stations provide hygienic food and accommodation. Anyone who falls acutely ill while at the station is taken to a hospital for treatment. The station also helps contact relatives and workplaces. If you lack the money for a ticket to your place of household registration or residence, you are provided with a travel certificate (ticket), meaning a bus or train ticket. The place of household registration is your hometown; the place of residence is where you regularly live. Relief duration is usually no more than 10 days. It can be extended while waiting for family, medical treatment, or placement arrangements. Police and other administrative staff who encounter homeless beggars while on duty must inform them that they can apply for relief. For people with disabilities, minors, the elderly, and those with mobility issues, they must be guided and escorted to the station (National, since 2003).
Use free public employment services and seasonal labor markets first when job hunting; do not use paid brokers
A

Employment service centers and human resource markets are government agencies; they provide job referrals, career guidance, policy consultation, job registration, and unemployment registration, all free of charge. The law explicitly prohibits them from profiting from these services. Registering and posting information at seasonal labor markets is also free. It is convenient to complete unemployment registration at the same time; receiving unemployment benefits and being recognized as a person with employment difficulties both require this documentation.

Free of charge. Go to a public employment service agency at the county level or higher (China) to register, such as an employment service center or human resource market. Local seasonal labor markets can also handle registrations. If you do not know the address, call 12333 to inquire.

The law stipulates that the following are all free: employment policy consultation; information on where is hiring or where there are labor shortages; career guidance and job referrals; job registration and unemployment registration; and employment support for people with employment difficulties. These agencies are not allowed to operate as businesses or rely on these services to make money. Information for job seekers and recruitment for seasonal work can also be registered and posted for free for the public, as it has been included in the scope of public employment information services. For the long-term unemployed (those who have not received work for a long time), low-income households, and other seasonal workers in difficulty, assistance must be strengthened (National).
Apply for temporary relief first if your household encounters an unexpected crisis
B

If a household suddenly faces an incident, such as a fire, traffic accident, or a family member's sudden severe illness, causing basic life to collapse temporarily, apply for temporary relief at the township government or neighborhood office where the incident occurred; you do not necessarily have to be a Minimum Living Guarantee (MLG) household. Such urgent cases are usually processed within 3 days, providing a maximum amount equal to 1 month of the local MLG level. Other cases provide a maximum of up to 6 months.

Free of charge. Submit an application to the township government or neighborhood office where the incident occurred (China), clearly stating what happened to the household. Examples include fires, traffic accidents, sudden severe illness of a family member, or a sudden spike in mandatory living expenses. For unexpected emergencies, use the "quick relief for small amounts" path: no asset checks, no public posting, usually completed within 3 days. If medical or education expenses spike suddenly, public posting is required before approval. Prepare documents according to the local list; usually requires 1 to 2 visits.

Two types of households are eligible for temporary relief. First, households that, due to unexpected accidents, sudden severe illness of a family member, or similar reasons, cannot temporarily afford even minimum expenses for food, housing, or medical treatment. Second, households already receiving the Minimum Living Guarantee (MLG) that face a sudden spike in mandatory expenses beyond their means. What incidents are covered and how much money is provided are determined and announced by local governments at the county level or higher (National system, amounts determined locally, since 2014). The Social Relief Law (China), effective July 1, 2026, defines the subjects as "persons facing sudden, urgent, or disastrous difficulties... causing basic life to temporarily fall into serious hardship," providing relief in cash or in kind. Applications for temporary relief are submitted to the township government or neighborhood office at the "place where the emergency occurred." In emergency situations involving small amounts, relief must be provided first and procedures completed later. A late 2025 document from the Ministry of Civil Affairs and the Ministry of Finance (China) regulates the disbursement method. Urgent matters like unexpected incidents, traumatic injuries, or severe illnesses follow the "quick relief for small amounts" path, skipping family economic status checks and public posting, with a processing time usually not exceeding 3 days and a maximum level not exceeding 1 month of the local MLG. Households near the MLG threshold and households in difficulty due to mandatory expenses, falling into hardship because of sudden spikes in medical or education costs, will have their cases publicly posted before relief is granted, following the principle of "one-time approval, phased disbursement." Aside from the quick relief path, other temporary relief amounts shall not exceed 6 times the local monthly MLG level (National, from 2026, specific levels determined locally).

Apply for the Minimum Living Guarantee if income is below the local threshold; if slightly above or if medical/education costs are too heavy, apply for medical, educational, housing, or employment relief
A

If the average per capita income of the whole household is lower than the local Minimum Living Guarantee (MLG) threshold and assets meet regulations, you can apply. At the end of 2024, the national average threshold (China) was ⟦798.1⟧ per person per month in cities and ⟦593.9⟧ in rural areas. Payments cover the difference, or can be paid in fixed tiers. If income is slightly higher than the threshold, or if medical/education costs are too high, you can still apply for medical, educational, housing, or employment relief even if you do not qualify for the MLG.

Free of charge. A family member living together submits a written application to the township government or neighborhood office where their household registration is located (China). If it is inconvenient to go yourself, ask the village committee or neighborhood committee to do it on your behalf. You must undergo an inspection of family income and assets. Usually requires 2 to 3 visits, bringing ID cards, household registration booklets, and documents proving income and assets. The difficulty lies in having to disclose all household assets for inspection and waiting for public posting. If you do not qualify for the MLG but are applying for medical, housing, or employment relief, also go to the township government or neighborhood office of your household registration. For educational relief, apply at the school the child is attending.

Divide the total household income by the number of members; if it is lower than the local Minimum Living Guarantee (MLG) threshold and household assets are within the regulated range, the MLG is granted (China). At the end of 2024, the national average threshold in cities was ⟦798.1⟧/person/month, and in rural areas ⟦593.9⟧/person/month. There were 6.25 million people guaranteed in cities and 33.615 million in rural areas. The subsidy is paid monthly based on the difference: the local threshold minus the family's per capita income. For example, if the local threshold is ⟦798.1⟧ and each person in the house earns ⟦500⟧ a month, each person receives ⟦298.1⟧ per month, not ⟦798.1⟧. The Social Relief Law (China), effective July 2026, allows an additional method of tiered fixed payments: subsidies "can be paid according to the actual difference between the family's per capita income and the local MLG threshold, or can be paid in fixed tiers." The threshold is determined as follows: take the average per capita consumption expenditure of local residents from the previous year, multiply it by a ratio, and adjust it periodically. Simply put, it takes the average amount a person in the locality spent last year and reduces it by a ratio (National average, varies by location). If you do not qualify for the MLG, there are two other tiers. Tier one is called "near-MLG households": assets meet regulations, and per capita income is below 1.5 times the local MLG threshold (2023 government document). The Social Relief Law effective July 2026 changes this to be determined by the province, as the MLG threshold plus a certain ratio. Tier two is called "households in difficulty due to mandatory expenses." The condition is that per capita income is lower than the local per capita disposable income of the previous year, and assets meet regulations. The ratio of mandatory expenses such as medical and education costs to total family income must also exceed the local regulated level. These two tiers receive medical relief, educational relief, and housing relief. Educational relief includes tuition waivers, scholarships, living subsidies, and student loans. Housing relief in cities prioritizes public rental housing or provides rental subsidies. Unemployed persons with labor capacity in near-MLG households and households in difficulty due to mandatory expenses also receive employment relief. Severely disabled persons or those with serious illnesses in near-MLG households can be individually included in the MLG category to receive monthly payments (National, from 2023, ratios and recognition methods determined locally).
If you have a Disability Certificate, apply for the two disability subsidies
A

Disabled persons in households receiving the Minimum Living Guarantee (MLG) receive a living subsidy. Persons with Grade 1 or Grade 2 disabilities who require long-term care receive a nursing subsidy; both can be received simultaneously. Levels are determined by each province and vary significantly; ask specifically at the neighborhood office. Bring your second-generation Disability Certificate to the neighborhood office or township government to apply once.
Free of charge. Bring the Disability Certificate to the neighborhood office or township government (China) and submit an application once to complete the process.

The State Council (China) established two subsidies. The first is the living subsidy for disabled persons in difficulty; the document defines the subjects as "disabled persons in households guaranteed the minimum living standard; where conditions permit, it can be gradually extended to low-income disabled persons and other disabled persons in difficulty." This means prioritizing disabled persons in MLG households, and extending it where the budget allows. The second is the nursing subsidy for severely disabled persons; the document defines the subjects as "severely disabled persons assessed as Grade 1 or Grade 2 who require long-term care." These two subsidies can be received at the same time.
Resident medical insurance is ⟦400⟧ per year, do not let it lapse; households in difficulty receive waivers or reductions
A

Each person pays from ⟦400⟧ per year; in 2025, the government budget will add a per capita subsidy of no less than ⟦700⟧. Especially impoverished persons receive full support, while Minimum Living Guarantee (MLG) recipients receive a fixed level of support. Lapses come at a price: if you do not participate during the centralized collection period or do not pay continuously, you will face a 3-month waiting period after paying during which medical expenses are not reimbursed; in principle, an additional 1 month is added for every year of lapse.

The individual contribution is no less than ⟦400⟧ per person per year. This is the national level (China) for 2024 and 2025; local levels may be higher. Payment must be made during the fixed annual centralized collection period. Especially impoverished persons receive full support, with the state paying the entire amount. MLG recipients receive a fixed level of support, with the state paying a fixed portion.

In addition to the individual contribution, the government budget adds a per capita subsidy. In 2024, it was no less than ⟦670⟧. In 2025, it increased by ⟦30⟧ over the previous year to no less than ⟦700⟧, while the individual contribution remained at no less than ⟦400⟧ (Document No. 22/2025 of the National Healthcare Security Administration of China, as recounted by provincial documents). The 2026 Government Work Report stated it would increase by another ⟦24⟧. For MLG recipients and especially impoverished persons, the remaining eligible medical costs after medical insurance reimbursement are further covered by medical relief at a rate of no less than 70%. The price of a lapse is a waiting period. If you do not participate during the centralized collection period or do not pay continuously, there is a fixed 3-month waiting period after payment during which medical expenses are not reimbursed. For every year of lapse, an additional 1 month is added in principle (from 2025, National).
For serious illnesses, use medical insurance, critical illness insurance, medical relief, and register for out-of-province treatment first; do not touch online loans
A

The sequence is fixed: before being hospitalized in another province, register via the "National Healthcare Security Administration" WeChat account; upon discharge, settle the bill directly so you don't have to advance the full amount. If the remaining balance is still unaffordable after reimbursement, apply for medical relief at the township or neighborhood office. Employees have a medical treatment period of 3 to 24 months depending on seniority, during which the company cannot fire you. Do not touch online loans or high-interest social loans.

Free of charge. The sequence is fixed; follow it step by step. Step one: before hospitalization in another province, register via the "National Cross-Province Medical Treatment Registration" mini-app within the "National Healthcare Security Administration" WeChat account (China). Step two: settle the bill directly at the hospital upon discharge. Step three: if the self-paid portion is still too heavy after insurance reimbursement, apply for medical relief at the township government or neighborhood office. Step four: if still employed, take sick leave according to the medical treatment period; this is the period during which you can be absent for illness without being fired; if it is a work-related injury, use work injury insurance. Step five: if credit card debt is unaffordable, proactively contact the bank to negotiate installments. Step six: if funds are truly insufficient, use personal crowdfunding platforms designated by the Ministry of Civil Affairs to raise donations. Main documents include diagnosis certificates, cost breakdowns, and payment receipts; requires 2 to 4 visits. The difficulty is that the sick person must still travel back and forth to complete procedures.

The state (China) combines basic medical insurance, critical illness insurance, and medical relief into what is called a "three-tier system," where each tier supports the next. For MLG recipients and especially impoverished persons, eligible medical costs are relieved at a rate of no less than 70%. Those who were not originally poor but became poor due to medical treatment can apply for additional relief themselves. Registering before out-of-province hospitalization allows for direct settlement upon discharge, avoiding the need to advance the full amount and claim it back from the insurance location later. If you must stop working due to illness, you have a medical treatment period of 3 to 24 months, the length of which depends on work seniority. During this time, the company cannot terminate the labor contract, and sick leave pay must not be lower than 80% of the local minimum wage. Persons with work-related injuries have a period of leave with full pay, meaning the period of recovery during which they do not work, but their old salary and benefits are still paid in full by the company monthly, usually not exceeding 12 months. If credit card debt exceeds the ability to pay but the individual still intends to pay, they can negotiate a personalized installment agreement with the bank, which restructures the debt plan for up to 5 years. Once the agreement is signed, the bank must stop debt collection. Online personal crowdfunding platforms for medical fundraising must be designated by the civil affairs department of the State Council. Platforms must verify that the help request information is true. Donated funds must only be transferred to the person seeking help or to the account they provide (National).
If you lose your ID card, replace it immediately; if needed urgently, apply for a temporary ID card first
A

A replacement card is issued within 60 days from the date of application. If needed urgently, apply for a temporary ID card at the same time; it is issued within 3 days and is valid for 3 months. Without an ID card, you cannot find work, rent housing, open accounts, or receive subsidies; it is a prerequisite for all procedures.

A card issuance fee must be paid. This is a statutory fee; the amount is determined by the state (China) and follows the locally posted rates. Submit the application at the public security station of your permanent household registration; requires 1 visit.

From the day you submit the "Resident Identity Card Application Form," the public security organ (China) must issue the card within 60 days. During the period of issuance, exchange, or replacement, if it is needed urgently, a temporary resident identity card can be obtained. The public security organ issues it within 3 days of receiving the application, and it is valid for 3 months (National).
After registering as unemployed, apply for recognition as a person with employment difficulties to receive social insurance subsidies or a public interest job position
B

Once recognized, self-paid social insurance is subsidized, in principle not exceeding two-thirds of the actual amount paid, for a maximum of 3 years. If hired by a company or placed in a public interest job, the company's portion of social insurance is also subsidized. Subsidies for public interest positions are referenced against the local minimum wage; these positions do not pay much but include social insurance, making them suitable for transitions. Most social insurance subsidies follow a "pay first, reimburse later" model, requiring you to advance the money.

Free of charge. Submit an application for recognition at the public employment service agency of the neighborhood office or community (China). Recognition criteria vary by location; common types include: older age, long-term unemployment, MLG households, disability, or zero-employment households. You must complete unemployment registration before you can apply. The difficulty lies in checking each condition to see if you qualify, and social insurance requires advancing the payment yourself.

Once recognized, individuals without a company who pay social insurance themselves (known as flexible employment) receive social insurance subsidies. The subsidy level is in principle no more than 2/3 of the actual amount paid, for a maximum of 3 years. If hired by a company or placed in a public interest job, the company receives subsidies based on actual payments for pension, medical, and unemployment insurance. Public interest jobs are positions created with government funding; their subsidies are referenced against the local minimum wage. Public interest positions created by the state prioritize the placement of people with employment difficulties. Additionally, there is a one-time job-seeking subsidy provided to graduates of universities and colleges. The scope includes graduates from MLG households, zero-employment households, and especially impoverished persons. Disabled graduates or those who have used national student loans also count. This amount is received during the graduation academic year (National framework, recognition criteria and amounts determined locally).
While unemployed, seek vocational training subsidies, job internship subsidies, and social insurance subsidies; do not pay for training classes yourself
A

If you undergo vocational training and obtain a regulated certificate, you can receive a vocational training subsidy, with each person eligible up to 3 times. University and college graduates within 2 years of graduation who have not found work, and unemployed youth aged 16 to 24, can participate in job internships and receive basic living allowances during the internship. First, check the "vocational training subsidy catalog" on the local human resources and social security department website (China); do not pay to register for classes yourself.

Free of charge. The training itself takes up a significant amount of time. The difficulty lies in having to complete the training in one go and pass the exam to obtain the certificate before the subsidy can be received.

Regulations from the Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (China) list a series of expenditures from employment subsidy funds, which are budget funds specifically earmarked for employment subsidies. If you undergo vocational training and obtain a regulated certificate, you receive a vocational training subsidy, with each person eligible up to 3 times. People with employment difficulties who pay social insurance themselves (flexible employment) receive subsidies for a maximum of 3 years; those with less than 5 years until statutory retirement age can have this extended until retirement. Graduates who pay social insurance themselves receive subsidies for a maximum of 2 years, or 1 year if hired by an enterprise. Graduates within 2 years of graduation who have not found work, and unemployed youth aged 16 to 24, can participate in job internships and receive basic living allowances during the internship.
When job hunting, don't just blast resumes; use a systematic approach: learn skills, set goals, and ask for help
A

People who participated in job-seeking support programs were 2.67 times more likely to find a job than those who did not. What works is: learning specific job-seeking skills, being able to clearly state who you are, setting clear goals, taking proactive action, and opening up to ask others for help.

Free of charge. Spend 1 to 2 hours every day for several consecutive weeks. There is no need to register for paid courses; use the free career guidance sessions provided by public employment service agencies instead. The difficulty lies in persisting every day without supervision and proactively asking others for help.

A meta-analysis of 47 studies on job-seeking support programs with controlled comparisons was calculated. These studies were experimental or quasi-experimental, all using group comparisons. Results: the group participating in the programs was 2.67 times more likely to find a job than the group that did not (OR = 2.67, i.e., odds ratio). The effective components in the programs were: one, teaching job-seeking skills; two, improving self-presentation (clearly stating who one is); three, enhancing self-efficacy (believing one can do it); four, encouraging proactive action; five, goal setting; and six, seeking social support (asking others for help). Programs that both taught skills and provided motivation had the greatest effect.
Do not pay deposits, do not hand over documents for safekeeping, do not sign "vocational training loans", do not join illegal multi-level marketing, and do not take high-interest loans
A

Recruitment units are not allowed to keep your ID card, collect deposits, or rename fees to collect money. If a broker fails to introduce a job, they must refund the brokerage fee. Taking a loan for vocational training before starting work, or recruiting people to earn money like illegal multi-level marketing, are scams that have been officially identified by the state (China). If the loan interest exceeds four times the 1-year LPR (Loan Prime Rate), the court will not recognize it, but the principal must still be repaid.

Zero cost. If you encounter the three phrases "pay first then start work", "study first then get a job placement", or "recruit people", refuse immediately. Keep chat messages and transfer records. The difficulty is that the more you lack money, the more you want to take a gamble; saying "no" on the spot is not easy.

Companies are not allowed to keep your ID card or other documents, force you to find a guarantor, or rename fees to collect money or items from you. Violators are forced to return them and are fined from ⟦500~2000⟧ for each worker. Employment brokers are also not allowed to keep documents or collect deposits; if they fail to introduce a job, they must refund the brokerage fee to you. Using the guise of recruitment to lure you into paying tuition or taking a loan first is a scam known as "recruitment turned into vocational training" or "vocational training loans" that the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (China) and other departments, five agencies in total, have issued warnings about. Relying on recruiting people to calculate commissions, where payment is required to join, is illegal multi-level marketing (pyramid scheme); participants can be fined up to ⟦2000⟧. For civil loan interest, the portion exceeding 4 times the 1-year LPR at the time the contract was signed is not recognized by the court. This new regulation replaces the old three-segment method based on the 24% and 36% benchmarks (national, since August 2020)
If facing housing difficulties, queue for public rental housing first
B

Three conditions must be met simultaneously: no local housing or housing area below the prescribed level; income and assets below the prescribed level; and for people from other places, they must have worked stably in the locality for the prescribed number of years. Waiting times are announced locally. This is a long-term solution that cannot solve an immediate crisis, but queuing is free, and early registration leads to an earlier turn.

No application fee. Submit documents to the city or county (China) housing security agency, and you must provide written consent for them to verify your declarations. If documents are missing, they will notify you once about what needs to be supplemented. The time spent waiting for housing is called the waiting period, which usually does not exceed 5 years.

Meeting all three conditions allows for an application. First, no local housing or housing area below the prescribed level. Second, income and assets below the prescribed level. Third, people from other places must have worked stably in the locality for the prescribed number of years. Specific conditions are set and announced by the housing security agencies of municipalities directly under the central government, cities, and counties. People already on the waiting list are called waiting subjects, and the housing security agency must arrange housing for them within the waiting period (national framework, thresholds and rents are determined locally, since 2012)
Push housing and food costs to the lowest: monthly co-renting instead of daily renting, self-cooking and subsidized canteens instead of ordering takeout
B

In 2025, in the national (China) per capita expenditure, food accounted for 29.3% and housing for 21.7%, totaling more than half, so squeezing these two items is most effective. According to the author's experience, rooms rented by the day or hour are more expensive than shared housing when calculated monthly; self-cooking is cheaper than ordering takeout. When looking for a job, ask clearly if food and housing are included; jobs that include them effectively eliminate these two major expenses.

Finding a room takes 1 to 3 days. The deposit is usually 1 month's rent (author's estimate). Self-cooking takes 30 to 60 minutes per day. The difficulty is having to do it yourself every day and resisting the urge to order takeout.

In 2025, the average national (China) resident spent ⟦29476⟧ per year (called per capita consumption expenditure). Of this, food, tobacco, and alcohol were ⟦8631⟧, accounting for 29.3%. Housing was ⟦6397⟧, accounting for 21.7%. The two items combined are more than half, so squeezing these two is most effective. Meal support services for the elderly are open to all elderly people, in the form of elderly canteens, elderly dining tables, and meal support points; elderly people in difficulty also receive separate subsidies at different levels. For reference: as of January 1, 2026, the lowest tier-one monthly minimum wage among provinces is Qinghai at ⟦2080⟧, and the highest is Shanghai at ⟦2740⟧ (national, 2025 to 2026)
Don't panic if social insurance is interrupted: pensions are calculated based on cumulative years, and medical insurance can be paid retroactively according to regulations
A

Pensions are calculated based on the total cumulative years, not continuous years; interruptions do not reset the count to zero; if you accumulate 15 years by retirement age, you receive a monthly payment. If employee medical insurance is paid for the required number of years, no further payments are needed after retirement; the number of years varies by location. Interruptions affect two things: after resuming resident medical insurance, there is a period where medical visits are not reimbursed; and buying a house, household registration, or points-based systems in various places often require continuous payments.

Zero cost. Resident pension insurance and resident medical insurance (China) can be paid individually by the year. If employee social insurance is interrupted, there is no need to spend money to have someone "place your name" in another unit just to "avoid interruption."

Basic pension insurance is calculated based on the total cumulative years of payment; interruptions in the middle are not cleared. Upon reaching the legal retirement age, accumulating 15 years allows for a monthly pension. If insufficient, payments can continue until 15 years are reached. When moving to a different workplace (officially called moving to a different fund management area), the pension insurance relationship follows the person, and the payment years continue to accumulate. If employee medical insurance is paid cumulatively for the number of years prescribed by the state, no further payments are needed after retirement. The price of an interruption in resident medical insurance is the waiting period: after paying again, there is a period where medical visits are not reimbursed (see resident medical insurance in section 9) (national)
Whether you have been to prison, gone bankrupt, or been blacklisted as dishonest, the law provides a path to start over; first, complete the procedures
A

Ex-prisoners are not discriminated against when seeking employment, education, or social security; the government helps arrange for those with living difficulties. For crimes committed under age 18 with a sentence of 5 years or less, the criminal record is sealed and does not need to be disclosed for military service or employment. The duration on the dishonest list is 2 years; if all debts are paid, the court must remove the name within 3 working days. Criminal records for adults are not sealed and must be truthfully disclosed for military service or employment.

No procedural fees. Ex-prisoners should report to the township justice office or neighborhood office of their registered household or residence (China) to request reintegration arrangements and assistance (arranged and supported by the government). Those on the list of dishonest judgment debtors should pay off the debt and then apply to the execution court for removal. Individuals who have participated in insurance in Shenzhen for 3 years can apply for personal bankruptcy. Every step requires preparing documents, passing interviews, and a 1 to 3-year probation period. The difficulty is having to repeatedly tell your past story to others and enduring the probation period.

Ex-prisoners enjoy equal rights as other citizens according to the law and are not discriminated against in employment, education, and social security. The government of their registered household or residence helps arrange, rescue, and assist those with living difficulties according to the law (Prison Law (China) amended in 2026, effective November 1). A 2010 central document (China) requires strengthening vocational training for them, including those eligible in the minimum living allowance, and building transitional arrangement bases. For crimes committed under age 18 with a sentence of 5 years or less, the criminal record is sealed and does not need to be disclosed for military service or employment; a certificate of no criminal record will be issued within 3 working days upon application. The duration for being listed as dishonest is 2 years. If the debt is paid, or a settlement is reached with the other party, the court must remove the name within 3 working days. The Shenzhen Special Economic Zone Personal Bankruptcy Regulations is currently the only personal bankruptcy regulation (China); after being declared bankrupt and passing a 3-year probation period, unpaid debts may be discharged. Legal person enterprises that cannot pay due debts and have more debt than assets (insolvency) can apply for restructuring, settlement, or bankruptcy liquidation. Upon completion of bankruptcy procedures, the enterprise undergoes deregistration. However, guarantors for the enterprise and others with joint liability "still continue to bear the responsibility for debt repayment according to the law." Business owners who signed personal guarantees for the company must still pay themselves. Adult criminal records are not sealed: Article 100 of the Criminal Law (China) stipulates that those who have received criminal penalties must truthfully disclose this when joining the military or seeking employment and must not hide it (national, personal bankruptcy only in Shenzhen)

Before getting seriously ill, besides basic medical insurance, buy an additional one-year medical expense insurance or critical illness insurance, and read the four words "guaranteed renewal" carefully
B

This type of insurance covers the portion you pay out-of-pocket after medical insurance has paid, and the loss of income when you have to stop working. Before buying, look for the four words "guaranteed renewal": without these four words, the product might stop being sold or the price might increase next year. Health status must be declared truthfully; hiding it may lead to a denial of claims. Pay for basic medical insurance first before considering this item.

For young people, a one-year reimbursement-type medical expense insurance costs a few hundred yuan per year. Reimbursement-type means it pays based on the amount you actually spend. Critical illness insurance costs from several thousand yuan per year (author's estimate, no official figure). Before buying, you must truthfully declare your health status, which takes half an hour.

The state (China) divides this type of product into two. Medical expense insurance pays based on the actual medical costs you spend. Disease insurance pays a lump sum according to the agreed amount as soon as a disease listed in the contract is diagnosed. Both cover the out-of-pocket portion after medical insurance and the loss of income during leave. If the insurance term is one year or less and the terms do not state guaranteed renewal, it is short-term health insurance. Only if it is over one year or states guaranteed renewal is it long-term health insurance. "Guaranteed renewal" means: upon expiration, the company must continue the insurance under the old terms and agreed premium. Insurance companies are not allowed to lure a person into buying multiple overlapping reimbursement-type medical expense insurance plans with similar functions. If you buy two, the same expense will only be paid once. The definition of diseases in critical illness insurance has a unified industry standard, including 28 major illnesses and 3 minor illnesses. Malignant tumors, acute myocardial infarction, and stroke sequelae are core diseases (national, since 2019, 2020)
If you truly have no place to sleep, 24-hour venues can only be used temporarily for one night; prioritize going to a relief station
B

Waiting areas at airports and train stations can last for one night, with toilets and power outlets, but there is no official data saying this is safe. Relief stations have 24-hour staff; arriving in the middle of the night still gets you priority assistance. In winter, some places also open temporary cold shelters. If you don't want to enter a station, patrol staff will also give you food and warm clothes.

Waiting areas at airports and train stations are usually free. Fast food restaurants and internet cafes require spending a little money to buy something. You cannot sleep peacefully, and belongings are at risk of theft. The difficulty is not daring to truly sleep all night.

Staying in a 24-hour venue can get you through the night, with toilets and phone charging. Whether it is safe there has no official data. Regarding relief stations, the Ministry of Civil Affairs (China) requires relief hotlines to be open all day, staffed 24 hours. People in difficulty who seek help will receive priority assistance according to policy. Workers without jobs, victims of theft or robbery, who suddenly lose their source of livelihood, are guaranteed emergency transitional living support. Places with conditions will open venues like community service centers as temporary shelters. In winter, people in difficulty are guided to relief stations or temporary cold shelters. For those who do not want to enter a station, patrol staff provide food, clothing, and warmth items, and leave contact information for help. At night, when it gets cold, or during rain, snow, and ice, patrols are intensified. Bus and train stations, pedestrian tunnels, underpasses, and construction sites are key patrol areas (national, civil affairs agencies have conducted special winter relief campaigns every year since 2013)

If you are owed wages, first see who hired you: small unlicensed workshops and contractors can still be reported to labor inspectors; only private work for families or individuals requires going to court
A

For small workshops or shops without licenses, you can still complain to labor inspectors or apply for labor arbitration if wages are owed; the boss themselves can be held liable. If a contractor takes work at a construction site and owes money, the main contractor or developer must pay. Only when working privately for a family or individual, such as a domestic helper, is it not considered a labor dispute, and a lawsuit must be filed in court.

Zero cost. First, clarify three things: is the other party running a shop or workshop; was the work assigned by a company or construction site; were you working inside someone's home. Whether the other party has a business license can be checked on the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (China).

The employer units mentioned in Article 2 of the Labor Contract Law (China) are organizations such as enterprises, individual economic organizations, and private non-enterprise units; a single individual does not count. The Supreme People's Court's (China) interpretation on labor disputes lists several types of disputes that do not belong to labor disputes. First, disputes between families or individuals and domestic service providers. Second, disputes between individual craftsmen and assistants or apprentices. Third, disputes between rural business contractors and employees. These types must be sued in court as ordinary civil disputes, with a 3-year statute of limitations. Units without business licenses are not among these exceptions. Article 93 of the Labor Contract Law deals with units without legal business qualifications. If you have already worked, the unit or the investor must pay wages, economic compensation, and damages. The investor is the person who provided the money to open the unit. Article 29 of that interpretation deals with three types of units: those that haven't applied for a license, those with revoked licenses, and those whose business term has expired but are still operating. If you have a dispute with such a unit, you must include the unit or the investor as a party. Article 33 of the Labor and Social Security Inspection Regulations (China) stipulates that places without a business license or with a revoked license that are hiring people will still be inspected by labor and social security authorities. If an individual contractor recruits people illegally and causes damage to the workers, the contracting organization and the individual contractor bear joint liability for compensation (Article 94 of the Labor Contract Law). Developers or main construction contractors sometimes subcontract or divide work to individuals or units without legal business qualifications. Therefore, wage arrears for migrant workers are paid by the developer or the main construction contractor (Article 36 of the Regulations on Guaranteeing Payment of Wages to Migrant Workers) (national)

If credit cards or online loans are unaffordable, call the bank hotline or platform yourself to request special installment plans or extensions; do not borrow new to pay old, and do not pay for "interest suspension", "credit repair", or "anti-debt collection" services
B

If you cannot pay your credit card but still want to, you can negotiate a special installment plan with the bank, for a maximum of 5 years; once the agreement is signed, the bank must stop debt collection. However, the bank may not agree, and existing overdue records will remain in the credit file. Services that charge money to help you with "interest suspension" or "whitewashing credit history" have been specifically warned against by regulatory authorities (China); do not seek them out.

Zero cost. Call the official hotline printed on the back of the card or published in the app, and clearly state that you cannot pay but want to. Prepare documents proving income, job loss, or illness; you usually have to call several times. If an agreement is reached, pay monthly according to the new plan; only after paying in full can you apply for a credit card again. The difficulty is having to proactively answer the bank's calls and repeatedly explain your hardships.

There are clear regulations for credit cards. If the debt exceeds your ability to pay but you still want to pay, the bank "may" negotiate equally with you to sign a special installment agreement. The agreement can last up to 5 years. The agreement must specify the total debt, the amount per period, and whether annual fees and interest are charged during the repayment period. Once both parties sign, the bank and its entrusted collection agencies must stop collecting. If you do not pay according to the agreement, you are no longer protected by this limit. For oral agreements, the bank must keep recordings for at least until the debt is paid off. Debts already in installments cannot be put into installments again; special installment plans are the only exception (2022 management notice). In 2025, when the People's Bank of China abolished old measures on bank cards, the document stated that credit cards continue to be managed under these regulations. Online loans do not have unified regulations like special installment plans; whether extensions or installments are possible depends on the contract and the lender. If the lender is a consumer finance company, regulations prohibit it from collecting debt through violence, threats, intimidation, or harassment. Neither banks nor consumer finance companies are allowed to collect debt from people unrelated to the debt. Regarding paid services, in 2026 the National Financial Regulatory Administration (China) and other agencies, five in total, jointly issued a risk warning. The warning stated that "loans and credit cards do not need to be repaid", "debt negotiation", "debt swapping", and "credit history whitewashing" are all false information. This type of "rights protection representative" will charge high service fees, and you may be sued for breach of contract if you withdraw midway. They will collect your bank cards, SIM cards, home address, and children's school information. Following their instructions to submit fake documents, intentionally evade debt, or pressure through complaints may violate the law or constitute a crime. In 2022, the Beijing banking and insurance regulator also named advertisements like "interest suspension", "stop collection", and "full interest waiver". The agency said that following those people and delaying payment without contacting the bank will likely leave bad overdue records in the credit file. In 2022, the National Development and Reform Commission (China) launched a special campaign to handle "credit history repair". The notice said these people intentionally confuse the concept of credit information complaints with credit restoration, using the guise of "repairing, whitewashing, or deleting credit history" to scam. Negative information in the credit file is kept for 5 years from the date the bad behavior or event ends; it is deleted after 5 years. During the retention period, you can add an explanation to that record, and the credit information organization must record it (national)
If you cause a traffic accident, stop the vehicle, save people, and report to the police first; do not flee
A

If you flee, the accident is by default considered your full responsibility. Your driver's license will be revoked; if fleeing constitutes a crime, you can never retake the test for life. There is a more practical layer: vehicle damage insurance and third-party liability insurance will not pay for someone who flees; you will have to pay hundreds of thousands of yuan out of your own pocket. Staying at the scene to save people and reporting to the police takes at most one or two hours.

Zero cost. Stop the car, turn on emergency lights, save people, call the police, and wait for the traffic police; it takes at most one or two hours. For minor collisions where no one is injured and both parties do not disagree on the facts, take photos first. Then record the names, phone numbers, license plate numbers, driver's license numbers, and insurance certificate numbers of both parties and the impact points. After both parties sign for confirmation, you can leave the scene first and then negotiate privately.

The party that flees must bear full responsibility for the accident. Only if you can prove the other party was also at fault can the responsibility be slightly reduced. Fleeing also leads to the revocation of the driver's license. If fleeing constitutes a crime, you can never be re-issued a driver's license for life. If the accident constitutes the crime of causing a traffic accident (China), fleeing results in a sentence of 3 to 7 years in prison. If fleeing causes the death of the victim, the sentence is 7 years or more. Insurance will not cover you either: in commercial motor vehicle insurance (China), vehicle damage insurance and third-party liability insurance do not compensate for cases of "fleeing after causing a traffic accident" or "intentionally destroying or faking the scene, or destroying evidence"; you must pay the compensation of hundreds of thousands of yuan yourself (applies throughout China)
If you realize you've been scammed, call 110 or 96110 immediately to request a payment stop; do not try to investigate first
A

The short period right after money is transferred is the most critical: the police can issue an emergency payment stop and perform a rapid freeze, and banks are mandated to cooperate. Once the money is transferred further or split up, the chance of recovery drops significantly. Therefore, call 110 or 96110 first; do not try to investigate or ask around beforehand. If you receive a call from 96110, it is the police trying to warn or stop you; you must answer it.
Free. Make a phone call, clearly state the time of transfer, the amount, and the recipient's account number. Keep screenshots of the transfer and chat messages.

Public security agencies (China) have the right to conduct immediate inquiries, issue emergency payment stops, and perform rapid freezes on funds involved in a case. Banks and payment institutions are mandated to cooperate. If funds are successfully frozen, they are returned to the victim according to procedures. Once money is transferred out or split up, the possibility of recovery decreases sharply, so stopping payment as early as possible is most effective. 96110 is the national unified anti-fraud warning hotline (China); an incoming call means the police are intervening to prevent a scam, and you must answer (applicable nationwide in China, since December 2022).

Remember the hard rules against fraud: do not trust strange calls, do not leak information, do not click links, and check multiple times before transferring money; the seven most common scams follow this pattern
B

Whenever someone asks you to transfer money, share your screen, download strange apps, click links, or read verification codes, hang up first, then call back using an official number to verify. The seven types are: "order brushing" tasks for commissions, fake financial investments, online loans, impersonating customer service, impersonating police/procuratorate/court, "pig-butchering" romance scams (luring into love then stealing money), and sexual solicitation combined with tasks; every type requires you to transfer money first. Recognizing it beforehand is much cheaper than trying to reclaim money later.

Free. Remember "three 'don'ts', one 'many'", read through the seven types below, install the "National Anti-Fraud Center" app (China), and definitely answer calls from 96110. Whenever someone asks you to transfer money, share your screen, download strange apps, click links, or read verification codes, hang up first, then call an official number to verify. The difficulty lies in the other party often creating a sense of extreme urgency; you must resist that pressure to hang up first.

The law (China) requires the government and relevant agencies to popularize information about telecommunications and network fraud methods. Police cooperate with financial, telecommunications, and internet management sectors to build a warning and intervention system to promptly stop those who may be about to be scammed. 96110 is that national unified warning hotline (China); incoming calls must be answered. In June 2026, the Ministry of Public Security (China) announced that the 10 most frequent types of fraud account for 85% of all telecommunications and network fraud cases. Commission-based tasks are the most common, accounting for 25%. Fake online financial investments cause the greatest losses, approximately 40% of total damages. The Fujian Provincial Public Security Department (China) breaks down the signs of each type as follows. Commission tasks: "anyone inviting you to make money together is likely trying to make money off you"; tasks are never finished, and the principal is never returned. Fake financial investment: the group has "shills" boasting about profits, giving you small initial returns to lure more capital; you must "pay taxes" to withdraw funds. Online loans: "loans that don't require a security deposit or bank statements are definitely fake." Impersonating customer service: claiming you opened a membership that will automatically deduct funds and affect your credit score, forcing you to transfer money to cancel. These scammers often ask you to download a "meeting app" and turn on screen sharing. Once shared, "everything on your phone, including message notifications, SMS verification codes, and passwords entered, is clearly visible." The Shanghai Anti-Fraud Center (China) reminds: "any mention of 'meeting codes', 'screen sharing', or 'remote control' is a scam." Impersonating police/procuratorate/court: "police, procuratorates, and courts do not have so-called 'safe accounts'; any 'agency' handling cases or taking statements via phone, QQ, WeChat, or the internet is a scam." Abroad, scammers also impersonate embassies or consulates, claiming you are suspected of money laundering, have important documents to collect, or have passport/visa issues, then transfer the call to domestic "police." The Chinese Embassy in the US specifically reminds students: "anyone claiming to be staff from an embassy, consulate, carrier, or customs, using the reason that you are suspected of legal violations to proactively transfer the call to police, is a scam!" Pig-butchering: "do not easily trust a 'lover' you have never met, only seen via photos or videos"; they never video call, never meet, but often have emergencies needing money. Sexual solicitation with tasks: arranging a meeting but requiring "tasks" first, with increasing deposits. Recognizing it beforehand is much cheaper than stopping payment later. How much can be recovered via payment stop depends on whether the money is still in the account when reported. For payment stop methods, see item 2 (call 110 or 96110 to request a payment stop) (applicable nationwide in China, since December 2022).
Seeing a face via video or hearing a voice over the phone does not count as verification; if money transfer is involved, hang up first and call back using the old number saved in your contacts
B

Seeing a face or hearing a voice does not count as verification. Whenever a money transfer is involved, hang up first, then call back using the old number saved in your contacts or ask a mutual acquaintance. If the other party claims "weak signal," "is in a meeting," or refuses a direct video call, consider it a scam immediately.

Free. Make one more call, wait a few more minutes. On normal days, avoid posting videos clearly showing your face or long audio recordings on public accounts. The difficulty lies in the other party often being very pushy; you must resist transferring money on the spot.

The Cybersecurity Bureau of the Ministry of Public Security (China) suggests three methods. The first is a movement test: ask the other party to turn their head in one continuous motion, or cover their face completely with their hand and remove it quickly. Original text: "current AI technology often flickers, blurs, or distorts when simulating these complex facial obstructions and lighting changes." The second is listening closely to the voice: "AI-generated voices sometimes lack natural breathing pauses, emotional inflection, or sound slightly robotic with unusual background noise." The third is multi-channel verification. The original text calls this the "core trick": "hang up and call the phone number they usually use that you are familiar with (do not call back the suspicious number that just called), or ask indirectly through a third party you both know." The mantra is "don't rush to trust video or voice; test movements and check multiple channels." Legally, using face-swapping or voice-faking for fraud has long been banned. Services for creating or swapping faces, synthesizing human voices, or mimicking voices must be clearly labeled by the platforms. No organization or individual may intentionally delete, modify, forge, or hide these labels.
