However, since platforms enforce the rules and scammers won't apply labels, the "absence of an AI label" cannot be used as evidence that the other party is a real person. The Criminal Investigation Bureau of the Ministry of Public Security (China) once announced a case where a gang of 14 people was caught with over 50.000 synthesized dynamic facial videos and over 500.000 pieces of personal information. Police also seized 60 cloud servers (applicable nationwide in China; labeling obligations from September 1, 2025).
If accused or summoned, hire a lawyer first; do not settle privately, and do not delete messages or data
A

You can hire a lawyer from the very first time you are called for questioning. If a lawyer requests to see you, the detention center must arrange it within 48 hours at the latest, and the conversation cannot be eavesdropped. You have the right not to answer questions unrelated to the case.

Legal fees start from several thousand yuan. If in financial difficulty, you can apply for legal aid to have a lawyer appointed for free. When questioned, only answer questions related to the case; let the lawyer handle the rest. The difficulty lies in staying calm on the spot and not rushing to explain yourself.

From the first interrogation or from the time compulsory measures (restriction of physical freedom) are applied, you have the right to hire a lawyer. While the case is in the hands of the police investigation, only a lawyer can be hired; non-lawyers cannot act as defenders. If a lawyer requests a meeting, the detention center must arrange it within 48 hours at the latest, and the meeting cannot be eavesdropped. No one can be forced to prove their own guilt. You have the right to refuse to answer questions unrelated to the case. Summons and forced appearance for questioning can last a maximum of 12 hours per instance, or 24 hours for particularly major or complex cases. A summons is a notice for you to appear for questioning; forced appearance is being brought in by force. Consecutive summonses cannot be used as a form of disguised detention. Fabricating facts to falsely accuse others with the intent of having them criminally prosecuted is punishable by up to 3 years in prison; if it causes serious consequences, 3 to 10 years. If detained or arrested and the case is later dismissed, not prosecuted, or found not guilty, you can apply for state compensation (China). Daily compensation is calculated based on the national average daily wage of workers from the previous year (applicable nationwide in China).

If something happens, take the initiative to report it: voluntary surrender can reduce the sentence by up to four-tenths, and minor crimes can be reduced even more or even exempted from punishment; the path of "hiding until the statute of limitations expires" has been blocked
A

Voluntary surrender can reduce a sentence by a maximum of four-tenths; for minor circumstances, no penalty may be imposed. If you only confess after being found, the reduction is usually a maximum of two-tenths. Fleeing or denying guilt gains nothing. Hoping to hide for a few years until the case expires won't work: if a case has been filed and you flee, the time spent in hiding is not counted toward the statute of limitations.

Free. Voluntarily go to the police station to report, or stay where you are and call the police, then recount the facts truthfully. The difficulty lies in resisting the thought of "let's wait and see, maybe no one will investigate."

Article 67 of the 刑法 (Criminal Law of China): automatically surrendering and truthfully confessing one's crime after committing it constitutes voluntary surrender. Those who surrender voluntarily may be given a lighter or reduced penalty, and for minor crimes, punishment may be exempted. If one does not surrender but truthfully confesses their crime (truthful confession), they may be given a lighter penalty; if a particularly serious consequence is avoided due to the truthful confession, the penalty may be reduced. Sentencing guidelines from the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate (China) provide clear ranges. The base sentence is calculated first according to the circumstances of the case, and the percentages below are deducted from that base. Voluntary surrender can reduce the base sentence by up to 40%; minor crimes can be reduced by more than 40% or exempted according to law. In truthful confessions, confessing one's crime reduces the sentence by up to 20%. Confessing a more serious crime of the same type that the judicial authorities were unaware of reduces it by 10% to 30%. Avoiding particularly serious consequences through truthful confession reduces it by 30% to 50%. Pleading guilty and accepting punishment reduces it by up to 30%. Having multiple circumstances simultaneously, such as voluntary surrender, major truthful confession, returning property, and receiving forgiveness from the victim through compensation, can reduce the sentence by up to 60%; minor crimes can be reduced by more than 60% or exempted according to law. The statute of limitations for prosecution is divided into four levels based on the maximum statutory penalty: 5 years, 10 years, 15 years, and 20 years (Article 87 of the Criminal Law of China). However, Article 88 clearly states exceptions. After the procuratorate, police, or national security agencies have initiated an investigation, or after a court has accepted a case, anyone who evades investigation or trial is not limited by the statute of limitations (applicable nationwide in China; sentencing ranges applicable from July 1, 2021).
If you have consumed alcohol, do not drive, including electric bicycles and "just moving the car a bit"; also, do not lend your vehicle to someone who has been drinking or does not have a license
A

Driving after drinking: license suspended for 6 months, fine of ⟦2000⟧; repeat offenses lead to administrative detention and license revocation. Drunk driving results in immediate license revocation, a 5-year ban on re-applying, and criminal prosecution for dangerous driving. Commercial insurance will not pay for accidents caused by driving under the influence. If you lend your car knowing the person has been drinking or lacks a license, you must also pay part of the damages if an accident occurs.
Hiring a designated driver or calling a taxi costs a few dozen yuan. Before a gathering, agree on who will not drink. The difficulty lies in refusing when pressured to drink at a party.

Driving after drinking: driver's license suspended for 6 months, fine of ⟦1000~2000⟧. Repeat offenses lead to up to 10 days of administrative detention and license revocation. Drunk driving results in immediate license revocation, a 5-year ban on re-applying, and criminal prosecution for the crime of dangerous driving (China), punished with criminal detention and a fine; criminal detention is short-term imprisonment. Driving commercial vehicles is even stricter: driving after drinking leads to 15 days of administrative detention, a ⟦5000⟧ fine, and a 5-year driving ban. Drunk driving leads to a 10-year driving ban and a lifetime ban on driving commercial vehicles. Driving after drinking or drunk driving that causes a serious accident constituting a crime results in a lifetime driving ban. Commercial vehicle insurance (China) does not compensate for driving after drinking or using drugs. Moving or parking a car within residential areas or parking lots while drunk, even for short distances, might not be prosecuted as a crime. However, the driver's license is still revoked, and fines and administrative detention are still applied at the level of driving after drinking. For electric bicycles, the State Council's implementation regulations (China) also clearly state "one must not be drunk while operating the vehicle"; violations result in a warning or a fine of ⟦5~50⟧. Handing a vehicle to someone without a license, or whose license has been revoked or suspended, results in a fine of ⟦200~2000⟧ and may also lead to the revocation of your own license. If an accident occurs while the car is lent out, the driver is responsible in principle. However, if you knew or should have known they had been drinking or lacked a license and still handed over the vehicle, the court will determine you are at fault and must pay a portion based on the degree of fault. In a case published by the Supreme People's Court (China) in May 2026, a car owner who knew a dining companion had been drinking but still handed over the car was ordered to pay 40% of the compensation alongside the driver (applicable nationwide in China).
Do not lend your bank card, SIM card, or payment accounts to anyone; "point running" (lending accounts to help transfer money) is not a part-time job
A

Renting, lending, or selling bank cards, SIM cards, or payment accounts to others is itself a violation of the law. Fines range from 1 to 10 times the illegal gains; if there are no gains or gains are under ⟦20000⟧, the maximum fine is ⟦200000⟧; serious cases lead to up to 15 days of administrative detention. If you know they are being used for crimes and still help receive or transfer money, it can become the crime of assisting information network criminal activities (China), punishable by up to 3 years in prison.
Free. If someone says "borrow your card to run some money through, I'll pay you a few hundred yuan," simply refuse.

Renting, lending, buying, or selling SIM cards, bank accounts, payment accounts, or internet accounts is itself a violation of the law (China). Illegal gains are confiscated, with an additional fine of 1 to 10 times that amount. If there are no gains or gains are under ⟦20000⟧, the maximum fine is ⟦200000⟧. Serious cases lead to up to 15 days of administrative detention. It can also be recorded in credit files, lead to restricted account functions, and suspension of non-counter transactions (only allowed at the bank counter). Knowing others are using the network to commit crimes and still assisting them with tasks like payments or transfers is a crime. The charge is the crime of assisting information network criminal activities (China), punishable by up to 3 years in prison and a fine (applicable nationwide in China).
Check your credit report for free twice a year to see if there are any loans or cards you didn't apply for
A

You can check your credit report online for free twice a year; it takes ten minutes. Use the official website of the Credit Reference Center of the People's Bank of China or a bank app; do not use third-party "credit check" apps. Negative information is stored for 5 years from the date the event ended; it must be deleted after that. If something is incorrect, you have the right to dissent, and they must provide a written response within 20 days.
Free. Check online; it takes ten minutes.

Administrative regulations (China) state "personal information subjects have the right to receive their own credit report for free twice a year." The storage period for negative information is "5 years from the date the negative behavior or event ended; it must be deleted after 5 years." If you find inaccuracies in the report, you can file a dissent. The credit reporting organization or the organization that provided the information must provide a written response within 20 days of receiving the dissent.
If there is a conflict, call the police first; do not strike first, as striking first makes it easier for the other party's counterattack to be considered justifiable defense
A

Hitting someone: 5 to 10 days of administrative detention and a fine of five hundred to ⟦1000⟧. Group fighting, hitting the elderly, pregnant women, children, or the disabled, or hitting multiple times: 10 to 15 days of detention and a fine of one to two thousand. Hitting someone and causing minor injury is a criminal case, punishable by up to 3 years in prison; serious injury is 3 to 10 years. Two people hitting each other is not considered justifiable defense, so back away and call the police first.
Free. Back away to a crowded area and call the police, so the other party's actions are captured on camera. The difficulty lies in refraining from arguing back or pushing.

Hitting others or intentionally causing injury: 5 to 10 days of administrative detention, plus a fine of ⟦500~1000⟧. Group fighting, hitting the elderly, pregnant women, children, the disabled, hitting someone multiple times, or hitting multiple people at once results in harsher punishment: 10 to 15 days of detention, plus a fine of ⟦1000~2000⟧. Brawling is punished administratively as provocative behavior under the Law on Penalties for Administration of Public Security (China), not yet a criminal offense, with a maximum of 15 days of detention and a fine of ⟦2000⟧; provocative behavior is picking quarrels and provoking trouble without cause. Intentionally injuring others that constitutes a crime is punishable by up to 3 years in prison; causing serious injury is 3 to 10 years. Two people hitting each other is legally called a mutual brawl and is not considered justifiable defense. However, if the other party strikes first, the counterattack is not clearly excessive, or you tried to avoid it but the other party continued to attack, your counterattack is usually recognized as defense. Striking back excessively is called exceeding the limits of defense and must meet two conditions simultaneously: clearly exceeding the necessary limit and causing serious damage. Even if it is exceeded, the penalty must be reduced or exempted (applicable nationwide in China; 治安管理处罚法 (Law on Penalties for Administration of Public Security of China) applicable from January 1, 2026).
If you are being assaulted and cannot avoid it, you can fight back, but only strike the person currently attacking; stop when they stop
A

When someone is assaulting you or others, taking action to stop them and injuring them is not a criminal responsibility as long as it is not clearly excessive. If the other party is committing assault, murder, robbery, rape, kidnapping, then injuring or killing them is not considered excessive. However, you may only strike the person currently attacking; stop when they stop. Even if the final conclusion is in your favor, you may still be prosecuted first and detained for several days.

Legal fees start from several thousand yuan; if in financial difficulty, you can apply for legal aid. The cost mainly lies afterward: you are often prosecuted first for the crime of intentional injury, must cooperate with the investigation, and may even be detained for over ten days. The difficulty lies in staying calm during those days.

The 刑法 (Criminal Law of China) defines justifiable defense. When the interests of the state, public interests, the person, property, or other rights of oneself or others are being unlawfully infringed upon, taking action to stop it and injuring the infringer is justifiable defense and carries no criminal responsibility. The same article also states: "justifiable defense that clearly exceeds the necessary limit and causes serious damage shall bear criminal responsibility, but the penalty shall be reduced or exempted." Another clause: "defense against ongoing violent crimes such as assault, murder, robbery, rape, kidnapping, and other violent crimes that seriously endanger physical safety, causing injury or death to the unlawful infringer, does not constitute exceeding the limits of defense and carries no criminal responsibility." Guiding opinions from two departments and one ministry (China) draw more detailed boundaries. Determining that defense exceeded limits requires both "clearly exceeding the necessary limit" and "causing serious damage"; lacking one is insufficient. "Causing serious damage" means causing serious injury or death to the infringer; minor or lesser injuries do not count. Only when the infringer has truly lost the ability to infringe, or has truly abandoned the infringement, is the infringement considered over. Defense must be aimed at the infringer themselves. If the infringement is very minor and you recognize this, yet immediately use a method sufficient to cause serious injury or death to stop it, it is not recognized as defensive behavior. The process cost is shown in official precedents. Guiding Case No. 47, the Yu Haiming case: on the night of August 27, 2018, police initiated an investigation for "intentional injury." On September 1, Kunshan City Police, based on Article 20, Paragraph 3 of the Criminal Law of China, recognized it as justifiable defense and dismissed the case. Guiding Case No. 45, the Chen case: a student surrounded and beaten by 9 people used a knife to fight back, injuring 3 seriously. Police investigated him for suspected intentional injury and criminally detained him. The procuratorate recognized it as justifiable defense and did not approve the arrest, so the police released him. After detention, if the police believe an arrest is necessary, they must request approval from the procuratorate within 3 days. Special cases can be extended by 1 to 4 days. For major suspects committing crimes across regions, multiple times, or in groups, it can be extended up to 30 days. The procuratorate then decides within 7 days (applicable nationwide in China).
If you have a grudge against someone (unpaid wages, being fired, being cheated out of money), seek mediation, arbitration, or litigation; do not go looking to settle scores personally
A

By following legal channels, the worst outcome is not getting your money back. By seeking revenge, you still won't get the money back, and for murder, the maximum penalty is death. Xu Jiajin was not granted a graduation certificate and was dissatisfied with his internship compensation; he killed 8 people and injured 17 with a knife and has been executed. For unpaid wages, file a complaint or seek arbitration; in 2024, ⟦8650000000⟧ was recovered nationwide (China) for 654,000 people.

Free of charge; both complaints and arbitration are free. You must make one or two trips and wait for several months. The difficulty lies in restraining yourself from taking action during those months.

Legal channels have official data. In 2024, labor inspectors nationwide (China) handled 137,000 cases, recovering ⟦8650000000⟧ in wages for 654,000 people. Another 998 people were convicted of the crime of failing to pay labor remuneration (China). For unpaid wages, how to complain to labor inspectors or apply for labor arbitration is detailed in Chapter 7, Section 2. The price of revenge is recorded in Article 232 of the 刑法 (Criminal Law of China): "Whoever intentionally kills another shall be sentenced to death, life imprisonment, or fixed-term imprisonment of not less than ten years; if the circumstances are relatively minor, he shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than ten years." Official case: Xu Jiajin failed his exams and was not granted a graduation certificate, and was dissatisfied with his internship compensation. On November 16, 2024, he returned to the Wuxi Vocational Institute of Arts and Technology and committed a knife attack, killing 8 people and injuring 17. He was sentenced to death in the first instance for intentional homicide and deprived of political rights for life; the execution was approved by the Supreme People's Court (China) on January 20, 2025. He was dissatisfied with the school and the compensation, but the victims were his classmates, and he did not receive a single cent of that compensation (Applicable throughout China)

No matter how much you hate, do not take it out on uninvolved people: driving into a crowd or committing assault in public is charged as endangering public safety by dangerous means, with a minimum of three years in prison, ten years to life or death if there are fatalities
A

Driving into a crowd or committing assault in public is charged as endangering public safety by dangerous means (China). Even if no one is injured, the sentence is at least three years. If there are fatalities, it is ten years or more, life imprisonment, or death. Fan Weiqiu, dissatisfied with the division of property in his divorce, drove into a crowd exercising at the Zhuhai Sports Center, killing 35 people and injuring 43; he has been executed.
Free of charge. The difficulty lies in suppressing that thought in the heat of anger.

Article 114 of the 刑法 (Criminal Law of China): "Whoever commits arson, breaches a dike, causes an explosion, spreads poison, radioactive substances, infectious disease pathogens... or uses other dangerous means to endanger public safety, if no serious consequences are caused, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than ten years." Even if no one is injured, it is at least three years. Article 115: if it causes serious injury or death to others, or causes heavy losses to public or private property, the sentence is fixed-term imprisonment of not less than ten years, life imprisonment, or death. Official case: Fan Weiqiu, due to a failed marriage and life setbacks, and dissatisfied with the property division in his divorce, "decided to vent his personal grievances by driving into a crowd." On the evening of November 11, 2024, he drove into a crowd exercising at the Zhuhai City Sports Center. This incident killed 35 people and injured 43. He was sentenced to death in the first instance for endangering public safety by dangerous means and deprived of political rights for life. On January 20, 2025, the execution was approved by the Supreme People's Court (China). He was dissatisfied with the property division, but the people he hit were joggers he did not know at all (Applicable throughout China)
If the thought "take others down with me" or "die together and get it over with" arises, treat it as a medical emergency: leave the area, give your car keys and knives to someone else, and call 12356
B

The time from when this thought arises to when action is taken is very short. Among 82 survivors of suicide attempts, 47.6% said the time from the first thought to the act was no more than 10 minutes. Therefore, what needs to be done is not to "think it through," but to first put the steering wheel, knives, gas valves, and ropes one step away from yourself and endure those ten minutes. Then call 12356.
Free of charge. The difficulty lies in admitting that you are not okay at that moment, and in handing your belongings over to someone else.

The interval between thought and action is very short. Researchers interviewed 82 survivors of suicide attempts within three days of hospital admission. Among them, 47.6% said the time from the first thought to the attempt was no more than 10 minutes. A 10-year systematic review (combining ten years of studies for a single review) suggests that evidence for restricting lethal means is growing stronger. After controlling for painkillers, related suicides dropped by 43%. At common jumping sites, after barriers were installed, suicides dropped by 86% (ranging from 79% to 91%). Putting the steering wheel, knives, gas valves, and ropes one step away is to wait for those ten minutes to pass. 12356 is the unified national psychological support hotline (China), answering calls for at least 18 hours a day (Applicable throughout China, from May 1, 2025)

If someone nearby says "no one will have peace" or "I'm taking the kids with me," do not treat it as words spoken in anger: relatives can take them directly for an exam, and police must handle the report
A

If a family member says "no one will have peace" or "I'm taking the kids with me," relatives can take them to a hospital, and the hospital cannot refuse diagnosis. If diagnosed with a severe mental disorder and they have already acted or are about to cause trouble, hospitalization does not require their consent. If you cannot tell if it is anger or serious, call 12356 to ask first, or call 110 for the police. Hiding it for them is not helping them.

Registration and examination fees range from a few dozen to a few hundred yuan. One trip to the hospital takes half a day to a full day. The difficulty lies in finding the words to persuade them to go with you.

Paragraph 2, Article 28 of the 精神卫生法 (Mental Health Law of China) states: "If a person suspected of having a mental disorder commits an act that harms themselves or endangers the safety of others, or is at risk of harming themselves or endangering the safety of others, their close relatives, employer, or local public security organs shall immediately take measures to stop them and take them to a medical institution for a mental disorder diagnosis." The same article also stipulates: "medical institutions receiving suspected mental disorder patients for examination shall not refuse to diagnose them." Article 29 requires hospitals to keep such persons for immediate diagnosis by a licensed psychiatrist and to provide a timely conclusion. Article 30 stipulates that inpatient treatment is based on the principle of voluntariness. However, there is an exception: if the diagnostic conclusion shows a severe mental disorder and the patient "has committed an act endangering the safety of others, or is at risk of endangering the safety of others." For this group, inpatient treatment must be provided without their consent. Threatening to hit someone is itself grounds to call 110 directly. Writing threatening letters or using other methods to threaten the personal safety of others can lead to administrative detention for up to 5 days or a fine of up to ⟦1000⟧. Threatening to commit arson, cause an explosion, or spread dangerous substances, thereby disturbing public order, can lead to 5 to 10 days of detention and a fine of up to ⟦1000⟧ (Applicable throughout China, 治安管理处罚法 (Public Security Administration Punishment Law of China) effective from January 1, 2026)
Do not insult people online, do not spread fabricated news, and do not share unverified stories; if you are cyberbullied, save evidence first and then report it to the police
A

Publicly insulting others or fabricating facts to defame them: administrative detention for up to 5 days or a fine of up to ⟦1000⟧; for relatively serious circumstances, 5 to 10 days of detention. Serious cases constitute the crime of insult or defamation (China), punishable by up to 3 years in prison. Conversely, when you are cyberbullied, insulted, or defamed, you generally must sue in court yourself, so you must take screenshots, screen recordings, and save links yourself.

Free of charge. Think for ten more seconds before posting. If attacked, take screenshots, record the screen, save links and account IDs, complain to the platform first, then report to the police. The difficulty lies in being insulted and restraining yourself from insulting back.

Publicly insulting others or fabricating facts to defame others: administrative detention for up to 5 days or a fine of up to ⟦1000⟧. For relatively serious circumstances, 5 to 10 days of detention. Repeatedly sending insulting, threatening, or harassing messages, stalking, or surreptitiously filming and disseminating the private affairs of others is punished similarly. Intentionally spreading rumors to disturb public order leads to 5 to 10 days of detention. Serious circumstances constitute the crime of insult or defamation, punishable by up to 3 years in prison. If defamed online and evidence is difficult to collect, you can apply for the court to request police assistance (Applicable throughout China, 治安管理处罚法 (Public Security Administration Punishment Law of China) effective from January 1, 2026)
Read the entire paper before signing; do not sign on behalf of others, and do not sign blank papers
A

Once signed, it is valid; a fingerprint is as valid as a signature. "I didn't read it carefully" or "I thought it was a different paper" is very difficult for a court to accept. Spend a few extra minutes reading from beginning to end; if you don't understand, ask on the spot and take a photo to save. Do not sign for others, do not sign blank papers, and clearly mark the purpose on photocopies of ID documents.

Free of charge. Spend a few extra minutes reading contracts, loan notes, guarantee papers, or employment documents from beginning to end. Ask about anything you don't understand on the spot, then take a photo to save. The difficulty lies in reading it all slowly right in front of the other party.

A legally concluded contract is protected by law and binds both parties who signed. Once signed, it must be fully performed according to the agreement. Article 490 of the 民法典 (Civil Code of China) states: for a contract concluded in written form, the contract "is concluded when the parties sign, seal, or press their fingerprints." Fingerprinting is on par with signing and sealing as one of three equal methods; once fingerprinted, the contract is concluded. "I didn't read it carefully" or "I thought it was a different paper" is very difficult for a court to accept. Not signing ensures you do not bear debts or responsibilities that do not belong to you (Applicable throughout China)
When lending money, write a clear loan note; before guaranteeing for someone, think carefully if you are willing to pay on their behalf
A

A loan note must include: lender, borrower, amount, interest rate, term, repayment method, and signatures of both parties. Transfer money electronically, do not give cash; clear records make it easier to sue. When guaranteeing for others, check carefully for the word "joint." In a general guarantee, the creditor must fail to recover money from the borrower through enforcement before it's your turn; in a joint guarantee, the creditor can demand payment directly from you.

Free of charge. Use a piece of paper to clearly record the lender, borrower, amount, interest rate, term, and repayment method, with both parties signing. Transfer the money to leave a trail; do not give cash.

A loan contract must be in writing, typically including the type of loan, currency, purpose, amount, interest rate, term, and repayment method. Having all details makes it easier to sue. If a guarantee contract does not specify the type of guarantee or is unclear, it is considered a general guarantee (China). A general guarantor is protected by priority. The creditor must first sue in court or arbitration, then apply for compulsory enforcement against the borrower's assets. Only if the debt is still not fully paid after enforcement is it your turn to pay. Conversely, signing a "joint and several liability guarantee" removes this layer of protection, and the creditor can demand payment directly from you (Applicable throughout China)
Claiming rights has a time limit: 3 years for civil litigation, 1 year for labor arbitration; once expired, the other party only needs to say "the statute of limitations has expired"
A

The statute of limitations for civil litigation is 3 years, starting from the day you know your rights were infringed. Once expired, the court will not raise it automatically, but if the other party says "the statute of limitations has expired" in court, it is enough: the debt still exists, you just can't recover it. Before the 3 years end, a recorded debt collection message can restart the 3-year period. Labor disputes are a different system, with a 1-year arbitration period.
Free of charge. Do not just demand debt in your heart; use WeChat, SMS, email, or registered mail to leave a trail.

The 民法典 (Civil Code of China) stipulates that "the statute of limitations for applying to a people's court for the protection of civil rights is three years." The starting point is "from the day the right holder knows or should have known that their rights have been infringed and knows who the obligor is," i.e., from the day you know you've been harmed and know who to find. The maximum is 20 years from the date of infringement. After the period expires, "the obligor may raise a defense of expiration to refuse performance." The court will not examine the statute of limitations on its own, but if the other party raises it in court, it is effective: the debt still exists, it just can no longer be recovered. Four actions can interrupt the statute of limitations, after which the 3 years restart from the beginning. First, you demand the debtor perform the obligation. Second, the other party agrees to perform. Third, you file a lawsuit or apply for arbitration. Fourth, other cases with equivalent effect. The interruption must occur before the 3 years expire; demanding after the deadline does not restart the clock. For installment agreements, it counts from the due date of the final installment. Four types of claims are not limited by the statute of limitations. First, claims to stop infringement, remove obstacles, or eliminate danger. Second, claims to recover one's registered real estate or movable property. Third, claims for child support, elderly support, or spousal maintenance. Fourth, other cases provided by law. Labor disputes are a different system: the arbitration period is 1 year, starting from the day the infringement was known or should have been known. However, "while the labor relationship exists, disputes arising from unpaid wages are not limited by the arbitration period in paragraph 1 of this article; but if the labor relationship terminates, it must be brought within one year from the date of termination" (Applicable throughout China)
If sued or under enforcement, report assets truthfully and pay what you can; do not transfer houses or money to relatives, friends, or companies
A

Giving away a house or fake-transferring it to a company, or transferring money to relatives and friends to make a judgment unenforceable, constitutes the crime of refusing to execute a judgment or order (China). This crime is punishable by up to 3 years in prison, or 3 to 7 years for especially serious circumstances. Relatives or friends who knowingly help hide money or transfer titles are considered accomplices, and the money will still be recovered. Refusing to report or falsely reporting assets can result in a fine of up to ⟦100000⟧ for individuals and detention for up to 15 days.

Free of charge. Report assets as required by the court: what you currently have, and what you had in the year prior to receiving the enforcement notice. Pay what you can first. If you cannot pay in full, negotiate a settlement or installment plan with the applicant for enforcement, i.e., the creditor.

The act of dissipating assets itself constitutes the crime. The Standing Committee of the National People's Congress of China once interpreted Article 313 of the 刑法 (Criminal Law of China). The interpretation directly includes "the person subject to enforcement hiding, transferring, intentionally destroying assets, or transferring assets for no consideration, or transferring assets at obviously unreasonably low prices, making the judgment or order unenforceable" in the list of "having the ability to execute but refusing to do so, under serious circumstances." Hiding money, transferring money, intentionally smashing your own belongings, giving things away, or selling them cheaply to make a judgment unenforceable all count. A 2024 interpretation by the two courts (Supreme People's Court and Supreme People's Procuratorate of China) added ten more cases. These include using fake mediation or fake transfers to dispose of property rights. It also includes buying others' assets at obviously unreasonably high prices or guaranteeing others' debts. These are all intentional hollowings of assets that should have been used to pay your debts. The crime of refusing to execute a judgment or order is punishable by up to 3 years. Especially serious circumstances are punishable by 3 to 7 years plus a fine. Especially serious cases include: using fake litigation, fake arbitration, or fake notarization to obstruct enforcement; gathering a crowd to storm an enforcement scene; surrounding, detaining, or beating enforcement officers; or causing the applicant for enforcement to commit suicide or self-harm due to non-execution. Outsiders who are not parties to the case but knowingly collude to help hide money or transfer titles are punished as accomplices. Illegally disposed assets must be recovered according to law or forced to be returned/compensated. Taking action to dissipate assets after the defendant receives notice to participate in litigation and before the judgment takes effect also counts. Civilly, for gifts or transfers at obviously unreasonably low prices, the creditor can apply to the court to cancel the transfer. For refusing to report or falsely reporting assets, the court can fine individuals up to ⟦100000⟧. Detention for up to 15 days is also possible (Applicable throughout China, interpretation by the two courts from December 2024)
If restricted from consumption or placed on the list of dishonest persons, first check which specific clause you were listed under, and apply for correction if it can be fixed
A

First, distinguish between being restricted from consumption and being on the list of dishonest persons; these are two different things. There are only six cases for being placed on the dishonest list, with a 2-year term; once fulfilled, it must be removed within 3 working days. High-level consumption restrictions ban nine types of spending, including G-series high-speed trains; items necessary for living or business can be applied for on a case-by-case basis.

Free of charge. Go to the enforcement court to check which item you were listed under. Prepare documents proving you have paid, followed the judgment (proof of performance), or prepare security documents. For consumption necessary for living or business, submit an application each time. The difficulty lies in having to make multiple trips and apply repeatedly.

There are only six cases for being included in the list of dishonest persons subject to enforcement (China). First, having the ability to perform but refusing to do so. Second, forging evidence or using violence/threats to obstruct or resist enforcement. Third, using fake litigation, fake arbitration, or hiding/transferring assets to evade enforcement. Fourth, violating the asset reporting system. Fifth, violating a consumption restriction order. Sixth, refusing to perform an enforcement settlement agreement without justifiable reasons. If adequate and effective security has been provided, or if assets seized, detained, or frozen are sufficient to pay the debt, one cannot be listed under item one (refusing despite ability). Minors subject to enforcement cannot be listed. The listing term is 2 years. Using violence/threats to obstruct/resist enforcement with serious circumstances, or multiple dishonest acts, can extend this by 1 to 3 years. If performance is completed, a settlement agreement is fulfilled, or the court decides to terminate enforcement... (seven cases in total), the court must remove the listing within 3 working days. Active performance or proactive correction of dishonest behavior can lead to early removal. Individuals restricted from consumption are prohibited from nine types of high-level consumption and non-essential living/work spending. First, flying, taking soft sleepers on trains, or second-class cabins or above on ships. Second, high-level consumption at star-rated hotels, nightclubs, or golf courses. Third, purchasing real estate, or building, expanding, or high-end decorating of houses. Fourth, renting offices in high-end office buildings, hotels, or apartments. Fifth, purchasing vehicles not necessary for business. Sixth, tourism or vacations. Seventh, sending children to high-fee private schools. Eighth, paying high insurance premiums for investment-linked insurance products. Ninth, taking any seat on G-series high-speed trains, or first-class seats or above on other high-speed trains. If one of these is necessary for living or business, one must apply to the court and receive approval first. If truly effective security is provided or the applicant for enforcement agrees, the court can lift high-level consumption restrictions (Applicable throughout China)
Scammed while shopping online or buying second-hand goods: complain to the platform first, then report to the police, then consider if it is worth suing
A

Find the platform first. Platforms have security deposits and penalty rules, providing the fastest resolution. Then report to the police: being scammed for ⟦3000~10000⟧ or more is enough to constitute the crime of fraud (China); each province has its own threshold, and if it's below that, it's a public security penalty. If you want to sue, online shopping disputes can be filed at the court in the place of delivery; for small amounts, use small claims procedures, which finish within 2 months and allow online filing.

Complaining to the platform and reporting to the police are both free. When suing, if the disputed amount does not exceed ⟦10000⟧, the case acceptance fee is ⟦50⟧; using summary procedures, mediation, or withdrawing the case reduces it by half. Filing, appearing in court, and enforcement each take at least half a day to a full day; online filing saves travel time. You must save order records, chat messages, transfer history, and delivery slips. The difficulty lies in not giving up halfway when having to travel back and forth.

Fraud of ⟦3000~10000⟧ or more is a "relatively large amount" for the crime of fraud (China); each province sets its own local threshold within this range. This level is punishable by up to 3 years in prison, with or without a fine. If it doesn't reach the criminal threshold, it's handled as a public security administration penalty: administrative detention for 5 to 10 days, or a fine of up to ⟦2000⟧. For relatively serious circumstances, detention is 10 to 15 days, and the fine can be up to ⟦3000⟧. Regarding civil matters, online shopping contract disputes can be sued at the court in the place of delivery, so you don't have to travel to where the seller lives. If the disputed amount does not exceed 50% of the previous year's average annual salary of employees in the province, small claims procedures apply. Small claims litigation uses a single-instance final judgment system (effective immediately, no appeal). It concludes within 2 months of acceptance, or 3 months for summary procedures. Civil litigation can be done online with the same effect as in-person (applies throughout China, 民事诉讼法 (Civil Procedure Law of China) from January 2024, 治安管理处罚法 (Public Security Administration Punishment Law of China) from January 2026).
Giving large sums while dating or in marriage: think carefully before handing it over; once given, in principle, it cannot be reclaimed
A

Once money is handed over, in principle, it cannot be reclaimed. For gifted items, they can only be revoked at will before the title is transferred to the other party. Once the title is transferred, it can only be revoked in three cases: the other party seriously infringes upon you or your close relatives, fails to fulfill a support obligation to you, or fails to perform an agreed-upon obligation. Therefore, before transferring a large sum, think clearly: is this a loan or a gift?

Costs nothing. Before transferring a large sum, think for a moment: is this a loan or a gift? If it's a loan, write a promissory note and record "loan" in the transfer remarks. The difficulty lies in speaking those words.

For gifted items, the gift can be revoked before the title is transferred; the law calls this milestone the transfer of property rights. Once the transfer or title change is complete, there are only three cases for revocation. First, the recipient seriously infringes upon you or your close relatives. Second, they have a support obligation to you but fail to fulfill it. Third, they fail to perform the obligations agreed upon in the gift contract. Gifts and cash gifts given on significant commemorative occasions such as holidays or birthdays that are not of great value are not considered betrothal gifts (China). Daily expenses to express or cultivate affection are also not considered betrothal gifts. These two types do not have to be returned like betrothal gifts upon breakup (applies throughout China).
Betrothal gifts should be transferred with clear remarks and messages kept; those who use marriage as a pretext to demand money can be sued for its return
A

The law prohibits using marriage as a pretext to demand property, and courts support the return of such funds. If the marriage was never registered, if it was registered but the couple never actually lived together, or if giving the betrothal gift before marriage caused the giver financial hardship, it can be reclaimed. If registered and lived together, it is usually not returned. Therefore, betrothal gifts, wedding gold, and "name-change" money should all be transferred with clear remarks; whoever provided the money should keep the evidence, regardless of gender.

Costs nothing. Betrothal gifts, the "three gold items," and name-change money should all be transferred, with the purpose of the funds clearly stated in the transfer remarks. For anything discussed verbally, leave a trail via text messages or have family members present to confirm.

The law prohibits using marriage as a pretext to demand property. If one party uses the name of betrothal gifts as a pretext for marriage to demand property, and the other party requests its return, the court will support it. There are three cases where return is supported. First, marriage registration was not completed. Second, registration was completed but they never actually lived together. Third, betrothal gifts were given before marriage to the extent that the giver fell into financial hardship. If registered and lived together, it is usually not returned. However, if the cohabitation period was short and the betrothal gift was excessively high, the court will determine a return ratio. This ratio considers how the money was actually spent, whether there was a dowry, whether there was a pregnancy or children, and whether either party was at fault. Cases where there was no registration but the couple lived together are also handled using such ratios (National China, from February 2024).
Pre-marital assets are nothing to fear, but adding a name to a house deed or parental contributions must be documented in writing beforehand
A

Pre-marital property is your separate property and does not become joint property just because you have been married for many years. Spouses can agree in writing that their respective pre-marital and post-marital assets remain separate. One point to note: if you promised to add the other person's name to the house, you can still retract it before the title transfer procedure is done; once transferred, it belongs to them. Upon divorce, a party who hides, transfers, squanders, or fakes debts may be awarded less or no share of the property.

Writing a property agreement yourself costs nothing; notarizing it incurs a fee. When parents provide money, ask them to write a one-sentence confirmation. This whole process takes only a few hours once. The difficulty is bringing up the topic of money with family members.

Pre-marital property is personal property and does not become joint property due to the length of the marriage. Spouses may agree in writing: pre-marital property and post-marital income shall be separate, joint, or partially joint; this agreement is binding on both parties. If parents provide money to buy a house before marriage, it is considered a gift to their own child unless clearly stated it is for both. If parents provide money after marriage, follow the agreement; if no agreement exists, it is handled according to joint property principles. Before or during marriage, if there is an agreement to gift one party's house to the other or make it joint property, it can still be revoked before the registration change procedure is completed. Once registered, it belongs to the other party. Upon divorce, a party who conceals, transfers, sells, squanders joint property, or fakes debts may be awarded less or no share (National China).
Before marriage, check the other person's marital status; using marriage as a front to scam money will lead to prosecution for fraud
A

Bigamy (marrying again while already married) is void. Marrying while already having a spouse, or marrying someone knowing they already have a spouse, is punishable by up to 2 years in prison. Using marriage as a front to scam money leads to prosecution for fraud; especially large amounts are punishable by 10 years to life imprisonment. Before registering, check the marital status listed on the other person's ID card and household registration booklet.

Costs nothing. Before registering, check the marital status on the other person's ID card and household registration booklet. For large transfers of money or assets, keep transfer histories and messages.

Bigamy is void. Marrying while having a spouse, or knowingly marrying someone who has a spouse, is punishable by up to 2 years in prison. Defrauding public or private property of a relatively large amount is punishable by up to 3 years in prison and a fine. A large amount is punishable by 3 to 10 years. An especially large amount is punishable by 10 years to life imprisonment, along with a fine or confiscation of property (National China).
Home repairs, vehicle inspections, renovations: ask for the price first before allowing work, and stand nearby to watch from start to finish
B

Home appliance repairers must disclose pricing, provide receipts and invoices, and are forbidden from faking malfunctions or replacing good parts; serious violations can result in fines up to ⟦30000⟧. All businesses must clearly post prices and cannot charge more than the posted price. Therefore, before allowing work, ask clearly about the price and parts to be replaced; after repair, get the receipt and invoice, and keep the old parts. If overcharged, call 12315 first.

Costs nothing. Before allowing work, ask clearly about the pricing method and which parts need replacing; photograph the quote or have them text it. After repair, get the repair slip and invoice, and keep the old parts. You also need to stand nearby and watch for an hour or two. The difficulty is supervising throughout without leaving.

Home appliance repair businesses must disclose price lists for services and parts, quality standards, warranty periods, and complaint numbers. They must provide customers with repair service slips and invoices, accurately recording the items and details repaired. They must not fabricate, exaggerate, or invent repair items, report non-existent part failures, or intentionally replace parts that are functioning normally. Serious violations are fined up to ⟦30000⟧. All businesses must post prices clearly, must not increase prices beyond the posted rate, and must not collect any fees not clearly stated. Luring customers with low prices then charging high prices, or fake discounts, constitutes price fraud. Businesses must clearly and visibly record the items, content, price, and calculation method of services, and must not use false or misleading advertising (National China).
Do not be a "nominal legal representative," do not lend your ID to others to register a company
B

The law defaults to the legal representative being the person managing the business; the phrase "I'm just a name on paper, I don't know anything" is not a valid excuse to escape liability. If a legal representative causes damage to others while working for the company, the company compensates first, but can then sue you for reimbursement if you were at fault. If you are already a nominal representative, the Company Law (China) allows you to resign, and the company must appoint a new legal representative within 30 days.
Costs nothing. If someone asks you to "just help by using your name, you don't have to do anything," just say no.

The legal representative is assumed by a board member or manager who is actually managing the company's affairs; the law defaults to you being the manager. If a legal representative causes damage to others while working for the company, the company compensates first. After compensating, the company can seek reimbursement from the legal representative at fault (reclaim that money). Board members and senior management have duties of loyalty and diligence to the company (being loyal to the company, working with full dedication). If they cause damage to others while working and are intentional or grossly negligent, they must also pay compensation out of their own pocket. Legally, "not knowing" is not an excuse to escape liability. Article 10 of the Company Law clearly states: "If the legal representative resigns, the company shall determine a new legal representative within thirty days from the date the legal representative resigns." (National China, from July 2024).
Do not carry items for strangers when crossing borders; do not accept parcels of unknown origin
B

The advice from the Consular Affairs Bureau of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (China) for citizens going abroad is: do not carry luggage or items for others, especially prohibited items or things you don't recognize. Every country prohibits the entry of drugs; if the luggage is in your hands, you are the one who must answer and declare it when passing through customs. The same applies to receiving express delivery items domestically, especially when asked to pay upfront and be reimbursed later.
Costs nothing. Just refuse.

The advice from the Consular Affairs Bureau of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (China) for citizens going abroad is "strictly avoid carrying luggage or items for others, especially prohibited items or things you are not clear about." The same passage clearly states "all countries prohibit the entry of drugs, protected animal and plant products...", requiring you to "truthfully declare restricted items and cash carried according to regulations," and "truthfully answer questions from customs and immigration officers...". If you carry items for others and cannot say what is inside, you cannot truthfully declare them. It is the same domestically. The 2025 risk warning from the Hubei Provincial Postal Administration (China) states that among the forms of delivery scams is "receiving high-value goods on behalf of others," and clearly notes "any request to pay upfront for 'fake orders' or 'tasks' via delivery is a scam."

Dogs must be leashed: causing trouble without a leash is strict liability (you must compensate regardless of fault), compensate to the end. Dogs must also be vaccinated against rabies on time and registered
A

If a dog bites someone, in principle, you must compensate whether you are at fault or not; only if you prove the other person was intentional or grossly negligent can compensation be reduced or waived. Without a leash, the only remaining reason for mitigation is "the other person was intentional"; more serious cases can lead to detention. Dogs not vaccinated against rabies as required will be ordered to correct, and may be fined. If a dangerous dog of a prohibited breed bites someone, there are no grounds for exemption from liability.

A leash costs a few dozen yuan. Rabies vaccinations and dog registration also cost money, with fees varying by location. The difficulty is remembering to leash the dog every time you go out and taking the dog for vaccinations when due.

If a domestic animal injures someone, the keeper or manager must compensate; the law calls this liability for infringement. Only if it is proven that the injured person intentionally provoked the animal or was grossly negligent can compensation be waived or reduced. However, if management regulations are violated and safety measures are not taken—for example, failing to leash when required—the only reason for mitigation is "the infringed person was intentional." If a dangerous dog of a prohibited breed injures someone, there is no ground for exemption. Article 89 of the Public Security Administration Punishment Law (China) stipulates: failing to take safety measures for an animal, allowing it to injure others, results in a fine of up to ⟦1000⟧. More serious cases result in detention for 5 to 10 days. Article 30 of the Animal Epidemic Prevention Law (China) requires dog owners to vaccinate against rabies periodically as regulated. Then, take the vaccination certificate issued by an animal medical institution (such as a pet hospital) to register the dog in your place of residence. Dogs must wear tags and be leashed as regulated when taken out. Article 92 of the same law stipulates that failing to vaccinate a dog against rabies as required will result in the agricultural and rural department ordering correction within a time limit. A fine of up to ⟦1000⟧ may be imposed. Failure to correct within the time limit results in a fine of ⟦1000~5000⟧, and an animal medical institution will be entrusted to handle it on your behalf at your expense.
If the other person is intoxicated to the point of unconsciousness, sleeping, or may be under 14, do not have sexual intercourse
B

Someone who is intoxicated to the point of unconsciousness or sleeping cannot give valid consent. Having sex at that time is legally considered rape, with a basic sentencing range of 3 to 10 years in prison. The safe way is to not have sex; when the party is over, hand the person over to their own friends or family. To determine age, see Chapter 9, Section 18 (under 14 years old).
Costs nothing. The price is stopping the act right then and there. The difficulty is being able to stop on the spot.

Article 236 of the Criminal Law (China): whoever rapes a woman by violence, coercion, or other means shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than three years but not more than ten years. "Other means" is not just physical force; if the other person is unconscious or sleeping, they cannot give valid consent, which falls exactly under these words. Raving a woman under serious circumstances, raping multiple women, etc., is punishable by ten years to life imprisonment or death. The same article also stipulates that sexual intercourse with a girl under fourteen years of age is considered rape and is punished more severely. For how to determine if it is a girl, see Chapter 9, Section 18 (under 14 years old). A legal outreach article from the Xicheng District People's Procuratorate in Beijing (China) states that drugging or intoxicating a woman "and then sexually assaulting her also constitutes the crime of rape." The key is "whether it is against the victim's true inner will"; whether the victim resisted at the time "is not the key." Article 237 of the Criminal Law (China) stipulates the crime of forcible indecency: whoever forcibly commits indecency against another person by violence, coercion, or other means shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years or criminal detention (National China).

After sex or nude chatting, if the other person threatens to report you to the police, leak photos, or notify your employer to demand money: do not give a single cent, do not delete a single line of messages, and report it to the police immediately
A

Using "I will go to the police" or "I will send photos to your employer" to force you to give money is extortion. Do not give a single cent, do not delete a single line of messages, and report it to the police immediately. If the other person actually leaks real photos, they are further violating your privacy. Extorting ⟦2000~5000⟧ or more is punishable by up to 3 years in prison; ⟦30000~100000⟧ or more is punishable by 3 to 10 years in prison.

Costs no money. Take screenshots of the other person's account, messages, and payment codes, and bring your phone to the police station. The difficulty lies in suppressing the thought of "giving money to settle things quietly first."

Article 274 of the Criminal Law (China): extorting public or private property, if the amount is relatively large or if extortion is committed multiple times, is punishable by fixed-term imprisonment of up to three years, criminal detention, or public surveillance, with or instead of a fine. Criminal detention is short-term detention; public surveillance is non-custodial but restricts freedom; "with or instead of a fine" means an additional fine or only a fine. If the amount is large or there are other serious circumstances, the punishment is three to ten years in prison, with a fine. If the amount is especially large or there are other especially serious circumstances, the punishment is ten years or more in prison, with a fine. The Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate (China) also issued an interpretation document on several issues regarding the application of law in handling criminal extortion cases (Interpretation No. 10/2013, effective from April 27, 2013). Article 1 of this document defines three monetary thresholds. Extorting property worth ⟦2000~5000⟧ or more is a "relatively large amount." From ⟦30000~100000⟧ or more is a "large amount." From ⟦300000~500000⟧ or more is an "especially large amount." Article 3: committing extortion three or more times within two years must be considered "multiple extortions" (National China). Article 1032 of the Civil Code (China): no organization or individual shall infringe upon the privacy of others by spying, harassing, disclosing, or making public... Article 1033 prohibits harassing the peace of private life via telephone, messages, messaging apps, etc. Therefore, if the other person leaks real photos, they are further violating your privacy, which is not your fault. The original warning regarding this type of case from the Fujian Provincial Public Security Department (China) is: "you must keep the evidence, call 110 immediately, and absolutely do not transfer any more money."

If you are falsely accused of fabricated stories, you can request prosecution: if it reaches the level of public security punishment, detention starts from 5 days; if it reaches the level of a crime, imprisonment is up to 3 years
A

Fabricating stories to falsely accuse others in order to have them prosecuted is itself a violation of the law. The penalty is detention for up to 5 days or a fine of up to ⟦1000⟧; for more serious cases, detention is from 5 to 10 days. If it reaches the level of a crime, it is the crime of false accusation and framing, punishable by up to 3 years in prison. However, remembering incorrectly or making a mistaken report does not count; to prosecute the other person, you must prove they intentionally made a false accusation.
Costs no money. Go to the police station to report it, clearly stating the other person fabricated the story. The difficulty lies in providing something that proves they intentionally fabricated it.

Article 50 of the Law on Public Security Administration Punishments (China) (revised June 27, 2025, effective January 1, 2026) regulates false accusations. Fabricating facts to falsely accuse and frame others, aiming to have them criminally prosecuted or punished under public security administration, shall be punished. The penalty is detention for up to five days or a fine of up to ⟦1000⟧. For more serious cases, detention is from five to ten days, possibly with a fine of up to ⟦1000⟧. Article 243 of the Criminal Law (China) regulates the crime of false accusation and framing. Fabricating facts to falsely accuse and frame others, aiming to have them criminally prosecuted, if the circumstances are serious, is punishable by fixed-term imprisonment of up to three years, criminal detention, or public surveillance. If it causes serious consequences, the punishment is fixed-term imprisonment of three to ten years. State functionaries who commit the crimes in the above paragraph shall be punished more severely, meaning they are punished on the heavier side within the same sentencing range. If it is not an intentional false accusation but a mistaken report or an untruthful tip-off, the above two paragraphs do not apply. Remembering incorrectly or making a mistaken report will not lead to prosecution under these two paragraphs (National China).
If evidence is insufficient, an acquittal must be declared, and coerced confessions must be excluded; even after conviction, appeals and retrials are still possible
A

The threshold for conviction is stated in the Criminal Procedure Law (China): evidence used to conclude a case must be verified as true according to legal procedures, and considering the evidence as a whole, all reasonable doubt must be excluded. If this cannot be done, an acquittal must be declared. Confessions obtained through torture, or testimony obtained through violence or threats, must be excluded and cannot serve as a basis for judgment. After a judgment takes effect, you, your legal representative, and your close relatives can still appeal.

The procedure itself costs no money, but appeals and retrials are very time-consuming. Usually, a lawyer must be hired, with fees starting from several thousand yuan. If facing economic hardship, you can apply for legal aid; see section 5 of this chapter (if accused, hire a lawyer first). The difficulty is waiting through round after round without giving up.

Article 55 of the Criminal Procedure Law (China): reliable and sufficient evidence must meet the following conditions: all evidence used to conclude the case has been verified as true according to legal procedures, and considering the evidence as a whole, the concluded facts have excluded all reasonable doubt. Excluding reasonable doubt means that when combining all evidence of the case, the concluded facts cannot have any other possible explanation. Article 56: confessions of suspects or defendants obtained by torture or other illegal means, as well as testimony from witnesses or statements from victims obtained by violence, threats, or other illegal means, must be excluded. If evidence that must be excluded is discovered during investigation, review for prosecution, or trial, it must be excluded according to law and shall not be used as a basis for prosecution recommendations, prosecution decisions, or judgments. Article 200, point (3): if evidence is insufficient and the defendant cannot be found guilty, a verdict of not guilty must be rendered on the grounds that the evidence is insufficient and the charged crime is not established. Article 252 opens the path for appeals. Parties and their legal representatives or close relatives may file an appeal with the people's court or the people's procuratorate against judgments or decisions that have already taken effect. However, an appeal does not stay the execution of the judgment or decision. Article 253 lists cases where the people's court must conduct a retrial (National China).
If you are detained and then the case is dismissed, not prosecuted, or you are acquitted, apply for state compensation, calculated by the day
A

If you are held in custody or arrested and later the case is dismissed, not prosecuted, or you are acquitted, you can apply for state compensation. Days spent in detention are compensated daily; as of May 18, 2026, it is ⟦495.94⟧ per day. Serious consequences warrant additional compensation for mental distress. If you committed a crime but were exempted from prosecution due to minor circumstances, you are not compensated; cases involving expired statutes of limitations, being under the age of responsibility, or making a false confession also do not qualify.
Costs no money. Send the compensation application to the exact agency that made the decision to detain, arrest, prosecute, or judge you previously.

Article 17 of the State Compensation Law (China) lists several cases where victims have the right to compensation. First is detention: detaining a citizen in violation of the criminal procedure law, or lawful detention that exceeds the statutory time limit. Subsequently, there is a decision to dismiss the case, not to prosecute, or an acquittal terminating criminal liability. Second is arrest: after arresting a citizen, there is a decision to dismiss the case, not to prosecute, or an acquittal terminating criminal liability. Third is retrial: the case is retried under the trial supervision procedure and changed to not guilty, and the penalty of the original judgment has already been executed. The trial supervision procedure is the process of reviewing a judgment that has already taken effect. Article 33: for infringement of a citizen's personal freedom, daily compensation is calculated based on the average daily wage of national employees in the previous year. Article 35: if mental distress is caused, the influence must be eliminated, reputation restored, and an apology made to the victim within the scope of the infringement's impact; if serious consequences are caused, corresponding compensation for mental distress must be paid. Article 19 lists six cases where the state does not compensate. One is intentionally making a false confession or forging other evidence of guilt, leading to detention or conviction. Two is a person not liable for criminal responsibility under Articles 17 and 18 of the Criminal Law (China) being detained. For example, being under the age of criminal responsibility, or a person with mental illness causing harm while unable to recognize or control their behavior. Three is a person not prosecuted for criminal responsibility according to the criminal procedure law being detained. This includes cases where circumstances are clearly minor, the harm is not great, and it is not considered a crime; the statute of limitations has expired; or the suspect has died. It also includes cases where the criminal circumstances are minor and the procuratorate decides not to prosecute, often called relative non-prosecution (or discretionary non-prosecution). Minors granted conditional non-prosecution who complete the probation period without prosecution, and cases of non-prosecution after reconciliation with the victim, also fall under this. Four is individual acts of law enforcement personnel unrelated to the performance of official duties. Five is damage caused by one's own self-injury, self-harm, and other intentional acts. Six is other cases prescribed by law. A 2015 judicial interpretation by the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate (China) on criminal compensation, Article 7, reaffirms: the state does not compensate those not liable for criminal responsibility or those granted relative non-prosecution who were detained. However, if after prosecution the court wrongly sentences them to criminal detention, fixed-term imprisonment, or life imprisonment and it has been executed, the portion of detention following the determination of the judgment must still be compensated. Article 8 of this interpretation: if the law enforcement agency uses the reason "you made a false confession" or "you self-injured or self-harmed" to deny compensation, the agency must prove it. The Supreme People's Procuratorate (China) issued a notice in May 2026. The National Bureau of Statistics (China) released 2025 data on May 15, 2026. The average annual wage for employees in non-private urban units nationwide was approximately ⟦129000⟧ (⟦129441⟧). This calculates to an average daily wage of ⟦495.94⟧. Procuratorates at all levels, when making state compensation decisions from May 18, 2026, shall calculate based on this figure. Compensation for infringement of a citizen's personal freedom is ⟦495.94⟧ per day. The previous rate was ⟦475.52⟧ per day, applied from May 2025 (National China).

If you are a victim seeking compensation, go through 12315, sue in court, or use a lawyer; do not meet the other party alone as requested, and do not bundle "giving money" and "I won't leak it" into the same sentence
B

As a victim, demanding compensation from the infringer has a legal basis and does not automatically become extortion just because you "demand a high amount." But the price can be huge: Guo Li was previously sentenced to 5 years in prison for extortion, and only much later was the case retried and he was declared innocent. Therefore, use channels that leave a trail, do not go alone to a place designated by the other party to talk, and do not verbally state a condition that bundles "giving money" with "then I won't leak it."

Costs no money. Demand through 12315, sue in court, or authorize a lawyer to make the request. When meeting to talk, record from beginning to end. The difficulty is restraining yourself from talking privately with the other party alone.

Official case: in 2008, after authorities (China) announced several batches of "Scient" brand milk powder contained melamine, the test result for Guo Li's daughter was "several punctate hyperechoic spots in the central renal pelvis system on both sides." Guo Li repeatedly demanded compensation from the seller and the Scient company, while also taking the story to the media. In June 2009, the two parties reached an agreement, and Scient compensated ⟦400000⟧. Guo Li wrote a commitment letter not to pursue the matter further and waived compensation claims. Later, the company reported the case, and Guo Li was sentenced to 5 years of fixed-term imprisonment for extortion by the Chao'an District People's Court (China). The Guangdong Provincial People's Procuratorate (China) submitted a retrial recommendation. The recommendation argued that "existing evidence is insufficient to prove Guo Li subjectively had the purpose of illegal possession." Guo Li was the legal guardian, "had the right to demand compensation from the milk powder manufacturer, and his act of demanding compensation had a legal basis." The recommendation also stated "consumers have the right to expose and criticize through mass media acts that infringe upon their legitimate rights and interests." On April 7, 2017, the Guangdong Provincial Higher People's Court (China) retried the case and declared Guo Li innocent. The reason was that "the original judgment's conclusion that Guo Li aimed for illegal possession and used threats and intimidation to extort property was unclear on facts and lacked sufficient evidence; the nature of Guo Li's behavior did not exceed the scope of a civil dispute." Guo Li was detained from July 23, 2009, to July 22, 2014, totaling 1,826 days (Guangdong, judgment overturned upon retrial in 2017).
Suffering from cyberbullying: turn on protection mode and preserve evidence first, then choose one of three paths: the platform, a court injunction, or reporting to the police
A

At that moment, do three things: turn on the platform's protection settings, use the quick evidence preservation function to save content, and then click the quick report button. Afterward, you can apply for a court injunction to force the other person to stop first. You can also sue in court yourself; if evidence collection is difficult, ask the police for assistance. If it causes serious consequences like suicide and the social impact is bad, it can be transferred to the procuratorate for prosecution.

Costs no money. It takes about ten minutes at the time to turn on protection and save evidence. If you proceed to the step of seeking an injunction or filing a lawsuit yourself, you must go to court and may need to hire a lawyer. The difficulty is preserving evidence first while being insulted, rather than insulting back.

Item 15 of Guiding Opinion No. 14/2023 (China) discusses injunctions. A rights holder has evidence proving the other person is committing or about to commit an illegal act infringing on their personal rights. If not stopped in time, their legitimate interests will suffer irreparable damage. If the rights holder applies under Article 997 of the Civil Code (China), the people's court may issue a personal rights infringement injunction according to law. A personal rights infringement injunction is a court order forcing the other person to stop first. Item 11 of this opinion discusses evidence collection. In self-prosecuted cases, "if it is truly difficult for the victim to provide evidence, they may request the public security organ for assistance." The public security organ must promptly clarify who the perpetrator is and collect evidence on the extent of spread and influence. Network service providers must provide necessary technical support. "After the public security organ assists in collecting evidence and the conditions for accepting a self-prosecuted case are met, the people's court must decide to file the case." If evidence cannot be collected, the public security organ must explain in writing. A self-prosecuted case is one where the victim must sue in court themselves. Item 12 of this opinion lists five cases that must be considered "seriously endangering social order" under Article 246, paragraph 2 of the Criminal Law (China). One is causing the victim or their close relatives to suffer mental disorders, suicide... serious consequences, and bad social influence. Two is targeting ordinary people arbitrarily, where widespread information causes a large number of vulgar, malicious comments and bad social influence. Three is insulting or defaming multiple people or spreading rumors multiple times, and bad social influence. Four is organizing or instigating others to spread rumors en masse across multiple platforms, and bad social influence. Five is other cases. Item 4 of this opinion: organizing "human flesh searches" (doxing), illegally collecting and publishing a citizen's personal information to many unspecified people, if the circumstances are serious, shall be punished as the crime of infringing on a citizen's personal information. Article 23 of the Provisions on the Administration of Cyberbullying Information (China) requires platforms to provide the following protection options: blocking strangers or specific people; limiting the viewing range of one's posts; prohibiting resharing or commenting; only receiving private messages from friends, or refusing all private messages. Article 25 requires a quick evidence preservation function. Article 26 requires a quick complaint and report button in a visible place. Article 15 requires platforms to promptly report signs of illegal acts or crimes to the public security organ.
The path of "buying insurance for someone and then acting" is blocked by law from the start: you won't get a single cent, and the crime is punished as a combination of murder and insurance fraud
A

Secretly buying a type of insurance for an adult family member that uses death as a condition for payment makes the contract void. If the policyholder intentionally causes the death of the insured, the insurance company will not pay; intentionally killing someone to leave an inheritance also results in the loss of inheritance rights. The Criminal Law (China) separates this type of insurance fraud into a specific point, punished together with murder, with a maximum penalty of death. You won't get a single cent.
Costs no money.

Article 34 of the Insurance Law (China): a contract using death as a condition for payment of insurance money is void unless the insured has consented and accepted the insurance amount. The insured is the person protected in the contract. Parents buying insurance for minor children are not subject to this restriction. Article 39: the policyholder's designation of a beneficiary must be consented to by the insured. The policyholder is the person paying, and the beneficiary is the person receiving the money when something happens. Article 43 discusses intentional harm.
