Article 360 of the Criminal Law (China) regarding the crime of spreading venereal diseases: Whoever, knowing that they suffer from a serious venereal disease such as syphilis or gonorrhea, engages in prostitution or solicits prostitution shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not more than five years, criminal detention, or public surveillance, and shall also be fined (China-wide, Public Security Administration Punishment Law applicable from January 1, 2026)

Pirating manga, reposting movies, sharing cloud storage links and pirated e-books: even if you don't take money, it is copyright infringement; adding ads or charging membership fees can lead to prison
A

Translating and posting someone else's work without permission, or uploading it to the internet, is infringement even if no money is taken; it must be removed and damages paid. As soon as ads are attached or membership fees charged, it is considered for-profit. Earning ⟦30000⟧, posting 500 works, or having 1,000 members is enough for a prison sentence, with a maximum of 10 years. The owner of the YYeTs (Renren Yingshi) subtitle group was sentenced to 3 years and 6 months in prison.

No cost. Items you buy or download for personal viewing or translation for fun are fine, just don't post them online for the public. Do not create websites or resource-sharing groups with ads, membership fees, or sell cloud storage links. The difficulty is refraining from being a 'porter' when 'everyone else is posting'.

First, the civil aspect. Among the rights the Copyright Law (China) grants authors is the right of translation, i.e., the right to transform a work from one language to another. There is also the right of communication via information networks, i.e., the right to make works available to the public online. Translating or uploading someone else's work without permission is infringement. The infringer must cease the act and compensate for losses. Only using a published work for personal study, research, or appreciation does not require permission or payment. Compensation is first calculated based on the actual loss of the right holder or the money you earned. If unclear, the court sets it between ⟦500~5000000⟧. Intentional infringement with serious circumstances can result in 1 to 5 times damages. Reasonable costs incurred by the right holder to stop the infringement must also be paid. Next, the criminal aspect. The condition of Article 217 of the Criminal Law (China) is 'for the purpose of making a profit.' To make money, making others' works available online without permission, if thresholds are met, is the crime of copyright infringement. Penalties are up to 3 years in prison plus a fine, or just a fine. Very large amounts or especially serious circumstances result in 3 to 10 years plus a fine. What counts as making money: besides sales, hosting ads on a site counts, as does using a paid membership model. Service fees, membership fees, and ad revenue are all considered illegal income. The crime is constituted if any one of the following is met: Illegal income of ⟦30000⟧. Illegal business turnover of ⟦50000⟧; in the YYeTs case, this was the total from membership fees, ads, and hard drive sales. Spreading a total of 500 works (sets). Being downloaded 10,000 times, or clicked/viewed 100,000 times. Spreading via membership with 1,000 registered members. If no single item is met, but two items each reach half the threshold, it also counts. Reaching 10 times these numbers enters the 3 to 10-year bracket. Fines are usually 1 to 10 times the illegal income. Official Case 1: Liang Yongping and accomplices downloaded unauthorized TV shows and movies from foreign sites, organized translators to make subtitles, and uploaded them. These were hosted on the 'YYeTs subtitle group' website and app for online viewing and downloading. The site had 32,824 unauthorized works and over 6.83 million members. From Jan 2018 to Jan 2021, they collected over ⟦2700000⟧ in membership fees and over ⟦8800000⟧ in ad fees. Selling portable hard drives with movies earned another ⟦1000000⟧. The site displayed 'donation' QR codes; donating granted membership privileges. The procuratorate determined this was membership fees under another name. On Nov 22, 2021, Liang Yongping was sentenced to 3 years and 6 months, fined ⟦1500000⟧. 14 others received 1.5 to 3 years, all suspended, with fines of ⟦40000~350000⟧. Official Case 2: Kha used data scraping software to get streaming addresses for over 50,000 movies, putting them on his website and app for free viewing. He placed ads on the startup screen, earning by impressions, totaling over ⟦350000⟧. In 2023, he was sentenced to 3 years, suspended for 4 years, and fined ⟦400000⟧. Official Case 3: Huang rented a server at home to set up a music download forum. He uploaded over 100,000 songs to 18 cloud storage accounts and posted links on the forum. Members had to pay to exchange for forum coins to get links and extraction codes. Members paid a total of over ⟦500000⟧. In 2023, he was sentenced to 3 years, suspended for 4 years, and fined ⟦550000⟧ (China-wide, judicial interpretation applicable from April 26, 2025)
Writing fanfiction or derivative works for publication or sale: get permission from the original author first, or change the names and relationships of borrowed characters to make them your own
B

Fanfiction, even if it only borrows names, personalities, and relationships, can be ruled as infringement if published. Jiang Nan's 'The Youth in Between' borrowed over 60 characters from Jin Yong; on appeal, he was ordered to pay ⟦1680000⟧ in damages plus ⟦200000⟧ in costs. The lawsuit lasted 9 years, ending in a settlement where he pledged not to reprint the original version. As for free fanfiction written for fun, the court says it requires specific analysis.

No cost. Before publishing or selling, find the copyright owner of the original work to negotiate a license. If an agreement cannot be reached, change the names, personalities, and relationships of the borrowed characters to your own. Book titles, subtitles, and promotional slogans should also not ride on the fame of the original work.

The novel 'The Youth in Between' by Jiang Nan used names of characters from Jin Yong's novels such as Guo Jing, Huang Rong, Qiao Feng, and Linghu Chong. The story tells of these people on a university campus. When published in 2002, the subtitle was 'The University Life of the Condor Heroes'. By the time of the lawsuit, the book had multiple editions and millions of copies in circulation. In 2016, Jin Yong sued Jiang Nan and the publisher, seeking ⟦5000000⟧. The first instance court held it did not constitute copyright infringement. Reason: detached from specific plots, names, relationships, and personalities alone are difficult to count as protected specific expressions. However, the court found Jiang Nan used the original work's fame to attract readers, constituting unfair competition. Calculating 30% of ⟦5600000⟧ in royalties over the years, it awarded ⟦1680000⟧ plus ⟦200000⟧ in legal fees. The appeal, heard by the Guangzhou Intellectual Property Court, modified the ruling to constitute copyright infringement. The appeal found the plots were not substantially similar, meaning the plot was not copied. However, the 'character group portrait' formed by over 60 characters, including names, personalities, relationships, and backgrounds, were Jin Yong's choices and arrangements. This is an expression protected by copyright law; Jiang Nan infringed on the copyright of four of Jin Yong's novel series. The subtitle's intentional link to 'The Condor Heroes' was additionally unfair competition. The appeal ordered Jiang Nan to cease unfair competition, publish an apology to eliminate the influence, and pay ⟦1680000⟧ plus ⟦200000⟧ in reasonable costs. Two publishing companies were held jointly liable for ⟦330000⟧ of that. The appeal did not order the cessation of the infringing act but required that future reprints pay the original copyright owner 30% of the reprint royalty income. After the appeal, both sides applied to the Higher People's Court of Guangdong Province for retrial. On September 19, 2025, the parties reached a settlement mediated by the Guangdong Higher Court. In the settlement, the parties agreed not to characterize the act as 'plagiarism'. Jiang Nan admitted that when creating, he lacked legal knowledge of copyright and did not seek Jin Yong's permission for adaptation beforehand, causing damage to Jin Yong. Jiang Nan agreed not to reprint the original version of this book. Future reprints will not use characters created by Jin Yong or related content. The parties confirmed the subtitle constituted unfair competition. The damages ordered by the appeal had already been paid by Jiang Nan. Upon receipt of the settlement document, the old first and second instance judgments lost legal effect. In another case, the defendant was 'Ghost Blows Out the Light' author Zhang Mujie (pen name Tian Xia Ba Chang). In 2006, he transferred all property rights in the copyright of the series to Shanghai Xuanting Entertainment Information Technology Co., Ltd. Later, he authorized the publication of a new book 'Mojin Xiaowei', which used character names, relationships, and tomb-robbing rules from 'Ghost Blows Out the Light'. The new book's cover used a poster from the movie 'Mojin: The Lost Legend', an adaptation of the original series. Xuanting sued for ⟦20000000⟧. The Pudong Court in Shanghai held the new book had its own independent plot and was not copyright infringement. However, the cover misled readers into thinking the book was related to the original 'Mojin: The Lost Legend', constituting false advertising. The court ordered two publishers to pay ⟦900000⟧, with the publishing house jointly liable for ⟦600000⟧; the appeal upheld this. According to the law, the right of adaptation is the right to change a work and create a new creative work. Using a work through adaptation, translation, or annotation without the copyright owner's permission results in civil liability such as ceasing the infringement and compensating for losses (China-wide)
Do not carry batons, stun guns, daggers, or pepper spray for self-defense; keeping them in a vehicle is also considered carrying
A

Knives are regulated like daggers and switchblades; if found during a check on the street, you can be detained for up to 5 days. Carrying them into stations, shopping malls, or buses leads to 5 to 10 days of detention. Batons are for police use only; individuals holding them will have them confiscated and may be detained. Using them in reality is also risky: one person was punched once with a bare hand, immediately used a concealed knife to stab the person, and was sentenced to 4 years in prison for exceeding the limits of self-defense.

Costs no money. If already purchased, keep them at home, do not take them out, and do not put them in the car. If an incident occurs, retreat and report to the police first; only fight back if unavoidable.

First, see Article 38 of the Public Security Administration Punishment Law (China). Illegally carrying crossbows, daggers, and other instruments regulated by state regulations results in up to 5 days of detention, with a possible additional fine of up to ⟦1000⟧. In minor circumstances, a warning or a fine of up to ⟦500⟧ is issued. Carrying them into public places or public transport results in 5 to 10 days of detention, with a possible additional fine of up to ⟦1000⟧. Article 130 of the Criminal Law (China) is more severe. Illegally carrying regulated knives into public places or public transport, threatening public safety in serious circumstances, results in up to 3 years in prison. Regarding what constitutes a regulated knife, the 2007 identification standards of the Ministry of Public Security (China) list five types. Type one is daggers: having a handle, a handguard, and a blood groove, with a tip angle of less than 60 degrees. Type two is three-edged scrapers. Type three is switchblades with automatic locks, commonly called flick knives. Type four is knives with a tip angle under 60 degrees and a blade longer than 150 mm. Type five is knives with a tip angle over 60 degrees and a blade longer than 220 mm. Martial arts knives and artistic gift knives that are unsharpened and have rounded tips are not included. Batons are police auxiliary tools. The People's Police Law (China) stipulates that auxiliary tools are only to be held and used by police. Others holding them will have them confiscated, be detained for up to 15 days or warned, and may be fined up to 5 times the illegal income. The railway industry's prohibited items list includes batons, pepper spray, stun guns, and self-defense tools as regulated instruments. When taking a train, these items cannot be carried on one's person or sent as luggage. The road passenger transport prohibited items list also classifies pepper spray and stun guns as regulated instruments; they cannot be carried on long-distance buses. Regarding whether stun guns can normally be kept, in 2013 the Shanghai People's Procuratorate announced a case. Four people selling stun guns to drivers at an intersection were prosecuted for the crime of illegal trading of police equipment, receiving sentences from one year and three months to six months in prison. The procuratorate cited two notices from the Ministry of Public Security (China). According to these notices, "this type of stun gun belongs to instruments regulated by the state and is also a type of police auxiliary tool." The procuratorate also clearly stated that this type of stun gun "is a prohibited item domestically, and individuals are prohibited from manufacturing, selling, or possessing them." The prosecutor added that self-defense items like high-concentration sprays belong to police equipment, and ordinary citizens are not allowed to buy them. Keeping them in a car is checked just the same: a driver carrying a regulated knife through a checkpoint was discovered by police and placed under administrative detention. As for actual use, see the guiding opinions on justifiable defense. This document lists "whether or not a weapon was used or prepared for use" as one of the circumstances distinguishing defense from fighting. Official case: A certain Yang got into an argument with someone; the other side threatened to find people for revenge, so he went home and hid two knives on his person. The other side returned and punched him once in the face with a bare hand; he took the knife and stabbed the person in the chest and abdomen, and the person died. The court determined his actions were defensive in nature, but because the other side only fought with bare hands and he stabbed a vital area, it exceeded the limits of self-defense. He was sentenced to 4 years in prison for the crime of intentional injury (National China, Public Security Administration Punishment Law applicable from 01/01/2026)
Fishing and harvesting: do not cast nets during closed seasons or in restricted areas; never use electric shocks, poison, or explosives to catch fish, and do not use prohibited fishing gear
A

Using electric shocks, poison, or explosives to catch fish in restricted areas or during closed seasons meets the threshold for the crime of illegal fishing of aquatic products, with a maximum sentence of 3 years. Only when the catch is small and the harm is clearly minor can prosecution be avoided. Electric fishing also results in fines, often up to ⟦200000⟧; bringing electric fishing equipment into the water can also lead to a fine. Along the Yangtze River, a person who used electricity to catch fish and sold them for ⟦9000⟧ was sentenced to 1 year in prison.

Costs no money. Before going into the water, check the restricted fishing areas, closed seasons, and restricted angling areas announced by local agricultural authorities. Do not buy electric fishing machines or similar tools, and do not bring them to the water's edge. If you want to fish, go to waters where angling is permitted, or to fishing ponds and fish farms. The difficulty lies in resisting the urge to follow suit when seeing others catch many fish using electric shocks.

Article 340 of the Criminal Law (China): fishing for aquatic products in restricted areas, during closed seasons, or using prohibited tools or methods, in serious circumstances, results in up to 3 years of fixed-term imprisonment, criminal detention (short-term detention), surveillance, or a fine. The 2022 judicial interpretation by the two supreme authorities (China) clearly defines "serious circumstances," where any of the following cases suffice. Illegally fishing 500 kg or more in inland waters, or a value of ⟦10000⟧ or more. Fishing 50 kg or more in aquatic germplasm resource reserves, or a value of ⟦1000⟧ or more. Fishing in restricted areas using electric shocks, poison, or explosives. Fishing during closed seasons using these methods. The same article also leaves a loophole: based on the quantity, value of the catch, and tools used, if the harm is determined to be clearly minor, prosecution may be waived or punishment exempted. Next is the Fisheries Law (China), amended in 2025, applicable from 01/05/2026. The law prohibits fishing in violation of regulations on restricted areas and closed seasons, and also prohibits angling in violation of regulations. The law prohibits fishing by means of explosives, poison, or electric shocks, and also prohibits bringing these devices into fishery waters. Using prohibited fishing gear or nets with mesh smaller than the minimum size for fishing is also prohibited. Penalties are as follows: fishing with electric shocks, poison, or explosives results in confiscation of tools, catch, and illegal income, plus a fine of up to ⟦200000⟧. In serious circumstances, the fine is ⟦200000~2000000⟧. Merely bringing electric fishing equipment into fishery waters results in confiscation of the equipment and a possible fine of up to ⟦100000⟧. Fishing in violation of regulations on restricted areas, closed seasons, or using prohibited gear results in a fine of up to ⟦200000⟧. Angling in violation of regulations in restricted areas or during closed seasons results in confiscation of the fish caught, illegal income, and fishing tackle, with a possible fine of up to ⟦50000⟧. The Yangtze River has an additional layer: the Yangtze River Protection Law (China) stipulates that in key waters such as the main stream, important tributaries, and large lakes connected to the river, productive fishing of natural fishery resources is completely prohibited. The ten-year fishing ban on the Yangtze River started on 01/01/2021. Fishing in restricted waters results in confiscation of fish, illegal income, boats, and gear, plus a fine of ⟦10000~50000⟧. Using electric shocks, poison, or explosives results in a fine of ⟦50000~500000⟧. Official case: Li Zigen knew well that the Jiangdu Jiajiang section of the Yangtze River in Yangzhou was a restricted fishing area, yet he still drove a motorboat using an electric shock kit to catch fish. From January 2018 to April 2019, he used electric shocks more than 60 times, catching over 900 Chinese catties (about 450 kg) of natural fish to sell, profiting ⟦9000⟧. He confessed, returned the illegal income, and had released the first batch of fingerlings, but was still sentenced to 1 year in prison for the crime of illegal fishing of aquatic products. According to the mediation agreement, he also had to make a public apology in provincial media and release two batches of fingerlings worth 25,000 and ⟦22500⟧. Another guiding case from the Supreme People's Court (China): 8 people in the East Dongting Lake restricted fishing area used small-mesh nets and homemade electric nets to catch fish thirty or forty times. Their sentences ranged from 3 months of criminal detention with a suspended sentence to 1 year and 1 month in prison. The illicit profit of ⟦100000⟧ was fully recovered (National China, Fisheries Law applicable from 01/05/2026)
When visiting graves, burning grass, or picnicking: do not light fires in forests and grasslands; if you see a forest fire, call 12119 or 119
A

During fire prevention seasons, lighting a fire in a fire prevention zone results in a fine of ⟦300~5000⟧ even if no fire breaks out. Burning 2 hectares of forested land is enough to establish a case for the crime of causing a fire through negligence, punishable by 3 to 7 years, or up to 3 years in minor circumstances. One person visiting a grave burned joss paper and caused a fire of 39 hectares, receiving a 1-year prison sentence suspended for 2 years, and was also required to replant 32 hectares of forest.

Costs no money. For grave visiting, switch to offering flowers, weeding, or planting flowers; do not burn joss paper, incense, candles, or firecrackers on the mountain. Do not burn weeds or straw in the fields. When picnicking, bring food that doesn't require fire and take cigarette butts down the mountain. The difficulty lies in the elderly at home feeling that grave visiting doesn't count if joss paper isn't burned.

The "Regulations on the Prevention and Extinguishment of Forest and Grassland Fires" (China) apply from 01/01/2026, simultaneously repealing the old forest fire prevention regulations and grassland fire prevention regulations. Article 27 of the Regulations: during fire prevention seasons, outdoor fire use is prohibited in fire prevention zones, and no one may discard fire sources in fire prevention zones. In hot, dry, or high-wind weather, local governments may issue orders strictly prohibiting all outdoor fire use. Article 54: during fire prevention seasons, using outdoor fire in a fire prevention zone without permission results in being forced to stop. Individuals are fined ⟦300~5000⟧, and units are fined ⟦20000~100000⟧. Article 34: anyone who discovers a forest or grassland fire must report it immediately. The Ministry of Emergency Management (China) specifies that the unified national forest fire reporting number is 12119. Once a fire occurs and reaches the case filing standards, it becomes a criminal case. Paragraph 2 of Article 115 of the Criminal Law (China) covers the crime of causing a fire through negligence: negligently causing a fire results in 3 to 7 years, or up to 3 years or criminal detention (short-term detention) in minor circumstances. Among the case filing standards, there is an item directly related to forest fires. If forested land is burned up to 2 hectares, or sparse forest land, shrubland, unstocked forest land, or nursery land up to 4 hectares, a case must be filed. 1 death, 3 serious injuries, direct damage of ⟦500000⟧, or the burning of houses of 10 households also all suffice for filing a case. In a Xinhua News Agency article reposted by the National Forestry and Grassland Administration (China), experts stated that human causes such as fire use during ritual offerings and farming account for more than nine-tenths of fire causes. In historical data, fire use during ritual offerings ranks first. First official case: In February 2021, a certain Xie Jun visited a grave and burned joss paper in the Qilian Mountains National Nature Reserve, causing weeds and shrubs to catch fire. The burned area was 39.2156 hectares, mostly natural shrubland. When the fire broke out, he called to report it, joined the firefighting efforts, and voluntarily surrendered, which was counted as a self-confession. He also pre-planted 9,420 Qinghai spruce trees elsewhere. Despite this, he was still sentenced to 1 year in prison suspended for 2 years for the crime of causing a fire through negligence. The court also ordered him to replant 32.05 hectares of forest in three phases; if not completed, he must pay the appraised amount. Second official case: In May 2022, a certain Wang Qian participated in a custom activity, using a lighter to burn an offering of "cypress incense branches." He used stones to press down on the fire source and left without confirming it was completely extinguished. The fire source ignited dry grass, burning 121.69 Chinese mu (about 8.1 hectares), with damages of approximately ⟦469000⟧ (specifically ⟦468578⟧). He was sentenced to 9 months in prison suspended for 1 year and 6 months. He must replant according to the plan; if not completed, he will bear ⟦986700⟧ in restoration costs (National China, Regulations applicable from 01/01/2026)

Civil service exams, postgraduate exams, driving tests, and vocational certification exams: do not take exams for others, do not ask others to take exams for you, do not buy or sell answers, and do not help organize cheating
A

Asking someone to take an exam for you or taking an exam for someone else are both crimes, punishable by criminal detention (short-term detention) and fines; if someone who asked another to take an exam becomes a civil servant, they will be dismissed from the civil service. Organizing cheating or selling answers can result in up to 7 years in prison. Driving tests also count; a driving school owner who organized student cheating was sentenced to prison. If it doesn't reach the level of a crime, results are annulled, and you may be suspended from exams or barred from retaking them for a year.

Costs no money. Do not believe in "guaranteed pass classes," "VIP channels," or groups selling answers. Do not bring phones, earphones, or other items capable of receiving or sending information into the exam room. If you fail, prepare for another attempt. The difficulty lies in being only a few points short of passing when someone offers a guaranteed pass for a price.

Article 284-1 of the Criminal Law (China) punishes four behaviors, provided the condition is a "state examination prescribed by law." Organizing cheating results in up to 3 years in prison or criminal detention, with or only a fine. Serious circumstances result in 3 to 7 years. Providing cheating equipment or other assistance to organizers carries the same penalty. Selling answers or providing answers for cheating also carries the same penalty. Taking an exam for someone else or asking someone else to take an exam for you is the crime of substitute testing, punishable by criminal detention or surveillance, with or only a fine. Which exams count can be found in the 2019 judicial interpretation by the two supreme authorities (China). College entrance exams, postgraduate exams, self-study exams, and adult college entrance exams count; central and local civil service exams count. Certification exams such as the legal professional qualification, teacher certification, certified public accountant, medical practitioner certification, and construction engineer certification also count. In 2024, the Supreme People's Court (China) clarified that driving tests also belong to this category of exams. Organizing cheating in college entrance exams, postgraduate exams, or civil service exams is directly counted as "serious circumstances." Organizing for 30 or more person-times, or illegal income of ⟦300000⟧ or more, also counts. If discovered before the exam starts but the questions and answers were already obtained, it is still counted as a completed crime. Selling incomplete or partially incorrect answers does not affect the conviction. Substitute testing in minor circumstances may receive a suspended sentence; insignificant circumstances may result in non-prosecution. The Supreme People's Court (China) statistics show that from November 2015 to April 2024, 11,146 people were prosecuted for these three crimes. If it doesn't reach the level of a crime, it is handled according to the regulations of each exam. In national education examinations (China), using devices to receive answers or having someone take the exam for you results in the results being voided, and may lead to a 1 to 3-year suspension from exams. In civil service exams, substitute testing or participating in organized cheating results in disqualification from the exam and a permanent record in the integrity file. If already employed, discovery leads to termination or dismissal. Cheating on a driving test results in disqualification, annulment of passed subjects, a fine of up to ⟦2000⟧, and a one-year ban on reapplying for a license. Taking a driving test for someone else results in your own license being revoked and a three-year ban on reapplying. First official case: Zhang Jie's gang used photoshopped images and fake IDs to have "hired test-takers" substitute for candidates 89 times in state exams like civil service exams. The three ringleaders were sentenced to 5 to 5 years and 6 months in prison. 18 candidates who hired substitutes were convicted of the crime of substitute testing, receiving 2 to 4 months of criminal detention and fines of ⟦30000~100000⟧. Those who became civil servants through substitutes were dismissed. Second official case: A driving school owner, from 2017 to 2023, organized student cheating in driving tests. Methods included modifying exam system data, having instructors take tests for students, and giving students earphones for remote prompting. The owner was also convicted of bribery, totaling 6 years and 6 months in prison; 23 others were sentenced to 6 months to 1 year and 10 months (National China)
Get to know many people, don't fixate on one: whether two people are compatible cannot be predicted before meeting
A

Two speed-dating studies had participants fill out over 100 questions about mate selection before meeting. The questionnaires only calculated who was generally prone to liking others and who was generally liked by many people, but could not calculate whether two specific people would have a "spark." Compatibility can only be known by meeting. It is more worthwhile to get to know several people than to pour everything into one person.
Costs no money. Spend time getting to know several people instead of thinking over and over about the same person. The hardest part is restraining yourself from fixating.

In two speed-dating studies, participants filled out over 100 self-assessment scales (self-scoring questionnaires) related to mate selection before the meeting. Researchers used a random forest model (an algorithm for finding patterns) to calculate. It calculated "to what extent a person is generally prone to liking others": these questionnaires explained 4%–18% of the variance. Variance is the level of difference between one person and another; the questionnaires only explained a small part. It also calculated "to what extent a person is generally liked": explaining 7%–27%. But "whether these two specific people have a spark" could not be calculated; matching characteristics and preferences before the meeting in any way did not work. The same research group had previously conducted another speed-dating experiment. Participants self-reported their ideal type before the meeting, such as valuing appearance or valuing economic prospects. These self-reported preferences did not predict who they would actually like at the meeting.
Stop when someone has clearly rejected you; persistent pestering is a violation of public order, not "sincerity"
A

If someone has clearly said no and you still send messages continuously or wait for them, affecting their normal life, then from January 2026 this is a violation of public order (China). You may be placed under administrative detention for up to 5 days or fined up to ⟦1000⟧. In more serious circumstances, detention is 5 to 10 days. Police can also issue an order prohibiting you from contacting the other person; violating this leads to an additional 5 to 10 days of detention.
Costs no money and no time. The hardest part is restraining yourself: no more messaging, no more waiting for them.

The 治安管理处罚法 (Public Security Administration Punishment Law of China) applicable from 01/01/2026 separates the behavior of pestering and stalking into a specific point. The law states: "repeatedly sending obscene, insulting, or threatening messages, or using other methods to harass, pester, or stalk..., affecting the normal life of others." This behavior results in administrative detention for up to five days or a fine of up to ⟦1000⟧. In more serious circumstances, detention is from five to ten days, with a possible additional fine of up to ⟦1000⟧. This point also has an additional layer: with the approval of the person in charge of the public security organ, the violator can be ordered not to contact the victim for a certain period. Violating the contact prohibition order results in an additional five to ten days of detention.
To know if someone likes you, look at actions rather than guessing "signals": who initiates, who arranges, who follows up
B

When male and female strangers talk for about ten minutes and then guess about each other, guessing "the other person is not flirting" is quite accurate, while "the other person is flirting" is very difficult to recognize. Therefore, do not conclude based solely on facial expressions or tone of voice in a single conversation. Someone who has more feelings for a person will more often initiate messages and ask to meet that person later, though this connection is relatively weak.
Costs no money and not much time. The hardest part is changing habits: stop sitting and guessing the person's facial expressions and tone, and switch to recording events.

Two studies measured the accuracy of people recognizing flirting. The first study had 52 pairs of unacquainted men and women talk for 10 to 12 minutes. Afterward, each self-reported whether they were flirting and whether they thought the other person was flirting. Results: "conversations without flirting were guessed more accurately, while those with flirting were guessed more incorrectly." The second study used 26 one-minute video clips for 261 outsiders to guess, with similar conclusions. People recognize quite reliably when "the other person is not flirting," but find it very difficult to recognize when "the other person is flirting." A third study looked at actions. It combined three rounds of speed dating, totaling 559 people and over 6,600 dates, and then followed up. During the meeting, the more someone specifically liked another, the more they would later message and ask that person out. The average correlation coefficient for these connections was about 0.15 (a relatively weak connection). This shows that interest will manifest as actions like initiating contact and asking to meet. However, this study did not compare actions with facial expressions or tone to see which predicts more accurately.
Whether a relationship is good depends mainly on your own feelings within it, not the other person's conditions
A

The clearest indicator of whether a relationship is good is your own feelings, not the other person's conditions. For example, whether you feel the other person is serious, whether they cherish you, or whether the two of you often argue. Your feelings are two to four times more useful than the other person's account. However, whether a relationship gets better or worse over time is almost impossible to calculate with any questionnaire.
Costs no money and not much time. The hardest part is changing perspective: put away the checklist of selection criteria and switch to looking at the process of living together.

A machine learning analysis of longitudinal tracking data of couples from 29 laboratories and 43 datasets; longitudinal tracking involves recording over a long period for the same group of couples. The factors that best predicted relationship quality all came from the individuals' feelings about the relationship: feeling the other person is committed, feeling appreciated, sexual satisfaction, feeling the other person is satisfied, and conflict. Among individual factors, the strongest were life satisfaction, negative affect, depression, avoidant attachment style, and anxious attachment style. These relationship factors, at the start of the survey, explained at most 45% of the variance. Variance is the level of difference in relationship quality between one couple and another; 45% is the part explained by these factors. By the end of the study, this only explained at most 18%. Furthermore, the predictive power of "factors reported by oneself" was two to four times that of "factors reported by the partner." Beyond self-reported feelings about the relationship, adding individual differences and the partner's reports did not add any predictive power. Whether a relationship improved or worsened during the study period was almost impossible to calculate using any set of self-reported indices, originally stated as "largely unpredictable from any combination of self-report variables."
To get closer, take turns answering a set of questions from shallow to deep, rather than learning "tricks"
B

Two strangers taking turns answering 36 questions from shallow to deep felt closer after 45 minutes than those who only engaged in small talk for the same amount of time. What works is taking turns speaking truthfully and gradually deepening layer by layer, not using tricks. This only shows they were closer at that moment; it doesn't mean it will become a long-term relationship.
Costs no money. Takes 45 minutes.

Pairing two unacquainted people and having them take turns answering three groups of increasingly deep questions, totaling 36 questions. Questions ranged from "who would you most like to invite to dinner" to "when was the last time you cried in front of another person." After 45 minutes, the level of perceived closeness was significantly higher than the control group that engaged in small talk for the same duration. It was also higher than the average score students in the study gave for their closest real-life relationships.
Long-distance relationships are no less than short-distance ones; the real challenge is the first three months after moving to the same city
B

Long-distance relationships are actually more stable during the time apart. Research suggests the reason is that it's easy to think of the other person as better than they actually are; the less you meet, the better you think of them. The real challenge lies after moving to the same city. In tracking data, about half of long-distance couples reach the step of moving to the same city, while the other half break up during the time apart. Among the half that reunited, one-third broke up within 3 months.
Costs money for travel and time on the road. You meet less often than in short-distance relationships. The hardest part is enduring long periods without meeting.

Two studies reached the same conclusion. Long-distance relationships are actually more stable than short-distance ones during the time apart. The reason is that in long-distance relationships, the level of thinking of the other person as better than reality is significantly higher; the study measured aspects: idealized distortion, romantic love, relationship memories, and perceived compatibility. And the less they met, the better they thought of each other. But this stability only holds while the two are still apart; once they are close, long-distance couples are more likely to break up. A study tracking the transition from long-distance to living close provided the rates: about half of long-distance couples reach the step of moving in close together, while the other half break up during the time apart. Among the half that reunited, one-third broke up within 3 months after reuniting. Changes mentioned by participants after reuniting included: loss of personal space, knowing more of both the good and bad of the other person, difficulty arranging time, and more arguing and jealousy. The longer the time apart with more infrequent meetings, the stronger the idealization, and the less stable the relationship after reuniting.
Check the registration figures before listening to elders: how marriage and divorce rates are calculated
A

In 2024, China recorded 6.106 million marriage registrations, 20% fewer than the previous year, and 3.513 million divorces. Online claims that the divorce rate is over half come from dividing these two numbers, approximately 57.5%. However, those divorcing and those marrying are not the same group; this should not be interpreted as half of all marriages ending. The marriage rate of 4.3‰ and divorce rate of 2.5‰ in the bulletin are calculated relative to the national population.
Free. It takes a few minutes to read the marriage registration section in the annual statistical bulletin of the Ministry of Civil Affairs (China).

In 2024, the country (China) processed 6.106 million legal marriage registrations, a 20.5% decrease from the previous year, with a marriage rate of 4.3‰. In the same year, 3.513 million legal divorce procedures were completed, including 2.622 million registrations at civil affairs agencies and 0.891 million divorces granted by courts or through mediation. The divorce rate was 2.5‰. The bulletin notes: marriage (divorce) rate = number of marriage (divorce) couples in the year / average population during the year !! 1000‰. This is the "crude rate," where the denominator is the total population, not the number of married people.
Account for the health benefits of marriage, but adjust for the fact that these are observational data
A

Among the elderly, married individuals have a mortality risk approximately 12% lower than those without a spouse over the same period; those who have never married have a risk approximately 24% higher than those who are married. However, these are merely concurrent observations; it is impossible to distinguish if marriage is the cause. These figures are almost entirely from Europe and the US; for China, they should only be used as a reference for magnitude.

Free of charge and time. Just remember one thing: these figures indicate that within the married group, the mortality rate is lower; these are two concurrent events, and it cannot be determined if marriage makes you live longer.

A meta-analysis of the elderly combined multiple studies for recalculation, totaling 53 comparison groups and over 250,000 people. All included were cohort studies, which only track and record without control groups. All-cause mortality for married individuals compared to those without a spouse: RR = 0.88, 95% CI 0.85 to 0.91 (RR is relative risk), with the probability of death in the same period being about 12% lower. In the same study, widowhood was 1.11, divorce or separation was 1.16, and never married was 1.11, which are approximately 11%, 16%, and 11% higher, respectively. There was no difference between men and women. The most conservative estimate was RR = 0.94, only about 6% lower. Another meta-analysis comparing never-married individuals to married individuals used 95 papers and over 500 million people. The result was HR = 1.24 (1.19 to 1.30), with the probability of death in the same period being about 24% higher. The difference decreases with age. Another meta-analysis segmented by gender, covering 21 studies and over 7.89 million people, found that for both men and women, being without a spouse was associated with overall mortality, cancer mortality, and cardiovascular mortality. For men, the differences in cardiovascular and overall mortality were larger. Never-married men compared to never-married women: 31% more stroke deaths and 9% more all-cause deaths.
Calculate time costs based on "unpaid labor"; clarify the division of labor before registering the marriage
A

The national time-use survey (China) statistics unpaid work such as housework and caring for family members. Among those who performed such tasks during the day, men averaged 1 hour 52 minutes per day, while women averaged 3 hours 29 minutes. The survey does not categorize by marital status, so there are no official figures for "how much more housework after marriage"; this gender gap serves only as a reference ceiling. How to divide labor can be negotiated as a different arrangement before registration.

Free. Before getting married, spend an hour or two clarifying who does the housework, who cares for the elderly and children, whose career takes a backseat, and how this unpaid labor is divided, then follow through. The hardest part is speaking up directly; do not delay the conversation.

The 2024 National Time Use Survey (China). Unpaid labor includes housework, caring for family members, and tasks without remuneration. People who performed these tasks during the day spent an average of 2 hours 45 minutes daily, with men at 1 hour 52 minutes and women at 3 hours 29 minutes. The proportion of people performing these tasks in a day: men 67.5%, women 83.9%. Average daily housework for the population was 1 hour 17 minutes; for those who actually did it, 1 hour 59 minutes, which is 28 minutes less than in 2018. Caring for family members averaged 30 minutes daily; for those who did it, 1 hour 46 minutes. 2018 figures: housework for men 45 minutes, women 2 hours 6 minutes; childcare for men 17 minutes, women 53 minutes.
Financial aspects of marriage: check the default legal rules first, then decide if a written agreement is needed
A

Without a written agreement, the law defaults to treating wages and bonuses earned after marriage, income from business and investment, and inherited or gifted assets as joint property. Assets owned before marriage, or assets explicitly designated for one person in a will or gift contract, are personal property. Two people can agree in writing to keep their assets separate; once signed, it is legally binding. A person who bears more burden for childcare or elderly care has the right to claim compensation upon divorce.

Free. Read the property sections in the Marriage and Family part of the 改改典 (Civil Code of the People's Republic of China). If necessary, sign a written property agreement; the law only requires it to be in writing, not notarized. The hardest part is being direct about money beforehand.

Default rules in the absence of a specific agreement: wages, bonuses, labor remuneration, income from production, business, and investment, intellectual property income, and inherited or gifted assets acquired after marriage are joint property of the spouses (Article 1062). Assets owned before marriage, compensation for personal injury, assets explicitly designated for one party in a will or gift contract, and personal daily necessities are separate property (Article 1063). Both parties may agree in writing that assets acquired before and after marriage belong to each individual, are joint, or are partially separate and partially joint. This agreement is legally binding on both (Article 1065). The party who bears more obligations for raising children, caring for the elderly, or supporting the other party's work has the right to claim compensation upon divorce (Article 1088).
Parents contributing money for a house: specify whether it is a loan or a gift at the time of transfer
A

If parents provide money for a house before marriage, it is defaulted as a gift to their own child. Money provided after marriage without an agreement is considered joint marital property. From February 2025, if one party's parents provide the full amount after marriage without specifying it is only for their child, the court may award the house to that child upon divorce and then decide whether to compensate the other party. To count it as a loan, specify it clearly that day with both parties signing.

Free. On the day the money is contributed, write a one-page explanation specifying whether the amount is a gift or a loan and to whom; the contributing parents and the child should all sign. If it is a loan, have both spouses sign, and ensure the bank transfer description matches that statement.

Money provided by parents for a house for the couple before marriage is identified as a gift specifically to their own child, unless the parents explicitly state it is for both. For money provided after marriage: if there is an agreement, follow the agreement. If there is no agreement or it is unclear, it is handled according to joint property principles. From February 1, 2025, an additional rule applies: during the marriage, if one party's parents provide the full amount and the gift contract does not specify it is only for their child, the court may award the house to the child of the person who provided the money during divorce property division. After that, the court considers various factors to decide if and how much to compensate the other party. These factors include the duration of the marriage, whether they have children together, fault leading to divorce, contribution to the family, and the market value of the house at the time of divorce. If one party's parents provide partial funding, or both sets of parents provide funding, the house is awarded to one party based on the source of funds and contribution ratio, with reasonable compensation (China-wide).
Large loans taken out by a spouse alone: if you did not sign and do not acknowledge it later, it does not automatically become your debt
A

If a spouse takes out a loan behind your back, as long as it clearly exceeds daily family living expenses and you did not sign for it or acknowledge it later, it does not automatically become your debt. The creditor must prove the money was used for joint living or joint business. However, for sums like a house purchase, if it has actually become a home where both live or co-own, the other party can usually prove this point.

Free. Do not sign as a "co-borrower" or "guarantor" on a spouse's loan or guarantee documents. Also, avoid messaging phrases like "we will pay this back," as it could be seen as a later acknowledgment of the debt. The hardest part is refraining from responding when debt collectors call.

The following loans are joint marital debts (China). First, those signed by both spouses. Second, those acknowledged by one party later, meaning both parties subsequently accept the debt. Third, a loan taken in an individual's name during the marriage for daily family living needs. A loan taken in an individual's name that clearly exceeds daily family living expenses is not a joint marital debt. The exception is if the creditor (the one collecting) proves the money was used for the couple's joint life, joint production and business, or was a debt accepted by both. House purchase money clearly exceeds daily living needs; the burden of proof lies with the creditor, who must provide evidence. However, if this money has actually become a house where the couple lives or co-owns, the creditor can usually prove it was "used for the couple's joint life." Therefore, the truly effective step is the one in item 11 (specifying if parental contributions are loans or gifts) (China-wide, since 2021).
Marriage registration only requires an ID card and a signed affidavit: no household register needed, no fee, certificate issued on the spot
A

Starting May 2025, marriage registration (China) requires only two things: your ID card plus a signed affidavit. The affidavit states you are currently unmarried and that you and the other person are not direct blood relatives or collateral relatives within three generations. You do not need to bring a household register (hukou), nor do you need to go to the place of household registration of either party. Registration is free of charge, and if requirements are met, the certificate is issued on the spot.
Free. Both parties must be present. The process usually takes a few dozen minutes.

The new Marriage Registration Regulations (China) effective May 10, 2025, changed the documents mainland citizens must submit when marrying. The regulations state only two items must be presented: "(1) personal resident identity card; (2) a signed affidavit stating that the individual is currently unmarried and has no direct blood relationship or collateral blood relationship within three generations with the other party." The household register is no longer a mandatory document. The registration authority is the "civil affairs department of the county-level people's government, or the township (town) people's government designated by the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or municipality directly under the Central Government based on the principle of convenience for the people." The restriction to "the place of permanent household registration of one party" in the old regulations has been removed. The regulations also explicitly state that "marriage registration authorities shall not charge fees for processing marriage registrations." They also specify that "for parties meeting the marriage conditions, registration must be completed on the spot and a marriage certificate issued." The regulations list four cases where registration is not permitted: "(1) not reaching the legal marriage age; (2) not being completely voluntary for both parties; (3) one or both parties already being married; (4) having a direct blood relationship or collateral blood relationship within three generations."
Have one pre-marital health check; serious illnesses must be disclosed to the other party before registration
B

If a serious illness is hidden from the other party before registration, that party can go to court to request the annulment of the marriage. The request must be made within one year of discovery. Since 2003, pre-marital health checks have not been a mandatory condition for registration; going is voluntary. Costs depend on local policies and take half a day.
Most regions (China) waive or reduce fees for people of age. Paying yourself only costs a few hundred yuan. Takes half a day.

The legal consequences of hiding an illness are clear. The new Marriage Registration Regulations (China) stipulate that "if one party suffers from a serious illness, they must tell the other party truthfully before marriage registration; if they do not, the other party may, based on Article 1053 of the 改改典 (Civil Code of the People's Republic of China), request the people's court to annul the marriage." The state (China) considers pre-marital health checks as the first gate for preventing birth defects. Current targets are to "keep the pre-marital health check rate and the pre-pregnancy health check coverage rate among the target population at 70% and 80% or above, respectively." Documents also require "placing pre-marital health check facilities near marriage registration offices for public convenience." Documents also promote "one-stop" services including "marriage registration, pre-marital health checks, and reproductive counseling." The Civil Code of China stipulates that if one party has a serious illness, they must disclose it truthfully before registration; otherwise, the other party may request annulment. The request for annulment must be made within one year from the date the reason for annulment was known or should have been known. Pre-marital health checks are not a mandatory condition for registration. The Tai'an Municipal Health Commission (China) in 2022, responding to a CPPCC proposal, stated: "The 2003 Marriage Registration Regulations, while abolishing 'mandatory pre-marital health checks,' explicitly required that registration authorities must not attach any other obligations when processing procedures." The list of registration documents in Article 8 of the current regulations does not include a pre-marital health check certificate.
Calculate the exit cost: consensual divorce has a 30-day cooling-off period, litigated divorce has legal conditions
A

Consensual divorce (China) is not finalized immediately upon signing. After filing, either party can withdraw within 30 days. After that period, both must personally go to receive the divorce certificate within the next 30 days; failure to do so is treated as a withdrawal. If the other party does not agree, the only way is to file a lawsuit. The court mediates first; if there is domestic violence, bigamy, separation for two years, etc., and mediation fails, a divorce must be granted.
Free. Before getting married, spend some time reading: how long it takes to exit and what procedures are involved. The hardest part is thinking about breaking up before even getting married.

Consensual divorce requires a written divorce agreement and personal application at the marriage registration office (Article 1076). Within 30 days of the office receiving the application, either party can withdraw. After the period expires, both parties must personally go to receive the divorce certificate within the next 30 days; failure to do so is treated as a withdrawal (Article 1077). If one party disagrees, they must litigate, and the court must mediate first. Situations such as bigamy or cohabitation with others, domestic violence or abuse, abandonment, gambling, or drug addiction that remains uncorrected after repeated education, or separation for two years due to incompatibility, require a divorce if mediation fails. If a divorce is denied but the parties then separate for another full year, a subsequent lawsuit must be granted (Article 1079). In 2024, China had 3.513 million divorces, of which 0.891 million went through court rulings or mediation.
If marrying "for the parents," record that as a separate item; do not mix it with your own benefits
C

The benefits for the elders—peace of mind, social face, an end to nagging—are real. But they do not automatically translate into health benefits or relationship quality for you. Meanwhile, the time costs, financial costs, and exit costs are all borne by you. Dividing a paper into two columns to list your benefits versus the elders' benefits will make it clear if it is worth it.

Free. Divide a piece of paper into two columns. One column is for the benefits of this marriage that belong to you, which can be calculated from previous items in this chapter. The other column is for the benefits belonging to the elders: peace of mind, social face, and stopping the marriage nagging. The hardest part is keeping the elders' column separate and not merging it into your own.

The benefits for elders are real. However, they do not automatically convert into your health benefits (item 8) or relationship quality (item 4; whether a relationship is good depends on your own feelings). Meanwhile, the time costs (item 9), financial costs (items 10 to 12), and exit costs (item 15) are all borne by the individuals involved. Once recorded separately, whether "marrying to complete a task" is worth it will become self-evident.
Treat relationship quality as a health investment: when arguing, focus on the facts, do not attack the person, do not swear, and do not be sarcastic
B

When couples are in harmony, their health is slightly better and their mortality risk is slightly lower. This correlation is not large, roughly the same as the link between diet and health. In one experiment, couples who consistently displayed a hostile attitude while arguing had small experimental wounds that healed slowly, at a rate only six-tenths that of peaceful couples.
Costs no money. When arguing, only speak about the immediate issue; do not swear, do not be sarcastic, and do not bring up old stories. The hardest part is holding your tongue when things get heated.

A meta-analysis of 126 studies involving over 72,000 people. The higher the marital quality, the better the health, with correlation coefficients (r) ranging from 0.07 to 0.21. A correlation coefficient of 0 means completely unrelated, while 1 means they move perfectly together. Within this, the correlation with a lower mortality risk was r = 0.11. Cardiovascular reactivity during arguments was lower, r = -0.13. The authors state these effects are small, similar in size to the link between health habits like diet and health. Another crossover experiment involved 42 healthy couples hospitalized twice for 24 hours each. Once they had a supportive conversation, and once they discussed a topic of disagreement. After arguing, blister wounds created for the experiment healed more slowly. Couples who were more hostile on both occasions had wounds that healed at only 60% of the speed of less hostile couples. The morning after arguing, their blood inflammation markers (IL-6, tumor necrosis factor) also increased more.

Same-sex couples should prepare powers of attorney, voluntary guardianship agreements, and wills while both are still of sound mind: under (Chinese) law, you are not considered close relatives; without these, you have no right to sign on their behalf or inherit
A

The group of "close relatives" under (Chinese) law is a narrow list: spouses, parents, children, siblings, etc.; romantic partners are not included. Without prior paperwork, when one person is seriously ill, the other cannot make decisions for them. When one person passes away, the other cannot inherit a single cent. Three types of documents each handle a different stage: while of sound mind, rely on a power of attorney; if cognitive capacity is lost, rely on voluntary guardianship; after death, rely on a will.

Voluntary guardianship and wills are done at a notary office; notary fees vary by location, starting from several hundred yuan. Hand-writing a will yourself costs no money. In total, it takes one or two sessions. The hardest part is for the two people to sit down and talk about illness and death.

The group of close relatives listed in Article 1045 of the 民法典 (Civil Code of the People's Republic of China) includes spouses, parents, children, siblings, paternal grandparents, maternal grandparents, paternal grandchildren, and maternal grandchildren. Legal heirs under Article 1127 are first spouses, children, and parents, followed by siblings, paternal grandparents, and maternal grandparents. Romantic partners are not listed anywhere. Article 1219 discusses surgery, special examinations, and special treatments. In cases where it is impossible or inappropriate to explain to the patient, medical personnel must explain to the patient's "close relatives" and obtain their consent. There are three paths to compensate for this. First, Article 33 allows an adult to agree in writing in advance with "another individual willing to be a guardian" to select a guardian. After the person loses all or part of their civil capacity, this person becomes the guardian, and the guardian is the legal representative. Second, Article 165 stipulates that a written power of attorney must clearly state the name of the authorized person, the authorized matter, the scope of authority, and the duration, and must be signed or sealed by the person themselves. If the person dies or loses civil capacity, the authorization terminates. Third, Article 1133 allows for a will to bequeath personal property to people outside the legal heirs. The Yichang Municipal Bureau of Justice (China) has a post on the website of the Hubei Provincial Department of Justice. The article clearly states that same-sex couples can notarize a voluntary guardianship agreement, designating the other person as their future guardian (China-wide).
Do not hide your sexual orientation to get married, and do not view a marriage of convenience as a way to avoid trouble: under the law, it is a real marriage, and the only way out is divorce
A

Hiding your sexual orientation to get married is not considered void under (Chinese) law, nor can it be annulled; the only way out is divorce. A marriage of convenience is also a real marriage; money earned after the wedding is considered common property of the spouses, debts signed by both are joint, and loans for daily family expenses are also considered joint. Upon divorce, the party who was deceived may demand a larger share of assets or compensation for mental distress, but whether the court will accept this is not yet settled.
Costs no money. The difficulty is enduring the pressure from family to get married, which may require holding out for many years.

Article 1051 of the 民法典 (Civil Code of the People's Republic of China) stipulates only three cases for a void marriage: bigamy, prohibited degrees of kinship, or being under the legal marriage age. Articles 1052 and 1053 stipulate only two cases for annulment: being coerced into marriage or the concealment of a serious illness before marriage. Article 17 of the Interpretation (1) on the Marriage and Family section (China) stipulates: if a request to confirm a marriage as void is based on reasons other than these three cases, the court shall dismiss it. Therefore, the only way out is divorce. A registered marriage of convenience is also a legal marriage. Article 1062 stipulates that wages, bonuses, and labor remuneration earned after marriage are the common property of the spouses. Article 1064 stipulates that debts signed by both parties, or debts borrowed by one party for the family's daily life, are joint debts. For compensation for damages upon divorce, see Article 1091. Cases where compensation can be claimed are limited to bigamy, cohabiting with another person, domestic violence, maltreatment or abandonment of family members, and "other major faults." Article 2 of Interpretation (1) limits "cohabiting with another person" to living with "another person of the opposite sex outside of marriage." Therefore, same-sex relationships can only be argued under "other major faults." Compensation includes mental distress; the deceived party must request it at the same time they file for divorce; if the court does not grant the divorce, the claim will not be accepted. Since the Civil Code (China) came into effect, no public court judgments of this type have been found. Under the old law, the website of the Jiangsu Provincial Higher People's Court (China) published an article in 2013 discussing a case where a wife sued for divorce because her husband hid his homosexuality. The article presented two views. One view held that homosexuality was not among the faults stipulated by the law at that time, so it did not accept a larger asset split or mental compensation. The author of the article agreed with the other view: treating the deceived party as the "no-fault party," favoring her in the asset division, and providing mental solace compensation (China-wide).
Relationships stuck in a cycle of arguing and the silent treatment: both people should go to couples therapy together; waiting around almost never improves things on its own
A

Couples who are stuck and complete couples therapy are significantly more satisfied with their relationship; about seven out of ten show improvement. Couples who are just on a waiting list show almost no change. However, the effect will fade: in follow-ups to the 5th year, about half still show clear improvement, while about a quarter have separated or divorced.

Costs money. Fees are charged per session and vary by location and hospital; no specific amount is listed here. In studies, sessions are usually once a week, with a trial lasting about 8 months. The hardest part is that both must go and must follow through to the end.

A 2020 meta-analysis combined 58 studies involving 2,092 couples. After completing couples therapy, the change in relationship satisfaction was g = 1.12 (95% CI: 0.92 to 1.31), which the authors described as a large effect. (g is the effect size; see the glossary in the README). For couples placed in a waiting group over the same period, g = 0.12 (-0.04 to 0.29), showing no clear improvement. The worse the relationship was at the start, the more it improved. A 2012 review article stated that couples therapy helps 70% of treated couples improve. Another randomized trial selected 134 couples with long-term, severe discord to undergo about 8 months of two types of behavioral couples therapy. Upon completion, satisfaction levels changed by d = 0.90 and 0.71. By the 5th year, 50.0% and 45.9% of the couples respectively still showed clear improvement. Here, the authors define clear improvement as "clinically significant improvement." At the same time, 25.7% and 27.9% had separated or divorced.

Even if you have had a wedding and a banquet, you must still register the marriage: without registration, you are not spouses under the law; if the other person dies, you have no right to inherit as a husband or wife
A

Since February 1994, having a wedding without registration means you are not spouses under (Chinese) law; it is only considered cohabitation. If the other person dies, you cannot inherit the estate as a husband or wife. When you want to separate, the court will not handle it as a divorce. Supplemental registration can solve this, and its validity is retroactive.
Costs no money. Both people go to the marriage registration office together; it takes a few dozen minutes.

The 民法典 (Civil Code of the People's Republic of China) stipulates that "the marriage relationship is established upon completion of marriage registration. Those who have not registered must perform supplemental registration." Interpretations from the Supreme People's Court (China) divide those who have not registered but live as husband and wife into two categories. Those who met the marriage requirements before 01/02/1994 are treated as a de facto marriage. After that date, the court "must inform them to perform supplemental marriage registration." If they do not, it is treated as a cohabitation relationship. If one party dies and the other wants to inherit as a husband or wife, this principle also applies. Spouses are first-order heirs, so an unregistered partner cannot be included. Regarding cohabitation relationships, the court does not accept requests to "terminate" them, only disputes over asset division and child custody. Once supplemental registration is done, the marriage's validity "dates back to when both parties met the substantive requirements for marriage under the Civil Code." Children are not affected. In the Inheritance section of the Civil Code (China), "children" explicitly includes children born out of wedlock, who are first-order heirs just like children born in wedlock.

If a spouse hides from you that they took joint money to give large gifts to a livestreamer or transferred it to someone outside the marriage: you can request a division of joint assets without divorcing; money transferred to an outsider can be recovered through a lawsuit
A

If a spouse takes joint money to give large gifts to a livestreamer without consulting you, you can ask the court to divide the joint assets without getting a divorce. Upon divorce, the other person may also be allocated a smaller share or no share at all. For money transferred to someone outside the marriage, you can sue the recipient for its return; even if they claim to have spent it, they must still pay it back. However, these actions require a lawsuit, you must pay your own legal fees, and the first instance takes several months.

Requires a lawsuit. You pay your own legal fees; they are not part of the court costs borne by the losing party. First-instance ordinary procedures are regulated to be resolved within 6 months (can be extended); summary procedures take 3 months. You must also personally find each transaction in bank statements and gift histories.

The 民法典 (Civil Code of the People's Republic of China) stipulates that spouses "have equal rights in the disposition" of common property. During the marriage, if one party conceals, transfers, sells, destroys, or squanders common property, the other party may request the court to divide the common property without first divorcing. When dividing assets upon divorce, the party who did so may be given a smaller share or no share. If discovered after divorce, one can sue again to demand a further division. Interpretation (2), applicable from 01/02/2025, clearly specifies two cases. Article 6 concerns livestream gifts. If one party, without the other's consent, uses common property to give gifts on a livestreaming platform and the amount clearly exceeds the family's normal consumption levels, it is considered "squandering." If the other party requests a division during the marriage, or that the gifter receives less or nothing upon divorce, the court must accept. Article 7 concerns transfers to outsiders. If one party, for the purpose of bigamy, cohabitation, or other violations of the duty of fidelity, gives common property to another person, and the other spouse seeks to declare the gift void, the court must accept. Once void, the recipient must return the money. This can also be grounds to request a division during the marriage or a reduced share for the other party upon divorce. In a typical case published by the Supreme People's Court (China), one party transferred ⟦730000⟧ to a person with whom they had an illicit relationship over 4 years of marriage, and that person transferred back ⟦170000⟧. The court ordered the person to return the ⟦560000⟧ actually received; the person's claim that "part of the money had been spent" was not accepted by the court (China-wide).

Spouses with minor children when divorcing: record in the divorce agreement who the child will live with, the monthly child support amount, and the visitation method and timing; the more specific it is, the fewer lawsuits will be needed later
A

You can discuss and record in the agreement who the child lives with, how much is paid monthly, and when you can see the child. If you cannot agree, the court will decide; for those with a fixed income, child support is usually 20% to 30% of the payer's monthly income. If the recorded amount is not paid, you can sue to recover it. If the other person prevents visitation, the court can fine or detain them, but it will not forcibly bring the child to meet you.

For an uncontested divorce, recording it in the agreement costs no money. The difficulty is that the two people must discuss details, such as which day of the month to pay, which account to pay into, which weekends to pick up the child, and how to split summer and winter breaks. If you cannot agree, you must sue. The court fee for a divorce case (China) is ⟦50~300⟧ per case. You pay your own legal fees; they are not part of the court costs borne by the losing party. First-instance ordinary procedures are resolved within 6 months (can be extended); summary procedures take 3 months. Subsequent disputes over child support or visitation require separate lawsuits.

The 民法典 (Civil Code of the People's Republic of China) stipulates that the amount and duration of child support, and the method and timing of visitation, are first determined by agreement between the parties; if they cannot agree, the court decides. Children under two years old, in principle, live with the mother. For children over two, the court follows the "principle of the best interests of the minor child." For children over eight, their wishes must be respected. From February 2025, if one party has situations such as domestic violence, gambling or drug addiction, infidelity or cohabitation, or snatching/hiding the child, the court prioritizes giving custody to the other party. The level of child support is based on the child's actual needs, the parents' ability to pay, and the local standard of living. Those with a fixed income usually provide 20% to 30% of their total monthly income. If supporting two or more children, the ratio can be increased, but usually does not exceed 50% of total monthly income. For those without a fixed income, it is based on that year's total income or the average income in the same industry, using these ratios as a reference. For example, with a monthly income of ⟦8000⟧, this ratio would be ⟦1600~2400⟧ per month (self-calculated). Child support is usually provided until the child is 18. An agreement stating that one party does not have to pay child support is also valid. However, if the living standard of the custodial parent drops significantly, or the child's necessary expenses increase significantly, the child can still demand payment from the other party. After divorce, if child support is not paid according to the agreement, a lawsuit can be filed to recover the debt. If a court judgment or mediation record is effective and the other party does not comply, one can request compulsory execution. For those who intentionally fail to cooperate with visitation, the court can detain or fine them, but "cannot use compulsory execution against the child's body or the act of visitation" (China-wide).
Before you start a task, ask one question: will the brand, platform, or company report this to the police? If you are prosecuted, find a criminal lawyer immediately
C

Before acting, ask: will the brand, platform, or company report this? Investigative agencies have the right to collect server logs, payment histories, and group chat histories. If you are actually placed in criminal detention, a decision on whether to formally arrest you will be made within a maximum of 37 days. You are entitled to a lawyer from your first interrogation; the lawyer can submit an opinion to the Procuratorate that "arrest should not be approved" or apply for bail.

Costs no money. Before acting, change the question from "is it technically possible" to: will the brand, platform, or company report this? The difficulty lies in suppressing the thought that "no one will care about such a small thing," because investigative agencies have the right to collect server logs, payment histories, and group chat histories.

Any unit or individual that discovers a criminal act has the right to report it. If an investigative agency finds a criminal act, it must file a case. Courts, Procuratorates, and public security organs "have the right to collect and obtain evidence from relevant units and individuals," and those units and individuals must provide it truthfully. After criminal detention, the police must request approval for arrest (asking the Procuratorate for formal detention) within 3 days. Special cases can be extended by 1 to 4 days. Cases such as mobile crimes (committing crimes consecutively in multiple locations) can be extended up to 30 days. The Procuratorate has an additional 7 days to decide. In total, a decision on whether to arrest will be made within a maximum of 37 days. When the Procuratorate considers approving an arrest, "if the defense lawyer requests it, they must listen to the defense lawyer's opinion." Lawyers also have the right to request a change in compulsory measures, such as changing from detention to release on bail pending trial; the investigative agency must respond within 3 days. You are entitled to a lawyer from the first interrogation or from the time compulsory measures (such as this type of detention or arrest) are applied. While the case is still with the investigative police, you may only hire a lawyer. If a lawyer requests a meeting, the detention center must arrange it within 48 hours at the latest. If you might only be sentenced to public surveillance or short-term criminal detention (lighter punishments than fixed-term imprisonment under Chinese law), or only a supplementary punishment without a main punishment, you may be released on bail pending trial. Release on bail pending trial involves providing a financial guarantee or finding a guarantor, allowing you to go home while waiting for the case to be resolved. Bail can last for a maximum of 12 months (China-wide).

Do not create or sell hacks or support software for games, even AI-based ones that "only read the screen and do not touch the memory"; also, do not sell modified versions of software like WeChat that add features
A

Selling a hack to 20 people or earning ⟦5000⟧ is enough to be sentenced to up to 3 years in prison; particularly serious cases carry 3 to 7 years.
