One person who made wallhacks and aimbots earned over ⟦80000⟧ in 3 months and was sentenced to 1 year in prison, suspended for 1 year, and fined ⟦5000⟧. Another person who used game server programs to open private servers and collected over ⟦20000000⟧ in top-ups received a maximum sentence of 4 years and a maximum fine of ⟦10000000⟧.
Costs no money. The cost is giving up the income from these types of jobs and "small tools." The difficulty is that this money comes quickly, and it seems like no one will prosecute.

Providing programs or tools specifically used to illegally intrude into or control computer information systems carries a sentence of up to 3 years in prison for serious circumstances, with or without a fine. "With" means both prison and a fine; "without" means just a fine. Particularly serious circumstances carry 3 to 7 years and a fine. The threshold for "serious circumstances" is providing tools to 20 or more people, or gaining illegal profits of ⟦5000⟧ or more. Illegal profit is the money earned from this activity. Intentionally circumventing or breaking technical protection measures set by the rights holder can also constitute a copyright infringement crime, punishable by up to 3 years in prison, or 3 to 10 years for serious cases. Official case: Wang and accomplices made and sold hacks that read and modified game memory for wallhacking and aimbotting. In 3 months, they sold over ⟦80000⟧ worth, with a profit of over ⟦30000⟧. Sentenced to 1 year in prison, suspended for 1 year, and fined ⟦5000⟧. A 1-year suspended sentence means being sentenced to 1 year but not having to go to prison yet; if no further crimes are committed within that year, they do not serve the time. Xiang and accomplices sold the "TZ" hack series with sales over ⟦200000⟧; Xiang was sentenced to 3 years, suspended for 3 years, and fined ⟦20000⟧. Liu and accomplices obtained game server programs, modified parameters, and opened private servers, collecting over ⟦20000000⟧ in top-ups. Sentenced to between 2 years 6 months and 4 years, with fines from ⟦1300000~10000000⟧. It's not just games. A company in Shanghai made ROM packages for phones that added dozens of features to WeChat, such as auto-forwarding, auto-liking, and mass messaging. These phones were sold as "marketing phones," totaling 2,381 units. In 2019, the Xuhui District Court in Shanghai fined the company ⟦500000⟧ for copyright infringement; the person in charge was sentenced to 1 year 6 months, suspended for 1 year 6 months (China-wide).
Do not write or sell scripts for ticket snatching, flash sales, order padding, or promotion hunting, even if it is just "automatic button clicking"
A

Scripts that do not modify memory or crack anything, but simply send requests faster than a human, can still lead to a conviction; earning ⟦5000⟧ or causing ⟦10000⟧ in losses to the other party is enough. One person used purchased 12306 accounts (China's railway ticket website) to snatch over 200 tickets for others, earning over ⟦20000⟧; they were sentenced to 1 year 6 months, suspended for 1 year 6 months, and fined ⟦5000⟧. Someone selling ticket-snatching software on an online shop was ruled to have engaged in unfair competition and ordered to pay ⟦20000⟧ in damages.
Costs no money and no time.

Intruding into a computer information system or using other technical means to obtain internal data carries a sentence of up to 3 years in prison for serious circumstances, with or without a fine; 3 to 7 years for particularly serious circumstances. The threshold for "serious circumstances" is illegal profit of ⟦5000⟧ or causing losses of ⟦10000⟧. Official case: a person used a hack to log into numerous purchased 12306 accounts and ran multi-threaded requests to flood the system for tickets. He snatched over 200 train tickets for others, earning over ⟦20000⟧. The court convicted him of illegally obtaining computer information system data and sentenced him to 1 year 6 months, suspended for 1 year 6 months, and a fine of ⟦5000⟧. Zheng sold ticket-snatching software targeting a specific ticketing app on an online shop; this was ruled as unfair competition, and he was ordered to pay ⟦20000⟧ (China-wide).
Crawlers should only scrape public pages that do not require login, do not bypass anti-crawling measures, do not touch personal information, and scraped data must not be sold
A

Bypassing logins, tokens, or signatures to obtain data can lead to up to 3 years in prison for serious circumstances, and 3 to 7 years for especially serious circumstances. Scraping personal information is even more troublesome. For travel itineraries, communication content, credit, or assets: 50 records already constitute "serious circumstances". For accommodation, health, or transactions: 500 records; for other types: 5,000 records; or earning ⟦5000⟧, the same applies.

Costs no money. A crawler is a program that automatically navigates websites to retrieve data. Before scraping, check the robots file and the API usage description; robots is a file placed in the website's root directory specifying which pages are off-limits. Data that requires login, tokens (temporary pass strings), or breaking signatures must not be scraped. The difficulty lies in the fact that technically this data is scrapable; whether to refrain or not depends entirely on self-discipline.

Bypassing protection layers to obtain data from a system carries the same penalties as item 3 (ticket-hunting scripts, flash sales, order buffing): up to 3 years in prison, or 3 to 7 years. Illegally obtaining, selling, or providing citizens' personal information is considered "serious circumstances" if it reaches any of the following levels: travel itineraries, communication content, credit, or assets from 50 records; accommodation, communication history, health, or transactions from 500 records; other personal information from 5,000 records; or illegal gains of ⟦5000⟧. Serious circumstances are punishable by up to 3 years in prison, with or without a fine; especially serious circumstances carry 3 to 7 years. Official case: A programmer named Li disguised a feature that stole phone photo albums as "beauty scoring" software, obtaining 1,751 face photos. He also resold data from a "social data warehouse" and was sentenced to 3 years in prison with a 3-year reprieve. A social data warehouse is a database that aggregates leaked personal information from various sources. A network technology company used crawlers to obtain store and order data from a food delivery platform, causing damages of over ⟦40000⟧, and was prosecuted for illegally obtaining computer information system data (China-wide).
Do not accept jobs to develop gambling, fraud, or pornography apps; do not set up payment channels or unlock accounts for "customers"
A

Knowing clearly that it is a gambling app but still accepting the job will lead to being prosecuted as an accomplice to the crime of opening a casino. The crime of opening a casino is punishable by up to 5 years in prison, or 5 to 10 years for serious cases, which is heavier than the crime of merely providing assistance (maximum 3 years). In one case involving an e-sports betting app, 28 people were sentenced for opening a casino to terms ranging from 1 year to 3 years and 6 months. A person who unlocked QQ accounts for a fraud gang was sentenced to 1 year and 6 months in prison and fined ⟦20000⟧.

Costs no money. The price is passing up high-paying freelance jobs with vague requirements. The difficulty is that the money offered by the other side is usually significantly higher than normal jobs.

Knowing clearly that others are using the network to commit crimes yet still providing technical support, payments, or similar help is punishable by up to 3 years in prison for serious circumstances, with or without a fine. If another crime is committed simultaneously, the heavier penalty applies. Opening a casino is punishable by up to 5 years in prison and a fine, or 5 to 10 years for serious circumstances. Official case: Zhang Sheng Group developed gambling games and then "packaged the web for external sale," charging web setup and reporting fees. The amount involved in the case was nearly ⟦7000000000⟧. Zhang Sheng was sentenced to 9 years and 9 months in prison and fined ⟦50000000⟧. 79 people in charge of outsourced development, including Wang Qiang, were sentenced to terms ranging from 6 months to 9 years and 9 months. Chen Dong and accomplices developed and operated an e-sports betting app with the technical team coding in Hainan; 28 people were sentenced for opening a casino to terms from 1 year to 3 years and 6 months, plus fines. Zhang M.M. opened a studio to unlock banned QQ accounts for fraud gangs and was sentenced to 1 year and 6 months in prison and fined ⟦20000⟧ (China-wide).
When resigning, hand over all accounts and access rights; do not delete databases, leave backdoors, or change passwords to lock the system, even if the company owes you money
A

Accounts and passwords are provided by the company; this does not mean they can still be used after resigning. Illegally controlling a system is punishable by up to 3 years in prison for serious circumstances. Deleting data that causes the system to fail is punishable by up to 5 years for serious consequences, and 5 years or more for especially serious consequences. One engineer who was laid off used an old admin account to delete data and logs, causing over ⟦120000⟧ in damages, and was sentenced to 3 years in prison with a 5-year reprieve and fined ⟦30000⟧.

Costs no money. If the company owes wages, claim them through labor arbitration; do not take matters into your own hands (see Chapter 7 for labor arbitration). The difficulty is having to refrain from touching the system when you are angry.

Illegally controlling a computer information system is punishable by up to 3 years in prison for serious circumstances, with or without a fine; especially serious circumstances carry 3 to 7 years. Deleting or modifying system functions or data, making the system unable to operate normally, is punishable by up to 5 years in prison for serious consequences, and 5 years or more for especially serious consequences. Official case: Senior IT engineer Lu M.M., after being laid off, used an old admin account to log into the company's shared server. He changed passwords and deleted data and logs, causing over ⟦120000⟧ in damages. He was sentenced to 3 years in prison with a 5-year reprieve and fined ⟦30000⟧. Software company employee Bai M.M., while writing an upgrade program, intentionally inserted bugged code, making customers unable to log into the system and causing over ⟦40000⟧ in damages. He was prosecuted for sabotaging a computer information system (China-wide).
Do not take source code, customer lists, or technical documents when resigning; do not upload them to personal cloud drives or reuse them at a new workplace
A

Code written during working hours usually belongs to the company's copyright, and customer lists can also be trade secrets; taking them is taking company property. One employee who resigned and took security inspection system source code to a new company was sentenced to 5 years in prison and fined ⟦500000⟧, while the new company was fined ⟦4000000⟧. Someone who exploited a system vulnerability to download over 33,000 design files was sentenced to 1 year and 10 months. The company can also file a separate lawsuit for compensation.

Costs no money. Before resigning, wipe all company documents from personal computers and cloud drives. The difficulty is that some files were written line-by-line by yourself, making them hard to let go.

Violating confidentiality obligations, disclosing trade secrets, or using them for oneself is punishable by up to 3 years in prison for serious circumstances, with or without a fine; especially serious circumstances carry 3 to 10 years and a fine. The Anti-Unfair Competition Law (China) also lists two infringing acts: using "electronic intrusion" (using technical means to penetrate systems) to obtain trade secrets; and instigating or helping others to violate confidentiality obligations. Official case: Sun M. Ming and former employees took the source code and core algorithms of a security inspection system to use in a new company's products. Sun M. Ming was sentenced to 5 years in prison and fined ⟦500000⟧, while the new company was fined ⟦4000000⟧. Dian M.M. exploited a system vulnerability to download over 33,000 design files and was sentenced to 1 year and 10 months in prison and fined ⟦100000⟧. Engineer Yang M.M. saved the source code of an app module to a personal computer and the cloud, changed jobs, and made a similar app; he was prosecuted for infringing on trade secrets (China-wide).
Do not run your own programs on others' computers, servers, or cameras; do not use company machines to mine cryptocurrency
A

Controlling others' computers, servers, or cameras without permission is punishable by up to 3 years in prison if it involves 20 or more machines, and 3 to 7 years for especially serious circumstances. If it does not reach the level of a crime, one can still be detained for up to 5 days and fined ⟦50000~500000⟧. Anyone criminally punished for this is banned for life from holding key positions in network security management and network operations.
Costs no money and no time.

Illegally controlling a computer information system is punishable by up to 3 years in prison for serious circumstances, with or without a fine; especially serious circumstances carry 3 to 7 years. Illegally controlling 20 or more machines constitutes "serious circumstances." If it does not reach the level of a crime, the police will confiscate illegal gains, detain the individual for up to 5 days, and may fine them ⟦50000~500000⟧. For relatively heavy circumstances, detention is 5 to 15 days, with a possible fine of ⟦100000~1000000⟧. Those who have received public security penalties are banned for 5 years, and those with criminal records are banned for life, from holding key positions in network security management and network operations. Official case: Li M. purchased IP addresses of network cameras and used software to control 105 cameras to spy on private lives; he was sentenced to 3 years in prison with a 5-year reprieve and fined ⟦20000⟧. Wu M. and accomplices installed trojans into phone motherboards, controlling over 3.3 million devices to intercept and send back verification codes; they were sentenced to terms ranging from 2 years to 4 years and 6 months (China-wide).
Do not test others' systems without a letter of authorization; "good intentions" and "reporting later" are not legal excuses for exoneration
A

The law convicts based on whether authorization was obtained and how much was taken, not your intent. Obtaining 500 sets of common account/password info, or earning ⟦5000⟧, or causing ⟦10000⟧ in damages is enough for up to 3 years in prison. To prove a vulnerability, simply exporting one user table often exceeds 500 sets. Using existing accounts/passwords outside of the permitted scope also counts as intrusion.

Costs no money. Before participating in a vendor's SRC or crowdsourced testing, obtain a document clearly stating the permitted scope, target list, and testing timeframe. An SRC is a Security Response Center established by a vendor to receive vulnerability reports from outsiders. Stop once a vulnerability is verified. The difficulty is resisting the urge to "just try one more thing."

Systems of companies and ordinary individuals fall under computer information systems outside the fields of state affairs, national defense construction, and cutting-edge science and technology. Intruding into such systems, or using other technical means to obtain data stored, processed, or transmitted within them, is punishable by up to 3 years of fixed-term imprisonment or short-term criminal detention (under Chinese law) for serious circumstances, with or without a fine. Especially serious circumstances carry 3 to 7 years and a fine. "Serious circumstances" include: obtaining 10 or more sets of identity authentication information (e.g., accounts, passwords) for online financial services like payments, stock trading, or futures trading; obtaining 500 or more sets of other identity authentication information; illegally controlling 20 or more machines; illegal gains of ⟦5000⟧, or causing economic losses of ⟦10000⟧. Five times these figures constitute "especially serious circumstances." Official case: Guiding Case No. 36 of the Supreme People's Procuratorate (China) established that: "using accounts and passwords to log into a computer information system beyond the scope of authorization constitutes an act of intruding into a computer information system." This means even if you have the account and password, using them outside the permitted scope is considered intrusion. In this case, three people used accounts, passwords, and tokens obtained during their employment to log into the company's internal system from elsewhere. They downloaded data outside their job scope and sold it online, making illegal gains of ⟦37000⟧. The three were sentenced to 4 years, 3 years and 9 months, and 4 years respectively, with each fined ⟦40000⟧ (China-wide).
Report vulnerabilities according to regulations; do not disclose details, release exploit tools, or send them abroad before a patch is completed
A

Individuals are also subject to the "Provisions on the Management of Network Product Security Vulnerabilities" (China). Before a vendor provides a patch, you must not disclose the vulnerability, nor disclose details of vulnerabilities in running systems. You must not post programs or tools specifically for exploiting vulnerabilities; any disclosure must include mitigation methods. Undisclosed vulnerabilities must not be provided to foreign organizations or individuals other than the vendor itself.
Costs no money. Report vulnerabilities to the product provider or to official platforms. Do not post details or Proof of Concept (PoC) code before the vendor finishes patching.

These regulations govern three groups: network product providers, domestic network operators, and organizations or individuals involved in discovering, collecting, and disclosing vulnerabilities. No organization or individual may exploit vulnerabilities to harm network security, nor illegally collect, sell, or disclose vulnerability information. Public disclosure must follow five rules. One, no disclosure before the provider issues a patch. Two, no disclosure of vulnerability details for networks, information systems, or equipment currently used by network operators. Three, no intentional exaggeration of harm and risk, and no malicious hype or fraud using vulnerability information. Four, no disclosure or provision of programs or tools specifically used to exploit vulnerabilities for harmful acts. Five, disclosure must simultaneously include patching or prevention measures. Additionally, undisclosed vulnerability information must not be provided to foreign organizations or individuals other than the product provider. The regulations encourage reporting to four official platforms: 1. The Cyber Security Threat and Vulnerability Information Sharing Platform of the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (China). 2. The vulnerability platform of the National Computer Information and Network Security Information Reporting Center (China). 3. The vulnerability platform of the National Computer Network Emergency Response Technical Coordination Center (China). 4. The vulnerability database of the China Information Technology Security Evaluation Center. Illegal collection or disclosure is handled by the MIIT and the Ministry of Public Security (China). Violations of the Cybersecurity Law (China) are punished accordingly. Public disclosure of network security information such as system vulnerabilities must follow state regulations. Violators will be ordered to correct, warned, and may be fined ⟦10000~100000⟧. Failure to correct or serious circumstances lead to fines of ⟦100000~1000000⟧. Related business operations may be suspended, or business licenses revoked. Directly responsible managers and other personnel are fined ⟦10000~100000⟧ (China-wide).
Do not sell firewall-circumvention tools or VPN accounts, and do not set up such nodes for others
B

Setting up your own international connection or using international channels other than the state's public channels can lead to the police ordering a disconnection, a warning, a fine of up to ⟦15000⟧, and confiscation of illegal gains. Making a business of this can lead to prosecution for illegal business operations, punishable by up to 5 years in prison for serious circumstances. This section refers to selling and setting up nodes. For personal use, the maximum penalty is a warning plus a fine.
Costs no money and no time.

Direct international networking must use international entry and exit channels provided by the state's public telecommunications network. No unit or individual may set up or use other channels: they may not build their own lines abroad, nor use lines built by others. Violators will be ordered by the police to disconnect, warned, and may be fined up to ⟦15000⟧ with confiscation of illegal gains. Making a business of this can lead to prosecution for illegal business operations. Serious circumstances carry up to 5 years in prison, with or without a fine of 1 to 5 times the illegal gains. Especially serious circumstances carry 5 years or more (China-wide).

If you signed a non-compete agreement and the company fails to pay monthly compensation after you leave, send a written demand; if they fail to pay for 3 months, you can terminate it; positions that never touched trade secrets can seek to invalidate the clause
A

Non-compete restrictions mean that after leaving, you cannot work for a competitor for a certain period, up to 2 years, and the company must pay monthly compensation. If no amount is agreed upon, it is 30% of the average salary of the 12 months before leaving, not lower than the local minimum wage. If they fail to pay for 3 months due to the company's fault, you can request termination. From 2025, positions that never had contact with trade secrets can seek to have the clause declared invalid.
Costs no money. When resigning, keep the original non-compete agreement and evidence that the company failed to pay monthly compensation.

Non-compete restrictions only apply to senior management, senior technical personnel, and others with confidentiality obligations. The maximum term is 2 years. During this period, the company must pay monthly economic compensation. If no amount is agreed, it is 30% of the average salary of the 12 months before leaving, and not lower than the local minimum wage. If the company fails to pay for 3 months for its own reasons, the employee can request to terminate the non-compete agreement. If the company proactively terminates it, they must pay an additional 3 months of compensation. From 2025, employees whose positions never knew or touched trade secrets can request to have the clause declared invalid. If the scope of the agreement is broader than the secrets the person actually knew, the excess part is void. Official case: A pharmaceutical company sued CTO Zheng M., demanding a penalty of ⟦7100000⟧. The court determined that the new workplace's products did not replace the old company's products, and the non-compete scope must be limited to the secrets he actually knew, dismissing all claims (China-wide).
Code written during work hours using company resources belongs to the company; for your own open-source projects, use your own time and equipment, and do not mix in company code
A

Software created primarily using the company's equipment, internal network, or business data, for which the company bears responsibility, belongs to the company's copyright; you only retain the right of authorship; the same applies if the contract so stipulates. Writing outside of hours but using company computers or business data can also be counted as belonging to the company. Inventions made primarily using company resources also belong to the company.

Costs no money. When starting a job, read the intellectual property clauses in the employment contract carefully. The difficulty is that personal projects and company work often reside on the same computer and must be separated.

Creative works created to fulfill the unit's work tasks are "works created in the course of employment" (things made while working at any unit, not just state agencies). Normally, the copyright belongs to the author, the unit has the right of priority use within its business scope, and for 2 years the author may not allow third parties to use it in the same way. However, there are two other types. One is works such as engineering designs or software created primarily using the unit's material and technical conditions and for which the unit bears responsibility. Two is works where the contract stipulates they belong to the unit. For these two types, the author only retains the right of authorship. The unit's material and technical conditions include things like equipment, internal networks, and company business data. Inventions created while performing the unit's tasks, or primarily using the unit's material and technical conditions, are "service inventions." The right to apply for a patent and the granted patent both belong to the unit (China-wide).
When using open-source code like GPL for products, open the source code or switch to a different license library as required; do not assume "no one is watching"
B

Infringing on copyright requires compensation based on the other party's losses or the amount you earned; intentional infringement with serious circumstances can lead to damages 1 to 5 times the base amount. There was a company that hired a competitor's former employees, created software that was essentially the same, and then argued that the other party used GPLv2 so they should have opened their source code. The Supreme People's Court (China) held that whether the other party opened their source code or not did not affect their copyright, and still ordered the infringement to stop with compensation of ⟦500000⟧.

No cost. Before using someone else's open-source code, review the license (the usage conditions clearly stated by the author). The GPL family requires products using it to also publish their source code, which conflicts with keeping code closed for sale; if there is a conflict, switch to another library. The difficulty lies in having to abandon a library you are already accustomed to using.

Copyright infringement is compensated based on the actual loss of the rights holder, or the amount earned by the infringer. If neither can be clearly calculated, it is based on the normal amount paid to purchase the right to use. Intentional infringement and serious circumstances can result in damages 1 to 5 times the base amount. Harming public interests can also lead to the confiscation of illegal gains and fines. Official case: Intellectual Property Civil Appeal Judgment No. 51/2021 of the Supreme People's Court (China). The defendant hired former employees of the plaintiff and created gateway software essentially identical to the plaintiff's software. The defendant argued that the plaintiff's software was based on GPLv2 and should have been open-source. The Supreme People's Court determined that "whether the developer themselves violated the GPLv2 license and whether they hold copyright over the software are two independent issues," ordering the cessation of infringement and compensation of ⟦500000⟧ (China-wide).
Develop apps that only collect personal information truly necessary for business operations, obtain guardian consent for those under 14, and write clear privacy policies
B

Only collect information necessary for business; those under 14 must have guardian consent. Violations will first be ordered for correction, and the app may be suspended. Failure to correct results in fines up to ⟦1000000⟧, with the person in charge fined ⟦10000~100000⟧. Serious cases carry fines up to ⟦50000000⟧ or up to 5% of the previous year's revenue, with the person in charge fined ⟦100000~1000000⟧.

No cost. Before launch, cross-check the list of permissions requested by the app against the privacy policy; remove any unnecessary permissions. The difficulty lies in the product side always wanting to keep a little extra data "in case it's needed later."

Processing personal information must have a clear, reasonable purpose directly related to that purpose, and use the method with the least impact on individual rights. Processing personal information must be consented to by the individual or fall under cases permitted by law. For persons under 14, consent from parents or guardians is mandatory. Violations will lead to regulatory authorities ordering corrections, warnings, confiscation of illegal gains, and ordering the infringing app to temporarily suspend or terminate services. Failure to correct results in fines up to ⟦1000000⟧, with the person directly in charge and other directly responsible persons fined ⟦10000~100000⟧. Serious circumstances carry fines up to ⟦50000000⟧, or up to 5% of the previous year's revenue. Responsible persons are fined ⟦100000~1000000⟧. These individuals may also be barred from serving as directors, supervisors, or senior managers of related enterprises for a period. Selling or providing personal information to a criminal extent is covered in section 4 (China-wide).
Complete ICP procedures for websites and apps before official launch, and keep logs for at least 6 months as required by multi-level protection
A

Registration is free; if the server is located in China and not registered, and you refuse to correct it, the site will be closed. Declaring the registration as a non-profit service while actually charging users results in fines of 3 to 5 times the illegal gains, or ⟦100000~1000000⟧. Logs must be kept for 6 months; failure to correct or causing consequences results in fines of ⟦10000~100000⟧.

ICP registration is free, following the process of the cloud provider; based on the author's experience, it takes from a few days to a few weeks. Multi-level protection assessment is charged by level. Multi-level protection (abbreviated as "Dengbao" in China) is a set of security management tasks classified by the state according to the importance of the system, which websites and systems are required to perform.

Commercial internet information services must apply for a license; non-commercial ones must register. Operations are not allowed without a license or registration. If unregistered, telecommunications regulators will order correction; failure to correct will lead to site closure. Operating a business without a license results in confiscation of illegal gains and fines of 3 to 5 times that amount, or ⟦100000~1000000⟧. Failure to display the registration number on the homepage results in fines of ⟦5000~50000⟧. Network operators must follow the multi-level protection system to establish security management rules, prevent attacks, store network logs for at least 6 months, and classify, back up, and encrypt data. Failure to do so results in ordered correction and warnings. Failure to correct or causing consequences results in fines of ⟦10000~100000⟧, with the manager in charge fined ⟦5000~50000⟧ (China-wide).
Conduct safety assessments and register algorithms according to regulations before providing generative AI services to the public; label generated content
B

Generative AI services aimed at the public that can influence public opinion or mobilize people must undergo safety assessments and algorithm registration before running; modifications or suspensions also require change or cancellation procedures. Generated images and videos must be labeled. Small tools for personal use not open to the public do not need to worry about these matters. Violations are punished according to the Cybersecurity Law (China) and other laws.

No cost, but you must follow the procedures of the cyberspace administration, which takes some time to complete. As long as the tool you create does not provide services to the public within China, it does not fall under the scope of these measures.

Providing generative artificial intelligence services with public opinion attributes or social mobilization capabilities must undergo safety assessment according to state regulations. Algorithm registration must also be completed according to algorithm recommendation management regulations, along with subsequent change and cancellation procedures. Public opinion attributes or social mobilization capabilities mean the ability to influence public thinking or organize and mobilize people. Providers must label generated content such as images and videos. The measures specify: enterprises, research institutions, etc., researching and applying generative AI technology that "do not provide generative AI services to the domestic public are not subject to the provisions of these measures." Violations are "punished according to the provisions of the Cybersecurity Law, Data Security Law, Personal Information Protection Law, and the Law on Progress of Science and Technology of the People's Republic of China and other laws and administrative regulations." The measures have been in effect since August 15, 2023 (China-wide).
Do not create or distribute tools that automatically skip or block ads from other apps; doing so for free can still be ruled as unfair competition
A

Creating software that skips or blocks ads of other apps on behalf of users can lead to lawsuits for unfair competition. Not charging money can still be counted, as the "business operators" governed by the law include individuals providing services. A browser that defaulted to blocking pre-roll ads on Mango TV was ordered to pay ⟦800000⟧. An app that allowed users to skip Mango TV's opening ads directly was ordered to pay ⟦80000⟧ in damages.
No cost. The price is giving up a very popular small tool. The difficulty lies in feeling that you aren't making a dime and are just clicking "skip" for the user.

The law stipulates that business operators must not use technical means to hinder or destroy the normal operation of network products and services legally provided by other business operators. Business operators here include natural persons, legal persons, and non-legal organizations providing goods or services. Causing damage to the other party requires compensation based on their actual losses, or the benefits you gained, plus reasonable costs incurred by the other party to stop the infringement. Market regulators can also fine ⟦100000~1000000⟧, or ⟦1000000~5000000⟧ for serious circumstances. Official case: a built-in feature of the 720 browser defaulted to blocking pre-roll and pause ads on the Mango TV site. The first instance dismissed Mango TV's lawsuit. The Guangzhou Intellectual Property Court reversed the judgment on appeal, identifying it as unfair competition and ordering ⟦800000⟧ in economic damages and reasonable costs. In 2021, the Supreme People's Court (China) included this in its list of typical cases. The "Lan Jing Ling" app allowed users to skip Mango TV's opening ads directly. The first instance ordered a stop and ⟦80000⟧ in economic damages and ⟦10000⟧ in reasonable costs. In April 2024, the Beijing Intellectual Property Court upheld this on appeal. The appeal held that the app essentially blocked the opening ads, rather than just clicking "skip" for the user (China-wide).
Do not set up "AI transit stations" to resell foreign large model APIs at low prices: a station owner in Shanghai has already been criminally detained
C

AI transit stations are websites that resell APIs of foreign large models at low prices. A station owner in Shanghai shared that he was criminally detained for 37 days for this, is currently on bail awaiting trial, will certainly be convicted, and has surrendered his illegal gains and assets. The Ministry of State Security (China) also issued a warning, stating some transit stations lack operating qualifications, and some even unauthorizedly transfer user data abroad.

No cost. The price is giving up an easy-to-enter side hustle with decent-looking revenue. If you truly want to build a model aggregation platform, take the proper route: apply for a business license and connect to models with official authorization; this costs significant time and money.

In June 2026, the Ministry of State Security (China) issued a risk warning. The warning stated that AI transit stations are proxy layers sandwiched between users and the official services of model companies. Some stations lack operating qualifications. Some lack the legal qualification to send data abroad and have not passed the security assessment process required by law, yet have transferred user input data to overseas servers. Some even help users bypass network access restrictions, official authorizations, and cross-border data transmission. In June 2026, the "China News" weekly reported a case. In May 2026, a transit station owner in Shanghai posted a closure notice on a technical community. He stated he was criminally detained by Shanghai police for 37 days for illegally obtaining large model APIs and is currently on bail awaiting trial. He said he "will certainly be convicted in the future," has surrendered illegal gains and assets, and must pay a fine. The article stated such stations register or purchase foreign large model subscription accounts in bulk, set up overseas servers as springboards, and then resell them cheaply to domestic users (China-wide / Shanghai).
Do not write, sell, or distribute crack patches, keygens, or cracked versions of software; selling enough to reach a certain amount is prosecuted as copyright infringement
A

Checking registration codes and dongles are technical measures of software; bypassing them without permission is an infringement, and compensation is required even if no money was collected. Cracking and selling crack tools for profit, with gains of ⟦30000⟧ or sales of ⟦50000⟧, is enough for criminal prosecution, with a maximum of 10 years in prison. Someone who sold cracked dongles with pirated software was sentenced along with two others to between 1 year and 3 years 2 months in prison.

No cost. The price is giving up quick-money side hustles like selling cracked versions, registration codes, or cracked dongles. Do not upload crack patches to forums or network drives either. The difficulty is that cracking seems like just a technical task, not like stealing.

First is civil. The Copyright Law (China) allows rights holders to attach technical measures to works. Technical measures are effective technologies, devices, or components used to prevent or restrict others from using works without permission. Without permission from the rights holder, no one may intentionally bypass or destroy technical measures. Nor may they manufacture, import, or provide to the public related devices or components intended to bypass technical measures. Nor may they intentionally provide technical services to help others bypass technical measures. Computer software is a work; doing these things constitutes infringement, requiring the cessation of infringement and compensation for damages. Compensation is calculated based on the actual loss of the rights holder or the amount you earned. If neither can be clearly calculated, it is based on the normal amount paid to purchase the right to use. Intentional infringement and serious circumstances result in damages 1 to 5 times the base amount. If public interests are also harmed, the copyright administration can also confiscate illegal gains. Illegal turnover from ⟦50000⟧ can be fined 1 to 5 times that amount. Below ⟦50000⟧ or if uncalculable, the fine can be up to ⟦250000⟧. Next is criminal. The Eleventh Amendment to the Criminal Law (China) included "intentionally bypassing or destroying technical measures" under the crime of copyright infringement, provided it is for the purpose of profit. Illegal gains from ⟦30000⟧, or illegal business turnover from ⟦50000⟧, results in up to 3 years in prison, with or without a fine. Ten times these amounts results in 3 to 10 years in prison and a fine. Persons who know others are committing copyright infringement and still provide them with devices, components, or technical services primarily used to bypass or destroy technical measures are also prosecuted under this crime if the amounts reach the same thresholds. Official case one: from March 2019 to July 2022, Liu Mou Sheng, wanting to make money, manufactured "dongles" that bypassed software technical measures. He also copied pirated software and sold it with the dongles. Illegal business turnover exceeded ⟦1060000⟧. The Shanghai No. 3 Intermediate People's Court identified the circumstances as particularly serious, convicting him of copyright infringement. The Supreme People's Procuratorate (China) stated this was the first case in the country regarding copyright infringement by "intentionally bypassing or destroying technical measures" after the Eleventh Amendment to the Criminal Law took effect. In April 2023, the Shanghai court sentenced three defendants in this chain to between 1 year and 3 years 2 months in prison, some with suspended sentences, and fines from ⟦80000~700000⟧. Official case two: medical equipment repairman Liu Mou spent ⟦80000⟧ to buy 50 sets of cracked dongles in a QQ group, then resold them online for several thousand yuan each. Plugging them in bypassed the medical equipment's identity authentication to access maintenance software. The Putuo District Court in Shanghai sentenced him to 1 year 2 months in prison with a suspended sentence and a fine of ⟦80000⟧. Official case three: starting May 2021, Li Mou Mou in Xuzhou and accomplices found someone to write game console crack programs and produced crack devices for sale. Illegal business turnover exceeded ⟦39000000⟧. In November 2024, 10 people were sentenced to between 2 years 6 months and 3 years 6 months in prison, some with suspended sentences, and fines from ⟦1500000~11000000⟧ (China-wide).
Do not help others with DDoS attacks, and do not sell or rent "load testing" platforms that fire traffic; even if you lose a game, do not crash the other party's server
A

Using DDoS to make someone else's website, server, or game inaccessible is the crime of sabotaging computer information systems. Serious consequences lead to up to 5 years in prison; particularly serious consequences lead to 5 years or more. People who pay to place orders for a platform to attack are also accomplices. Someone who opened a DDoS site charging membership fees and taking orders was sentenced to between 10 months and 5 years 6 months in prison.

No cost. DDoS involves controlling many machines to simultaneously send requests to a target, clogging the server until it is unusable. The price is giving up a business charging per-instance or selling traffic packages, and also suppressing temporary anger. If there is a conflict with others in games or business, report it, complain, or call the police; do not pay to hire someone to attack.

Interfering with the functions of a computer information system, making it unable to operate normally, results in up to 5 years of fixed-term imprisonment or short-term criminal detention (under Chinese law) for serious consequences. Particularly serious consequences result in 5 years or more. Courts consider DDoS as the "interference" mentioned here. "Serious consequences" have several criteria. One is that the main software or hardware of 10 or more computer information systems cannot operate normally. Another is illegal gains from ⟦5000⟧, or economic damage from ⟦10000⟧. Another criterion is a system serving 10,000 or more users being stopped from normal operation for a cumulative total of 1 hour or more. Numbers of machines or money 5 times these levels constitute particularly serious consequences. Knowing others are sabotaging in this way and still providing programs or tools used for sabotage is punished as an accomplice. The threshold is illegal gains from ⟦5000⟧, or providing to 10 or more person-times. Helping them by providing server hosting or technical support with illegal gains from ⟦5000⟧ is the same. Some people provide programs or tools specifically used to illegally intrude into or control computer information systems. Providing to 20 or more person-times, or illegal gains from ⟦5000⟧, results in up to 3 years in prison, with or without a fine. If it does not reach the level of a crime but interferes with system functions or provides such tools, causing harm, it results in up to 5 days of detention, or 5 to 15 days for relatively heavy circumstances. Official case one (Guiding Case No. 69): in early 2017, Yao Xiaojie and accomplices were hired to form the "Anye Group" abroad. They bought large amounts of server resources and used controlled trojans for DDoS attacks. They attacked the IPs of three game companies hosted on an internet company's cloud server three times; the games could not be logged into, and players repeatedly dropped. The victim company spent over ⟦40000⟧ to recover. In June 2018, the Nanshan District Court in Shenzhen sentenced 11 people for sabotaging computer information systems to between 1 and 2 years in prison. Official case two: in March 2017, Tang Mou and Wang Mou set up a DDoS site where users could top up for membership and submit attack tasks. They took orders and attacked the traffic of over 80 target IPs. The Haimen Court in Nantong sentenced Tang Mou and accomplices for sabotaging computer information systems to between 10 months and 5 years 6 months in prison. Zhang Mou placed orders on this site to suppress industry competitors, submitting over a hundred attack tasks targeting 11 IPs or domains of the rival company. The court determined the order-placer and the website operator were accomplices. The order-placer was the initiator and principal offender. Official case three: Wang Mou set up a DDoS platform, publicly selling "Bronze," "Silver," "Gold," and "Diamond" attack packages. He was prosecuted by the Haidian District Procuratorate in Beijing for illegal use of information networks; in 2020, the first instance sentenced him to 1 year in prison and a fine of ⟦50000⟧ (China-wide).
Only start a business with money you can afford to lose: do not touch family savings, and do not borrow money to open a shop
B

Individual industrial and commercial households (China) must use the money and assets in your name to pay debts. If it cannot be distinguished whether the whole family is working together, family assets are used for repayment. Setting up a company is not necessarily safe: when a company cannot pay its debts, creditors can demand you pay in advance any capital you promised to contribute but which is not yet due. Therefore, spend only an amount that "if lost entirely, you can still pay the mortgage and go to the doctor."

No cost. Before starting, set a figure for yourself: this amount can be lost entirely without affecting mortgage payments, raising children, or medical treatment. Do not exceed that figure. Family money and borrowed money are not included in this figure. The difficulty is refraining from pouring more money in when the business seems to be picking up.

Losses are not just about losing money. For debts of an individual industrial and commercial household (China), if you operate alone, the money and assets in your name are used for repayment (liability with personal assets). If the whole family operates together, or it cannot be distinguished who operates, the money and assets of the whole family are used for repayment (liability with family assets). A debt signed by both spouses is a joint debt, repaid by both. Subsequent consent by one party also counts. For a debt in one person's name, if the creditor proves the money was used for the couple's joint business, both are still liable. There is also a regulation for companies. The amount shareholders promise to contribute to the registered capital is called subscribed capital. When a company cannot pay a due debt, creditors can demand shareholders pay in advance the portion of that capital not yet due for contribution (China-wide).
Do not sign personal guarantees for company loans, and especially do not let your spouse co-sign
A

If you sign a "joint and several liability guarantee," the creditor can bypass the company and demand payment directly from you if the company cannot pay. If it says "general guarantee," the creditor must sue the company first, and only after selling all company assets can they come to you for the remainder. If a spouse co-signs, the assets of both are dragged in, and the "limited" nature of a limited liability company effectively ceases to exist for you personally.

No cost. When banks, suppliers, or landlords ask you to sign a "personal joint and several shareholder guarantee" or for a "spouse signature," stop for a moment. Signing that page means you are personally removing the "company debt does not reach individuals" protection layer (waiving limited liability). If you can avoid signing, don't sign. If you must sign, only sign a "general guarantee" and clearly state the maximum amount you are guaranteeing. The difficulty is that the other party often says "no signature, no disbursement," so you must stand firm.

The wording in a guarantee document means "if the debtor doesn't pay, you pay." If it says "joint and several liability guarantee," the creditor can skip the company and come straight to your house to demand payment. If it says "general guarantee," the creditor must first sue the company or go to arbitration, then ask the court to enforce the sale of company assets to offset the debt. Only after the sale, if there is still a shortfall, is it your turn to make it up. A debt signed by both spouses is a joint debt, repaid by both. Subsequent consent by one party also counts. A spouse's signature means the assets of both are dragged in (China-wide, since 2021).
Choose the right business type before opening: sole proprietorships and general partners pay debts to the end, only limited companies are truly "limited"
A

Sole proprietorships and general partners must pay whatever they owe; shareholders of a limited company are only liable up to the amount they promised to contribute at registration. But whatever you promise, you must actually contribute within 5 years: recording ⟦1000000⟧ means you may owe ⟦1000000⟧. If you mix company books with personal books or use the company to evade debt, the "limited" status loses its effect. If the company has only you as a shareholder, you must provide the books yourself to prove there is no commingling.

Register on the local public service portal, taking a few hours each time. Once a limited company is established, you must keep books and declare taxes every month, which is a long-term expense: doing it yourself takes time, hiring a service accountant costs money, and prices vary by location.

Debts of a sole proprietorship (China) are paid using personal money and assets, or the money and assets of the entire household. Members of a general partnership (China) bear unlimited joint and several liability for the debts of the enterprise. This means you pay whatever is owed; it is not over until it is fully paid. Creditors can even target just one person among them and force that person to pay the entire amount. Limited partnerships are different: limited partners therein are only liable up to the amount they promised to contribute (within the scope of the committed capital contribution). Shareholders of a limited liability company are also only liable up to the amount they promised to contribute (within the scope of the committed capital contribution). However, the "limited" status loses its effect in three cases. First, the promised contribution must be fully paid within 5 years from the company's establishment; when the company cannot pay a debt that has become due, creditors can demand the contribution in advance. Second, if capital is contributed and then withdrawn (illegal withdrawal of capital), it must be returned. Third, if the company is used as a shell to evade debt, causing serious damage to creditors, you personally must jointly pay the company's debt (joint and several liability). Companies with only one shareholder are even stricter: that shareholder must personally prove that the company's money and their own money are separate. If it cannot be proven, that individual must jointly pay the company's debt. The court mainly looks at whether the money and books are separated. If a shareholder uses company money arbitrarily without recording it, or if company books and personal books are not separated, it is considered commingling (All China, from July 2024)
Do not act as a nominee shareholder, do not hold shares on behalf of others
A

Once your name is recorded in the register, you are a shareholder in the eyes of the law. The money promised at registration must be fully contributed on time; if it cannot be contributed, in addition to making up the contribution, you must compensate the company for damages. At the time of establishment, if other shareholders do not actually contribute, you must jointly pay for whatever is missing. The business belongs to someone else, but the debt is in your name.
No cost. If anyone asks to "borrow your ID to be a nominee shareholder" or "temporarily put shares in your name," refuse them all.

A shareholder named in the register is a shareholder by law. You must contribute the promised amount in full, without missing a single cent, according to the deadline specified in the company's articles of association (fully pay the committed capital contribution). Failure to contribute on time requires making up the contribution and compensating the company for damages. If a shareholder does not contribute actual money at the time of establishment, other founding shareholders must jointly pay within the scope of that deficiency (joint and several liability). When the company cannot pay a debt that has become due, creditors can demand that the portion of capital not yet due for contribution be paid in advance. The actual business operator is not named in the registration, but the debt is in your name (All China, from July 2024)
Before accepting a franchise, check the registration records at the Ministry of Commerce, obtain a hard copy of the information disclosure, and include a "consideration period" in the contract
A

According to regulations, the brand owner must personally open 2 direct stores and operate them for at least 1 year; within 15 days of signing the contract, they must also register with the commercial authority. Before signing, they must provide you with a written document covering 12 items, such as franchise fees, how deposits are returned, and whether existing stores are profitable or losing money. If no registration is found, they refuse to provide documents, or they demand payment before showing the contract, walk away immediately.

No cost. Go to the "Franchise Information Management System" of the Ministry of Commerce (China) to check if the brand is registered. Then require the other party, before signing, to provide the mandatory disclosures in writing along with the contract. It takes a few hours.

Regulations require the brand owner (referred to as the franchisor in documents) to have at least 2 direct stores opened and operated by themselves for over 1 year. Within 15 days from the date the first franchise contract is signed, they must register with the commercial management authority. Failure to register results in a fine of ⟦10000~50000⟧. If they still fail to register after the deadline, the fine is ⟦50000~100000⟧ and the fact is publicly announced. Before signing, they must provide you with a written disclosure covering a total of 12 items. These include the types and amounts of franchise fees; circumstances under which deposits are returned; the number of existing franchisees and their business performance. It also includes a summary of audit reports for the last 2 years and litigation/arbitration cases in the last 5 years. The contract must also clearly state: within a certain period after signing, the franchisee can unilaterally withdraw (unilaterally terminate). If the brand owner hides information or provides false information, the franchisee can terminate the contract (All China, from May 2007)
Before registration, finalize the name, business location, industry, and registered capital; if the documents are complete, receive the license on the spot
A

The registration itself is free; registration fees have been suspended since 2015; anyone collecting money is not collecting a registration fee. The dossier consists of only five items: application, identity or status documents, business location documents, articles of association or partnership agreement, plus whatever additional items are specified by regulations. If the dossier is complete, the license is issued on the spot; if not possible on the spot, it is completed within 3 working days, or an additional 3 working days for complex cases.

The registration step is free. Registration fees for enterprises and sole proprietorships (China) have been suspended since January 1, 2015. Do it yourself on the local public service portal or at a public administrative center, taking a few hours each time. Carving a seal, hiring a service accountant, or renting an address for registration (address service) are market services, not state fees.

The regulations strictly list five items for the dossier. "(1) Application form". "(2) Documents on the applicant's status or personal identity documents". "(3) Documents related to the headquarters or main business location". "(4) Articles of association for companies, non-company enterprise legal persons, specialized agricultural cooperatives (unions), or partnership agreements for partnership enterprises". "(5) Other documents required by laws, administrative regulations, and the market supervision and management authority of the State Council". To put it simply: an application, a document proving who you are or your eligibility. Plus a document proving you have the right to use the premises or office, along with the articles of association or partnership agreement. Submit whatever else regulations specify. Companies must also submit appointment and identity documents for the legal representative, board members, supervisors, and senior management. Sole proprietorships do not need to submit articles of association. The name is "self-declared by the applicant according to law," meaning you choose and declare it yourself. Registered capital "implements a committed capital registration system," meaning you record the amount you promise to contribute later, rather than paying on the spot. The business industry is chosen from the classification table published by the registration authority. If the dossier is complete and follows the template, it is "confirmed and registered on the spot." If not completed on the spot, it is finished "within 3 working days," with 3 additional working days for complex cases. "The date the business license is signed and issued is the establishment date of the market subject": the date printed on the license is the day the company or store was founded (All China, from March 2022)
If the industry requires a license, do not open without one
A

Opening without a license will be handled by the authority governing that specific license according to their regulations. If you lack even a business license and there are no specific sanctions, you will be forced to stop, your earnings confiscated, and fined up to ⟦10000⟧. Specialized or monopoly sales, or engaging in securities, futures, insurance, or payments without permission, can constitute the crime of illegal business operations if the circumstances are serious, with a minimum sentence of up to 5 years in prison.

No cost. Before opening, clarify whether the business you intend to do requires a license. Running a restaurant or selling food requires a food business license (China). If you only sell pre-packaged food made by others, no license is needed, only a filing. Open for business only after obtaining the license.

Operating without a license will be handled by the authority designated by laws and regulations. If you operate without a business license and the law does not specify the penalty, you will be forced to stop, all earnings (illegal gains) confiscated, and fined up to ⟦10000⟧. There is a heavier framework: specialized, monopoly, or legally restricted goods traded without permission; or securities, futures, insurance, or fund clearing performed without approval. In these two cases, serious circumstances constitute the crime of illegal business operations (China). This is punishable by up to 5 years in prison or criminal detention (custody), along with a fine of 1 to 5 times the earnings. Especially serious circumstances lead to 5 years or more in prison (All China)
For food business, check your category first: production and restaurants need licenses, selling only pre-packaged food requires filing, selling fresh meat and vegetables needs no license
A

Making your own food to sell, such as snack stalls, braised goods, baked goods, or homemade pickles, requires a license; small workshops and street vendors follow specific provincial regulations. Selling only pre-packaged food as defined in standards does not require a food business license but does require filing. Selling fresh meat or vegetables requires no license. Operating without a required license can result in a fine of ⟦50000~100000⟧ even if the batch value is under ⟦10000⟧.

The license itself is free. However, the premises and equipment must meet standards; physical inspections plus paperwork take several weeks. For selling meat, each batch must also have a quarantine certificate and a meat quality inspection certificate.

Food Safety Law (China): food businesses must have a license first. Food production, food sales, and catering services all require a license by law. "However, selling edible agricultural products and only selling pre-packaged food does not require a license. Selling only pre-packaged food must be filed with the food safety supervision and management authority of the local government at or above the county level where the business is located." Edible agricultural products are unprocessed items like fresh meat and vegetables. Pre-packaged food must be assessed according to applicable standards; it is not enough to just see if it was pre-made by others or has packaging. See section 9 (pre-packaged food labeling) for specific definitions. "Specific management measures for small food production and processing workshops, food street vendors... are issued by provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government," meaning these two groups are regulated by each province. Operating a food business without a license results in the confiscation of all earnings, food, tools, equipment, and raw materials. If the total value of the batch based on the selling price (commodity value) is under ⟦10000⟧, an additional fine of ⟦50000~100000⟧ is imposed. If the commodity value is ⟦10000⟧ or more, the fine is 10 to 20 times the commodity value. Pig Slaughtering Management Regulations (China): pigs may only be slaughtered at state-designated slaughterhouses with centralized quarantine. "Except for individuals in rural areas who slaughter for their own consumption, all units and individuals not designated shall not slaughter pigs." "Pig products sold by units or individuals, used in food processing, or used by catering service providers and collective canteens must be pig products that have passed quarantine and quality inspection from a designated slaughterhouse." Therefore, the pork you sell or use must come from a designated slaughterhouse and pass both quarantine and quality inspection. Illegal slaughtering outside designated houses results in forced closure and confiscation of pigs, tools, equipment, and earnings. Penalties follow the same framework as unlicensed food business above. Animal Epidemic Prevention Law (China): animal products sold and transported must be accompanied by a quarantine certificate and quarantine mark. Failure to comply results in forced correction and a fine of up to one time the value of the goods based on compliant items of the same type. Judicial Interpretation (China) adjusts punitive damages, i.e., additional compensation beyond a refund. If food made by small workshops or street vendors fails to meet food safety standards, the court must accept a buyer's claim for ten times compensation (All China)
When selling pre-packaged food, check the label first: production date, shelf life, and ingredients must be fully recorded as regulated
A

Whether food is pre-packaged depends on whether it is pre-packaged in fixed quantities with a uniform weight or volume; it is not just about having a bag. Items weighed and bagged at the time of purchase, made and sold on-site, or restaurant takeout cannot be considered pre-packaged food just because they have a bag or box. Pre-packaged food missing mandatory label content is fined ⟦5000~50000⟧ for batches under ⟦10000⟧. Bulk food must also display the name, date, and other information.
Printing labels costs a few cents to a few dozen cents (RMB) each. Every batch must have the correct date and ingredients filled in, which takes some time.

Until October 2026, the current GB 7718-2011 standard (China) requires pre-packaged food to be pre-packaged in fixed quantities or pre-made in materials or containers. The packaging must state a uniform weight or volume. Items weighed and bagged upon customer purchase cannot be considered pre-packaged food just because there is a bag. Food made and sold on-site does not follow this general labeling standard, and restaurant takeout cannot be subjected to it just because there is a box. The Food Safety Law (China) requires labels on pre-packaged food. For direct sale to consumers, unless standards allow omissions, the label must state the name, specifications, net weight, production date, ingredients or ingredient list, manufacturer's name, address, contact info, and shelf life. It also includes the product standard code, storage conditions, the common name of food additives used as per national standards, and the production license number. Any additional items required by laws, regulations, or safety standards must also be recorded. For bulk food, the container or outer packaging must state the name, production date or batch number, and shelf life. The name, address, and contact info of the producer/operator must also be recorded. Producing or selling pre-packaged food without a label, or with labels/instructions that violate this law, results in confiscation of earnings and food. If the commodity value is under ⟦10000⟧, an additional fine of ⟦5000~50000⟧ is imposed. If the value is ⟦10000⟧ or more, the fine is 5 to 10 times the value. Serious circumstances lead to forced suspension of production/business, up to license revocation. If the label/instructions only have minor errors (defects) that do not affect food safety or mislead consumers, correction is ordered first. Failure to correct results in a maximum fine of ⟦2000⟧. The new "General Standard for the Labeling of Pre-packaged Foods" GB 7718-2025 was announced on March 16, 2025. This version takes effect on March 16, 2027, with a two-year transition period. The new version includes food pre-packaged and then sold by weight or piece, but restaurant food and food made/sold on-site are still excluded. The new version requires a dedicated area on the packaging to display both the production date and expiration date simultaneously. The date must use high-contrast, easy-to-read fonts and colors, and be arranged in year-month-day order (All China)
Ordinary food must not claim to treat diseases: labels, instructions, advertisements, and livestreaming speech all count
A

Labels, instructions, and advertisements for ordinary food must not claim to prevent or treat diseases. Except for medical, drug, and medical device advertisements, no other advertisements may claim to treat diseases or use words that sound like medicine. Fines are 1 to 3 times the advertising cost; if the cost cannot be calculated, the fine is ⟦100000~200000⟧. Serious circumstances may lead to business license revocation.

No cost. Review advertising slogans, product detail pages, and livestreaming scripts. The difficulty lies in refraining from phrases like "lowers blood fat, blood pressure, blood sugar" or "cures constipation."

Food Safety Law (China): "Labels and instructions for food and food additives shall not contain false content and shall not mention disease prevention or treatment functions. Producers and operators are responsible for the content of the labels and instructions they provide." "Food advertising content must be true and legal, shall not contain false content, and shall not mention disease prevention or treatment functions. Food producers and operators are responsible for the truthfulness and legality of food advertising content." This means packaging, instructions, and ads must not claim to prevent or treat diseases; the seller is responsible for what is written. Boasting about food and deceiving consumers is penalized under the Advertising Law (China). The Advertising Law also contains a prohibition: "Except for medical, drug, and medical device advertisements, all other advertisements are prohibited from mentioning disease treatment functions, and shall not use medical terminology or words that easily confuse the advertised goods with drugs or medical devices." Except for those three types, no other ads can claim to cure diseases or use words that sound like drugs or medical devices. Violation results in a forced stop of the advertisement. The advertiser is also required to publicly correct and eliminate the influence within the scope of the publication. Then a fine of 1 to 3 times the advertising cost is imposed. If the cost cannot be calculated or is clearly under-declared, the fine is ⟦100000~200000⟧. Serious circumstances result in a fine of 3 to 5 times the cost, or ⟦200000~1000000⟧. Business license revocation is also possible, effectively ending the business (All China)

The food industry has a criminal red line: selling meat from diseased livestock or substandard goods is enough to constitute a crime; mixing in toxic substances does not require a monetary threshold, with the first tier reaching 5 years in prison
A

Previous items were about fines; this one is about arrests. Selling meat from diseased livestock, meat that fails inspection, or items severely exceeding standards for pesticides, veterinary drugs, or heavy metals can lead to 3 years in prison. It only needs to be "sufficient to" cause serious poisoning to be a crime; no one actually needs to eat it. Mixing non-food, toxic, or harmful ingredients into food starts at up to 5 years in prison, regardless of how much money you made.

No cost. Follow the workflow in item 8 (for food business, check your category first): keep quarantine certificates and purchase invoices, and only use ingredients with traceable approval numbers in your formulations.

Article 143 of the Criminal Law (China) governs this framework. If the food you make or sell fails to meet food safety standards and is "sufficient to cause a serious food poisoning incident or other serious food-borne disease," it is a crime. Punishable by up to 3 years in prison or criminal detention (custody), plus a fine. Causing serious harm to others' health or other serious circumstances leads to 3 to 7 years in prison and a fine. Especially serious consequences lead to 7 years to life imprisonment, a fine, or confiscation of all property. Article 144 governs mixing. Mixing toxic or harmful non-food raw materials into food produced or sold, or selling it while knowing it has been mixed, is punishable by up to 5 years in prison and a fine. Causing serious harm to others' health or other serious circumstances leads to 5 to 10 years in prison and a fine. Causing death or other especially serious circumstances is handled under Article 141 (10 years, life, or death penalty). The Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate (China) issued an interpretation (the Two Courts' Interpretation). This document lists cases considered "sufficient to cause a serious food poisoning incident or other serious food-borne disease." First, "containing pathogenic microorganisms, pesticide residues, veterinary drug residues, biotoxins, heavy metals, and other pollutants that seriously exceed standard limits." Second, "belonging to meat and meat products of livestock, poultry, beasts, or aquatic animals that died of disease, unknown causes, or failed quarantine inspection." Third, "belonging to types prohibited by the state for production and sale due to special needs such as epidemic prevention." Fourth, "nutritional components of special medical purpose formula foods, or primary and secondary foods exclusively for infants and young children, that seriously fail to meet safety standards." Using additives in excessive doses or in the wrong place to the extent of causing the above consequences is also prosecuted under Article 143. What constitutes "toxic or harmful non-food raw materials" is not decided by you. One type is substances prohibited by laws and regulations from being added to food. The other type is substances on lists published by relevant departments of the State Council (China), such as prohibited pesticides or drugs banned for food animals. There is another case considered "other serious circumstances" under Article 144: producing or selling between 100,000 and under ⟦200000⟧. Locations include primary schools, middle schools, childcare facilities, elderly care facilities, and surrounding areas. Targets include minors and the elderly. Setting up an unauthorized pig slaughterhouse and selling the meat is handled as the crime of illegal business operations if circumstances are serious. Reaching ⟦100000⟧ or more, or earning ⟦50000⟧ or more, is considered "serious circumstances" (All China)
Once you have a business license, declare taxes on time and truthfully; even with no revenue, you must declare, and only file a zero return if eligible
A

Even if no tax is due, you must file on time; revenue, costs, and expenses must be filled in according to reality; you cannot fill in all zeros just because there is no revenue. Failure to file results in a forced correction within a deadline, with a possible fine of up to ⟦2000⟧, or ⟦2000~10000⟧ for serious cases. Failure to file any tax for three consecutive months results in being classified as an abnormal taxpayer and suspension of invoice usage.

No cost. File yourself on the electronic tax system monthly or quarterly, taking a few minutes each time. Hiring a service accountant is a separate market expense. If you hire employees, you must also register for social insurance within 30 days of establishment. The difficulty is remembering to file on time even during months with no business activity.

"Taxpayers who have no tax payable during the tax period must still perform tax declaration procedures according to regulations": even if not a single cent of tax is due this period, the return must still be submitted. The Tax Collection and Management Law (China) also requires truthful declaration. Having no revenue, no profit, and no tax payable are three different things. Even without revenue, incurred expenses like rent and wages must be filled in truthfully. Tax-exempt income must also be entered in the correct box and cannot be treated as zero revenue. Whether a zero return can be filed depends on the conditions and requirements of each tax type. The Foshan Tax Bureau (China) provides an example: only after submitting financial reports where revenue, costs, and cumulative profits are all zero can a one-touch zero return be filed. Even then, the number of employees and total assets must be filled in; the entire return is not zeros. Failure to file on time results in "the tax authority ordering correction within a deadline, with a possible fine of up to ⟦2000⟧; serious circumstances may result in a fine of ⟦2000~10000⟧." Failure to file resulting in underpayment leads to recovery of tax, plus daily late fees and a fine of "50% to 5 times" the underpaid tax. Late fees are 0.05% per day. "Failure to declare any tax for three consecutive months results in the tax collection system automatically identifying the entity as an abnormal taxpayer and suspending the use of invoice books and invoices." After three months of no filings, the system automatically classifies you as abnormal; invoices cannot be obtained or issued. It is automatically cleared after filing supplements and paying fines. Entities that hire people "must, within 30 days of establishment... apply to the social insurance agency at the place of registration for social insurance registration procedures" (All China)
Only issue invoices for real transactions; small-scale taxpayers should utilize full tax exemptions
A

Small-scale taxpayers (China), until the end of 2027, are exempt from value-added tax (VAT) if monthly sales are less than ⟦100000⟧ or quarterly sales are less than ⟦300000⟧. During the same period, the 3% levy rate is also reduced to 1%. Conversely, asking someone to issue an invoice for tax deduction purposes is considered false invoicing; penalties start at up to 3 years in prison and a fine of ⟦20000~200000⟧.
Zero cost. Do not buy invoices, do not sell invoices, and do not "run invoice books" for others. Issue invoices and declare taxes based on actual business activities.

The group of small-scale taxpayers who pay taxes according to a simplified method are called small-scale taxpayers. The law states: "if sales do not reach the tax threshold, VAT is exempt." This is known as the tax threshold. From January 1, 2026, to December 31, 2027, the threshold is ⟦100000⟧ per month or ⟦300000⟧ per quarter. For transactions calculated by instance or by day, the threshold is ⟦1000⟧; no tax is due if sales are below this amount. During the same period, the 3% levy rate is reduced to 1%, except for the sale of real estate, property leasing, and the transfer of land use rights. Conversely, issuing special VAT invoices without a real transaction, or other invoices used for tax deduction, constitutes false invoicing. This is punishable by up to 3 years in prison or criminal detention, plus a fine of ⟦20000~200000⟧. Issuing for others, issuing for oneself, asking others to issue for oneself, or introducing others to issue invoices all count. If the tax amount involved is relatively large, the sentence is 3 to 10 years. If the amount is exceptionally large, the sentence is 10 years to life imprisonment (China-wide).

Anyone claiming to be from the tax authority who calls or texts urging you to transfer money to a designated account to pay taxes is a scammer; tax matters are only handled through the electronic tax system and the 12366 hotline
A

Tax authorities will not call to ask for your bank card password, payment password, or SMS verification code, nor will they provide an account number for you to transfer tax money into.
