Real auditors must present an inspection notice and an inspection ID. If you receive such a call, hang up first, then call 12366 to verify. If you have already transferred money, call 110 or 96110 immediately to block the payment.

Zero cost. If you receive a call or text about a "random tax audit," "abnormal account," "fine for not filing taxes," or if someone tries to friend you, hang up first and do not reply. Then call 12366 or the landline of your local tax office to verify.

Verbatim reminder from the State Taxation Administration (China): "Tax authorities do not request bank card passwords, payment passwords, account balances, or SMS verification codes related to bank card transactions via WeChat mini-programs, phone calls, or text messages." "Some criminals pose as tax officials, using the guise of 'filing taxes on your behalf,' 'processing tax incentives,' or 'policy guidance' to approach taxpayers." To verify, call the "12366 tax and fee service hotline or the landline of the managing tax authority." Real auditors "must present an inspection notice and an inspection ID." "Tax payments are only made through the electronic tax system or at the tax service hall; tax authorities do not provide designated accounts." There are also regulations for tax intermediaries. "Extorting money from taxpayers or withholding agents in the name of tax authorities and tax officials" is punishable by fines depending on the severity. Posing as a state official to commit fraud is punishable by 10 to 15 days of detention, with a possible additional fine of up to ⟦1000⟧. If an act constitutes both fraud and the crime of impersonating an official, it is "convicted and punished according to the heavier regulation" (China-wide).
When receiving money, record it as a "deposit" (diànjīn) rather than an "advance payment"; clearly state the amount of breach-of-contract penalties; treat trade credit as a loan
A

Recording it as a "deposit" (China) triggers the double-refund rule: if you breach the contract, you lose the deposit; if the other party breaches, they must pay you double. Any portion exceeding 20% of the contract value is not counted. If recorded as an "advance payment," this legal rule does not apply. Allowing trade credit (debt) is essentially lending your money for free; if the other party collapses, it becomes bad debt.

Zero cost. Use the specific term "deposit" in the contract, with the amount not exceeding 20% of the total contract value. Receive payment before delivering goods. Before agreeing to let the other party take goods first and pay later (trade credit), conduct a thorough background check on them.

A deposit is only established upon actual delivery to the other party. If the party paying the deposit breaches the contract, they cannot recover it. If the party receiving the deposit breaches, they must return the original amount plus an equal amount (double refund). The portion exceeding 20% of the total value of the contract (the subject matter of the main contract) is not recognized as a deposit. If the agreed breach penalty is excessively high or low compared to actual losses, the court may adjust it up or down at the request of a party. If a contract includes both a breach penalty and a deposit, only one can be chosen in the event of a breach; both cannot be claimed (China-wide, since 2021).
Sign a written contract within the first month of hiring; register for social insurance within 30 days
A

If an employee has worked for a full month without a written contract, starting from the second month, you must pay double salary for each month until one year is reached. Social insurance must be registered within 30 days of the start of employment; failure to do so or failure to rectify after the deadline results in a fine of 1 to 3 times the required insurance premium. The law does not recognize the concept of "employees voluntarily waiving social insurance."

The portion of social insurance paid by the company is a recurring cost; rates vary by location. Signing the contract itself is free; you can use the standard contract templates provided by the local labor authority.

If an employee has worked for more than one month but less than one year without a written contract, double salary must be paid for each month. Social insurance (China) must be registered for them within 30 days of their first day of work. Failure to do so results in a mandatory rectification order. If the deadline passes, a fine of 1 to 3 times the insurance premium is imposed, and the person directly in charge is fined separately ⟦500~3000⟧. If social insurance is not paid on time or in full, a late fee of 0.05% per day is added from the date of delinquency. If still unpaid after the deadline, an additional fine of 1 to 3 times the debt is imposed. The unit must declare and pay in full and on time. Only legally defined force majeure reasons, such as natural disasters, allow for delayed or reduced payments. There is no provision for "voluntary waiver by employees" (China-wide).
Pay wages according to the contract and the law; document salary increases, loans, and bonuses in writing
C

Wages must be paid on time and in full according to the contract and the law. If wages are owed, employees can apply directly to the court for a payment order. If salary increases, bonuses, or advances are only verbal, the party that cannot provide evidence will suffer in a real dispute. While the law does not mandate a written document for personal loans from an employer to an employee, it is best to write a loan agreement specifying the amount, interest, and repayment date.

Zero cost. Clearly state the salary in the contract. For salary increases, bonuses, advances, or loans, have both parties sign and keep a copy of the document. Do not make verbal promises. Do not pay company wages out of your own pocket. The difficulty lies in sticking to these rules even when acquaintances ask for favors.

Mandatory contents of a labor contract (China) include the method of wage payment and social insurance contributions. The unit must pay wages promptly and in full according to the contract and state regulations. If payment is delayed, employees can apply directly to the court for a payment order (a debt collection document issued by the court). If an owner uses their own money to lend to an employee, it is a loan contract. The Civil Code of China states: "A loan contract shall be in writing, unless otherwise agreed upon for loans between individuals." An individual owner lending to an employee qualifies as a loan between two individuals, so the law does not mandate a written form. Contract content "usually includes terms on the type of loan, currency, purpose, amount, interest rate, term, and repayment method." Writing a loan note based on these items is the author's recommendation. Verbal bonus promises without black-and-white documentation will disadvantage whichever party lacks evidence in a dispute (China-wide).
Sell before you build: use pre-orders and small orders to test for buyers before investing in production
B

A study in Italy showed that entrepreneurs who set hypotheses first and then used market feedback to test them performed better. They were also more likely to pivot in a timely manner without quitting early. Therefore, if no one is willing to pay in advance or place a small order, do not believe that "if you build it, they will come."

A few dozen to a few hundred yuan to make a prototype or a landing page. Then find a few dozen real customers to pay in advance or place small orders. This is a few weeks slower than starting production immediately. The difficulty is resisting the urge to produce the goods first.

A randomized controlled trial (RCT) followed 116 startups in Italy for about a year. An RCT involves randomly dividing people into two groups, training only one group, and comparing the results. Result: entrepreneurs who were trained to make decisions by "setting hypotheses first and then rigorously testing them with market feedback" had better business outcomes. They were also more likely to pivot their plans in a timely manner, and their early exit rate was not higher. The author refers to projects that look promising but are actually unfeasible as false positives. The author explains that this method reduces the likelihood of continuing to pour money into such projects (Italy, published in 2020).
After finishing the prototype, review the mass production checklist before discussing the start of construction
C

The difference between one prototype and one thousand units lies in where the capital is tied up. The yield rate determines the actual cost; the minimum order quantity (MOQ) and payment terms determine how much cash you must advance; inventory determines when the money returns. Products in the mandatory certification catalog cannot be shipped or sold without certification and the certification mark.

A few hundred yuan to run a small trial batch. Then spend a few hours calculating the yield rate—how many out of 100 units produced are sellable. Clearly calculate each item: the supplier's MOQ and payment terms, how much capital inventory occupies, packaging and shipping, certifications and licenses, and trademarks. The difficulty is resisting the urge to skip this step and start construction immediately.

The difference between one prototype and one thousand units lies in where the capital is tied up. The yield rate determines the actual cost; yield is the proportion of a batch that meets standards for sale. Suppliers require a minimum order quantity (MOQ), and there is a duration before payment is received (payment terms); these two factors determine how much cash you must advance. Inventory determines when the money returns. Products in the mandatory product certification catalog (China) must pass certification and have the certification mark attached before they can be shipped and sold. Shipping or selling without certification results in penalties under certification and accreditation regulations. Opening a restaurant or selling food requires a food business license (China-wide).

Keep vouchers and supplier information for every batch; do not import if the price is significantly lower than market value: if employees import counterfeit goods for the company, the owner is also convicted when the company commits a crime
A

Selling goods with counterfeit trademarks and earning ⟦30000⟧, or having sales reach ⟦50000⟧, is enough for a conviction and up to 3 years in prison. Unsold goods valued at three times the sales threshold also count. "I didn't know they were fake" is not enough: if the purchase price is significantly lower than market value without explanation, it can be determined that you knew. Keeping purchase contracts, invoices, payment vouchers, and supplier information is the only way to be exempt from compensation.

Zero cost. For each batch, keep several items: purchase contract, invoice, payment voucher, business license, and authorization letter from the supplier. Then set an internal rule: whoever imports the goods must sign for them, and any price significantly lower than market value is strictly rejected. The difficulty is passing up cheap batches that look very profitable.

Selling goods while knowing they bear counterfeit registered trademarks, where the illegal gain reaches ⟦30000⟧, meets the threshold for conviction. The same applies if the sales amount reaches ⟦50000⟧. Punishment is up to 3 years in prison plus a fine, or just a fine. At ten times these levels, the sentence is 3 to 10 years plus a fine. Unsold goods in the warehouse also count: if their value is three times the sales threshold or more, it constitutes a crime. "Knowing" does not require your admission. A 2025 judicial interpretation by the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate (China) lists five scenarios where knowledge can be directly determined unless you provide evidence proving otherwise. 1. Knowing the registered trademark on the goods has been altered, swapped, or covered. 2. Forging or altering the trademark owner's authorization, or knowing it is forged/altered. 3. Having been criminally or administratively punished for selling fakes and then selling the same type of goods again. 4. Importing or selling at a price significantly lower than market value without a legitimate reason. 5. Being discovered by administrative or judicial authorities and then dispersing or destroying infringing goods and accounting vouchers, or providing false evidence. If a company commits this crime, "the unit shall be fined, and the person directly in charge and other directly responsible personnel" are punished under the same article. Thus, even if an employee imported the goods, the decision-maker is still convicted. Conversely, the Trademark Law (China) provides an out: if you truly did not know the goods infringed a registered trademark at the time of sale, "proving the goods were legally obtained and identifying the supplier exempts you from compensation." Whether you are exempt depends on having vouchers and supplier info; without them, this clause cannot be used (China-wide, judicial interpretation effective April 26, 2025).
Images on goods, packaging, tags, and advertisements must be either self-made or licensed; changing colors or adding a logo does not count as "edited"
A

Changing colors, changing the background, or adding your logo to someone else's image is still using their work without permission. Copying someone else's artistic work for profit, earning ⟦30000⟧, reaching a turnover of ⟦50000⟧, or printing 500 copies constitutes copyright infringement, punishable by up to 3 years in prison. For trademarks, "similarity to the point of causing confusion" is itself an infringement.

Stock photo licenses from agencies start at a few dozen yuan per image. Hiring a designer costs a few hundred to a few thousand yuan. For every image used on goods, keep a copy of the license and purchase voucher. The difficulty is not using images conveniently found on the internet.

The Copyright Law (China) treats "using a work by means of adaptation, translation, annotation, etc., without the permission of the copyright owner" as equivalent to direct copying; both are infringing acts. Thus, changing colors, backgrounds, or adding a logo to the original image is still unauthorized use. The threshold for conviction is here: for profit, without the permission of the copyright holder, printing and selling artistic works (copying and distribution). Reaching any of these three numbers constitutes a crime: illegal gain of ⟦30000⟧, illegal business volume of ⟦50000⟧, or a total of 500 copies (pieces). Reaching any of these constitutes the crime of copyright infringement (China). Punishment is up to 3 years in prison plus a fine, or just a fine. At ten times these levels, it is 3 to 10 years. Simply selling infringing goods printed by others, earning ⟦50000⟧ or more, or selling ⟦100000⟧ or more, is punished as the crime of selling infringing copies, with up to 5 years in prison. Trademarks are similar; the following two cases of "likelihood of confusion" fall within the scope of infringement: 1. Using a trademark similar to a registered trademark on the same type of goods. 2. Using an identical or similar trademark on similar goods. "Similar" is an infringement case explicitly stated in the law. Using someone else's trademark with slight modifications is still infringement if it easily leads to confusion (China-wide, judicial interpretation effective April 26, 2025).
Follow protocols in your job role; for kindness outside of protocol, think clearly about who bears responsibility
B

Take nurses as an example: regulations clearly state that if a patient is in critical condition, they must report to the doctor immediately; if a medical order violates regulations, they must raise it with the doctor who issued it. Other roles are the same: check where your protocol marks the "must report" points. Additionally, voluntarily providing emergency assistance that causes injury to the person being rescued does not require compensation.

Zero cost. At work, follow the system, orders, and protocols. Do not make decisions on behalf of others outside your authority. Before wanting to help, ask yourself: if something goes wrong, who is responsible? The difficulty is standing firm against requests to "make an exception" on the spot.

Using nurses as an example, legal documents (China) clearly define work boundaries as follows: If a patient's condition is critical, report to the doctor immediately. In emergencies, to save a critical patient, necessary first aid measures can be taken first. If a medical order violates laws, regulations, or technical standards for diagnosis and treatment, it must be raised with the doctor, and if necessary, reported to the department head. The Civil Code of China further stipulates: A person who voluntarily provides emergency assistance and causes injury to the person being rescued shall not be held liable for compensation (no civil liability) (China-wide).
If you lose money, withdraw according to the correct procedures: if it can be simplified, dissolve it; if debts exceed assets, file for bankruptcy; do not just abandon it
A

If you owe no one, have no unpaid wages, taxes, or social insurance, and all investors sign a commitment letter that is publicly posted for 20 days without objection, a simplified dissolution can be performed. Individual industrial and commercial households do not need public posting; if no one objects within 10 days, it is terminated immediately. If a company cannot pay its debts, it can apply for bankruptcy. If abandoned, failing to submit annual reports for 2 years and being unreachable will lead to the revocation of the business license, and the legal representative will be prohibited from serving as a legal representative for 3 years.

Simplified dissolution (China) can be done by yourself: post publicly for 20 days on the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (China). If debts are not yet paid off, the books must be cleared first—collect what needs to be collected and pay what needs to be paid; this step is called liquidation. Filing for bankruptcy requires a court application and takes several months. The difficulty is that once a loss occurs, people do not want to face it and keep dragging it out without taking action.

Neither owing others nor being owed by others, or all debts have been settled. No unpaid wages, no unpaid social insurance, no unpaid taxes. All investors provide written commitments. With these conditions met, and after 20 days of public posting without objection, a simplified dissolution can be performed. Individual industrial and commercial households do not need public posting; if relevant authorities do not object within 10 days, it is terminated immediately. If a company cannot pay its due debts and debts exceed existing assets (insolvency), it can apply to the court for restructuring, mediation, or bankruptcy liquidation. If dissolved but not yet liquidated and debts exceed assets, the person responsible for liquidation must apply for bankruptcy liquidation. The consequences of abandonment are as follows: failure to disclose annual reports on time leads to being placed on the list of abnormal business operations (China). Failing to submit annual reports for 2 consecutive years, being on the abnormal list without correction, and being unreachable at the registered address leads to the revocation of the business license. If an enterprise's license is revoked and the legal representative bears personal responsibility, they cannot serve as a legal representative, board member, supervisor, or senior manager of a company for 3 years. These 3 years are counted from the date of revocation. Once on the list of abnormal business operations, even simplified dissolution cannot be performed (National China).

Before spending money to hire someone to operate an online shop, taking a shop-opening course, or doing "dropshipping," ask clearly if you will have to pay more money later and where the sales come from
B

This type of scam collects an upfront fee, then uses "upgrade packages," advance payments for goods, or unblocking fees to force you to pay more time and again. Orders and profits in the management dashboard may be faked; when you want to withdraw money, you cannot. Relying on fake orders to boost sales is itself illegal; if the third-party operator is caught, they will be fined.

Costs no money. Before paying, demand three things: a written contract, the full name of the other party's company, and refund conditions. Only pay the exact company listed on the contract; do not transfer to personal accounts. The difficulty is when the other party shows screenshots of "students earning more than 10,000 a month," you must resist paying on the spot.

The High People's Court of Guangdong Province (China) tried a case of fraudulent third-party operation. 55 people, including Jiang X and Xu X, opened multiple companies in Guangzhou, Nanning, and Hangzhou. The court determined they "clearly knew they had absolutely no capacity or technical conditions for e-commerce third-party operation." They still used the name of Taobao shop operation to lure 7,711 victims into buying and upgrading "service packages." In total, they scammed over ⟦52994000⟧. The two ringleaders were sentenced to 14 years and 13 years and 6 months for fraud, respectively. The court stated the scam was "tightly designed" and "many victims were scammed repeatedly." The Jiangsu Provincial Public Security Department (China) in 2025 broke down the "dropshipping" cross-border e-commerce scam into four steps. Step one: post ads like "no experience needed" or "no need to hold stock" on social media. Step two: friend you under the guise of "operation guidance" and tell you to download a designated platform. Step three: after you open the shop, the first order arrives very quickly. The other party tells you to pay the cost of goods upfront, saying the buyer's money is being held by the platform and will be unblocked after receipt. Then the management page generates a series of orders, forcing you to pay more continuously. Step four: when you want to withdraw money, they claim "account abnormality" or "system maintenance" and demand more money for unblocking or handling fees. Ms. Zhang in the case advanced over ⟦900000⟧; 3 days later, the website was inaccessible. Then there are fake orders. A third-party operator organized fake group buys for stores to boost rankings. The market supervision authority fined them ⟦100000⟧, the platform deducted ⟦50000⟧ from the security deposit, and the court upheld the platform's deduction. The Supreme People's Court (China) in 2026 included this in typical cases, stating "fake transactions and creating fake orders to boost reputation are behaviors clearly prohibited by law." The State Administration for Market Regulation (China) in 2025 also announced a case. A company selling "one-click shop transfer" and "one-click dropshipping" software, which took product information from other platforms to post, was fined ⟦530000⟧. The Administration reminded business owners that "shop-stealing transfers" and "dropshipping business" are illegal acts. The remedy lies in the Civil Code of China: if a contract is signed due to the other party's fraudulent means, you can apply to the court or arbitration to cancel it. This must be raised within 1 year from the date you knew you were scammed. Once canceled, the money the other party gained from that contract must be returned (National China).

When establishing a company or an individual industrial and commercial household, submit the previous year's annual report online from January 1 to June 30 every year; even if there is no business, you must submit it; annual reports are free of charge
A

If you establish a company or an individual industrial and commercial household (China), you must submit the previous year's annual report online during the first half of every year. Failure to submit leads to being placed on the list of abnormal business operations; after a supplemental submission, you can apply for removal. Annual reports are free; anyone who calls saying you forgot to submit and tells you to pay via a mini-app or social media account to do it for you is a scammer—check the publicity system yourself first. Ringleaders of this type of scam have been sentenced to over 10 years in prison.

Costs no money. Log in to the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (China) yourself to fill it out once a year. Individual industrial and commercial households can also submit a paper version. The annual report is submitted to the market supervision authority, which is different from filing taxes monthly or quarterly with the tax authority. Having filed taxes does not mean you have submitted the annual report. The difficulty is that it only happens once a year, so it is easy to forget.

Companies must "from January 1 to June 30 each year, submit the previous year's annual report to the market supervision authority via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System and disclose it to the public." Failure to submit on time leads to being placed on the list of abnormal business operations "and administrative penalties according to law." The list of abnormal business operations is posted on the publicity system for anyone to check. In occasions such as public procurement or project bidding, enterprises on the list are restricted or prohibited from participating. Individual industrial and commercial households (China) must also submit the previous year's annual report from January 1 to June 30 each year, either online or in paper form. Households newly opened during the year start submitting from the following year. Individual industrial and commercial households can choose whether to disclose the contents of the annual report, but failure to submit still leads to being placed on the list of abnormal business operations. If placed on the list for failing to submit, once the missing years are submitted, you can apply to the market supervision authority where you registered for removal. A company's annual report must be disclosed to the public. If an individual household chooses not to disclose the content, the system still discloses that the household "has submitted the annual report." Therefore, whether it has been submitted or if it is on the list can be checked on the publicity system. The State Administration for Market Regulation (China) once warned about a scam. Someone "posing as a market supervision official" calls, saying you are overdue and have been placed on the abnormal list. Then they "guide you to a so-called mini-app or social media account," telling you to authorize them and pay. The Administration stated "annual reports are free of charge." Submitting annual reports and applying for removal from the abnormal list "must go through official channels such as the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System." Courts have tried such cases as fraud. The Jingde County People's Court in Anhui (China) concluded a case where a registration agency told call center staff to "intentionally hide their identity" so households would think they were from the market supervision authority. The staff then led people to a third-party mini-app, charging a ⟦98~398⟧ "manual filing document fee." They scammed 10,099 households nationwide, totaling over ⟦3190000⟧. 3 ringleaders were convicted of fraud and sentenced to between 10 years 6 months and 10 years 8 months in prison. In a case tried by the Nanhu District People's Court in Jiaxing (China), the mini-app actually had small print saying "free submission." The court still convicted them of fraud because the staff "intentionally hid the fact that business owners could do it themselves online and fabricated stories of large fines." In this case, 9 people were sentenced to between 8 months and 4 years in prison (National China).

When raising capital for business, only talk directly to relatives, friends, and employees; do not post on personal pages or in groups for public solicitation, and do not let relatives recruit more people for you
A

Borrowing money or contributing capital with relatives, friends, and employees is not illegal in itself. What is illegal is public advertising, collecting money from strangers, and promising to pay back principal and interest or share profits. Collecting up to ⟦1000000⟧, or collecting money from 150 people, is enough for a conviction, with a starting sentence of up to 3 years. If the money is used for legitimate business and fully repaid before prosecution, the penalty may be waived.

Costs no money. When borrowing or inviting capital contributions, only seek out relatives, friends you know, and employees, and speak to each person directly. Do not post on personal pages, do not post in groups, do not print flyers, and do not hold presentation sessions. If a relative says "let me ask others for you," stop them immediately. The difficulty is that when short of money, "bringing in a few more people" seems like the fastest way to get funds.

Article 176 of the Criminal Law (China) regulates "illegally absorbing public deposits or absorbing public deposits in a disguised form, disrupting the financial order." Punishment is up to 3 years in prison or criminal detention, plus a fine, or only a fine. If the amount is huge or there are other serious circumstances, 3 to 10 years in prison. If the amount is especially huge or there are other especially serious circumstances, 10 years or more. Judicial interpretations from the Supreme People's Court (China) specify that four conditions must be met simultaneously. First, not authorized by competent authorities according to law, or using a legal business shell to collect money. Second, public advertising to society via the internet, media, presentations, flyers, text messages, etc. Third, promising to pay back principal and interest or return profits in cash, goods, or shares within a certain period. Fourth, collecting money from unspecified persons in society. The same article continues: "If money is not publicly advertised to society and is only raised from specified targets within the scope of relatives, friends, or internal units, it does not constitute illegal absorption or disguised absorption of public deposits." However, a joint opinion from two courts and one ministry (China) outlines two exceptions that still count as collecting from the public. First, when collecting from relatives or employees, knowing they are collecting from strangers on your behalf and allowing it. Second, to collect money, first hiring outsiders as employees and then collecting from them. There are three thresholds for conviction; hitting one counts: collecting ⟦1000000⟧ or more, collecting from 150 people or more, or causing a direct loss of ⟦500000⟧ or more. Collecting ⟦5000000⟧ or more, from 500 people or more, or causing a loss of ⟦2500000⟧ or more falls into the 3 to 10-year bracket. The amount is calculated based on the total collected. If the money is mainly used for normal production and business and all collected funds are repaid before prosecution, the penalty may be waived. If the circumstances are clearly minor and the harm is not great, it is not considered a crime. If it does not reach the level of conviction, there are still administrative penalties. The local lead agency for handling illegal fund-raising (China) fines from 20% to 1 time the amount raised. For the fund-raising unit, the legal representative and directly responsible persons are given a "warning and fined from ⟦500000~5000000⟧" (National China, judicial interpretation effective from March 1, 2022).

When renting premises to open a shop, check before signing if the building is allowed to host your type of shop: converting a residence into a shop requires consent from all owners in the building; oil-fume restaurants cannot be newly opened in residential buildings
A

Converting a residence into a shop requires the unanimous consent of all other owners in the same building; one household's objection is enough to stop it. If neighbors sue you to restore the original state and pay compensation, the court will grant it. Residential buildings and mixed-use buildings without dedicated chimneys are not allowed to open new oil-fume restaurants; if discovered, you will first be ordered to rectify. Failure to rectify leads to closure and a fine of ⟦10000~100000⟧; renovation costs and deposits may be lost entirely.

Costs no money. Before signing a lease, paying a deposit, or renovating, spend a few hours clarifying three things. First, whether the intended use on the property certificate is residential or commercial. Second, whether the building is purely residential, mixed-use, or a separate shop, and if there are residents upstairs. Third, for a restaurant, check if there is a dedicated chimney, then ask the local market supervision authority if a food business license can be obtained. The difficulty is when landlords or agents say "it's fine, the previous tenant already opened one," you must still check yourself.

Article 279 of the Civil Code of China: "An owner who changes a residence into a building for business purposes shall, in addition to complying with laws, regulations, and management rules, obtain the unanimous consent of the owners with an interest." Judicial interpretations from the Supreme People's Court (China) provide more detail. All other owners in the same building are considered "owners with an interest." Owners in other buildings in the same complex must prove their property value or quality of life is affected to count. If converted without their unanimous consent, and they request a stop, restoration, or compensation, the court must grant it. Using the excuse that "the majority of owners agreed" is not accepted by the court. The Ecological Environment Code (China), effective from August 15, 2026, simultaneously repeals the Law on the Prevention and Control of Atmospheric Pollution (China). Article 250 of the code prohibits new construction, renovation, or expansion of catering service projects that generate oil fumes, odors, or exhaust in three places. First, residential buildings. Second, mixed-use buildings without dedicated chimneys. Third, commercial floors adjacent to residential floors in mixed-use buildings. Violators are first forced to rectify. If they refuse, they are forced to close and fined ⟦10000~100000⟧. The code also requires local governments to remind applicants of prohibition requirements during the registration phase when choosing a restaurant location. To apply for a food business license, the premises must suit the type and quantity of food handled and be a specified distance from toxic substances and other pollution sources. Conversely, if the building itself does not meet the mandatory requirements of laws or administrative regulations regarding usage conditions, you can terminate the lease. The condition is that the inability to use it was not caused by you (National China).

When several people contribute capital to open a shop, write a written agreement before opening: how much each contributes, how money is shared, who decides, who receives a salary, and how to withdraw
C

If no agreement is written, the law sets the rules for you. Decisions must be unanimous, profits are shared according to the amount each person actually contributed, and the person managing the shop daily defaults to receiving no salary. If no cooperation period is agreed upon, anyone can withdraw after giving reasonable notice to the others. To change these rules, the only way is to record them in an agreement beforehand.

Costs no money. The partners sit down once or twice to talk and record about ten items, and everyone signs. You can find partnership agreement templates online; just fill in each item according to the ten items listed in the Partnership Enterprise Law (China). The difficulty is that people who know each other feel "talking about money hurts feelings" and are hesitant to speak up.

Article 4 of the Partnership Enterprise Law (China) specifies that the partnership agreement is negotiated and agreed upon by all partners and established in writing. Article 18 lists ten items the agreement must include. These include the method of contribution, the amount and timing of contributions, methods for sharing profits and losses, and who performs common tasks. It also covers joining and leaving the partnership group, how to resolve disputes, dissolution and liquidation, and liability for breach of contract. If a partnership enterprise is not established and it is just several people pooling together, the partnership contract rules in the Civil Code of China apply. If the contract does not specify, the Civil Code has several default rules. Decisions on common matters, unless the partnership contract agrees otherwise, must be unanimously agreed upon by all partners. Partners performing common tasks cannot demand remuneration for it unless the contract agrees otherwise. Profits and losses are shared according to the contract. If not agreed, they are negotiated. If negotiation fails, they are shared in proportion to the actual capital contributed. If the proportion cannot be determined, they are shared equally. Partners are jointly and severally liable for common debts; anyone who pays more than their share can recover it from the others. If no period is agreed, it is considered an indefinite partnership; a partner can terminate at any time, provided they give reasonable notice to the others. If a partnership enterprise is established without an agreed period, a partner can withdraw by giving 30 days' notice to the others. The agreement also cannot state that all profits go to only some people or that some people bear all the losses (National China).
If someone collapses, is unresponsive, and not breathing normally: perform chest compressions immediately, ask someone nearby to call 120 and find an AED
A

Cardiac arrest often happens at home. People who receive timely chest compressions have a higher rate of surviving to discharge. If they are unresponsive and not breathing normally, press; occasional gasping does not count as normal breathing. Overlap your hands, press hard on the chest, and simultaneously ask someone nearby to call 120 and find an AED.

Costs no money. Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) classes by the Red Cross or hospitals take half a day to a day; learning once lasts for many years. Even without training, you can do it: overlap your hands, place them in the center of the line connecting the two nipples, and press down hard about 2 times per second without stopping.

A meta-analysis of 79 studies involving 142,740 people. For out-of-hospital cardiac arrest, only 7.6% overall survived to discharge. CPR performed by a bystander is associated with a higher survival-to-discharge rate. When dividing groups by the existing survival rates of each study, the survival-to-discharge rate for those receiving bystander chest compressions ranged from 3.9% to 16.1%. These two figures come from different groups and should not be interpreted as the change before and after compressions. Cases witnessed at the time of onset accounted for 53%, but only 32% actually received bystander compressions. China's BASIC-OHCA registry recorded 38,227 cases received by emergency services. Among them, 30,282 cases (79.2%) of cardiac arrest occurred at home. In this group, the rate of bystander compressions was 20.3%, and the survival-to-discharge rate was 1.2%. The sequence is chest compressions first, then asking a second person to call and get an AED. Once the machine is on, follow its voice instructions. Whether to press depends on whether breathing is normal. The 2025 International First Aid Guidelines from the Red Cross state: in the first few minutes after the heart stops, the patient may still have irregular, labored gasping or loud snorting. This type of breathing is not normal breathing. If unsure if breathing is normal, treat it as abnormal. Abnormal breathing, including gasping, irregular breathing, and no breathing, requires immediate CPR.

If an elderly person falls or someone collapses: sit down and call out to them, call 120, do not rush to help them up; for strangers, walking away in China is not illegal, but if you stop, do not carry them yourself
B

This method is mainly for the elderly at home and acquaintances. Sit down and call them first to see if they are breathing normally; if they do not answer and are not breathing normally, follow item 1 (press the chest hard). If they are breathing normally, still do not pick them up; they may have had a stroke or fainted before falling, and forcing them up will worsen it. Ask if they remember how they fell; if they have back pain or look like they have a fracture, absolutely do not move them; call 120 on the spot.

Costs no money. Sitting down to ask a question and making a phone call takes a few minutes. The hardest part is restraining the hand that wants to help them up. For strangers, you must consider an additional cost: calling 120 will leave your phone number, you may be called back, and you may be asked for a statement once. If their family truly clings to you, litigation is measured in months or more. Even if the court eventually rules in your favor, you still pay your own lawyer's fees.

The "Technical Guidelines for Fall Intervention in the Elderly" by the Ministry of Health (China) states two key points. One is that "falls are the leading cause of injury-related death for people aged 65 and older in our country." The other is "when discovering an elderly person has fallen, do not rush to help them up; handle it according to the specific situation." For those who are drowsy or unconscious: call for emergency help immediately. For those vomiting: turn their head to one side and clear the mouth and nose. For those with respiratory or cardiac arrest: perform chest compressions immediately. "If movement is necessary, it must be done gently, trying to keep them lying flat." For those who are conscious: first ask if they remember the fall; "if they cannot remember, it may be syncope or a cerebrovascular accident." For those with severe headaches, or a drooping mouth, difficulty speaking, or limb weakness: "helping the elderly person up immediately may worsen cerebral hemorrhage or ischemia, making the condition more severe." For those with signs of fracture, or back pain, or incontinence: "if you lack relevant professional knowledge, do not move them arbitrarily." All the above cases require calling for emergency help immediately. If the elderly person wants to stand up themselves, you can help them up slowly, "let them sit or lie down to rest and observe, and only leave after confirming they are fine." Regarding the "fear of being framed," the law stipulates as follows. Article 90 of the Supreme People's Court (China) interpretation on the application of the Civil Procedure Law of China has two sentences. The first is "parties must provide evidence to prove the facts on which their claims are based..." The second is "if a party fails to provide evidence before the judgment, or the evidence is insufficient to prove the facts stated, the party with the burden of proof shall bear the adverse consequences." Original text of Article 1198 of the Civil Code of China: "Operators or managers of business premises or public places such as hotels, shopping malls, banks, stations, airports, stadiums, and entertainment venues..., or organizers of mass activities, who fail to fulfill their safety assurance obligations and cause damage to others, shall bear liability for compensation." Article 184 of the Civil Code of China: "a rescuer shall not bear civil liability for causing damage to the person being rescued when voluntarily providing emergency rescue." The Supreme People's Court (China) once published a typical case. A pharmacy owner performed CPR on someone in cardiac arrest and broke their ribs. The rescued person was hospitalized for 18 days and demanded over ⟦9000⟧ in compensation. The court ruled the rescuer bore no civil liability.
Sudden drooping of the mouth, weakness in one arm, or slurred speech: call 120 immediately, do not wait, and do not drive yourself
A

If the mouth droops, one arm is weak, or speech is slurred, call 120 immediately. For a stroke, if clot-busting medication can be used, the earlier the treatment, the greater the chance of recovery. Even if more than 4.5 hours have passed or the onset time is unknown, do not skip emergency care; let the doctor examine and decide. Record the time of onset, do not give water or medicine, and do not drive yourself.
Costs no money. Three actions, known after seeing once: ask them to smile, raise both arms forward, and say a full sentence.

A meta-analysis of individual patient data from 9 randomized trials of intravenous thrombolysis, involving 6,756 people with acute ischemic stroke. Ischemic stroke is a stroke caused by a blocked blood vessel; intravenous thrombolysis is the administration of medication to clear the blocked vessel. This study looked at whether patients had significant disability after 3 to 6 months (modified Rankin Scale 0–1). Using alteplase within 3 hours of onset, the odds ratio was 1.75, with a 95% confidence interval from 1.35 to 2.27. The actual rate was 32.9% in the treated group and 23.1% in the control group, a difference of 9.8 percentage points. The odds ratio is not a ratio of two probabilities and should not be read as a 1.75 times higher chance of recovery. At 3 to 4.5 hours, the odds ratio was 1.26 (1.05–1.51). Beyond 4.5 hours, it was 1.15 (0.95–1.40), and this study found no statistically significant difference. This does not mean it is untreatable after 4.5 hours. The 2026 guidelines from the American Heart Association and American Stroke Association support extending the thrombolysis window for certain patients. Those with unknown onset time, or onset between 4.5 and 9 hours, may still be eligible for thrombolysis after screening with specialized imaging. Whether medication can be used is assessed by a doctor; go to the hospital as soon as possible. The 2017 Expert Consensus on Pre-hospital Emergency Care by the Emergency Medicine Branch of the China Stroke Association requires emergency personnel to transport suspected stroke patients "in the shortest time to the nearest certified stroke center or hospital capable of intravenous thrombolysis and (or) endovascular intervention," and to "pre-notify the receiving hospital before the suspected stroke patient arrives." The consensus also notes that acute stroke patients may have respiratory compromise due to reasons such as "aspiration."
Sudden dizziness and spinning making it impossible to stand, double vision, one eye going dark, or fingers failing to touch your nose: also consider it a stroke and call 120
B

If you only look for the three signs "drooping face, arm weakness, speech," more than one-tenth of stroke cases are missed because some cases do not initially have a drooping mouth or paralyzed arm. Including inability to stand, double vision, or loss of a field of vision reduces the miss rate to 4.4%. If you suddenly feel dizzy and spinning, cannot stand, see double, or cannot touch your nose with your finger, also call 120 and record the time.

Costs no money. In addition to the three "FAST" actions (item 3, sudden drooping mouth, slurred speech), add two more. First, ask them to stand straight and close their eyes to see if they sway, then ask if their vision is doubled or if a patch is missing. Second, when self-suspecting, touch your nose with your finger, then close your eyes and touch it again.

In 2014, the stroke center at the University of Kentucky (USA) reviewed records of 736 acute ischemic stroke cases (stroke due to blocked blood vessels). Among them, 14.1% of patients at onset completely lacked the three symptoms of facial drooping, arm weakness, and slurred speech (FAST). Adding "unsteady gait, leg weakness, and ocular symptoms" to the screening reduced the miss rate from 14.1% to 4.4%. Two hospitals in the USA reviewed emergency records of 465 ischemic stroke cases; 22% were initially missed. If the blood vessels supplying the back of the brain were blocked (posterior circulation stroke), 37% were initially missed, compared to only 16% for the front. People with dizziness were approximately 1.99 times more likely to be missed than those without (odds ratio 1.99), and those with nausea or vomiting were 4.02 times more likely. The 2025 International First Aid Guidelines from the Red Cross also include "sudden blurred vision in one or both eyes" and "sudden difficulty walking, dizziness, loss of balance or coordination" among stroke signs.
One eye suddenly goes dark as if a curtain is being pulled down, even if it resolves after a few minutes, treat it as a stroke and go to the emergency room on the same day
B

One eye suddenly darkening like a curtain being pulled down may indicate a blocked blood vessel in the fundus; the longer the blockage, the less retina can be saved. It is also a form of cerebral ischemia; you must go even if it resolves in minutes. When minor strokes and transient ischemic attacks were switched to same-day evaluation and treatment, the 90-day recurrent stroke rate dropped from 10.3% to 2.1%. Go to the emergency department of a hospital with a stroke center on the same day; do not wait until the next day.
Free. Emergency examination and vascular checks take half a day to a full day.

The 2021 Scientific Statement from the American Heart Association on Central Retinal Artery Occlusion (blockage of the main blood vessel in the fundus) states: "acute central retinal artery occlusion is an emergency." The medical system must recognize it as an emergency and triage it accordingly. The longer the duration of ischemia, the less salvageable retina remains. The EXPRESS study in Oxford looked at two types of patients: minor stroke and cerebral ischemia where symptoms resolve spontaneously (medically called a transient ischemic attack). This group was later switched to same-day evaluation and same-day treatment initiation. After the switch, the 90-day recurrent stroke rate dropped from 10.3% (32/310) to 2.1% (6/281). The summary of the aforementioned scientific statement also notes that central retinal artery occlusion is a form of acute ischemic stroke and a harbinger of subsequent cerebrovascular and cardiovascular events. The UK National Health Service (NHS) classifies "blurred vision or loss of vision in one or both eyes" as a stroke symptom and specifies that you must seek immediate medical attention even if symptoms resolve after a while. If you had stroke symptoms in the past 24 hours that have now resolved, you must still call emergency services.
One eye is both tense and painful, red, seeing rainbow halos around lights, accompanied by headache and nausea: go to the eye emergency room on the same day
B

This could be an acute glaucoma attack (acute high intraocular pressure): fluid in the eye cannot drain, pressure spikes, and crushes the optic nerve connecting to the brain. The longer it is left, the greater the chance of permanent vision loss. During the lockdown in Wuhan, patients waited an average of 241 hours for treatment, and 21.87% went blind. During the same period the following year without lockdown, the average was 121 hours, and 7.84% went blind.
Free. Eye emergency services to measure intraocular pressure and examine the anterior chamber take half a day.

An eye hospital in Wuhan compared patients with acute primary angle-closure glaucoma during two periods. During the 76-day lockdown in 2020, there were 54 people (64 eyes); during the same period in 2021, there were 46 people (51 eyes); the demographics of both groups were similar. From symptom onset to treatment, the lockdown group took 241.84 ± 211.95 hours, while the control group took 121.53 ± 96.12 hours (P = 0.001). Intraocular pressure upon arrival was 52.63 ± 12.45 mmHg compared to 45.16 ± 9.79 mmHg (P = 0.001). The blindness rate was 21.87% compared to 7.84%. Glaucomatous optic nerve damage was detected in 20/64 eyes (31.25%) compared to 7/51 eyes (13.73%) (P = 0.03). A hospital in South Korea reviewed 50 eyes that had suffered an acute attack and subsequently underwent lens extraction. One year later, 25 eyes (50%) still had visual field defects of varying degrees. The longer the interval from symptom onset to pressure reduction, the greater the likelihood of remaining defects (P = 0.005). Another prospective study had 43 people with shallow anterior chambers lie prone for 1 hour in a dark room. Intraocular pressure in both eyes increased significantly (P < 0.01). The dominant eye increased by a median of 3.60 mmHg, and the other eye by 2.70 mmHg (P < 0.05). The NHS states that glaucoma sometimes develops suddenly, with symptoms including intense eye pain, redness, rainbow-colored halos around bright lights, blurred vision, nausea, vomiting, and headache; if these appear suddenly, call emergency services or go to the emergency department. It is usually caused by fluid being unable to drain, increasing pressure and damaging the optic nerve. Those at higher risk are people over 50, those with parents or siblings with glaucoma, people of Asian descent, and people with myopia, hyperopia, or diabetes. The Zhongshan Ophthalmic Center (Guangzhou) treated 243 angle-closure glaucoma patients aged 40 or younger between 2012 and 2019.

Chest pain that feels like pressure, tightness, or squeezing lasting over 15 minutes without relief, or pain accompanied by cold sweats, nausea, and shortness of breath: call 120, do not try to endure it and do not drive yourself
B

If chest pain feels like pressure, tightness, or squeezing and does not subside after 15 minutes, call 120. If the pain is severe, accompanied by cold sweats or shortness of breath, call even if it has only lasted a few minutes. If a patient reaches the hospital and has the vessel cleared within 55 minutes, the 30-day mortality rate is 2.8%. Beyond 55 minutes, it is 9.7%. Do not drive yourself to the hospital.
Free.

Israel conducted a national survey on acute coronary syndrome. The subjects analyzed were patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), a type of heart attack. The time interval was measured from hospital arrival to balloon inflation to clear the blocked vessel (ballooning). If this interval was ≤ 55 minutes, 30-day mortality was 5/178 (2.8%). If the interval was > 55 minutes, 30-day mortality was 15/155 (9.7%). The chest pain guidelines from the UK National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) list symptoms suggestive of acute coronary syndrome: pain in the chest, or in the arms, back, or jaw, lasting more than 15 minutes; chest pain accompanied by nausea, vomiting, profuse sweating, or shortness of breath. The 2025 International First Aid Guidelines from the Red Cross state that for severe pain, shortness of breath, pale or gray skin, and cold clamminess, call emergency services immediately, "even if the pain has only lasted a few minutes." A heart attack can also cause pain in the jaw, upper abdomen, or between the shoulder blades. Women, the elderly, and people with diabetes may have atypical symptoms.
Sudden severe pain like being torn apart, pain traveling from the chest to the back and down to the lower back: call 120 and clearly state "tearing pain"
B

Severe tearing pain traveling from the chest to the back and down to the lower back requires calling 120; state clearly "tearing pain, the pain is moving down." For Type A aortic dissection without surgery (medication only), the in-hospital mortality rate is 58%. It is managed differently from a heart attack, and doctors must suspect it first to test for it. If blood pressure differs significantly between arms or a pulse is missing on one side, report that as well.
Free.

The International Registry of Acute Aortic Dissection (IRAD) included 464 cases from 12 centers. Aortic dissection is a disease causing severe, tearing chest and back pain. Among the first symptoms reported by patients, the most common is sudden onset of sharp, severe pain. However, presentations vary widely; typical signs like a missing pulse on one side occur in only 15.1% of people. The overall in-hospital mortality rate is 27.4%. For Type A dissection without surgery, using medication only, the mortality rate is 58%. The 2022 guidelines for aortic disease from the American Heart Association and the American College of Cardiology use a scoring system to assess the likelihood of dissection. High-risk conditions include connective tissue diseases like Marfan syndrome, a family history of aortic disease, or known thoracic aortic aneurysm. High-risk pain features are chest, back, or abdominal pain that is sudden in onset, very severe, and tearing. High-risk examination signs include a missing pulse on one side or a significant difference in systolic blood pressure (the top number) between arms. The guidelines also state that poorly controlled blood pressure is a known risk factor for aortic rupture and dissection.
Sudden "worst headache of your life," reaching peak intensity within one hour: go to the emergency room for a brain CT scan immediately
A

The key is how fast it reaches its worst: for severe headaches peaking within one hour, about 6% are due to a ruptured blood vessel on the brain's surface. If you are over 40, have neck pain or stiffness, or someone saw you faint, go to the emergency room for a brain CT. Onset during exertion, an immediate explosive pain, or inability to bend the neck forward also count. Most people who get checked are fine, but missing it can lead to re-bleeding.
The emergency visit itself is not very expensive. A brain CT scan in the emergency department costs a few hundred yuan.

10 emergency departments in Canada conducted a prospective cohort study on 2,131 cases of "severe headache peaking within one hour": criteria were pre-defined and then monitored throughout. Among them, 132 cases (6.2%) were subarachnoid hemorrhages (ruptured blood vessels on the brain's surface). The Ottawa SAH Rule has six items: age 40 or older, neck pain or stiffness, and witnessed syncope. The other three are onset during exertion, a sudden thunderclap onset, and limited neck flexion on physical exam. Meeting any one criterion requires testing. This rule identified all patients with hemorrhage, with 100% sensitivity and a 95% confidence interval from 97.2% to 100.0%. The trade-off is that among those without hemorrhage, only 15.3% were ruled out by the criteria (15.3% specificity).
Elderly person hits their head, then two to three weeks or months later becomes unsteady, slow, sleepy, or weak on one side: get a brain CT scan
B

When an elderly person hits their head, blood often doesn't accumulate until the third week. The impact is often minor; more than half of patients cannot recall being injured. The recurrence rate after surgery for this condition can be up to 33%, and the mortality rate up to 32%. If an elderly person suddenly becomes confused, walks unsteadily, is constantly sleepy, or has a weak arm, ask if they fell and hit their head in the last two or three months, then get a CT scan.
A brain CT scan costs two to three hundred yuan.

The Neurosurgery Branch of the Chinese Medical Association and other units published the "Chinese Expert Consensus on the Medical Treatment of Chronic Subdural Hematoma." Chronic subdural hematoma is a pool of blood that gradually accumulates between the layers of the meninges. Technically, it is blood between the arachnoid and dura mater, forming a chronic space-occupying mass. It "usually forms in the third week after a traumatic brain injury" and is common in the elderly. The recurrence rate after surgery can reach 33%, and mortality can reach 32%. For patients over 90, generally only 24% have a good recovery. Systematic review: globally, there are 3.39 to 39.1 new cases per 100,000 people annually, increasing with age; for those over 80, it can be three times higher. The most common causes are trauma and falls, followed by chronic alcoholism, use of anticoagulants, and violence. Geriatric review: manifestations "often include confusion, cognitive decline, gait disturbance, or lethargy, which can mimic other geriatric syndromes." This review also notes the increasing incidence is due to more people using anticoagulants, antiplatelet drugs (like aspirin, clopidogrel), and the elderly being more prone to falls. Another literature review states there is an interval between injury and symptom onset; the trauma is often very mild and thus frequently overlooked. Over 50% of patients deny having been injured.
One leg suddenly swells, becomes tense, and is painful to the touch: seek medical attention early; if accompanied by sudden shortness of breath or chest pain, call 120 immediately
B

If one leg suddenly swells, becoming visibly larger than the other and painful to the touch, get a leg vein ultrasound early. If accompanied by sudden shortness of breath or chest pain, call 120 directly: 17.4% of people diagnosed with pulmonary embolism die within 3 months. For car or plane trips over 4 hours, the risk approximately doubles; stand up and walk occasionally. People at high risk for blood clots should ask a doctor about compression stockings before traveling.
A leg vascular ultrasound (lower limb venous ultrasound) costs one to two hundred yuan.

The International Cooperative Pulmonary Embolism Registry (ICOPER) included 2,454 patients diagnosed with acute pulmonary embolism from 52 hospitals in 7 countries. Pulmonary embolism is a blood clot blocking a pulmonary artery. This group had a 3-month all-cause mortality rate of 17.4% (426/2,454). The World Health Organization's WRIGHT project: continuous travel for 4 hours or more "approximately doubles" the risk of blood clots forming in the veins and traveling to the lungs (venous thromboembolism). However, for an individual, the probability remains very low: sitting still for over 4 hours is "about one in six thousand." The UK National Health Service (NHS) advises: for plane, train, or car trips over 4 hours, wear loose clothing, drink plenty of water, avoid alcohol, and stand up to walk if possible. In 2021, Cochrane synthesized 12 randomized trials where passengers were on flights over 5 hours. People wearing graduated compression stockings had about nine-tenths fewer cases of asymptomatic deep vein thrombosis (detected only by testing): OR 0.10, 95% CI 0.04 to 0.25. Among 2,637 people, 50 cases were found: 3 in the stocking group and 47 in the non-stocking group. No deaths, pulmonary embolisms, or symptomatic clots occurred in these trials. Therefore, whether compression stockings prevent those actual bad outcomes could not be calculated.
Heavy bleeding: first apply firm pressure to the wound with your hands; if pressure on a limb cannot stop it, apply a tourniquet and call 120
A

First apply very firm pressure with hands or clothing; if pressure on a limb cannot stop the bleeding, apply a tourniquet, then call 120; once applied, do not loosen it. Among wounded soldiers on the battlefield, nine-tenths of those who had a tourniquet applied before shock survived, while only one-tenth of those who had it applied after shock survived; all 5 people who needed a tourniquet but did not receive one died. Apply above the wound, twist until bleeding stops, and record the time; do not use shoelaces or rope as substitutes. The neck and torso should only be pressed, never tied.

A windlass tourniquet costs a few dozen to over a hundred yuan; keep one in your car and first aid kit. Learning once how to "apply above the wound, twist until bleeding stops, and record the time" takes a few minutes.

11 Level I trauma centers in Texas (USA) received 1,026 cases of extremity vascular injuries over 6 years. Among them, 181 cases (17.6%) had a tourniquet applied before hospital arrival. Without adjustment, the tourniquet group had a 3.9% mortality rate, while the non-tourniquet group had 5.2%. After balancing other conditions (multivariate adjustment), tourniquet use remained independently associated with survival. Adjusted OR 5.86, 95% CI 1.41 to 24.47. Among 232 wounded soldiers at a Baghdad field hospital: 90% of those who had a tourniquet applied before shock survived, compared to only 10% after shock. All 5 people who needed a tourniquet but did not get one died, while 87% of those who received one survived. The sequence is: direct pressure (clothing or towels are fine) → if limb bleeding cannot be stopped by pressure, apply a tourniquet → call 120 → do not loosen.
Bitten or scratched by a dog or cat: first wash alternately with soapy water and running water for 15 minutes, and get vaccinated on the same day
A

Once rabies symptoms appear, the mortality rate is nearly 100%, so neither wound cleaning nor vaccination should be skipped after a bite. First wash alternately with soapy water and clean running water for 15 minutes, and get vaccinated on the same day. Bites that penetrate the skin or licks on broken skin are Category III exposures and require passive immunization. "Pet dog, already vaccinated" does not change the protocol; the level of care is based on the wound, not the dog's history.

Wound cleaning is free. A full course of rabies vaccine costs a few hundred yuan. Category III exposure also requires rabies passive immunization (direct injection of pre-made antibodies), costing a few hundred to over ⟦1000⟧. The highest cost is delay.

Original text from the 2023 regulations of the National Disease Control and Prevention Administration and the National Health Commission (China): "the mortality rate of rabies is nearly 100%." The procedure is to "use soapy water (or other mild alkaline detergents) and clean running water with certain pressure to thoroughly wash all bite and scratch sites alternately for about 15 minutes." Minor bites on bare skin or scratches without bleeding are Category II exposures and require vaccination. Penetrating bites or licks on broken skin are Category III exposures, which "require wound treatment, injection of rabies passive immunization products, and rabies vaccination." WHO: approximately 59,000 people die from rabies worldwide each year, 99% transmitted by dogs.
For burns, immediately rinse with cool running water for 20 minutes; do not apply toothpaste or soy sauce
A

Children who receive cool running water for a full 20 minutes within 3 hours of a burn are less likely to need skin grafts later. Use cool water, not ice water; applying ice will worsen the injury. If clothing sticks to the burn, do not try to pull it off; after rinsing, cover with a clean cloth and go to the hospital; do not apply toothpaste, soy sauce, sesame oil, or flour. If you only remember later, rinsing within 3 hours is still effective.
Free. Takes 20 minutes.

Australia followed 2,495 children with burns. For children who received cool running water for 20 minutes within 3 hours of injury, the odds ratio for needing a skin graft later was 0.6, 95% CI 0.4 to 0.8. This means the likelihood of needing a graft is lower, but it cannot be stated directly that the probability is only six-tenths. A pooled result of 7 studies also found that "cool running water for 20 minutes within three hours of injury significantly reduces the likelihood of skin grafting and surgical wound debridement." The 2025 International First Aid Guidelines from the Red Cross specify not to rinse with ice water or apply ice, as it worsens the injury. The NHS specifies that clothing and jewelry near the burn should be removed, but anything stuck to the wound should be left alone, and no creams, oils, or butter should be applied to the burn.
Sudden rash all over the body, difficulty breathing, or fainting: treat as anaphylactic shock, call 120 immediately and state clearly
B

If a sudden rash appears all over the body, accompanied by difficulty breathing or fainting, treat it as anaphylactic shock. Call 120 immediately and state clearly "suspected anaphylactic shock" so the emergency team brings adrenaline. Antihistamines and corticosteroids are slow-acting and cannot replace adrenaline. People who have had a severe allergic reaction once should ask their doctor if an auto-injector can be prescribed; inject into the middle of the outer thigh, it can be injected through a layer of clothing if it is not thick.
Free. For people who already know they have severe allergies and carry their own adrenaline auto-injector, there is a cost, and it is a prescription drug.

Adrenaline is the first-choice drug (first-line drug) for anaphylaxis grade II or higher; guidelines categorize it as a strong recommendation. Antihistamines and corticosteroids are slow-acting and cannot replace its position. The 2025 International First Aid Guidelines from the Red Cross clearly state that adrenaline auto-injectors can be injected through clothing, as long as the clothing is not thick. If a doctor has prescribed it and local laws allow, a bystander can assist with the injection if the patient cannot self-inject.

Someone has a seizure and falls: clear the surrounding area, place them on their side, check the watch for timing, do not put anything in their mouth; the same applies to children with febrile seizures
B

Move hard objects away, place the person on their side with the mouth facing downwards, and check a watch to record the time. Do not hold them down, and do not put anything in their mouth; doing so only causes damage to the teeth and jaw. If it lasts more than 5 minutes, if it is the first seizure, or if they do not wake up after the seizure, call an ambulance. Do the same for children with seizures during a high fever; do not remove their clothes or wipe them with cold water to reduce the fever.
Free.

Avoid broken teeth and jaw injuries from prying the mouth open or inserting hard objects. Avoid fractures from trying to hold the person down. More than 5 minutes without stopping is the mandatory threshold to call an ambulance. Seizures in children during a fever are called febrile seizures. The UK National Health Service (NHS) says they are common in children aged 6 months to 6 years. They usually last 2 to 3 minutes, rarely more than 10 minutes, and generally do not harm the child or leave sequelae. The NHS lists cases where an ambulance must be called: first seizure, seizure lasting more than 5 minutes, difficulty breathing, or seizure on only one side of the body. Other cases include being more drowsy than usual for more than 1 hour after stopping, and having more than one seizure within 24 hours. The 2011 guidelines from the American Academy of Pediatrics state that children aged 6 to 60 months with simple febrile seizures usually do not need additional EEGs, blood tests, or brain imaging. Doctors primarily look for the cause of the fever. The NHS also reminds not to remove clothes or wipe the child with cold water to reduce fever.
Diabetic patients suddenly trembling, breaking out in a cold sweat, or speaking unclearly: give 15 grams of sugar first, re-measure after 15 minutes
A

Eat 15 grams of sugar first; sugar cubes or a small box of fruit juice are both fine. Re-measure after 15 minutes; if it is still low, give another dose. Blood glucose below 3.0 mmol/L is hypoglycemia that must be taken seriously by medical professionals; if it is severe enough to require help from others to manage, it can be fatal. If the person is not conscious, do not give them even a single bite to eat as they will choke into the trachea; call 120 directly.
Free. Carry a few sugar cubes or a small box of fruit juice with you.

Blood glucose below 3.0 mmol/L is clinically significant hypoglycemia. People with altered consciousness or movement who must rely on others for help are experiencing severe hypoglycemia, which can be fatal.
Someone is electrocuted: cut the power first, then use a dry wooden stick or similar object to push the power source away, do not pull with your hands
B

Cut the power first, or use a dry wooden stick or similar object to push the power source away before touching the person. Pulling directly with your hands will turn one victim into two. Once separated from the power source, if they are not breathing normally, perform chest compressions immediately according to section 1 (push hard on the chest); do not be afraid to touch them just because it was an electric shock. If high-voltage wires fall to the ground near a transformer, do not handle it yourself; move far away and wait for the power department to cut the electricity.
Free.

Avoid the rescuer also being electrocuted, turning one victim into two. Once separated from the power source, if breathing stops or there is no pulse, perform CPR according to section 1 of this chapter (push hard on the chest). US CDC first aid steps: look first, do not touch, the person may still be in contact with electricity. If the power can be cut, cut it first; if not, use a non-conductive object like cardboard, plastic, or wood to push the power source away. Once separated from the power source, if breathing stops or the pulse is lost, perform CPR immediately. A review article indicates that people who suffer cardiac arrest due to electric shock and are resuscitated usually recover quite well.
CO alarm sounds, or everyone in the room has a headache and nausea: go outside first before calling
B

If the alarm sounds, or everyone in the room has a headache, nausea, or dizziness, get everyone outdoors first before calling. Do not stay inside to find the cause, and do not go back in to close valves. Symptoms are flu-like; "feeling better after leaving the house" is the strongest sign. In 2018, China recorded 11,523 deaths from CO poisoning, mostly in winter; during the three winter months, about seven out of ten died at home.
Free.

The China CDC's death cause surveillance system in 2018 recorded 11,523 deaths due to CO poisoning. The highest numbers were in January (2,845 cases), February (2,321 cases), and December (2,010 cases). During these three winter months, deaths at home accounted for 66% to 73%. These are numbers reported to the system, not estimates based on the national population. In the US, more than 400 people die each year from unintentional CO poisoning not related to fires. More than 100,000 people visit emergency departments, and more than 14,000 are hospitalized. The US CDC states that CO poisoning symptoms are often described as "flu-like". The NHS specifies: symptoms worsen when in the problematic room and improve when leaving it or going outdoors.

Accidentally ingesting detergents, pesticides, or medicine: do not rush to induce vomiting, take the bottles to the clinic immediately; if splashed in eyes or on skin, rinse with plenty of clean water for at least 15 minutes
B

If detergents, pesticides, or medicines are accidentally ingested, do not induce vomiting: vomiting can damage the throat and may cause choking. If strong acidic or strong alkaline detergents are accidentally ingested, the China CDC advises drinking a little milk or egg white first, then taking the bottles to the hospital immediately. If splashed on skin or in eyes, rinse with plenty of clean water for at least 15 minutes; for eyes, pull the eyelids open to rinse, do not rub. Using disinfectant together with toilet cleaner will produce chlorine gas.
Free. Keep detergents, disinfectants, pesticides, and medicines in high places out of children's reach, or in a locked cabinet. Never transfer them into drinking water bottles.

The Institute of Occupational Health and Poison Control under the China CDC divides management into four cases. Ingestion (via digestive tract): immediately drink a moderate amount of milk or egg white, "remember, do not induce vomiting". Go for a check-up as soon as possible, bringing the packaging or instructions "so the doctor can quickly identify the ingredients and plan the treatment". Inhalation (via respiratory tract): move immediately to a well-ventilated area, loosen the collar for easier breathing. If coughing severely, panting, or having difficulty breathing, seek medical attention immediately. Skin contact: immediately rinse the affected area with plenty of clean water for at least 15 minutes, taking care not to let the rinse water splash into the eyes or other healthy skin areas. Eye contact: immediately rinse the eyes with plenty of clean water or physiological saline for at least 15 minutes. When rinsing, pull the eyelids open to let the water flow over the entire eyeball and the inner surface of the eyelids, "absolutely do not rub the eyes". Go to the ophthalmology department immediately after rinsing. Dangerous products are identified by their acidity-alkalinity (pH). Type pH < 3 includes toilet cleaners, descalers, floor cleaners, and stainless steel polishers. Some strong drain cleaners also contain dilute sulfuric acid. Type pH > 11 includes drain cleaners, strong kitchen degreasers, dishwasher powder, oxygen bleach powder, and scouring powder. There is also a type of combined use that causes trouble on the spot: using disinfectant with toilet cleaner containing hydrochloric acid will produce chlorine gas. Chlorine gas irritates the respiratory tract, causing severe coughing and panting, and can even be life-threatening. Not inducing vomiting applies not only to detergents. The NHS poisoning page lists medicines, household cleaning products, certain plants and mushrooms, and pesticides as common causes of poisoning. The NHS clearly states that if you suspect someone has swallowed something harmful, do not make them vomit, "they could choke or stop breathing", and do not give them anything to eat or drink. If the patient vomits, keep some of the vomit for the doctor to see. The 2025 International First Aid Guidelines from the Red Cross clearly state: do not let the person who swallowed poison vomit, "it can damage the throat". Hand over bottles, packaging, and labels to emergency personnel.

Acid, alkali, or other chemicals splashed on the body: remove contaminated clothing immediately, rinse with plenty of running clean water, pull eyelids open for eyes, rinse for sufficient time before leaving
B

Step one, immediately remove contaminated clothing, shoes, and socks; areas where clothing fits tightly are where the injury is most severe. Step two, rinse with plenty of running water at room temperature, do not use hot water, for at least 15 minutes for both skin and eyes. For skin wounds, the Hunan Provincial Emergency Management Department (China) gives a range of 20 to 30 minutes; follow the longer duration. Step three, for eyes, pull the eyelids open to rinse, then go straight to the ophthalmology department.
Free. On your first day of work, check the location of the eyewash station and emergency shower; do not wait for an incident to start looking.

Three steps on-site. Step one, immediately remove contaminated clothing, shoes, and socks: the poison will continue to penetrate the skin, and areas where clothing fits tightly are most severely injured. Step two, rinse with plenty of running clean water. The minimum level provided by the Institute of Occupational Health and Poison Control under the China CDC is "at least 15 minutes" for each area of skin and eyes.
