In 2026, researchers from the University of California, Santa Barbara and other institutions conducted a measurement study. They purchased 28 paid relay stations from Taobao, Xianyu, and overseas online stores, and collected 400 free stations from public communities. Results: 1 paid station and 8 free stations injected malware into returned tool calls. A tool call is a command the AI tells your computer to run, such as installing a software package. Two stations chose specific moments to act; for example, the paper noted they only targeted fully autonomous sessions. 17 stations accessed Amazon cloud service keys intentionally placed by the research team. One station transferred funds from the research team's Ethereum wallet; only a small amount was left in the wallet, with losses under 50 US dollars. The modification demonstrated in the paper was very subtle: changing "requests" in an installation command to "reqeusts" with a similar spelling, which is hard to detect at a glance (Nationwide China).
Check once a year how many SIM cards and bank cards are in your name; if you find any you didn't create, cancel them
C

Some criminals use other people's IDs to get SIM cards for fraud, and the actual owner often doesn't know. There are now official free inquiry channels: you can find out how many SIMs are in your name, how many app accounts are linked to your phone number, and which UnionPay cards you have. If you find something you don't recognize, contact the carrier or bank to verify and cancel it.

Free. For SIM cards, check via the "Gong Xin Wei Bao" official account of the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (China) or the "One-ID Inquiry" mini-program on Alipay; for bank cards, check the "One-Touch Card Inquiry" section in the UnionPay (Cloud QuickPass) app. Each takes a few minutes to fill out, and results are sent via SMS within one or two days. The difficulty is that no one reminds you; you must remember to check once a year yourself.

The Anti-Telecom and Online Fraud Law (China) explicitly states that telecommunications regulatory authorities must "provide convenient channels for users to inquire about SIM card information in their name." The People's Bank of China and other agencies must "provide customers with convenient channels to inquire about bank accounts and payment accounts in their name." The national mobile SIM "One-ID Inquiry" service, directed by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, was launched on September 14, 2021. Using an ID card, one can find the number of SIMs in their name and the carrier for each. The service was created because during the fight against telecom fraud, authorities found that some SIMs involved in cases were obtained by impersonating others. The actual owners were unaware, and their personal credit could be affected. Results are sent via SMS from 10699000 within 48 hours. If the numbers don't match, go to the carrier for details; with authorization, the owner can verify, detach, suspend, or cancel the subscription. In July 2022, "One-ID Inquiry 2.0" was released. Using a phone number and the last six digits of an ID card, one can find how many internet accounts are linked to that number. At that time, it supported companies like Tencent, Alibaba, Baidu, Kuaishou, Douyin, JD, and Meituan, providing only the count. Regarding bank cards, on June 29, 2022, China UnionPay opened the "One-Touch Card Inquiry" feature on the Cloud QuickPass app for all provinces and cities nationwide. Select the bank to query, pass identity verification, and submit. A report is provided within 24 hours, with card information partially masked, and it is automatically deleted after 7 days (Nationwide China).
Before changing or discarding your phone number, transfer bank links, payment accounts, and social media to the new number; don't just let the old number be cut off due to unpaid bills
C

Once a phone number is canceled, carriers can reassign it to someone else after as little as 90 days. Accounts you haven't unlinked are still tied to this number; verification codes will be sent to the new owner's phone, and they could use them to log into your accounts. Therefore, before changing numbers, transfer both your accounts and the phone number registered at the bank to the new one.

Free. You must change the linked phone number for each account individually, and for bank-registered numbers, you must go to the bank. For those with many frequently used accounts, it may take one or two hours. The difficulty is that it's easy to miss accounts you rarely use.

The Telecommunications Service Standards (China) explicitly state: "the minimum freezing period for mobile phone numbers is 90 days," which is the interval from when a number is canceled until it can be reused. After 90 days, the number can be assigned to a new user. The Q1 2025 Telecommunications Service Quality Report from the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology reminded users they can use the "Refresh Reassigned Number" service in the apps of the three major carriers. If you receive a number previously used by someone else, you can use this service to unlink the number from internet accounts registered before you opened it. The Q2 2026 report stated this service covered 258 common internet apps, with unlinking requests exceeding 850 million. The fact that new owners must manually unlink shows that the previous owner's accounts are still tied to the number when it changes hands. In 2024, customer service staff from the three major carriers told the People's Post and Telecommunications News that after a number is canceled, new users can still use SMS verification codes to log into accounts registered by the old user. They reminded users to unlink Alipay, WeChat, and other apps before changing or canceling a number, and to promptly update the registered phone number for bank cards (Nationwide China).
When renting, specify the deposit amount, return date, and deduction conditions in the contract
A

The deposit amount, when it will be returned, and under what circumstances it can be deducted must be written in the contract before signing. Any reason for deduction not in the contract cannot be used by the landlord to deduct from your deposit when you move out.
Free. Takes an extra ten minutes when signing the contract. The difficulty is having to speak up about this directly to the landlord.

State Council Regulations (China) explicitly state: "If the lessor receives a security deposit, the lease agreement shall agree on the deposit amount, the time for return, and the circumstances for deducting the deposit. Except for the circumstances agreed upon in the housing lease agreement, the lessor shall not deduct the security deposit without justifiable reasons." Three things must be recorded: how much the deposit is, when it is returned, and in what cases it is deducted. Any reason not recorded in the contract cannot be used by the landlord to take your money.
If water or electricity is cut, locks are changed, or you are threatened in person: call the police and keep evidence; the law prohibits these methods to force you out
A

Landlords are not allowed to cut off water or electricity, change locks, or use personal threats to force you to terminate a contract or move out; legal documents clearly prohibit this. If this happens, call the police first and keep evidence. Do not confront them physically yourself.
Free. Making a phone call to the police can be done on the spot.

State Council Regulations (China) explicitly state: "The lessor shall not use violence, threats, or other illegal means to force the lessee to terminate the housing lease agreement or return the leased house." Returning the house means forcing you to move out. If this happens, call the police first and keep evidence. Do not confront them yourself.
Brokers are not allowed to collect or pay rent and deposits on your behalf; pay the money directly to the landlord
A

According to regulations, rent and deposits must not be collected or paid by brokers; pay the money directly to the landlord. Every time money passes through a broker's hands, it is another opportunity for them to abscond with the funds. Before paying, check if the recipient is the person named on the property ownership certificate.
Free. Checking the recipient before paying takes a few minutes. The difficulty is being firm when the broker asks you to transfer money to them.

State Council Regulations (China) classify "collecting or paying housing rent and security deposits on behalf of others" as prohibited acts for real estate brokerage organizations; brokers may not receive rent and deposits from you on behalf of the landlord. Money passing through a broker's hands is another chance for them to run away with it.
When renting from a long-term rental company, first check the company's fund supervision account; do not pay a full year upfront just for a discount
A

Paying a full year upfront offers very little discount. If the company goes bust, your deposit and the remaining ten-plus months of rent could be lost entirely. It is even worse if you sign a rental loan: if the company flees, you still have to pay off the loan installments. Before signing, check if the company has disclosed a fund supervision account.
Free. Checking once takes about ten minutes.

State Council Regulations (China) require housing rental enterprises operating under a sublease model to "establish a housing rental fund supervision account and disclose it to the public." Subleasing is when an enterprise rents an entire unit from a landlord and then rents it to you. The small discount for paying a full year upfront does not offset the risk of the enterprise absconding and losing both the deposit and the remaining rent. If a rental loan is also signed, the risk is even greater.
If a house is sold during a lease term, the lease remains valid and you do not have to move out
A

If a house is sold during a lease term, your lease remains valid. The new owner must allow you to stay according to the old contract until it expires. You do not have to move out, nor do you have to renegotiate the price. The condition is that you moved in legally; keep the contract, bank statements, and evidence of the move-in date carefully.
No cost

The Civil Code of China has a rule called "sale does not break the lease." The original text of the law: if the leased property changes ownership during the lease term, it does not affect the validity of the lease contract. During the lease term, if the house changes owners, the signed lease contract remains valid. The new owner must allow you to stay according to the old contract until it expires.
Before signing a lease, check the title certificate and mortgage status; all payments should be made via bank transfer with clear descriptions
A

Before signing, request the landlord to provide identification and the house ownership certificate. Then take your ID card to the real estate registration authority to check if the house is mortgaged or frozen; you can check even before signing the contract. If the house was mortgaged or frozen before the lease and is later auctioned to a new owner, you cannot demand to continue staying. All money should be transferred via bank with clear descriptions to serve as evidence.
No cost. Taking your ID card to the real estate registration authority takes about half an hour. The difficulty lies in requesting the landlord to present the certificate in person.

Before signing, the landlord must show you their identification and the real estate ownership certificate. If there is no certificate, they must provide other documents proving their right to lease. The landlord must also cooperate for you to look up and verify the house information; this is an obligation imposed on the lessor by the State Council (China) regulations. Before signing a contract, you can take your ID card to the city or county real estate registration authority where the house is located (China) to look up several things. You can find: the basic status of the house, whether there are co-owners, whether there is a registered mortgage or right of residence, and whether it is frozen by a court. After signing the contract, you can use the lease contract to look up registration results. This step is important because the "sale does not break the lease" rule has two exceptions. If the house was mortgaged to a bank before the lease and is later auctioned to pay off debt, you cannot demand the new owner let you stay under the old contract. The same applies if the house was frozen by a court before the lease. When the court auctions it, if the lease hinders a prior mortgage right, the court will set aside the lease before selling. Conversely, if the house was leased to you first and you already moved in, and then the owner mortgages it, the mortgage does not affect your lease. If the house is frozen or has ownership disputes that prevent you from living there, you can terminate the contract. If others claim rights that prevent you from living there, you can demand a reduction or non-payment of rent. All payments should be transferred with the description "rent for month ... house number ...", which is the author's experience: if a dispute arises, it proves you paid and what you paid for.
When buying a second-hand house and letting a broker collect the payment, it must go through a dedicated transaction account opened by the broker at a bank
A

If a broker collects payment on behalf of the parties, regulations mandate it must go through a dedicated account they open at a bank. This account is supervised; money must not be transferred to the brokerage company's private account, and certainly not to an individual broker's account.
No cost. The difficulty lies in insisting on using the dedicated account, which may involve some arguing with the broker.

Ministry-level regulations (China) clearly state: if the parties to a real estate transaction agree to let a brokerage organization collect and pay transaction funds on their behalf, the money must be transferred through a dedicated deposit account for customer transaction settlement funds opened by the brokerage organization at a bank. The house payment goes into a supervised dedicated account, not the brokerage company's private account, nor any individual broker's personal account.
Do not rent partitioned rooms: the smallest rental unit is a room according to the original design; kitchens, bathrooms, and balconies must not be used as living spaces
A

According to regulations, the smallest rental unit is a room based on the original design. Kitchens, bathrooms, balconies, and basement storage rooms must not be used as living spaces. Additionally, during the lease term, the landlord cannot arbitrarily increase the price at will.
No cost. The price is that for the same budget, you either live further away or in a slightly more cramped space.

Ministry-level regulations (China) clearly state: the smallest rental unit is a room according to the original design; one room must not be partitioned into several rooms for separate rental. The average residential construction area per person must not be lower than the local minimum requirement. Kitchens, bathrooms, balconies, and basement storage rooms must not be leased for living. During the lease term, the lessor also cannot unilaterally increase the rent arbitrarily. Violations of Article 8 will result in the management authority requiring the lessor to correct it within a time limit; failure to correct it may result in a fine of ⟦5000~30000⟧.
If you have an urban household registration (hukou) and want to live in the countryside, only rent farmers' houses; do not buy rural land to build houses or houses built on such land
A

People with urban household registration are not allowed to go to the countryside to buy land to build houses allocated to villagers, farmers' houses, or "small-title houses" (houses built on collective land without state-issued ownership certificates); state documents clearly prohibit this. Even if villagers say "just write a contract," it is still not allowed. If you want to stay long-term in the countryside, sign a lease contract, with a maximum term of 20 years each time, and renew upon expiration.
No cost. The price is that the house does not belong to you, each lease term is a maximum of 20 years, and you must renegotiate with the owner upon expiration.

Documents from the General Office of the State Council (China) clearly state: "Urban residents are not allowed to go to the countryside to buy land for building houses, farmers' houses, or 'small-title houses'." The same document also stipulates: farmers who have sold or leased their houses will not have applications for new residential land approved. In 2019, a document from the Central Rural Work Leading Group Office and the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs (China) reiterated: "Urban residents are strictly prohibited from going to the countryside to buy land for building houses." The same document provides a legal path: urban residents are allowed to rent farmers' houses for living or business. The lease contract term must not exceed twenty years, and both parties can renegotiate upon expiration.
When buying an uncompleted house, check the pre-sale permit first; deposits, down payments, and loans must only be transferred to the pre-sale supervision account specified in the contract
A

An uncompleted house is a house under construction that is being sold. Without a pre-sale permit, the developer is not allowed to sell or collect deposits. Your down payment and loans, by regulation, must all go into the supervision account until the house meets delivery conditions. Money transferred to other accounts falls outside this protection.

No cost. Before signing, check the pre-sale permit; before paying, verify the account; it takes a few minutes. The difficulty is when sales staff tell you to transfer to another account, you must firmly refuse.

Uncompleted houses are legally referred to as the pre-sale of commercial housing, meaning the developer sells you a house currently under construction. In August 2026, the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development, the Ministry of Natural Resources, and the National Financial Regulatory Administration (China) issued a document stipulating: "House payments paid by buyers, such as down payments and individual housing loans, must all be deposited into the fund supervision account." Supervision is only lifted when the house passes completion inspection and water, electricity, gas, and heating meet delivery conditions. Developers must clearly state the rights and responsibilities regarding depositing house payments into the supervision account in the purchase contract. If the developer violates this and fails to deliver the house on time, you are entitled to terminate the contract as agreed. The developer must refund the money according to the contract and bear liability for breach. The People's Bank of China and the National Financial Regulatory Administration simultaneously stipulated: individual housing loans for purchasing pre-sale houses are transferred directly by the bank into the project's pre-sale fund supervision account. The 2022 document from the three agencies clearly stated: deposits, down payments, and mortgage loans "must all be deposited directly into the supervision account." For projects without a pre-sale permit, developers are not allowed to pre-sell or collect deposits through registration, booking, reservations, or issuing VIP cards. Pre-sale contracts signed without a pre-sale permit are determined by courts to be void. If the developer obtains the permit before litigation, it may be recognized as valid. Money paid outside the supervision account is not part of this supervision mechanism. The same 2026 document also stipulates: for projects sold as completed houses, after obtaining a construction permit, the developer is allowed to collect "a small deposit" in advance. The deposit is supervised by the housing fund supervision authority and deposited in a "deposit supervision account" opened at the project's lead bank; supervision is lifted only when the house meets delivery conditions.

If you have paid a registration deposit or down payment for a new house but cannot sign the formal contract or obtain a loan (e.g., policy tightening or bank stops lending) through no fault of your own, demand a refund from the developer
A

If you pay a registration deposit but cannot sign the formal contract or obtain a loan, first determine who is at fault. If the cause is not due to you or the developer, the developer must refund the deposit or the purchase price plus interest. Policy tightening or banks stopping lending after signing is usually considered no-fault. If you have overdue debt in your credit history or insufficient income, it is considered your fault, and the deposit may not be recoverable.
No cost. When signing the registration form and formal contract, read two extra clauses. If the developer refuses to refund, you must file a lawsuit in court.

The judicial interpretation of the Supreme People's Court (China) clearly states: if a developer has collected a deposit through registration, ordering, or reservation, and a formal sales contract cannot be signed due to one party's reasons, it is handled according to deposit rules. The deposit rules are: if the payer breaches, they lose the deposit; if the receiver breaches, they refund double, see Chapter 12 Section 15 (record it as a deposit when receiving money). If the contract cannot be signed due to reasons not attributable to either party, "the seller must refund the deposit to the buyer." Another clause concerns loans. If the sales contract agrees on payment via loan, and a loan contract cannot be signed due to one party's reasons, making the sales contract unenforceable, the other party may terminate the contract and seek compensation. If the loan contract cannot be signed due to reasons not attributable to either party, both parties may terminate the contract. The developer must refund the principal received and interest, or refund the deposit. Regarding what constitutes reasons not attributable to either party, the law only states principles; here are the author's examples. If local housing loan policies tighten after signing and the bank stops lending, it is usually considered no-fault. If you have overdue debt in your credit history or insufficient income on your statements, it is your fault. If the project lacks procedures and the bank refuses to lend for this project, it is the developer's fault. These two points only apply to commercial housing bought from developers, not to second-hand houses.
When buying a new house, check carefully how area discrepancies are handled before signing; take photos of promises in sales materials, advertisements, and scale models to keep as evidence
A

Unless the contract agrees otherwise, if the registered area after delivery differs from the contract within 3%, the excess is paid for and the deficit is refunded based on actual area. If the discrepancy exceeds 3%, you have the right to return the house, and the developer must refund the money plus interest within 30 days. Promises in advertisements about the house and community facilities, if very specific and influential to your purchase decision, are valid even if not written into the contract.
No cost. Read two extra clauses before signing, and conveniently take photos or screenshots.

Regulations from the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development (China) clearly state: if pricing is based on area, the contract must specify how area discrepancies are handled. If the contract is silent, follow these rules. "If the absolute value of the area discrepancy ratio is within 3% (inclusive), the house payment is settled based on actual area." If it exceeds 3%, you have the right to return the house. If you return it, the developer must refund the collected payment within 30 days of your request, plus interest. If you do not return it and the registered area is larger than the contract, you pay for the portion within 3%, while the portion exceeding 3% is borne by the developer, and ownership still belongs to you. If the registered area is smaller than the contract, the developer refunds you for the portion within 3% and refunds double for the portion exceeding 3%. Regarding advertisements, the judicial interpretation of the Supreme People's Court (China) states: sales advertisements and introductory materials are usually just invitations to negotiate, not contracts. However, if the developer makes specific, clear statements about the house and facilities within the project's development planning scope, and this significantly influences your decision to sign or the house price, it is considered part of the contract. "Such introductions and promises are part of the contract even if not recorded in the commercial housing sales contract"; violations entail liability for breach of contract.
If a developer delivers a new house late or delays the title certificate: send a formal demand letter first to keep evidence, then claim breach of contract penalties
A

If the developer delivers the house late, send a written demand first; if they still haven't delivered after three months, you can return the house. If the contract doesn't specify penalties, compensation is based on the rent of similar houses in the same area. If you don't have a title certificate due to the developer's fault, they must also compensate; if the delay exceeds one year, you can also return the house. The right to return the house has a time limit, do not hesitate indefinitely.
No cost. Write a demand letter, send it via express mail, and keep a copy. If you truly want to return the house or claim compensation, you will likely need to sue.

The judicial interpretation of the Supreme People's Court (China) clearly states: if the developer delivers late and fails to deliver within 3 months after your demand, you may terminate the contract, unless agreed otherwise. The right to terminate has a time limit. If the developer demands your response, you must decide within 3 months. If the developer does not demand it, you must exercise this right within one year from the date you knew you could terminate; otherwise, it is lost. If the contract does not specify penalties or compensation calculation, late delivery is calculated based on the rent of similar houses in the same area during the delay. If due to the developer's fault you still lack a title certificate by the following milestones, the developer bears liability for breach. There are three milestones: the deadline agreed in the contract; 90 days from delivery for uncompleted houses; 90 days from signing for completed houses. If the contract does not specify penalties, it is calculated based on the total purchase price paid, at the overdue loan interest rate set by the People's Bank of China. If the deadline passes and is delayed by another year, and registration is still impossible due to the developer's fault, you may terminate the contract and seek compensation. If agreed penalties are excessively high and the developer requests a reduction, the court uses 30% above actual losses as the standard for adjustment.
Before signing a house purchase, verify if the house is frozen or mortgaged; after signing, go to the real estate registration authority for advance notice registration
A

Before signing, take your ID card to the real estate registration authority to check if the house is mortgaged, frozen, or has a prior registration for someone else. Agree in the contract to perform advance notice registration and do it immediately after signing. Once done, the seller cannot resell or re-mortgage without your consent, as the registration authority will not process it. When formal title transfer becomes possible, you must transfer the title within 90 days, or the advance notice registration becomes invalid.
Before signing, take your ID card for a check, half an hour. After signing, go with the seller to the registration authority with documents, and pay the registration fee according to local rates.

The Civil Code of China clearly states: once a house purchase agreement is signed, to ensure the future acquisition of the house, advance notice registration can be requested as agreed. "After advance notice registration, any disposal of the real estate without the consent of the right holder of the advance notice registration shall not result in property right effects." Advance notice registration has a duration. If the contract is terminated or similar cases occur, or if no application is made within 90 days from the date formal registration becomes possible, the advance notice registration loses effect. The implementation rules of the Ministry of Natural Resources (China) delegate this to registration authorities: it can be done for both pre-sale commercial housing and second-hand house sales. While the advance notice registration is valid, if the seller applies for registration without your written consent, the authority will not process it. If the developer of an uncompleted house does not go with you to apply as agreed, you can apply by yourself. What can be checked before signing: an intended buyer with an ID card can check if the house has mortgages, advance notice registrations, objection registrations, or is frozen. Online contract signing and filing do not determine whether a contract is valid. The judicial interpretation of the Supreme People's Court (China) states: a pre-sale contract that is not filed is still valid, unless both parties agreed it only becomes valid upon filing.

If you are paying a floating-rate mortgage with an interest rate significantly higher than that of new mortgages, negotiate with the bank for a lower rate or apply for a new loan to replace the old one
A

Mortgage interest rates consist of a benchmark rate plus a few points; previously, the added margin was fixed, but since 2024, you are allowed to negotiate changes with the bank. If your rate is significantly higher than the national average for new mortgages, you can ask the bank to lower it or apply for a new loan to replace the old one. For a loan of ⟦1000000⟧ over 30 years, an interest rate lower by half a percentage point reduces the total interest by approximately ⟦100000⟧.
Free. Call the bank's hotline or submit a request via the bank's app; each attempt takes a few dozen minutes. The bank may not necessarily agree.

A 2024 announcement from the People's Bank of China allows borrowers and lenders to negotiate changes to the margin added to the LPR for mortgage rates. LPR is the Loan Prime Rate quoted by the market; mortgage rates equal LPR plus or minus a few points. A representative of the People's Bank of China told reporters that previously, the margin in the contract was fixed for the entire loan term; this has now changed. In August 2026, the People's Bank of China and the National Financial Regulatory Administration further documented: for disbursed floating-rate mortgages, when the rate deviates from the national new mortgage rate to a certain extent, "the borrower may negotiate with the banking financial institution to change the agreed interest rate level in the contract, or apply for a new personal floating-rate mortgage to replace the old one, whichever method the borrower chooses." The amount of the new loan must not exceed the remaining principal of the old one. Regarding savings, here is an example calculated using the equal installment formula (equal monthly principal and interest). For a loan of ⟦1000000⟧ over 30 years, a 4.0% annual interest rate results in a monthly payment of about ⟦4774⟧, while 3.5% results in about ⟦4490⟧. This saves about ⟦284⟧ per month, and over 30 years, the interest paid is reduced by approximately ⟦100000⟧.

When buying your first home and needing a loan, use the Housing Provident Fund loan first; if the limit is insufficient, add a commercial loan to create a combined loan rather than taking a full commercial loan immediately
A

The interest rate for a Housing Provident Fund loan for a first home, with a term over 5 years, is 2.6%; as of June 2026, the interest rate for new commercial mortgages was about 3.1%. For a loan of ⟦1000000⟧ over 30 years, using the full provident fund results in approximately ⟦96000⟧ less interest than a full commercial loan. Provident fund loans have a cap; if insufficient, the remainder is covered by a commercial loan, known as a combined loan.

Free. Requires one or two extra trips to the Housing Provident Fund center or a designated bank; disbursement may be a few days slower than a standalone commercial loan. The condition is that you have contributed to the provident fund continuously for a certain period.

On May 7, 2025, the People's Bank of China issued a document lowering Housing Provident Fund loan rates, effective May 8. For first homes, the rate for terms over 5 years is 2.6%, and 2.1% for 5 years or less. For second homes, it is no less than 3.075% for over 5 years and no less than 2.525% for 5 years or less. As of October 2026, this remains the most recent adjustment. Commercial mortgage rates equal LPR plus or minus a few points; LPR is the Loan Prime Rate quoted by the market. On September 20, 2026, the LPR for terms over 5 years was 3.5%. The People's Bank of China's Q2 2026 Monetary Policy Implementation Report stated that in June, "the interest rate for newly disbursed personal housing loans was approximately 3.1%." Regarding savings, here is an example calculated using the equal installment formula (equal monthly principal and interest). For a loan of ⟦1000000⟧ over 30 years, a 2.6% interest rate results in a monthly payment of about ⟦4003⟧, while 3.1% results in about ⟦4270⟧. This saves about ⟦267⟧ per month, and over 30 years, the interest paid is reduced by approximately ⟦96000⟧. If the limit only covers ⟦600000⟧ from the provident fund and the remaining ⟦400000⟧ is a commercial loan, it is still more profitable than a full commercial loan. This saves about ⟦160⟧ per month, and over 30 years, the interest paid is reduced by approximately ⟦58000⟧. For a second home, the minimum provident fund rate is 3.075%, which is close to the 3.1% commercial rate, resulting in negligible savings.

If a management company cuts off your water, electricity, heating, or gas to force payment of service fees, complain to the local housing authority; if you actually owe service fees, the management company can only urge payment, file a lawsuit, or request arbitration
A

Management companies are not allowed to cut off water, electricity, heating, or gas to force you to pay service fees; if this happens, complain to the local housing authority. If the management company has provided services as agreed, you cannot use the excuse of "not using" them to avoid payment; if you default indefinitely, they can sue. You may refuse to pay unauthorized additional or duplicate fees, and if already paid, they can be reclaimed.
Free. Call or write a complaint letter, taking a few dozen minutes. If the management company does not rectify the issue and you want to claim compensation, you must file a lawsuit in court.

Article 944 of the Civil Code of China has three points. First point, original text: "The management service provider shall not use methods such as stopping the supply of electricity, water, heat, or gas... to demand management service fees." Second point: if the management company has provided services as agreed, the owner shall not use the reason of "not receiving or not needing to receive" services to refuse payment. Third point: if the owner is late in paying, the management company may urge payment within a reasonable period. If payment is still not made after the deadline, the management company may file a lawsuit or request arbitration. The Regulations on Property Management (China) also state: if an owner is late in paying fees, the owners' committee should urge payment within a timeframe. If still unpaid after the deadline, the property management enterprise may file a lawsuit in court. Complaints should be sent to the real estate administrative department of the government at or above the county level (China); regulations require these authorities to handle owner complaints promptly. A judicial interpretation by the Supreme People's Court (China) clarifies: if a management company unilaterally expands the scope of fees, raises fee levels, or charges repeatedly, you can use that as a reason for non-payment. Fees paid contrary to regulations can be reclaimed.

When receiving a new home, inspect it on-site and record defects in the handover report; for leaks or faulty electrical/plumbing systems, contact the developer for repairs within the warranty period specified in the "Residential Quality Guarantee"
A

Upon delivery, the developer must provide you with a "Residential Quality Guarantee." Minimum legal warranty periods for construction units are: 5 years for leaks in bathrooms, roofs, and exterior walls; 2 years for electrical/plumbing systems and finishing work, all starting from the date of completion acceptance. The warranty period the developer gives you must not be shorter than the remaining warranty period of the construction unit. If the developer fails to repair or delays repairs during the warranty period, you can find someone to fix it yourself and have the developer pay.
Free. Takes an extra two to three hours on handover day to inspect every room's walls, floors, doors, and utilities, and take photos. Hiring a professional home inspector costs extra money.

Regulations from the Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development (China) state: when selling commercial housing, the developer must provide the buyer with a "Residential Quality Guarantee" and a "Residential User Manual." The developer is responsible for the quality warranty of the sold house, with the warranty period starting from the date of delivery. The warranty period for commercial housing must not be lower than the remaining period in the quality guarantee provided by the construction unit to the developer. If quality issues within the scope of the warranty occur during the period, the developer must repair them and compensate for resulting damages. The developer is not responsible for damage caused by force majeure or improper use. Minimum warranty periods for construction units are set by State Council (China) regulations, starting from the date of qualified completion acceptance. Roof waterproofing; leak prevention for bathrooms, rooms requiring waterproofing, and exterior wall surfaces: 5 years. Heating and cooling systems: 2 heating/cooling seasons. Electrical wiring, water supply and drainage pipes, equipment installation, and finishing: 2 years. Foundation and main structure: reasonable service life according to design documents. A judicial interpretation by the Supreme People's Court (China) clarifies: the developer is responsible for repairs during the warranty period. "If the seller refuses to repair or delays repairs beyond a reasonable period, the buyer may repair it themselves or hire others. Repair costs and other damages during the repair period shall be borne by the seller." If quality issues seriously affect normal living, you may terminate the contract and demand compensation. If the main structure is verified as unqualified through inspection, the contract can also be terminated with compensation. Inspecting every room, recording defects in the handover report, and taking photos on handover day is the author's experience. Improper use is not covered by the warranty, so defects recorded at delivery make it difficult for the developer to claim you damaged them during renovations.
Take medication exactly as prescribed; do not stop just because you feel better
A

People who take medication exactly as directed by their doctor have a mortality rate during the same period that is about half that of those who take it inconsistently. This figure should be viewed with a discount. Even those who consistently take placebos have lower mortality rates, meaning part of the benefit comes from the fact that "people who are diligent about taking medication are already more health-conscious."
Free, and it saves money on treating future complications. Taking medication only takes a few minutes each day; the difficulty lies in doing it every day without skipping.

A meta-analysis of 21 studies involving 46,847 people: compared to those who took medication intermittently, those who adhered to prescriptions had a roughly 44% lower risk of death during the same period. The base figure is an odds ratio of 0.56, with a 95% confidence interval from 0.50 to 0.63. Considering only treatments that are actually effective, the risk was about 45% lower (0.55; 0.49 to 0.62).

Complete the procedures for chronic or special outpatient disease recognition first, then register for cross-regional medical treatment: hypertension, diabetes, chemotherapy/radiotherapy, dialysis, and anti-rejection drugs will be settled directly elsewhere
A

Hypertension, diabetes, outpatient chemotherapy/radiotherapy for cancer, dialysis for end-stage renal disease, and anti-rejection drugs after organ transplantation: these five conditions can almost always be settled directly via medical insurance when visiting outpatient clinics in other provinces. You do not have to pay out-of-pocket first and then return to your insurance location for reimbursement. However, you must first complete the chronic or special outpatient disease recognition procedures at your insurance location, then register for cross-regional treatment. Both steps must be completed for this to work.
Free. Before leaving, complete the cross-regional medical treatment registration once on the medical insurance app (China); it can be done right on your phone.

A document from the National Healthcare Security Administration (China) states that this stage has been reached. The original text says "basically achieved direct inter-provincial settlement for the costs of 5 chronic and special outpatient diseases including hypertension, diabetes, outpatient chemotherapy/radiotherapy for cancer, dialysis for end-stage renal disease, and anti-rejection treatment after organ transplantation, accessible at the county level." "Accessible at the county level" means it can be done once you reach the county level. The document also added 5 more diseases beyond these five.
Follow up at the exact intervals scheduled by your doctor, and record your readings in the same notebook each time
B

Chronic diseases require monitoring how indicators change over time, not just a single measurement. Simply measuring blood pressure at home does not show that blood pressure decreases as a result. Bringing measurements to a doctor so they can adjust medication based on them leads to a greater reduction in blood pressure. When changing hospitals, if test results are printed with mutual recognition marks, the hospital generally cannot force you to repeat them.
Each test costs several dozen to several hundred yuan. A hospital visit plus waiting for results takes some time. The difficulty is having to go at regular intervals, which is easy to procrastinate.

Chronic diseases require seeing how indicators change over time; a single look is insufficient. For hypertension, a meta-analysis of individual patient data from 7,138 people in 15 randomized trials showed that compared to those receiving usual care, those who self-monitored blood pressure at home had a mean change in clinic systolic blood pressure of −3.2 mmHg after 12 months (95% CI −4.9 to −1.6). Self-monitoring alone, without other measures, showed no effect: −1.0 mmHg (−3.3 to 1.2, difference could be due to chance). The group with the most additional support saw a reduction of 6.1 mmHg (3.2 to 9.0). Additional support means doctors, pharmacists, or the patients themselves adjusting medication based on readings, combined with health education and lifestyle guidance. The authors concluded: self-monitoring alone does not lower blood pressure; it must be accompanied by medication adjustment based on readings to be effective. These figures all refer to blood pressure, not directly to mortality. When changing hospitals, regulations from the National Health Commission (China) and three other agencies specify: if the laboratory and imaging results brought by the patient meet mutual recognition conditions and diagnostic needs, hospitals and doctors must not repeat them. Mutually recognized result sheets are printed with an "HR" mark, such as "全国 HR (National HR)".
Do not abandon conventional treatment to try folk remedies or dietary supplements
B

For treatable cancers, those who use only alternative therapies and no conventional treatment have a 2.5 times higher risk of death than those receiving conventional treatment. People who use complementary therapies while undergoing treatment are more likely to refuse surgery, chemotherapy, or radiotherapy; the excess mortality lies here. Some herbs even reduce the effectiveness of anti-rejection or anticoagulant drugs; consult your treating physician before use.
Free, and it saves money on supplements. No time lost. The difficulty is standing firm when others repeatedly advise you to try them.

Two studies using US cancer registry data examined patients with non-metastatic breast, prostate, lung, and colorectal cancers, which are treatable. The first study looked at those who used only alternative therapies and none of surgery, radiotherapy, chemotherapy, or hormone therapy. Compared to matched patients receiving conventional treatment, their risk of death was 2.5 times higher (HR 2.50, 95% CI 1.88 to 3.27, about 1.5 times higher). Breast cancer was 5.68 times higher (3.22 to 10.04), lung cancer 2.17 times (1.42 to 3.32), and colorectal cancer 4.57 times (1.66 to 12.61). The second study looked at those using both conventional and complementary therapies. Their refusal rate for surgery was 7.0% vs 0.1%, for chemotherapy 34.1% vs 3.2%, for radiotherapy 53.0% vs 2.3%, and for hormone therapy 33.7% vs 2.8%. The 5-year survival rate was 82.2% vs 86.6%, with a 2.08 times higher risk of death (HR 2.08, 1.50 to 2.90, an increase of about 108%). When delays and refusals of treatment were accounted for, complementary therapy itself was no longer associated with mortality (HR 1.39, 0.83 to 2.33). The authors concluded that the excess mortality comes from refusing conventional treatment. The State Administration for Market Regulation (China) requires health food labels to state: "Health food is not medicine and cannot replace medicine to treat diseases." The US National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health (NCCIH) states that St. John's wort reduces the effectiveness of many drugs, including the anti-rejection drug cyclosporine and the anticoagulant warfarin.
If a chronic disease is stable, you can obtain up to 12 weeks of medication at once from a community-level hospital
A

Patients with stable conditions whose medications are not changing can receive a prescription for up to 12 weeks of medication at a time from a community health service center. This saves half a day each month spent traveling to and queuing at large hospitals for registration. Within the same insurance area, hospitalization at primary-level medical institutions is, in principle, reimbursed at a rate about ten percentage points higher than at higher-level hospitals.
Free. Just ask at a community health service center (China) if they can issue long-term prescriptions; one question is all it takes.

Eliminates the need to travel to large hospitals and queue for medication every month. Within the same insurance area (also known as a fund coordination area), hospitalization at primary-level medical institutions is, in principle, reimbursed at a rate about 10 percentage points higher than at higher-level hospitals.
Before signing a contract with a community family doctor, ask clearly which parts are covered by medical insurance and which are out-of-pocket
A

Basic service packages are covered by medical insurance (China) according to regulations when the contract is signed. Personalized service packages are paid entirely by you. When offered an "upgraded package," ask beforehand: is this a basic or personalized package, has it been registered with the health authorities, and how much does it cost per year.
Free. Asking one extra question before signing takes one minute.

Basic service packages are covered by medical insurance according to regulations. Personalized service packages are paid entirely by you; this type of package must also be registered with the county-level health authority.
Get a fundus examination immediately upon diagnosis of diabetes, then follow the doctor's scheduled intervals; have a foot examination once a year
A

Diabetes damages the fundus and the feet, but there are almost no symptoms until vision is lost or foot ulcers appear. Early detection allows for treatable outcomes. For type 2 diabetes, a dilated fundus exam should be performed at the time of diagnosis; for type 1, exams begin 5 years after onset. If one or two exams show no issues and blood sugar targets are met, the interval can be extended to every one or two years. Feet should be examined once a year.

A fundus examination with dilating eye drops costs from several dozen to several hundred yuan. Foot examinations are usually part of an outpatient visit and incur no extra cost. The difficulty lies in remembering to go for check-ups even when eyes and feet feel fine.

Diabetes damaging the fundus is called retinopathy; damaging the feet is called diabetic foot. These two conditions have almost no symptoms before serious problems occur. Early detection is still treatable. Waiting until vision is lost or feet are ulcerated is too late.
If you have had kidney stones, drink 2.5–3 liters of water daily and reduce salt intake to no more than 6 grams
A

For those with first-time calcium stones of unknown cause, about one-quarter will recur within five years if no action is taken. For those who drink enough water daily, the recurrence rate is just over one-tenth in five years, a reduction of more than half. UK guidelines recommend drinking 2.5 to 3 liters of water daily and limiting salt to no more than 6 grams.
Costs nothing. Turn regular water consumption into a habit. Drink more on days when you sweat a lot; the difficulty is remembering to do it every day.

A 5-year randomized controlled trial involved 199 patients with first-time idiopathic calcium stones. One group drank at least 2 liters of water daily, while the other had no intervention. Over 5 years, the high-water group had 12/99 recurrences (12.1%), and the no-intervention group had 27/100 (27.0%), P = 0.008. Smaller P-values indicate differences are less likely due to chance. Average time to recurrence: 38.7 ± 13.2 months vs. 25.1 ± 16.4 months, P = 0.016. Baseline 24-hour urine volume was significantly lower in stone-formers: males 1,057 ± 238 mL vs. 1,401 ± 562 mL (P < 0.0001), females 990 ± 230 mL vs. 1,239 ± 440 mL (P < 0.001). NICE guideline NG118, section 1.8.1, recommends adults drink 2.5 to 3 liters of water daily, and children/adolescents drink 1 to 2 liters depending on age. Add a bit of fresh lemon juice to water, avoid carbonated drinks, and adults should limit salt to 6 grams daily. Section 1.7.1 of the same guideline recommends adults with a history of kidney or ureteral stones consider a one-time stone composition analysis. For recurrent cases where stones are more than half calcium oxalate, section 1.8.3 suggests considering potassium citrate. Regarding 24-hour urine testing, NICE found insufficient evidence to make a recommendation. The European Association of Urology (EAU) guidelines differ: every stone-former should have a reliable stone analysis. Recurrent patients are high-risk and should undergo two consecutive 24-hour urine collections for specific metabolic testing. The general prevention goal in this guideline is 2.5 to 3 liters of fluid intake daily, with a daily urine output of 2 to 2.5 liters.

If diagnosed with gout and you have tophi, X-rays show bone erosion, or you have 2 or more flares per year, take long-term uric acid-lowering medication to keep blood uric acid below 360 µmol/L permanently
A

If you have tophi, bone erosion, or 2+ flares per year, you must take long-term uric acid-lowering medication to keep uric acid below 360 µmol/L. For fewer flares, discuss medication with a doctor. When nurses adjust dosages based on test results, 95% of patients reach the target after two years, compared to only 30% with standard care. Once the target is reached, do not stop medication; dietary restrictions have limited impact on lowering levels.

Allopurinol costs several to several dozen yuan per month. Initially, test blood uric acid every few weeks to adjust the dose; once stable, every few months. For the first 3 to 6 months, an additional medication is needed to prevent flares. The difficulty is continuing to take it regularly even when there is no pain.

A randomized controlled trial involved 517 adults who had gout flares in the previous 12 months. One group was nurse-led, receiving education and dose adjustments until uric acid targets were met. The other group received standard GP care. After 2 years, the proportion with blood uric acid below 360 µmol/L (6 mg/dL) was 95% vs. 30%. The likelihood of reaching the target was 3.18 times higher (RR 3.18, 95% CI 2.42 to 4.18), P < 0.0001. Secondary outcomes in year 2, such as flare frequency, tophi, and quality of life, were all better than the standard group. Each Quality-Adjusted Life Year (QALY) gained cost £5,066. A follow-up study using questionnaires (82% response from 438 people) showed the target group had a median of 0 flares in the past 12 months (IQR 0–0), while the standard group had 1 (0–3), P < 0.001. The target group was 1.19 times more likely to still be taking medication (adjusted RR 1.19; 1.09 to 1.30). The 2020 American College of Rheumatology (ACR) guideline strongly recommends starting urate-lowering therapy (ULT) for three groups: those with subcutaneous tophi, radiographic gouty erosions, or 2+ flares per year. For those with >1 flare but <2 per year, ULT is conditionally recommended (doctor-patient shared decision). For first-time flares, ULT is conditionally recommended against, except for patients with stage 3+ CKD, uric acid > 9 mg/dL, or urolithiasis, where it is conditionally recommended. The strategy is treat-to-target, aiming for < 6 mg/dL. Allopurinol is the preferred first-line agent, including for stage 3+ CKD, starting at ≤ 100 mg/day. Concomitant anti-inflammatory prophylaxis is used for at least 3 to 6 months. The guideline cites an observational study where only 13% (27/211) of patients who stopped ULT after long-term control remained flare-free over 5 years. Regarding diet, limiting alcohol lowers uric acid by 1.6 mg/dL; one beer increases it by 0.16 mg/dL. Healthy diets (Mediterranean, DASH) have smaller effects. There is disagreement on the preferred drug. ACR strongly recommends allopurinol as first choice due to efficacy, tolerability, safety, and cost. It conditionally recommends switching from febuxostat in patients with cardiovascular disease history or new events if alternatives exist, matching the FDA's boxed warning. This was based on the CARES trial (6,190 patients), where febuxostat had a 1.22 times higher risk of all-cause mortality (HR 1.22, 95% CI 1.01 to 1.47) and 1.34 times higher cardiovascular mortality (1.03 to 1.73) than allopurinol. However, the European FAST trial (6,128 patients over 60) concluded febuxostat was not associated with more major cardiovascular events than allopurinol (HR 0.85; 0.70 to 1.03). For uricosuric agents, ACR conditionally recommends against urine alkalinization due to lack of evidence. It does require advising these patients to drink plenty of water. Uricosurics should be avoided in those with kidney stones or stage 3+ CKD. The HLA-B*5801 allele is most common in Han Chinese, Korean, and Thai populations (7.4%), African Americans (3.8%), and Whites/Hispanics (0.7%). Asians and African Americans have a 3-fold higher risk of allopurinol hypersensitivity syndrome; testing for HLA-B*5801 is conditionally recommended for these groups (very low certainty evidence).
If you have a history of gout, avoid eating excessive amounts of meat and seafood at barbecues or parties, and limit alcohol consumption
B

For people with a history of gout, those with the highest purine intake in the preceding two days are nearly 5 times more likely to have a flare than those with the lowest intake, even if taking uric acid-lowering medication. Drinking two to four glasses of alcohol the day before increases the flare risk by about half; this includes beer, spirits, and wine.
Costs nothing. Order fewer meat and seafood skewers and drink less alcohol at gatherings. The difficulty is self-control at the dining table.

An online follow-up study of 633 gout patients over 1 year compared the two days before a flare with two non-flare days for the same individual (case-crossover study). Purines from food turn into uric acid. Total purine intake was divided into five levels; compared to the lowest level, the subsequent four levels had flare odds ratios of 1.17, 1.38, 2.21, and 4.76 (P for trend < 0.001). For animal purines alone, the ratios were 1.42, 1.34, 1.77, and 2.41. For plant purines, they were 1.12, 0.99, 1.32, and 1.39. Results were consistent across gender, alcohol use, and medication use (diuretics, allopurinol, NSAIDs, colchicine). Another study by the same authors looked at alcohol intake in 724 gout patients 24 hours before a flare. Compared to no alcohol, >1 to 2 drinks increased risk by 1.36 times (95% CI 1.00 to 1.88), and >2 to 4 drinks by 1.51 times (1.09 to 2.09). Wine, beer, and spirits were all associated with flares. For those never diagnosed with gout, a 12-year follow-up of 47,150 US men showed that the highest quintile of meat intake had a 41% higher risk of gout (RR 1.41; 1.07 to 1.86) than the lowest. Seafood intake increased risk by 51% (1.51; 1.17 to 1.95). Conversely, the highest dairy intake quintile had a 44% lower risk (0.56; 0.42 to 0.74). High-purine vegetables and total protein showed no association. In the same group, one 12-ounce (approx. 355 mL) beer daily increased risk by 49% (1.49; 1.32 to 1.70). One daily serving of spirits increased risk by 15% (1.15; 1.04 to 1.28). Wine showed no statistically significant difference (1.04; 0.88 to 1.22).
If you test positive for HBsAg, get a liver ultrasound and AFP test every six months; consult a doctor regarding antiviral medication and do not stop taking it on your own
A

For Hepatitis B carriers, semi-annual ultrasound and AFP testing reduced liver cancer deaths by nearly 40% in a Shanghai trial. Higher viral loads correlate with higher future liver cancer risk. For those with severe fibrosis or cirrhosis, antiviral medication reduces liver cancer risk by about half. Most medications require long-term use; stopping on your own can cause the virus to rebound.

Visit a hepatology or infectious disease department every six months for blood work and ultrasound; costs vary by location. For those needing medication: China's National Healthcare Security Administration stated that after centralized procurement, the annual cost of entecavir has dropped to just over ⟦100⟧. The difficulty is attending regular check-ups and taking medication indefinitely even when feeling fine.

A randomized trial in Shanghai with 18,816 people (ages 35–59) with HBV or chronic hepatitis history showed that the group screened every 6 months with AFP and ultrasound had 32 liver cancer deaths, compared to 54 in the control group. The mortality rate was 83.2 vs. 131.5 per 100,000. The screening group's risk was 0.63 times the control (95% CI 0.41 to 0.98), about 37% lower. 46.5% of liver cancers in the screening group were surgically resectable, vs. 7.5% in the control. A Taiwan follow-up study of 3,653 HBsAg-positive individuals (ages 30–65, mean follow-up 11.4 years) found that higher baseline viral load predicted higher cancer risk. At <300 copies/mL, the rate was 108 cases per 100,000 person-years; at ≥1 million copies/mL, it was 1,152 cases. Cumulative incidence was 1.3% vs. 14.9%. This trend held after adjusting for sex, age, smoking, alcohol, liver enzymes, and cirrhosis. An Asian randomized trial of 651 chronic HBV patients with severe fibrosis or cirrhosis showed that lamivudine (median 32.4 months) reduced liver cancer incidence to 3.9% vs. 7.4% for placebo (HR 0.49; P = 0.047). Disease progression was 7.8% vs. 17.7% (HR 0.45, ~55% lower). The 2022 Chinese Medical Association guidelines specify that chronic HBV patients should have abdominal ultrasound and AFP every 6 months for cancer screening. High-risk individuals should be screened every 3 to 6 months. Carriers not yet needing medication should have blood counts, liver function, viral markers, AFP, and ultrasound every 6 to 12 months. Once criteria are met, treatment should start immediately. Antiviral therapy is recommended for those with detectable virus over age 30, regardless of liver enzyme levels, or those with a family history of HBV-related cirrhosis or liver cancer. Recommended drugs are entecavir or tenofovir. The guidelines state most patients require long-term therapy, as relapse rates after stopping are high.
If diagnosed with COPD, have a doctor or pharmacist check your inhaler technique at every follow-up; if hospitalized for an exacerbation, attend pulmonary rehabilitation after discharge
A

Only about 30% of inhaler users use them perfectly; errors can prevent medication from reaching the lungs. Patients making critical errors are about twice as likely to be hospitalized or visit the ER for exacerbations. Pulmonary rehabilitation after hospitalization for an exacerbation reduces the risk of re-hospitalization by more than half and improves quality of life and walking distance. Impact on mortality is not yet clear.

Checking inhaler technique costs nothing extra: bring your medication to follow-ups and demonstrate its use, which takes a few minutes. Pulmonary rehabilitation involves supervised exercise, education on medication, and self-management; it requires multiple sessions, and costs vary. The difficulty is attending sessions regularly while still feeling weak after discharge.

A national survey in China measuring respiratory function in 50,991 adults (20+) found a COPD prevalence of 8.6% (95% CI 7.5 to 9.9), roughly 99.9 million people. For those 40+, it was 13.7%. Only 12.0% of patients had previously undergone spirometry. A meta-analysis of 144 studies (54,354 patients) observed inhaler use: 31% were correct, 41% acceptable, and 31% poor. No improvement was seen over 40 years. For metered-dose inhalers (press-and-spray), 45% failed to coordinate pressing with inhalation. 44% failed to inhale fast or deep enough, and 46% failed to hold their breath. A French observational study of 2,935 COPD patients found errors in over half of inhaler uses. Critical errors preventing drug delivery ranged from 15.4% to 46.9% depending on the device. Hospitalization or ER visits in the past 3 months occurred in 3.3% of those without errors vs. 6.9% of those with critical errors (OR 1.86, 1.14 to 3.04). The GOLD 2023 report emphasizes teaching both doctors and patients correct inhaler use and re-checking at every visit. It also recommends flu and pneumococcal vaccinations. A 2016 Cochrane review of 20 RCTs (1,477 people) compared pulmonary rehab after an exacerbation to standard care. 8 studies (810 people) showed the rehab group had a 56% lower risk of re-hospitalization (OR 0.44, 95% CI 0.21 to 0.91), with moderate quality evidence, though results varied. 6 studies (670 people) showed a mortality OR of 0.68 (0.28 to 1.67), which could be due to chance (low quality evidence). Quality of life improved significantly (high quality evidence). The 6-minute walk distance increased by an average of 62 meters (38 to 86 meters), with high quality evidence.
If you have diabetes, test your urine albumin/creatinine ratio and blood creatinine once a year; those with hypertension should also be tested to detect chronic kidney disease early
B

In China, only one-tenth of adults with chronic kidney disease (CKD) are aware of their condition. Annual urine and blood tests for diabetics allow for earlier detection. For those found to have high proteinuria, using drugs like dapagliflozin can reduce the composite risk of declining kidney function, progression to dialysis, or death by about 40%, and reduce mortality by about 30%.

Requires a one-time urine sample for albumin/creatinine ratio and a blood sample for creatinine; these can be ordered during a follow-up visit. The difficulty is remembering to get tested when the kidneys do not yet feel uncomfortable.

China's 2018–2019 national chronic disease surveillance tested 176,874 adults. CKD prevalence was ~8.2% (~82 million people). 73.3% were in early stages (1–2). Only 10.0% were aware of their condition. Another survey of 9,672 type 2 diabetics in 45 Chinese hospitals found 31% had CKD; of these, only 27% had been previously screened. KDIGO 2024 guidelines state high-risk individuals need simultaneous testing of albuminuria and GFR. Priority groups are those with hypertension, diabetes, and cardiovascular disease. 2026 ADA standards state type 2 diabetics, regardless of treatment, must have annual urine albumin/creatinine ratio and eGFR tests. Type 1 diabetics with a 5-year history should do the same. For diabetes with hypertension and moderate albuminuria (30–299 mg/g), ACE inhibitors ("-pril") or ARBs ("-sartan") are recommended. Once detected, effective treatments exist. A randomized controlled trial of 4,304 CKD patients (GFR 25–75, albumin/creatinine ratio 200–5000) found that over a median of 2.4 years, 9.2% of the dapagliflozin group experienced a primary event (50%+ GFR decline, end-stage kidney disease, or renal/CV death) vs. 14.5% in the placebo group. HR 0.61 (95% CI 0.51 to 0.72), ~39% lower. Mortality was 4.7% vs. 6.8%, HR 0.69 (0.53 to 0.88), ~31% lower. Efficacy was similar regardless of diabetes status.
After surgery and chemotherapy for colon cancer, participate in a supervised exercise program and persist for three years
A

After colon cancer surgery and chemotherapy, those who participate in a three-year supervised exercise program have a 28% lower risk of recurrence, new cancer, or death, and a 37% lower risk of death. After 8 years, the survival rate was about 90% for the exercise group vs. 83% for those receiving only educational materials. Exercisers experienced slightly more muscle and joint injuries.

Walking and similar activities are free. Visiting a rehabilitation department or exercise prescription clinic for fitness assessment and programming involves consultation and testing fees; hiring a private trainer adds cost. It requires several hours of exercise per week and three years of persistence. Exercisers have a slightly higher risk of muscle and joint injuries.

The CHALLENGE randomized controlled trial at 55 centers involved 889 colon cancer patients (high-risk stage II or stage III) who had completed surgery and adjuvant chemotherapy without metastasis. They entered the study 2–6 months post-chemo, having previously exercised <150 minutes/week. 445 joined a 3-year exercise program, and 444 received only health education. For the first 6 months, the exercise group met a consultant bi-weekly for sessions and one supervised workout. From months 6–12, meetings were in-person or by phone, tapering to minimal support by year 3. The goal was to increase physical activity by 10 MET-hours/week (moderate intensity or higher); most chose walking. After one year, leisure activity in the exercise group increased by 15.6 MET-hours/week vs. 5.1 in the control. Median follow-up was 7.9 years. Recurrence, new cancer, or death was 28% lower in the exercise group, HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.55 to 0.94). At 5 years, disease-free survival was 80.3% vs. 73.9%. Mortality was 37% lower, HR 0.63 (0.43 to 0.94). 8-year survival: 90.3% vs. 83.2%. Musculoskeletal side effects: 18.5% vs. 11.5%. A cost analysis within the Canadian public health system showed the program cost $2,917 CAD per person upfront, but due to fewer recurrences, total 5-year costs decreased by $1,589 CAD per person.
While an elderly person is still of sound mind, designate a guardian in writing for the future
A

While an elderly person is still mentally clear, spend a few hundred yuan at a notary office to create a document specifying who will be their guardian. Without this, if they become unable to make decisions, the law follows a set order: spouse first, then parents and children, then other close relatives. If family members dispute this, the neighborhood committee, village committee, civil affairs department, or court will appoint one.

Creating a document at a notary office costs a few hundred yuan. It can be settled in one conversation. The hardest part is starting the conversation: you must speak directly about the day they can no longer care for themselves.

The Civil Code of the People's Republic of China (民法典) stipulates that an adult of sound mind (legally an "adult with full capacity for civil conduct") can consult with others in advance to choose their future guardian. The chosen person can be a relative, or another individual or organization willing to serve. This must be "determined in writing." When the person later loses all or part of their capacity for civil conduct, the designated person takes charge. Without this document, guardianship follows the order in Article 28: spouse; parents/children; other close relatives; then other willing individuals/organizations approved by the neighborhood/village committee or civil affairs department. Article 31 states that disputes over guardianship are settled by the neighborhood/village committee or civil affairs department; if dissatisfied, one can petition the court for appointment, or apply directly to the court.
Make a will, and remember that a later version replaces an earlier one; notarized wills are no longer automatically prioritized
A

Chinese law recognizes six types of wills, each with mandatory procedures. A holographic (handwritten) will must be written entirely by hand, signed, and dated by the testator. If multiple wills exist with conflicting content, the last one created prevails. Since 2021, a notarized will is no longer automatically given priority over others.

Writing a holographic will by hand costs nothing. Going to a notary office costs from several hundred to over ⟦1000⟧. The hardest part is starting the conversation: discussing what happens after you pass away with your family.

The Civil Code of the People's Republic of China (民法典) recognizes six forms of wills: holographic (handwritten), made on behalf of the testator, printed, audio-visual, oral, and notarized. Each has specific mandatory procedures ("formal requirements"). For holographic wills, Article 1134 requires they be "handwritten and signed by the testator, with the year, month, and day specified." If multiple wills conflict, the last one is the standard. Since 2021, notarized wills no longer have automatic priority.
Keep the elderly's money in a separate account; set a rule requiring two people to confirm large expenses
B

Scammers targeting the elderly often give small gifts and show kind concern first to build trust before stealing large sums. Scammers also frequently instruct victims to "not tell anyone." Agree on a rule in advance: any expenditure over a certain amount must be discussed with a specific person first. This way, family members know before the money leaves the pocket, and the decision to spend is delayed slightly.
Free. Discuss it with family once and fix a number. The hardest part is starting the conversation so the elderly person doesn't feel you are being suspicious of them.

In 2022, the Supreme People's Procuratorate (China) released typical cases of elderly fraud. The office stated that these criminals use small favors and family-like concern to gain trust first, then use false advertising and promises of high returns to steal large assets. In one case, a company selling fake collectibles sent employees to clean houses, chat with the elderly, and even act as "adopted children." When selling goods, they put items in sealed black bags and told the elderly not to open them so family members wouldn't find out. This company collected over ⟦1920000⟧; the owner was sentenced to 7 years and 6 months in prison for fraudulent fund-raising. In 2023, the Beijing Local Financial Supervision and Administration Bureau (China) reminded the elderly not to believe a scammer's "don't tell anyone." When in doubt, discuss more with family, children, and trusted neighbors or friends; consult family more before investing. The US Federal Trade Commission statistics show the total fraud losses reported by people aged 60 and older. In 2020 it was about 600 million US dollars, and by 2024 it increased to about 2.4 billion US dollars. The increase was mainly in cases where more than 100,000 US dollars were lost at a time. Agreeing in advance that "expenditures over a certain amount must be told to someone first" ensures family knows before the money is gone and delays the decision.
Prepare a refusal phrase for the elderly that can be said at any time: "Let me go home and discuss it with my family first"
B

Sales pitches and scams rely on on-the-spot pressure, wanting you to pay before you have time to think. People whose emotions have been stirred are more likely to buy items in exaggerated advertisements, and the elderly are more prone to this than young people. Agree on a phrase with the elderly: "Let me go home and discuss it with my family first." They can say it at any time to have an immediate exit strategy, then decide after calming down at home.
Free. Practice once with the elderly; it takes a few minutes.

Both sales pitches and scams rely on creating on-the-spot pressure. The US Federal Trade Commission's fraud prevention guide states: scammers want you to act before you have time to think. When calling, they tell you not to hang up so you cannot verify the information. The suggested method is: before doing anything, tell one person—a friend, family member, or neighbor; speaking out may help you realize it's a scam. A 2021 risk warning from the former China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission also advised the elderly to discuss more with family before buying investment products. An experiment involved 116 elderly people aged 65 to 85 and 115 people aged 30 to 40. Researchers used a win-loss game to stir the emotions of some participants, then showed them exaggerated, false advertisements. Those whose emotions were stirred were indeed more likely to want to buy the advertised items. Regardless of emotional state, the elderly were more likely to want to buy than younger people. The authors recommend waiting for emotions to subside before deciding to spend money. Another experiment involved people who had previously been scammed by mail, most of whom were elderly. Among those not warned in advance, nearly half agreed immediately when receiving a simulated scam sales call. For those called and warned two to four weeks prior, the number who agreed immediately decreased significantly. Agreeing on the phrase "Let me go home and discuss it with my family first" gives the elderly an exit strategy so they don't have to decide on the spot.

Avoid any "retirement investment" that requires the elderly to pay upfront: membership cards, bed space purchases, retirement apartments, retirement tourism, or buying products for the elderly are all the same illegal fund-raising scheme
A

Retirement schemes that require upfront payment and promise interest are all the same scam. Common ones include making cards, buying bed spaces, retirement apartments, retirement tourism, or holding seminars to sell products to the elderly. According to regulations (China), losses of this type must be borne by the individual. One perpetrator used the guise of pre-ordering retirement apartment bed spaces to collect ⟦136000000⟧, defrauding over 2,100 people.

Free. Read the types of schemes below to the elderly once; it takes a few minutes. If encountered later, refuse directly: don't attend lectures, don't go on tours, don't leave a phone number. The hardest part is when the elderly have already gone a few times and become close to the people, making it hard to persuade them to stop.

The Ministry of Civil Affairs (China) lists five forms of these schemes; recognizing the scheme is more reliable than recognizing the person. Form one, using the name of a retirement facility: no real facility exists, they rent a temporary place and claim to have signed cooperation agreements with retirement facilities to "piggyback" on them. Form two, under the guise of "providing retirement services": selling "VIP cards," "membership cards," or "prepaid cards," requiring upfront payment of "retirement service fees." The promised services clearly exceed the number of beds available. Form three, under the guise of investing in "retirement projects." Common schemes include investing in health and retirement zones or selling non-existent retirement apartments. There is also long-term leasing of retirement beds or mutual-aid retirement like "time banks." The tactic is to sell with a promise of capital return, lease-back after sale, or promised buy-back. Form four, under the guise of selling "products for the elderly": buying back goods, consignment sales, cashback on purchases, free health check-ups, gifts, sales seminars, health talks, or free expert consultations. Form five, under the guise of "retirement tourism": cheap or free travel, interest returns on deposits, or retirement points. Money cannot be recovered; the terms are clearly stated. Article 25 of the Regulations on the Prevention and Handling of Illegal Fund-raising (China) stipulates that "losses caused by participating in illegal fund-raising shall be borne by the participants themselves"; lost money can only be accepted as a loss. In cases announced by authorities, Dai Mouping's group used the guise of pre-ordering retirement apartment bed spaces to illegally raise ⟦136000000⟧ from over 2,100 victims. Dai Mouping was sentenced to 15 years for fraudulent fund-raising and fined ⟦400000⟧. Cao Mouming used the guise of investing in the retirement industry to fraudulently raise ⟦13207000000⟧, involving over 110,000 people. Cao Mouming was sentenced to life imprisonment, deprived of political rights for life, and had all personal property confiscated. Seminars selling functional foods fall under fraud. Ni Mourong used free banquets, gifts, and private shuttle buses to lure the elderly to lectures. The lecturer used "fake characters, fake cases, and fake bargaining with inflated prices" to fabricate anti-cancer effects. The elderly were lured into buying "dihydroquercetin" at dozens of times the cost price. Sales totaled over ⟦620000⟧. Ni Mourong was sentenced to 10 years and 3 months and fined ⟦120000⟧ (Nationwide China, regulations applicable from May 1, 2021).
