Except for reverse mortgage retirement insurance from insurance companies, avoid all other types of "mortgaging your home for retirement"; never mortgage your home to buy investment products
B

There is only one legitimate type of mortgaging a home for retirement: reverse mortgage retirement insurance from an insurance company, and it is still in a pilot phase (China). The "mortgaging home for retirement" mentioned by scammers has nothing to do with it; they lure the elderly into mortgaging their home and then using the loan to buy investment products they recommend. Some people don't even know their home has been mortgaged until they lose it and are left with debt.

Free. Do not give the house deed to anyone who comes to the door in the name of "mortgaging the home for retirement." Before signing mortgages, guarantees, or loans, have children review the contracts. The hardest part is that those who come to the door are often very enthusiastic and visit many times, making the elderly reluctant to refuse.

The Consumer Rights Protection Bureau of the (former) China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission has clarified the truth. There is only one legitimate type of home mortgage for retirement, called "reverse mortgage retirement insurance for the elderly." The elderly person with full, legal ownership mortgages the house to an insurance company. They still live in, use, and can rent out the house. Selling or disposing of it requires the mortgagee's (insurance company's) consent. The elderly receive a retirement pension according to agreed terms until death. This business is currently in the pilot stage with few participants. The "mortgaging home for retirement" mentioned by criminals is "completely unrelated" to the state-piloted reverse mortgage insurance; it is a "tactic using state policy to create momentum and promote illegal fund-raising." Their method is to lure the elderly into mortgaging the house and using the loan to buy recommended investment products, "often a Ponzi scheme using new investors' money to pay old ones." The consequence, verbatim: "some participants did not even know their house was mortgaged, eventually losing the house and carrying the loan." This warning also sets a threshold for interest rates. Verbatim: "if an investment product promises an interest rate over 6%, it must be questioned; over 8% is very dangerous; 10% or more means preparing to lose all principal; 'guaranteed principal with high returns' is financial fraud." The same warning requires "caution during the contract signing stage; do not sign blank contracts" (Nationwide China, June 2021).

If an elderly family member is bedridden for a long time or has severe loss of self-care ability, apply for long-term care insurance at the medical insurance agency where they are insured; it is not only for the elderly
A

Long-term care insurance (China) pays for care services and usually does not provide direct cash. If a household member has a severe loss of self-care ability lasting half a year or more, apply at their medical insurance agency. There is no deductible for care costs; those insured as employees are covered for about 70%, and urban/rural residents for about 50%; bed and food costs are not covered. The documents do not set an age limit; young people with severe loss of self-care ability can also apply.
Apply at the medical insurance agency once. Then undergo a self-care ability assessment once. If the initial assessment qualifies, the assessment fee is paid by the fund, not out of pocket.

Regulated long-term care service costs do not have a deductible. A deductible means having to pay a certain amount yourself before coverage begins; that is not the case here. For those participating under employer policies, the fund pays about 70%. For unemployed urban and rural residents, it is about 50%. The maximum annual payout (annual maximum benefit) does not exceed 50% of the previous year's average per capita disposable income for urban and rural residents in the fund's jurisdiction. Eligible recipients are those who have paid insurance premiums according to regulations, whose loss of self-care ability has typically lasted 6 months or more, and who have applied and been assessed; the initial phase prioritizes those with severe loss of self-care. The documents do not set an age limit; unemployed persons under 18 participating through parents are eligible under urban/rural resident rates if they meet the criteria. The fund primarily pays care facilities and caregivers; in principle, it does not provide direct cash to the person with loss of self-care. Facility bed fees, food, and non-care-related items are not paid by the fund.
For long-term bedridden family members, treat pressure ulcers as enemy number one: use electric air mattresses, turn them on a schedule, and check bony protrusions every day
B

Elderly patients with hip fractures (proximal femur) who have pressure ulcers before surgery have a 30-day mortality rate about two-tenths higher. Switching to an electric air mattress reduces the number of new ulcers by about six-tenths. In the ICU, using sensor reminders for scheduled turning reduces ulcers by about seven-tenths; however, prone positioning significantly increases pressure ulcers. Check the sacrum, heels, hips, and shoulder blades daily; if you see redness that doesn't blanch when pressed, report it to a nurse or doctor that day.

Alternating pressure electric air mattresses for home use start from a few hundred yuan. Turning someone once takes only a few minutes. The difficulty is turning every two to three hours, including at night; one person cannot handle this alone.

19,520 patients underwent hip fracture surgery (US NSQIP, 2016 to 2019). Those with pre-existing pressure ulcers had a higher 30-day mortality rate. Even after adjusting for other factors, this association remained (OR = 1.2, 21% increase, P = 0.004). These patients were also more likely to experience other issues: deep vein thrombosis (OR = 1.59), pneumonia (OR = 1.39), and unplanned readmission (OR = 1.43). The average hospital stay was also 0.4 days longer. 324 hospitalized elderly patients (average age 86) were followed for a median of 18 months. Pressure ulcers independently predicted long-term mortality (HR = 1.500, 95% CI 1.059 to 2.126, P = 0.020). Independent prediction means it still predicted mortality after excluding other factors. 65 randomized trials were pooled (network meta-analysis). Comparing active electric air surfaces with standard hospital mattresses (standard hospital bed support surfaces). Active electric air surfaces are electric air mattresses. Users had a lower rate of pressure ulcers (RR = 0.42, 95% CI 0.29 to 0.63, moderate certainty). Hybrid electric air surfaces had an RR = 0.22 (0.07 to 0.66). A Cochrane review included 11 trials with 4,462 people (updated 2024). Turning every 2 hours compared to every 4 hours showed no clear difference (RR = 1.05, 95% CI 0.79 to 1.39, very low certainty). Comparisons between other turning intervals were also very uncertain. In a trial of 1,226 ICU patients, using wearable sensors for real-time reminders with visual alerts ensured 2-hour turning was actually performed. The pressure ulcer rate was lower than standard care (RR = 0.28, 95% CI 0.10 to 0.75, moderate certainty). In a trial of 116 people, the prone group had a higher pressure ulcer rate than the supine group (RR = 4.55, 95% CI 2.31 to 8.98).
If an elderly person's cataracts affect their ability to see the road, have an eye exam to evaluate surgery; if both eyes are affected, don't wait too long for the second eye
B

Women aged 70 and older who had early surgery on their first cataract eye had about 34% fewer falls in a year, and fewer fractures. However, the number of people who fell at least once did not decrease. Whether to operate on the second eye has not shown a clear difference regarding falls. Elderly people who had surgery had about a 16% lower rate of hip fractures (proximal femur) within one year.

First, take the elderly person for an eye exam to let the doctor decide if surgery is needed. Each eye is operated on once; many hospitals perform it as day surgery, allowing the patient to go home immediately. If both eyes are cloudy, two surgeries are required. Out-of-pocket costs depend on the type of intraocular lens (artificial lens) used and local medical insurance coverage; ask for details before surgery.

A randomized trial involved 306 women aged 70 and older with cataracts. Half had surgery on the first eye within about 4 weeks, while the other half waited the usual 12 months. In one year, those with early surgery had about 34% fewer falls. The original figure was a fall rate ratio of 0.66, 95% CI 0.45 to 0.96. People who fell at least once: 49% in the surgery group, 45% in the waiting group—no decrease. People who fell twice or more: 18% in the surgery group, 25% in the waiting group. The surgery group had 4 fractures (3%), while the waiting group had 12 (8%). A Cochrane review included this trial, concluding that in women, first-eye surgery reduces the number of falls, but second-eye surgery does not. A randomized trial on the second eye involved 239 women aged 70 and older. The surgery group had a 32% lower fall rate, but the difference could be due to chance (fall rate ratio 0.68, 95% CI 0.39 to 1.19). In a 5% sample of US Medicare data, there were 1,113,640 cataract patients aged 65 and older (2002 to 2009). This study only tracked records and had no control group. Those who had surgery had about a 16% lower chance of hip fracture within one year (OR = 0.84, 95% CI 0.81 to 0.87). The absolute difference was 0.20 percentage points, meaning about 2 fewer cases per 1,000 people.
When the elderly walk the dog, hold the leash in the palm, don't wrap it around the hand, keep the leash short, and train the dog beforehand so it doesn't bolt
B

In the US, the number of people aged 65 and older who fell and broke bones while walking a dog was about 1,700 in 2004 and increased to about 4,400 in 2017. Eight-tenths are women, nearly three-tenths require hospitalization, and by specific location, hip fractures (proximal femur) are the most common. At one hand surgery clinic, about three-quarters of people injured by dog leashes were hurt because the leash was wrapped around their hand when the dog jerked. Therefore, hold the leash in the palm, keep it short, and train the dog not to bolt.

Holding the leash and keeping it short is free; walk with the elderly person once to show them. Training the dog not to bolt takes time; you can teach it yourself or hire a trainer; hiring a trainer costs money, and prices vary widely. The difficulty is that the elderly may be used to retractable leashes or wrapping the leash around their wrist and must change their habits.

US emergency surveillance data estimated nationwide that the number of people aged 65 and older who fell and broke bones while walking a dog was 1,671 in 2004 and 4,396 in 2017, a statistically significant increase. Among those with fractures, 78.6% were women and 28.7% were hospitalized. By location, the hip was most common at 17.3%. By major group, upper extremities were most common at 52.1%. Another US-wide emergency dataset for 2001 to 2018 estimated about 360,000 dog leash-related injuries (exact figure 356,746). Of these, 193,483 were injuries from being pulled by the dog, and 136,767 were from tripping or leash entanglement. Injuries per million population rose from 25.4 to 105.5. A hand surgery clinic treated 443 people for dog leash-related hand injuries over 5 years. About three-quarters were due to the hand or fingers being wrapped in the leash when the dog jerked (summary notes 337 people, 75.9%). About one-fifth required surgery (96 people, 21.6%). The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported that from 2001 to 2006, there were about 86,629 fall injuries related to dogs and cats annually. Of these, 88.0% were dog-related. Among dog-related falls, 26% occurred while walking the dog, and 21.2% were from being pushed or pulled down by the dog.

When placing an elderly person in a nursing home, first check if it is registered with the civil affairs department and sign a written agreement; deposits are capped at 12 months' bed fees and must be transferred to a dedicated bank account
A

Legitimate nursing homes must register with the civil affairs department (China) and sign a written agreement with you. Deposits are collected up to a maximum of 12 months' bed fees, and service fees are prepaid for a maximum of 12 months. Deposits and membership fees must be transferred to a dedicated account opened by the home at a bank. If they exceed the cap, ask to transfer to a personal account, or provide only a receipt instead of an invoice, do not pay yet.

Free. Before signing, call the local county-level civil affairs department or ask the nursing home for their registration receipt. Then cross-check the agreement, fee schedule, and payment account; half a day is enough. The difficulty is the shortage of nursing home beds, making family members hesitant to point out contract flaws.

The Management Measures for Nursing Care Facilities of the Ministry of Civil Affairs (China) stipulate that nursing facilities must register with the civil affairs department within 10 working days of admitting an elderly person. If the documents are complete, the department issues a registration receipt. The facility must sign a service agreement with the elderly person or their representative, specifying the care level, fee rates, refund procedures, and liability for breach. Failure to sign an agreement results in a mandatory correction order, warning, or a fine up to ⟦30000⟧ for serious cases. A 2024 document from the Ministry of Civil Affairs and six other departments (China) sets caps on prepayments. Retirement service fees are prepaid for a maximum of 12 months. Deposits are capped at 12 times the monthly bed fee for that individual. Deposits may only be used for refunds, advancing costs for sudden medical treatment, offsetting unpaid fees, and compensation. Public nursing homes and public-owned/privately-operated homes may not collect membership fees. Facilities not yet built or not yet authorized to admit residents also cannot collect membership fees. Deposits and membership fees must be deposited entirely into a dedicated deposit account supervised by a third-party bank; personal accounts are prohibited. Payments must be invoiced; receipts are not a substitute. If a contract is canceled before move-in, the facility must immediately refund prepayments. After move-in, after deducting used portions, the remainder should in principle be refunded in one lump sum via the original payment path. This document applies from October 1, 2024; provinces may set stricter rules. 2025 supervision guidelines require that when a nursing home requests a refund, the supervising bank must refund the full amount via the original path on the same day, or the next day at the latest.

If you are an only child and your parent is hospitalized, check your province's regulations for nursing leave; if available, submit a written application with the hospitalization certificate to your employer
B

Some provinces (China) stipulate that only children are entitled to nursing leave when a parent is hospitalized; the number of days varies by province. Henan provides no less than 20 days per year, Fujian no more than 10 days, and Guangdong no more than 15 days during hospitalization. Henan specifies it counts as work time; Fujian specifies salary and benefits remain unchanged. If the employer refuses or deducts pay, Fujian and Guangdong specify you can contact human resources and social security authorities.

Free. Search the national laws database (China) for your province's two relevant regulations; it takes about ten minutes. Then take the hospitalization certificate and submit a written application to your employer. The difficulty is that employers may be reluctant to grant it, and employees may fear offending the boss by asking.

Provinces record nursing leave in different local regulations. The Regulations of Henan Province on the Protection of the Rights and Interests of the Elderly (China) stipulate that elderly people who have received an Only Child Parent Honor Certificate are entitled to nursing leave from their child's employer during hospitalization. Nursing leave shall not be less than 20 days cumulatively per year, and this time is treated as work time. The Regulations of Fujian Province on the Protection of the Rights and Interests of the Elderly stipulate that for only children whose parents are at least 60 years old, the employer must provide nursing time during the parent's illness and hospitalization. Nursing time shall not exceed 10 days cumulatively per year, with salary and benefits unchanged. If the employer fails to pay salary or benefits during this time, human resources and social security or related authorities shall order payment within a time limit. The Regulations of Guangdong Province on Population and Family Planning apply to couples with provincial household registration (China) who voluntarily had only one child during the years the state encouraged one child per couple. When they reach 60, the employer provides 5 days of nursing leave annually. During illness and hospitalization, this is no more than 15 days cumulatively per year. If the employer fails to implement the leave, human resources and social security authorities at or above the county level shall order correction. The legal liability chapter of the Henan regulations does not specify penalties for employers who refuse nursing leave.

If an elderly person's memory is increasingly failing and starting to affect daily life, take them to a memory clinic or a hospital's neurology department for an examination to first rule out correctable causes such as depression, current medications, or hearing and vision impairment
B

Worsening memory is not necessarily senile dementia. First, check for depression, improper medication use, or poor hearing and vision, as these are correctable causes. However, actual cures are very rare; among people with dementia, fewer than 1% truly improve. Early examination has another benefit: while the elderly person is still capable of making decisions, it allows them to finalize who will handle their finances and medical treatment in the future.

Register for one visit to a memory clinic or neurology department, perform a cognitive test, and have blood and urine tests, taking half a day to a full day. Costs depend on local pricing; health insurance pays according to regulations. The difficulty lies in the elderly person's refusal to admit they are confused or their refusal to go.

The NICE (UK) dementia guideline (NG97) requires that when dementia is suspected, a medical history should first be taken from the patient and a family member familiar with them. A physical exam, blood tests, and urine tests must also be conducted to rule out reversible causes, followed by a cognitive test. The guideline specifically names four groups to check first: delirium (sudden episodes of confusion), depression, poor vision or hearing, and medications with a high anticholinergic burden. If these are ruled out and dementia is still suspected, refer to a specialist such as a memory clinic for diagnosis. A 2003 meta-analysis synthesized 39 studies involving 5,620 people diagnosed with dementia. Alzheimer's disease accounted for 56.3%, and vascular dementia for 20.3%. Reversible causes accounted for 9%, but actual improvement occurred in only 0.6%: partial improvement in 0.29% and full recovery in 0.31%. The same NICE guideline requires early discussion with the patient and family to make advance arrangements. Matters to discuss include granting power of attorney for health and finances, and their wishes for future care. The 2024 action plan from the National Health Commission (China) and 14 other departments requires strengthening initial cognitive function screening for people aged 65 and older and encourages hospitals to open memory clinics.
Calculate expected receipts in advance: state child-rearing subsidy (China) of ⟦3600⟧ per child per year, paid until age 3; personal income tax deduction of ⟦2000⟧ per child per month
A

Children under 3 years old receive a ⟦3600⟧ annual child-rearing subsidy, which is tax-free. For children born before 2025, it is calculated based on the remaining months. Additionally, from birth until the completion of formal education, each child qualifies for a ⟦2000⟧ monthly deduction from the parents' taxable income. If one person takes the full deduction, someone in the 3% tax bracket pays ⟦720⟧ less per year, and someone in the 10% bracket pays ⟦2400⟧ less.

Free of charge. For the subsidy, apply at the child's place of household registration (China); one visit is sufficient. For the tax deduction, fill it out on the "Individual Income Tax" mobile app, or have your employer assist with the filing.

The plan issued by the General Office of the CPC Central Committee and the General Office of the State Council (China) stipulates: starting January 1, 2025, children under 3 will receive a subsidy paid until they reach age 3, at a rate of "⟦3600⟧ per child per year". Children born before January 1, 2025, who are not yet 3 will have their subsidy calculated by the remaining months. A parent or other guardian applies for it. This subsidy is "exempt from personal income tax". When assessing aid such as minimum living allowances, this amount is "not included in household or individual income". ⟦3600⟧ is the "national basic standard"; "any local increase in the rate shall be funded by the local budget". The plan also stipulates that "governments at the county level and below shall not independently issue child-rearing subsidy policies or rates"; provincial or municipal governments wishing to issue different policies or increase rates must report to superior authorities for registration. Regarding taxes, in 2022 the State Council established a deduction for care of children under 3. In 2023, this was increased along with the child education deduction; as of January 1, 2023, both are ⟦2000⟧ per child per month. The child education deduction applies from age 3 until before primary school, and for the duration of formal education from primary school to doctoral level. Parents "can choose to have one person take 100% of the deduction, or each take 50%"; once chosen, it cannot be changed within the year. Example calculation: for one child, a monthly deduction of ⟦2000⟧ times 12 months equals ⟦24000⟧. If one person takes the full deduction, a person in the 3% bracket pays ⟦720⟧ less, and in the 10% bracket ⟦2400⟧ less. If two people each take half (⟦12000⟧ each): the 3% bracket pays ⟦360⟧ less, and the 10% bracket ⟦1200⟧ less. Tax brackets are based on annual taxable income: not exceeding ⟦36000⟧ is 3%, the portion between ⟦36000~144000⟧ is 10%.

Maternity leave is 98 days, with maternity allowances paid by the maternity insurance fund (China) based on the employer's average monthly salary of the previous year; paternity leave and childcare leave for both parents follow provincial regulations
A

Giving birth entitles you to at least 98 days of maternity leave, with additional days for difficult births or multiples, during which the maternity insurance fund (China) pays a maternity allowance. If your employer does not contribute to maternity insurance, they must pay it themselves. For paternity leave and childcare leave for both parents, check your provincial regulations. In Beijing, husbands get 15 days of paternity leave, and for children under 3, each parent gets 5 working days of childcare leave per year.
Free of charge. The employer handles the declaration; you do not need to go yourself.

The number of maternity leave days is stipulated by the State Council (China). "Female employees giving birth are entitled to 98 days of maternity leave, including 15 days of prenatal leave; 15 additional days for difficult births; and 15 additional days for each additional child in multiple births." The money received during maternity leave is called a maternity allowance. For those enrolled in maternity insurance, the "maternity insurance fund pays according to the average monthly salary of the employer's employees in the previous year." For those not enrolled, the employer pays according to your pre-leave salary. Paternity leave and childcare leave are stipulated by the population and family planning regulations of each province. Beijing: the wife's maternity leave is extended by 60 days, and the husband gets 15 days of paternity leave. Before the child reaches age 3, the couple "each receives five working days of childcare leave per year," with no salary reduction. Shanghai: the wife's maternity leave is extended by 60 days, and the husband gets 10 days of paternity leave. Before the child reaches age 3, "each side receives five days of childcare leave per year," with normal salary. Guangdong: the wife gets 80 days of bonus leave, and the husband gets 15 days of paternity leave. For children under 3, the father and mother each receive 10 days of childcare leave per year, with salary. Sichuan, 2025 version: the wife's maternity leave is extended by 90 days, and the husband gets 30 days of nursing leave. For children under 3, the couple each receives 10 working days of childcare leave per year, counted as time worked. In 2024, the General Office of the State Council (China) required local authorities to ensure that "all types of birth-related leave, such as maternity leave, bonus birth leave, paternity leave, and childcare leave, are fully implemented."
Remember this: salary reduction or dismissal due to pregnancy, childbirth, or breastfeeding is prohibited
A

It is illegal for an employer to reduce your salary or dismiss you because of pregnancy, childbirth, or breastfeeding. If your child is under one year old, you are entitled to 1 hour of breastfeeding time per day, and the employer cannot force you to work overtime or night shifts; violations result in a fine of ⟦1000~5000⟧ per person. See Chapter 19 for how to claim compensation.
Free of charge

The State Council (China) stipulates: "Employers shall not reduce the salary of, dismiss, or terminate the labor or employment contract with female employees due to pregnancy, childbirth, or breastfeeding." During these three periods, the employer cannot reduce your pay, nor can they fire you or terminate your contract. Those breastfeeding a child under 1 year old are entitled to 1 hour of breastfeeding time per day. Employers also cannot extend your working hours or assign night shifts. Violations such as forced overtime or night shifts during the breastfeeding period are fined between ⟦1000~5000⟧ per person. Regarding salary reduction or dismissal, this specific regulation does not include a fine amount; those illegally dismissed should apply for labor arbitration (China) to request reinstatement or compensation.
Calculate the cost of child-rearing based on "whose time is occupied," not on "how hard it is"
C

Convert the hours spent looking after the child each day and the number of nighttime awakenings into time. Then multiply by the hourly wage of a person performing those tasks. The resulting figure is usually much larger than the cost of milk and diapers. Therefore, the division of labor should be discussed and settled before birth.
Costs time, not money. Before a child turns 3, almost the entire day is occupied. The difficulty is that it is like this every day; it's not something that passes after a few days of effort.

Convert daily childcare time and the number of nighttime awakenings into hours. Then multiply by the hourly wage of a person performing those tasks. The resulting figure is usually much larger than the cost of milk and diapers. Although no one pays for childcare, cooking, or waking up at night, they are included in the cost this way. The calculation method is similar to how Chapter 10 calculates housework. Discuss the division of labor first, then decide whether or not to have a child.
Calculate financial costs in three stages: 0 to 3 years old, compulsory education, and post-compulsory education
C

The cost for a child from 0 to 3 years old mainly depends on who provides care: parents, grandparents, or a hired nanny. From primary to junior high school, costs mainly lie in housing and extracurricular activities. Afterward, costs mainly lie in the path of higher education. These three stages involve completely different spending patterns; grouping them together only produces a total figure that might panic you.

There is no fixed figure for how much it costs; it varies greatly by city and parenting style. The difficulty lies in sitting down to calculate the three stages separately rather than just guessing a number based on feeling.

From 0 to 3 years old, the largest expense is the method of childcare: self-care, grandparents, or a hired nanny. During the compulsory education stage (primary to junior high school), the largest expenses are housing and extracurricular spending. Afterward, the largest expense is the path of higher education. Money in these three stages is spent on completely different things; grouping them together only produces a total figure that will panic you.
Having a child for parents, for marriage, or for old-age security: record each as a separate item
C

Others wanting you to have a child may be a factor for consideration. However, the time and money should be recorded in your own ledger. "Raising children for old-age security" must be calculated as a separate item, as it bets on the economic capacity and willingness of another person twenty years later. Write down the consequences of not having a child as well, and compare the two side-by-side.
Costs a serious conversation, not money. The difficulty is speaking plainly without being evasive.

The logic is similar to Chapter 10. Others' wishes may be a factor for consideration. However, the costs must be recorded in your own ledger, not theirs. "Raising children for old-age security" especially needs to be calculated separately, as it assumes the economic capacity and willingness of another person twenty years later.
If planning to give birth in a few years, consider the wife's age in advance: around age 40, both natural pregnancy rates and IVF success rates decrease significantly
A

The older the wife, the harder it is to conceive naturally; in the early 40s, the monthly probability of pregnancy is only about half that of the early 30s. Once pregnant, the miscarriage rate also increases, being about one-third between ages 40 and 44. In vitro fertilization (IVF) cannot compensate for this; at age 43 or 44, each single embryo transfer has only about a 5% chance of resulting in a live birth.
Costs a serious conversation, not money. The difficulty is integrating childbirth with career and home buying into a single plan, rather than simply postponing it.

Regarding natural pregnancy, a US follow-up study of women aged 30 to 44 with no history of infertility who had just started trying to conceive showed that compared to ages 30-31, the monthly probability of pregnancy at ages 40-41 was about 53% lower (ratio 0.47, 95% CI 0.28 to 0.78), and at ages 42-44 it was about 59% lower (0.39, 0.16 to 0.93). At ages 38-39, it was about 30% lower (0.70, 0.48 to 1.01), with the confidence interval just touching the "no difference" level. Ages 32-33 did not differ from 30-31. Women who have never been pregnant have a lower probability of pregnancy at any age. In a similar Danish study, the probability for women aged 35-40 was 0.77 times that of those aged 20-24. The husband's age has much less impact (0.95 for men aged 35-39). Regarding miscarriage, Norwegian registry data for approximately 420,000 pregnancies from 2009 to 2013 showed the lowest miscarriage rate at ages 25-29 (9.8%). It was 10.8% for ages 30-34, 16.7% for 35-39, 32.2% for 40-44, and 53.6% for age 45 and older. Regarding embryo chromosomes, a study of 15,169 IVF embryos at a US fertility center showed chromosomal abnormalities increased steadily with age after 26. Among those undergoing IVF at ages 26-37, the rate of people whose viable embryos were all chromosomally abnormal was 2% to 6%; at age 42 it was 33%, and at age 44 it was 53%. Regarding IVF success rates, 2022 preliminary data from the UK fertility regulator showed that using one's own eggs with fresh embryo transfer, the live birth rate per embryo transferred was: 35% for ages 18-34, 26% for 35-37, 18% for 38-39, 10% for 40-42, and 5% for 43-44. Regulations in China: The 2003 "Human Assisted Reproductive Technology Specifications" by the Ministry of Health (China) explicitly states "it is prohibited to perform assisted reproductive technology for couples who do not comply with national laws and regulations on population and family planning, and for single women." In 2024, the General Office of the State Council (China) required local authorities to include appropriate assisted reproductive technology services within the scope of health insurance (China) coverage. By July 2025, the National Healthcare Security Administration (China) stated that all 31 provinces and the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps had included assisted reproductive technology in coverage, with over 1 million people benefiting in 2024.
Overtime pay is calculated at three rates: 1.5x, 2x, and 3x; if unpaid, complain to the labor inspectorate; if still unpaid after the deadline, an additional 50% to 100% must be paid
A

Overtime on regular workdays is paid at 1.5 times the wage. Overtime on weekly rest days without compensatory time off is 2 times. Working on statutory holidays such as New Year's Day, Lunar New Year, International Workers' Day, or National Day is 3 times, and the law does not provide the option of using compensatory leave instead of this payment. If the company does not pay, complain to the labor inspectorate. If ordered to pay within a deadline and they still fail to do so, the employer must pay an additional amount ranging from half to the full amount of the debt.

Free of charge. Routinely save copies of attendance records, shift schedules, overtime approval forms, and take screenshots of messages from supervisors assigning tasks in work group chats. The difficulty is remembering to save them every month.

The law stipulates that normal working hours shall not exceed 8 hours per day and an average of 44 hours per week. Regular weekday overtime should generally not exceed 1 hour per day. For special reasons requiring more, it must not exceed 3 hours per day and a total of 36 hours per month. Overtime pay is divided into three levels. If forced to work extended hours on workdays, pay shall be no less than 150% of the wage. If forced to work on weekly rest days without compensatory leave, no less than 200%. If forced to work on statutory holidays, no less than 300%. Specifically for the statutory holiday rate, the law does not offer the option of "substituting with compensatory leave." If an employer fails to pay overtime, the labor administrative department shall order payment within a deadline. If still unpaid after the deadline, the employer is forced to pay the employee compensation of 50% to 100% of the amount owed in addition to the debt (applies across China). For statutory holidays, see Article 2 of the State Council (China) Holiday Measures: New Year's Day (1 day), Lunar New Year (4 days), Tomb-Sweeping Day (1 day), International Workers' Day (2 days), Dragon Boat Festival (1 day), Mid-Autumn Festival (1 day), and National Day (3 days). Article 7 of these Measures allows for "unified holiday shifting" to connect these holidays with weekends into longer breaks.
Annual leave is calculated based on total cumulative work seniority: 5, 10, or 15 days; unused days are converted to cash at 300% of the daily wage
A

Combine seniority from all employers; if you have worked at least 1 year but less than 10 years, you get 5 days of annual leave. 10 years gets 10 days, and 20 years gets 15 days; seniority continues to accumulate even if you change jobs. If the employer cannot arrange leave and you agree not to take it, those days must be paid at 3 times the daily wage. If you sign a "voluntary waiver of annual leave" form, you only receive your normal salary.

Free of charge. Total all the years you have worked across all employers; social security contribution records serve as proof. The difficulty is having the courage not to sign when the company presents a "voluntary waiver of annual leave" form.

Working continuously for 12 months entitles one to annual leave. The number of days is based on cumulative working time, adding up years from all employers. 1 to less than 10 years is 5 days; 10 to less than 20 years is 10 days; 20 years or more is 15 days. Statutory holidays and weekly rest days are not counted toward annual leave days. If an employer truly cannot arrange leave due to work needs and you agree not to take it, the days that should have been taken must be paid as "annual leave wages at 300% of the employee's daily wage income." This 300% includes the normal wage already paid for the workday, so you effectively receive an additional 200%. Daily wage = monthly wage ÷ 21.75. The monthly wage is the average of the 12 months prior to payment, excluding overtime pay. Those who join an employer mid-year have their leave converted based on the remaining days of the year at that employer. Upon resignation, leave is converted based on time worked that year and settled in full; if too much leave was taken, it is not deducted back. If an employer neither grants leave nor pays the wage, they are ordered to correct it within a deadline. If still not corrected after the deadline, they must pay an additional compensation equal to that amount in addition to the annual leave wage (applies across China, effective January 1, 2008).
Probation has legal maximum limits, salary must not be lower than 80%, and it can only be agreed upon once
A

For contracts from 3 months to 1 year, probation is a maximum of 1 month; from 1 to 3 years, a maximum of 2 months; from 3 years or more, a maximum of 6 months. A company can only put you on probation once; making you undergo probation again after becoming a permanent employee just because you changed positions is illegal. Probationary salary must not be lower than 80% of the lowest level for the same position or the salary stated in the contract, and must not be lower than the local minimum wage.
Costs no money. Before signing, spend a few minutes comparing the contract term with the length of the probation period.

For contracts of 3 months or more but less than 1 year, probation shall not exceed 1 month. From 1 year or more but less than 3 years, it shall not exceed 2 months. For 3 years or more, and open-ended contracts (no expiration date), it shall not exceed 6 months. For contracts based on the completion of a specific task, or contracts totaling less than 3 months, no probation period may be agreed upon. "An employer and an employee may only agree on a probation period once"; the same company and the same person can only try once. If the contract only specifies a probation period, that probation period is not established, and that term is the term of the labor contract. Probationary salary "must not be lower than the lowest salary for the same position in the unit or 80% of the salary agreed upon in the labor contract, and must not be lower than the minimum wage where the employer is headquartered." If a probation period longer than the law allows is agreed upon and the person has actually worked it, the unit must pay an additional compensation amount. This is calculated based on the monthly salary after probation for the excess time. During probation, if the unit wants to terminate the contract, it can only do so in the cases listed by law and must clearly state the reason to the employee (applies to all of China).
If laid off, calculate N clearly first: one month's salary for each full year, half a month for less than six months
A

When laid off, the economic compensation the company must pay is calculated as follows: one month's salary for each full year worked; six months or more but less than one year counts as one year; less than six months pays half a month. The monthly salary here is the average of the 12 months prior to leaving; bonuses, allowances, and subsidies must all be included. If the salary is higher than 3 times the local average monthly salary of the previous year, it is capped at 3 times, and the number of years is capped at 12 years.
Costs no money. Use a calculator once, ten minutes.

Economic compensation under the Labor Contract Law is the amount the unit must pay when laying you off, often called N. Calculation method: "for each full year of work, one month's salary is paid... six months or more but less than one year is counted as one year; less than six months, the employee is paid half a month's salary." If the monthly salary is higher than three times the average monthly salary of local employees in the previous year, it is capped at three times, and seniority is only counted up to a maximum of twelve years.
If the company fires you because you cannot work after an illness, fail to meet job requirements, or major circumstances change without 30 days' notice, they must pay an extra month's salary
A

If the company fires you because you cannot work after an illness, fail to meet job requirements, or major circumstances have changed significantly, they must give 30 days' written notice. If they do not notify you, in addition to N, they must pay an extra month's salary; this is what people often call N+1. When negotiating, keep this one month separate; do not let the company lump it into N.
Costs no money.

The Labor Contract Law stipulates that there are two ways for an employer to terminate a contract under this article. One is to "give thirty days' written notice to the employee themselves." The second is to "pay the employee an additional month's salary and then terminate the labor contract." If they want you to leave immediately, they must pay an extra month's salary. This extra month is often called pay in lieu of notice, which is a separate amount from N. This one month is calculated based on your previous month's salary, while N is calculated based on the average salary of the 12 months before leaving; the two amounts have different bases.
If the company terminates the contract illegally, the compensation is double the economic compensation
A

If the company terminates the contract illegally, the compensation is double the economic compensation, often called 2N. Whether it is illegal or not depends on the specific case. Ask for legal aid or a lawyer for clarification first, then decide whether to negotiate with the company or go to arbitration.
Costs no money. Going to arbitration requires waiting several months. The difficulty is having to follow through to the end during those months without giving up halfway.

The Labor Contract Law stipulates that if an employer violates this law when terminating or ending a labor contract, they "must pay the employee compensation equal to twice the economic compensation stipulated in Article 47 of this Law." The calculation method is to first calculate one part according to the economic compensation method, then double it to pay you.
Do not sign "voluntary resignation for personal reasons"; signing it means losing N
B

Signing an acknowledgment of "voluntary resignation for personal reasons" usually means losing both economic compensation and unemployment benefits. Resigning on your own is not among the cases eligible for compensation, unless the company is at fault, such as owing wages or not paying social insurance. You don't need to sign on the same day; stay calm overnight and then decide.
Costs no money. The difficulty is withstanding the pressure to sign on the spot.

The Labor Contract Law limits the cases where economic compensation must be paid to several types listed in the law. Employees resigning on their own are not included, unless it is because the company is at fault according to the law, such as owing wages or not paying social insurance. Once "voluntary resignation" is signed, economic compensation and unemployment benefits are usually both lost.
Before leaving, save your payslips, timekeeping records, labor contract, social insurance book, and messages
B

In disputes like being laid off or having wages deducted, the unit must provide evidence, but for overtime, you must prove it first, and the unit only has to keep payroll records for two years. Once you return your computer and account, you can no longer get these documents. Having payslips, timekeeping, social insurance books, and original messages in hand allows you to present them when the unit denies it.
Costs no money. Spend half an hour saving documents. The difficulty is remembering to save them before leaving.

Once the computer and account are returned, these documents can never be retrieved. Labor disputes follow the principle of "whoever makes the claim must prove it": you must provide evidence for the matters you raise. If the evidence is in the hands of the unit, the unit must provide it; if not, the unit bears the adverse consequences. During arbitration, if you cannot get documents held by the unit, the arbitration committee can order the unit to submit them within a time limit. For disputes regarding firing, layoffs, contract termination, wage reduction, and seniority calculation, the unit bears the burden of proof. Overtime pay is different; you must first prove that you actually worked overtime. If you prove that the overtime records are in the hands of the unit and the unit does not submit them, then the unit bears the adverse consequences. The unit is only obligated to keep payroll records for two years or more. When paying wages, the unit must also provide you with an individual payroll statement. When a written contract has not been signed, payroll records, social insurance payment records, and employee IDs can all be used to prove you have a labor relationship with the unit. Recruitment registration forms, timekeeping records, and statements from other employees can also be used. Legally, messages are electronic data and can be used as evidence. Evidence must be submitted as originals; prints directly from original records are also considered originals. The Shanghai People's Procuratorate (China) once handled a case. A worker claimed the minimum wage difference for ten years; the first and second instances only recognized the last two years before leaving. The court's reason was that the unit only had to keep records for two years, and for the previous eight years, the worker had to prove it himself. He had payslips and bank statements for the full ten years, but the unit did not admit the payslips were real. In August 2024, he requested procuratorial supervision. After the procuratorate's protest, the unit settled and paid ⟦19000⟧ in compensation. He had been litigating since the company's mass layoffs in 2021, and by the time of the supervision request, about three years had passed (applies to all of China).
Before taking a position with dust, noise, or chemicals, check if the contract clearly states the hazards; three occupational health exams are arranged and paid for by the unit
A

When signing the contract, the unit must truthfully record in the contract: what occupational disease risks the position has, how to protect yourself, and what benefits you are entitled to. If they hide it from you, you have the right to refuse that work, and the unit cannot fire you for it. Three occupational health exams: before taking the job, while working, and when leaving the position, are all arranged and paid for by the unit. If the exam before leaving the position has not been done, the unit cannot terminate the contract with you.

Costs no money. When signing the contract, read every line of the "occupational disease risk notification" section. For each exam, keep a copy of the results yourself. The difficulty is speaking up to ask directly and getting the papers in hand.

The Law of the People's Republic of China on the Prevention and Control of Occupational Diseases stipulates that when signing a labor contract, the unit must clarify four things. Those four things are: what occupational disease risks the work may cause, what the consequences are, how to protect yourself, and what benefits you are entitled to. The original text of the law is "truthfully inform the employee and clearly state it in the labor contract, and must not conceal or deceive." If after signing the contract they transfer you to toxic work not mentioned in the contract, they must truthfully inform you again and negotiate with you to amend the contract terms. If the unit fails to do so, "the employee has the right to refuse work with occupational disease risks, and the employer shall not terminate the labor contract signed with the employee for this reason." A total of three exams: before taking the job, during the period of work, and when leaving the position. "The cost of occupational health examinations shall be borne by the employer," the money is paid by the unit, and the results must be reported in writing to you personally. For those who have not had an exam before taking the job, the unit must not arrange for them to work in contact with occupational disease risks. People whose physical condition is inherently unsuitable for this type of work (having occupational contraindications) must also not be assigned to prohibited tasks. If work-related health damage is discovered, the person must be transferred from their old position and properly settled. "For employees who have not undergone an occupational health examination before leaving their position, the labor contract signed with them shall not be terminated or ended." When leaving, you "have the right to request a copy of your occupational health monitoring records, and the employer must provide them truthfully and free of charge, and sign and seal the copy." For these health monitoring records, the unit must provide a true copy to you for free and must seal the copy (applies to all of China).

Many injuries from dust, noise, and chemical toxins are irreversible (such as pneumoconiosis, noise-induced deafness): the unit must provide protective gear, and you have the right to refuse work without protective measures
A

Pneumoconiosis, noise-induced deafness, and chemical eye burns are all legal occupational diseases; once the lungs and hearing are damaged, they cannot be cured. You have the right to know what hazards the position has and the right to request the unit to provide equipment and protective gear. If there is no protection, you can choose not to work. Any reduction in salary or firing by the unit for this reason is invalid.

Costs no money. The difficulty is having to wear particulate respirators, earplugs, and safety goggles all the time, and also having to refuse work without protection, the price of which might be being criticized by colleagues as "troublesome."

Starting from August 1, 2025, legal occupational diseases (China) include 12 major groups and 135 diseases, including 4 open-ended clauses. At the top of the first group is occupational pneumoconiosis. This includes silicosis, coal workers' pneumoconiosis, graphite pneumoconiosis, carbon black pneumoconiosis, asbestos pneumoconiosis, and talc pneumoconiosis. There are also cement pneumoconiosis, mica pneumoconiosis, potter's pneumoconiosis, aluminum pneumoconiosis, electric welder's pneumoconiosis, caster's pneumoconiosis, plus an open-ended clause. Occupational ENT and oral diseases include noise-induced deafness and blast-induced deafness. Occupational eye diseases include chemical eye burns and electro-optical ophthalmia. Among these, damage from pneumoconiosis and noise-induced deafness is permanent. The US National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH) states that silicosis is permanent lung damage that will worsen, and there is currently no cure. A review article in The Lancet states that after the patient is no longer exposed to dust, lung function still declines as the disease progresses. The US Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) states that noise-induced hearing loss is permanent; surgery and medicine cannot fix it. The law gives you four rights that can be used immediately. One is to know what occupational disease risks exist in this workplace, what the consequences are, and what protective measures must be in place. Two is to request the unit to provide standard-compliant protective equipment and personal protective gear and to improve working conditions. Three is to criticize, report, and denounce acts that violate the occupational disease prevention law and acts that endanger life and health. Four is to "refuse to follow regulations that violate instructions and refuse to be forced to perform work without occupational disease protective measures"; for incorrect instructions and lack of protection, you can choose not to work. And "if an employer reduces wages, benefits, and other treatments, or terminates or ends the labor contract signed with an employee because the employee exercises their legitimate rights according to the law, such action is invalid." If they reduce your salary, benefits, or fire you because you use these rights, those actions have no value (applies to all of China).
If injured while working, or hit by a car on the way to or from work, the first thing is to complete the work-related injury recognition procedure; if the unit doesn't file, you file it yourself
A

Being injured while working because of the job is a work-related injury; being hit by a car on the way to or from work where you are not primarily at fault also counts. But if you don't complete the work-related injury recognition procedure, medical expenses, salary during the recovery period, and disability benefits will all be lost. The unit must file within 30 days. If the unit does not file, you, your family, or the union can file it yourself with the social insurance administrative department within one year.

Costs no money, one trip to the social insurance administrative department (China). You need to bring three things: a work-related injury recognition application form, documents proving the labor relationship, and a diagnosis from a medical institution.

If the work-related injury recognition procedure is not completed, medical expenses, salary during the recovery period (salary during the period of leave with pay), and disability benefits will all be lost. If the unit fails to file for more than 30 days, the costs of work-related injury benefits incurred during that period shall be paid by the unit itself.
Don't believe "trying to make it to the workplace counts as a work-related injury": if you suddenly feel unwell, call 120 first, don't try to rush to clock in
A

Suddenly feeling unwell and trying to rush to the company won't help you get an extra penny. Deeming it a work-related injury requires the person to fall ill during working hours and at the workplace; falling ill on the way before reaching the position already doesn't count. Conversely, if emergency treatment exceeds 48 hours, it also doesn't count. The few dozen minutes lost trying to meet the conditions could cost you your own chance of survival.
Costs no money.

Deeming it a work-related injury requires the person to suddenly fall ill and die "during working hours and at the workplace," or fail to survive emergency treatment within 48 hours. Trying to meet these two conditions and delaying going to the hospital costs you your own chance of survival, and the compensation gained in return is not guaranteed.
If the employer fails to pay occupational injury insurance for you, you are still entitled to full occupational injury benefits, and the employer must pay the full amount themselves
A

If the employer does not pay occupational injury insurance for you, you still have occupational injury benefits. It simply shifts to the employer paying the full amount themselves according to the exact items and rates, without missing a single cent. By not paying insurance, the employer faces additional penalties: they are forced to pay the arrears, with a daily late fee of 0.05% added, and if overdue, they are fined 1 to 3 times the amount owed. Saying "The company didn't buy occupational injury insurance so we can't compensate" is a lie.

No cost. If the employer does not accept the claim, you must go to arbitration or even sue, which takes at least a few months. The difficulty lies in having to follow through to the end during those months.

The regulations clearly state: if an employer fails to pay occupational injury insurance for an employee and the employee suffers an occupational injury, that employer shall pay the money according to the items and rates prescribed by the regulations. Which items must be paid and how much for each are identical to those who have paid insurance; it simply shifts to the employer paying it themselves.
Once the injury has stabilized, undergo an assessment of labor capacity; the disability grade translates directly into money
A

Once the injury has stabilized, undergo an assessment of labor capacity; the grade translates directly into money. The one-time disability subsidy is calculated based on your salary: Grade 5 is 18 months, Grade 6 is 16 months, Grade 7 is 13 months. Grade 8 is 11 months, Grade 9 is 9 months, Grade 10 is 7 months. Do not sign a "final one-time settlement" agreement until you have the assessment results.
No cost. Going through the entire labor capacity assessment process requires waiting for some time.

The one-time disability subsidy is converted from the disability grade into a number of months' salary, paid in a lump sum. Grade 5 is 18 months, Grade 6 is 16 months, Grade 7 is 13 months of your own salary. Grade 8 is 11 months, Grade 9 is 9 months, Grade 10 is 7 months of your own salary.
Three types of payments for death due to occupational injury must be clearly separated: funeral subsidy, survivor's pension for dependent relatives, and one-time occupational injury death subsidy
A

There are three types of payments for death due to occupational injury; do not negotiate for just one. The funeral subsidy equals 6 months of the average monthly salary of local workers from the previous year. The survivor's pension for dependent relatives is paid monthly based on the deceased's salary, with 40% per month for a spouse and 30% per month for each other relative. The one-time occupational injury death subsidy equals 20 times the national per capita disposable income of urban residents from the previous year; there is only one such figure for the whole country.
No cost, requires completing one set of procedures.

Payments for death due to occupational injury are divided into three items. The first item is the funeral subsidy, equal to 6 months of the previous year's average monthly salary of workers in the insurance participation area (coordination area). The second item is the survivor's pension for dependent relatives, paid monthly based on the deceased's salary, with 40% per month for a spouse and 30% per month for each other relative. The third item is the one-time occupational injury death subsidy, equal to 20 times the national per capita disposable income of urban residents from the previous year. There is only one such figure for the whole country, not divided by region. For someone dying from an occupational injury in 2026, this amount is approximately ⟦1130000⟧ (specifically ⟦1130040⟧). Calculation method: national per capita disposable income of urban residents from the previous year ⟦56502⟧ multiplied by 20.

If bullied, verbally abused, or harassed for a long time at the workplace, do not just endure it: record evidence first, then depending on the nature, file a complaint, report to the police, or go to arbitration
B

People bullied at the workplace have about a six-tenths higher risk of heart disease and stroke later on; the more bullying, the higher the risk. People bullied are about twice as likely as others to have suicidal thoughts a few years later. Being scolded or oppressed is not a small matter that will pass by just putting up with it.

No cost. Time must be spent recording: dates, people present, verbatim words of the other person, and keeping original photos of messages and emails. Arbitration and litigation take several months. Changing jobs is the highest price; whether to stay or go is for you to decide.

Regarding health, pooling three cohort groups in Sweden and Denmark, a total of 79,201 working people aged 18 to 65. Initially, none had cardiovascular disease, with an average follow-up of 12.4 years. 9% said they had been bullied at the workplace in the past year. Bullied individuals had an approximately 59% higher risk of cardiovascular disease (coronary heart disease and cerebrovascular disease) (HR 1.59, 95% CI 1.28 to 1.98). Those who experienced workplace violence were about 25% higher (HR 1.25, 1.12 to 1.40). For both types, the more frequent the exposure, the higher the risk. A national random sample follow-up survey in Norway of 1,846 working people, measured every two to three years for a total of three times. Those bullied later developed suicidal thoughts with about twice the likelihood of others (OR 2.05, 95% CI 1.08 to 3.89). Conversely, those with prior suicidal thoughts were not more likely to be bullied later. Regarding law, China has no specific law on "workplace bullying"; it must be assessed based on specific behaviors. Employers who insult, physically punish, beat, illegally search, or detain employees face administrative penalties, must compensate for damages, and face criminal responsibility if a crime is constituted. If an employer uses violence or threats to force you to work, you can terminate the contract immediately without notice and receive economic compensation. Employers must have measures to prevent and stop people from using their authority or superior-subordinate relationships for sexual harassment. Victims can demand civil liability from the harasser. Labor arbitration must be completed within 45 days of acceptance, with complex cases extended by a maximum of 15 days.
When leaving a job, request a certificate of termination from the employer, clearly stating the contract term, termination date, position, and years of service
A

Whether you are laid off, the contract expires, or you resign, the employer must provide you with a certificate of termination when you leave, and within 15 days, they must transfer your files and social insurance. The certificate must state the contract term, termination date, position, and years worked at this unit. Unemployment registration requires this certificate. If the employer fails to provide it, the labor authority will force a correction, and they must compensate you for any losses caused.

No cost. Before leaving, request it in person or send a written message to request it, keeping evidence of the request. The difficulty is that the relationship may be strained, yet you still have to speak up. If the employer delays providing it, you must file a complaint or request arbitration, which takes several dozen days to a few months.

The Labor Contract Law stipulates that the employer must issue a certificate of termination upon the termination or expiration of a labor contract. The law does not distinguish who initiated it; contract expiration without renewal, resignation, or being laid off are all included. The employer must also complete the procedures for transferring your files and social insurance relationship within 15 days. The implementation regulations specify that the certificate must record four things: the labor contract term, the date of termination or expiration, the job position, and the years of service at this unit. The Unemployment Insurance Regulations stipulate that after becoming unemployed, workers must take this certificate from the employer to the social insurance agency in a timely manner to register for unemployment. Unemployment benefits are calculated from the date of registration. If the employer fails to issue a written certificate, the labor administrative department shall order a correction. If it causes damage to you, the employer must compensate. The law also stipulates that if a new employer hires someone who has not terminated their contract with their old employer, causing damage to the old employer, they shall bear joint and several liability for compensation. The certificate of termination is the written evidence showing you have terminated your contract with the old employer (applies throughout China).

When receiving severance pay, check the personal income tax first: the portion within 3 times the local average annual salary of the previous year is tax-exempt; the excess is taxed separately and not combined with the annual salary
A

For the one-time compensation received due to the termination of a labor contract, the portion within 3 times the local average annual salary of workers from the previous year is exempt from personal income tax. The excess is taxed separately and not added to the annual salary. If the employer combines the entire amount into that month's salary for tax deduction, clarify with the employer first, then call 12366 to ask the tax authority.

No cost. Look up the local average annual salary of workers from the previous year, then spend a few minutes checking how the employer deducted the tax. In the personal income tax app (China), you can see the tax filing details for each item of income.

The Ministry of Finance and the State Taxation Administration (China) issued a document adjusting the one-time compensation income received by individuals upon termination of labor relations with employers. This income includes economic compensation, living subsidies, and other subsidies. Among these, the portion within 3 times the local average annual salary of workers from the previous year is exempt from personal income tax. The portion exceeding 3 times is not included in the comprehensive income for the year but is taxed separately according to the comprehensive income tax rate table. In this table, the portion within ⟦36000⟧ for the whole year is subject to a 3% tax rate, and the portion from ⟦36000~144000⟧ is subject to 10%. It increases progressively up to 45%. For example, if the local average annual salary is ⟦100000⟧, 3 times is ⟦300000⟧. If you receive ⟦360000⟧ in compensation, tax is only calculated on the ⟦60000⟧ excess, which is ⟦3480⟧. If the entire ⟦360000⟧ were calculated according to this table, it would be ⟦58080⟧. This regulation applies from January 1, 2019, with no expiration date specified (applies throughout China).
If moving to another city for work, transfer your pension and medical insurance relationships to the new location; the years of contribution will continue to accumulate; do not withdraw the insurance
A

When changing cities for work, both pension and medical insurance relationships can follow you, and the years already contributed will continue to add up. If you have not reached retirement age, you are not allowed to withdraw the insurance to take the money out. If medical insurance contributions are interrupted for more than 3 months, you may have to wait up to 6 months at the new location before being reimbursed, so do not leave too long a gap in between.

No cost. After participating and contributing at the new location, the new employer or you yourself submit a transfer request, either by visiting a counter or doing it online. The pension side takes several dozen working days, and the medical side takes about 15 working days.

The Social Insurance Law of China stipulates that for individuals moving to another location for work (officially called transferring coordination areas), the pension insurance relationship follows the person, and the contribution years are accumulated. The same applies to employee medical insurance; the relationship follows the person and years are accumulated. Upon retirement, the pension is calculated in stages and paid uniformly. Transferring pension relationships to another province follows the transition measures issued by the General Office of the State Council (China). Before reaching the age to receive benefits, the pension relationship cannot be terminated for withdrawal. The Social Insurance Law of China also clearly states that personal accounts cannot be withdrawn early. The money in the personal account is transferred in full, including principal and interest. The employer's contribution portion is called the coordination fund, transferred at 12% of your actual contribution salary for each year from 1998 onwards. When receiving the pension, it is calculated based on your contribution salary, your years of contribution, and the average salary of each year at the receiving location. The procedure is that after contributing at the new location, the employer or you yourself submit a written request to the new location. The new location reviews it within 15 working days; once the old location receives the written acceptance, it completes the transfer within 15 working days. Once the new location receives the relationship and funds, it completes the process within another 15 working days. According to the 2020 inter-provincial procedure list, this must be achievable inter-provincially by the end of that year. You just need to apply at the destination; you don't have to return to the origin. Employee medical insurance must be stopped at the old location first, and after participating at the new location, a transfer can be requested. This can be requested online on the national medical insurance service platform (China) or at a counter. The old location transfers out within 10 working days, and the new location accepts within 5 working days; the personal account balance is transferred along with it. If contributions were interrupted for less than 3 months before the transfer, and arrears are paid according to the new location's rules, there is no waiting period; reimbursement starts in the month of contribution, and the gap period is also reimbursed. If interrupted for more than 3 months, the waiting period follows local regulations, in principle not exceeding 6 months (applies throughout China).

If you have worked for a full month and the employer has not signed a written labor contract with you, from the second month you can demand double salary for up to 11 months; if it reaches one year without a contract, it is deemed that an open-ended contract has been signed
A

If you work for a full month and the employer has not signed a written contract with you, from the second month they must pay an additional portion of salary each month, for a maximum of 11 additional months. If it reaches one year without signing, it is deemed that a contract with no expiration date has been signed. If the employer provides a contract, sign it; if you intentionally delay signing it yourself, you will not receive this payment.

No cost. Keep evidence of working daily: salary statements, attendance records, employee badges, messages in work chat groups. If the employer does not accept the claim, you must request labor arbitration (China). Arbitration is free, completed within 45 days of acceptance, with a maximum extension of 15 days. If you disagree, you can go to court; the first instance under ordinary procedures is generally completed within 6 months as per regulations, with possible extensions; lawyer fees are self-paid. The difficulty is that for someone still working there, demanding money requires being able to withstand the pressure.

The Labor Contract Law stipulates that to establish a labor relationship, a written labor contract must be signed. If not signed on the first day of work, it must be signed within one month of starting work. If working for more than one month but less than one year without signing, the employer must pay you double salary each month. The implementation regulations clearly state the start and end points: calculated from the day after the completion of one month of work until the day before the contract is retroactively signed. If working for a full year without signing, double salary is calculated until the day before the one-year mark, for a maximum of 11 months. From the one-year mark, it is deemed that both parties have signed an open-ended labor contract, and the employer must sign it retroactively immediately. An open-ended contract is one where no expiration date is agreed upon. A judicial interpretation by the Supreme People's Court (China) applicable from September 2025 stipulates that double salary is calculated by the month; for less than a month, it is calculated by actual working days. If the employer proves that the failure to sign was due to force majeure, or due to your own intentional refusal or serious fault, they do not have to pay. Within the first month of work, if the employer notifies you in writing to sign and you refuse, the employer can notify you in writing to terminate the labor relationship. In this case, the employer does not pay economic compensation, only the salary for the days you worked. If a period has already been deemed an open-ended contract, the court will not accept a claim for double salary for that period (applies throughout China).

If the employer fails to pay or underpays social insurance, first file a complaint to force retroactive payment; if you want to resign because of this and receive economic compensation, the resignation notice must clearly state it is because the employer failed to pay social insurance according to law
A

If the employer does not pay or underpays social insurance for you, you can file a complaint to force the employer to pay the arrears and an additional late fee. You can also notify the employer in writing to terminate the contract and demand economic compensation. The notice must clearly state the reason is that the employer failed to pay social insurance according to law; if you state personal reasons, you will not receive it. Agreements where "employees voluntarily waive social insurance" are invalid.

No cost. First, check your social insurance contribution history, take screenshots or print them out for records. To force retroactive payment, call 12333 or file a complaint with the labor inspection department of the human resources and social security bureau (China). For economic compensation, go to labor arbitration (China), which is free, completed within 45 days, with a maximum extension of 15 days. If you disagree, go to court; the first instance under ordinary procedures is generally completed within 6 months, with possible extensions; lawyer fees are self-paid. The difficulty is that after resigning, you must have your next source of income ready.

The Social Insurance Law of China stipulates that employers must truthfully declare and pay social insurance in full and on time. Except for legal reasons such as force majeure, payments cannot be delayed, exempted, or reduced. If the employer violates your social insurance rights, you can request the social insurance administrative department or the social insurance premium collection agency to handle it according to law. If the employer fails to pay in full and on time, the collection agency shall order payment within a time limit, with a daily late fee of 0.05% calculated from the date of arrears. If still not paid after the deadline, a fine of 1 to 3 times the amount owed is imposed. Labor and social security inspections include the employer's participation and payment of social insurance. After a case is filed, it must be resolved within 60 working days, with complex cases extendable by 30 working days. The Labor Contract Law stipulates that if the employer fails to pay social insurance for you according to law, you can terminate the labor contract, and the employer must pay economic compensation. If you give 30 days' notice and resign voluntarily, the employer does not have to pay economic compensation. Therefore, the notice must clearly state that the termination is because the employer failed to pay social insurance according to law. A judicial interpretation by the Supreme People's Court (China) applicable from September 2025 clearly states that agreements between the employer and you not to pay social insurance, or your own commitment not to require payment, are void. If the employer fails to pay social insurance according to law and you terminate the contract based on that and demand economic compensation, the court will accept it according to law. If the employer fails to handle social insurance for you and the social insurance agency cannot retroactively handle it, causing you to lose benefits, you can demand compensation for damages from the employer. This falls under labor disputes accepted by the court (applies throughout China).

When leaving a job and the company demands you pay a breach of contract penalty, first check what type it is: penalties can only be agreed upon for service periods after professional training and non-compete clauses; law does not allow penalties under other names
A

If the contract says "early resignation requires compensation," the law only allows this in two cases: the company paid for your professional technical training, or a non-compete agreement. If there was real professional training, the penalty cannot exceed the training costs and must be prorated according to the unserved portion of the service period.

No cost. Take out the labor contract, training agreement, and non-compete agreement to compare them, which takes a few minutes. If the company deducts salary to offset the penalty, you must go to labor arbitration (China) to get it back. Arbitration is free, completed within 45 days, with a maximum extension of 15 days. If you disagree, go to court; the first instance under ordinary procedures is generally completed within 6 months, with possible extensions; lawyer fees are self-paid.

The Labor Contract Law stipulates that except for the two cases of service periods after professional training and non-compete clauses, the employer shall not agree with the employee on a breach of contract penalty. The first case is when the employer pays for professional training and sends you for professional technical training; they can agree with you on a service period. If you violate the service period by leaving early, you pay the penalty as agreed. The penalty shall not exceed the training costs incurred by the employer. The amount the employer can actually demand shall not exceed the portion of the training costs allocated to the unserved part of the service period. For example, if the training cost was ⟦30000⟧ for a 3-year service period and you leave after 2 years, they can demand a maximum of ⟦10000⟧. Training costs must have vouchers, including tuition, travel expenses during the training period, and other direct expenses incurred due to the training. If you terminate the contract according to law and leave because the employer is at fault (such as not paying social insurance or owing salary), it is not considered a violation of the service period, and the employer cannot demand a penalty.
