The second case is non-compete, see Chapter 11 Section 12 (non-compete agreements). Additionally, contract terms where the employer exempts themselves from legal liability or eliminates the rights of the employee are void (applies throughout China).
If the employer wants to transfer your position or reduce your salary and you do not agree, state so immediately in writing; do not silently comply with the new arrangement for more than a month
B

Changing positions or salaries constitutes a contract modification, which requires mutual agreement and must be in writing. However, if you remain silent and follow the new position and salary for more than a month, courts usually will not rule the change invalid just because no written document was signed. If you disagree, say so immediately in writing; WeChat messages and emails both count.

Free. Upon receiving notice of a transfer or pay cut, send a written message clearly stating your disagreement and keep a screenshot; it takes a few minutes. The difficulty lies in the fact that you are still working there and must withstand face-to-face pressure. If the employer fires you or deducts pay because of this, you must go to labor arbitration (China). Arbitration is free, completed within 45 days of acceptance, with a maximum extension of 15 days. If you disagree with the result, go to court; first-instance ordinary procedures are generally completed within 6 months, extensions are possible, and lawyer fees are paid by yourself.

The Labor Contract Law stipulates that the employer and the employee must negotiate and reach a consensus to change the contents agreed upon in the labor contract. Changes must be in writing. The judicial interpretation of the Supreme People's Court (China) adds an article: if both parties negotiate and agree to change the contract orally, and then actually follow the new content for more than one month, the change is still valid. In such cases, using the reason "not in writing" to claim the change is invalid will not be accepted by the court. The condition is that the changed content does not violate the law, public order, or good customs. The calculation method of the Beijing High Court and Arbitration Commission is as follows: If the contract does not specify a position or specifies it unclearly, and the employer has a legitimate reason to transfer the position reasonably based on business needs, it is considered the employer's autonomy in labor use. Whether it is reasonable depends on four things: business necessity, legitimacy of purpose, whether you can perform the new position, and whether salary and benefits are worsened. If the contract clearly specifies the position without an agreement on transfer methods, a unilateral transfer by the employer is a breach of contract, and they must compensate for the salary difference from the old position. If the contract specifies the workplace as a broad range like "national" or "Beijing", it is considered an unclear agreement, and the place where you actually work is taken as the standard. The employer cannot change this location without a legitimate reason. If the employer fails to pay wages in full and on time, you can terminate the labor contract, and the employer must pay economic compensation (applies throughout China; Beijing's calculation method applies only in Beijing).

If dispatched to work for another company, wages must be calculated the same way as regular employees in the same type of position; if harmed at the workplace, both companies are jointly liable for compensation
A

Dispatched workers sign contracts with the dispatch company, but the entity where you work daily also has legal obligations. Wages must be calculated the same way as those in the same type of position at that entity; overtime pay and performance bonuses are also paid by that entity. If you suffer harm at that entity, both companies compensate jointly; you can claim from either company. During months when you are returned and have no work, the dispatch company must still pay you based on the minimum wage.

Free. Take out your labor contract and see which company's seal is on it; takes a few minutes. Then ask the dispatch company about the wages and social insurance specified in the dispatch agreement; the company is obligated to inform you. If a real dispute arises, go to labor arbitration (China); it is free, completed within 45 days of acceptance, with a maximum extension of 15 days. If you disagree, go to court; first-instance ordinary procedures are generally completed within 6 months, extensions are possible, and lawyer fees are paid by yourself.

The Labor Contract Law stipulates that the labor dispatch company is your employer and must sign a fixed-term contract of 2 years or more with you, paying wages monthly. During periods when you are not dispatched to work, they must pay monthly according to the local minimum wage. The dispatch company must inform you of the contents of the dispatch agreement and must not skim off the wages paid to you by the entity where you work (legally called the labor-using entity). Neither party may charge you fees. Dispatched workers have the right to equal pay for equal work as the labor-using entity's employees. The labor-using entity must use the same labor remuneration distribution method for the same type of position. If there is no similar position, refer to the remuneration of the same or similar positions in the locality. The labor-using entity must pay overtime, performance bonuses, and provide benefits related to the position, and must not discriminate against dispatched workers. For continuous use, wages must be adjusted normally. Dispatch can only be used for temporary, auxiliary, or substitutable positions; temporary positions are those existing for no more than 6 months. The number of dispatched workers in a labor-using entity must not exceed 10% of its total workforce. If the labor-using entity causes harm to the dispatched worker, the dispatch company and the labor-using entity bear joint and several liability. Joint and several means you can demand full compensation from either company or both. If you have a labor dispute with either company, both are joint parties in arbitration. In case of a work-related injury at the labor-using entity, the dispatch company applies for work injury recognition and bears work injury insurance responsibility; the labor-using entity must assist in the investigation. The labor-using entity can only return you in a few cases stipulated by law. Using the name of contracting or outsourcing while actually using labor in a dispatch manner is also handled according to dispatch regulations (applies throughout China, interim regulations applicable from March 1, 2014).
Place infants on their backs to sleep, on a firm flat surface, sharing a room but not a bed, with no soft objects in the bed
A

When the child is young, place them on their back, face up, to sleep on a firm flat surface, not inclined. Inclined sleepers and baby seats should not be used as beds. Adults and the child should sleep in the same room, but not in the same bed. Do not place pillows, blankets, crib bumpers, stuffed animals, or other soft objects in the bed. In the US alone, about 3,500 infants die each year from sleep-related causes.
Free. The mattress must be changed to a firm type, costing a few hundred yuan. The difficulty lies in standing firm against grandparents' advice and consistently following these practices.

In the US, about 3,500 infants die each year from sleep-related causes. These include Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (SIDS), unknown causes, and accidental suffocation in bed. According to the American Academy of Pediatrics, a safe sleep environment is "back to sleep; use a firm, flat, non-inclined sleep surface; room-sharing without bed-sharing; avoid blankets, pillows, and soft objects in the sleep area, and avoid overheating." A few other things also help reduce risk: breastfeeding, avoiding exposure to nicotine and alcohol, timely vaccination, and using a pacifier.
Administer the first dose of Hepatitis B vaccine within 24 hours of birth
A

Within 24 hours of birth, the child must receive the first dose of the Hepatitis B vaccine. About 95% of those infected with Hepatitis B as infants or young children develop chronic hepatitis. Most people infected as adults recover on their own, so this dose is more beneficial the earlier it is given. If the mother is Hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) positive, the child must also receive Hepatitis B immune globulin within 12 hours of birth.
Free. The Hepatitis B vaccine is part of the national immunization program (China) and is already free. The child receives the injection on the day of birth at the hospital, requiring no extra trips.

The World Health Organization (WHO) states: "All infants should receive their first dose of hepatitis B vaccine as soon as possible after birth (within 24 hours)." The reason is that "about 95% of infections in infancy and early childhood lead to chronic hepatitis." Most people infected as adults recover on their own (without treatment). According to the WHO's original text, for adult infections, "less than 5%" become chronic. The mother-to-child transmission prevention norms of the National Health Commission (China) require: children of HBsAg-positive mothers must "receive the first dose of hepatitis B vaccine as soon as possible within 12 hours after birth, and simultaneously receive 100 international units of hepatitis B immune globulin."
Receive all vaccines in the national immunization program, completely free; if a schedule is missed, only catch up on the missing doses
A

Vaccines in the national immunization program (China) are completely free; vaccination units are not allowed to charge fees. Vaccination records are checked when children enter nursery or school; missed doses are usually detected and caught up. If a schedule is missed, only catch up on the missing doses, no need to restart from the beginning; switching manufacturers is still acceptable for subsequent doses.

Free. The law (China) clearly states "vaccination units administering national immunization program vaccines shall not charge any fees." You must take your child to the vaccination clinic several times according to their age in months. Keep the vaccination record carefully; do not lose it.

When children enter nursery or school, the nursery or school must check the vaccination record. If children are found not to have received the required program vaccines, they must report to the vaccination unit and cooperate in urging guardians to catch up on vaccinations. Therefore, missed doses are usually detected during record checks at entry. The 2026 version of the immunization schedule is currently in use. The HPV (Human Papillomavirus) vaccine has been included in the national immunization program. The starting age for the DTaP (Diphtheria-Tetanus-Pertussis) vaccine has changed from 3 months to 2 months old. A total of 5 doses are given at 2 months, 4 months, 6 months, 18 months, and 6 years old, one dose each time. Children of eligible age in Tibet, Qinghai, Xinjiang, and the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps will also receive routine Japanese Encephalitis vaccination starting March 2026. Multiple vaccines can be given on the same day: currently, all national program vaccines can be administered simultaneously according to the schedule or catch-up principles. For two or more types of injectable vaccines, they must be injected at different sites; "it is strictly forbidden to mix two or more vaccines and draw them into the same syringe for injection." If not given on the same day, injectable live attenuated vaccines must be spaced at least 28 days apart. There is no interval limit between inactivated vaccines, oral live attenuated vaccines, and other vaccines. For children under 18, the catch-up principle is to catch up as soon as possible, "only needing to complete the unfinished doses, no need to restart the entire course"; switching manufacturers for the same type of vaccine is acceptable (National, 2026 version schedule).
Exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months, not even water is needed; from 6 months, start complementary feeding and continue breastfeeding
A

Start breastfeeding within the first hour after birth. For the first six months, only breastfeed; even water is not necessary. At 6 months, start complementary feeding, ensuring daily intake of iron-rich animal foods, and continue breastfeeding until 2 years or older. If breast milk is insufficient or breastfeeding is not possible, use infant formula.
Free, and it saves money on formula. The cost is time; breastfeeding takes several hours each day. The difficulty lies in consistent breastfeeding without interruption for the first 6 months.

The World Health Organization (WHO) recommendation is to "initiate breastfeeding within the first hour of birth." For the first six months, "exclusive breastfeeding, meaning no other food or drink, not even water." Then "from 6 months of age, start safe and nutritionally adequate complementary foods while continuing breastfeeding until 2 years of age or beyond." The service guidelines of the National Health Commission (China) also encourage exclusive breastfeeding from 0 to 6 months. These guidelines also require that from 6 months old, "daily complementary meals must include iron-rich animal foods."
Prepare formula with water at 70 ℃ or higher, let it cool before feeding, and discard leftovers
A

Infant formula is not sterile and can be contaminated with a bacterium that kills four to eight out of ten infected newborns. Pour hot water into the bottle first, wait until it drops to about 73.8 ℃ before adding formula; in most cases, this kills the bacteria to less than one-hundred-thousandth of the original amount. Hot water reduces some Vitamin C, but measured levels in various formulas still meet standards. Let it cool before feeding, and discard leftovers.

Free. Each time requires waiting a few extra minutes for the milk to cool. The difficulty is when the baby is crying from hunger, you still have to wait for the water temperature to drop before mixing.

Infant formula is not sterile and can be contaminated with Cronobacter sakazakii. Reported mortality rates in infected newborns range from 40% to 80%. Experimental studies show: pouring hot water into the bottle first and waiting until it drops to about 73.8 ℃ before adding formula results in the milk temperature remaining above 70 ℃ in the vast majority of cases. This reduces the bacteria by more than 5 log cycles, to less than one-hundred-thousandth of the original. The cost of hot water lies in Vitamin C. In 2006, the WHO and the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) held an expert meeting. Data reviewed at the meeting showed: when prepared with boiling water, only Vitamin C decreased significantly, dropping by 5.6% to 65.6% in 4 types of formula. Formula is originally fortified with extra Vitamin C at the factory. Even the type with the largest reduction still had 9.0 mg per 100 kcal after preparation, higher than the minimum 8 mg required by international Codex standards. The meeting had only this one study, so no definitive conclusion was reached.
Do not give honey to children under 1 year old
A

Do not give honey to children under 1 year old. This includes honey water, honey mixed into complementary foods, and cakes containing honey. Honey can contain bacteria that cause botulism. An adult's intestinal flora can control it, but an infant's cannot.
Free

The US CDC states: "Do not give honey to a child under 1 year old," because "honey can contain the bacteria that cause infant botulism." An adult's intestinal flora can control these spores (the dormant state of the bacteria), but an infant's cannot.
The Vitamin K injection at birth must be administered
B

Newborns have very low Vitamin K stores; without supplementation, they may suffer from bleeding, with late-onset cases often manifesting as brain hemorrhages. In Tashkent, where prevention was not widespread, 478 out of 100,000 newborns suffered this type of bleeding. With prevention, it is estimated to decrease by more than 78%. If giving birth at home or in an informal facility, proactively ask if the child has been injected.
From 0 to a few dozen yuan. This is usually included in the hospital birth fees and not paid separately.

Newborns have very low Vitamin K stores. Without supplementation, Vitamin K Deficiency Bleeding (VKDB) can occur, with late-onset cases often presenting as intracranial hemorrhage (bleeding in the brain). A Belgian expert consensus recommends "a single intramuscular injection of 1 or 2 mg of Vitamin K at birth." In regions without systematic prevention, the rate of VKDB is 478 cases per 100,000 infants. This figure is based on 42,000 newborns in Tashkent. The study authors estimate that with prevention, the incidence rate decreases by "more than 78.5%."
If an infant under 3 months has a fever of 38 ℃, go to the hospital immediately; do not monitor at home
A

If a child is under 3 months old and their temperature reaches 38 ℃, go to the hospital immediately. Do not monitor at home, and do not give fever reducers first to see what happens. The American Academy of Pediatrics has a specific guideline for febrile infants who appear well, so "seeing the child is still alert" is not a reason to wait at home. UK guidelines also classify infants under 3 months with a 38 ℃ fever as high risk for serious illness.
Examination and test fees of a few hundred yuan.

The American Academy of Pediatrics has specific guidelines for full-term infants aged 8 to 60 days who appear well. This guideline defines fever as "temperature ≥38.0 ℃." It divides them into three groups: 8 to 21 days old, 22 to 28 days old, and 29 to 60 days old, with a management strategy for each. Infants under 8 days old are not within the scope of this guideline. The NICE (UK) fever guidelines apply to children under 5 years old. The guidelines state clearly: for infants under 3 months, a temperature of 38 ℃ or higher belongs to the "high-risk group for serious illness."
No matter how tired or frustrated you are, never shake a baby
B

Infants have large heads and weak necks. Violent shaking can cause bleeding in the brain and eyes, which can be fatal or lead to lifelong disability. Gentle rocking to soothe them to sleep is fine; the danger lies in uncontrolled, violent shaking. When you are about to lose your temper, put the baby back in the crib and walk away for a few minutes. Letting the baby cry for a while is safer than holding them and shaking them.
Free. The difficulty lies in stopping yourself exactly when you are most exhausted and frustrated.

An infant's head is large relative to its body, and neck muscles are weak. Violent shaking causes intracranial and retinal hemorrhages (bleeding in the brain and eyes), which can be fatal or cause lifelong disability. Gentle rocking to soothe sleep does not count; the danger is uncontrolled violent shaking. Medicine calls this type of injury from shaking or impact "Abusive Head Trauma." It is the leading cause of death from head injury in children under 2 years old. In the US, from 1999 to 2014, it caused the deaths of nearly 2.250 children under 5 years old.
Choose diapers based on three factors rather than brand: fit, frequency of changes, and absence from quality inspection failure lists
C

No official agency has ranked "the best brand." Only two things can be verified: quality inspection results from the State Administration for Market Regulation (China), and regulatory investigation results for specific cases. Expensive does not mean safe, and imported does not mean compliant. Buy a small trial pack for a week to see if the baby gets diaper rash or pressure marks; only buy in bulk if it suits them.
Between two or three hundred to over ⟦1000⟧ per month, depending on the type you use.

No official agency has published a ranking of "the best brands," so this book does not recommend specific brands. Only two types of information are verifiable. One is the random quality inspection announcements from the State Administration for Market Regulation (China). The second is the results of regulatory investigations into specific incidents. In June 2026, after the "formamide in baby diapers" issue gained attention, the State Administration for Market Regulation led an inter-departmental investigation team to verify the matter.
For large items, consider the order "borrow, buy used, buy new"; do not buy everything at once
C

Strollers, swaddles, and toys are used for a short time, so try to borrow first; if not possible, buy used, and only buy new as a last resort. If buying a used car seat, ensure it has not been in a moderate-to-severe accident, has not been recalled, and has all parts; if unsure, do not use it. In a Scottish study, infants who usually slept on a mattress used by another child had about 3 times the risk of sudden death, though it is unclear if the mattress was the cause. It is best to buy mattresses new.
No extra cost; savings are often measured in thousands of yuan. The difficulty lies in resisting the urge to buy everything brand new at once.

Strollers, cribs, swaddles, and toys are used for very short periods; in the second-hand market, supply far exceeds demand. Used items must maintain three safety boundaries. First is car seats. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) recommends that seats involved in moderate or severe accidents must be replaced and never reused. A crash is considered minor (and the seat reusable) only if all five conditions are met: the car could be driven away, the door nearest the seat was undamaged, no one in the car was injured, airbags did not deploy, and there is no visible damage to the seat. Used seats must meet five criteria: no moderate-to-severe accidents, labels with manufacture date and model are present, not recalled, all parts present, and manual included. Date and model are used to check for recalls and age. Second is mattresses. A study in Scotland compared sudden infant deaths with healthy controls of the same age, tracing their mattress use. Infants usually sleeping on a mattress used by another child had a higher risk of Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (OR 3.07, approx. 3 times, 95% CI 1.51 to 6.22). Mattresses from another home had an OR of 4.78, while those from the same home were 1.64 (the latter not statistically significant). The authors stated current evidence is insufficient to conclude the mattress itself is the cause. Third is cribs. The US implemented new mandatory standards for cribs on June 28, 2011; old cribs must also comply. Traditional drop-side cribs have been eliminated. The Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) states that old cribs require destructive testing to verify compliance, so no self-check method is provided. From November 2007 to April 2010, the US recorded 147 deaths related to standard-sized cribs, including 35 due to structural issues and 18 related to broken drop-sides. Loose screws caused at least 10 deaths. US law bans the sale of inclined infant sleepers regardless of manufacture year, and they were included in regulatory requirements in 2023 (US, UK).
If a child has severe eczema or egg allergy, do not avoid peanuts; introduce them early under a doctor's guidance, but never give whole peanuts
A

For infants with severe eczema or egg allergy, feed peanut products regularly from 4 to 11 months of age. Among children who initially had no skin test reaction, by age 5, only 1.9% of the group fed peanuts were allergic, compared to 13.7% in the avoidance group. For those with a mild initial reaction, 10.6% of the fed group were allergic versus 35.3% in the avoidance group. Consult a doctor before starting, and never give whole peanuts as they are a choking hazard for the trachea.
A jar of peanut butter costs a few dozen yuan. Feed it a few times a week; it is easy to do. A doctor's visit for evaluation is required before starting.

The LEAP randomized trial in the UK involved 640 infants with severe eczema, egg allergy, or both, aged 4 to 11 months. They were randomly assigned to either consume peanut products regularly or avoid them entirely until 60 months of age to assess peanut allergy rates. Among 530 infants with negative skin tests at entry, 13.7% of the avoidance group were allergic versus 1.9% of the consumption group (P<0.001). Among 98 infants with mild positive skin tests at entry, 35.3% of the avoidance group were allergic versus 10.6% of the consumption group (P=0.004). Serious adverse events did not differ between groups.

Watch for signs of neonatal jaundice: go to the hospital immediately if jaundice appears within 24 hours, or if the baby is difficult to wake or won't feed; see a doctor early if jaundice deepens or stools are pale
B

Over 80% of newborns have some degree of jaundice. If jaundice appears before 24 hours of age, or if it is accompanied by excessive lethargy, inability to wake, refusal to feed, or being floppy or stiff, go to the hospital immediately. If jaundice deepens after 24 hours or stools are pale, seek medical attention early; pale stools can indicate biliary atresia. Excessively high bilirubin can cause brain damage and lifelong disability.

Examination and bilirubin testing cost under a few hundred yuan. If phototherapy is needed, it usually requires about two days of hospitalization. The difficulty is going to the hospital even when the baby seems otherwise fine.

The 2022 American Academy of Pediatrics guidelines state: "more than 80% of newborns have some degree of jaundice." Excessively high bilirubin causes acute bilirubin encephalopathy and kernicterus. The guidelines describe kernicterus as a "permanent disabling neurologic condition" characterized by athetoid cerebral palsy, upward gaze palsy, enamel dysplasia of deciduous teeth, and hearing loss. The guidelines list "jaundice appearing within the first 24 hours after birth" as a risk factor for severe jaundice. The UK National Health Service (NHS) categorizes advice for parents into two levels. Level one (emergency/A&E): jaundice accompanied by excessive lethargy, inability to wake, refusal to feed, being floppy or stiff, or seizures. Jaundice within the first 24 hours also falls into this level. Level two (early doctor appointment): jaundice after 24 hours that does not improve or worsens, dark yellow or brown urine, or pale cream-colored stools. Globally, in 2010, approximately 480.000 newborns suffered from Rh hemolytic disease or extreme hyperbilirubinemia. Of these, 24% died and 13% developed kernicterus. Among kernicterus survivors, over 83% had one or more impairments. Pale stools can indicate biliary atresia, which requires Kasai surgery within 60 days for significantly better outcomes. Since 2004, Taiwan has included stool color cards in all newborn health booklets. The rate of surgery within 60 days increased from 60% in 2004 to 74.3% in 2005. In another population study in Taiwan, after using the color cards, the mortality rate for biliary atresia children dropped from 26.2% to 15.9%. This was a before-and-after comparison, not a randomized trial.

If pregnant or breastfeeding on a vegetarian diet, take Vitamin B12 supplements or eat fortified foods; complementary foods for infants must include animal products; consult a doctor before a vegan diet
B

Vitamin B12 is found almost exclusively in meat, eggs, and dairy; vegans must rely on fortified foods or supplements. If a vegan mother does not supplement, her breastfed infant is prone to deficiency. Problems often appear between 4 to 8 months: growth retardation, developmental delays, and potentially irreversible neurological damage if deficiency is prolonged. Complementary foods must include animal products daily.

A bottle of Vitamin B12 tablets costs a few dozen yuan, taken once daily. Adding eggs, meat, or fish to complementary foods is inexpensive. The difficulty lies in changing a family's belief that a vegetarian diet is healthier.

In 2003, the US CDC reported two infants. Both were breastfed by vegetarian mothers, both had Vitamin B12 deficiency, and both showed growth retardation and developmental delays. The first mother had been vegan for 7 years. The infant was hospitalized at 15 months with severe anemia; a brain MRI showed global brain atrophy. After B12 supplementation, the child improved, but at 32 months, speech and language skills remained delayed. The report stated the most common cause of B12 deficiency in infants is a maternal dietary deficiency. In breastfed infants, it typically manifests at 4 to 8 months. Prolonged deficiency can lead to irreversible neurological damage, varying by severity and duration. Reliable non-fortified sources are only animal foods: meat, milk/dairy, and eggs. Most natural B12 in plants is not bioavailable. Fortified cereals, soy milk, and nutritional yeast can be stable sources. The report requires vegetarians, especially pregnant and lactating women, to know their B12 intake or consult nutrition professionals. The 2016 position statement of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics (US) states: "Vegans need reliable sources of vitamin B12, such as fortified foods or supplements." The 2017 position paper on complementary feeding from ESPGHAN states: all infants should receive iron-rich complementary foods, including meat or iron-fortified foods. Vegan diets should only be practiced under appropriate medical or nutritional supervision, and parents must understand the serious consequences of failing to follow supplementation recommendations. The 2020 core feeding messages from the National Health Commission (China) require daily complementary foods to include no fewer than 4 types, including at least one animal food, one vegetable, and one grain/tuber.
When buying baby gear, do not buy walkers with wheels; use stationary activity centers or playpens instead
B

A baby in a walker can travel over 0.9 m in 1 second; most accidents occur while adults are standing right next to them. In the US from 1990 to 2014, approximately 230.000 emergency room visits were due to walkers; nine out of ten involved head and neck injuries, mostly from falling down stairs. Walkers also do not help children learn to walk.
Free, and saves the cost of a walker. Stationary activity centers or playpens must be purchased separately or borrowed. The difficulty is discarding one if it was a gift or already purchased.

In the US from 1990 to 2014, an estimated 230.000 (specifically 230.676) emergency room visits for infants under 15 months were due to walker injuries. Of these, 90.6% were head or neck injuries, and 74.1% involved falling down stairs while in the walker. 4.5% required hospitalization, and 37.8% of those hospitalized had skull fractures. The US implemented mandatory safety standards for walkers in 2010. In the four years following, average annual injuries dropped 22.7% compared to the four years prior. However, the study authors stated walkers remain an important source of preventable injury. A 2001 position statement from the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) noted 34 walker-related deaths in the US from 1973 to 1998. Warning labels, education, adult supervision, and stair gates have proven ineffective at preventing these injuries. As walkers offer no clear benefit, the AAP advocates for a ban on the manufacture and sale of wheeled walkers, recommending stationary activity centers instead. AAP materials for parents state most walker accidents happen while an adult is watching. A baby in a walker can move more than 3 feet (about 0.9 m) in 1 second. Regarding whether walkers help children learn to walk, the AAP says no, and they may even delay it. Evidence for delays is not definitive. An Irish survey of 190 infants found walker users walked independently about 3 weeks later on average (61.12 weeks vs 58.14 weeks), with more use correlating to later walking. However, this was a questionnaire survey without a control group. A small 2002 review found two randomized trials, neither of which showed a significant effect on the onset of walking. Pooling four studies showed a delay of 11 to 26 days, but study quality was low.
Give 400 IU of Vitamin D daily from birth, especially for breastfed babies; full-term infants usually do not need calcium supplements in the first 6 months
B

Breast milk contains very little Vitamin D, and infants should avoid excessive sun exposure, so daily supplementation is necessary. In rural Turkey, 3.8% of unsupplemented infants developed rickets in one year, while none in the supplemented group did. Follow the doctor's dosage. Normal full-term infants usually do not need extra calcium in the first 6 months.
A bottle of Vitamin D drops costs a few dozen yuan, administered once daily. The difficulty is remembering to give it every day, at least until age 1.

A 2020 Cochrane review states Vitamin D levels in breast milk are low, making exclusively breastfed infants prone to deficiency. The American Academy of Pediatrics says infants outdoors for long periods must use sun protection, so all infants should supplement Vitamin D. The 2020 core feeding messages from the National Health Commission (China) state: "Infants should be supplemented with 400–800 IU of Vitamin D daily from birth as guided by a doctor." The same section states: "Normal full-term infants in the first 6 months after birth usually do not need calcium supplements." The 2016 Global Consensus on Rickets, involving 11 international academic organizations, states 400 IU (10 micrograms) daily is sufficient to prevent rickets. All infants from birth to 12 months should supplement, whether breastfed or formula-fed. This is a strong recommendation with moderate quality evidence. In a study in rural northeastern Turkey, no infants receiving 400 IU daily developed rickets, while 3.8% of unsupplemented infants developed new-onset rickets over 12 months. The consensus also noted no global reports of infants diagnosed with rickets via X-ray while consistently taking 400 IU daily. In 1992, a Chinese study in four northern and southern cities supplemented infants with 100, 200, or 400 IU daily. By 6 months, no infants in any group had rickets. However, cord blood Vitamin D in northern newborns was only about one-third of those in the south (12.5 vs 35.0 nmol/L). Higher supplementation led to higher levels at 6 months; the authors recommended 400 IU daily.
When bathing an infant, add cold water first then hot, test with the inside of your wrist or elbow before putting the baby in; set water heaters below 50 ℃ if adjustable
B

Contact with 65 ℃ water for 2 seconds causes third-degree burns in most adults; an infant's skin is even thinner. Add cold water to the tub first, then hot, stir well, and test with your inner wrist or elbow. Never bathe a baby under running water. One US state lowered the factory-set temperature of water heaters to 49 ℃, and hospitalizations for tap water burns in children dropped by more than half.
Free. Each bath takes an extra minute or two to test the water. For more certainty, buy a water thermometer. The difficulty is remaining patient and testing the water even when the baby is fussy.

The US Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) states most adults suffer third-degree burns from 2 seconds of contact with 150 ℉ (approx. 65 ℃) water. Contact with 140 ℉ (60 ℃) for 6 seconds, or 130 ℉ (approx. 54 ℃) for 30 seconds, also causes burns. Even 120 ℉ (49 ℃) can cause third-degree burns with 5 minutes of immersion. A World Health Organization (WHO) report states infant skin is thinner than adult skin, so lower temperatures can cause deeper burns. The American Academy of Pediatrics teaches parents to test tub water with the inside of the wrist or elbow; it should feel "warm, not hot." "Never bathe a baby under running water" because pipe water temperatures fluctuate and even small changes can cause burns. Washington State (US) passed a law in 1983 requiring new water heaters to be factory-set at 49 ℃. By 1988, average home hot water temperatures dropped from 61 ℃ (in 1977) to 50 ℃. Hospitalizations for tap water burns in children dropped from 5.5 per year in the 1970s to 2.4 per year. Burn area, skin grafting, mortality, and hospital stay duration all decreased. This was a before-and-after comparison. Australia regulates bathroom tap water to a maximum of 50 ℃. In New South Wales from 1989 to 1996, hospitalizations for burns in children aged 0-4 dropped 13%. Severe burns requiring 10+ days of hospitalization dropped 30% in the latter two years of the second period. In three Chinese statistics on pediatric burn hospitalizations, scalds from hot liquids accounted for 87.6% to 90.6%, with children under 3 being the most affected.
Before traveling, check the Ministry of Foreign Affairs security warnings; do not go to places marked "do not travel for the time being"
A

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs (China) categorizes overseas security risks into four levels, the highest being "do not travel for the time being." Since September 15, 2026, avoiding high-risk countries and regions has been codified in administrative regulations. Staff will remind you during document processing and at border exits, and will advise against travel when necessary. Checking the page takes only a few minutes before you go.
Free. It takes just a few minutes to browse the China Consular Service website.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs publicly issues overseas security warnings based on risk levels. From low to high, there are roughly four levels: "be aware of safety," "enhance security precautions," "travel with caution," and "do not travel for the time being." New regulations effective September 15, 2026, codify individual obligations into administrative law. Original text: "Chinese citizens shall pay attention to overseas security warnings and travel risk notifications for destinations, and avoid traveling to or staying in high-risk countries or regions." The regulations also require immigration authorities (at document issuance and border control) to remind those planning to visit high-risk areas. Original text: "For Chinese citizens preparing to travel to countries or regions with the highest risk level, or places where incidents seriously threatening life safety occur suddenly and frequently, they shall be dissuaded from traveling when necessary."

Save the 12308 number and the consular protection number of the embassy or consulate at your destination in your phone, and keep a physical copy in your wallet; do not wait for an emergency to look for them
A

In case of an emergency, first call the global consular protection hotline of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (China). Within the country, call 12308; from abroad, call +86-10-12308. Since its launch, this hotline has received over 3 million calls. During the same period, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and overseas representative offices have handled over 500,000 consular protection cases.
Free. Saving two numbers and making a copy takes only a few minutes.

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs operates a 24-hour global emergency hotline for consular protection and services. Within the country, dial 12308. From abroad, dial +86-10-12308 or +86-10-65612308. Since its launch in 2014, the hotline has received a total of over 3 million calls. During the same period, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and overseas representative offices have handled over 500,000 consular protection cases of various types.
Understand what consular protection can and cannot do: they can visit you, but cannot get you out, and you must still pay your own costs
A

If you are arrested abroad, what the (Chinese) embassy or consulate can do is: clarify the situation with the host country, request fair treatment according to the law, visit you, and attend court hearings. They cannot change a sentence for you, nor can they bring you home. Costs for accommodation, travel, and medical treatment advanced by others must ultimately be paid by you. Therefore, before going abroad, prepare funds and insurance; do not use "the state will take care of it if something happens" as your plan.
Free. Spend a few minutes reading to understand these boundaries.

When you are arrested, the embassy or consulate can perform several tasks. They clarify the situation with the relevant authorities of the host country and request fair treatment according to the law. The original text of the regulations states: "in accordance with the laws of the receiving state and international treaties signed or participated in by our country and the receiving state, visit or contact the person, understand their needs, and request the relevant authorities of the receiving state to provide the Chinese citizen with humane and fair treatment." Simply put: the embassy or consulate relies on the laws of the host country and signed treaties to visit you, contact you, ask what you need, and request the host country to treat you according to humane and fair standards. During trial, the embassy or consulate may attend court hearings and request that your procedural rights be guaranteed. If you are injured or encounter a natural disaster, they can urge the host country to provide emergency relief and help the family with funeral arrangements. However, regarding costs, the regulations are equally clear: "Chinese citizens, legal persons, and non-legal person organizations that receive items and services such as food, accommodation, travel, and medical care provided by a third party during the process of consular protection and assistance must pay the portion of the costs they are responsible for." Costs for accommodation, travel, and medical treatment advanced by others remain your responsibility to pay.
Purchase an insurance package that covers overseas medical treatment and medical evacuation; do not just buy flight delay insurance
C

Overseas medical treatment must be paid for out of pocket. Domestic (Chinese) medical insurance almost never covers it, and embassies or consulates do not provide advances. What can truly bankrupt a family is not outpatient fees, but hospitalization after a serious injury and repatriation, which requires a private jet or medical escort. When buying travel insurance, primarily look at two limits: overseas medical expenses, and emergency medical evacuation and repatriation.
A short-term overseas travel insurance package costs between a few dozen to a few hundred yuan.

Overseas medical treatment costs must be paid by oneself. Domestic medical insurance almost never covers overseas costs. Consular protection also does not advance these funds; see item 3 (what consular protection can and cannot do). The basis is Article 26 of the regulations. What truly bankrupts a family is not outpatient fees, but hospitalization after a serious injury and medical evacuation. Transferring a patient from an overseas hospital back home requires a private jet or medical escort, which is among the most expensive out-of-pocket items. According to the US CDC, emergency medical evacuation from a remote location to a good hospital can cost over $100,000 if paid out of pocket. When purchasing insurance, prioritize two limits. One is the limit for overseas medical expenses. The second is the limit for emergency medical evacuation and repatriation, which is the maximum compensation for hospital transfers and bringing the person home in the event of an incident.
Treat all "high-paying overseas recruitment" offers as scams; if tricked into telecommunications fraud, you may be banned from leaving the country upon return
A

Be wary of unreasonably high monthly salaries, no questions about qualifications or experience, no proper contracts, being told to gather first in a border city, or having your passport held for you. In these types of jobs, neither the person nor the passport remains in their own control. If exit documents are forged, border control will block departure. Anyone who violates the law or commits a crime abroad, endangering national security and interests, may be banned from leaving the country for 6 months to 3 years upon return.
Free. The difficulty lies in personally turning down a job that looks very good.

Authorities view these cases very directly. In recent years, there has been a trend of people being "tricked into leaving the country or fabricating reasons for illegal exit to participate in cross-border gambling, telecommunications network fraud, and other illegal activities, seriously threatening the safety of lives and property of the people." This means being tricked into going out, or fabricating reasons to sneak out, to engage in gambling and telecommunications fraud. New regulations tighten both ends. At the exit end: "the reasons for applying for exit, entry, stay, or residence must be truthful and legal." Submitting forged documents or making false statements gives exit-entry management authorities the right to refuse documents and block departure. At the return end: "Chinese citizens who violate the law or commit crimes abroad and endanger national security and interests may... be decided not to be allowed to leave the country for a period of 6 months to 3 years from the date of return." Persons administratively detained for fraud to obtain documents or for illegal exit/entry are also banned from leaving for 6 months to 3 years.

Overseas cash withdrawals are limited to ⟦100000⟧ per year, totaling all cards in your name; when carrying cash through customs, the maximum is 20,000 RMB, and foreign currency over 5,000 USD must be declared
A

Overseas cash withdrawals are calculated by totaling all bank cards in your name, with a maximum of ⟦100000⟧ per year; if exceeded, you cannot withdraw for the rest of that year and the following year. Card payments are not affected. When carrying cash through customs, the maximum is 20,000 RMB; foreign currency over 5,000 USD must be declared. Failure to declare may result in a fine; hiding it is considered smuggling, and the cash will be confiscated.

Free. Before leaving, estimate how much cash is needed for the trip and use cards for the rest. The difficulty is breaking the habit: if you can swipe a card, do not withdraw cash. Anyone needing to take large amounts of foreign currency cash abroad must apply for a certificate from the bank in advance, requiring an extra trip.

The basis is the "Notice on Standardizing Large Overseas Cash Withdrawal Transactions Using Bank Cards" by the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) (China) (Document No. 29 of 2017, effective January 1, 2018). Article 1: "Individuals using domestic bank cards to withdraw cash abroad, the total for all cards in their name (including supplementary cards) per calendar year shall not exceed the equivalent of ⟦100000⟧. If the annual limit is exceeded, overseas cash withdrawals using domestic bank cards will be suspended for the remainder of that year and the following year." Paragraph 2 of the same article: "Individuals shall not circumvent or help others circumvent overseas cash withdrawal management regulations by borrowing others' bank cards or lending their own cards." Article 2: SAFE sends a suspension list to card-issuing banks daily; by 17:00 (Beijing time) at the latest on the same day, the issuing bank must suspend overseas cash withdrawals for individuals on the list. Article 3: Persons on the suspension list can bring valid identification to a SAFE branch to inquire about their overseas withdrawal details. Article 4: The daily limit per card for foreign currency cards was changed from the equivalent of 1,000 USD to the equivalent of ⟦10000⟧; RMB cards remain at a daily limit of no more than the equivalent of ⟦10000⟧. Article 6: Issuing banks, domestic RMB card clearing organizations, and individuals violating this notice are penalized according to the relevant provisions of the Foreign Exchange Administration Regulations (China). SAFE's response to reporters clarified several points. The notice does not affect individual card spending abroad. Current account transactions such as food, accommodation, travel, and shopping during tourism, business trips, or overseas study can all be paid by bank card. These expenditures do not count toward the individual's annual 50,000 USD convenience foreign exchange purchase limit. The annual limit is calculated by SAFE by aggregating data from card issuers; since real-time control would slow transaction responses, "SAFE uses a delayed control measure" (not blocked instantly). Additionally, statistics show that in 2016, 81% of overseas cash withdrawals using domestic bank cards were under ⟦30000⟧ (nationwide). Carrying cash through customs has a separate set of regulations. The new customs declaration form used from April 1, 2025, states on the back: "Each person per entry/exit may carry no more than ⟦20000⟧ RMB." For foreign currency cash upon entry, "if it exceeds the equivalent of 5,000 USD, it must be declared in writing to customs." When exiting with between 5,000 and 10,000 USD equivalent, one must first apply for a "Permit for Carrying Foreign Exchange Out of the Country" from a bank and then declare it to customs. For amounts over 10,000 USD, the permit must be obtained from SAFE. SAFE regulations state that exiting persons "in principle shall not carry foreign currency cash exceeding the equivalent of 10,000 USD abroad." Customs regulations for monitoring luggage and items state: carrying cash exceeding the specified amount requires a written declaration to customs for both entry and exit. If customs begins an inspection before the written declaration is completed, it is considered undeclared. If undeclared but not hidden, customs issues a warning and may fine up to 20% of the value. Hiding, disguising, or making false declarations is considered smuggling, resulting in confiscation of the cash and a possible additional fine up to the equivalent value.
Take photos of your passport, visa, and ID card and save them to the cloud; if lost, report to the police first before applying for a travel document
C

If you lose your passport, the (Chinese) embassy or consulate can issue a travel document for you to return home, but you must prove who you are. Having photos of the information page, visa page, and entry/exit records makes the replacement process much faster. You must also report to the local police first to get a receipt; many countries require this paper for exit checks and insurance claims. Phones are often lost along with passports, so do not only save photos on your phone.
Free. Take a few photos before you leave.

If a passport is lost, overseas representative offices can issue a travel document for you to return home, but first you must prove your identity. Whether you have clear photos of the passport information page, visa page, and entry/exit records makes a significant difference in the replacement speed. Simultaneously, you must report to the local police and obtain a report receipt. Many countries require this document for exit inspections and insurance compensation. The contact information for the embassy or consulate is the two consular protection numbers saved in item 2.
If driving yourself abroad, first confirm if the destination recognizes Chinese driver's licenses; "international driving permits" sold online are mostly worthless paper
A

"International driving permits" made through online agents have no value in mainland China. That document is a translation recognized among participants of the 1949 Geneva Convention, and mainland China is not among the 103 participants. Therefore, any such document made for you domestically has no legal effect. Whether you can use a Chinese license to drive depends on the regulations of the destination; do not drive without clear confirmation.
Free. Check the destination's regulations once before leaving.

The so-called "International Driving Permit" (IDP) is a translation recognized among countries participating in the 1949 Convention on Road Traffic. This convention was signed in Geneva on September 19, 1949, and became effective on March 26, 1952. There are currently 103 participating parties (countries and territories that have signed). Mainland China is not on this list. Therefore, China does not issue this type of international driving permit. Any domestic organization "assisting with international driving permits" has no legal effect. Whether a Chinese license can be used to drive depends on the regulations of the destination country or region. Some places recognize Chinese licenses with a notarized translation, some require switching to a local license, and some do not recognize them at all.
When using agencies for visas, overseas study, or migration, first ask if they are registered with the exit-entry management authorities
A

Starting September 15, 2026, agencies for visas, overseas study, and migration must register with the (Chinese) exit-entry management authorities. Exaggerated advertising to lure customers and providing or assisting in providing forged documents are explicitly prohibited. Be alert to phrases like "guaranteed pass," "guaranteed visa," or "let us handle the documents for you."
Free. Ask one more question about whether they are registered, and keep your documents safe.

In 2018, China abolished the industry entry permit for exit-entry agencies for private matters (opening an agency no longer required prior permit approval). Since then, the number of organizations has grown rapidly, and situations have emerged where "the number of organizations is unknown, and some provide illegal or non-compliant services, harming the legitimate rights of people traveling in and out"; authorities could not even count how many existed. From September 15, 2026, these agencies will switch to a registration-based management system. Organizations must register with the exit-entry management authority where they are headquartered within 15 days of establishment. Existing agencies must complete supplementary registration within 90 days of the regulation's effective date. Explicitly prohibited behaviors include several types. First is "posting false information or luring customers with exaggerated or misleading advertisements." Second is "providing or assisting in providing forged documents, helping others violate regulations regarding visas, stay/residence permits, passports, and other exit-entry documents or procedures." Third is "illegally disclosing, selling, or providing... privacy or personal information." Fourth is "organizing or helping others participate in cross-border illegal or criminal activities." Foreign enterprises and organizations are not permitted to provide these agency services within the territory of China.
Do not write invitation letters for strangers, and do not let others use your name for exit-entry procedures
A

If you write an invitation letter or application for someone else and the content is untrue, the person penalized is the writer. Individuals are fined ⟦5000~10000⟧, and any illegal gains are confiscated. Organizations are fined ⟦10000~50000⟧, and the person directly responsible is separately fined ⟦5000~10000⟧. One moment of doing a favor could result in you paying this amount yourself.
Free. The difficulty is having to directly refuse a request.

The writer of an invitation letter must be responsible for the truthfulness of the content. The original text: "Individuals who write false invitation letters or false application documents for others to apply for exit, entry, stay, or residence shall be fined by the (Chinese) exit-entry management authority between ⟦5000⟧ and ⟦10000⟧; any illegal gains shall be confiscated." Organizations writing false documents are fined between ⟦10000~50000⟧. Simultaneously, the person directly in charge and other directly responsible personnel (the manager in charge and the person who did the work) are additionally fined between ⟦5000~10000⟧.
Before leaving the country, send your itinerary, accommodation, and travel companions to a family member, and agree on how often to check in
C

If contact is lost abroad, family members can ask the embassy or consulate for help; they will inform the family how to report to the local police and will urge action once a case is filed. The condition is that someone at home must know where you are supposed to be and when you are supposed to be in contact. Sending flight numbers, accommodation addresses, companions' phone numbers, and agreeing on a contact frequency to one family member is sufficient.
Free. Send one message before you leave.

If a Chinese citizen goes missing abroad, relatives can seek help from overseas diplomatic missions. The original text of the regulations is "overseas diplomatic missions shall provide methods for reporting to the local police and other information to obtain assistance." After the local police file a case, the embassy or consulate will urge them to handle it promptly. Whether these assistance steps can be initiated depends on whether someone at home knows where you were supposed to be and when you were supposed to make contact.

Check destination regulations before taking medicine abroad: cold or cough medicine containing pseudoephedrine or codeine; sleeping pills, psychiatric drugs, and strong painkillers — bring in original packaging with a prescription or doctor's note, and only in personal-use quantities
A

Cold or cough medicines with over 10% pseudoephedrine or over 1% codeine are regulated as stimulant precursors or narcotics in Japan and require prior permission. Bringing more than a one-month supply of sleeping pills to Japan also requires prior paperwork; in Singapore, medicines with controlled ingredients require prior approval. Bringing original packaging, accompanied by a doctor's note, and only in personal-use quantities is the only way to avoid confiscation, fines, or even imprisonment.

Free. Check the official website of the destination once before leaving, which takes a few minutes. Anyone carrying controlled medicines must make an extra trip to the hospital for a certificate and submit an application about two weeks in advance.

Japan regulates medicine by ingredient, divided into several categories. Medicine with over 10% pseudoephedrine is considered a "stimulant raw material." Medicine with over 1% codeine is considered a narcotic. These two types require permission from the Narcotics Control Department of the Japanese Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare before entry, at least 14 days in advance. The medicine must be carried by the user themselves; it cannot be sent by mail or carried by family members. Psychotropic drugs like diazepam or triazolam do not require permission if carried in a one-month supply. Common medicines also have limits: prescription drugs in a one-month supply, other medicines in a two-month supply. Exceeding these levels requires an "import certificate" in advance. A reminder from the Chinese Embassy in Japan states verbatim: bringing medicine... into Japan illegally or against regulations, "violators will be fined, detained, or even sentenced to prison, and prohibited items will be confiscated." Singapore's Health Sciences Authority (HSA) regulations state: medicines without controlled ingredients can be brought in up to a 3-month supply. A copy of the prescription or a doctor's letter must be carried. Medicine must be in original packaging with the pharmacy label attached. Medicines with controlled ingredients require permission at least 2 weeks in advance. Exceeding a 3-month supply is prohibited in all cases, even for medicinal chewing gum. Carrying medicine for others is only allowed for prescription drugs of immediate family members. Non-compliant medicine will be confiscated and may lead to prosecution. On the Chinese side, the Customs Law (China) requires personal items carried during entry/exit to be "limited to reasonable personal-use quantities." Narcotics and Category I psychotropic drugs, with a hospital diagnosis and ID documents, can be carried in the maximum quantity of a single prescription. Customs allows passage based on the principle of reasonable personal use.

When returning to China from abroad, do not bring meat or meat products (including ham and vacuum-packed jerky), cheese, fresh fruit, or seeds; if carrying animal or plant products, use the Red Channel to declare
A

When returning to China, meat — whether raw or cooked — is prohibited; this includes ham, jerky, and sausages, no matter how tightly sealed. Cheese, butter, fresh eggs, fresh fruits, vegetables, and seeds are also on the prohibited list. Bringing them in will result in return or destruction. Carrying animal or plant products without declaring can also lead to fines, with a maximum of ⟦5000⟧.
Free. Avoid these items when buying specialties abroad, and check your luggage once before returning. If unsure about an item, go through the Red Channel at customs and wait in line a bit longer.

In 2021, the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs and the General Administration of Customs (China) published a list of prohibited items. Carrying items in person, in checked luggage, by mail, by express delivery, or purchasing directly through cross-border e-commerce all fall within the scope of this list. The most relevant categories for regular tourists are as follows. The first category is meat, verbatim: "meat (raw or cooked) (including internal organs) and meat products"; the list has no exceptions for packaging methods. The second category is milk and eggs, including cream, butter, cheese, condensed milk, as well as century eggs, salted eggs, and mayonnaise. The third category is "fresh fruits and vegetables" and cut fresh flowers. The fourth category is seeds, seedlings, and other plant materials capable of propagation. The fifth category is live animals, except for cats and dogs. Bird's nests are also prohibited, except for canned bird's nests that have undergone commercial sterilization. Article 29 of the Law on the Entry and Exit Animal and Plant Quarantine (China) clearly states that bringing items on the list into the territory shall be "handled by return or destruction." Animal and plant products not on the list can be brought in but must be declared. Customs measures for supervising luggage and items specify that animal and plant products must be declared in writing to customs. If customs begins inspection before the written declaration is completed, it is considered non-declaration. The measures also state verbatim: "If customs regulations are unclear or you do not know which channel to choose, you must choose the 'Red Channel'." Sanctions for non-declaration are found in Article 39 of the Quarantine Law: "failure to declare for quarantine" results in a fine. Article 59 of the Implementation Regulations of the Quarantine Law sets this fine at ⟦5000⟧ or less.
Before entering a karaoke bar, bar, or escape room, look up to see where the emergency exits are; if that exit is locked or blocked, change to another establishment
A

According to regulations (China), entertainment venues must keep evacuation routes and emergency exits clear during business hours: they must not be obstructed, locked, blocked by objects, or have their signs covered. Internet cafes are also prohibited from blocking doors or locking windows. Failure to comply is illegal, and you can report it. If a karaoke room is in a basement with only one exit and corridors are piled with stuff, switch to another place.
Free. Spend 10 seconds looking up when entering.

This is a statutory obligation of the business owner. Failure to comply is illegal, and you can report it. The regulations state verbatim: "During business hours, entertainment venues must ensure that evacuation routes and emergency exits are clear; they must not block or lock evacuation routes and emergency exits, and must not place barriers or other obstacles that affect evacuation at evacuation routes and emergency exits." The regulations also require that "conspicuous signs must be placed at evacuation routes and emergency exits, and signs must not be obstructed or covered." The same applies to internet cafes, which are required "during business hours to prohibit blocking or locking entrance doors, windows, safe evacuation routes, and emergency exits," and "prohibit lighting with open flames and prohibit smoking."
Demand a price list before ordering: entertainment venues are required to post prices, do not accept the "play first, pay later" approach
A

According to regulations (China), entertainment venues selling services or goods must clearly post prices and proactively provide the price list for you to see. So-called "sky-high price alcohol" scams often happen when customers haven't seen the price list and are charged based on verbal quotes at checkout. Upon entering a room, demand the menu and take a photo first; after ordering, ask for a confirmation list. If a payment dispute arises, call 12315 (China) immediately on-site.
Free. Open your mouth to ask for the menu once. The difficulty lies in the potential embarrassment of asking for prices in front of others.

The regulations state verbatim: "Entertainment venues providing entertainment services and selling goods must clearly post prices and provide the price list for consumers to see; they must not coerce or deceive consumers into receiving services or purchasing goods." Violations of price laws are penalized by relevant authorities according to the law. Common "sky-high price alcohol" disputes involve not providing a price list and then charging based on verbal quotes. This advice is based on the author's experience; no official statistics were found.
If someone brings out "stuff" in a venue, get up and leave immediately; harboring or providing is not "helping a friend"
A

Entertainment venues (China) are not allowed to sell drugs, provide drugs, or allow others to use them there. Violations result in suspension of business for rectification for 3 to 6 months, or revocation of the license in severe cases. Allowing others to "use a little" in a karaoke room you booked or where you stay can constitute the crime of harboring others to use drugs. If someone takes out unknown powders, tablets, or e-cigarette tips and invites you to try, leave immediately.
Free. Get up and walk out. The difficulty lies in leaving the table in front of the whole group.

Regulations (China) explicitly prohibit entertainment venues from "selling or providing drugs, or organizing, coercing, instigating, enticing, deceiving, or harboring others to smoke or inject drugs." Employees are also prohibited from using drugs or facilitating the above actions for customers. Violations lead to public security organs confiscating illegal gains and property, and forcing business suspension for 3 to 6 months. Serious circumstances lead to the revocation of the entertainment business license. Regulations also require warning signs prohibiting drugs, gambling, and prostitution to be hung in conspicuous places in halls, karaoke rooms, and private rooms, along with reporting hotlines. Regarding individuals: the Criminal Law (China) stipulates that "harboring others to smoke or inject drugs shall be punished by fixed-term imprisonment of up to three years, criminal detention, or public surveillance, and a fine." Judicial interpretations by the Supreme People's Court (China) list cases for prosecution, including: harboring multiple people at once, harboring multiple times within two years, harboring minors, or harboring for profit. If it does not reach the level of a crime, according to the Public Security Administration Punishment Law of China, it results in administrative detention for 10 to 15 days and a possible fine of up to ⟦3000⟧. Minor circumstances result in up to 5 days of detention or a fine of up to ⟦1000⟧. Smoking or injecting drugs itself also results in 10 to 15 days of detention and a possible fine of up to ⟦3000⟧.
Do not eat candy or snacks given by strangers, do not drink beverages that have left your sight, and do not accept e-cigarette tips offered by others
A

Modern drugs do not look like drugs. "High" e-cigarettes mixed with synthetic cannabinoids look almost identical to regular ones; some people specifically offer them to others in bars, KTVs, and hotels. In China, deceiving others into smoking them results in 10 to 15 days of detention and a fine; smoking them yourself also leads to detention, though being deceived may result in a lighter penalty or no fine. If a drink has left your sight, get a new glass.
Free. Do not accept anything offered by anyone. If your glass has left your sight, change it.

Modern drugs do not look like drugs. Since July 1, 2021, the entire class of synthetic cannabinoids has been placed under control as a group, and this entire large group is regulated as narcotics (China). Some people mix them into e-liquid to make "high" e-cigarettes. In a case reported by the Supreme People's Procuratorate (China), investigators described this e-liquid as "capable of having food coloring added to create various colors and flavors," and "outwardly basically identical to regular e-cigarettes." Sellers entice friends and solicit in bars, KTVs, and hotels, tricking others into smoking. According to the article, in cases handled locally that year, minors accounted for nearly four-tenths of users. Etomidate was added to the Category II psychotropic drug list starting October 1, 2023. Deceiving others into use is itself a violation. Enticing, instigating, deceiving, or coercing others to smoke or inject drugs results in 10 to 15 days of detention and a fine of ⟦1000~5000⟧. If it constitutes a crime, the penalty is up to 3 years; 3 to 7 years for serious circumstances; 3 to 10 years for coercion; and harsher penalties if targeting minors. Smoking or injecting drugs yourself results in 10 to 15 days of detention and a possible fine of up to ⟦3000⟧. Minor circumstances result in up to 5 days of detention or a fine of up to ⟦1000⟧. If coerced or deceived into use, the same law stipulates "lighter punishment, mitigated punishment, or no punishment." One may also be simultaneously banned from entertainment venues for 6 months to 1 year. Addicts are forced into 3 years of community-based drug rehabilitation. Refusing community rehab or using again during that period results in 2 years of compulsory isolated drug rehabilitation, which can be extended by a maximum of 1 year (national China, Public Security Administration Punishment Law applicable from January 2026).
Do not play script-based role-playing games or escape rooms located in apartment buildings, residential housing, or from the second basement level downwards
A

A 2022 notice from five ministries (China) clearly states: script-based role-playing businesses must not be opened in residential housing, nor from the first basement level downwards (excluding B1). These places are often dark with narrow passages, some decorated with flammable materials, and evacuation routes may be locked or blocked, making escape very difficult during a fire. Before booking, check the address and floor on review sites; if it doesn't comply with regulations, change locations.
Free. Ask one question before booking: what floor is the address on.

A 2022 special notice from five ministries (China) is very specific: "Script-based role-playing business venues shall not be located in residential housing, below the first basement level of a building (excluding the first basement level), and similar locations." The notice also requires these venues to implement the requirements of the Work Safety Law and the Fire Protection Law (China), "regularly identifying, inspecting, and rectifying fire hazards themselves, and improving the ability to organize evacuation and extinguish early-stage fires in emergencies." The same notice also requires scripts to indicate appropriate ages. Scenes inappropriate for minors must not allow minors to enter. Except for statutory holidays, weekends, and winter/summer breaks, script-based role-playing games must not be provided to minors. At the end of 2021, fire protection and cultural tourism authorities in Qingpu District, Shanghai inspected 13 such establishments. The results stated these places were often dark with cramped passages, and had issues such as flammable decorations and locked or occupied evacuation routes.
If your mood is bad enough to be depression, walk or jog; the antidepressant effect increases with exercise intensity
A

For people with major depression, brisk walking or slow jogging shows the most significant improvement. This is followed by yoga, strength training, tai chi, and qigong, with little difference between these. Higher intensity yields better results; strength training and yoga are the easiest to maintain. Evidence quality in this area is still low, but what is certain is that movement is better than no movement; choose an activity you can stick with.
Free. About half an hour each time. The difficulty is that when your mood is bad, you are least likely to move, so you must give yourself a push.

This is a meta-analysis of 218 randomized controlled trials (RCTs), including 495 groups and 14,170 participants meeting clinical criteria for major depression. Exercise modalities were compared against each other (Bayesian network meta-analysis). The comparison groups were usual care and placebo pills (active control). Effect size was calculated using Hedges' g, where more negative numbers indicate greater symptom reduction. Brisk walking or jogging −0.62 (95% CI −0.80 to −0.45). Yoga −0.55 (95% CI −0.73 to −0.36). Strength training −0.49 (95% CI −0.69 to −0.29). Mixed aerobics −0.43 (95% CI −0.61 to −0.24). Tai chi or qigong −0.42 (95% CI −0.65 to −0.21). The article states verbatim that "the effect of exercise was proportional to the intensity prescribed": the higher the intensity, the better the effect. Strength training and yoga were the best tolerated and easiest to maintain.
Anxiety affecting your life: Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction classes are as effective as commonly used anti-anxiety medications
A

People diagnosed with anxiety disorders who took an 8-week Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) class saw symptom improvements nearly equal to taking the anti-anxiety drug escitalopram. Nearly eight-tenths of those taking the medication experienced side effects, causing some to quit. Only about 15% of those in the class experienced side effects, and none quit. It must be a standard 8-week course; a random meditation app does not count.
Registering for the class costs some money. An 8-week course, one class per week, with daily practice at home. The difficulty is practicing every day for 8 consecutive weeks.

This was a trial conducted at 3 urban academic medical centers in the US to see if the class was non-inferior to medication (non-inferiority randomized controlled trial). 276 adults diagnosed with anxiety disorders were randomly assigned to two groups in a 1:1 ratio. One group took an 8-week MBSR course. The other group took escitalopram (flexible dose 10 to 20 mg). 208 people completed the trial. At the end, based on anxiety severity scores rated by doctors (Clinical Global Impression-Severity scale), the mindfulness group decreased by 1.35 and the medication group by 1.43. The difference between the two groups was −0.07 (95% CI −0.38 to 0.23; P = 0.65, meaning this difference is indistinguishable from no difference). The lower bound of this interval did not cross the pre-defined "not considered inferior" line (non-inferiority margin −0.495). Side effects differed greatly: in the medication group, 78.6% experienced at least one trial-related side effect, and 10 people withdrew because of them. In the mindfulness group, it was 15.4%, and no one withdrew for this reason.
To calm down immediately on the spot: practice "cyclic sighing" for 5 minutes — inhale twice, then a long exhale
B

Practicing breathing for 5 minutes daily for one month improves mood and slows breathing rate better than mindfulness meditation of the same duration. Among several breathing techniques, "cyclic sighing," which emphasizes a prolonged exhale, is the best. Method: take a breath through the nose, take another short breath to fill the lungs, then exhale everything very slowly through the mouth. This is only one trial and relies on self-reporting, but it is free.
Free. 5 minutes per day.

This was a randomized controlled trial conducted at home, comparing three types of 5-minute daily breathing exercises with mindfulness meditation of the same duration over 1 month. The three breathing types were: cyclic sighing (emphasizing prolonged exhalation), box breathing (equal duration inhale, hold, exhale), and cyclic hyperventilation with retention (long inhale, short exhale). Aggregating individual data from each session (mixed-effects model), all breathing exercises were better than mindfulness meditation, especially cyclic sighing, which focuses on the exhale. This type was better both for improving mood (P < 0.05) and reducing respiratory rate (P < 0.05).
Treat "regularly meeting people" as a health expense; do not only seek others when in a bad mood
A

People who have very little social interaction on a daily basis have a mortality risk about three-tenths higher during the same period. Those who feel lonely are about one-quarter higher, and those living alone are about three-tenths higher, with the effect being more pronounced for those under 65. These are all observational tracking data; it is also possible that people with poor health are more likely to live alone.
Costs a small amount of money, plus time for meeting. The difficulty lies in proactively making appointments even when in a good mood.

This is the pooled result of 70 studies that recorded initial status and followed up later (meta-analysis), totaling 3.4 million participants with an average follow-up of 7 years. Social isolation, feelings of loneliness, and living alone were all associated with higher mortality rates. After adjusting for confounding factors such as age and health status, the weighted average odds ratios (OR) were: social isolation 1.29, loneliness 1.26, and living alone 1.32. Translated, the probability of death during the same period was higher by about three-tenths, about one-quarter, and about three-tenths, respectively. The effect sizes of the three factors were nearly identical, and larger in the under-65 group than in the elderly group.
Consider greenery around the house when choosing a residence, but do not expect "visiting parks often" to make you live longer
A

The more greenery within 500 meters of a residence, the lower the mortality risk during the same period; calculated by vegetation index, each 0.1 increase corresponds to about 4% lower risk. What was measured was greenery around the residence, not the number of times you visit a park. People living in green areas are often wealthier, and the air quality is better. Therefore, do not interpret this as visiting parks leads to longevity; simply factor in the greenery around the house when choosing a place to live.
No cost. Conveniently check the surrounding greenery when viewing a house.

This is the pooled result of 9 studies tracking groups of people for many years (meta-analysis of cohort studies), across 7 countries, involving 8.32 million people. The factor examined was the level of greenery within 500 meters of the residence, measured by the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI, a value converted from ground green cover).
