For every 0.1 unit increase in the greenery index, the pooled hazard ratio (HR) for all-cause mortality was 0.96 (95% CI 0.94 to 0.97). The probability of death during the same period was about 4% lower, with the true value roughly between 3% lower and 6% lower. 7 out of 9 studies found that more greenery was associated with lower mortality rates, and the difference did not appear to be due to chance. The remaining 2 studies found no correlation.
Do not soak in hot springs, use saunas, or soak in hot tubs at home after drinking alcohol
B

In Finland, half of the people who died in saunas had consumed alcohol. In Tokyo, about one-quarter of people who died while bathing and underwent an autopsy had significant blood alcohol levels; in a set of bathtub drowning records, drunkenness was the most common contributing factor. Japanese official agencies include "do not soak in the tub after drinking" in their key points for drowning prevention. If your companions have drunk a lot, do not let them soak alone.

No cost. If you have been drinking, wait for another day to soak; just take a quick shower at home. The difficulty is that hot springs and saunas are often the "second round" after a drinking session with a group; you must speak up and decline to go.

Finland examined every death in saunas from 1990 to 2002, based on police and forensic reports. This type of death occurs at a rate of fewer than 2 per 100,000 people per year; the original article stated "overall, 50% were under the influence of alcohol." The authors noted that alcohol-related risks are increasing, and prevention focuses on drinking less and not leaving intoxicated people alone in saunas. Tokyo forensic examiners handled 3,289 deaths while bathing from 2009 to 2011. Among 550 autopsied cases, 140 had blood alcohol levels above 0.5 mg per ml, accounting for about one-quarter. Another set of autopsy records in Tokyo included 77 bathtub drowning deaths; among the factors contributing to drowning, drunkenness was the most frequent (25 cases), followed by heart disease (22 cases). A December 2025 reminder notice from the Consumer Affairs Agency of Japan stated that in 2024, Japan had 7,776 bathtub drowning deaths, of which 7,363 were aged 65 or older. Key points for accident prevention noted: do not soak in the tub immediately after eating, drinking alcohol, or taking medication. The Chinese Embassy in Japan reminded that "one should not take a soak after drinking alcohol," because "soaking after drinking can easily cause acute heart or vascular system diseases." A public health article from the Shaanxi Provincial Health Commission (China) stated that soaking in hot springs after drinking alcohol causes blood vessels to dilate, which can lead to a drop in blood pressure, hypoglycemia, or even fainting.
Wear a helmet when skiing, snowboarding, rollerblading, or mountain biking
A

Wearing a helmet while skiing or snowboarding reduces the risk of head injury during falls or collisions by about one-third; for children under 13, it is about six-tenths lower. Wearing a helmet while cycling reduces serious head injuries by about seven-tenths and fatal head injuries by about two-thirds. Wearing a helmet does not make the neck more prone to injury.
Buying one costs a few hundred yuan. Putting it on and fastening the strap takes a few seconds each time.

Skiing and snowboarding data are taken from a meta-analysis of 12 studies. Most studies compared people with head injuries to others to see who was wearing a helmet (case-control studies). Helmet wearers had a head injury odds ratio (OR) of 0.65 (95% CI 0.55 to 0.79), about 35% lower. In studies involving children under 13, the OR was 0.41 (0.27 to 0.59), about 59% lower. Neck injury OR was 0.89 (0.72 to 1.09), showing no increase. Cycling data are taken from 40 studies involving over 64,000 people who fell or were in collisions. Head injury OR was 0.49 (0.42 to 0.57), about 51% lower. Serious head injury OR was 0.31 (0.25 to 0.37), about 69% lower. Fatal head injury OR was 0.35 (0.14 to 0.88), about 65% lower. Facial injury OR was 0.67 (0.56 to 0.81), about 33% lower. Neck injury OR was 0.96 (0.74 to 1.25), showing no correlation. The Beijing Municipal Bureau of Sports (China) stated that the 2017 revised local standards for Beijing ski resorts require wearing a helmet to enter high-level slopes.
If you are under 16, "working for hire" is not an option: employers are fined ⟦5000⟧ per month, and those willing to hire are all illegal employers
A

Finishing middle school usually happens at age 15 to 16, exactly at this threshold. If you are under 16, except for special recruitment by arts or sports units, any unit that hires you is breaking the law and will be fined ⟦5000⟧ per child laborer per month. Therefore, places willing to hire you are all operating illegally. If something happens, medical expenses and compensation can only be claimed from that specific unit.
No cost. Takes one minute to calculate how old you are.

Compulsory Education Law (China) Article 11: "When children reach the age of 6, their parents or other legal guardians shall send them to school to receive and complete compulsory education." Article 14: "Employers are prohibited from recruiting children and adolescents of compulsory education age." Article 58: If there is no justifiable reason for not sending children or adolescents of school age to school according to this law, the local township government or county-level education administrative department shall "criticize, educate, and order correction within a time limit." Provisions on the Prohibition of Using Child Labor (China) Article 2: State organs, social organizations, enterprises, public institutions, private non-enterprise units, or individual industrial and commercial households "shall not recruit minors under the age of 16." Article 6: "A fine of ⟦5000⟧ per month shall be imposed for each child laborer used"; if not corrected after the deadline, the fine is ⟦10000⟧ per person per month. Article 7: Anyone who introduces a child to work shall be "fined ⟦5000⟧ for each person introduced." Article 10: If a child laborer falls ill or is injured, the employer "must be responsible for sending them to a medical institution for treatment and bear all medical and living expenses during the treatment period"; in case of disability or death, a lump-sum compensation must also be paid. Article 13 leaves only one exception: arts and sports units, with the consent of parents or other guardians, may recruit professional artists or athletes under the age of 16 (National).
Include "is schooling useful" in the mortality ledger: for every additional year of education, the risk of adult mortality decreases by about 1.9%
A

For every additional year of education, the risk of mortality in adulthood is on average about 1.9% lower. This is most evident in people aged 18 to 49, where each year is about 2.9% lower; for those over 70, it is only 0.8% lower. People who can study continuously often have better initial conditions, so it is impossible to isolate exactly how much is due solely to schooling.

No cost. What must be spent is the time and effort of several additional years of study; for tuition fees, see item 4 of this chapter (vocational secondary school tuition and study subsidies). The difficulty lies in studying continuously without dropping out midway.

Collected all previous studies and calculated a combined result (systematic review and meta-analysis). The search range was from January 1980 to May 2023, ultimately including 603 studies, 59 countries, 70 locations, and 10,355 observations. Education and adult mortality (all-cause mortality) have a dose-response relationship (more education leads to greater reduction). For every additional year of education, the risk of death decreases by an average of 1.9% (95% uncertainty interval 1.8 to 2.0; the true value lies roughly in this range). For those aged 18 to 49, it decreases by 2.9% (2.8 to 3.0) per year. For those over 70, it decreases by 0.8% (0.6 to 1.0). No difference was found between men and women. No difference was found when categorized by the country's development level (Socio-demographic Index).

Before concluding that "degrees are devalued," look at the national educational structure first: for every 100,000 people, only 15,467 have a university degree (2020 Census; 2025 sample survey implies about 19%)
A

During the 2020 National Census, about 15% of the national population (China) had reached junior college level or higher. The 2025 sample survey implies about 19%, an increase of a few percentage points over five years. In both instances, people with a junior high school education were the largest group. People aged 15 and over have an average of only 9.91 years of schooling, just past the junior high school graduation level. Therefore, in China, the junior high school level is the most populous group and is not rare at all.
No cost. Just look through the figures below.

The reference point for the Seventh National Population Census (China) was November 1, 2020. In the national population, those with a university degree (junior college or higher) numbered 218,360,767. Senior high school (including secondary vocational) 213,005,258. Junior high school 487,163,489. Primary school 349,658,828. Compared to the Sixth Census in 2010, for every 100,000 people, the number with a university degree increased from 8,930 to 15,467. Senior high school increased from 14,032 to 15,088. Junior high school decreased from 38,788 to 34,507. Primary school decreased from 26,779 to 24,767. The average years of schooling for people aged 15 and over increased from 9.08 to 9.91 years. The illiteracy rate decreased from 4.08% to 2.67%. The reference point for the 2025 1% National Population Sample Survey was November 1, 2025, with a sample of 20.52 million people. Extrapolating from the sample to the national population gives 1,405.45 million people. Among them, university (junior college or higher) 272.33 million, senior high school (including secondary vocational) 242.72 million, junior high school 452.83 million, and primary school 331.22 million. The bulletin did not provide figures per 100,000 people. Calculating based on the total population, university accounts for about 19.4%, and junior high school accounts for about 32.2%, remaining the largest group.

If you "don't have enough money for school," check the policies first: public vocational secondary schools have waived tuition for most rural and disadvantaged students, with a ⟦2300⟧ study subsidy and up to ⟦20000⟧ in annual student loans
A

In public vocational secondary schools (China), rural students, urban students in agriculture-related majors, and students from families with financial difficulties have their tuition waived. The national study subsidy for vocational secondary and senior high school students, starting from the spring semester of 2025, is ⟦2300⟧ per year. For university, the study subsidy is ⟦3700⟧ per year, and student loans can be up to ⟦20000⟧ per year. If money is tight, calculate all these items first before deciding whether to drop out and work.
No cost. Before enrollment, go to the school's student aid management department to inquire and submit an application once.

The tuition waiver for vocational secondary education has been a policy since the autumn semester of 2012. The original text states "waive tuition fees for all rural students (including those from counties and towns), urban students in agriculture-related majors, and students with financial difficulties who are in the first, second, and third years of full-time regular programs with official records at public vocational secondary schools (except for students in arts-related performance majors)." In 2024, student aid policies were adjusted. The national study subsidy for university and junior college students increased from 3,300 to ⟦3700⟧ per person per year. National encouragement scholarships increased from 5,000 to ⟦6000⟧. These two items apply from the autumn semester of 2024 (encouragement scholarships calculated from 2024). National study subsidies for vocational secondary schools and senior high schools both increased from 2,000 to ⟦2300⟧ per person per year, effective from the spring semester of 2025. National student loans were also adjusted, starting from the autumn semester of 2024. For university and junior college students, "the loan limit per person per year increased from no more than ⟦16000⟧ to no more than ⟦20000⟧." For postgraduate students, it "increased from no more than ⟦20000⟧ to no more than ⟦25000⟧." The interest rate is the Loan Prime Rate (LPR) of the same maturity minus 70 basis points (0.7 percentage points lower) (National).

Failing to get into a regular senior high school does not mean the end of the road: vocational secondary schools have articulated recruitment and separate exams, and public institutions can lower degree requirements for skilled positions
A

The Vocational Education Law (China) of 2022 clearly states: vocational education and general education are equally important. Vocational secondary schools can have articulated recruitment with vocational colleges, and vocational colleges are required to reserve quotas or organize separate exams to recruit vocational secondary graduates. Employers are also prohibited from setting barriers because you graduated from a vocational school. If you don't have enough points for a regular senior high school, you are switching to another path, not stopping at a junior high school level.
No cost. Before filling out senior high school entrance exam preferences, check your province's vocational education recruitment website once.

Vocational Education Law of China (effective May 1, 2022) Article 3: "Vocational education is a type of education that holds an equally important position as general education." Article 37: Vocational secondary schools "may, in accordance with state regulations, in relevant majors, conduct articulated recruitment and training with higher vocational education." Higher vocational colleges "may, in accordance with state regulations, recruit students through assessments combining cultural knowledge and professional skills." Education administrative departments at the provincial level or above must establish a unified recruitment website for vocational education to aggregate and publish information on schools, majors, and recruitment, along with inquiry and registration services. Article 53: "Vocational school students enjoy equal opportunities with students of the same level from general schools regarding further education, employment, and career development." Higher vocational colleges and universities with vocational training "shall determine a corresponding proportion in recruitment quotas or use separate examination methods to specifically recruit vocational school graduates." "Employers shall not set application, recruitment, or contracting conditions that hinder vocational school graduates from seeking employment equally and competing fairly." Public institutions recruiting for positions with vocational skill level requirements "may reasonably lower degree requirements" (National).
Frame the "schooling vs. working" issue as a math problem: three years of early wages from working first, versus the annual income gap over several decades from continuing education
B

Working first allows you to earn wages a few years earlier, but this is a one-time gain. Continuing education means earning a bit more each year than those who did not study, lasting for thirty or forty years. Therefore, these two amounts must be compared side-by-side. In urban China, each additional year of schooling resulted in an annual income about 4.0% to 10.2% higher, though these figures are from before 2001 and should only be used as a rough guide.
No cost. Sit down and calculate once, takes about half an hour.

This is an estimate for urban China from 1988 to 2001. How much higher income is for each additional year of schooling is called the rate of return on education. The original text states "it rose sharply from 4.0% per year of schooling in 1988 to 10.2% in 2001." The increase mainly occurred after 1992. It reflects that the gap between what university graduates earn compared to those who did not (the university wage premium) was growing. This is a domestic Chinese scale that can be used when converting "one additional year of schooling" into an annual income difference. For the global average, see item 7 of this chapter (global average benefit of one additional year of schooling).
Remember the benchmark first: an extra year of schooling provides a global average private return (the portion that goes to your own income) of about 9% per year
A

On a global average, an extra year of schooling results in an annual personal income that is about 9% higher, with benefits for women consistently higher than for men. This figure refers to formal education; it cannot be applied directly to enrolling in a single course. Use it as a yardstick: if a course costs you ⟦30000⟧ and half a year, ask whether the change in income it brings is equivalent to an extra year of schooling.
Zero cost. Remember this number and use it as a benchmark for every "learn something extra" option.

A review covering the period from 1950 to 2014, across 139 countries with 1,120 estimates, calculated: "the global average private return of an extra year of schooling is 9% per year". Private return is the portion that falls into the learner's own income: for an extra year of schooling, average income is about 9% higher. The private returns to higher education are increasing. The social returns to education (the portion that falls to society as a whole rather than the learner themselves) remain very high. The average benefit when women receive schooling is consistently higher than for men.

Before spending money on certification exams, check if the certificate is in the national vocational qualification catalog or on the list of assessment organizations registered with the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security
A

Some organizations disguise themselves as new professions or skill levels to open classes and collect fees indiscriminately, issuing certificates rampantly; some even impersonate authorities. The Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (China) has launched a specific rectification campaign. Before registering, check in three steps: is this profession in the national vocational qualification catalog, is the issuing body an assessment organization registered with the human resources and social security sector, and can the certificate number be verified on the official website. If you cannot find it, do not register.
Zero cost. Checking once takes about ten minutes.

The Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security of China launched a specific national rectification campaign for this issue. Violations named in the document include "some organizations and units using the name of new vocational qualifications or vocational skill levels... to arbitrarily organize training, assessment, and certification, collecting fees indiscriminately and issuing certificates rampantly; some organizations and units use false or exaggerated advertising, even impersonating authorities to organize training, assessment, and certification". Measures include coordinating with cyber security, police, and market regulation departments to handle cases, "resolutely cracking down on the assessment and certification activities of organizations impersonating appraisal agencies or assessment organizations registered with the human resources and social security sector". Non-compliant advertisements on websites and social media are shut down according to the law. The document also requires "guiding the public on channels and methods to look up certificates, to self-assess whether certificates are legal, compliant, and valid".
When learning a trade, prioritize channels with state support; do not immediately pay out of pocket for commercial classes
A

From 2025 to the end of 2027, the state (China) intends to open subsidized training courses for more than 30 million people. Funding comes from various sources: employment support funds, unemployment insurance funds, corporate employee training funds... The more a profession lacks workers and the higher the training costs, the more support is provided. Those currently working should ask their employer first; others should check the support catalog of the local human resources and social security bureau before deciding what to learn.
Zero cost, or significantly reduced. Learning itself takes time. The difficulty lies in restraining the impulse to pay for a class yourself; check the support catalog first.

The scale at the national level is clear: from 2025 to the end of 2027, "focus on high-tech, cutting-edge industries and industries in urgent need, key employment groups, opening subsidized training for more than 30 million people". Funding sources are pooled into one package: employment support funds, unemployment insurance funds, industry development funds, East-West cooperation funds, corporate employee training funds... Support levels are determined by the degree of urgency, shortage of the profession (job), and training costs, differing for each profession. For enterprises, there is also a requirement to "fully set aside and use employee training funds according to regulations, ensuring at least 60% is used for the education and training of front-line workers".
When choosing a skill, prioritize seeing "if it must be done by hand and requires on-site judgment": this type is the hardest to replace with automation
B

According to estimates in the US, about 47% of jobs are at high risk of being replaced by computers; later estimates based on specific tasks show a much lower percentage. Machines find it hard to pass three gates: manual dexterity, creative thinking, and working with people. Therefore, jobs that require going to a site, working in non-standard environments, and making on-site judgments are harder to replace; fixed-process positions that primarily process information carry the highest risk.
Zero cost. Before choosing, use this criterion to evaluate the jobs you intend to learn.

Estimates for each of 702 occupations in the US on "how much probability this job can be assigned to a computer" (computerization probability assessment) found that about 47% of jobs are in the high-risk zone. In the model, what determines high or low risk are three gates that machines cannot yet pass, which the authors call "engineering bottlenecks". One is perception and manipulation, including finger dexterity, manual dexterity, and working in cramped spaces and awkward positions. Two is creative intelligence (the ability to come up with new ideas). Three is social intelligence (the ability to work with people). Therefore, work in non-standard environments that requires craftsmanship and on-site judgment always has a lower probability of replacement; it is not a coincidence for a few professions. Fixed-process positions that primarily process information have the highest risk.
Before learning, confirm if that skill is assessed by levels and if those levels can be converted into money
B

The state (China) is promoting the "New Eight-Tier Technician" system, requiring enterprises to link position salaries with skill levels; outstanding workers can even be directly recognized at a level without considering seniority. This is a policy direction; every place and enterprise varies greatly. If a skill has national vocational standards and a path for advancement, then you can talk about level-based salary increases later; check if it exists before learning.
Zero cost. Checking once is enough.

The Chinese state is promoting the "New Eight-Tier Technician" vocational skill level system. The document clearly requires linking levels with salary, verbatim: "strengthen the skill-oriented wage distribution system... guide enterprises to adopt a distribution method that dual-links position salary with position value and skill level". Localities must "increase the intensity and number of assessment and appointment rounds for senior technicians and above". Qualified enterprises can self-assess skill levels for employees. For outstanding workers, "conditions regarding years of service, levels, seniority, etc., can be broken, and the corresponding vocational skill level can be directly recognized".
Do not take "the internet says the salary is high" as a sign of labor shortage; check the shortage occupation list and local training support catalogs
C

Localities (China) provide more training support for professions based on the degree of urgency, shortage, and training costs, so looking at the support level tells you if the locality lacks people. "Profession X earns how much per month" on the internet is mostly the price listed on recruitment sites or personal anecdotes. The people you see are mostly those who have made money, and they haven't accounted for working hours, commute, occupational diseases, or off-peak and peak seasons.
Zero cost. Check two local documents.

The support level itself is the state's way of pricing "which professions lack people". Policy requires "improving the differentiated support mechanism, determined by the degree of urgency, shortage of the profession (job), training costs...", and localities rely on this to determine the scope of their subsidized vocational skill training programs. Therefore, for the same profession, the difference in support levels between cities directly reflects the level of shortage in that location.
Given the same amount of money and time, prioritize short courses that allow you to start working immediately
C

Policy (China) encourages "short, concise, fast" training courses that help with employment in a short time, and "micro-majors" in vocational schools. Choose a course based on one thing: after finishing, is there a specific job position to apply for? If a course takes half a year or a year, and after finishing you still need to "accumulate more experience", the actual time spent far exceeds the figure on paper. Before starting, write down an exit condition: at what point will you stop if you still haven't found a job.

Must pay tuition for short-term courses, the amount is not large. It takes up a block of time. The difficulty lies in stopping according to the set conditions if you don't see results halfway through.

The policy direction aligns with this: supporting "private training institutions to implement high-quality market-oriented vocational skill training programs and 'short, concise, fast' vocational skill training programs that help with employment in a short time". It also promotes vocational schools "focusing on knowledge and skills that the labor market urgently needs... opening micro-majors and vocational competency training courses".
After learning, close the book and test yourself once; do not go back and re-read
A

Compared to reading and then reading again, closing the book and testing yourself once is more effective. Adding small in-class tests results in a moderate increase in scores. When ranking ten commonly used study methods, self-testing is in the highest group. After reading a section, write down the main points from memory first, then flip back to compare.

Zero cost, and total time does not increase. Take the time originally used for re-reading and change it to closing the book and writing from memory or doing exercises. The difficulty is that self-testing immediately reveals what you haven't remembered, which feels more uncomfortable than re-reading.

A meta-analysis of 222 independent studies involving 48,478 students: in-class testing increased academic performance, with a moderate effect size (g = 0.499). The magnitude of the effect is influenced by several conditions: what study method the control group used, whether the test format matched the final exam, whether the materials matched, and whether there was corrective feedback. Also, how many times the test was repeated, where and when it was tested, how long the intervention lasted, and what experimental design was used. Another review evaluated ten commonly used study methods in turn, placing "practice testing" and "distributed practice" in the highest group (high utility). The reason is that they are effective for learners of many ages and ability levels, and have been verified in many forms of assessment and in real classrooms.
Spread the same amount of time over several days; do not study everything at once
A

For the same amount of time, dividing it over several days results in longer retention than studying all at once. There is also a usable rule: the longer you need to remember something, the longer the review interval should be. The further away the exam, the longer the interval, but research does not provide a universal number for exactly how many days apart.

Zero cost, and total time remains unchanged. Only change the arrangement: instead of 3 hours at once, split it into three days, 1 hour each. The difficulty is that you must start a few days in advance and not cram until the final night.

A meta-analysis synthesized 184 articles, 317 experiments, and 839 evaluations of the effectiveness of distributed practice. It compared two things: studying all at once versus dividing it into multiple sessions (the spacing effect), and short intervals versus long intervals (the lag effect). The conclusion is that the review interval and "how long you need to remember" together determine the level of retention on the final test: the longer the retention period required, the longer the review interval for the best retention level. Another review evaluated ten commonly used study methods in turn, placing distributed practice in the highest group (high utility).
Do not use underlining main points, re-reading, or writing summaries as your primary study methods
A

The methods most used by students are underlining main points and re-reading, but in the ranking of ten commonly used study methods, both are in the lowest group. Writing summaries, memorizing with keywords, and imagining illustrative images for the reading are also in the lowest group. They are not completely useless, but the conditions for them to be effective are too narrow; it is more worthwhile to switch to self-testing for the same amount of time.
Zero cost; in fact, it saves time. The difficulty is that these tasks are the most convenient to do and give the strongest feeling of "I am studying".

A review evaluated ten commonly used study methods, ranking them by "whether the effectiveness can be extended across different learning conditions, learner characteristics, material types, and assessment formats". Ranked in the highest group are practice testing and distributed practice. Ranked in the middle group are elaborative interrogation, self-explanation, and interleaved practice. The five methods in the lowest group are: writing summaries, underlining (or highlighting) main points, keyword mnemonics, imagery for text, and re-reading. The review clearly states: most students say they use re-reading and underlining, but these two methods do not consistently improve scores. The review suggests switching to other methods, such as using practice tests instead of re-reading.
Interleave different types of practice; do not do twenty consecutive questions of the same type
A

Completing a string of identical problems feels smooth during the process. However, mixing several types of problems for practice yields better long-term effectiveness, at a moderate level. But this method is selective about materials: it is most effective for materials where one can recognize an artist's style visually; the effect is smaller for mathematical problems; for vocabulary learning, it is the opposite, being less effective than blocked practice.

Zero cost. Change the way you use workbooks from doing them sequentially by type to mixing them. The difficulty lies in the fact that during interleaved practice, the accuracy rate is lower, which can feel like regression.

A multilevel meta-analysis of 59 studies, 238 effect sizes, and 158 samples. The overall effect of interleaved practice compared to blocked practice was moderate (Hedges' g = 0.42). Categorized by material, paintings performed best (g = 0.67), and other visual materials were also quite good. Mathematical problems had a smaller effect (g = 0.34). Explanatory texts and gustatory materials had overall effects that were not statistically significant. For vocabulary, the opposite was true; blocked practice was better (g = -0.39). Regression analysis showed that the more similar the categories are, the more different the items within a category are, and the more complex the material is, the greater the benefits of interleaving.
Do not choose learning methods based on "I learn by sight, he learns by ear"
A

Many believe individuals have unique learning styles, such as visual or auditory, and that teaching to these styles improves learning. Very few studies have rigorously tested this; almost none support it, and some even show the opposite. While people do have preferences, there is no evidence that teaching according to preferences leads to better learning; there is no need to pay for learning style assessments.
Zero cost. Simply stop choosing materials or courses based on this classification and stop paying for learning style assessments.

A review commissioned to evaluate evidence on learning styles pointed out: to prove that "teaching to learning styles" is effective, students must first be grouped by style, then randomly assigned to different teaching methods within each group. Finally, they must be tested with the same assessment. Evidence of effectiveness would be a specific type of interaction: the teaching method most effective for one style is not the most effective for another. The review's conclusion was: this type of interaction is almost never seen. Although literature on learning styles is vast, studies using standard experimental designs are extremely rare, and some of those show results directly contradicting the "matching hypothesis." Therefore, the authors argue that existing evidence is insufficient to incorporate learning style assessments into educational practice.
For content that needs to be memorized, create self-tests in the format they will be used later; do not just memorize verbatim once
A

Closing the book to self-test provides benefits beyond just the words memorized. Aggregating 192 comparisons and over ten thousand participants, it is also beneficial for modified questions, application questions, and inference, at a small-to-moderate level. However, the effect is weakest in two cases: swapping questions and answers, and content found only in the book that has never been tested.

Zero cost and no extra time required. Simply change the practice method: from "verbatim memorization" to "creating self-tests in the format they will be used later." The difficulty lies in clearly thinking beforehand how these things will be used in the future.

A meta-analysis synthesizing over 40 years of research, including 67 published and unpublished papers, 122 experiments, 192 transfer effect sizes, and a total of 10,382 participants. Compared to the control group that "reviewed once without testing," what was learned through practice testing truly transferred to other situations, with an effect size d = 0.40 (95% CI [0.31, 0.50]). Transfer was strongest in several cases: testing with different question formats, testing application and inference questions, medical diagnostic-style questions, and testing with synonymous cues. Transfer was weakest in cases such as swapping stimuli and responses, material seen initially but never tested, and worked-example style questions. Three moderators strongly influenced whether positive transfer occurred: whether the response format during practice and testing was the same, whether recall practice was accompanied by detailed feedback, and whether the first test was answered correctly. The authors also used two methods to adjust for publication bias. The effect sizes of the moderators were minimally affected, but the intercept estimate was significantly pulled down: when none of the above conditions were met, positive transfer was generally not observed.
When applying for professional titles, first clarify your system and level, then find the application channel based on your unit type
A

Professional titles (China) are divided into 27 systems nationwide, each divided into junior, intermediate, and senior levels. Usually, one must apply level by level. Those working in public institutions have their units review, publicize, and then submit the application. Those in private enterprises can go to title evaluation reception points or apply through human resources service agencies or industry associations. Freelancers apply to evaluations organized by the local human resources and social security department.
Zero cost. Check your province's application notice for the year once; it takes about half an hour.

There are 27 title systems in China, such as economics, engineering, medicine, and publishing. Titles are divided into three levels: senior, intermediate, and junior. Order No. 40 of the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (China) applies to enterprises, public institutions, social groups, individual economic organizations, and also to freelancers. Applicants usually must apply level by level. Your employer must review the application and publicize it within the unit for no less than 5 working days. Private enterprises and freelancers can have human resources agencies etc. review, publicize, and recommend on their behalf. Localities must set up title evaluation reception points in science and technology parks, high-tech zones, etc.; they can also receive applications through human resources service agencies, industry associations, and scientific societies. Freelancers who meet the requirements participate in evaluations organized by the human resources and social security department where they live. Documents verifiable online must not require separate certification. If an application is incomplete, the evaluating party must notify you once of what is missing. Employees of private enterprises usually apply where their labor relationship is located. Those sent to work elsewhere continuously for one year can apply at the destination. Retired persons cannot apply. Employees of public institutions under disciplinary action of "demerit" or higher cannot apply during the disciplinary period (National).
Junior and intermediate titles in fields like accounting are obtained through national exams: check degree and years of work experience before registering
A

In some systems (China), junior and intermediate titles are obtained through exams; passing is sufficient, with no further evaluation. Accounting is one such field: assistant accountants need a high school diploma or higher; accountants need a bachelor's degree with 4 years of accounting work, or a junior college degree with 5 years. Those who already hold certain professional certificates may also be directly recognized as having the corresponding title.
Registration fees are paid according to each province's rates. Exam preparation takes several months of off-duty time.

The 2016 Reform Opinions (China) stipulate: for fields where junior and intermediate titles are subject to unified national exams, the corresponding titles will no longer be evaluated or recognized separately. In fields where titles and professional certificates are closely linked, holding a professional certificate means recognition of the corresponding title, which can also be used as a condition for applying for higher levels. Take accounting as an example. Assistant accountants and accountants take unified national exams. Senior accountants use a combination of exam and evaluation, while principal senior accountants are usually evaluation-only. Exam eligibility is as follows. Assistant accountant: high school graduate or higher, including specialized secondary schools, vocational high schools, and technical schools. Accountant: holds a PhD; or a master's degree with 1 year of accounting work; or a second bachelor's degree/postgraduate class graduate with 2 years; or a bachelor's degree with 4 years; or a junior college degree with 5 years. Those with a professional Master of Accounting or PhD in Accounting are exempt from the "Financial Management" subject for the accountant exam (National).
Do not use intermediaries for title evaluation, do not buy ghostwritten papers, and do not forge documents: discovery leads to title revocation and a 3-year record of dishonesty
A

Professional titles (China) obtained through forged documents, ghostwritten papers, or plagiarized research results will be revoked upon verification. A record of dishonesty is kept for 3 years and uploaded to the national credit platform. If the commitment letter signed during application is untruthful, re-application is prohibited for 3 years. Human resources and social security departments also specifically handle false advertising, fake evaluations, and fake certificates from intermediaries.
Zero cost. The difficulty lies in resisting advertisements claiming "guaranteed pass for a fee."

Order No. 40 of the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (China) stipulates that anyone who submits forged documents, plagiarizes others' academic works or achievements, or uses other improper means to obtain a title will have it revoked. Simultaneously, it is recorded in the title evaluation integrity file and uploaded to the national credit information sharing platform for a period of 3 years. The 2024 supervision measures name several types of violations by applicants: untruthful commitments and falsification of information, forging papers, ghostwriting, forging achievements, and using personal connections to pull strings. A personal commitment letter must be signed at the time of application; if the commitment is untruthful, application is prohibited for 3 years. Human resources and social security departments cooperate with public security, cyber security, and market regulation to handle fake websites, false advertisements, contract traps, fake evaluations, and fake certificates from intermediaries. Serious cases involving suspected crimes are transferred to competent authorities (National).
Having a title does not mean a salary increase: clarify whether the unit evaluates and appoints based on position ratios, or if evaluation does not guarantee appointment
B

Professional titles (China) are the basis for appointment, evaluation, and promotion, but being recognized and being appointed are two different things. Public institutions applying position-based management usually evaluate within position ratios. Units not managed by position may separate evaluation and appointment; after evaluation, the unit may not necessarily provide the corresponding position and salary. Changing units or regions may require the title to be re-evaluated or re-confirmed.
Zero cost. Simply ask the unit's human resources department once.

Article 2 of Order No. 40 of the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (China): title evaluation results are an important basis for the appointment, evaluation, and promotion of professional and technical personnel. The 2016 Reform Opinions stipulate that public institutions fully implementing position-based management usually evaluate titles within the position structure ratio. Units not managed by position, along with systems with broad common use and new professions, can separate evaluation and appointment. Professional and technical personnel moving across regions or units shall have their titles re-evaluated or re-confirmed according to management authority, unless otherwise regulated by the state (National).

Should you pursue a master's degree after graduation: calculate tuition and two or three years of lost wages first, then see if your field offers extra earnings; working professionals can choose part-time programs, which have the same validity as full-time ones
B

Pursuing a master's degree requires paying tuition and losing two or three years of wages; the latter is usually the larger portion. A UK study, after controlling for family background and undergraduate results, found that at age 35, women with a master's degree earned only about 2% more, while men earned about 2% less, with huge variations by field. Working professionals can choose part-time programs (China), which have the same legal status as full-time ones but are not eligible for national student stipends.
Zero cost. Check admission notices and tuition rates once, then calculate based on current job opportunities; takes about one or two hours.

Look at costs first. A 2013 state opinion (China) stipulates that tuition for full-time academic master's degrees should in principle not exceed ⟦8000⟧ per year. Full-time professional master's degrees follow old fee policies and are not subject to this cap, often being much more expensive. Full-time students within the enrollment quota receive a national postgraduate student stipend, at least ⟦6000⟧ per year for master's students, with specific rates set locally. Then look at benefits. A study published by the UK Department for Education in 2020 used national educational and tax records to track university graduates from the mid-1990s to mid-2000s. The study controlled for family background and undergraduate results to look at income at age 35. The original text states: "we estimate returns of 2% (women) and -2% (men) for masters." Women with a master's degree earned about 2% more than those with only a bachelor's, while men earned about 2% less. Differences between fields were huge. Women with master's degrees in law, economics, and management earned about 20% more, while those in arts, English, and philosophy earned over 10% less. For men, master's degrees in most fields had clearly negative returns, but law, economics, management, and engineering remained clearly positive. Working professionals can take the exam for part-time master's programs to work and study simultaneously. A 2016 Ministry of Education (China) notice stipulates that part-time and full-time programs use the same exam and are trained to the same standards. Graduation certificates and degree certificates for both "have the same legal status and equal validity," with the mode of study noted on the graduation certificate. National student stipends are only provided to full-time students within the enrollment quota; part-time students do not receive them. In 2019, the Ministry of Education and five other departments issued a notice. Civil service recruitment and public recruitment in public institutions and state-owned enterprises must provide equal employment opportunities for students of different study modes. These recruitments must not set application conditions unrelated to position requirements. The 2021 graduate employment notice from the Ministry of Education explicitly states that recruitment notices from Party and government organs, public institutions, and state-owned enterprises must not use the mode of study as a restrictive condition. The 2022 notice further clarifies that all on-campus recruitment activities must not have such restrictions.
Should you pursue a PhD after a master's: only do it if the target position explicitly requires a PhD; calculate the psychological burden before starting
B

In the same UK study, after controlling for family and undergraduate differences, at age 35, women with a PhD earned about 8% more than those with only a bachelor's, while men earned about 9% less. The psychological burden of a PhD is also heavy: among PhD students in various countries, about one-quarter have clear depressive symptoms and about one-sixth have clear anxiety symptoms. Therefore, first check if the target job will not hire without a PhD, then decide whether to study.
Zero cost. Check the degree requirements in recruitment notices for target units, then find two or three current PhD students to talk to once.

The 2020 UK Department for Education study cited in item 24 of this chapter (master's degrees) also calculated PhDs. The original text states: "8% (women) and -9% (men) for PhDs": after controlling for family background and undergraduate results, at age 35, women with a PhD earned about 8% more than those with only a bachelor's, while men earned about 9% less. The study also found that a PhD reduces the likelihood of unemployment and annual income below £30,000, but also reduces the likelihood of annual income above £40,000. Fields vary greatly; math PhDs have particularly low returns, while psychology PhDs are among the highest. For the psychological burden during a PhD, see a 2021 meta-analysis. Across 16 studies and 23,469 PhD students, the pooled prevalence of clear depressive symptoms was about 24% (95% CI [18%, 31%]). Across 9 studies and 15,626 PhD students, the prevalence of clear anxiety symptoms was about 17% ([12%, 23%]). Results varied greatly between studies (I² approx. 98%). Domestic costs (China) according to the 2013 opinion: tuition for full-time academic PhDs should in principle not exceed ⟦10000⟧ per year, and the national postgraduate student stipend is at least ⟦10000⟧ per year.
For common illnesses, visit community health centers first, then get referred upward through the primary level; the deductible for hospitalization is calculated cumulatively
A

If you visit a community health center first and are then referred by them to a large hospital for inpatient care, the amount you must pay out-of-pocket (deductible) is calculated cumulatively rather than starting from zero again. Specific calculations are decided by each locality; Sichuan only requires paying the difference in deductibles between the two hospitals. If transferred from a large hospital back to a community health center for continued inpatient care for the same illness in the same episode, the deductible is not charged again.
Zero cost. Requires an initial trip to the community health center. The difficulty lies in resisting the urge to register directly for a specialist appointment.

When insured persons are referred level-by-level through primary-level medical institutions, the hospitalization deductible at higher-level hospitals is calculated continuously. The deductible is the amount you must pay out-of-pocket for each hospitalization before medical insurance (China) begins to pay. Documents from the General Office of the State Council (China) do not specify how continuous calculation works, leaving it to localities. Sichuan's approach is to only pay the difference in deductibles between the two hospitals: if the county Traditional Chinese Medicine hospital's deductible is ⟦600⟧ and the patient is transferred to the County People's Hospital (deductible ⟦800⟧), they only pay an additional ⟦200⟧. Inpatients transferred from higher-level hospitals back to the primary level for the same illness episode do not have to pay an additional deductible.
Within the same health insurance coverage area, the lower the hospital level, the higher the reimbursement rate; each level differs by approximately 10 percentage points
A

According to the regulations, for the same medical bill, the lower the hospital level, the higher the reimbursement rate. Localities must widen these tiers, with each level up differing by about ten percentage points. For example, for a ⟦10000⟧ medical bill, if the reimbursement rate drops from eight-tenths to seven-tenths, your out-of-pocket portion increases from 2,000 to ⟦3000⟧. The additional health insurance funds are also concentrated at the primary level.
No cost. The difficulty lies in resisting the urge to rush to large hospitals.

The document requires localities to widen the inpatient reimbursement gap between medical institutions of different levels, in principle differing by about 10 percentage points per level. Based on this gap, for the same medical bill, every time you go to a hospital one level higher, your additional payment is about 10% of that reimbursed cost. For example, for a ⟦10000⟧ medical bill within the scope of coverage, if the reimbursement rate drops from 80% to 70%, the out-of-pocket portion increases from 2,000 to ⟦3000⟧. The ⟦1000⟧ extra is only one-tenth of the total cost, but it is more than half of your original out-of-pocket portion. Actual rates vary by location, and deductibles and caps also change the gap; this is only an illustrative calculation based on the 10 percentage point level in the document. The annual increase in the health insurance fund (China) is also concentrated at the primary level.
If you want to go to a large hospital, follow the referral path from the primary level or through the hospital's referral center; do not look for appointment scalpers
A

Large hospitals leading a medical alliance must reserve a portion of outpatient slots and hospital beds exclusively for patients referred from the primary level. Hospitals must also establish referral centers or designate a fixed department specialized in handling referrals, with full coverage by 2027. Failing to register for an appointment does not mean there is no way; there is no need to find scalpers.
No cost. Requires an extra step of referral procedures.

The leading hospital of a tight medical alliance must reserve a percentage of outpatient slots and beds for primary-level institutions and promptly accept patients referred by them. A tight medical alliance is a group of several hospitals and community health centers linked together for coordination. Therefore, being referred by community health services provides dedicated slots and beds, avoiding the crowds competing for numbers in the lobby. Medical institutions must establish referral centers or designate fixed departments, with full coverage by 2027.
Before going to another province for medical treatment, ask locally first; whether the trip is necessary must, in principle, be evaluated by a doctor at the level of deputy chief physician or above
A

Whether it is necessary to go elsewhere for treatment is, in principle, evaluated by a doctor at the level of deputy chief physician or above at a secondary or tertiary hospital. Reimbursement for temporary out-of-town treatment will differ from hospitals of the same level in your insurance area; see local regulations for specifics. Asking locally before you go is better than arriving only to find it is not covered.
No cost. Ask one more question before setting out.

Whether medical treatment outside the coverage area or province is necessary is, in principle, evaluated by a person with the title of deputy chief physician or above at a secondary or tertiary hospital. Outside the coverage area means leaving the place where you participate in health insurance (China). Whether going elsewhere is necessary must, in principle, be voiced by a doctor of sufficient rank. The reimbursement level for people temporarily seeking treatment in another province maintains a reasonable gap compared to institutions of the same level in the insurance area. For the same illness treated elsewhere, the reimbursed amount will be less than at home.
After each visit, keep a copy of the medical record, test results, and diagnostic imaging
A

Viewing and copying your medical records is a right granted to you by law. Outpatient records, inpatient records, test reports, films, surgery and anesthesia records, pathology documents, and itemized hospital bills can all be copied. The hospital must designate a department or specialized person to handle this and may only charge for printing costs. Changing hospitals, seeking a second opinion, claiming commercial insurance, or actual disputes all rely on this stack of papers.
No cost. Hospitals may charge printing fees as regulated, and the rates must be public. The difficulty lies in remembering to get a copy after every visit.

Legal documents clearly state that viewing and copying medical records is a patient's right. The scope includes all documents: outpatient records, inpatient records, test reports, diagnostic imaging materials, surgery and anesthesia records, pathology materials, medical expenses... Changing hospitals, seeking a second opinion, claiming commercial insurance, or actual disputes all rely on these items.
If there are doubts about treatment, request the medical records be sealed on the spot, with both parties present, a list created, and each side keeping a copy
A

If there are doubts about treatment, you can request the medical records be sealed. Sealing must involve both the hospital and the patient, with a list created, signed, and stamped, and each side keeping a copy. If the record is not yet finished, seal the completed portion first. If the suspicion involves IV fluids, blood transfusions, injections, or medications, the fluid bags, medicine bottles, and IV sets must also be sealed together.
No cost. Request the hospital to seal them and wait for both parties to be present to complete the procedure. The difficulty lies in having the courage to say this in front of the doctor.

Regulations state that "when a medical dispute occurs and medical record materials need to be sealed or unsealed, it must be done in the presence of both the medical institution and the patient." The items sealed can be originals or copies, kept by the medical institution. If a medical record is incomplete and needs sealing, the completed part is sealed first, and the subsequent part is sealed after completion. The medical institution must create a sealing list for the sealed records, signed or stamped by both parties, with each side keeping a copy. If IV fluids, blood transfusions, injections, or medications are suspected of causing adverse consequences, both parties must seal and unseal the physical items on-site. If testing is needed, both parties jointly entrust a qualified testing organization. If they cannot agree, the health administration of the local county government designates one. If a blood transfusion is suspected of causing adverse consequences and blood needs to be sealed, the medical institution must notify the blood station to send a representative. There is also a hard constraint: "No unit or individual may alter, forge, conceal, destroy, or seize medical record materials." After sealing, if the dispute is resolved or if 3 years pass without a request for resolution, the medical institution may unseal them on its own (National, effective from 01/10/2018).
For serious illness or injury, go directly to the emergency triage desk; do not wait in line at the registration counter
A

Emergency care is not first-come, first-served, but prioritized by severity into four levels. The triage location is the desk at the entrance of the emergency department, not the registration counter. Upon arrival, immediately state the most dangerous symptom: heavy bleeding, inability to breathe, loss of consciousness, chest pain like a heart attack, or unbearable pain.
No cost. Walk a few extra steps inside to find the emergency triage desk. State the most dangerous symptom clearly in one sentence.

The 2024 Emergency Medicine Quality Control Indicators by the National Health Commission (China) stipulate that emergency triage must "categorize patients into four levels according to the criticality of the illness." "Level I is for critically ill patients who need immediate rescue." "Level II is for severely ill patients, usually evaluated and rescued simultaneously." "Level III is for urgent patients who need treatment within a short time." "Level IV is for non-urgent or sub-acute patients, treated in order in the general clinic area." Emergency triage means that upon entering the emergency department, a specialist evaluates the severity first, then determines the order of treatment. Beijing's implementation standards set response requirements for each level. Level 1: "immediate evaluation and rescue, patient moved to the resuscitation or emergency room." Level 2: "immediate monitoring of vital signs, rescue within 10 minutes, patient moved to the emergency room." Level 3: "treated before Level 4 patients, arranged to wait in the general clinic area; if waiting exceeds 30 minutes, re-evaluation is required." Level 4: "treated in order, unless the condition changes, otherwise the waiting time is quite long; if waiting exceeds 4 hours, re-evaluation is possible." In the Beijing standards, indicators for Level 1 include "acute consciousness disorder." Level 2 includes "ongoing or severe blood loss," "severe dyspnea," "cardiac-like chest pain," and "intense pain from any cause (7–10 points)." Triage must "adhere to the principle of prioritizing critically and severely ill patients," and an emergency triage area must be visible at the entrance of the emergency department (the four-level standard is national; response times are Beijing standards).
Even without money, identification, or the ability to identify yourself, the emergency room must still provide rescue first
A

The state (China) has an emergency disease relief fund specifically to pay for emergency care for two types of people: those whose identity cannot be determined, and those who cannot afford to pay. Hospitals must not refuse or delay emergency care, and emergency centers must not withhold ambulances due to money issues. So do not endure at home because of no money, and do not fear debt and fail to call an ambulance. This fund only covers the emergency portion; subsequent hospitalization still follows health insurance and medical assistance.
No cost.

The targets of the emergency disease relief system (China) are "patients with acute, severe, or critical illnesses or injuries within Chinese territory who need emergency rescue but whose identity is unknown or who lack the ability to pay the corresponding costs." The fund pays for two types of costs: "emergency costs for patients whose identity cannot be verified," and "outstanding emergency costs for patients with clear identities but no ability to pay." The document also clearly states that "medical institutions of all levels and types and their staff must provide timely and effective rescue to acute, severe, and critically ill or injured patients, and must not use any reason to refuse, push away, or delay rescue." Pre-hospital emergency care also has regulations: the national pre-hospital emergency number is "120." Emergency centers (stations) "must not refuse, push away, or delay pre-hospital emergency services for reasons of command and dispatch," nor "refuse or delay pre-hospital emergency services due to cost issues." Patient transfer follows the "principle of nearest, most urgent, meeting professional needs, and considering patient wishes" (National, since 2013).
Disability assessment must wait until treatment is finished or clinical results have stabilized before being conducted
A

The amount of compensation is mainly based on the assigned level, which in turn is based on the remaining functional impairment after treatment. Standards clearly state it must be done after treatment is finished or clinical results have stabilized. Assessing before bones have healed does not meet this requirement. Common fractures that heal well without affecting function usually do not qualify for a level.

Assessment fees range from a few hundred to ⟦2000⟧, usually advanced by the party requesting the assessment. Must wait until treatment is finished or clinical results are stable; the wait time depends on the injury and is decided by the doctor. The difficulty lies in wanting to settle quickly before the wound is fully healed; one must be patient.

The assessment principle of the "Classification of Disability Levels for Human Body Injuries" (China) is to "take the consequences or outcomes after injury treatment as the basis, and objectively evaluate the degree of tissue/organ loss and/or functional impairment." The standard stipulates the timing of assessment "must be conducted after the primary injury and its truly related complications have finished treatment or the clinical treatment results have stabilized." The standard "divides the degree of disability from human body injury into 10 levels, from level one (100% disability rate) to level ten (10% disability rate), with a 10% difference between each level." The basis for evaluation is "the degree of tissue/organ structure destruction, functional impairment, and the degree of dependence on treatment and care, taking into account the reasonable impact of the disability on social interaction and psychology." Within level ten, clauses related to fractures include the following: First, "compression fracture of one vertebral body (compression up to 1/3) or comminuted fracture." Second, "pelvic fracture in two or more places or comminuted fracture, malunion." Third, "loss of function of 25% or more in any major limb joint (except the ankle joint)." Disability at the same location and of the same nature cannot be counted repeatedly. For disabilities in two or more places, the level of each place must be recorded separately (National, effective from 01/01/2017).
If functional impairment truly remains after treatment, go to the County Disabled Persons' Federation where your household registration is located to apply for a Disability Certificate
A

The Disability Certificate is the gateway to receiving benefits for disabled persons, not an injury certificate. It is divided into seven types: visual, hearing, speech, physical, intellectual, mental, and multiple disabilities, each from level one to level four. The process involves application, acceptance, evaluation at a designated institution, public notice, review, and issuance; the card is valid for ten years and renewed for free upon expiration. If you disagree with the evaluation conclusion, you can request a re-evaluation.

The card itself has no printing fee. Evaluation fees and photo costs are in principle self-paid; those in difficulty can apply for reductions or waivers. Bring your ID card, household registration booklet, and 3 two-inch white-background photos to the County Disabled Persons' Federation where your household registration is located (China). If the evaluation passes, it is posted in the village (community) for 5 working days; the Disabled Persons' Federation completes the review within 10 working days. The difficulty lies in making several trips and waiting for a period of time.

The Disability Certificate "is the legal document to confirm a person with a disability, their type of disability, and level of disability, and is an important basis for persons with disabilities to enjoy national and local government preferential policies according to law." The evaluation standard is the national standard "Classification and Grading of Disabilities" (GB/T 26341-2010). Issuance follows the principle of voluntary application and territorial management. Persons with any of the seven types of disabilities—visual, hearing, speech, physical, intellectual, mental, and multiple—can apply, with disability levels from level one to level four. The County Disabled Persons' Federation handles acceptance and issuance based on the evaluation conclusion from a hospital or specialized institution designated by the provincial level. If the evaluation conclusion meets the standard, it is posted in the village (community) for five working days, and the County Disabled Persons' Federation "completes the review within ten working days." "No printing fee is charged for making the Disability Certificate." Evaluation fees and photo costs "are in principle borne by the applicant; where conditions permit, they may be supported by the local budget, and for particularly difficult applicants, coordination with relevant departments for reductions or waivers should be made." The card is valid for ten years and renewed for free upon expiration. If the type or level of disability changes, a re-evaluation can be requested. If you disagree with the evaluation conclusion, you can apply for a re-evaluation at the Municipal Disabled Persons' Federation within ten working days. If still in disagreement, the Provincial Disability Evaluation Expert Committee provides the final conclusion (National, effective from 01/01/2018).

To thank the doctor who saved you, write a thank-you letter, gift an embroidered banner, and give a high satisfaction rating; do not give red envelopes: the rules ban money and property, not words of gratitude
A

Giving money upfront does not buy priority: outpatient slots, beds, scarce medicines, and surgery schedules are all prohibited from being traded for benefits. Afterward, if you want to thank the doctor who saved your life, go ahead and thank them, but do not give cigarettes, alcohol, or red envelopes; it is a violation for them to accept. To show gratitude, seriously fill out a satisfaction survey once, or write a signed thank-you letter, or gift an embroidered banner.
No cost. Writing a thank-you letter or filling out a satisfaction survey takes about ten minutes.

"Nine Rules for Integrity in Practice for Medical Institution Staff" (China) (National Health Commission Document No. 41 of 2021), Rule 7: "Maintain medical order, do not undermine fairness in seeking treatment. Adhere to the principle of equality and jointly build a fair medical environment. It is strictly forbidden to use outpatient slots, beds, scarce medicines/materials, and other medical resources or the arrangement of examinations, surgeries, and other medical activities to obtain benefits or harm the public interest for personal gain." Rule 8: "Jointly build harmonious relationships, do not accept 'red envelopes' from patients. Maintain medical ethics and strict self-discipline." This same rule also clearly states "it is strictly forbidden to solicit or accept gifts, congratulatory money, shopping cards, valuable papers, stocks, other financial products, and other property from patients and their relatives or friends." Meals and entertainment paid for by patients are the same: "it is strictly forbidden to participate in banquets or travel, exercise, entertainment, and other activities arranged, organized, or paid for by them." The document also requires medical institutions to fulfill their primary responsibility, conduct supervision and inspection, and "resolutely handle violations." Satisfaction evaluation is included in the performance appraisal of tertiary public hospitals. The basis is the "Opinions of the General Office of the State Council on Strengthening the Performance Appraisal of Tertiary Public Hospitals" (General Office Document No. 4 of 2019). The document states: "The performance appraisal index system for tertiary public hospitals consists of indicators in 4 aspects: medical quality, operational efficiency, sustainable development, and satisfaction evaluation." It also clearly states: "Hospital satisfaction consists of two parts: patient satisfaction and medical staff satisfaction..." It further says to "measure the patient's sense of benefit and the staff's enthusiasm through satisfaction surveys of outpatients, inpatients, and medical staff." This evaluation also has a unified national platform: "The state shall establish a satisfaction management system for public hospitals..." The implementation schedule was: "Before the end of March 2019, all tertiary public hospitals nationwide were included in the National Health Commission's satisfaction survey platform. Localities must use the National Health Commission's satisfaction survey platform and include the survey results in the performance appraisal of tertiary public hospitals." Hospitals are also mandatory to manage complaints. The basis is Article 2 of the "Measures for the Management of Complaints in Medical Institutions" (China) (National Health Commission Order No. 3, effective 2019). Complaint management refers to patients providing "opinions, suggestions, or complaint requests" regarding medical service behavior, medical management, medical quality, and safety... Hospitals must handle investigation, processing, and feedback. "Medical institutions at the secondary level and above must establish a doctor-patient relationship office or designate a department (hereinafter collectively referred to as the complaint management department) to uniformly handle complaint management." The duties of the complaint management department include "uniformly receiving complaints, investigating and verifying complaint content, proposing handling opinions, and responding to patients in a timely manner." Medical institutions "should encourage staff to proactively collect patient opinions and suggestions regarding medical services, medical quality, and safety..." (National)
Before getting dental implants, ask clearly about the items included in the package price, prioritize facilities committed to price management, and do not believe low-price advertisements
A

After the centralized price reduction in 2023, the total cost of a conventional dental implant decreased from an average of ⟦15000⟧ to ⟦6000~7000⟧. Tertiary public hospitals charge a service fee for one implant that, in principle, does not exceed ⟦4500⟧, with the implant post and crown charged separately. Dental implants, dentures, and orthodontics are not covered by medical insurance (China), while most dental treatment items are covered in most regions.

Free. Before visiting the dentist, spend about ten minutes checking the list of facilities on the official WeChat account of the National Healthcare Security Administration (China) and asking about the price list directly.

A January 2024 announcement from the National Healthcare Security Administration (China) stated that the cost of a conventional dental implant consists of three parts. The first part is the medical service fee, charged as a package. The package scope includes "examination fees, biochemical testing and imaging fees for the entire implantation process, implant placement fees, crown attachment fees, scanning, design, and modeling fees; excluding tooth extraction, scaling, root canal treatment, bone grafting, and soft tissue grafting." "The medical service fee for a conventional dental implant at tertiary public hospitals in various places shall, in principle, not exceed ⟦4500⟧," with developed economic regions allowed a maximum 20% increase according to the 2022 special rectification notice. The second part is the implant post; in January 2023, national centralized procurement took place, with "winning bid prices ranging from ⟦548⟧ to ⟦1855⟧, averaging over ⟦900⟧." The Sichuan Provincial Healthcare Security Administration (the lead unit) announced: high-priced imported brands dropped from a median purchase price of ⟦5000⟧ to about ⟦1850⟧, and the most used brands dropped from about ⟦1500⟧ to about ⟦770⟧. The third part is the crown, with "prices ranging from ⟦100⟧ to ⟦656⟧, averaging over ⟦300⟧." A press conference in the second half of 2023 by the National Healthcare Security Administration (China) stated that rectification measures were fully implemented in all regions by late April and early May, and "the total cost of dental implants dropped from an average of ⟦15000⟧ to about ⟦6000~7000⟧." Regarding medical insurance coverage: a 1999 document from the Ministry of Labor and Social Security (China) and other agencies listed "dentures" and "orthopedic or cosmetic surgery not for functional purposes" as items not covered by basic medical insurance. In 2019, the National Healthcare Security Administration replied to a proposal from the CPPCC stating: "cosmetic medical items (including restoration of missing teeth, orthodontics, etc.) are not included in the scope of medical insurance fund payments. However, therapeutic dental treatment items are not excluded at the national level, and most local regions have already included them in medical insurance coverage" (National, as of October 2026)

If a hospital says a national price-negotiated drug is out of stock or not stocked, ask the doctor for a prescription and take it to a designated "dual-channel" pharmacy; it will still be reimbursed according to regulations
A

If a hospital says a national price-negotiated drug is out of stock or not stocked, it does not mean the drug is not covered. If this drug is on your province's "dual-channel" list, ask the doctor to write a prescription as usual and take it to a designated "dual-channel" pharmacy; the reimbursement policy is the same as buying it at the hospital. According to national documents, hospitals are also not allowed to use total medical insurance expenditure limits or drug-to-total-cost ratios as reasons to delay providing medication.
Free. You must ask the doctor for a prescription and then make a trip to the designated pharmacy. In some places, you must first complete a one-time qualification verification for the medication.

Price-negotiated drugs are medications for which the National Healthcare Security Administration (China) has negotiated prices with pharmaceutical companies and included in the medical insurance catalog. A 2021 policy explanation from the National Healthcare Security Administration stated that the catalog is adjusted once a year, resulting in drugs "entering medical insurance first, entering hospitals later," so some negotiated drugs face difficulty "entering hospitals." Therefore, the National Healthcare Security Administration and the National Health Commission (China) issued Document No. 28 of 2021. The document defines "dual-channel" as the supply of negotiated drugs "through two channels: designated medical institutions and designated retail pharmacies," "and simultaneously incorporating them into the medical insurance payment mechanism." For drugs in the "dual-channel," "a unified payment policy applies at both designated medical institutions and designated retail pharmacies." Whether purchased at a pharmacy or a hospital, the reimbursement rules are the same. Which drugs are included is, in principle, decided by the provincial healthcare security authority. Which pharmacies are included must be "timely and proactively disclosed to the public" by the healthcare security authority. Prescriptions are transmitted to pharmacies through a prescription circulation center within the medical insurance system, requiring "ensuring the smooth circulation of electronic prescriptions." Document No. 182 in September of the same year required that for negotiated drugs that hospitals cannot temporarily provide, they must "improve drug accessibility through 'dual-channel' and other channels." Reasonably used negotiated drugs are calculated separately and not included in the hospital's drug-to-total-cost ratio indicators. The document also clearly states "total medical insurance expenditure limits, limits on the number of drugs in the medical institution's catalog, drug-to-total-cost ratios... shall not be used as reasons to affect the use of negotiated drugs." At that time, it was also required that by the end of November 2021, each prefecture-level city should have at least one "dual-channel" retail pharmacy. The notice on the 2025 version of the medical insurance drug catalog (Document No. 33 of 2025 from the National Healthcare Security Administration) reiterated this "shall not be used as reasons..." statement.
