The notice also stated that, in principle, a drug should not be removed from the "dual-channel" just because it transitioned from a negotiated drug to a regular drug in the catalog. For designated pharmacies selling "dual-channel" drugs, these prescriptions "must all circulate through the electronic prescription center." The new catalog applies from January 1, 2026 (National, as of October 2026)

For chronic diseases already diagnosed by a hospital and currently stable that require a refill, you can have a follow-up online at the same hospital's Internet hospital; first-time visits for a condition are not allowed online
A

For chronic diseases already diagnosed by a hospital that are stable and using the same old medications, you can have an online follow-up with the original hospital, and the medicine can be sent to your home. Where local medical insurance has included this, it can be paid directly via medical insurance. For the first visit for a condition, or if the condition has changed, the doctor must require you to visit the hospital in person.

Free. You must find the hospital's Internet hospital portal on your phone and verify your identity once. Online follow-ups at public hospitals charge a consultation fee according to standard outpatient rates. Home delivery fees for medication are self-paid and not covered by medical insurance.

What is saved is the time spent traveling to the hospital and queuing for registration each time. The "Administrative Measures for Internet Diagnosis and Treatment (Trial)" (China) stipulates that only follow-up visits for certain common and chronic diseases are allowed online. The condition is that you have been clearly diagnosed by a physical medical institution, the doctor has access to your medical records, and the follow-up is for the same diagnosis. The measures clearly state "Internet diagnosis and treatment shall not be performed for patients' first visits." If the condition changes and requires an in-person examination, the hospital must immediately stop the online consultation and guide you to a physical hospital. Online prescriptions must have the doctor's electronic signature and be reviewed by a pharmacist before they can be entrusted to a third party for home delivery. Narcotic drugs, psychotropic drugs, and other drugs requiring special management cannot be prescribed online. For online prescriptions for children under 6 years old, a guardian and relevant specialized physician must be present. For medical insurance payments, see Document No. 45 of 2020 from the National Healthcare Security Administration (China). The document states that for follow-ups and prescriptions at designated "Internet+" hospitals within their medical insurance coverage area, consultation fees and drug costs can be paid according to local medical insurance regulations. The self-paid portion can be paid using the individual medical insurance accounts of employees according to regulations. Drug delivery fees are not covered by medical insurance. Localities can start with chronic diseases and specific outpatient diseases and gradually expand the scope of coverage. Local medical insurance agencies must disclose the list of such designated hospitals to the public. Document No. 47 of 2019 from the National Healthcare Security Administration stipulates that for Internet follow-ups at public hospitals, regardless of the doctor's rank, fees are charged at the standard outpatient consultation rate (National, as of October 2026)

When hospitalized, request an itemized bill to verify each charge; for self-paid items outside of medical insurance, ask for clarification before agreeing; if discrepancies are found, complain to the hospital first, and if unresolved, report to the healthcare security authority
A

When hospitalized, you can request an itemized bill showing the unit price, quantity, and date for each medication and test. For medications and tests not covered by medical insurance, except in emergencies, the hospital must obtain consent from you or your family beforehand. If you find duplicate charges or charges for items not performed, first call the hospital's price complaint number; if the hospital does not accept it, report it to the healthcare security authority.
Free. During hospitalization, request an itemized bill every few days; checking it takes about ten minutes. The difficulty lies in speaking up to ask the doctors and nurses.

The "Regulations on the Supervision and Administration of the Use of Healthcare Security Funds" (China) stipulate that designated hospitals must "truthfully provide insured persons with expense vouchers and relevant materials." Insured persons also have the right to request the hospital to provide them truthfully. Designated hospitals must not perform excessive testing, and must not engage in duplicate charging, overcharging, or unbundling charges. Medical services and medications outside the scope of medical insurance fund coverage, except in emergencies, must be agreed upon by the insured person or their close relatives or guardians. For violations of these rules, the healthcare security authority shall order corrections. If damage is caused to the medical insurance fund, reimbursement is required, followed by a fine of 1 to 2 times the amount of damage. Using items not covered by medical insurance without consent and refusing to correct it results in a fine of ⟦10000~50000⟧. The "Regulations on the Management of Internal Price Behavior in Medical Institutions" of 2019 by the National Health Commission (China) requires hospitals to establish an itemized billing system, including electronic bills. If a patient needs it, the hospital must print it. The bill must clearly state the name and code of the item, drug, or material, along with the unit price, unit of measurement, date of use, quantity, and total amount. Charges by disease type or DRG (Diagnosis-Related Group package payment) are not subject to this requirement. Hospitals must display consultation and price complaint phone numbers in prominent places, following a first-receiver responsibility system where the receiver must record the content and processing results. Reports to the healthcare security authority can be made via websites, phone numbers, faxes, or mailing addresses disclosed by the authority. Reports can be anonymous; for named reports, personal information is kept confidential. If verified as true, the whistleblower is rewarded according to state regulations (National, as of October 2026)

If someone passes away at home or outside, first distinguish between a natural death and an abnormal death: for accidents, unknown causes, or living alone for a long time before being discovered, report to the police immediately and do not touch the body or the scene
A

If someone dies due to an accident, for unknown reasons, or lived alone for a long time before being discovered without receiving hospital treatment, the police will issue the death certificate. If the scene is disturbed, it becomes difficult to clarify the situation and difficult to issue the certificate. Without this document, cremation, household registration cancellation, and subsequent insurance claims will all be blocked. If you cannot distinguish the type, call 110 first; the police will still issue the certificate after their investigation.
Free. Just one phone call.

Article 8, Paragraph 2 of the Household Registration Regulations (China): "If a citizen dies due to an accident or unknown causes, the head of the household or the person who discovered the death must immediately report to the local police station or the township/town people's government." This means: in case of an accident or unknown cause of death, the household head and the discoverer must immediately report to the police station or local government. Article 23 of the Funeral Management Regulations (China): "For individuals who die naturally, the medical institution shall timely issue a death certificate. For deceased persons in abnormal death cases handled by public security organs according to law who have not received treatment at a medical institution, the public security organ shall issue the death certificate." This means: for those who die of natural illness, the medical institution that treated them issues the death certificate. For those who did not receive hospital treatment and fall under police jurisdiction, the police issue it. If the scene is disturbed, it is both difficult to clarify and difficult to issue the certificate. Cremation, household registration cancellation, and subsequent insurance claims are all stuck on this exact document
The death certificate is the key to everything that follows: whoever provided treatment issues it; for natural deaths at home, seek out the community health center, issued within one day
A

If the death occurs at a hospital, go to the specific department responsible for treatment to request the death certificate. For natural deaths at home, find the community health center or township health center where the deceased resided. For natural deaths with a clear cause, the certificate is issued within one day. You need it for household registration cancellation, cremation, withdrawing housing provident funds, receiving social security benefits, insurance claims, and inheritance; once obtained, make several photocopies.
Free.

The "Specifications for the Management of Population Death Information Registration (Trial)" (China) states: for those who die in a medical institution, it is "issued by the medical institution responsible for the treatment," meaning if the death occurs at a hospital or health center, go to the place that provided treatment. For those who die naturally at home or elsewhere, it is "issued by the community health center or township (street) health center in the jurisdiction," meaning find the community health center or health center of the township or ward where the deceased lived. If public security or judicial authorities determine it is an abnormal death, it is handled by public security or judicial authorities according to current regulations and procedures. A 2026 notice from five agencies states: the death certificate "paper version and electronic version have the same legal effect," and the electronic version can be used like the paper version. For natural deaths with a clear cause, the certificate must be issued within one day of the death. If the certificate is lost, a one-time reissue can be requested from the original issuing authority. If basic information is incorrect, bring supporting documents to request a one-time reissue of a new version
Transporting, storing, and cremating bodies can only be done by funeral parlors; hospital mortuaries do not organize funerals and storage usually does not exceed 3 days
A

Transporting, storing, embalming, dressing, and cremating bodies can only be done by funeral parlors. Hospital mortuaries do not handle funeral affairs and at most allow for temporary placement of the body. Funeral parlor storage usually does not exceed 3 days; to stay longer, extension procedures must be completed. Cremation requires a death certificate and a cremation confirmation; the cremation certificate received after cremation is also needed for inheritance and insurance claims.
Free.

Article 25 of the Funeral Management Regulations (China): "Services for transporting, storing, anti-decomposition, dressing, and cremating bodies are provided by specialized funeral parlors." These tasks cannot be done elsewhere. Article 24: "Mortuaries of medical institutions shall not be leased out, shall not provide funeral services, and may provide conditions for temporary placement of bodies." Hospital mortuaries only allow temporary placement and are not permitted to handle funeral affairs. Article 27: "Funeral parlors store bodies usually for no more than 3 days; if an extension is needed, the family of the deceased or the party handing over the body must complete extension procedures at the funeral parlor." To stay for a few more days, go to the funeral parlor for an extension. Article 28: "Funeral parlors cremate bodies based on the death certificate and cremation confirmation, and issue a cremation certificate." It is not allowed without either document; after cremation, you will receive a cremation certificate. Article 29: "In areas where cremation is applied, bodies must be cremated locally at the nearest funeral parlor," meaning find the funeral parlor nearest to where the person died for cremation
If you suspect the cause of death, request and perform an autopsy within 48 hours, and simultaneously seal the medical records
A

If you suspect the cause of death, an autopsy must be performed within 48 hours after death; if the hospital has cold storage facilities, this can be extended to 7 days. An autopsy must have the signed consent of the next of kin; if they do not consent or let the deadline pass, that party bears responsibility if the cause of death cannot be determined. When requesting an autopsy, also request the sealing of medical records. Once a body is cremated, an autopsy can never be performed.
Free. The difficulty is remembering to request it at that time.

The time limit for autopsies is stated in Article 26 of the Regulations on the Prevention and Handling of Medical Disputes (China). Original text: "If a patient dies and the patient's side and the medical side have different opinions on the cause of death, an autopsy shall be performed within 48 hours after the patient's death; where conditions for cold storage of the body exist, it can be extended to 7 days." Therefore, to clarify the cause of death, an autopsy must be performed within 48 hours of death, extended to a maximum of 7 days if the hospital has cold storage. This same article also states: "An autopsy must be consented to and signed by the deceased's next of kin; refusal to sign is deemed as the next of kin not consenting to the autopsy." If the family does not sign, it is considered non-consent. It also states: "Refusal to consent or delaying the autopsy beyond the prescribed time limit, affecting the determination of the cause of death, shall result in the party that refused or delayed bearing the responsibility." Whoever does not consent or lets the deadline pass will be held responsible for the inability to clarify the cause of death later. Article 24: sealing and unsealing of medical records "must be done in the presence of both the patient's side and the medical side." Both you and the hospital must be present when the medical records are sealed and when they are opened
There is a legal time limit for canceling the household registration of a deceased person: before burial in cities, and within one month in rural areas
A

In cities, household registration must be canceled before burial; in rural areas, within one month. Bring the death certificate and the household register (hukou booklet) to the police station. If left undone, transferring inheritance, receiving benefits, and withdrawing insurance will all be blocked by the household registration status.
Free. Take the death certificate and household register to the police station for one trip.

Article 8, Paragraph 1 of the Household Registration Regulations (China): "When a citizen dies, in cities before burial, and in rural areas within one month, the head of the household, relatives, fosterers, or neighbors shall report the death registration to the household registration authority and cancel the household registration. If a citizen dies at a place of temporary residence, the household registration authority at the place of temporary residence shall notify the household registration authority at the place of permanent residence to cancel the household registration." This means: in cities, do it before burial; in rural areas, do it within one month. The household head, relatives, fosterers, or neighbors can all go to the household registration authority (police station) to report the death and cancel the registration. If the person dies while temporarily residing elsewhere, the police station at the temporary residence notifies the police station where the registration is held to cancel it
Funeral services are divided into basic and non-basic items; basic items have a catalog and prices are set by law
A

Transporting the body, storing the body, farewell ceremonies, cremation, ash storage, and ecological burial are all in the state's catalog of basic items. Storing ashes in niches provided by public facilities is also included. Prices for these items are set according to regulations; other services must also be included in a catalog, and no additional items may be created to collect fees. Before going, ask clearly which items are basic and what the local prices are before discussing other matters.
Free. Spend a few minutes checking the catalog before going.

Transporting the body, storing the body, farewell ceremonies, cremation, ash storage, and ecological burial are all in the state's catalog of basic items (China). Storing ashes in niches provided by state funeral service facilities is also in the catalog. Prices for these items are set by law and regulation, not simply decided by the funeral parlor. The catalog of non-basic items is determined by the civil affairs department at or above the level of a city with districts (civil affairs department at or above the level of a prefecture-level city)" (National, as of October 2026)
Encountering forced tie-in sales, additional charges beyond the listed price, or splitting one item into multiple fees: record and then complain
A

Price violations named in the Regulations include: failing to list price lists, charging additional fees beyond the listed price, forcing the purchase of funeral goods as tie-ins, and forcing you to accept paid services from other parties. Splitting one item into multiple fees is also a disguised price increase. On-site, ask for the price list first, keep payment receipts and messages, and it will still be in time to complain later. For price issues, find the market supervision authority; for funeral services, find the civil affairs authority.
No cost. The difficulty is wanting to calculate things clearly at that exact moment.

The Regulations (China) list five types of price violations, four of which are discussed below. Not displaying a price list or charging more than the listed price constitutes failing to clearly list prices or charging additional fees beyond the listed price. Refusing to do one thing unless another is purchased is forced selling through tie-ins or unreasonable conditions. Forcing you to take a paid service from another party is coercion, or disguised coercion, to accept third-party paid services. Changing names to charge extra is a disguised increase in fee levels. Additionally, "disguised increases in fee levels through methods such as splitting items or expanding the scope of collection" are prohibited. Splitting one service into multiple items to charge separately, or expanding the scope of collection, both fall under prohibited categories.
Intermediaries such as funeral service agents, funeral goods purchasing agents, planners, and ceremony leads must register with the county-level civil affairs authority
A

Intermediaries such as those providing funeral service agency, funeral goods purchasing, planning and ceremony leading, or information consulting must register with the county-level civil affairs authority. Parties that have not registered will not be in the funeral service information system of the civil affairs authority. Whether you can check this yourself varies by location; the surest way is to call the county-level civil affairs authority. Any party using deceptive tricks to charge arbitrary fees or selling information of the deceased will be handled according to the law.
No cost. Ask one question: have you registered?

Unregistered intermediaries are not in the funeral service information system managed by the civil affairs authority (China). Any party using deceptive means to charge fees against regulations, enticing people to hold large funerals, forcing service acceptance, or selling information of the deceased will be handled according to the law. They will also be marked in the system and made public to society, viewable by everyone.
Money scattered in many places must be withdrawn individually: housing provident fund balance, social insurance benefits, work injury insurance benefits
A

The housing provident fund balance can be withdrawn by heirs; this amount is not in a bank account and is easily overlooked. Remaining funds in personal pension insurance accounts are also inheritable. Families of enterprise employees participating in pension insurance who die from illness also receive additional funeral subsidies and survivor benefits ranging from 3 to 24 months. If death is due to a work injury, there are three separate work injury insurance payments.
No cost, but requires visiting several offices. Before going, prepare sufficient death certificates and documents proving kinship.

The housing provident fund account balance (China) (the remaining amount in the deceased's fund account) can be withdrawn by heirs or legatees. A legatee is someone named in a will to receive assets. For deaths due to work injuries, there are three specific items: funeral subsidy, survivor benefits for supported relatives, and a one-time work injury death subsidy. For remaining funds in personal pension insurance accounts, the Social Insurance Law (China) clearly states they are inheritable. For employees participating in pension insurance who die from illness or non-work-related causes, the family receives funeral subsidies and survivor benefits, collectively called survivor benefits. The rate for enterprise employees is calculated using a unified national formula. The funeral subsidy equals 2 times the average monthly per capita disposable income of urban residents in the province for the previous year. Survivor benefits also use this average monthly income as a base, paid for 3 to 24 months based on the years of contribution. Under 5 years pays 3 months, 5 to 10 years 6 months, 10 to 15 years 9 months, and for 15 years or more, 1 additional month per year, up to 24 months. For retirees, 1 month is deducted for each year they have received a pension, with a minimum of 9 months.
Accounts and personal information of the deceased: next of kin may request to view, copy, correct, or delete
A

After a person dies, the next of kin, for their own legitimate and justified interests, may request platforms to view, copy, correct, or delete the personal information of the deceased. If the platform refuses, they must state the reason. You can also file a lawsuit in court. There is one exception: if the deceased made other arrangements while alive, such as appointing an account heir or leaving clear wishes, those arrangements will be followed.
No cost. Complaints or lawsuits are only necessary if the platform does not cooperate.

The law clearly states: when an individual dies, the next of kin, for their own legitimate and justified interests, may exercise the rights to view, copy, correct, delete, etc., regarding the relevant personal information of the deceased. Next of kin can request the platform to provide the deceased's information for viewing, provide a copy, correct errors, or delete it. Article 50 requires platforms to establish convenient mechanisms for receiving and processing requests, and "if a request to exercise individual rights is refused, the reason must be stated." If the platform refuses, "the individual may file a lawsuit in a people's court according to the law."
If a relative dies leaving debts, heirs only pay using the portion of the estate they receive; to avoid liability, declare a waiver of inheritance in writing before the estate is divided
A

When a person dies, the debt does not disappear. However, children, spouses, and other heirs only pay using the portion of the estate they receive; they do not have to pay the shortfall out of their own pockets. If you do not want to be involved in this debt, you must write a declaration waiving the inheritance before the estate is divided, and you will not receive the estate either. Silence is counted as accepting the inheritance.

Writing a written declaration costs no money. The real price is that houses, deposits, and other heritage must also be given up. If you accept the inheritance, creditors can sue you, you must appear in court, and you must provide documents showing how much the estate is worth.

Article 1161 of the Civil Code (China): "An heir shall pay the taxes and debts that the decedent should have paid according to the law within the limit of the actual value of the estate obtained. The portion exceeding the actual value of the estate that the heir pays voluntarily is not subject to this limit." This means: for the deceased's taxes and debts, you only pay using the portion of the estate you receive. You do not have to pay the excess unless you volunteer. Paragraph 2 of the same article: "An heir who waives inheritance may not be held liable for the taxes and debts that the decedent should have paid according to the law." Article 1159 of the Civil Code (China) states that when dividing an estate, the deceased's taxes and debts must be paid first. Article 1124 of the Civil Code (China): to waive inheritance, one must "before the disposition of the estate, express the waiver of inheritance in writing; failure to express it is deemed as acceptance of the inheritance." Article 33 of Interpretation (1) of the Supreme People's Court (China) on the inheritance section: the written declaration is given to the estate administrator or other heirs. Article 35 of this Interpretation: if a waiver is declared after the estate is divided, the thing being waived is no longer the right of inheritance, but the property already received. Article 1145 of the Civil Code (China): heirs can appoint an estate administrator; if not, they act together. Article 1147 of the Civil Code (China): the estate administrator must inventory the estate, create an estate list, and handle the deceased's claims and debt obligations. A case in Wuzhou, Henan: a borrower died of illness in March 2023, and the children did not declare a waiver of inheritance in writing. In May 2023, the court ruled the children must pay ⟦95000⟧ in principal and interest within the scope of the actual value of the estate received. The children said the inherited company's value could not be calculated, and the judgment could not be enforced. Accounts and cars in the children's names were frozen and seized, and they were placed on the high-consumption restriction list. It dragged on until February 2025 before a settlement was reached to pay ⟦90000⟧. A case in Chongqing: a borrower died of illness before paying off the principal and interest of a ⟦400000⟧ loan; all heirs declared a waiver of inheritance. However, his wife and daughter had withdrawn his basic pension and occupational annuity, which were counted as his estate. The procuratorate determined the two had not clearly expressed a waiver and were deemed to have accepted the inheritance; in November 2025, the wife settled with the creditor and paid in full. This type of debt ranges from tens of thousands to several hundred thousand yuan, so the benefit is categorized as large.

When handling inheritance for a deceased relative, do not default to needing notarization first: if deposits do not exceed ⟦50000⟧ at one bank, go directly to the bank to withdraw; for houses, all heirs go together to the real estate registration office
A

If the deceased's total deposits at one bank do not exceed ⟦50000⟧, the spouse, children, or parents can withdraw them by bringing documents, without needing notarization. For houses, notarization is also not mandatory; all heirs can go together to the real estate registration office to process it. Notarization costs money; taking Fuzhou and Xiamen as examples, houses are charged by area, with each unit in principle charged a maximum of ⟦10000⟧.

No cost. You must visit each bank where there are deposits. For houses, you must schedule all heirs to arrive at the registration window on the same day. If someone refuses to come or disagrees with the division method, this path cannot be taken, leaving only notarization or litigation.

Regarding deposits, Document No. 18 of 2021 from the Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission and the People's Bank (China) stipulates that small deposits meeting conditions no longer require notarization. There are three conditions. First, the total balance of accounts at the same bank does not exceed ⟦10000⟧; banks can raise this themselves, up to ⟦50000⟧. Second, the applicant is the spouse, child, parent, or an heir or legatee designated in a notarized will. Third, it is a one-time full withdrawal, and the account is closed after. Spouses, children, or parents must submit four things: a death certificate; documents proving kinship such as a household registration booklet, marriage certificate, or birth certificate; their own identification; and a hand-signed commitment letter. Document Jin Gui No. 6 of 2024 stipulates that from June 1, 2024, the unified limit is raised to ⟦50000⟧. Small and medium-sized rural banks have until December 31, 2025. Gold accumulation products, government bonds, and wealth management products sold by the bank also qualify for withdrawal this way upon maturity or settlement, with the amount counted toward the ⟦50000⟧. Funeral subsidies and survivor benefits transferred to the deceased's account do not count toward the ⟦50000⟧; spouses, children, or parents can also withdraw them using this set of documents. Regarding houses, Article 14 of the Implementation Details of the Interim Regulations on Real Estate Registration (China): when applying for registration due to inheritance or legacy, one "must submit death certificates, a will, or an agreement by all legal heirs on the division of the real estate, and documents regarding kinship with the decedent..., or may submit notarized documents or effective legal documents." Notarization is only one optional method. In 2016, the Ministry of Justice (China) issued a document abolishing a 1991 joint notice that required mandatory notarization for house registration. The Fuzhou Real Estate Registration and Transaction Center has explained how to proceed without submitting notarized documents. All legal heirs or legatees must go to the registration office together to verify documents and sign an undertaking (a written declaration ensuring the documents are true). Costs based on Fujian rates: inheritance notarization not involving houses is charged at 0.8% for the portion under ⟦200000⟧, with a minimum of ⟦300⟧. Houses are charged by area; in Fuzhou and Xiamen, no more than ⟦70⟧ per square meter, with each unit in principle not exceeding ⟦10000⟧. Calculating by these rates, the notarization fee for ⟦50000⟧ in deposits is ⟦400⟧, and for a 90-square-meter house in Fuzhou, it is a maximum of ⟦6300⟧. Savings range from several hundred to several thousand yuan, so the benefit is categorized as medium.
Platforms should not collect money themselves and then transfer it to sellers; let the money pass through a licensed payment institution and pay the seller directly
A

If the buyer's money enters your account first and then you transfer it to the seller, you are performing payment services. Doing this requires approval from the People's Bank of China and a real capital contribution of ⟦100000000⟧. Doing it without approval leads to closure, confiscation of earnings, fines, and separate fines for the boss and direct personnel; serious cases can lead to imprisonment. There is only one safe way: the money does not enter your account.

No cost. It takes a little time to integrate the product of a licensed payment institution. A licensed payment institution is a company that has been granted a payment license by the central bank. Use their split-payment or guaranteed transaction functions so the buyer's money goes straight to the seller without passing through the platform's own account.

Payment services are defined by regulation as "transferring funds according to electronic payment orders sent by the payee or payer." Simply put, it is transferring money on behalf of others according to their orders. To do this, one "must be approved by the People's Bank of China and hold a payment business license." The minimum registered capital is ⟦100000000⟧, which must be a real monetary contribution, meaning this 100 million must actually be transferred to the company account. "Anyone who establishes a non-bank payment institution without approval according to the law, or engages in or disguisedly engages in payment services, shall be dissolved by the People's Bank of China according to the law, and illegal gains shall be confiscated." Doing it without approval leads to immediate closure and confiscation of earnings. If illegal gains are ⟦500000⟧ or more, an additional fine of 1 to 5 times that amount is imposed. If there are no illegal gains or they are below ⟦500000⟧, the fine is ⟦500000~2000000⟧. Legal representatives and directly responsible persons are fined separately between ⟦100000~500000⟧. The Criminal Law of China also considers "illegal engagement in payment and settlement services" as the crime of illegal business operations. Serious circumstances can lead to up to 5 years in prison; especially serious circumstances lead to 5 years or more. What constitutes "serious circumstances" has been defined by the interpretations of the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate (China). That boundary is an illegal business amount of ⟦5000000⟧ or more, or illegal gains of ⟦100000⟧ or more (national, as of May 2024).

Most websites that collect money must have a license; self-selling without allowing others to open stalls does not require one; acting as a broker to match transactions is a different license; free websites only need filing
A

Websites that collect money from users mostly must obtain a Value-Added Telecommunications Business License (China) first; individuals cannot obtain this license. The Guangdong Provincial Communications Administration (China) replied: if you only sell goods on your own website or app and do not allow others to open stalls, you do not need it. Only opening a mini-app on WeChat or Alipay or opening an online store also does not require it. If you are required to have it but don't, and still open a website to collect money, your earnings will be confiscated and you will be fined; serious cases lead to website closure.

Filing is free. A Value-Added Telecommunications Business License costs money; it determines "whether a website that collects money from users can be opened." To apply for this license, you must first have a company. For business within one province, the registered capital must be at least ⟦1000000⟧. For inter-provincial business, it must be at least ⟦10000000⟧. The review period is 60 days, and the license is valid for 5 years.

The original regulation states: "The state implements a licensing system for profit-oriented Internet information services; it implements a filing system for non-profit Internet information services. Those without a license or who have not completed filing procedures shall not provide Internet information services." If you collect money, you must have a license first; if not, you must file first; without either, you cannot open the website. What is profit-oriented? The regulation says it is "the activity of providing paid services such as information or website design to Internet users via the Internet." Simply put, it means collecting money from users. The type of brokerage that matches transactions is called an Online Data Processing and Transaction Processing service, abbreviated as EDI in the industry. Regulations define it as "services using data processing and transaction/work processing application platforms connected to public telecommunications networks or the Internet to provide users with online data processing and transaction/work processing services." it also "includes transaction processing services, electronic data interchange services, and network/electronic device data processing services." That is, the website processes online data on behalf of users or matches and processes transactions on behalf of buyers and sellers. Operating without a license or operating beyond the scope results in confiscation of illegal gains and an additional fine of 3 to 5 times those gains. Operating beyond the scope means having a license but doing work that exceeds the scope listed on it. If there are no illegal gains or gains are below ⟦50000⟧, the fine is ⟦100000~1000000⟧. Serious circumstances lead to mandatory website closure (national). Collecting money does not necessarily mean a license is required. A Q&A issued by the Guangdong Provincial Communications Administration in October 2025 stated that, according to the requirements of the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (China), the following three cases do not require this license. First, an enterprise on its own website or app "directly sells its own goods or services or those of other enterprises in the form of self-operation," and no other units or individuals open stalls. Second, an enterprise on its own website or app only posts its own information and does not provide a platform for others to post information. Third, an enterprise only does business through mini-apps, official accounts, video channels, or online stores on platforms like WeChat or Alipay, "and has no other independent operating platform." Conversely, if you allow others to open stalls or allow users to post information on your page, you do not fall into these three cases.
Doing livestreaming requires an Online Culture Business License; audio-visual program licenses are almost impossible for private enterprises to obtain
A

To do livestreaming or game commentary, you must have an Online Culture Business License issued by the provincial-level cultural authority (China), and the business scope must clearly state online performances. Results are provided 20 days after acceptance, and the license is valid for 3 years. Broadcasted videos must be self-stored for at least 60 days. Opening for business without a license leads to mandatory suspension, warnings, and fines up to ⟦30000⟧; failure to stop leads to being blacklisted.

The Online Culture Business License (China), commonly called the "Net Culture License," determines "whether you can make money through livestreaming or game commentary." Provincial cultural authorities review and provide results within 20 days of acceptance; the license is valid for 3 years and must be renewed 30 days before expiration. The audio-visual program license determines "whether programs can be broadcast on the network"; it requires the applicant to be a 100% state-owned unit or a unit where the state holds a controlling stake.

Units engaged in online performances must have a license first. The original regulation states: "must, in accordance with the 'Interim Provisions on the Administration of Internet Culture,' apply to the provincial cultural authority for an 'Online Culture Business License,' and the business scope in the license must clearly state online performances." Playing games for others to watch or game commentary is also managed this way; the original text says "managed with reference to these measures." All online performance video materials "must be stored for no less than 60 days"; you must store broadcasted videos for a full 60 days. Engaging in profit-oriented Internet cultural activities without approval leads to mandatory suspension, warnings, and an additional fine of up to ⟦30000⟧. Failure to stop when ordered leads to being blacklisted in the cultural market. Broadcasting programs on the network is a different license, "must have an 'Information Network Transmission Audio-Visual Program License'." Applicants must "have legal person status and be a 100% state-owned unit or a unit where the state holds a controlling stake," meaning it must be state-owned or state-controlled; private companies almost cannot obtain it. Doing it without this license leads to warnings, mandatory correction, and possible additional fines up to ⟦30000⟧. Serious circumstances are punished according to the Regulations on the Administration of Radio and Television (national).
Servers located domestically must be filed; apps and mini-apps must also be filed before going live; access providers must themselves have a value-added telecommunications license
A

If the server is located in China, it must be filed before opening the website; it is free and usually takes a few days to a few weeks. Failure to file leads first to mandatory correction and a ⟦10000⟧ fine; failure to correct leads to website closure. Apps and mini-apps must also be filed in advance; without filing, app stores and mini-app platforms are not allowed to let you go live.

Filing is free. Documents are submitted along with the server through the service provider, usually waiting a few days to a few weeks. App and mini-app filing is submitted through the service provider or app store; with complete documents, it is finished within 20 working days. Checking once to see if the provider has a license takes only ten minutes.

The original regulation states: "those who have not completed filing procedures shall not provide non-profit Internet information services within the territory of the People's Republic of China." Websites that do not collect money from users, as long as they are located domestically, must also be filed in advance. Failure to file leads to mandatory correction within a time limit and an additional fine of ⟦10000⟧. Intentional failure to correct leads to website closure. Providers who help you put your server online are also regulated: they "shall not provide Internet access services to organizations or individuals who have not completed filing but provide non-profit Internet information services." Providers who collect money on your behalf are the same. Regulations say this type of provider "shall not provide access or collection services to units or individuals who do not have a business license according to the law or have not completed filing procedures for non-profit Internet information services." This means honest providers cannot accept websites without a license or filing. Furthermore, renting space in a data center or cloud servers is called an Internet Data Center service in the regulations, and broadband access is called an Internet Access service. These two types themselves require licenses; the provider must have a license first. If the website homepage does not display the filing number, correction is mandated with an additional fine of ⟦5000~50000⟧. From September 2023, apps and mini-apps must also be filed. A notice from the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (China) says app supervisors providing services domestically "who have not completed filing procedures shall not provide Internet information services via APP." Distribution platforms include mini-app platforms. The notice requires app stores, mini-app platforms, and phone manufacturers "not to provide network access, distribution, pre-installation... for APPs that have not completed filing procedures." If the provincial Communications Administration receives complete and accurate documents, it "must complete the filing within twenty working days." The filing number must be displayed in a prominent place within the app. The Anti-Telecom and Online Fraud Law (China) also clearly states that establishing an app "must complete licensing or filing procedures with the telecommunications authority according to relevant state regulations" (national).
When allowing users to sell on a platform, the platform must verify, record, report information, and retain records for three years
A

If you allow others to sell on your platform, you must first verify their identity, address, contact information, and licenses, then record and create a file. Once the file is created, it must be re-verified at least every six months. You must report the identity of sellers to the market regulatory authority (China), report tax status to the tax authority every quarter, and retain product and transaction information for three years. Failure to perform any of these tasks will first result in a mandatory correction order; failure to correct will lead to a fine of ⟦20000~100000⟧.

No monetary cost. You must implement a seller document verification section in the admin panel and establish a recording system. Report tax-related information once per quarter and store transaction data for three years. The difficulty lies in this being a year-round task, not a one-time setup.

The law contains a section requiring platforms to: "request business operators applying to enter the platform to sell goods or provide services to submit authentic information regarding identity, address, contact details, administrative licenses, etc., conduct verification and recording, establish recording files, and periodically verify and update." Sellers must submit their identity, address, contact info, and required licenses before joining. You must verify these once, record them, and create a file, then re-verify periodically. How long is "periodically"? Departmental regulations clarify this as "at least once every six months for verification and updates." You must also report the identity information of business operators on the platform to the market regulatory authority. Tax information must also be reported; the original text states "in accordance with laws and administrative regulations on tax collection management, report identity information and tax-related information of business operators on the platform to the tax authorities." Thus, report who the sellers are to the market regulator, and report their identities and tax status to the tax authority. Information on goods, services, and transactions must be "retained for no less than three years from the date the transaction is completed." Failure to perform any of the above will result in a mandatory correction order within a time limit. Failure to correct will lead to a fine of ⟦20000~100000⟧. Serious circumstances will lead to a mandatory suspension of business for rectification and an additional fine of ⟦100000~500000⟧. Tax-related information must be reported "within the month immediately following the end of the quarter." Failure to report on time carries the same penalties (National).
You must manage user-posted content: have a review mechanism, a report button, and immediately stop transmission and report upon detecting violations
A

The platform is responsible for managing user-posted content: registration, post review, comment review, daily patrols, and emergency handling; every stage must have regulations. Place a violation report button in a visible location on the page. If illegal information is detected, stop its transmission immediately, save records, and report to the regulatory authority. Failure to do so can result in a fine of ⟦50000~500000⟧, or more in serious cases.

Money must be spent on hiring moderators, which is the platform's largest long-term expense. Reporting portals and every handling action must leave a trail. The difficulty is that someone must be on watch every day; a single day off could lead to issues.

Regulations state that platforms "must fulfill the primary responsibility for information content management," meaning the platform is responsible for what users post. Specifically, they must "improve regulations for user registration, account management, post review, comment review, page section environment management, real-time patrols, emergency response, and handling of online rumors and black industry chain information." From registration and posting to daily patrols and incident handling, every stage must have written regulations. Furthermore, they "must place a convenient complaint and violation reporting section in a prominent position"; the report button must be where users can see and click it instantly. Upon detecting illegal information, they "must immediately apply legal handling measures, retain relevant records, and report to the relevant regulatory authorities." The Cybersecurity Law (China) is more specific, stating: "upon discovering information that laws or administrative regulations prohibit from being published or transmitted, [they] shall immediately stop the transmission of that information, adopt measures such as deletion and prevention of dissemination, retain relevant records, and report to the relevant regulatory authorities." Failure to do so results in a correction order, warning, public criticism, and a potential fine of ⟦50000~500000⟧. Intentional failure to correct or serious circumstances leads to a fine of ⟦500000~2000000⟧. It may also lead to mandatory suspension of business for rectification, closure of the website or application, and revocation of permits or business licenses. Directly responsible individuals are fined separately from ⟦50000~200000⟧ (National).
Providing posting or instant messaging services requires mandatory real-name identity information from users
A

If your website allows posting or messaging, you must require users to provide authentic identity information when they start using the service. If they do not provide it, do not allow them to use it. Livestreaming regulations follow the "real name in the backend, nickname of choice in the frontend" principle; verification can be done via phone number. Failure to implement real-name verification first results in a mandatory correction order. Failure to correct leads to a fine of ⟦50000~500000⟧ and potential website closure.

Must connect to a real-name identity verification channel, which charges per verification. Regarding the product, design it according to the principle of "real-name verification in the system, user-selected display name": the system stores the real name while the page displays a nickname.

The original text of the law is: "network operators, when providing network access services, domain name registration for users, procedures for landline or mobile phone network entry..., or providing users with services such as information posting or instant messaging, must require users to provide authentic identity information when signing agreements or confirming service provision. If users do not provide authentic identity information, network operators shall not provide them with relevant services." Failure to require real names, or allowing use despite users not providing real identities, results in a correction order. Intentional failure to correct or serious circumstances leads to a fine of ⟦50000~500000⟧. It may also lead to mandatory temporary suspension of relevant services, suspension of business for rectification, closure of the website or application, and revocation of permits or business licenses. Directly responsible individuals are fined separately from ⟦10000~100000⟧. Livestreaming services follow the principle of "real name in the backend, nickname of choice in the frontend," implementing "authentic identity information verification based on mobile phone numbers or other methods." This means the platform's system stores the user's real name, while the nickname displayed on the page is decided by the user, verified via phone number or similar. Livestreaming sales have stricter requirements, namely "authentic identity information verification based on ID documents, Unified Social Credit Code, etc." The Unified Social Credit Code is the number on a business license (National).
Do not allow persons under 16 to open livestream channels; handle livestream gifting based on age tiers
A

Persons under 16 are not allowed to register livestreaming accounts on your platform. Those 16 and older must verify their identity and obtain consent from parents or other guardians. Gifting (donating) is divided into three tiers: under 8s cannot gift, 8 to 16s require guardian consent, and those 16 and older require guardian consent or verification of income documents. If a child gifts money behind a guardian's back and the guardian demands it back, the court will rule for a refund.
No monetary cost. Add a step in both the registration and payment processes: determine age first, then confirm guardian consent.

The original text of the law is: "livestream service providers shall not provide livestream account registration services to minors under the age of sixteen; when providing livestream account registration services to minors who have reached the age of sixteen, they must verify identity information and obtain consent from parents or other guardians." Regulations also require "establishing a dynamic verification mechanism for the authentic identity information of livestreamers," meaning you must be able to re-verify the identity of channel owners at any time. Additionally, they must "reasonably limit the single consumption amount and total daily consumption amount of minors of different ages when using services," meaning setting spending caps per transaction and per day for minors based on age. Gifting is currently divided into three tiers: "Gifting services shall not be provided to minors under the age of eight. Providing gifting services to minors aged eight to sixteen must have guardian consent. Providing gifting services to minors aged sixteen and older must have guardian consent or verification of their income documents." One more point: if a person with limited civil capacity gifts money without guardian consent and the guardian demands the money back, the court must accept it, and the money is recoverable. A person with limited civil capacity is a minor who is not yet fully legally self-determined (National).
Handle infringement notices promptly; if a counter-notice is forwarded and there is no action for 15 days, restore the content
A

If someone sends an infringement notice with preliminary evidence, you must promptly delete, block, or disconnect the link, and simultaneously forward the notice to the seller. If you do nothing, you must jointly compensate the seller for any increased damages. If the seller submits a counter-notice, forward it to the other party and wait 15 days. If the other party does not file a complaint or lawsuit, restore the goods.
No monetary cost. A fixed process must be established: receive notice, forward to seller, receive seller's counter-notice, and publicize the result. Every step must be documented.

A rights holder "has the right to notify the e-commerce platform operator to take necessary measures such as deletion, blocking, disconnecting links, and terminating transactions and services. The notice shall include preliminary evidence constituting infringement." A rights holder is the owner of rights such as trademarks, copyrights, or patents. Simply sending a statement is insufficient; it must include preliminary evidence. Upon receiving a notice, the platform "must promptly take necessary measures and forward the notice to the business operator on the platform; failure to take necessary measures promptly results in joint liability with the business operator on the platform for the increased portion of the damages." If you ignore it, you must compensate for the increased damages alongside the seller. After the seller counter-notices, the platform "if it does not receive notice that the rights holder has filed a complaint or lawsuit within fifteen days after the counter-notice is forwarded to the intellectual property rights holder, shall promptly terminate the measures taken." This means forwarding the seller's counter-notice to the rights holder and waiting 15 days. If the other party does not complain or sue, restore what was deleted or removed. If the platform knows or should have known about an infringement but fails to act, it bears joint liability with the infringer. Intellectual property authorities can also order you to correct within a time limit; failure to correct results in a fine of ⟦50000~500000⟧, and serious circumstances lead to a fine of ⟦500000~2000000⟧. Conversely, "intentionally sending a false notice, causing damage to the business operator on the platform, results in liability for double compensation" (National).
Do not arbitrarily transfer user information abroad; cross-border transfers are subject to legal conditions and population thresholds
A

Transferring domestic user information to overseas machines is called cross-border transfer; placing servers abroad is the same. Usually, this requires a security assessment by the cyberspace authority (China), or certification, or signing a standard contract. If the cumulative total in a year is less than 100,000 people and contains no sensitive information, you are exempt from all three. You must also inform users who the overseas recipient is, the purpose of the transfer, and obtain their separate consent.
No monetary cost. The easiest way to avoid work is to keep user data domestic. If you truly must transfer it abroad, follow the standard contract or obtain certification.

Providing domestic user information to overseas companies or storing it on overseas machines is legally termed providing personal information abroad and "must meet" one of four conditions. One is passing a security assessment organized by the cyberspace authority. Two is obtaining personal information protection certification from a professional organization. Three is signing a contract with the overseas recipient based on the standard contract issued by the cyberspace authority. Four is other conditions stipulated by laws and administrative regulations. Simultaneously, you must inform users of the following: name and contact details of the overseas recipient, purpose of processing, processing methods, types of personal information, and how they can exercise their rights. You must also "obtain separate consent from the individual," meaning asking the user specifically about this once. Specific thresholds are based on cumulative numbers. Ordinary enterprises are referred to in regulations as data processors that are not critical information infrastructure operators. This type of enterprise has an exemption threshold: "cumulatively providing personal information of fewer than 100,000 individuals (excluding sensitive personal information) abroad since January 1 of that year." Below this threshold, they are exempt from reporting for assessment, signing standard contracts, and certification. From 100,000 to fewer than 1 million people, they must sign a standard contract or pass certification. For 1 million people or more, or sensitive personal information of 10,000 people or more, a security assessment must be reported (National, effective March 2024).
When choosing a server, first check if it can withstand a crash, then check for an operator, and finally compare prices
C

The difference between the three levels is not in the price, but in what you have in hand when something goes wrong. Large providers have public registration channels, licenses, failure notifications, compensation clauses, and reachable staff. Small providers are half the price, but when they oversell capacity, disappear, or get locked by their upstream provider, you won't know who to find. For static websites with no user data, a VPS for a few dozen RMB is enough.

Cloud servers from major providers cost several hundred to several thousand RMB per month. VPS from small providers starts from a few dozen RMB per month. A VPS is a small virtual private server. Renting space for a private server costs from several thousand RMB per year, plus you must buy the hardware yourself.

The difference between the three levels is not in the price, but in what you have in hand when something goes wrong. Large cloud providers have public registration channels and licenses; they provide notifications during incidents, contracts have compensation clauses, and you can find someone if there is a problem. Small providers may have prices half as low, but when they oversell capacity, run away, or are locked by their upstream provider, you have no one to complain to. Therefore, before discussing price, go to the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (China) system to check if they have a value-added telecommunications business license. Renting space for a private server is only worthwhile when two conditions are met: bandwidth or hardware costs are significantly cheaper, and you have staff to operate it yourself. How to choose: for static websites without user data, the cheapest VPS is enough. For sites with user registration and transactions, choose a cloud server that is flexibly scalable and supports snapshots for backups, with backups stored in at least two locations.
If user information on a website or app is leaked, rectify immediately, notify users and regulators; if attacked, report to the police
A

If user information is leaked or potentially leaked, you must rectify it immediately and notify the regulatory authority and affected users. Hiding it will first result in a correction order; failure to correct leads to a fine of up to ⟦1000000⟧, and serious cases up to ⟦50000000⟧. If users suffer damage as a result and you cannot prove you were not at fault, you must compensate them. If you have implemented protection measures, handled it according to a plan, and reported promptly, you may be considered for leniency or exemption.

No monetary cost. A response plan must be written in advance: who decides, which loopholes to plug first, and how to word the notification to users. The difficulty is that when something happens, the natural reflex is to hide it and not want users to know.

The original text of the Personal Information Protection Law (China) is: "if leakage, tampering, or loss of personal information occurs or may occur, the personal information processor shall immediately take remedial measures and notify the department performing personal information protection duties and the individuals." The notification must state three things: the type of information leaked, the cause, and possible harm; what you have done to rectify it and what users can do to mitigate harm; and your contact information. If your remedial measures effectively avoid harm, you may not need to notify users. However, if the regulator believes harm may occur, they have the right to require notification. The Network Data Security Management Regulations (China) state that notification can be via "phone, text message, instant messaging tools, email, or announcements." If signs of crime are discovered during handling, it must be reported to public security or national security agencies. Failure to perform these duties results in a correction order, warning, confiscation of illegal gains, and the infringing app may be ordered to temporarily or permanently suspend services. Intentional failure to correct leads to a fine of up to ⟦1000000⟧, with directly responsible individuals fined from ⟦10000~100000⟧. Serious circumstances lead to a fine of up to ⟦50000000⟧ or up to 5% of the previous year's revenue, with responsible individuals fined from ⟦100000~1000000⟧. Civilly, if users suffer damage and you "cannot prove you were not at fault, you shall bear tort liability such as compensation for damages." Large-scale leaks must also be reported on time. Measures by the Cyberspace Administration of China (China) define a leak of personal information of 1 million or more people as a "relatively large network security incident." For such incidents, ordinary websites and apps must report to their provincial cyberspace authority "no later than 4 hours," with one channel being the 12387 hotline. A summary report must be submitted within 30 days of completion. Late, incomplete, false, or hidden reporting causing serious harmful consequences results in heavier penalties. Conversely, if reasonable and necessary protection measures were taken, handled according to the plan, and reported promptly, "leniency or exemption may be granted depending on the situation" (National, reporting measures apply from November 2025).
When selling auto-renewing memberships, clearly remind users before registration and before each deduction; the cancellation button must be easy to find
A

If selling auto-renewing memberships, you must remind users in a prominent way before they register and before each deduction. During the membership period, there must be a place to cancel or change at any time, which must be easy to find, easy to click, and no unreasonable fees may be charged. Deducting money without a reminder can result in a fine of 1 to 5 times the illegal gains; if there are no illegal gains, the fine is up to ⟦300000⟧.

No monetary cost. Clearly state the auto-renewal policy on the registration page, send a separate reminder message before each deduction, and place a button on the profile page that allows cancellation at any time. The difficulty is that some users will cancel immediately upon receiving the reminder.

The original text of the Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Online Transactions (China) is: providing services via automatic extension or auto-renewal "shall remind consumers to pay attention in a prominent manner before consumers receive the service and before the date of automatic extension or auto-renewal, for consumers to choose." During the service period, they must also "provide consumers with options to cancel or change at any time that are prominent, simple, and shall not charge unreasonable fees." The Implementing Regulations of the Consumer Rights Protection Law (China) have similar reminder requirements. Failure to remind results in penalties under the implementing regulations: correction order, potential warning, confiscation of illegal gains, and a fine of 1 to 5 times the illegal gains. If there are no illegal gains, the fine is up to ⟦300000⟧. Serious circumstances lead to a mandatory suspension of business for rectification and revocation of the business license. Failure to provide a convenient cancellation path results in a correction order within a time limit and a potential fine of up to ⟦30000⟧ (National).
If planning to become pregnant, start taking 0.4 mg of folic acid daily and continue through the end of the first trimester
A

Taking one folic acid tablet daily before and during pregnancy reduces the likelihood of neural tube defects in the child by about seven-tenths. Neural tube defects are a group of birth defects such as anencephaly and spina bifida. For those who have previously given birth to a child with such a defect, taking folic acid reduces the risk for the next child to about one-third of the previous risk.
A few dozen RMB per bottle. Rural women (China) do not pay, as the state's free folic acid supplementation program distributes it. One pill a day; the difficulty is remembering to take it every day.

A Cochrane systematic review pooling 5 trials and 6,708 births calculated this, with the quality of evidence rated as high. Daily folic acid supplementation around the time of conception reduces the risk of fetal neural tube defects with an RR of 0.31 (95% CI 0.17 to 0.58), a reduction of about seven-tenths. For those who have already had a child with a neural tube defect, the risk for the next child is RR 0.34 (95% CI 0.18 to 0.64), a reduction to about one-third. By group, the 0.4 mg dose and higher doses did not differ in effectiveness. Taking folic acid alone versus a multivitamin also showed no difference. The 2010 Folic Acid Supplementation Program Management Plan of the Ministry of Health (China) clearly states: distribute folic acid for free to rural women preparing for pregnancy, "to be taken from 3 months before pregnancy through the end of the first 3 months of pregnancy," with the distributed type being 0.4 mg folic acid tablets. The US CDC states that neural tube defects occur in the first few weeks of pregnancy, often before you know you are pregnant.
Before week 13 of pregnancy, go to the community health station to establish a "Maternal and Child Health Handbook" and use all free prenatal check-ups
A

At least five prenatal check-ups, plus one postpartum home visit and one check-up 42 days after birth, are paid for by the state. To receive them, go to a community health station before week 13 to establish a "Maternal and Child Health Handbook". If you do not establish it, these free visits will be lost.
No cost; this is a service under the National Basic Public Health Service Program (China). You must go several times according to the gestational week.

The "National Basic Public Health Service Specifications (Third Edition)" (China) includes health management services for pregnant and postpartum women. Pregnant and postpartum women residing in the area are entitled to the following: 1 health check-up in the first trimester, 2 in the second trimester, 2 in the third trimester, 1 postpartum visit, and 1 health check-up 42 days after birth. The handbook must be established before week 13, along with the 1st prenatal check-up. The two visits in the second trimester are at weeks 16 to 20 and weeks 21 to 24, respectively. The two visits in the third trimester are at weeks 28 to 36 and weeks 37 to 40, respectively. The local service catalogs published also include a series of initial tests and postpartum depression screening.
During the first prenatal check-up, perform all three tests for HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis B; if HIV is detected, free transmission blocking medication is available
A

Perform all three tests for HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis B at the first prenatal check-up. Initial HIV screening is free of charge. Detecting the disease is not a dead end. If HIV is detected, the state provides free treatment and counseling. If syphilis is detected, treat with penicillin as soon as possible. If hepatitis B is detected, the newborn receives both the vaccine and immunoglobulin simultaneously to block mother-to-child transmission.

Initial HIV screening and counseling are free according to regulations (China). For syphilis and hepatitis B tests, national documents do not state they are free; inquire at the hospital where the prenatal check-up is performed regarding fees.

Mother-to-child transmission is the transmission of disease from mother to child. The "Specifications for the Prevention of Mother-to-Child Transmission of HIV, Syphilis, and Hepatitis B (2020 Edition)" (China) provides requirements. At the first prenatal check-up, hospitals must provide relevant information, "provide appropriate, standardized testing, and follow-up counseling based on results". If testing is not completed by the time of delivery, the case is handled as an infection in principle. The specifications require that for pregnant or postpartum women detected with syphilis, "standardized penicillin treatment should be administered as soon as possible", and the newborn should receive preventive penicillin treatment immediately. Pregnant or postpartum women who are hepatitis B surface antigen positive are provided with antiviral treatment after explanation and consent, if conditions are met. A positive detection is not a dead end. The "Regulations on AIDS Prevention and Control" (China) Article 23 stipulates that for those voluntarily seeking HIV counseling and testing, "free counseling and initial screening tests shall be provided". Article 44 stipulates providing HIV-infected pregnant and postpartum women with "free treatment and counseling to prevent mother-to-child transmission of HIV". Article 43 requires providing transmission blocking services (to prevent the disease from passing to the child), treatment, postpartum visits, monitoring, and testing for the child. If the mother is hepatitis B surface antigen positive, the newborn must receive both the hepatitis B vaccine and hepatitis B immunoglobulin at birth (see Chapter 20, Section 2).
No cigarettes and no alcohol throughout pregnancy; family members should also not smoke indoors
A

Smoking during pregnancy increases the likelihood of preterm birth, low birth weight, and cleft lip or palate; the risk of abnormal bleeding during pregnancy and delivery doubles. If the mother smokes during pregnancy, or the child inhales secondhand smoke after birth, the risk of sudden infant death is higher. It is never too late to quit.
No cost, and it saves money on cigarettes and alcohol. The difficulty lies in getting those living with you to quit as well.

According to the US CDC: smoking during pregnancy can cause a baby to be "born too small even if full-term" and "can cause preterm birth". It "doubles the risk of abnormal bleeding during pregnancy and delivery". It increases the risk of birth defects such as cleft lip and cleft palate. It also "damages the developing lungs and brain of the fetus, damage that can last into childhood". Infants whose mothers smoked during pregnancy, and infants exposed to secondhand smoke after birth, have a higher risk of Sudden Infant Death Syndrome (SIDS). The official recommendation is "it is best to quit before pregnancy, but if already pregnant, quitting is still beneficial", "it is never too late to quit". Regarding alcohol, the US CDC states that during pregnancy "there is no known safe amount of alcohol", and there is no stage during pregnancy when drinking alcohol is safe. The baby's brain develops throughout pregnancy, and exposure to alcohol at any time can have an impact.
Those with high-risk factors for preeclampsia should take one low-dose aspirin daily after week 12 as prescribed by a doctor
A

Preeclampsia is a hypertensive disorder in pregnancy. Those who had it in a previous pregnancy, are carrying multiples, have chronic hypertension, had diabetes before pregnancy, or have kidney disease or autoimmune diseases belong to the high-risk group. If high-risk individuals take low-dose aspirin daily as prescribed by a doctor starting from week 12, preeclampsia decreases by about 15%, and preterm birth and perinatal mortality decrease by about 20%. Others should not take it on their own.
A few dozen yuan. Take the medication daily as prescribed by a doctor until delivery. The difficulty is not forgetting any day.

The US Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF) provides a Grade B recommendation: for individuals at high risk of preeclampsia, start taking low-dose aspirin (81 mg/day) after week 12 to prevent the disease. Preeclampsia is a hypertensive disorder in pregnancy. Aggregated studies show the following results: Preeclampsia RR 0.85 (95% CI 0.75 to 0.95, 16 studies), a reduction of about 15%. Preterm birth RR 0.80 (95% CI 0.67 to 0.95, 13 studies), a reduction of about 20%. Perinatal mortality RR 0.79 (95% CI 0.66 to 0.96, 11 studies), a reduction of about 21%; perinatal mortality is death occurring around the time of birth. Small for gestational age / intrauterine growth restriction RR 0.82 (95% CI 0.68 to 0.99, 16 studies), a reduction of about 18%; meaning the fetus is smaller than other fetuses of the same gestational age.
From week 24 onwards, perform a screening for gestational diabetes; do not hesitate to drink the glucose solution
A

Gestational diabetes is high blood sugar that only appears after becoming pregnant. After week 24, spend half a morning drinking a glucose solution and having blood drawn several times to detect it. Without testing or management, the risks of macrosomia (large baby), difficult labor, cesarean section, preeclampsia, and neonatal hypoglycemia all increase.
A few dozen to over a hundred yuan. Must arrive fasting and have blood drawn several times, taking up half a morning.

The US Preventive Services Task Force (USPSTF) Grade B recommendation: for asymptomatic pregnant women (those who do not feel any discomfort), screen for gestational diabetes from week 24 onwards. Gestational diabetes is high blood sugar that only appears after becoming pregnant. If screening only once, it must be scheduled from week 24 onwards. Regarding whether screening before week 24 is beneficial, the task force concluded that current evidence is insufficient to assess the benefits and harms (Grade I). Unmanaged gestational diabetes increases the risk of: macrosomia (the fetus growing too large), difficult labor, cesarean section, preeclampsia, and neonatal hypoglycemia.
Memorize this "go to the hospital immediately" list, applicable both during pregnancy and for one year postpartum
A

If you have any of the signs below, go to the hospital immediately that day, do not wait overnight at home; this also applies for one year postpartum. Headache that does not improve or gets worse, distorted vision, fever reaching 38 °C, significant swelling of hands or face. Shortness of breath, chest pain or rapid heartbeat, severe abdominal pain that does not improve, the fetus stops moving or moves significantly less. Vaginal bleeding or leaking fluid, one arm or leg that is both swollen and painful, thoughts of harming yourself or your baby.
No cost. Spend five minutes to memorize it, and ideally let those living with you know as well.

The US CDC lists urgent warning signs during and after pregnancy including: headache that won't go away or gets worse, dizziness or fainting, distorted vision, body temperature of 38 °C or higher; significant swelling of hands or face, thoughts of harming yourself or your baby, shortness of breath, chest pain or rapid heartbeat; severe nausea and vomiting, severe abdominal pain that won't go away, the fetus stops moving or moves significantly less during pregnancy; vaginal bleeding or leaking fluid during pregnancy, abnormal vaginal bleeding or discharge after birth; one arm or leg with severe swelling, redness, or pain. These problems can occur within one year postpartum; it is not "over once the confinement period ends".
If your water breaks, lie down immediately on the spot, elevate your hips, and call 120; do not walk, do not bathe
B

When your water breaks, it is not a time to leisurely pack things before leaving. The correct way is to lie down immediately on the spot, elevate your hips, and call 120. Standing or walking makes the amniotic fluid flow out faster, and the umbilical cord could be carried down with it. This is an emergency that can claim the baby's life.
No cost.

Management instructions provided by the Beijing Municipal Health Commission (China): if you discover your water has broken, "immediately find a place to lie flat so the amniotic fluid does not flow out", "do not walk around arbitrarily", and "immediately call the emergency number 120". While waiting for the ambulance, notify family members to bring belongings to meet at the hospital. Health education articles from medical institutions further explain the reason: when a person stands, amniotic fluid is lost faster, and the baby's umbilical cord may fall out with it, called umbilical cord prolapse, which is a life-threatening emergency for the fetus. Therefore, you must lie down, elevate your hips, and you may lie on your left side.
If you want painless labor, just say so; it does not increase the risk of needing a cesarean section
A

Painless labor involves an anesthetic injection in the back to suppress labor pain. It provides better pain relief than other methods and does not make you more likely to need surgery.
