The claim that "painless anesthesia causes lifelong back pain" is also groundless. It now has its own billing item (China), making hospitals more willing to perform it.
A few hundred to over ⟦1000⟧, prices vary by location. You must ask the hospital and the anesthesiology department in advance if it is available. The difficulty lies in speaking up for yourself.

Cochrane systematic review conclusion: epidural analgesia reduces labor pain and makes postpartum women more satisfied with pain relief compared to non-epidural methods. Painless labor primarily uses epidural analgesia. The same review also states "epidural analgesia does not affect the risk of cesarean section and long-term back pain". The phenomenon of increased instrumental delivery (using tools to pull the baby out) has not been seen in studies after 2005. Starting from 2024, the National Healthcare Security Administration (China) guidelines for establishing medical service price items for obstetrics have separated items for "labor analgesia", "doula-assisted delivery", and "family member assisted delivery". The main reason is that previously there was no separate price item, making hospitals unenthusiastic about providing labor analgesia.
Unless medically indicated, do not demand a cesarean section, and do not have surgery to choose a specific date
A

According to the World Health Organization, once the cesarean section rate in a region exceeds 10%, there is no evidence that maternal and neonatal mortality continues to decrease. If surgery is necessary, it must be performed. Choosing surgery for a specific date or out of fear of pain means undergoing an unnecessary major abdominal surgery.
No cost. The difficulty lies in standing firm against family opinions.

2015 statement from the World Health Organization: when the cesarean section rate in a population increases to about 10%, maternal and neonatal mortality decreases. Beyond 10%, there is no evidence that mortality rates improve further. The World Health Organization also emphasizes that every effort should be made to provide cesarean sections to women in need, rather than striving to achieve a specific rate.
Before becoming pregnant, check your maternity insurance status; even if a spouse is unemployed, medical costs for delivery can be reimbursed
A

If the employer has paid into maternity insurance (China), medical costs for delivery and allowances during maternity leave are paid from this fund. If a spouse is unemployed, their medical costs are also reimbursed. You must clarify in advance whether the required months of contribution have been met and if registration is required for giving birth in another province.
No cost. Make a phone call to social security or medical insurance.

"Social Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China" Article 54: if the employer has paid maternity insurance premiums, the employees of the unit are entitled to maternity insurance benefits. The unemployed spouse of an employee is entitled to medical cost benefits for delivery according to national regulations, paid from the maternity insurance fund. If the unit pays for maternity insurance, the employee themselves receives benefits, and the medical costs for delivery of an unemployed spouse are also covered by this fund. The maternity insurance system is divided into two parts: first, medical costs for delivery, i.e., medical expenses for the birth itself; second, maternity allowance, i.e., the money paid to you during maternity leave. Article 56 lists three cases for receiving maternity allowance: female employees taking maternity leave for childbirth, leave after family planning surgery, and other cases stipulated by laws and regulations. The maternity allowance is "calculated based on the average monthly salary of the employees at the employer unit in the previous year", meaning it is based on the average monthly salary of your entire unit last year, not your individual salary.
Complete the "Medical Certificate of Birth" before discharge; decide on the child's name in advance to avoid typos
A

This certificate is a mandatory document for household registration, insurance enrollment, and school admission (China). If born in a hospital, obtain it at the facility where the delivery took place. If not born in a delivery facility, a parent-child relationship appraisal must be performed before issuance. Check in advance if the characters in the child's name can be typed into the civil registration system.
Free of charge. Complete it during the hospital discharge process.

"Maternal and Infant Health Care Law (China)" Article 23: Medical institutions and home birth attendants shall, in accordance with the regulations of the health administrative department under the State Council (China), issue a medical certificate of birth for newborns in a unified format. This certificate is a prerequisite for all subsequent matters: household registration, insurance participation, medical insurance card application, kindergarten, and school enrollment all require it. The 2015 Opinion of the General Office of the State Council (China) on resolving household registration for unregistered persons specifies: for births in delivery facilities, apply for the "Medical Certificate of Birth" at that facility. For births outside delivery facilities, a parent-child relationship appraisal certificate issued by a qualified appraisal organization must be obtained first, then the application is made at a facility authorized by the county-level health authority.
Do not refuse newborn heel prick blood screening and hearing screening for your child
A

A single heel prick and a single hearing test can detect hypothyroidism, phenylketonuria, and hearing loss while the child still appears completely normal. If you wait for symptoms to appear, the intellectual damage will be irreversible.
Free in most places, or a few dozen yuan. Some expanded items require out-of-pocket payment. Performed once after the child is born.

"Administrative Measures for Newborn Disease Screening" (China) Article 3: "National newborn screening diseases include neonatal inherited metabolic diseases such as congenital hypothyroidism, phenylketonuria, and hearing loss." These two groups of diseases share a common trait: they show no abnormalities in the early stages, but by the time symptoms are clear, intellectual damage is irreversible. Early detection and early intervention yield excellent results; methods include thyroid hormone supplementation, special formula milk, hearing aids, or cochlear implants. Article 10 stipulates that if screening results are positive, the facility must promptly notify the guardian to take the child for a definitive diagnosis.
Apply for resident medical insurance for your child as soon as you have the birth certificate; do not wait for household registration
A

With a birth certificate, you can enroll the child in insurance online without waiting for household registration. Once enrolled, hospitalization costs can be settled immediately upon discharge. Newborn hospitalization costs are not small; the difference between having insurance and not is significant.
Resident medical insurance (China) premiums are paid once a year, amounting to a few hundred yuan.

According to the Chinese Government Service Portal in 2024: "newborns with a birth certificate can participate in insurance online" without needing prior household registration. "Newborns can have their medical expenses settled directly upon discharge." The previous method required household registration before insurance participation, meaning hospitalization costs had to be paid in full upfront and reimbursed later. The average time for enrollment and payment procedures has also decreased from 28.7 working days at the beginning of the year to 6.4 working days.
Within one month of the child's birth, report to the police station for birth registration
A

The child's household registration must be reported within one month of birth; simultaneously, you must go to the hospital of birth or the local vaccination point to create a vaccination record book. These are two separate tasks; vaccinations must be given on schedule even if household registration is not yet complete.
Free of charge. Requires one visit to the household registration desk at the police station (China).

"Regulations on Household Registration (China)" Article 7: "Within one month after a baby is born, the head of the household, relatives, foster parents, or neighbors shall report the birth registration to the household registration authority in the place of the baby's permanent residence." This is a legally mandated deadline, not just advice. Household registration and vaccination are handled separately. The "Vaccine Management Law (China)" requires that within one month of birth, parents must go to the local vaccination point or the hospital of birth to create a vaccination record. These units cannot refuse. Vaccination is managed by place of residence and does not require prior household registration. Children without household registration must still be vaccinated promptly according to the immunization schedule.
Do not skip the 42-day postpartum check-up; in some places, this also includes postpartum depression screening
A

This follow-up visit is free. According to local service catalogs, it includes a complete blood count, vaginal discharge test, and a postpartum depression screening. Major issues can occur within the first year after birth; do not assume you are safe just because the confinement period is over.
Free of charge, as it is part of the Basic National Public Health Services (China). Takes half a day. The difficulty lies in laziness right after the confinement period ends.

In the maternal health management section of the "National Basic Public Health Service Standards (Third Edition)" (China), there is 1 postpartum visit and 1 health check-up at 42 days postpartum. Local service catalogs show this visit includes tests (blood count, vaginal discharge) and 1 postpartum depression screening. The 2020 Special Service Work Plan for Depression Prevention and Control by the National Health Commission (China) requires pilot areas to "include prenatal and postpartum depression screening into routine prenatal care and postpartum visits." Therefore, whether postpartum depression screening is included depends on local implementation. Severe complications can appear within one year postpartum. In the "hospitalize immediately" list in section 7, "thoughts of harming oneself or the child," "abnormal vaginal bleeding or discharge after birth," and "severe swelling or pain in one limb" all belong to the postpartum stage.
No need to give away the cat when pregnant; have someone else clean the litter box daily, cook meat thoroughly, and wear gloves when touching soil
B

Toxoplasma is a parasite. A first-time infection during pregnancy can cause miscarriage, and the child may suffer eye and brain damage. Keeping a cat indoors does not make one more likely to be infected; there is no need to give the cat away. What needs more prevention is eating undercooked meat and touching soil without washing hands; for cat litter, just have someone else clean it daily.

Free of charge. Delegate litter box cleaning to a family member daily. If you must do it yourself, buy a box of disposable gloves. The difficulty lies in ensuring meat is fully cooked; rare steaks and rare lamb are not allowed.

The US CDC states that a first-time toxoplasma infection just before or during pregnancy can be transmitted to the fetus. Most infected infants show no symptoms at birth but may develop blindness or intellectual disabilities later in life. A small number are born with severe eye or brain damage. The UK National Health Service (NHS) says infection during pregnancy can cause miscarriage. The Toxoplasmosis Reference Center in Lyon, France, recorded 603 pregnant women diagnosed with infection during pregnancy, most of whom took antiparasitic drugs. The total transmission rate to the fetus was 29% (95% CI 25–33). Infection at week 13 has a ~6% transmission rate, while at week 36 it is ~72%. The earlier the infection, the more likely the child will show symptoms. Infection between weeks 24 and 30 carries the highest risk (~10%) of the child showing early symptoms. A study in six European cities compared newly infected pregnant women with non-infected ones. Keeping a cat indoors had an OR of 1.0 (95% CI 0.7–1.5), showing no difference. Cleaning the cat litter tray yourself had an OR of 1.3 (95% CI 0.8–2.1), a difference that could be due to chance. Eating undercooked lamb had an OR of 3.13 (95% CI 1.4–7.2), about 3 times the risk of those who didn't. Touching soil had an OR of 1.81 (95% CI 1.2–2.7), about 80% higher. In these cities, 30% to 63% of infections were attributed to undercooked or cured meat, and 6% to 17% to touching soil. The US CDC advises pregnant women: have someone else change the cat litter if possible. If no one else can, wear disposable gloves and wash hands with soap and water afterward. Change the litter daily, as toxoplasma in cat feces takes 1 to 5 days to become infectious to humans. Do not get a new cat, adopt, or touch stray cats—especially kittens—during pregnancy. Keep cats indoors, feed them only cat food or cooked food, and do not feed them raw meat. A public education article from the China CDC also suggests that cleaning the litter tray should be the future father's job; with good protection, the cat can stay. The NHS explicitly states that touching or owning a cat does not cause toxoplasmosis infection.
If pregnant during flu season, get an inactivated flu vaccine; it can be given at any stage of pregnancy; do not use the nasal spray type
A

Pregnant women with the flu are more likely to be hospitalized than non-pregnant women. Getting a flu shot during pregnancy reduces the mother's own hospitalization for flu by about 40%. For the child in the first 6 months after birth, confirmed flu cases are reduced by about half, and flu-related hospitalizations by about 70%. Vaccination has not been found to increase miscarriage, stillbirth, or birth defects.

Self-paid, one dose costs a few dozen to over a hundred yuan. Requires one visit to a community vaccination clinic. The difficulty lies in choosing a brand where the instruction manual does not list pregnancy as a contraindication.

The 2022 World Health Organization position paper synthesized existing studies. Pregnant women with flu have about 7 times the risk of hospitalization compared to non-pregnant women (OR 6.8, 95% CI 6–7.7). A trial in Bangladesh randomly assigned 340 pregnant women into two groups. One group received the inactivated flu vaccine, and the control group received a pneumococcal vaccine, with follow-up until 24 weeks after birth. The flu vaccine group had 6 children with confirmed flu, while the control group had 16, a vaccine efficacy of 63% (95% CI 5–85). Maternal fever with respiratory illness was reduced by 36% (95% CI 4–57). Two trials in South Africa used placebos where neither doctors nor participants knew which shot was given. In the HIV-negative group, confirmed flu decreased from 3.6% to 1.8%, an efficacy of 50.4% (95% CI 14.5–71.2). Their children saw a decrease from 3.6% to 1.9%, an efficacy of 48.8% (95% CI 11.6–70.4). Pooling 4 trials and 3 observational studies, confirmed flu in infants during the first 6 months was reduced by about 48% (95% CI 33–59). Four observational studies looking at infant hospitalizations for confirmed flu showed a reduction of about 72% (95% CI 39–87). Another meta-analysis pooling only two trials showed a 34% reduction in confirmed flu (95% CI 15–50). However, "influenza-like illness" in children showed no difference; this refers to cases with flu-like symptoms but no laboratory testing. Regarding maternal hospitalization, a study of medical records in four countries from 2010 to 2016 showed that those vaccinated had about 40% lower hospitalization rates for confirmed flu (95% CI 12–59). Regarding safety, a meta-analysis of 40 studies found that in vaccinated women, the aOR for stillbirth was 0.84 (0.65–1.08) and for congenital malformations was 1.03 (0.99–1.07). Both differences were within the margin of error. Preterm birth was 0.87 (0.78–0.96), about 13% lower. A US study of three flu seasons from 2012 to 2015 found that vaccination within 28 days before miscarriage had an aOR of 0.9 (0.6–1.5), showing no association. The 2024–2025 China CDC guidelines list pregnant women as a priority group for vaccination. The guidelines state that vaccination at any stage of pregnancy protects infants under 6 months, though vaccination in the third trimester is more effective. Live attenuated vaccines are prohibited for pregnant women.
After the 28th week of pregnancy, sleep on your side; either left or right is fine, but do not sleep on your back
B

Going to sleep on your back after the 28th week increases the risk of stillbirth by about 2.6 times compared to side-sleeping. Left and right sides are the same; choose whichever is comfortable. If you wake up in the middle of the night on your back, do not panic; just roll back onto your side and go back to sleep. This figure is based on retrospective data and remains debated.
Free of charge. The difficulty lies in changing habits for those used to sleeping on their backs.

Stillbirth here refers to fetal death in utero after the 28th week. A meta-analysis pooled individual participant data from five studies. Four were in New Zealand, Australia, and the UK, and one was an international online survey. A total of 851 pregnant women who experienced stillbirth were compared with 2,257 women with normal pregnancies as controls. The study method involved asking them after the event how they recently went to sleep. Compared to falling asleep on the left side, falling asleep on the back had an aOR for stillbirth of 2.63 (95% CI 1.72–4.04), about 2.6 times higher. Sleeping on the right side had an aOR of 1.04 (0.83–1.31), no different from the left side. This association remained similar regardless of whether the baby was small for gestational age, or if the mother was obese or a smoker. The authors estimated that if all pregnant women after 28 weeks fell asleep on their sides, stillbirths in this period could be reduced by about 5.8% (3.2%–9.2%). The UK National Health Service (NHS) lists "do not go to sleep on your back after 28 weeks" as one way to reduce the risk of stillbirth. The NHS also states that if you wake up on your back, do not worry; just roll onto your side and go back to sleep.
Resume contraception as soon as sexual activity resumes after birth; breastfeeding is not a reliable contraceptive; wait at least 18 months before the next pregnancy
B

You can get pregnant again 3 weeks after giving birth, even if you are breastfeeding and haven't had a period. Breastfeeding only prevents pregnancy if three conditions are met: exclusive breastfeeding, no period yet, and the baby is under 6 months old. Getting pregnant less than half a year after birth increases the risk of preterm birth for the next child by about 40%. The WHO recommends waiting at least two years after birth before getting pregnant again.
Condoms cost a few dozen yuan per box. IUDs or implants require a hospital visit, with prices varying by location. The difficulty lies in being too busy after birth to prioritize this.

The UK National Health Service (NHS) states that you can get pregnant 3 weeks after birth, even if breastfeeding and without a period. Unless you want another child immediately, use contraception every time. Relying on breastfeeding for contraception is called the Lactational Amenorrhea Method (LAM), which requires three conditions simultaneously: exclusive breastfeeding, no period, and the baby is under 6 months old. When used correctly, it is over 99% effective. Without strict adherence, about 2 out of 100 people get pregnant within 6 months. If any of the following occur, switch methods: baby is over 6 months, starts formula, solids, or uses a pacifier, your period returns (even spotting counts), you stop night feedings, or feeding frequency decreases. A meta-analysis of 67 studies, adjusted for maternal age and family background, used a birth-to-conception interval of 18 to 23 months as a baseline. An interval under 6 months had an OR for preterm birth of 1.40 (95% CI 1.24–1.58), about 40% higher. Low birth weight was 1.61 (1.39–1.86), and small for gestational age was 1.26 (1.18–1.33). Intervals of 6 to 17 months, or over 59 months, also showed higher risks. A Canadian study of over 148,000 pregnancies compared a 6-month interval to an 18-month interval. For mothers aged 35+, mortality or severe morbidity was 0.62% vs 0.26%, aRR 2.39 (2.03–2.80), about 2.4 times higher. For mothers aged 20–34, there was no difference (0.92, 0.83–1.02). In mothers aged 20–34, the composite of stillbirth, early neonatal death, very small for gestational age, or very preterm birth was 2.0% vs 1.4%, aRR 1.42 (1.36–1.47). A 2005 WHO expert meeting recommended waiting at least 24 months after a live birth before attempting the next pregnancy. The consensus among experts was to avoid pregnancy within 18 months. After a miscarriage or abortion, wait at least 6 months.
Do not use extreme fasting, starvation, or self-induced vomiting to maintain weight; if you want to lose weight, do it by increasing physical activity
A

People with anorexia nervosa have a mortality rate about 5.9 times higher than their peers. For every 1,000 people followed for one year, 5.1 die, with about one-fifth of those deaths being suicides. Dieters are more prone to eating disorders: a three-year study of students in 44 high schools found that girls who dieted severely were 18 times more likely to develop an eating disorder than non-dieters. To maintain weight, exercise more; do not eat so little that you starve.
Free of charge. In fact, it saves money on weight loss products.

A meta-analysis of 36 studies calculated that the anorexia nervosa group was followed for a total of 166,642 person-years. Their Standardized Mortality Ratio (SMR) was 5.86, meaning their mortality risk is about 5.9 times that of their peers. There were 5.1 deaths per 1,000 person-years. About 1/5 of deaths were due to suicide. Bulimia had an SMR of 1.93, and other eating disorders were 1.92, each about 1.9 times the risk of their peers. Another study in 44 high schools in Victoria, Australia, followed students aged 14–15 for 3 years with 6 survey waves. Among girls, the incidence of eating disorders was 21.8/1,000 person-years. Severe dieters had an 18-fold risk compared to non-dieters, while moderate dieters had a 5-fold risk. After adjusting for dieting history and psychiatric symptoms (removing the influence of "previous dieting" and "pre-existing psychiatric symptoms"), BMI, activity level, and gender no longer predicted new-onset eating disorders. The authors concluded: "in adolescence, weight control through exercise rather than dietary restriction appears to carry less risk of leading to an eating disorder."
Before injections, thread lifting, or surgery, check two things: whether the facility's license specifies "medical aesthetics" and whether the practitioner is a lead attending physician
A

The use of needles, scalpels, or medical equipment that breaks the skin or enters the body is classified as medical treatment. These procedures must only be performed at facilities with a license specifying "medical aesthetics," and the practitioner must be a registered practicing physician. Beauty salons, studios, and hotel rooms are not permitted. Anyone performing these acts without physician status is practicing medicine illegally: causing serious injury is punishable by 3 to 10 years in prison, and causing death is punishable by 10 years or more.

Free. Checking these two documents only takes a few minutes. Facilities must display their "Medical Institution Practicing License" (China) in the lobby. A physician's qualifications can be verified through the practicing physician lookup section of the health authority (China).

Article 2 of the "Measures for the Administration of Medical Aesthetic Services" (China) defines medical aesthetics. The original text is "the use of surgery, drugs, medical devices, and other traumatic or invasive medical technical methods to repair and reshape the appearance and shape of human body parts." Put simply, any act that breaks the skin, involves needles, or enters the body is considered medical treatment. Articles 8 and 24 require a "Medical Institution Practicing License" first, and approval from the registration authority for the medical aesthetic treatment category before procedures can be performed. If the license does not list "medical aesthetics," it is not permitted. Article 11 requires the lead attending physician (the person directly performing the procedure) to have practicing physician qualifications and be registered. Performing aesthetic surgery also requires 6 or more years of clinical experience in a related specialty; aesthetic dentistry requires 5 years; and aesthetic traditional Chinese medicine and aesthetic dermatology each require 3 years. Article 20 requires that before the procedure, indications, contraindications (cases where it should or should not be done), medical risks, and precautions must be reported in writing, and a signature of consent must be obtained. Article 336 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China punishes the crime of illegal medical practice. Illegal medical practice refers to a person without physician qualifications who performs injections, surgery, or medical examinations on others. Serious circumstances are punishable by up to 3 years in prison, short-term detention, or public surveillance, with or without a fine. Causing serious harm to a patient's health is punishable by 3 to 10 years in prison, plus a fine. Causing the death of a patient is punishable by 10 years or more in prison, plus a fine.
Avoid the bridge of the nose, the area between the eyebrows, and the forehead when getting facial fillers; never go to unlicensed facilities just to save money
B

Among people who went blind after filler injections, more than half were injected in the nose area, followed by the glabella (between the eyebrows), forehead, and nasolabial folds; more than 80% used hyaluronic acid. Among those who went blind, only about 20% fully recovered their vision, more than 10% partially recovered, and nearly 20% suffered brain damage. Currently, there is no consistently effective emergency treatment, so these areas must be avoided from the start.
Free. It simply involves changing the injection site or not undergoing the procedure.

A meta-analysis of case reports published in journals worldwide. From January 2015 to September 2018, there were 48 additional cases of partial or total vision loss after filler injections. The most frequent site of complications was the nose, accounting for 56.3%. This was followed by the glabella at 27.1%, forehead at 18.8%, and nasolabial folds (the creases from the side of the nose to the corners of the mouth) at 14.6%. 81.3% of cases used hyaluronic acid (HA) fillers. 43.8% had skin changes. 18.8% had central nervous system complications (brain involvement). 10 cases (20.8%) fully recovered vision, 8 cases (16.7%) partially recovered, and the remainder did not recover. The authors concluded that management approaches varied widely and no treatment has been proven to be consistently effective.
Do not buy weight loss pills, weight loss coffee, weight loss candies, or "enzyme plums" (plums advertised as enzyme-soaked) that promise "rapid weight loss"
A

These products are often found to be secretly laced with sibutramine, a weight loss drug that was suspended in China in 2010. For overweight individuals aged 55 and older with heart disease or diabetes, taking it for more than three years increases non-fatal myocardial infarction by about 30% and stroke by about 36%. Weight only decreased by an additional 1.7 kg. By the time sample testing detects it, you have already ingested it.
Free. On the contrary, it saves money on these products. The difficulty lies in accepting that there is no such thing as "losing several kilograms in a week."

The SCOUT trial enrolled 9,804 participants. They were all 55 years or older, overweight or obese, and had cardiovascular disease or type 2 diabetes. These individuals were randomly assigned to a drug group or a non-drug group, with an average treatment duration of 3.4 years. The primary outcomes were pre-defined adverse events: non-fatal myocardial infarction, non-fatal stroke, resuscitated cardiac arrest, and cardiovascular death. The rate of these events was 11.4% compared to 10.0%. HR = 1.16 (95% CI 1.03 to 1.31, P = 0.02), meaning those taking the drug were about 16% more likely to experience an event. The true value lies roughly between 3% and 31% higher. Non-fatal myocardial infarction was 4.1% vs 3.2%, HR = 1.28 (1.04–1.57), about 30% higher. Non-fatal stroke was 2.6% vs 1.9%, HR = 1.36 (1.04–1.77), about 36% higher. Cardiovascular death and all-cause mortality did not increase. After randomization, the sibutramine group lost an average of 1.7 kg more. The former State Food and Drug Administration (China), based on safety assessments, determined that the "risks of weight loss treatment outweigh the benefits," and in October 2010 announced the cessation of production, sale, and use of sibutramine preparations and raw materials. Sibutramine and phenolphthalein are both prohibited from being added to food, including health supplements.
Do not use anabolic steroids ("muscle-building injections," "muscle-building pills") to gain muscle
A

Men who test positive for doping at the gym have a mortality risk 3 times higher than peers of the same age, and their number of hospital visits per year is more than double. Acne, gynecomastia (male breast enlargement), and erectile dysfunction: at least one in ten users is affected. In China, these are prescription drugs; any channel selling them to you without a prescription is already breaking the law.
Free, and saves money on drugs. The difficulty lies in accepting that muscle growth will be slower.

A Danish study reviewed records, matching each drug user with a control subject of the same age. The users were 545 men who tested positive for androgenic anabolic steroid doping at gyms from 03/01/2006 to 01/03/2018, matched with 5,450 controls. Additionally, it was cross-checked with 644 individuals who refused testing and 6,440 controls. Results: the mortality rate of users was 3 times that of the control group, HR = 3.0 (95% CI 1.3 to 7.0), with the true multiplier roughly between 1.3 and 7. The median number of hospitalizations or visits per year was 0.81 compared to 0.36 (P < 0.0001). The median is the number where half the people are higher and half are lower. This P-value shows the difference is almost certainly not due to chance. Acne, gynecomastia, and erectile dysfunction each affected more than 10% of users, meaning at least one in ten users was affected, all significantly higher than the control group (P < 0.0001). The cross-check group showed similar results. Article 7 of the "Anti-Doping Regulations" (China): The state strictly manages prohibited substances in the doping list; no unit or individual may illegally produce, sell, import, or export them. The same regulations specify that protein anabolic preparations and peptide hormones are managed as prescription drugs, meaning they can only be purchased with a doctor's prescription; "protein anabolic preparations" is the legal term for these drugs.

If you want to take weight loss pills or semaglutide-type weight loss injections, go to a hospital for a prescription, increase the dose, and follow up as scheduled; do not buy from online shops that deliver without a prescription, and do not get injections at beauty salons
B

Prescription drugs must be sold with a prescription; online sales also require a real prescription and identity verification. Online shops that deliver without asking about your condition, or beauty salons that perform home injections, mostly provide drugs of unknown origin, with no one taking responsibility for dosage or contraindications. One year after stopping weight loss injections, about two-thirds of the weight lost will return, so it must be considered a long-term treatment.

One consultation registration fee plus a round trip. A few dozen RMB and half a day. Those taking weight loss injections must also return for follow-up visits as scheduled by the doctor. Drug costs are separate, and since most weight will return after stopping, this should be budgeted as long-term medication.

The "Measures for the Supervision and Administration of the Quality of Drug Business and Use" (China) stipulates that retail pharmacies must comply with the classification management system for prescription and over-the-counter drugs. This system divides drugs into two types: one requires a doctor's prescription to purchase, and the other can be purchased independently. Pharmacies must sell prescription drugs according to regulations and keep prescriptions for at least five years. If a pharmacist or other professional pharmaceutical staff is absent, a sign must be posted; prescription drugs cannot be sold without their review. Prescription drugs must not be displayed on open shelves for customers to pick themselves. Article 9 of the "Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Online Drug Sales" (China) stipulates: selling prescription drugs online to individuals must ensure the prescription has a real, reliable source and implement a real-name system. Article 10 requires prominent display of risk warning information under each drug display page. Before the prescription is reviewed, the instruction manual must not be displayed, nor can a purchase be allowed. If the prescription is not approved, the page must not even have a purchase button. Article 8 stipulates that drugs under special state management cannot be sold online. This category includes vaccines, blood products, narcotics, psychotropic drugs, medical toxic drugs, radioactive drugs, and precursor chemicals for drugs. The "Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Treatment of Obesity (2024 Edition)" by the National Health Commission (China) clearly states: there are five drugs approved by the National Medical Products Administration (China) for weight loss in adults with primary obesity. These five drugs are orlistat, liraglutide, beinaglutide, semaglutide, and tirzepatide. The same guidelines consider a BMI from 24 to less than 28 as overweight, and 28 or above as obese. Medication is only considered for overweight individuals with related diseases such as high blood sugar, high blood pressure, dyslipidemia, fatty liver, or those who are already obese. The condition is that lifestyle changes have failed to achieve weight loss, and medication is added on that basis. The guidelines require a full assessment of the disease and contraindications before use, and regular follow-ups as directed by a specialist during use. Semaglutide starts at 0.25 mg per week, with a maintenance dose of 2.4 mg or 1.7 mg. Tirzepatide starts at 2.5 mg per week, up to a maximum of 15 mg. If weight loss is less than 5%, the guidelines recommend stopping the drug. What happens after stopping? Look at three trials. The STEP 1 extension study followed 327 people: semaglutide injections for 68 weeks resulted in an average weight loss of 17.3%. One year after stopping, weight increased by 11.6 percentage points, leaving a net loss of 5.6%. The authors concluded that the weight regained was two-thirds of the weight lost, and most cardiometabolic indicators also returned near baseline. STEP 4 took 803 people who had injected for 20 weeks, losing an average of 10.6%, and randomized them. Those who continued lost an additional 7.9% after 48 weeks, while those who switched to placebo regained 6.9%. In SURMOUNT-4, 670 people injected tirzepatide for 36 weeks first, losing an average of 20.9%. Subsequently, those who continued lost an additional 5.5%, while those who switched to placebo regained 14.0%. In July 2026, the Yinchuan Municipal Market Supervision and Administration Bureau (China) issued a risk warning. The warning stated that "weight loss needles" and "slimming injection pens" popular online are mostly unverified decanted drugs, smuggled drugs, or counterfeit drugs. Buying online or through agents for self-injection can easily cause severe allergies, acute pancreatitis, organ damage, and injection site infections. Medical aesthetic services involving injections must only be performed at facilities with medical aesthetic qualifications; home injections or secret injections at beauty salons are all against regulations, see section 2 of this chapter (check two things before injections, thread lifting, or surgery).
Sex hormone medications should only be used when prescribed by a doctor with regular follow-ups; do not buy online and do not increase the dose yourself
A

This is not about whether they should be used, but how. Transgender women using estrogen experience significantly more blood clots in blood vessels compared to peers of the same age: for every 1,000 people, there are about 4 more cases after two years and about 17 more cases after eight years. This risk must be monitored through regular follow-ups; if you buy drugs online and adjust the dose yourself, no one is checking for you.
Regular consultation registration plus blood tests during follow-ups. A few hundred RMB per year and a few half-day sessions.

Researchers followed a group of people through electronic medical records from the Kaiser Permanente health group. This included 2,842 transgender women and 2,118 transgender men. The average follow-up time was 4.0 years and 3.6 years. Each person was matched with approximately 10 times as many cisgender controls based on birth year, race, clinical site, and study entry time, totaling 48,686 cisgender men and 48,775 cisgender women. Transgender women experienced more venous thromboembolism (blood clots causing blockage) than the control group. Compared to cisgender men, after 2 years there were 4.1 more cases per 1,000 people (95% CI 1.6 to 6.7). After 8 years, it was 16.7 cases (6.4–27.5). Thus, for 1,000 people, there were 4.1 more cases after two years and 16.7 more cases after eight years. Compared to cisgender women, these two figures were 3.4 (1.1–5.6) and 13.7 (4.1–22.7). Ischemic stroke (stroke caused by blocked blood vessels) and myocardial infarction were generally comparable between groups. However, in transgender women who only started hormone therapy during the follow-up period, the differences in venous thromboembolism and ischemic stroke were more pronounced. Evidence in transgender men was insufficient to draw conclusions. The authors concluded that "these results may suggest a need for long-term vigilance regarding the vascular side effects of estrogen in gender-affirming hormone therapy."
If the feeling that "I am ugly" has reached the point of repeatedly checking the mirror and wanting constant corrections, get a body image assessment once before considering surgery
B

Among people seeking cosmetic surgery, about 15% suffer from Body Dysmorphic Disorder (BDD), which involves exaggerating a flaw that others can barely see, to the point that it affects daily life. Among those visiting dermatology clinics, it is about 13%; over 70% in both groups are female. Get an evaluation once to see if you fall into this category before deciding whether to have surgery.
A single consultation registration at a psychiatry or clinical psychology department, costing a few dozen RMB. The difficulty is being willing to take this step before scheduling surgery.

A meta-analysis of 33 studies following a standardized process. Among people seeking cosmetic surgery, the prevalence of Body Dysmorphic Disorder (exaggerating a flaw that others can barely see, to the point of affecting life) was 15.04%, with studies ranging from 2.21% to 56.67%. In terms of numbers: for every 100 people seeking cosmetic surgery, about 15 meet the criteria, ranging from 2 to 57 depending on the study. This group had an average age of 34.54 ± 12.41, and 74.38% were female. Among dermatology patients, the rate was 12.65%, with studies ranging from 4.52% to 35.16%, an average age of 27.79 ± 9.03, and 76.09% female. The authors recommend that plastic surgeons and dermatologists proactively assess and identify high-risk individuals and coordinate multi-disciplinary management. Another study surveyed 200 people with BDD: 71.0% had sought non-psychiatric treatment such as dermatology or aesthetics, and 64.0% had actually undergone it. The authors concluded that these treatments "rarely improve" BDD and appear to be ineffective for this condition.
For teeth straightening, find a qualified orthodontist for a direct examination and follow-up as scheduled; do not buy aligner kits online to wear at home yourself
C

In China, clear aligners are Class II medical devices, and the instruction manual must state they are to be worn under the guidance of a qualified orthodontist with regular follow-ups. The U.S. drug regulatory agency states they have not authorized any aligners sold directly to consumers without a dentist's prescription. Without a direct examination, you may suffer from a misaligned bite, teeth moving to the wrong positions, pain, or even tooth loss.

Compared to buying online, it costs more for consultations and follow-ups, requiring visits to the clinic over time. The difficulty is that the treatment usually lasts one to two years, requiring persistent follow-ups.

The 2022 "Guiding Principles for the Technical Review of Registration of Bracketless Orthodontic Appliances" by the Center for Medical Device Evaluation of the National Medical Products Administration (China) states that these aligners "belong to management category II." The document requires the instruction manual to clearly state "must be worn under the guidance of a qualified orthodontist during treatment" and list "requirements for diet, tooth brushing, and regular follow-ups." Product names "should not contain illusory or hypothetical conceptual names such as 'invisible'." The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) states: "The FDA has not authorized clear aligners that are sold directly to consumers without a prescription and supervision by a dentist or orthodontist." The FDA also states: "In-person examination by a dentist or orthodontist can help lower the risks of uneven bite, unintended tooth movement, pain, and tooth loss." After starting treatment, regular in-person follow-ups are necessary to confirm that teeth are moving safely according to plan. Both documents are regulatory and do not provide incident rates.

When buying anti-freckle or skin-whitening creams, first check the special cosmetic registration number on the packaging against the National Medical Products Administration (China) website; do not use anti-freckle creams sold via social media or custom-mixed salon creams
B

In China, anti-freckle and skin-whitening creams must be registered with the National Medical Products Administration first, and must have a "Guozhuang Tezi" (domestic special cosmetic registration) number to be sold. Sample testing has previously detected anti-freckle creams with mercury levels thousands of times over the limit; the packaging still printed this code, but the manufacturer listed on the label claimed they never produced that batch. Mercury absorbed through facial skin can damage the kidneys; most recover after stopping use and receiving treatment, but healing takes several months to two years.
Free; checking a code takes a few minutes. The difficulty is resisting types that acquaintances or social media sellers are most enthusiastically promoting.

Article 16 of the "Cosmetic Supervision and Administration Regulations" (China) classifies anti-freckle and skin-whitening cosmetics as special cosmetics. Article 17 stipulates that special cosmetics must be registered with the drug regulatory department of the State Council (China) before they can be produced or imported. Article 36 requires the label to show the special cosmetic registration certificate number. Article 20 requires the disclosure of registration information, so the code can be looked up on the National Medical Products Administration (China) website. Article 62 of the "Measures for the Administration of Cosmetic Registration and Filing" (China) stipulates that the code for domestic products is "Guozhuang Tezi" plus the year and sequence number, while imported goods are "Guozhuang Tejizi." Announcement No. 14 of 2026 by the National Medical Products Administration (China) disclosed two batches of anti-freckle cream with mercury levels of 4,938 mg/kg and 9,281 mg/kg respectively. The limit in the announcement appendix is no more than 1 mg/kg; these two batches exceeded it by thousands of times. They were purchased at two small cosmetic shops in Sichuan and Anhui, with the "Guozhuang Tezi" code printed on the packaging. The manufacturer listed on the packaging appealed, and the Guangdong Provincial Drug Administration investigated and determined the enterprise had never produced that batch. A review article compiled 30 cases published in journals, all of whom suffered from nephrotic syndrome after using mercury-containing whitening creams, meaning a large amount of protein leaked into their urine. All 30 were Asian women, mostly aged 18 to 52. The time from starting use to disease onset was 1 to 60 months, with half within 5 months. Kidney biopsies mostly showed minimal change disease (67%) or membranous nephropathy (23%), which are two diseases of the glomerulus. Very few recovered spontaneously within a month and a half after stopping use. In recorded cases, those using mercury-expelling drugs saw urinary protein turn negative after 1 to 9 months, with a median of 2 months. 3 cases not using mercury-expelling drugs took over 12 months. A hospital in Beijing admitted 288 people with mercury poisoning from 2014 to 2019, 84 of whom (29.27%) were related to cosmetics. In women, the primary source of poisoning was cosmetics. Among 18 people with nephrotic syndrome who were followed up, 15 saw their urinary protein and albumin return to normal after an average of 22.67 months. The mercury in these 18 people did not come entirely from cosmetics.

In the first few days after losing a loved one, do not stay alone; those with heart disease, hypertension, or diabetes should continue taking their medication regularly; if you feel crushing chest pain, call 120
A

On the first day after a loved one passes away, the risk of a heart attack is 21.1 times higher than normal, then gradually decreases day by day. For people aged 60 to 89, in the 30 days after a spouse dies, the rate of heart attack or stroke approximately doubles, then drops after one month. Those with existing cardiovascular disease should not stop their medication during these days. If you experience crushing chest pain, difficulty breathing, or weakness on one side of the body, call 120 immediately.
Free. Do not stay alone during these days, and continue taking medication as usual.

1,985 patients with acute myocardial infarction were each compared to themselves at different time intervals before the onset of the disease. Among them, 270 people (13.6%) lost a significant person within 6 months before the onset, and 19 people lost someone within 1 day before the heart attack. In the 24 hours after a significant person passed away, the rate of acute myocardial infarction increased 21.1 times (95% CI 13.1 to 34.1, meaning the true increase lies roughly between 13 and 34 times). It then decreased daily. Translated into actual numbers: in a group with a 10-year heart attack risk of 5%, there is 1 additional case for every 1,394 people who just lost a loved one. In a group with a 20% risk, there is 1 additional case for every 320 people. Another study in the UK compared 30,447 widowed individuals aged 60 to 89 with 83,588 controls in similar conditions. In the 30 days after losing a partner, the widowed group had 50 people (0.16%) suffer a heart attack or stroke. The control group had 67 people (0.08%). IRR = 2.20 (1.52 to 3.15), meaning the likelihood of an event is about 2.2 times that of the control. Specifically, for heart attack it was 2.14 (1.20 to 3.81), about 2.1 times. For stroke it was 2.40 (1.22 to 4.71), about 2.4 times. After 30 days, the risk decreased. Within 90 days, the study also examined two other conditions. One is acute coronary syndrome other than myocardial infarction (acute cardiac ischemia but not yet a heart attack), IRR = 2.20 (1.12 to 4.29). The second is pulmonary embolism (blood clot blocking a vessel in the lungs), IRR = 2.37 (1.18 to 4.75). How to recognize these diseases: The UK National Health Service (NHS) lists signs that require an immediate emergency call. A heart attack is chest pain that feels like pressure or squeezing, which may radiate to the arms, neck, or jaw, accompanied by shortness of breath. A stroke is one side of the face drooping, one arm or one side of the body feeling weak or numb, and slurred speech.
In the week you receive a serious diagnosis, do not go to get the results alone; postpone all decisions other than medical treatment
A

In the first week after receiving a cancer diagnosis, the risk of suicide is 12.6 times higher than those not diagnosed, and the risk of death from cardiovascular disease is 5.6 times higher. By the end of the first year, the suicide risk decreases to 3.1 times; the more difficult the cancer is to treat, the more pronounced this is. Therefore, bring someone with you when collecting results and do not stay home alone. Quitting your job, selling your house—save those matters for after your next appointment.
Free. Ask someone to accompany you to get the results. Postpone major non-medical decisions for a few days.

The Swedish national registry followed over 6.07 million people (6,073,240 people) from 1991 to 2006. Compared to those not diagnosed with cancer, the relative risk of suicide in the first week after diagnosis was 12.6 (95% CI 8.6 to 17.8), or approximately 12.6 times. The true level lies roughly between 8.6 and 17.8 times. The incidence rate during this week was 2.50/1,000 person-years, meaning 2.5 cases per 1,000 people followed for one year. By the first year, this decreased to 3.1 (2.7 to 3.5; 0.60/1,000 person-years), or about 3.1 times. Cardiovascular mortality in the first week was 5.6 (5.2 to 5.9; 116.80/1,000 person-years), or about 5.6 times. In the first four weeks, it was 3.3 (3.1 to 3.4; 65.81/1,000 person-years). The increased risk level decreases rapidly during the first year after diagnosis. The more difficult the cancer is to treat and the lower the survival probability, the more pronounced the increase. Comparing each patient with themselves at different time intervals yielded the same conclusion.
If you lose your job, first maintain your daily routine, keep your health insurance, and maintain a steady job-seeking pace; do not stay cooped up at home all day
A

People who lose their jobs later have a mortality rate about six-tenths higher than those currently working; this is more pronounced in men and younger people, with the first ten years being the highest. Excluding the effects of smoking and alcohol, the increase is reduced by about one-quarter; this part you can control yourself. First, register for unemployment and receive unemployment benefits.
Free. First, register for unemployment and receive unemployment benefits (China), then schedule job-seeking as a fixed routine. The difficulty is waking up on time when no one is urging you.

A meta-analysis of 42 studies, 235 mortality risk estimates, involving over 20 million people. After adjusting for age and other conditions, the all-cause mortality risk for unemployed individuals had an average HR of 1.63, about six-tenths higher than those currently working. Men were higher than women. The effect was clear for those in the early and middle stages of their careers, and smaller in the late stage. The risk was highest in the first ten years of follow-up, then decreased. In studies that accounted for health behaviors such as smoking and alcohol, the average HR was 24% lower, meaning the calculated increase was reduced by about one-quarter.
If a loved one dies by suicide, accident, or homicide, do not expect to endure it alone; proactively seek professional help
A

People whose spouse dies by suicide are about eight-tenths (men) and seven-tenths (women) more likely to be diagnosed with a mental disorder within 5 years compared to the general population. Compared to those whose partner died of other causes, it is also 70%–100% higher, or 1.7–2 times. People who lose loved ones this way often feel alienated by others and feel ashamed. This is precisely why you must proactively find someone and not wait to get better on your own.
Calling 12356 is free. If you want to see a doctor, visit a psychological clinic; the price is the same as a regular check-up. The difficulty is opening up to ask for help.

The Danish national registry followed 6.7 million adults from 1980 to 2014, totaling over 136 million person-years. For those widowed by a partner's suicide, the IRR for a new mental disorder diagnosis within 5 years compared to the general population was 1.8 for men (95% CI 1.6 to 2.0), or about eight-tenths higher. For women, it was 1.7 (1.6 to 1.8), or about seven-tenths higher. Compared to those widowed by a partner's death from other causes, the IRR for men was 1.7 (1.5 to 1.9) and for women was 2.0 (1.9 to 2.2), which is 70%–100% higher, or 1.7–2 times. In this group, the rates of suicidal behavior, mortality, and the need for local government assistance were also higher. The risk of physical illnesses such as cirrhosis and sleep disorders also increased. Another review looked at each of 57 studies individually without pooling numbers. Bereavement by suicide was associated with four things: First, an increased suicide risk for the partner. Second, after a child's suicide, an increased risk of psychiatric hospitalization for parents. Third, after an adult child's suicide, an increased suicide risk for the mother. Fourth, after a parent's suicide, an increased risk of depression for the child. Compared to those who lost loved ones to other violent deaths, those bereaved by suicide reported feeling more alienated and ashamed.
In the first six months after losing a spouse, assign three meals, sleep, chronic medication, and follow-up schedules to a specific person to watch over
A

Less than six months after losing a partner, the probability of death within the same period is about four-tenths higher than those not widowed. After six months, it decreases to about 15% higher. For men, it is about 23% higher; in women, the difference is so small it might just be a coincidence. What should be done is to hand over medication, meals, and follow-up appointments to a specific person; do not rely on your own memory.
Free. Find a specific person—children, siblings, or friends—and ask them to visit or call periodically. The difficulty is speaking up to entrust them with this.

A meta-analysis of 15 prospective cohort studies involving 2,263,888 people. For those widowed for less than 6 months, the mortality RR was 1.41 (95% CI 1.26 to 1.57), meaning the probability of death in the same period was about four-tenths higher than non-widowed individuals. After 6 months, it was 1.14 (1.10 to 1.18), decreasing to about 15% higher. For men, the RR was 1.23 (1.18 to 1.28), about 23% higher. For women, it was 1.04 (1.00 to 1.08, not statistically significant, meaning this difference could be a coincidence). No clear difference was found between the group under 65 and those 65 and older. Another analysis pooled 123 papers, 1,377 risk estimates, and over 500 million people. After adjusting for differences in conditions, the HR was 1.23 (1.19 to 1.28), or generally about 23% higher. Men remained higher than women. Men were 1.27 (1.19 to 1.35), 27% higher. Women were 1.15 (1.08 to 1.22), 15% higher.
If you have no relatives or friends, replace "someone to watch over you" with three things: a neighbor who can enter your home, a community visitation list, and emergency contacts in your phone
B

If you have no relatives or friends, you need to worry about two things: someone discovering you if something happens, and taking medication and eating on time daily. For medication and meals, manage them yourself: write a list, set alarms, and do not rely on memory. For being discovered, rely on three things: give a neighbor a spare key, ask the community committee to be put on a visitation care list, and set up emergency contacts in your phone and do not turn it off.
Free. The difficulty is proactively speaking up and telling a neighbor or the community committee (China), "I live alone, and something just happened at home."

44,573 outpatients, all with a risk or history of atherothrombotic disease (a type of vascular disease with plaque, prone to blockage by blood clots). They were enrolled by doctors in various countries into the international REACH project for follow-up, entering the study from December 2003 to December 2004, and followed for 4 years. Among them, 8,594 people (19%) lived alone. Over 4 years, all-cause mortality for those living alone was 14.1%, while for those living with others it was 11.1%. Cardiovascular mortality was 8.6% compared to 6.8%. Both log-rank tests had P<0.01, meaning the difference is unlikely to be by chance. The difference varied by age group (interaction P=0.03). From ages 45 to 65, mortality for those living alone versus those living with others was 7.7% vs 5.7%. Adjusting for other conditions, the HR was 1.24 (95% CI 1.01 to 1.51), about 24% higher. From ages 66 to 80, it was 13.2% vs 12.3%, HR 1.12 (1.01 to 1.26), about one-tenth higher. Over age 80, it was 24.6% vs 28.4%, HR 0.92 (0.79 to 1.06), showing no increase. A 2022 guideline from the Ministry of Civil Affairs (China) and nine other departments stipulates the implementation of visitation care services. The targets are elderly people living alone, living in empty-nest homes, left behind in rural areas while children work elsewhere, those who have lost the ability to care for themselves, the severely disabled, and families under special family planning policies. The format includes "regular home visits, phone calls, video calls, and remote monitoring." Townships and sub-districts conduct screenings, and village or community committees provide support, gathering basic information and "wishes to receive visitation care services," incorporating them into grassroots grid management (divided by area, assigned to specific monitors). By the end of 2025, "ensure the monthly visitation rate for elderly people in extreme difficulty reaches 100%," and "for elderly people in extreme difficulty who have lost the ability to care for themselves, visitation care shall be no less than once a month." The document also encourages families to install smart calling systems, smart electricity and water meters, health monitoring products, and elderly care monitoring devices, so that "once an abnormality is detected, a timely alarm is triggered and an SMS is simultaneously sent to emergency contacts." If a service provider discovers an emergency, they "must immediately assist in calling emergency services."
If a parent passes away, tell the child the truth and let them attend the farewell ceremony
B

Children who lose a parent before age 18 are about five-tenths more likely to die later in life than children who do not experience this. If a parent dies by accident or suicide, the risk is about eight-tenths higher; if by illness, it is about three-tenths higher. The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends telling children the truth about what happened and supporting their attendance at funerals and farewell ceremonies.
Free. The difficulty is that you are also in pain but still must explain clearly to your child.

Calculated from the entire population born in Denmark from 1968 to 2008, and in Sweden from 1973 to 2006. Additionally, 89.3% of people born in Finland from 1987 to 2007 were sampled. Totaling over 7.3 million people. Among them, 189,094 lost a parent before age 18. The all-cause mortality rate for this group of children was 50% higher than those who did not lose a parent (mortality rate ratio 1.50, 95% CI 1.43 to 1.58, or about 1.5 times). Parents dying from unnatural causes such as accidents or suicide was 1.84 (1.71 to 2.00), about eight-tenths higher. Dying from natural causes such as illness was 1.33 (1.24 to 1.41), about three-tenths higher. The risk was highest when the child's cause of death was the same as the parent's. A 2016 clinical report from the American Academy of Pediatrics for pediatricians required: when talking to children who have just lost a loved one, explain clearly what happened, what it means, and correct misinformation and misunderstandings the child may have heard. The report also provided suggestions on how to support children attending funerals and other farewell rituals.
If grief remains stagnant after six months and daily life is unbearable, visit a psychiatric or clinical psychology department
A

About one in ten adults who lose a loved one becomes stuck. If after more than half a year you still miss the deceased so much that you cannot eat, work, or care for your children, feel numb, and feel that life has no meaning. This is not about not being strong enough; it has diagnostic criteria and its own treatment. Specialized therapy has a 51% response rate, while conventional psychotherapy is 28%, and it works faster.
Consultation fees plus treatment fees. This type of therapy follows a course, averaging 16 sessions over 19 weeks in trials. The difficulty is taking the step to go for a check-up.

A meta-analysis of 14 studies involving adults whose loved ones did not die from violence and who were not currently seeking psychiatric care. The prevalence of Prolonged Grief Disorder was 9.8% (95% CI 6.8 to 14.0), meaning about 10 out of every 100 adults who lose a loved one. The rate increases with age. Another study tested the accuracy of these diagnostic criteria, selecting 291 bereaved individuals and interviewing them three times at 0–6, 6–12, and 12–24 months after the loss. The core manifestation of the diagnosis is intense yearning for the deceased. Plus at least five of the following nine manifestations. The first five are emotional numbness, shock, feeling life is meaningless, mistrusting others, and distress over the loss. The last four are difficulty accepting the loss, identity confusion, avoiding reality, and inability to move on. These manifestations must occur daily or be severe enough to impair functioning. And they must persist at least 6 months after the loss, still affecting daily life. A trial of 95 people randomized into two groups for 16 therapy sessions over an average of 19 weeks found that therapy targeting complicated grief had a 51% response rate. Conventional interpersonal psychotherapy was 28% (P=0.02, difference unlikely to be by chance). The former also worked faster. The number needed to treat (NNT) was 4.3, meaning on average, for every 4.3 people treated, one more person improved.
Do not rush to spend money on grief counseling; first see if your sadness is truly stuck (see the manifestations in item 8)
A

Arranging psychological counseling for all bereaved individuals provides very small benefits that disappear shortly after, as most people will naturally recover. However, for those clearly unable to adapt, therapy is as effective as treating other psychological issues. Therefore, first check against item 8 (if grief is stuck, visit a psychiatric department); if it matches, then spend this money.
Free; in fact, it saves a portion of counseling fees.

A meta-analysis of 61 controlled studies. Universal psychological intervention for bereaved individuals showed very small benefits immediately after completion, which disappeared upon follow-up. Interventions that only accepted bereaved individuals who were "clearly unable to adapt" were as effective as psychotherapy for other psychological issues. Studies without pre-screening showed poor results because the non-intervention group also naturally recovered over time. A meta-analysis of 14 randomized trials: therapy for those with existing problems was significantly better than the control both immediately after therapy and at follow-up, with the effect size increasing over time. Universal preventive intervention for those without problems was not effective. Another study followed 205 people from before widowhood to 6 and 18 months after. This study identified five patterns of progression: common grief, chronic grief, chronic depression, improvement during bereavement, and resilience. Resilience was the most common pattern, while common grief was relatively rare.
After separation or divorce, do not let health insurance lapse, and do not rely on alcohol to cope
A

Separated or divorced individuals have a significantly higher risk of early death compared to those still married; the increase is greater for men and younger people. This is not necessarily caused by the divorce itself; divorced individuals may already differ in health and income. There are two things you can maintain yourself: do not let health insurance lapse, and do not rely on cigarettes or alcohol to cope.
Free. Continue paying for health insurance (China), quit alcohol. The difficulty is that it is very easy to rely on alcohol to cope during this time.

A meta-analysis of 32 prospective cohort studies involving over 6.5 million people, 160,000 deaths, and over 755,000 divorces across 11 countries. Compared to those still married, separated or divorced adults had a significantly increased risk of early death. The increase was more pronounced for men and younger individuals than for women and older individuals. The authors discussed four possible pathways. First, social selection: individuals who already differ in health or conditions are more likely to divorce. Second, loss of resources: income and insurance coverage are cut. Third, changes in health behavior: smoking, alcohol, and routines worsen. Fourth, chronic psychological pressure (prolonged stress).
If you need someone to talk to, call 12356; minors and youth call 12355; if you need to see a doctor, visit a psychological clinic
B

If you want to find someone to talk to, call 12356, the national psychological support hotline (China), which is free. Minors and youth also have the 12355 comprehensive service platform for youth. If you want to see a doctor, visit a psychological clinic in a psychiatric department, psychology department, or clinical psychology department. In the event of family crises, job loss, or dropping out of school, community grid officers and social workers are responsible for proactive detection.
Free. Both hotlines are free. Psychological clinics issue appointments like regular check-ups.

A 2026 plan from the National Health Commission (China) and 25 other departments requires improving the working system of the 12356 psychological support hotline. Stable operation must be ensured, and the connection rate increased. The construction of provincial-level 12356 information platforms must be promoted. Coordination mechanisms with service lines like 110 must be strengthened. The 12355 comprehensive service platform for youth must be well-built and utilized, coordinating with 12356. There are three goals for 2030. First, over 80% of administrative villages and urban communities should have psychological counseling rooms or social work rooms providing psychological services. Second, all public psychiatric specialty hospitals at all levels, and at least one hospital in each county (district), should provide psychological clinic services. Third, each province should complete the construction of a provincial-level 12356 psychological support platform. Psychological crisis intervention and support teams consist of psychiatrists, psychotherapists, psychological counselors, professional social workers, and volunteers. The plan also requires three groups of people to pay attention in daily life for early detection: grid officers (those in charge of specific areas within a community), professional social workers, and volunteers. They must promptly detect psychological crisis risks caused by family crises, job loss, or dropping out of school (National, issued March 2026).
For the first three months after a major incident, postpone all major irreversible decisions
B

During this time, your ability to judge "opportunities" is at its worst. In experiments, people in a sad state were willing to accept between 10% and 30% less money just to avoid waiting 3 months. Any matter where the amount exceeds one month's income, or where changing your mind would incur a very high price, should be postponed for three months. First, tell someone who has no vested interest in the matter; do not finalize anything on the same day.
Costs no money, only involves postponing a decision, though some opportunities might be missed as a result. The difficulty is that at the time, you will feel like opportunities wait for no one.

Avoid disposing of assets in an irreversible manner right when you have just been struck by a crisis, as judgment is at its weakest. These actions include selling a house, quitting a job, investing pension or compensation funds in a lump sum, rushing into remarriage, or acting as a guarantor for others. The amounts involved in these decisions usually range from tens of thousands of yuan to an entire house, so the benefit is ranked as medium. Official documents (China) also classify "family crisis, job loss, dropping out of school" as psychological crisis risks that communities must proactively screen for; the state during this period is already considered to require outside help. The grief guidelines from the U.S. National Institute on Aging (NIA) list "great difficulty making decisions" as a common manifestation of grief. The NIA advises: if you have a choice, postpone major life decisions until you feel better. When grieving, you may not be thinking clearly; it is best not to make major changes like selling a house or quitting a job. One study conducted three experiments. Researchers randomly assigned groups, putting some participants into a sad state, then gave them a choice between "receiving money now" or "receiving money 3 months later." Compared to people in a normal mood, those who were sad were willing to accept 13% to 34% less money to avoid waiting 3 months. This was sadness induced in an experiment, not the actual loss of a loved one. In 2023, the U.S. Federal Trade Commission (FTC) warned of a scam: someone impersonates a funeral home, telling the family that if they don't pay immediately, the funeral will be canceled. The first tip the FTC provides is to resist the pressure to "act immediately"; a legitimate business will give you time to decide.
Do not view death as a way to pay off debt: life insurance does not pay out within two years, it is not recognized as a work-related accident, and debts are still deducted from the estate first
A

For life insurance contracts, suicide within two years results in no payout, only a refund of the small amount of refundable value in the contract. It is also not recognized as a work-related accident; none of the three types of payments for death due to work-related accidents are provided. Debts are deducted first from the estate you leave behind; family members only receive the remainder. They also bear the health costs mentioned in Section 4 of this chapter (loss of a loved one due to suicide or violent death).
Costs no money, just a matter of calculating this clearly.

Article 44 of the Insurance Law (China) applies to contracts where the death of the insured is the condition for payment. Starting from the date the contract is established or the date it is reinstated, if the insured commits suicide within two years, the insurance company is not liable for the insurance payout. If the insured is a person without civil capacity at the time of suicide—meaning someone the law considers unable to be responsible for their actions—this case does not apply. In the event of non-payment, the insurance company must refund the cash value of the contract as agreed, meaning only the small amount of refundable money in the contract is returned, not the sum insured. Life insurance amounts are usually around several hundred thousand yuan, so the benefit is ranked as high. Article 16, Clause 3 of the Work-Related Injury Insurance Regulations (China) stipulates: self-inflicted injury or suicide is not recognized as a work-related accident or treated as such. The three types of benefits for death due to work-related accidents under Article 39 are therefore all lost. First is the funeral subsidy, equal to 6 months of the average monthly salary of local workers in the previous year. Second is the pension for dependent relatives. Third is the lump-sum work-related death subsidy, equal to 20 times the national per capita disposable income of urban residents in the previous year. Article 1159 of the Civil Code (China) stipulates: the distribution of an estate must first settle the taxes and debts that the deceased was legally required to pay, meaning the estate pays taxes and debts first, and only the remainder is distributed. Article 1161 stipulates: heirs settle debts within the limit of the actual value of the estate received, meaning they only use the inheritance to pay and do not have to use their own money; those who renounce the inheritance may not be held liable for payment.

If you experience a car accident, assault, or natural disaster, do not rely on a single psychological debriefing session immediately after the event; if nightmares, flashbacks, and constant anxiety remain severe after one month, see a psychiatric department for trauma-focused psychotherapy
A

When a major event occurs, experiencing nightmares and being easily startled in the first few weeks is very common; most people will recover on their own. If symptoms remain severe after one month, it may be Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD); psychotherapy specifically targeting trauma is clearly effective. However, the type of session that pulls people in immediately after an event to recount everything once—a single debriefing session—does not prevent this illness. In one trial, those who did it were even worse off after three years.
Cost of examination plus treatment fees, usually 8 to 12 sessions. The difficulty is that therapy requires you to go back and touch upon the experiences you are most afraid to remember.

The "Guidelines for Diagnosis and Treatment of Mental Disorders (2020 Edition)" by the National Health Commission (China) clearly states: on average, about 8% of people who experience mental trauma will develop PTSD. There are three core manifestations. First are nightmares, flashbacks, and the scene of the event constantly reoccurring. Second is avoiding topics, places, and people related to the event. Third is being constantly alert, easily startled, and suffering from insomnia. A diagnosis is only made if symptoms last more than 1 month and severely affect family, school, or work. In the section on acute stress disorder, the guidelines state that most people recover through self-adjustment or acute-phase crisis intervention. For treatment effectiveness, see a 2020 meta-analysis of 114 randomized controlled trials involving 8,171 people. Trauma-focused cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) compared to waiting for treatment or usual care had an SMD of −1.32 (95% CI from −1.57 to −1.08), with moderate quality evidence. Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR) was −1.23 (from −1.69 to −0.76), with low quality evidence. SMD and d are the same measure; 0.8 or higher is considered large; both methods exceeded this mark. General supportive counseling compared to waiting for treatment showed no difference (−0.43, from −0.90 to 0.04). A 2013 Cochrane review by the same group of authors included 70 trials and 4,761 people, showing the same direction. Trauma-focused CBT was −1.62 (from −2.03 to −1.21), and EMDR was −1.17 (from −2.04 to −0.30). However, at that time, the quality of evidence was rated as very low. The 2018 NICE guidelines (UK) are organized as follows: Adults with severe symptoms within one month of the event receive individual trauma-focused CBT. The same applies after one month if diagnosed or symptoms are clear, usually 8 to 12 sessions. For non-combat trauma that has not resolved after 3 months, EMDR is added. For mild symptoms not meeting diagnostic criteria, monitor for the first month and schedule a follow-up within a month. The psychotherapies listed in domestic (China) regulations are also these types: prolonged exposure, cognitive processing therapy, and EMDR. Regarding single-session debriefing immediately after the event, see three documents. Cochrane 2002 pooled 11 trials: a single individual debriefing session does not reduce distress nor prevent PTSD. At 3 to 5 months, the OR was 1.22 (from 0.60 to 2.46), showing no difference. One trial followed up for 1 year, where those who received debriefing had a higher risk of the disorder, OR 2.88 (from 1.11 to 7.53), about 2.9 times. The authors concluded that traumatized individuals should no longer be mandated to participate in such debriefings. Another trial selected hospitalized patients after car accidents, randomized into groups. After 3 years, the debriefed group was significantly worse regarding psychiatric symptoms, travel anxiety, pain, physical problems, general functioning, and financial problems. For those who initially had severe flashbacks and avoidance, those who were debriefed still had symptoms 3 years later, while those who weren't had recovered. NICE guidelines clearly state: do not provide psychological debriefing primarily to prevent or treat PTSD. The reason is that neither individual nor group sessions showed benefit, and there were signs of being worse than doing nothing.
If a child says they have sudden, severe pain that is getting worse: take them to the hospital immediately, do not let them endure it until school is over
A

Some illnesses are measured in hours. A boy suddenly experiencing severe pain on one side of the scrotum could be testicular torsion, meaning the spermatic cord connecting to the testicle is twisted, cutting off blood flow. If treated within 6 hours, the testicular salvage rate is 97.2%. If left for 19 to 24 hours, it drops to 42.5%. This pain cannot wait until school is over, nor can it wait until after an exam.
Costs no money. Take half a day off and take the child to the emergency room.

A systematic review gathered 30 case series reports involving 2,116 patients with testicular torsion for pooled analysis. Among them, 1,283 cases were categorized by 6-hour intervals. Counting from the onset of pain, the salvage rate for 0 to 6 hours was 97.2%. 7 to 12 hours: 79.3%. 13 to 18 hours: 61.3%. 19 to 24 hours: 42.5%. 25 to 48 hours: 24.4%. Over 48 hours: 7.4%. Grouped into larger intervals: within 12 hours was 90.4%, 13 to 24 hours was 54.0%, and over 24 hours was 18.1%.
