The service period is three years, during which, under equal conditions, benefits are the same as those for permanent teachers in local public schools. After three years, if the evaluation is satisfactory and the teacher wishes to stay, the regulations require they be promptly granted permanent establishment.

No monetary cost. The price is three years of teaching at a rural compulsory education school, and you must pass the teacher certification exam before entering. The difficulty lies in staying for the full three years.

The 2024 Special Post Teacher plan notice states the recruitment conditions are: "requires a bachelor's degree or higher, primarily in education; for primary schools, graduates from teacher training colleges may be appropriately recruited." "No older than 30 years." A corresponding teacher certificate is also required. The notice also states: "Volunteers who participated in the 'Western Program for University Student Volunteers,' have teaching experience, and education graduates who have completed a teaching internship of half a year or more shall be given priority for recruitment under equal conditions." "Support and encourage qualified discharged military personnel to teach in primary and secondary schools; factors such as years of service may be considered to appropriately relax the age limit for discharged military personnel." Regarding benefits and permanent establishment, see these sentences: "From January 1, 2024, the salary subsidy for special post teachers will be increased; the central budget... for the central region will increase from an average of ⟦35200⟧ per person per year to ⟦38800⟧, and for the western region from ⟦38200⟧ to ⟦41800⟧." "Under equal conditions, they shall enjoy the same benefits as permanent teachers in local public schools regarding salaries, bonuses, professional title evaluations, awards, and annual evaluations." "Ensure that special post teachers who complete three years of service with a satisfactory evaluation and wish to stay are promptly granted permanent establishment and assigned job positions, and that the transition of personnel relations, salaries, and continuity of professional and teaching seniority is handled well, with no further probation period applied" (National).
Firefighters and military civilian personnel are two other public recruitment channels with lower thresholds than the civil service exam
A

Neither of these paths is blocked by a "junior college or higher" threshold. Firefighters recruit individuals aged 18 to 22 with a high school education or higher; those with a junior college degree or higher and discharged soldiers have the limit relaxed to 24. Military civilian personnel only need to be at least 18 years old, with entry-level positions recruiting up to a maximum age of 35. The common trade-off is that political vetting and medical examinations will filter out some candidates.

No monetary cost. From registration to recruitment, one must pass a medical exam, political vetting, physical fitness test, psychological test, and interview, which takes several months in total. The difficulty lies in the fact that each stage filters out candidates.

For firefighters, see the "Measures for the Recruitment of Firefighters for the National Comprehensive Fire and Rescue Team" (China). Basic conditions in Article 5 include "aged 18 to 22" (including those exactly 22; see specific recruitment notices for exact deadlines) and "having a high school education or higher." Article 6: "For those with a junior college degree or higher, discharged soldiers from the PLA and People's Armed Police, and personnel from government professional fire teams and forest fire teams with 2 or more years of actual firefighting and rescue experience, the age limit may be relaxed to 24; for special professional talents urgently needed for fire and rescue work, with approval from the Ministry of Emergency Management, the age limit may be further relaxed, in principle not exceeding 28 years." Article 7: "Firefighters are recruited publicly from society, mainly from permanent residents of the provincial-level region, but may also be recruited from other provinces when necessary." Article 9 lists the recruitment process as "publicity and mobilization, organized registration, qualification review, medical examination, political vetting, physical fitness and job suitability testing, psychological testing and interview, public listing, and recruitment." For military civilian personnel, see Article 18 of the "Regulations on Civilian Personnel of the Chinese People's Liberation Army": "The military implements a recruitment system for civilian personnel that combines open competitive examination, direct recruitment of talents, and specialized recruitment." These are three tracks: open exams to recruit people, direct attraction of existing talent, and dedicated recruitment for specific groups. Basic conditions in Article 9 of these regulations include "at least 18 years old," "meeting the political conditions for military recruitment of civilian personnel," and "having the educational level, professional level, and work ability suitable for the position requirements." Article 19 specifies that the maximum age for first-time recruitment into low-level positions is 35. The regulations also state "civilian positions must prioritize the recruitment of qualified discharged military personnel" (National).

Degrees are not a one-time deal: self-study exams have no age or prior education limits, adult college entrance exams and open universities can make up for education; degrees only count if searchable on CHSI, do not register for 'exam-free guaranteed pass' upgrade classes
A

If you couldn't continue your studies at 18, there are still three formal paths: self-study exams, adult college entrance exams, and open universities. Self-study exams have no age or prior education limits, but students currently in full-time education cannot register. Graduation certificates must be searchable on the CHSI (China) website to count; once searchable, schools cannot change them. If anyone says "no study required" or "exam-free guaranteed pass," do not pay them.

Registration fees and textbook costs are a few hundred yuan per year. The price is long-term self-study or part-time study; a part-time top-up program from junior college to a bachelor's degree takes at least two and a half years; the difficulty lies in long-term persistence.

For self-study exams, see the "Interim Regulations on Higher Education Self-Study Examinations" (China). Article 3: "Citizens of the People's Republic of China, regardless of gender, age, ethnicity, race, and prior educational level, may participate in higher education self-study examinations according to the provisions of these regulations." Article 20: "Students currently studying in formal schools of all levels and types may not register for the exam." Article 25 lists three conditions for obtaining a graduation certificate: passing all subjects, completing a graduation thesis or practical task, and receiving a satisfactory evaluation of ideological character. Fulfilling these leads to the issuance of a graduation certificate. This article also states "those who receive a junior college (foundation level) or undergraduate graduation certificate shall have their education recognized by the State." Article 32 discusses the salary treatment of degree holders: "unemployed persons after recruitment shall be treated the same as graduates of the same type from ordinary universities and colleges." Article 21 of the Higher Education Law (China): "The State implements a higher education self-study examination system; those who pass the exams shall be issued a diploma or other corresponding academic certificates." For adult college entrance exams, see the "Measures for the Recruitment of National Adult Higher Education Institutions in 2025" (China). The target audience for registration is "working people and others in society, excluding students currently studying in secondary schools, universities, and colleges with state-recognized education." "Candidates registering for high-school-to-undergraduate or high-school-to-junior-college programs must have graduated from high school or have equivalent academic ability. Candidates registering for junior-college-to-undergraduate top-up programs must already hold... a junior college graduation certificate, a certificate of completion of an undergraduate program or higher." "The shortest study period for full-time programs is: four years for high-school-to-undergraduate, and two years for high-school-to-junior-college and junior-college-to-undergraduate top-up; the shortest study period for part-time programs is: five years for high-school-to-undergraduate, and two and a half years for high-school-to-junior-college and junior-college-to-undergraduate top-up." Full-time means quitting work to study all day at school; part-time means not quitting work, working while studying. For open universities, see the "Opinions of the Ministry of Education on Doing a Good Job in Open Universities" (China). The document states: "Open universities implement registration-based admission; learners who complete courses and earn corresponding credits shall be issued course certificates; those who earn the required credits and meet relevant requirements shall be issued corresponding diplomas and non-degree certificates; those qualified for a degree shall be granted the corresponding degree" (National). To check if a degree is real or fake, see the "Measures for Electronic Registration of Student Status and Education of University and College Students" by the Ministry of Education (China). Article 2 explicitly states that self-study exam graduation certificates must also be electronically registered. Article 5: The CHSI website "is the only website for querying electronic registration information of student status and education of university and college students." Article 19: After education is registered and made searchable online, "schools may not change the content of the diploma or the registration information." For red lines in recruitment advertising, see the 2021 notice from the Ministry of Education (China) and five other agencies. Advertisements for continuing education offering degrees "must not contain false or violating content such as 'no study required' or 'no classes required'." They also "must not contain explicit or implied guarantees of educational outcomes such as 'fast degree,' 'exam-free guaranteed pass,' or 'refund if you fail'." Institutions such as training institutes or research academies are not authorized to grant degrees, and advertisements must not equate them with degree-granting universities.
Flexible employment without joining an organization: pension and medical insurance must be handled personally at the place of work, household registration limits have been removed
A

Not joining an organization or unit does not mean social insurance is no longer relevant; it just means no one is paying the other half for you. Regulations require localities to remove household registration (hukou) limits for flexible workers to participate in insurance at their place of work, with a few megacities allowed to phase this out gradually. Therefore, do not misunderstand "freedom" as not needing to worry about social insurance. If payments are intermittent, both the pension and medical insurance payouts will be calculated according to the rules for interrupted contributions.

You must pay the full amount for pension and medical insurance yourself, calculated based on the local contribution base, which is over ⟦1000⟧ per month. The contribution base is a standard figure used to calculate insurance premiums. This is the fixed expense most often overlooked when working flexibly; the difficulty is making payments on time every month.

Regarding insurance participation, see the "Guiding Opinions on Protecting the Labor Rights and Interests of Workers in New Forms of Employment" (China). The document states: "Localities must remove household registration limits for flexible workers to participate in basic pension insurance and basic medical insurance at their place of work; some megacities that find it difficult to do so in one step must combine local realities and actively create conditions to phase them out gradually. Organize flexible workers who have not participated in basic pension insurance for employees and basic medical insurance for employees to participate in basic pension insurance for urban and rural residents and basic medical insurance for urban and rural residents according to regulations, ensuring that everyone who needs insurance has it. Urge enterprises to participate in social insurance according to the law. Enterprises must guide and support workers in new forms of employment who do not fully meet the conditions for establishing a labor relationship to participate in social insurance suitable for their situation." The same document divides labor usage into three types: "If the conditions for establishing a labor relationship are met, the enterprise must sign a labor contract with the worker according to the law. If the conditions for establishing a labor relationship are not fully met but the enterprise exercises labor management over the worker... then guide the enterprise and the worker to sign a written agreement... Individuals who rely on a platform to independently conduct business activities or work as freelancers... their rights and obligations are governed by civil law" (National, since 2021).
Food delivery, ride-hailing, and intra-city freight: platforms pay occupational injury insurance for you per order, you do not have to pay
A

For food delivery workers, ride-hailing drivers, and intra-city freight carriers, the platform must pay occupational injury insurance for you per order; you do not spend a penny, and every order you accept is insured. This is still a pilot program; before accepting orders, check if your province and platform are within the scope. Those who already have a labor relationship with the platform are covered by work-related injury insurance and do not follow this mechanism.

No monetary cost; this amount is paid by the platform. Your job is to check if the platform you are taking orders from is part of the pilot. There are two ways: look for the "occupational injury protection" section on the insurance or benefits page in the app, or call your provincial Department of Human Resources and Social Security (China) to ask if the platform is registered.

For this protection, see the "Measures for Occupational Injury Protection for Workers in New Forms of Employment (Trial)" (China). Article 2 states: "Platform enterprises must participate in occupational injury protection for workers in new forms of employment according to the provisions of these measures... pay occupational injury protection fees for workers in new forms of employment who register and receive orders through the platform, providing various types of labor such as travel, instant delivery, and intra-city freight in the name of the platform enterprise to receive remuneration or income, ensuring every order is insured and every person is insured. Workers who fall under the scope of the 'Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance' must be covered by work-related injury insurance by the enterprise according to the law, and these measures shall not apply to them." Article 9: "During the trial period, the travel industry shall implement a rate of ⟦0.01⟧ per order; the instant delivery industry shall implement rates of ⟦0.07⟧ and ⟦0.25⟧ per order; the intra-city freight industry shall implement a rate of ⟦0.18⟧ per order." Regarding the expansion of the pilot, see this section: "From July 1, 2025, based on the 7 provinces and 7 platform enterprises previously piloted... 10 more provinces will be added: Tianjin, Hebei, Liaoning, Zhejiang, Anhui, Fujian, Shandong, Hubei, Guangxi, and Ningxia... In 2026, promote the implementation of occupational injury protection pilots in all 31 provinces and the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps; bring all platform enterprises in the three industries of travel, instant delivery, and intra-city freight into the scope of occupational injury protection pilots" (Pilot, expanding gradually each year).
Two paths that almost guarantee permanent establishment on the day of university application: government-funded education students and targeted medical students, the price is a 6-year commitment
A

In both paths, the State pays for you upfront, and upon graduation, you follow the agreement to work in a designated location for 6 years. Government-funded education students are only recruited at six normal universities directly under the Ministry of Education, through early-batch admission. Targeted medical students must sign a tripartite agreement before receiving their admission notice. Breaking the commitment requires refunding the money, paying a penalty, and being recorded in the social credit system (China). Think carefully about whether you can accept these 6 years before filling out your preferences.

You do not have to pay tuition or dormitory fees and even receive a living allowance. The price is that for 6 years after graduation, you cannot freely choose your job; breaking the commitment requires refunding the money, paying a penalty, and being recorded in the social credit system (China), which records the fulfillment or breach of promises. The difficulty lies in the inability to change the workplace during these 6 years.

For government-funded education students, see the "Measures for the Implementation of Government-Funded Education for Undergraduate-Master's Integrated Education Students at Normal Universities Directly Under the Ministry of Education" (China) (2024, the 2018 measures were simultaneously abolished). Article 2: The central budget covers tuition, dormitory fees during the study period, and living allowances. Article 3: The focus is on training for levels at or below the prefecture level (city, prefecture, league) outside provincial capitals in the central and western regions. This article also states "no orientation for teaching in municipalities directly under the Central Government, cities specifically designated in the state plan, or the main urban areas of provincial capitals (except for the five autonomous regions, provinces with land borders, Hainan Province, Guizhou Province, and Qinghai Province)." Article 9: After graduation, students generally return to teach in primary or secondary schools in the oriented prefecture (city, prefecture, league) of their province of origin, "committing to engage in primary or secondary education work for 6 years or more." Those who return to work in township or urban schools "must go to teach in rural compulsory education schools for at least 1 year." Article 13: Failure to fulfill the commitment or fulfilling it for less than the required term results in liability according to the agreement. One consequence is that "the breach of contract behavior shall be recorded in the credit file, shared promptly with the national credit information sharing platform, and relevant breach documents shall be placed in the individual's personnel file." Another sentence states "before completing the commitment task, one may not go to teach outside the oriented prefecture (city, prefecture, league) and may not be recruited (selected) as other public servants. Upon completion of the commitment task, the relevant credit rating shall be restored." If the service period in the agreement is not completed, one cannot register for other public service positions; once completed, the credit file is restored. Article 6: After admission, if found unsuitable for teaching after review, within 1 year of enrollment, the student must refund the government-funded education costs received and may transfer to a non-education major. Article 14: Failure to obtain a Master of Education degree and a teacher certificate within the prescribed study period shall be treated as a breach of commitment, requiring a refund and payment of a penalty. Article 21: Localities shall resolve the permanent establishment for government-funded education students returning to teach in primary and secondary schools within the existing total number of public institution establishments. Article 12 states: Prefecture and city levels shall organize schools to use specialized recruitment for government-funded education students, "through methods such as mutual selection between both parties, ensuring that a teaching school and position are truly arranged for every graduating government-funded education student." For targeted free medical students for rural areas, see another notice. After admission and before receiving the admission notice, an agreement must be signed with the training school and the health department and human resources and social security department of the county where the work is oriented. The agreement must "commit to serving for 6 years at the oriented rural grassroots medical institution after graduation." Fulfilling the commitment means completing the full term at the designated location according to the agreement. Regarding permanent establishment, the notice states provincial health departments "must actively seek the support of local establishment departments to properly resolve the employment arrangement for targeted medical graduates within the local total establishment according to prescribed procedures." Those reporting for duty in the central and western regions shall be recruited through specialized county recruitment, "completing the recruitment procedures for formal employees of public institutions." After reporting for duty according to the commitment, they must participate in 3 years of standardized residency training in general medicine, referred to as post-graduate standardized training. "Gui pei" is the stage after graduation where skills continue to be practiced in hospitals according to unified standards. During the training period, the original personnel relationship and salary remain unchanged. Breach of contract records are placed in the individual's personnel file, serving as a basis for integrity evaluation when administrative and public institutions such as medical facilities recruit publicly, when recruiting for standardized residency training, and when selecting graduate students. Those who intentionally breach the contract will be publicly announced nationwide through the "Credit China" website and subjected to inter-departmental punishment for dishonesty. The training years of contract breakers shall not be counted toward the service period. Anyone who does not refund costs and penalties according to the agreement will have them recovered by the county health department through legal channels (National).
To work abroad, first check if the company is qualified for foreign labor cooperation: the company is not allowed to collect a deposit from you
A

Regarding working abroad, the law does not regulate you, but the company that organizes your departure. Only enterprises with a Certificate of Qualification for Foreign Labor Cooperation that have completed registration procedures are allowed to do this. Hearing the phrase "just go on a tourist visa first and then change to a work visa" itself indicates that the other party is breaking the law. The company is also not allowed to collect a deposit from you under any name or require you to provide property as a guarantee.
No monetary cost. Before going, spend ten minutes checking the company's qualifications, then read both contracts in full.

Article 5 of the "Regulations on the Administration of Foreign Labor Cooperation" (China): engaging in foreign labor cooperation must be approved by the provincial or city-with-districts commerce department and possess business qualifications. This business qualification is the Certificate of Qualification for Foreign Labor Cooperation; without it, one cannot organize people to work abroad. Article 7: The list of qualification certificates is reported to the commerce department of the State Council and notified to Chinese embassies and consulates abroad. This article also states "those without a Certificate of Qualification for Foreign Labor Cooperation according to the law and who have not completed registration procedures shall not engage in foreign labor cooperation." Article 8: "No unit or individual may use the name of trade, tourism, study abroad... to organize workers to work abroad." Article 9: Within 5 working days of registration, the enterprise must deposit a "foreign labor cooperation risk disposal reserve fund of no less than ⟦3000000⟧" into a designated bank; the list of deposits is made public. Article 10: The reserve fund is used to pay service fees that must be refunded, labor wages, and damages that must be compensated according to the law which the enterprise refuses or is unable to pay. The fund is also used for "expenses for workers to return home or receive emergency relief due to unexpected events." Article 11: Organizing workers to work abroad in jobs related to gambling or prostitution is prohibited. Article 12: Workers may not be sent abroad without organized training. Article 13: Personal accident insurance must be purchased for workers during their time working abroad. Articles 21 and 23: Written contracts must be signed with the foreign employer and the worker respectively; workers may not be organized to go abroad before signing. Article 25: "No deposit shall be collected from workers under any name, nor shall workers be required to provide property as a guarantee." Article 26: Within 10 working days of signing the contract, it must be reported to the commerce department for filing. Article 29: If the actual rights of the worker do not match the contract, the enterprise must assist in seeking compensation; if adequate compensation is not received, the worker has the right to demand the enterprise bear the responsibility for compensation. Article 31: If the security situation in the relevant country or region makes it difficult to ensure personal safety, the enterprise shall not organize workers to go there. Article 37: The commerce department shall establish a system for recording and announcing records of violations and dishonesty. Sanctions are found in the subsequent articles. Article 39: Engaging in foreign labor cooperation without qualification will result in investigation, handling, and a ban on activities; if it constitutes a crime, criminal responsibility will be pursued. Article 40: Using the name of trade, tourism, or study abroad to organize departures, lending qualifications, or organizing work related to gambling or prostitution will result in the revocation of the business qualification certificate. Article 43: Failure to sign a contract, or hiding information or providing false information to organize departures, results in a fine of ⟦100000~200000⟧. The main person in charge is also fined ⟦20000~50000⟧ (National).

Working remotely from home for a foreign company, this money is domestic income under tax law: personal income tax must be self-declared, and foreign currency received falls under 'labor remuneration'
A

Whether this money is considered domestic or foreign income depends on where you work, not where the money is transferred from. Working remotely from within the country for a foreign company is domestic income, and domestic personal income tax must be paid. If the foreign company has no establishment in China, no one will withhold it for you; you must declare this tax yourself. When the money is transferred back, it falls under the category of "labor remuneration."

No monetary cost. A final settlement is done once a year between March 1 and June 30 of the following year. When the received amount exceeds the annual total limit, you must also prepare a labor contract and proof of income. The difficulty is remembering to declare this tax yourself.

To see if this money is considered income generated within the country, see Article 3 of the "Implementation Regulations of the Personal Income Tax Law" (China) (State Council Order No. 707, effective January 1, 2019). The regulations state: "Unless otherwise provided by the finance and tax departments of the State Council, the following income, regardless of whether the place of payment is within the territory of China, is income generated within the territory of China: (1) income obtained from holding a position, being employed, or performing a contract... by providing labor within the territory of China." Article 6 of the same regulations defines two tax items. One is wages and salaries: "Income from wages and salaries refers to wages, salaries, bonuses, year-end salary increases, labor dividends, allowances, subsidies, and other income related to holding a position or being employed obtained by an individual." Two is labor remuneration: "Income from labor remuneration refers to personal income obtained from engaging in labor services, including income obtained from design, decoration, installation, drafting, testing, medical, legal, accounting, consulting, lecturing, translation, manuscript review, calligraphy and painting, sculpture, film and television, sound recording, video recording, performance, show, advertising, exhibition, technical services, introduction services, brokerage services, agency services, and other labor services." Article 6 of the "Personal Income Tax Law" (China) states the method for calculating taxable income: "The comprehensive income of a resident individual shall be the balance of the income of each tax year after deducting expenses of sixty thousand yuan and specialized deductions, specialized additional deductions, and other deductions determined according to the law." The same article also states "income from labor remuneration, author's remuneration, and royalties shall be the balance of the income after deducting twenty percent of the expenses." The 20% deduction only lists these three items; wages and salaries are not among them. Thus, wages and salaries are fully counted as income; the two tax items result in different tax amounts. Article 9: "Personal income tax shall take the person receiving the income as the taxpayer and the unit or individual paying the income as the withholding agent." Article 10: "In any of the following cases, the taxpayer shall file a tax return according to the law: ... (2) having taxable income without a withholding agent; ... (4) having income from abroad." Article 11: "Resident individuals who have comprehensive income shall calculate personal income tax on an annual basis... those who need to perform a final settlement shall do so between March 1 and June 30 of the year following the year the income was obtained." Regarding the transfer of money, see the "Measures for the Administration of Individual Foreign Exchange" (China) (People's Bank of China Order No. 3 of 2006, effective February 1, 2007). Article 9: "For the sale of foreign exchange by individuals and the purchase of foreign exchange by domestic individuals, annual total limit management is implemented. Within the annual total limit, procedures are handled at the bank with the individual's valid identity document; exceeding the annual total limit, current account transactions are handled at the bank with the individual's valid identity document and relevant supporting documents showing the transaction amount." Article 7: "Banks and individuals must comply with the relevant provisions of these measures when conducting individual foreign exchange business, and must not split transactions or use other methods to evade quota management, nor use false certificates or commercial invoices to evade authenticity management." "Detailed Rules for the Implementation of the Measures for the Administration of Individual Foreign Exchange" (China) (SAFE Document No. 1 of 2007) Article 2: "For the sale of foreign exchange by individuals and the purchase of foreign exchange by domestic individuals, annual total limit management is implemented. The annual total limit is the equivalent of 50,000 US dollars per person per year." Article 10: "Domestic individuals selling foreign exchange belonging to non-business current account transactions that exceed the annual total limit shall handle procedures at the bank with their valid identity documents and the following supporting documents: ... (7) labor remuneration: labor contract and proof of income" (National).
Starting a business independently without joining a unit, look first at guaranteed entrepreneurship loans for initial funds: individuals up to ⟦300000⟧, the budget pays half the interest
A

If you belong to a key group such as graduates, discharged military personnel, or the unemployed, and want to borrow startup funds, look at this interest-subsidized loan first. Individuals can borrow up to ⟦300000⟧ for a maximum of 3 years, with the budget paying half the interest. When applying, you and your spouse must not have any other loans in your name; mortgages, car loans, student loans, and small consumer loans not exceeding ⟦50000⟧ are not counted.

Inquiring for information is free. First, go to the human resources and social security department once for qualification assessment, then to the guarantee organization and the implementing bank (the lending bank) once each for procedures. The difficulty is that the loan must eventually be repaid.

Conditions for individual applications are listed in Article 6 of the "Measures for the Administration of Special Funds for the Development of Inclusive Finance" (China) (Ministry of Finance Document No. 75 of 2023). The first condition is belonging to a key employment group. The document lists registered urban unemployed persons, people with employment difficulties (including the disabled), and discharged military personnel. It also includes university and college graduates (including village officials who are students and returning overseas students), and workers and unemployed persons from enterprises undergoing capacity reduction. It also includes rural laborers returning home to start businesses, online shop owners, people lifted out of poverty, and farmers starting their own businesses in rural areas... The second condition is having no other loans in one's name: "Except for student loans, micro-credit for people lifted out of poverty, housing loans, car loans, and small consumer loans not exceeding ⟦50000⟧ (including credit card consumption), the applicant and their spouse shall have no other loans when applying for a guaranteed entrepreneurship loan." Article 9: "For qualified guaranteed entrepreneurship loans, the financial department shall provide interest subsidies at 50% of the actual loan interest rate. For guaranteed entrepreneurship loans that are extended or overdue, the financial department shall, in principle, not provide interest subsidies." Interest subsidy means the budget pays half the interest for you. Extension means the deadline is pushed back, and overdue means the deadline has passed without repayment; in these two cases, the budget will no longer pay for you. Article 10: Guaranteed entrepreneurship loans not exceeding ⟦100000⟧ applied for by individuals shall, in principle, waive counter-guarantees, meaning no need to find additional people or provide property as a guarantee to the guarantee organization. Article 11: Individual guaranteed entrepreneurship loans eligible for rewards and subsidies shall have "a limit not exceeding ⟦300000⟧ and a loan term not exceeding 3 years." Partnership startups can have the limit appropriately increased, up to a maximum of 110% of the total maximum limits for individuals. The interest rate ceiling for rewarded and subsidized loans is divided into three levels: the eastern region is LPR+50BPs, the central and western regions are LPR+150BPs, and areas lifted out of poverty are LPR+250BPs. LPR is the bank's Loan Prime Rate, and BPs are basis points; the more added, the higher the interest. Those who "repay actively, create good employment, and have good startup projects" can apply again upon maturity, for a total of no more than 3 times. Article 8: Applicants first apply to the local human resources and social security department for qualification assessment, then submit applications to the guarantee organization and the implementing bank. Article 12: With the consent of the provincial government, localities may expand the scope of support and increase the limits and interest subsidy ratios (National).

If you graduated within the last two years and want to take the civil service exam, check how the recruitment notice defines "fresh graduate" before signing a job contract or transferring your files: the national civil service exam requires files and household registration to remain at the school or a talent service organization
A

In the Chinese national civil service exam, many positions primarily recruit fresh graduates. If you graduated within two years and have not yet had an employer, and your files and household registration (hukou) are still at the school or a talent service organization, you are also considered a fresh graduate. Each province has different rules: in Fujian, even if you have signed a contract and paid social insurance, you are still counted. Therefore, before signing for a job or transferring files, check the notice of the exam you wish to take.

Free. Before signing with an employer, spend half an hour finding the notices for the exams you want to take and read them through. The difficulty is that each place has its own rules, so you must check each exam individually.

The 2027 National Civil Service Recruitment Notice states: "agencies directly under the municipal (district) level and below" of central agencies "primarily recruit fresh college and university graduates." Question 3 in the exam guide for the same year specifically answers whether graduates from previous years are considered fresh graduates. Original text: "Full-time college and university graduates recruited under the unified national plan who, upon leaving school and during the job selection period (the job selection period stipulated by the State is two years), have not yet had an employer, and whose household registration, files, and organizational relations remain at the graduating school, or at graduate employment management agencies at all levels (graduate employment guidance and service centers), talent exchange service organizations at all levels, and public employment service organizations at all levels, may be treated as fresh college and university graduates." The job selection period is two years of job searching after graduation. Thus, the national civil service exam requires two conditions simultaneously: being within two years without an employer, and files, hukou, and organizational relations not having been transferred to an employer. Provincial exams are determined by the provinces themselves. Fujian's 2023 notice states: "Fresh graduates of the current year signing employment agreements, labor contracts, or paying social insurance... do not affect the determination of fresh graduate status; graduates from previous years with work experience and a history of social insurance payments can still register for positions reserved for fresh graduates." This applies to civil servants, public institutions, state-owned enterprises, and central enterprise units in Fujian. Chongqing's 2025 notice separates two types of exams. For the Chongqing civil service exam, the national exam's wording is copied exactly. For Chongqing public institutions and state-owned enterprises, one only needs to have not been recruited into a budgeted (bianzhi) position within two years; "signing employment contracts (agreements), work experience, social insurance payments... do not affect exam registration" (nationwide, provinces decide individually).
Before paying tuition, check if the school is on the list of institutions recognized by the Service Center for Scholarly Exchange
A

If you return home for further study, work, or exams that require this degree, you can apply for recognition from the Service Center for Scholarly Exchange (CSCSE) under the Ministry of Education (China). The center publishes a list of schools that have had degrees recognized in the last five years. Being on the list does not guarantee recognition, and not being on it does not necessarily mean the application will be rejected. Check once before paying tuition; if the name is not there, ask for clarification.
Free. Type the school name once into the "search for schools with recognized degrees" section of the CSCSE (China) website; it takes a few minutes.

Article 1 of the Regulations on the Recognition of Foreign Academic Degrees and Diplomas by the Service Center for Scholarly Exchange of the Ministry of Education (China) clearly states that recognition is to "meet the needs of applicants for further study, employment, exams, etc." Article 2 states that recognition is done "at the voluntary request of the applicant." The center has a search section for schools with recognized degrees, searchable by school name. The usage notes state that the list includes foreign schools granting degrees found in recognized files over the last five years, "only for the reference of students studying abroad, and is not a guarantee or basis for recognition." The notes also clarify that the scope of applications accepted "is not limited to the schools displayed by this search function"; each application is evaluated individually, and whether the school is legal and has the right to grant degrees is only one of the factors considered. The list is updated once a year. The 2025 update removed 270 schools that had no degrees recognized in the last 5 years. Additionally, the Ministry of Education (China) foreign-related education supervision information website publishes supervision information on joint education programs and overseas training institutions.

Follow the lawsuit regarding the new U.S. F-1 regulations: the "maximum four years, must leave 30 days after completion" rule was set to take effect on September 15, 2026, but was stayed by a court one day prior; it currently remains "duration of status"
A

The U.S. intended to change F-1 status to a maximum of four years, requiring departure 30 days after completion. One day before it took effect, a federal court stayed this regulation. Therefore, the old rule still applies: stay as long as you are studying, with 60 days to prepare for departure after completion. A stay is not a cancellation; the government can still appeal, and the law could change back at any time.

Free. Copy the program end date from your I-20 into your calendar and set a reminder 90 days before. The I-20 is the certificate of eligibility for student status issued by your school. Additionally, check the school's international student office announcements once per semester to see if there are new developments in this lawsuit.

The U.S. Department of Homeland Security published a regulation on July 17, 2026, scheduled to take effect on September 15, 2026. It stated that F-1 students would no longer be admitted under "duration of status" but for a fixed term of up to four years, requiring a separate extension upon expiration. After completing studies or practical training, only 30 days would be allowed to prepare for departure. On September 14, 2026, Judge Saylor of the U.S. Federal District Court for the District of Massachusetts, based on Section 705 of the Administrative Procedure Act (U.S.), stayed the effective date of this regulation. The stay applies nationwide and to the entire regulation. The court did not cancel the regulation; the request for cancellation was denied but allowed to be refiled later. The case is still ongoing. According to this order, holders of F, J, and I visas are still admitted under "duration of status," the 60-day grace period to depart remains, and no separate extension is required.
If working while studying abroad, first check the maximum working hours for each country (USA, Canada, UK, Australia); calculate separately for semesters, breaks, and different types of work
A

Working hours must be cross-referenced by country, type of work, and semester. In the U.S., on-campus work during the semester is limited to 20 hours per week. In the UK, eligible courses allow 20 or 10 hours per week. In Canada, off-campus work during the semester is limited to 24 hours per week. In Australia, it is 48 hours per fortnight during the course session. Breaks, internships, and remote work for foreign employers have specific rules and do not follow a single cap.
Free. Keep your own record of hours worked each week. The difficulty is that employers might say "working a few extra hours won't be checked," which should not be believed.

F-1 students in the U.S. working on-campus may not exceed 20 hours per week during the semester. Part-time off-campus employment authorized under paragraph (f)(9) of the regulations is also limited to 20 hours per week during the semester. During eligible breaks, full-time work is permitted. Curricular Practical Training (CPT) and other types of work are governed by the type of internship and the scope authorized; the above caps cannot be applied to all off-campus work. For UK student visas, hours depend on the school and whether the course is eligible. If sponsored by a university with a track record of compliance and studying a full-time course at degree level or above, 20 hours per week is allowed during the semester. Full-time courses below degree level sponsored by such institutions allow 10 hours per week. Eligible short-term exchange programs at universities also allow 20 hours per week during the semester. Other courses, including part-time courses, do not allow work. Generally, self-employment is not permitted, nor is working as a professional athlete or entertainer. The basis is the student section of the UK Immigration Rules, Appendix Student, items ST26.1, ST26.5, ST26.8. In Canada, eligible students may work off-campus up to 24 hours per week during regular academic sessions; multiple off-campus jobs are cumulative. The basis is Section 186(v) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR). During regularly scheduled breaks, eligible students may work full-time. Remote work for an employer outside Canada does not count toward this 24-hour cap but must still meet study permit conditions. For work eligibility in the final semester and during the transition between programs, see Section 4 (full-time, leave of absence, and school transfer). For Australian student visas, the limit is 48 hours per fortnight during the course session. Masters by research, doctoral students, and their family members are not subject to this limit.
Before reducing to part-time study, taking a leave of absence, dropping out, or transferring schools while studying abroad, cross-check work eligibility and exceptions
A

Whether you can work while studying abroad must be checked against the country you are in and your current academic status. In Canada, if you are on an approved leave of absence or transferring schools and not studying, you cannot rely on your study permit to work off-campus. However, if you are in your final semester with a reduced course load, or have finished one program and are transitioning to a new one, you may still be eligible to work if conditions are met. An unexpired visa does not replace the need to verify work eligibility.
Free. Before dropping out, taking a leave, or changing schools, visit the school's international student office first to clarify your residency status.

In Canada, when working under the authority of a study permit, you cannot work off-campus during an authorized leave of absence. If you are transferring schools and not studying, you also cannot work off-campus and must wait until you resume studies. However, there is an exception for the final semester: if you switch to part-time only because you do not need a full course load to complete your program, and you were a full-time student prior to that, you can still work off-campus. Other work conditions must also be met. For the gap between completing one program and starting a new one, there is a set of conditions for full-time work that must be met simultaneously: you were previously eligible to work off-campus; you have a valid study permit or applied for an extension before it expired; you have written confirmation of program completion from the old school and a letter of acceptance for a new full-time program at a Designated Learning Institution (DLI). The new program must start within 150 calendar days of receiving confirmation of completion of the previous program. This is different from transferring schools before finishing; you cannot rely solely on "having a new acceptance letter" to work. In the U.S., on-campus work eligibility requires the F-1 student's SEVIS status to be "Active." SEVIS is the residency record system for international students in the U.S.; "Active" means currently studying and valid. Students must also meet academic requirements to maintain status; before dropping a course, ask the school to check for exceptions. Work authorization in the UK is granted based on the type of school and course; part-time courses do not allow work.
USA: if you move, you must report your new address within 10 days
A

If you change your place of residence in the U.S., the law requires you to notify immigration authorities within 10 days. Failing to report is not a minor matter. First, the failure itself is a violation of the law; second, mail from immigration authorities might not reach you.
Free. Submit the change of address online once; it takes ten minutes.

U.S. Federal Immigration Regulation 8 CFR 265.1 states: an alien required to be registered under the law must, within 10 days of a change of address, notify USCIS (U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services) in the manner requested, reporting both the fact of the change and the new address.
Before leaving and during your studies, check the study abroad warnings from the Ministry of Education (China)
A

The Ministry of Education (China) occasionally issues specific warnings for a certain country or region, stating that the recent security situation or policies there are unfavorable for Chinese students. These are risk warnings published officially by a state agency, in black and white, searchable, and more reliable than the words of a brokerage firm. Checking them costs nothing.
Free. Check once before leaving, then once every semester.

The Ministry of Education (China) publishes study abroad warnings on its foreign-related education supervision information website. In 2025, a total of 4 issues were released. Issue No. 1 warned about higher education bills passed by some U.S. states containing negative provisions targeting China (April 9, 2025). Issues No. 2 and No. 3 twice warned that the Philippines had many cases targeting Chinese citizens and a poor study environment (July 18, 2025, August 30, 2025). Issue No. 4 warned that the security situation and study environment in Japan were poor, advising cautious consideration when planning to study in Japan (November 16, 2025).
Australia: OSHC international student health insurance must cover the entire duration of your stay in Australia without gaps; failure to present insurance upon entry may result in refusal of entry
A

Australia makes international student health insurance a visa condition; it is not optional. Insurance must cover the entire duration of your stay in Australia. When renewing a visa and changing insurance contracts, there must be no gap in between. If you cannot present an insurance certificate upon entry, you may be refused entry on the spot. Family members staying with you must also have this insurance.
A few thousand to over ⟦10000⟧. Purchase once according to the visa duration; buy as many years as you will be studying.

The Australian Department of Home Affairs stipulates that student visa applicants and accompanying family members must purchase Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC), which must be maintained for the entire duration of the stay in Australia without gaps. Insurance must be provided by an Australian-approved insurance provider, except for those exempt under regulations. There must be no gap between a new insurance contract and the insurance from a previous visa. Failure to provide evidence of insurance upon entry may result in refusal of entry. For those arriving in Australia before the course start date, the insurance start date must be the actual date of arrival in Australia.
UK: in addition to the visa fee, there is an annual health surcharge; students pay £776 per year, paid in full at the time of application
A

Going to the UK involves more than just the visa fee. You must also prepay the health surcharge based on the number of years on the visa; only after paying can you use the UK National Health Service (NHS). For a two-year visa, you pay £1,552 at once. Combined with the visa fee, this amount must be paid in full before you go; do not omit it from your budget.
Visa fee £558. Health surcharge £776 per year. Both are paid in full at the time of application.

The UK student visa fee is £558. Whether applying from outside the UK, or renewing or switching visas while in the UK, the amount is the same. Additionally, there is a health surcharge, which must be paid to use the UK National Health Service, prepaid in full at the time of application based on the number of years of the visa. Students and their dependents pay £776 per year; for example, a 2-year visa costs £1,552. Applicants in other categories pay £1,035 per year. Visas over 6 months but under 1 year are rounded up to one year.
Before returning home, allow time for degree recognition: the Service Center for Scholarly Exchange takes 10 to 20 working days to process
A

If you want to use a foreign degree upon returning home, you must first apply for degree recognition. The assessment phase alone takes 10 to 20 working days, not including the time to prepare documents. Autumn recruitment, civil service exam registration, and household registration all have deadlines; do not wait until you need the degree to start the process.
Submit application online, pay fees online. Document preparation plus processing time, calculated in working days, takes about one month in total.

Recognition of foreign academic degrees and diplomas is done on the online service portal of the Service Center for Scholarly Exchange (CSCSE) under the Ministry of Education (China). The process has four steps: account registration and identity verification, online submission of application and documents, online fee payment, and waiting for evaluation and approval. The announced processing time for recognition is 10 to 20 working days. Working days do not include weekends and holidays; this is the period the Center uses to assess the file.

Before applying to a school, search for the school's name once in the Service Center for Scholarly Exchange announcements; if a school is under "enhanced verification," degree recognition will take at least 60 working days
A

The Chinese Service Center for Scholarly Exchange (CSCSE) has named a series of foreign schools, implementing enhanced verification specifically for degree recognition from these institutions, and sometimes temporarily suspending applications for certain schools. Searching for the school's name once before applying is much less trouble than filing an appeal later.
Free. Before applying to a school, search for the school's name once in the announcement section of the Chinese Service Center for Scholarly Exchange.

The Service Center for Scholarly Exchange under the Ministry of Education (China) continuously issues announcements regarding enhanced verification for the recognition of academic degrees from certain foreign schools (degrees from these schools undergo an additional round of independent checking). The latest announcement is No. 9 (October 28, 2025), naming 4 schools. During the enhanced verification period, recognition applications for these schools "in principle shall not be less than 60 working days from the date (inclusive) of submission." The basis is Article 28 of the Regulations on the Recognition of Foreign Academic Degrees (China): when recognition data is abnormal or reports of issues are received, the Center may initiate enhanced verification, requiring the applicant and the school to assist in providing documents, while extending the recognition period. In May 2025, the Center also issued an announcement to "re-enhance verification" for 3 schools. The Center has also previously issued announcements temporarily suspending recognition applications for several foreign schools. An anti-fraud reminder in August 2025 clearly states: "Any organization or individual claiming 'guaranteed recognition,' 'recognition through internal channels,' 'supplementing documents due to the pandemic,' or 'expedited recognition' is engaging in false advertising."
USA: when on OPT after graduation, record the number of unemployed days; the cumulative total must not exceed 90 days, and for those with a STEM extension, the total must not exceed 150 days
A

OPT is a US authorization for F-1 students to intern or work after graduation; during this time, your residency status depends on being employed. If the cumulative number of unemployed days exceeds 90, your residency status may be terminated. For those with a STEM extension, the total combined time before and after the extension must not exceed 150 days. If the school's system has not recorded employer information, it is also counted as being unemployed.

Free. Record the start and end dates for each period of unemployment. Once you find a job, immediately report the employer information to the school. The difficulty lies in when the job search is not smooth and the number of days keeps increasing day by day.

US Federal Immigration Regulation 8 CFR 214.2(f)(10)(ii)(E) states: during the post-completion OPT period, residency status depends on whether one is employed. The cumulative number of unemployed days must not exceed 90 days. For those with a 24-month STEM extension, the total OPT time combined must not exceed 150 days, including the period before the extension. Official guidance from the US Student and Exchange Visitor Program (SEVP) clearly states: if the SEVIS record lacks employer information, it is counted as unemployment. Upon reaching 90 cumulative days, SEVP officers may manually terminate the student's residency status. SEVIS is the US record system for international student status. Regarding the application timeline according to the US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) website: applications can be submitted starting 90 days before graduation, and no later than 60 days after graduation. After the school enters the recommendation into SEVIS, the application must be submitted within 30 days.

Canada: before applying for a study permit, obtain a Provincial Attestation Letter (PAL/TAL) through the school; starting in 2026, those studying for a master's or doctoral degree at public schools will not need one
A

When going to Canada to study, most people must submit a Provincial Attestation Letter when applying for a study permit; this letter confirms you have been allocated a study spot by that province. This letter cannot be submitted as a supplement later. If a study permit is approved or rejected and then reapplied for, or if you transfer schools, you must obtain a new letter. Those studying for a master's or doctoral degree at public schools do not need one.

No extra cost; just request it from the school that accepted you. In most cases, you must accept the offer and pay a portion or all of the tuition fees first before the school will process it for you.

Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) states that the attestation letter is issued by the province or territory where you will study. The letter confirms you have been allocated a spot to study there. Most study permit applications must include this letter, and it must be submitted with the application; it cannot be supplemented later. Those studying from kindergarten to grade 12 do not need it. From January 1, 2026, those in master's or doctoral programs at public schools also will not need it. For those studying in Québec, this is replaced by a Québec Acceptance Certificate (CAQ). Exchange students who do not pay tuition, those renewing a permit at the same school and same level of study, and certain other special cases also do not need it. Those who do not need to submit it must include proof of exemption when applying. Attestation letters are usually only valid for the year they are issued; a letter issued in 2026 expires on December 31, 2026. It only needs to be valid at the time the permit application is submitted; it does not matter if it expires by the time classes start. If a study permit is approved or rejected and then reapplied for, a new letter must be obtained. From January 22, 2025, transferring schools also requires obtaining a new letter.
People with spinal cord injuries experiencing sudden severe headache and sweating: assist them to sit upright, loosen clothing first, and simultaneously call 120
B

In people with spinal cord injuries, the body's alarm system is partially severed. A full bladder or tight clothing might not be felt by them, but their blood pressure can spike very rapidly. Signs include a sudden severe headache and profuse sweating. At that moment, first assist the person to sit upright, loosen tight clothing, check for urinary retention, and simultaneously call 120.
Free. Three actions, completed in a few dozen seconds.

This episode is called autonomic dysreflexia. A systematic review searched four databases—Medline, CINAHL, EMBASE, and PsycINFO—including 31 studies, 6 of which were randomized controlled trials. The review clearly states that immediate non-pharmacological management during an episode consists of three steps: placing the patient in an upright sitting position, loosening restrictive clothing, and removing the triggering stimulus. These three steps are based on clinical consensus and physiological data, classified as Level 5 evidence. The body of the review specifies that this condition is common in injuries at the T6 level or above, with the most common triggers being bladder or bowel irritation. Stimuli below the level of injury cause a massive sympathetic discharge, causing blood pressure to spike, while sensation below the level of injury is partially or completely lost. Symptoms include severe headache and profuse sweating above the level of injury, though it can also be entirely asymptomatic. Failure to manage it can lead to intracranial hemorrhage, seizures, or even death. No studies have independently measured the effectiveness of sitting up during an episode, but in people with spinal cord injuries, resting blood pressure decreases significantly when moving from a flat lying position to sitting or tilting. Antihypertensive medication is only used if blood pressure remains elevated; prazosin has Level 1 evidence, while nifedipine and prostaglandin E2 have Level 2 evidence. The review also notes that prevention strategies mainly target the two most common groups of triggers—the urogenital system and surgery—most of which only have Level 4 and Level 5 evidence.
The first ten years after a spinal cord injury causing disability is a high-risk period for suicide; do not treat it as something that can be resolved just by "thinking positively"
A

Long-term monitoring at two spinal cord injury centers in the UK shows that the suicide rate for this group is five times higher than that of the general population. Over 90% of suicides occur within the first ten years after the injury. For those whose primary cause of injury was a suicide attempt, the risk is significantly higher.
Free. Make a phone call or book one medical appointment.

A study followed 2,304 patients with traumatic spinal cord injuries, newly admitted between 1991 and 2010, who survived the first year post-injury and had residual neurological functional impairment upon discharge; they were followed until the end of 2014. Among them, 63 people (2.7%) were injured primarily due to a failed suicide attempt. By the end of the follow-up period, 533 people had died, of which 4.2% died by suicide; 91% of suicides occurred within the first ten years post-injury. The age-standardized suicide mortality rate was 62.5 cases per 100,000 person-years (95% CI 36.4 to 88.6), five times the suicide rate of the general population in England and Wales in 2014 (12.2 cases per 100,000 people). Compared to other causes of injury, the group injured by a failed suicide attempt had an odds ratio (OR) for death of 4.32 (P<0.001) and for suicide of 9.46 (P<0.001).
Hospitalization for mental disorders is based on the principle of voluntariness; only two cases allow for detention without the individual's consent
A

A statement from family members or an employer is not enough to detain someone in a psychiatric hospital. The law only recognizes two cases, and first, there must be a diagnosis of a severe mental disorder: having self-harmed or being at risk of it, or having endangered others or being at risk of it. In the first case, the guardian's consent is required for admission. In the second case, if the individual does not consent, they can request a re-diagnosis within three days and can subsequently hire an independent expert evaluation.
Free. Remember these two cases so you can state them when necessary.

Article 30 of the Mental Health Law (China) clearly states that "inpatient treatment for mental disorders shall be carried out according to the principle of voluntariness." Only when diagnostic conclusions and health assessments show that the person being examined has a severe mental disorder and falls into one of the following cases must inpatient treatment be provided. The first case is "having committed acts of self-harm, or being at risk of self-harm." The second case is "having committed acts endangering the safety of others, or being at risk of endangering the safety of others." Article 31: in the first case, the medical institution may only provide inpatient treatment if the guardian agrees; if the guardian does not agree, it shall not be done. Article 32: in the second case, if the patient or the guardian does not agree, they may request a re-diagnosis, which must be requested within three days of receiving the diagnostic conclusion and performed by two licensed psychiatrists who were not the original diagnosing physicians; if they still disagree with the re-diagnosis conclusion, they may independently hire a legally qualified appraisal organization to conduct a medical appraisal of the mental disorder. Article 35: if the re-diagnosis conclusion or appraisal report shows that it cannot be determined that the patient has a severe mental disorder, or that the patient does not require inpatient treatment, the medical institution shall not provide inpatient treatment. Article 78: intentionally admitting a person who does not have a mental disorder into a medical institution for treatment as a mental disorder patient shall result in compensation according to the law (national, effective from May 1, 2013, amended in 2018).
Long-term caregivers for disabled family members also need someone to look out for their own health
A

Caregiver burnout is not an exaggeration. A US study followed over eight hundred elderly people for four years. The group that was both caring for a spouse who had lost the ability to care for themselves and reported experiencing mental stress had a mortality risk about sixty percent higher than those who were not caregiving. Caregivers who did not report stress did not show such an increase. Therefore, what needs attention is not the act of caregiving itself, but the prolonged stress.
Free. Delegate part of the caregiving tasks to others, then go for a health check-up yourself.

This was a prospective community-based cohort study from 1993 to 1998, with an average follow-up of 4.5 years, conducted in four US communities. There were 392 caregivers and 427 non-caregivers, aged 66 to 96, all living with a spouse. Over the four years, 103 people (12.6%) died. After adjusting for socio-demographic factors, pre-existing conditions, and subclinical cardiovascular disease, those who were both caregiving and reported mental or emotional stress had a 63% higher mortality risk than the non-caregiving control group (RR 1.63, 95% CI 1.00 to 2.65). Caregivers who did not report stress (RR 1.08, 95% CI 0.61 to 1.90) and those whose spouse had lost self-care ability but who were not themselves caregiving (RR 1.37, 95% CI 0.73 to 2.58) did not show an increased mortality rate after adjustment.
For long-term wheelchair use, switch to a pressure-relieving seat cushion and check the ischial and coccygeal areas once daily
B

Elderly people in nursing homes using pressure-relieving cushions had significantly fewer pressure ulcers in the ischial area compared to those using standard contoured foam cushions, but no difference was found when including the coccyx. In the trial, everyone was fitted with a properly sized wheelchair first, so the wheelchair itself must be chosen according to the user's dimensions, rather than just buying any generic model.
A pressure-relieving cushion costs from a few hundred to over ⟦1000⟧. Checking once a day takes one minute.

This randomized clinical trial was conducted in 12 nursing homes; from 2004 to 2008, it recruited 232 residents over age 65 who used a wheelchair for more than 6 hours per day and had a Braden score of 18 or less. Everyone was fitted with a properly sized wheelchair first, then randomly assigned to two groups. One group used skin protection cushions (air, viscous fluid with foam, or gel with foam), and the other group used 7.6 cm thick contoured foam cushions. Follow-up lasted 6 months or until a pressure ulcer developed. Ulcers in the ischial tuberosity area: 8 cases (6.7%) in the contoured foam group, 1 case (0.9%) in the skin protection group, P=0.04. Combined ulcers in the ischial tuberosity and sacrococcygeal areas: 21 cases (17.6%) in the contoured foam group, 12 cases (10.6%) in the skin protection group, P=0.14, showing no significant difference.
Do not buy therapies or devices claiming to "cure paralysis, blindness, or deafness"
A

The Advertising Law (China) is explicit: advertisements for medical services, drugs, and medical devices must not guarantee effectiveness, state cure rates or efficacy rates, or use spokespersons for recommendation or certification. Therefore, phrases like "stand up after three courses of treatment" or "how many people have been cured" are inherently illegal advertisements; there is no need to even investigate the principles they claim. Items that are not medical devices are not even permitted to mention curing diseases.
Free, and actually saves money. The difficulty is that family members may still hold onto hope and cannot be easily persuaded.

Article 16 of the Advertising Law (China) stipulates that advertisements for medical services, drugs, and medical devices shall not contain the following content: "(1) assertions or guarantees regarding efficacy or safety; (2) statements regarding cure rates or efficacy rates; (3) comparisons with the efficacy and safety of other drugs or medical devices or with other medical institutions; (4) use of advertising spokespersons for recommendation or certification." Article 17 stipulates that, except for advertisements for medical services, drugs, and medical devices, "all other advertisements are prohibited from mentioning therapeutic effects, and shall not use medical terminology or words that easily cause the goods being offered to be confused with drugs or medical devices." Article 4 stipulates that advertisements shall not contain false or misleading content and shall not cheat or mislead consumers; advertisers are responsible for the truthfulness of the advertising content (national, amended in 2021).
Once you have a disability certificate, go to the county-level Disabled Persons' Federation once to ask about all available benefits
A

The disability certificate itself does not issue money; it is a key. Linked to it are many separate benefit programs, each of which must be applied for individually; they do not come to you automatically. The first time you visit the Disabled Persons' Federation, go through the list and ask about each benefit one by one to avoid multiple trips.
Free. One trip to the county-level Disabled Persons' Federation (China) takes one morning to inquire. Afterward, you will have to visit more than one agency.

There are at least six benefit programs linked to the certificate, each with its own basis. Living allowance for disabled persons in financial difficulty and nursing allowance for persons with severe disabilities: see Chapter 7, Section 8 (two allowance items). Rehabilitation support for children with disabilities: see this chapter, Section 8 (rehabilitation support). Subsidies for basic assistive devices, based on Article 26 of the Regulations on Disability Prevention and Rehabilitation of Disabled Persons (China). Subsidies for home accessibility modifications: see this chapter, Section 9 (modifying ramps, handrails, and bathrooms). Proportional employment and employment services: see this chapter, Section 10 (proactively mention having a certificate). Personal income tax reduction: see this chapter, Section 11 (personal income tax reduction). Article 26 of these Regulations also clearly states that the State implements key rehabilitation projects to provide basic rehabilitation services for impoverished disabled persons in urban and rural areas, persons with severe disabilities, and "subsidies for the fitting of basic assistive devices according to relevant State regulations." Article 20 stipulates that relevant departments of people's governments at or above the county level and the Disabled Persons' Federation shall utilize community resources, establish rehabilitation sites or purchase services, to carry out community-based rehabilitation work such as rehabilitation guidance, daily living skills training, recovery nursing, fitting of assistive devices, information consultation, and referrals (national, effective from July 1, 2017). Article 21 of the same Regulations stipulates that providing rehabilitation services requires a needs assessment first, followed by the formulation of an individual plan based on the assessment results. A 2016 State Council (China) document states: "places with the conditions may provide subsidies for impoverished disabled persons in urban and rural areas and persons with severe disabilities when fitting basic rehabilitation assistive devices." The 2026 three-year action plan from the Ministry of Civil Affairs (China) and other departments clearly states the need to "standardize and strengthen the subsidy system for the installation and adjustment services of basic assistive devices for disabled persons." Disabilities resulting from work-related injuries follow a different path. The Management Measures for the Fitting of Assistive Devices under Work-Related Injury Insurance (China) apply to prosthetics, orthotics, prosthetic eyes, dentures, wheelchairs, and similar items. These measures stipulate that fitting must be confirmed by the Labor Capacity Appraisal Committee (China) beforehand. Costs for fitting, repair, and training are paid by the work-related injury insurance fund according to regulations. If fitted without prior confirmation or at a facility without an agreement, the insurance agency will not pay.
For children under 7 with disabilities or autism, visit the county-level Disabled Persons' Federation to apply for rehabilitation support
A

The State (China) has established a rehabilitation support system for children with disabilities and children with autism aged 0 to 6, covering surgery, assistive devices, and rehabilitation training. Priority is given to families in difficulty; local governments may relax age and family economic conditions if their budgets allow. According to regulations, support is provided up to age 6, so do not wait until the child is about to start school. Facilities must be chosen from the list designated by the Disabled Persons' Federation.
Free of charge. Apply once at the county-level Disabled Persons' Federation (China), then select a facility from the designated list.

The Opinions of the State Council (China) on Establishing a Rehabilitation Support System for Disabled Children clearly state that the targets for support are eligible children aged 0 to 6 with visual, hearing, speech, physical, intellectual, and other disabilities, as well as children with autism. This includes disabled children from families receiving urban or rural minimum living guarantees, registered poor families, and disabled children raised by child welfare institutions; orphaned disabled children and disabled children under the care of extremely impoverished individuals; and disabled children from other economically disadvantaged families. The specific criteria for "other economically disadvantaged families" are issued by local governments at or above the county level. The document also specifies that "regions with appropriate conditions may expand the age range for rehabilitation support for disabled children and may also relax the family economic conditions for those receiving support." Funding levels are determined by local governments at or above the county level for different groups based on local budgets, the number of recipients, and types of disabilities, with a periodic adjustment mechanism. Applications are submitted to the county-level Disabled Persons' Federation where the child's household registration (or residence permit) is located. Upon approval, guardians select a designated rehabilitation facility. Designated facilities are "selected based on principles of openness and quality" by local Disabled Persons' Federations at or above the county level in coordination with health, education, and civil affairs departments. Costs incurred at designated facilities are settled directly between the financial authorities and the facilities. "Costs incurred when the county-level Disabled Persons' Federation approves rehabilitation services at a non-designated facility shall be settled according to methods determined by the county-level Disabled Persons' Federation in consultation with the financial authorities at the same level." The document required provincial governments to issue local systems and supporting policies before the end of September 2018. The higher-level legal basis is Article 26 of the Regulations on Disability Prevention and Rehabilitation for Persons with Disabilities (China): The State establishes a rehabilitation support system for disabled children, "gradually ensuring that children aged 0 to 6 with visual, hearing, speech, physical, intellectual, and other disabilities, and children with autism, receive free services such as surgery, fitting of assistive devices, and rehabilitation training" (National, since 2018)
For installing ramps, handrails, and renovating bathrooms at home, you can apply for subsidies from the government at or above the county level
B
